column.value: He took curds and milk and the calf which he had prepared, and set it before them; and he was standing by them under the tree ①as they ate. ▷ ①Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to him, “Where is your wife Sarah?” And he said, “There, in the tent.”

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “I will certainly return to you ①at this time next year; and behold, your wife Sarah will have a son.” And Sarah was listening at the tent door, which was behind him. ▷ ①Lit when the time revives

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham and Sarah were old, advanced in age; Sarah was past ①childbearing. ▷ ①Lit the way of women

column.name: text
column.value: So Sarah laughed ①to herself, saying, “After I have become old, am I to have pleasure, my lord being old also?” ▷ ①Lit within

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh, saying, ‘Shall I actually give birth to a child, when I am so old?’

column.name: text
column.value: Is anything too ①difficult for the LORD? At the appointed time I will return to you, ②at this time next year, and Sarah will have a son.” ▷ ①Or wonderful ②Lit when the time revives

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah denied it, however, saying, “I did not laugh”; for she was afraid. And He said, “No, but you did laugh.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men rose up from there, and looked down toward Sodom; and Abraham was walking with them to send them off.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said, “Shall I hide from Abraham what I am about to do,

column.name: text
column.value: since Abraham will certainly become a great and ①mighty nation, and in him all the nations of the earth will be blessed? ▷ ①Or populous

column.name: text
column.value: For I have ①chosen him, so that he may command his children and his household after him to keep the way of the LORD by doing righteousness and justice, so that the LORD may bring upon Abraham what He has spoken about him.” ▷ ①Lit known

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said, “The outcry of Sodom and Gomorrah is indeed great, and their sin is exceedingly grave.

column.name: text
column.value: I will go down now and see whether they have done entirely as the outcry, which has come to Me indicates; and if not, I will know.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men turned away from there and went toward Sodom, while Abraham was still standing before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham approached and said, “Will You indeed sweep away the righteous with the wicked?

column.name: text
column.value: Suppose there are fifty righteous people within the city; will You indeed sweep it away and not ①spare the place for the sake of the fifty righteous who are in it? ▷ ①Or forgive

column.name: text
column.value: Far be it from You to do ①such a thing, to kill the righteous with the wicked, so that the righteous and the wicked are treated alike. Far be it from You! Shall not the Judge of all the earth ②deal justly?” ▷ ①Lit like this thing ②Lit do justice

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said, “If I find in Sodom fifty righteous within the city, then I will ①spare the entire place on their account.” ▷ ①Or forgive

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham replied, “Now behold, I have ①ventured to speak to the Lord, although I am only dust and ashes. ▷ ①Or resolved

column.name: text
column.value: Suppose the fifty righteous are lacking five, will You destroy the entire city because of five?” And He said, “I will not destroy it if I find forty-five there.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he spoke to Him yet again and said, “Suppose forty are found there?” And He said, “I will not do it on account of the forty.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Oh may the Lord not be angry, and I shall speak; suppose thirty are found there?” And He said, “I will not do it if I find thirty there.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Now behold, I have ①ventured to speak to the Lord; suppose twenty are found there?” And He said, “I will not destroy it on account of the twenty.” ▷ ①Or resolved

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Oh may the Lord not be angry, and I shall speak only this once: suppose ten are found there?” And He said, “I will not destroy it on account of the ten.”

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as He had finished speaking to Abraham the LORD departed, and Abraham returned to his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham journeyed from there toward the land of the ①Negev, and ②settled between Kadesh and Shur; then he lived for a time in Gerar. ▷ ①I.e., South country ②Lit dwelt

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham said of his wife Sarah, “She is my sister.” So Abimelech king of Gerar sent men and took Sarah.

column.name: text
column.value: But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Behold, you are a dead man because of the woman whom you have taken, for she is ①married.” ▷ ①Lit married to a husband

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abimelech had not come near her; and he said, “Lord, will You kill a nation, even though ①blameless? ▷ ①Lit righteous

column.name: text
column.value: Did he himself not say to me, ‘She is my sister’? And she herself said, ‘He is my brother.’ In the integrity of my heart and the innocence of my ①hands I have done this.” ▷ ①Lit palms

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to him in the dream, “Yes, I know that in the integrity of your heart you have done this, and I also ①kept you from sinning against Me; therefore I did not let you touch her. ▷ ①Lit restrained

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, return the man’s wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live. But if you do not return her, know that you will certainly die, you and all who are yours.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech got up early in the morning and called all his servants, and told all these things in their ①presence; and the people were greatly frightened. ▷ ①Lit ears

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech called Abraham and said to him, “What have you done to us? And ①how have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? You have done to me ②things that ought not to be done.” ▷ ①Lit what ②Lit deeds

column.name: text
column.value: And Abimelech said to Abraham, “What have you ①encountered, that you have done this thing?” ▷ ①Lit seen

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham said, “Because I thought, surely there is no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Besides, she actually is my sister, the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife;

column.name: text
column.value: and it came about, when God caused me to wander from my father’s house, that I said to her, ‘This is ①the kindness which you will show to me: ②everywhere we go, say of me, “He is my brother.” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit your ②Lit at every place where

column.name: text
column.value: Abimelech then took sheep and oxen and male and female servants, and gave them to Abraham, and returned his wife Sarah to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abimelech said, “Behold, my land is before you; ①settle wherever ②you please.” ▷ ①Lit dwell ②Lit it is good in your sight

column.name: text
column.value: To Sarah he said, “Look, I have given your brother a thousand pieces of silver. ①It is ②your vindication before all who are with you, and before everyone you are cleared.” ▷ ①Lit Behold, it is ②Lit for you a covering of the eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech and his wife and his female slaves, so that they gave birth to children.

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD had completely closed all the wombs of the household of Abimelech because of Sarah, Abraham’s wife.

column.name: text
column.value: After these things the word of the LORD came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Do not fear, Abram, I am a shield to you; ①Your reward shall be very great.” ▷ ①Or Your very great reward

column.name: text
column.value: But Abram said, “Lord ①GOD, what will You give me, since I ②am childless, and the ③heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?” ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD ②Lit go ③Lit son of acquisition

column.name: text
column.value: Abram also said, “ ①Since You have given me no ②son, ③one who has been born in my house is my heir.” ▷ ①Lit Behold ②Lit seed ③Lit then behold, a son of my

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, the word of the LORD came to him, saying, “This man will not be your heir; but one who will come from your own ①body shall be your heir.” ▷ ①Lit inward parts

column.name: text
column.value: And He took him outside and said, “Now look toward the heavens and count the stars, if you are able to count them.” And He said to him, “So shall your ①descendants be.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then he believed in the LORD; and He ①credited it to him as righteousness. ▷ ①Or imputed

column.name: text
column.value: And He said to him, “I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans, to give you this land to ①possess it.” ▷ ①Or inherit

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Lord ①GOD, how may I know that I will ②possess it?” ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD ②Or inherit

column.name: text
column.value: So He said to him, “ ①Bring Me a three-year-old heifer, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.” ▷ ①Lit Take

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ①brought all these to Him and cut them ②in two, and laid each half opposite the other; but he did not cut the birds. ▷ ①Lit took ②Lit in the midst

column.name: text
column.value: And birds of prey came down upon the carcasses, and Abram drove them away.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and behold, ①terror and great darkness fell upon him. ▷ ①Or a terror of great darkness

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Abram, “Know for certain that your ①descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, ②where they will be enslaved and oppressed for four hundred years. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them

column.name: text
column.value: But I will also judge the nation whom they will serve, and afterward they will come out with ①many possessions. ▷ ①Lit great

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, you shall go to your fathers in peace; you will be buried at a good old age.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in the fourth generation they will return here, for the wrongdoing of the Amorite is not yet complete.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when the sun had set, that it was very dark, and behold, a smoking oven and a flaming torch appeared which passed between these pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying, “To your ①descendants I have given this land, From the river of Egypt as far as the great river, the river Euphrates: ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: the land of the Kenite, the Kenizzite, the Kadmonite,

column.name: text
column.value: the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Rephaim,

column.name: text
column.value: the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Girgashite, and the Jebusite.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD took note of Sarah as He had said, and the LORD did for Sarah as He had ①promised. ▷ ①Lit spoken

column.name: text
column.value: So Sarah conceived and bore a son to Abraham in his old age, at the appointed time of which God had spoken to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham named his son who was born to him, the son whom Sarah bore to him, Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, as God had commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah said, “God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh ①with me.” ▷ ①Lit for

column.name: text
column.value: And she said, “Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I have given birth to a son in his old age.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the child grew and was weaned, and Abraham held a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore she said to Abraham, “Drive out this slave woman and her son, for the son of this slave woman shall not be an heir with my son ①Isaac!” ▷ ①Lit with Isaac

column.name: text
column.value: The matter ①distressed Abraham greatly because of his son Ishmael. ▷ ①Lit was very grievous in Abraham’s sight

column.name: text
column.value: But God said to Abraham, “ ①Do not be distressed because of the boy and your slave woman; whatever Sarah tells you, listen to her, for through Isaac ②your descendants shall be named. ▷ ①Lit Do not let it be grievous in your sight ②Lit your seed will be called

column.name: text
column.value: And of the son of the slave woman I will make a nation also, because he is your ①descendant.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham got up early in the morning and took bread and a ①skin of water, and gave them to Hagar, putting them on her shoulder, and gave her the boy, and sent her away. And she departed and wandered about in the wilderness of Beersheba. ▷ ①I.e., a skin used as a bottle

column.name: text
column.value: When the water in the skin was used up, she ①left the boy under one of the bushes. ▷ ①Lit cast

column.name: text
column.value: Then she went and sat down opposite him, about a bowshot away, for she said, “May I not ①see the boy die!” And she sat opposite him, and raised her voice and wept. ▷ ①Lit look at the death of the child

column.name: text
column.value: God heard the boy crying; and the angel of God called to Hagar from heaven and said to her, “ ①What is the matter with you, Hagar? Do not fear, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he is. ▷ ①Lit What to you; an idiom

column.name: text
column.value: Get up, lift up the boy, and hold him by ①the hand, for I will make a great nation of him.” ▷ ①Lit your

column.name: text
column.value: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went and filled the ①skin with water and gave the boy a drink. ▷ ①See note v 14

column.name: text
column.value: And God was with the boy, and he grew; and he lived in the wilderness and became an archer.

column.name: text
column.value: He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother took a wife for him from the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about at that time that Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, spoke to Abraham, saying, “God is with you in all that you do;

column.name: text
column.value: so now, swear to me here by God that you will not deal falsely with me or with my offspring or with my descendants, but according to the kindness that I have shown to you, you shall show to me and to the land in which you have resided.”

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham said, “I swear it.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Abraham ①complained to Abimelech because of the well of water which the servants of Abimelech had seized. ▷ ①Lit rebuked

column.name: text
column.value: And Abimelech said, “I do not know who has done this thing; you did not tell me, nor did I hear of it ①until today.” ▷ ①Lit except

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham took sheep and oxen and gave them to Abimelech, and the two of them made a covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: But Abraham set seven ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech said to Abraham, “What do these seven ewe lambs mean, which you have set by themselves?”

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “You shall take these seven ewe lambs from my hand so that it may be a witness for me, that I dug this well.”

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore he called that place ①Beersheba, because there the two of them took an oath. ▷ ①I.e., well of an oath

column.name: text
column.value: So they made a covenant at Beersheba; and Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, got up and returned to the land of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree at Beersheba, and there he called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God.

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham resided in the land of the Philistines for many days.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham was old, advanced in age; and the LORD had blessed Abraham in every way.

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham said to his servant, the oldest of his household who was in charge of all that he owned, “Please place your hand under my thigh,

column.name: text
column.value: and I will make you swear by the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of earth, that you shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I live;

column.name: text
column.value: but you will go to my country and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son Isaac.”

column.name: text
column.value: The servant said to him, “Suppose the woman is not willing to follow me to this land; should I take your son back to the land from where you came?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham said to him, “Beware that you do not take my son back there!

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD, the God of heaven, who took me from my father’s house and from the land of my birth, and who spoke to me and who swore to me, saying, ‘To your ①descendants I will give this land’—He will send His angel ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: But if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be free of this oath of mine; only do not take my son back there.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the servant placed his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham, and swore to him concerning this matter.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the servant took ten camels from the camels of his master, and went out with a variety of good things of his master’s in his hand; so he set out and went to ①Mesopotamia, to the city of Nahor. ▷ ①Heb Aram-naharaim, Aram of the two rivers

column.name: text
column.value: He made the camels kneel down outside the city by the well of water ①when it was evening, the time when women go out to draw water. ▷ ①Lit at time of evening

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “LORD, God of my master Abraham, please ①grant me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham. ▷ ①Lit cause to occur for me

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I am standing by the ①spring, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water; ▷ ①Lit fountain of water

column.name: text
column.value: now may it be that the young woman to whom I say, ‘Please let down your jar so that I may drink,’ and ①who answers, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels also’—may she be the one whom You have appointed for Your servant Isaac; and by this I will know that You have shown kindness to my master.” ▷ ①Lit she will say

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rebekah, who was born to Bethuel the son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor, came out with her jar on her shoulder.

column.name: text
column.value: The young woman was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had ①had relations with her. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came up. ▷ ①Lit known her

column.name: text
column.value: Then the servant ran to meet her, and said, “Please let me drink a little water from your jar.”

column.name: text
column.value: And she said, “Drink, my lord”; then she quickly lowered her jar to her hand, and gave him a drink.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will also draw water for your camels until they have finished drinking.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, and ran back to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the man was taking a close look at her ①in silence, to find out whether the LORD had made his journey successful or not. ▷ ①Lit keeping silent

column.name: text
column.value: When the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold ring weighing a ①half-shekel, and two bracelets for her ②wrists weighing ten shekels in gold, ▷ ①A shekel was about 0.5 oz. or 14 gm ②Lit hands

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, “Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room for us to stay overnight at your father’s house?”

column.name: text
column.value: She said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, Milcah’s son, whom she bore to Nahor.”

column.name: text
column.value: Again she said to him, “We have plenty of both straw and feed, and room to stay overnight.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man bowed low and worshiped the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned His kindness and His trustworthiness toward my master; as for me, the LORD has guided me in the way to the house of my master’s brothers.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the young woman ran and told her mother’s household about these things.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rebekah had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran outside to the man at the spring.

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw the ring and the bracelets on his sister’s ①wrists, and when he heard the words of his sister Rebekah, saying, “ ②This is what the man said to me,” he went to the man; and behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring. ▷ ①Lit hands ②Lit Thus the man

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Come in, blessed of the LORD! Why do you stand outside, since I have prepared the house, and a place for the camels?”

column.name: text
column.value: So the man entered the house. Then ①Laban unloaded the camels, and he gave straw and feed to the camels, and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: But when food was set before him to eat, he said, “I will not eat until I have stated my business.” And he said, “Speak on.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “I am Abraham’s servant.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has greatly blessed my master, so that he has become ①rich; and He has given him flocks and herds, and silver and gold, and servants and slave women, and camels and donkeys. ▷ ①Lit great

column.name: text
column.value: Now my master’s wife Sarah bore a son to my master ①in her old age, and he has given him all that he has. ▷ ①Lit after she was old

column.name: text
column.value: My master made me swear, saying, ‘You shall not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live;

column.name: text
column.value: but you shall go to my father’s house and to my relatives, and take a wife for my son.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said to my master, ‘Suppose the woman does not follow me.’

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to me, ‘The LORD, before whom I have walked, will send His angel with you to make your journey successful, and you will take a wife for my son from my relatives and from my father’s house;

column.name: text
column.value: then you will be free from my oath, when you come to my relatives; and if they do not give her to you, you will be free from my oath.’

column.name: text
column.value: “So I came today to the spring, and said, ‘LORD, God of my master Abraham, if now You will make my journey on which I have been going successful;

column.name: text
column.value: behold, I am standing by the ①spring, and may it be that the ②young unmarried woman who comes out to draw water, and to whom I say, “Please let me drink a little water from your jar”; ▷ ①Lit fountain of water ②Or virgin

column.name: text
column.value: and she says to me, “You drink, and I will draw for your camels also”—let her be the woman whom the LORD has appointed for my master’s son.’

column.name: text
column.value: “Before I had finished speaking in my heart, behold, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder, and went down to the spring and drew water, and I said to her, ‘Please let me drink.’

column.name: text
column.value: She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels also’; so I drank, and she watered the camels also.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I asked her, and said, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor’s son, whom Milcah bore to him’; and I put the ring on her nose, and the bracelets on her ①wrists. ▷ ①Lit hands

column.name: text
column.value: And I bowed low and worshiped the LORD, and blessed the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had guided me in the right way to take the daughter of my master’s brother for his son.

column.name: text
column.value: So now if you are going to ①deal kindly and truthfully with my master, tell me; and if not, tell me now, so that I may turn to the right or the left.” ▷ ①Lit show kindness and truth to

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban and Bethuel replied, “The matter has come from the LORD; so we cannot speak to you bad or good.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is Rebekah before you, take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master’s son, as the LORD has spoken.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Abraham’s servant heard their words, he bowed himself to the ground ①before the LORD. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: And the servant brought out articles of silver and articles of gold, and garments, and gave them to Rebekah; he also gave precious things to her brother and to her mother.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank and spent the night. When they got up in the morning, he said, “Send me away to my master.”

column.name: text
column.value: But her brother and her mother said, “Let the young woman stay with us a few days, say ten; afterward she may go.”

column.name: text
column.value: However, he said to them, “Do not delay me, since the LORD has prospered my way. Send me away so that I may go to my master.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “We will call the young woman and ①ask her.” ▷ ①Lit ask her mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Then they called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent away their sister Rebekah and her nurse with Abraham’s servant and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “May you, our sister, Become thousands of ten thousands, And may your ①descendants possess The gate of those who hate them.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rebekah got up with her female attendants, and they mounted the camels and followed the man. So the servant took Rebekah and departed.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Isaac had come back from ①a journey to Beer-lahai-roi; for he was living in the ②Negev. ▷ ①Lit coming to ②I.e., South country

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac went out to ①meditate in the field toward evening; and he raised his eyes and looked, and behold, camels were coming. ▷ ①Or stroll; meaning uncertain

column.name: text
column.value: Rebekah raised her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she dismounted from the camel.

column.name: text
column.value: She said to the servant, “Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?” And the servant said, “He is my master.” Then she took her ①veil and covered herself. ▷ ①Or shawl

column.name: text
column.value: The servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her; so Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

column.name: text
column.value: Now ①Sarah lived 127 years; these were the years of the life of Sarah. ▷ ①Lit the life of Sarah was

column.name: text
column.value: Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan; and Abraham ①came in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. ▷ ①Or proceeded

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abraham arose from mourning before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “I am a stranger and a foreign resident among you; give me ①a burial site among you so that I may bury my dead out of my sight.” ▷ ①Lit possession of a burial place

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him,

column.name: text
column.value: “Hear us, my lord: you are a ①mighty prince among us; bury your dead in the choicest of our graves; none of us will refuse you his grave for burying your dead.” ▷ ①Lit prince of God

column.name: text
column.value: So Abraham stood up and bowed to the people of the land, the sons of Heth.

column.name: text
column.value: And he spoke with them, saying, “If ①you are willing to let me bury my dead out of my sight, listen to me, and plead with Ephron the son of Zohar for me, ▷ ①Lit it is with your soul

column.name: text
column.value: that he may give me the cave of Machpelah which he owns, which is at the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in ①your presence for ②a burial site.” ▷ ①Lit the midst of you ②Lit possession of a burial place

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham ①so that the sons of Heth heard, that is, all who entered the gate of his city, saying, ▷ ①Lit in the ears of

column.name: text
column.value: “No, my lord, listen to me; I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Abraham bowed before the people of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But he spoke to Ephron ①so that the people of the land heard, saying, “If you will only please listen to me; I will give the price of the field, accept it from me so that I may bury my dead there.” ▷ ①Lit in the ears of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,

column.name: text
column.value: “My lord, listen to me: a plot of land worth ①four hundred shekels of silver—what is that between me and you? So bury your dead.” ▷ ①About 12.5 lb. or 5.7 kg

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham listened to Ephron; and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver which he had named in the ①presence of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, currency acceptable to a merchant. ▷ ①Lit ears

column.name: text
column.value: So Ephron’s field, which was in Machpelah, which faced Mamre, the field and the cave which was in it, and all the trees which were in the field, that were ①within all the confines of its border, ②were deeded over ▷ ①Lit in all its border around ②Or were ratified

column.name: text
column.value: to Abraham as a possession in the presence of the sons of Heth, before all who entered the gate of his city.

column.name: text
column.value: After this, Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah facing Mamre (that is, Hebron), in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: So the field and the cave that was in it ①were deeded over to Abraham for ②a burial site by the sons of Heth. ▷ ①Or were ratified ②Lit possession of a burial place

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham took another wife, ①whose name was Keturah. ▷ ①Lit and her name

column.name: text
column.value: She bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

column.name: text
column.value: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All of these were the sons of Keturah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac;

column.name: text
column.value: but to the sons of ①his concubines, Abraham gave gifts while he was still living, and sent them away from his son Isaac eastward, to the land of the east. ▷ ①Lit concubines which belonged to Abraham

column.name: text
column.value: These are ①all the years of Abraham’s life that he lived, 175 years. ▷ ①Lit the days of

column.name: text
column.value: Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man and satisfied with life; and he was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre,

column.name: text
column.value: the field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Heth; there Abraham was buried with his wife Sarah.

column.name: text
column.value: It came about after the death of Abraham, that God blessed his son Isaac; and Isaac ①lived by Beer-lahai-roi. ▷ ①Lit dwelt

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the records of the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s slave woman, bore to Abraham;

column.name: text
column.value: and these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, ①in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, ▷ ①Lit in regard to their generations

column.name: text
column.value: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

column.name: text
column.value: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages, and by their camps; twelve princes according to their ①tribes. ▷ ①Or peoples

column.name: text
column.value: These are the years of the life of Ishmael, 137 years; and he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: They ①settled from Havilah to Shur which is ②east of Egypt ③going toward Assyria; he ④settled in defiance of all his relatives. ▷ ①Lit dwelt ②Lit before ③Lit as you go ④Lit fell over against

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the records of the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham fathered Isaac;

column.name: text
column.value: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the ①Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the ②Aramean, to be his wife. ▷ ①I.e., Syrian ②I.e., Syrian

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was unable to have children; and the LORD ①answered him, and his wife Rebekah conceived. ▷ ①Lit was entreated of him

column.name: text
column.value: But the children struggled together within her; and she said, “If it is so, why am I in this condition?” So she went to inquire of the LORD.

column.name: text
text
column.value: When her days leading to the delivery were at an end, behold, there were twins in her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the first came out red, all over like a hairy garment; and they named him Esau.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward his brother came out with his hand holding on to Esau’s heel, so he was named ①Jacob; and Isaac was sixty years old when she gave birth to them. ▷ ①I.e., one who takes by the heel or supplants

column.name: text
column.value: When the boys grew up, Esau became a skillful hunter, a man of the field; but Jacob was a ①civilized man, living in tents. ▷ ①Lit complete

column.name: text
column.value: Now Isaac loved Esau because ①he had a taste for game; but Rebekah loved Jacob. ▷ ①Lit game was in his mouth

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob had cooked a stew one day, Esau came in from the field and he was exhausted;

column.name: text
column.value: and Esau said to Jacob, “Please let me have a mouthful of ①that red stuff there, for I am exhausted.” Therefore he was called ②Edom by name. ▷ ①Lit the red, this red ②I.e., red

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob said, “ ①First sell me your birthright.” ▷ ①Lit Today

column.name: text
column.value: Esau said, “Look, I am about to die; so of what use then is the birthright to me?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob said, “ ①First swear to me”; so he swore an oath to him, and sold his birthright to Jacob. ▷ ①Lit Today

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew; and he ate and drank, and got up and went on his way. So Esau despised his birthright.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a famine in the land, besides the previous famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. So Isaac went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt; stay in the land of which I shall tell you.

column.name: text
column.value: Live for a time in this land and I will be with you and bless you, for to you and to your ①descendants I will give all these lands, and I will establish the oath which I swore to your father Abraham. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: I will multiply your ①descendants as the stars of heaven, and will give your ②descendants all these lands; and by your ③descendants all the nations of the earth ④shall be blessed, ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit seed ③Lit seed ④Or bless themselves

column.name: text
column.value: because Abraham ①obeyed Me and fulfilled his duty to Me, and kept My commandments, My statutes, and My laws.” ▷ ①Lit listened diligently to My voice

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac lived in Gerar.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of the place asked about his wife, he said, “She is my sister,” for he was afraid to say, “my wife,” thinking, “ ①the men of the place might kill me on account of Rebekah, since she is beautiful.” ▷ ①Lit lest...place

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when he had been there a long time, that Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through a window, and saw them, and behold, Isaac was caressing his wife Rebekah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech called Isaac and said, “Behold, she certainly is your wife! So how is it that you said, ‘She is my sister’?” And Isaac said to him, “Because I thought, ‘otherwise I might be killed on account of her.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And Abimelech said, “What is this that you have done to us? One of the people might easily have slept with your wife, and you would have brought guilt upon us.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech commanded all the people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife will certainly be put to death.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Isaac sowed in that land and ①reaped in the same year a hundred times as much. And the LORD blessed him, ▷ ①Lit found

column.name: text
column.value: and the man became rich, and continued to grow ①richer until he became very ②wealthy; ▷ ①Lit great ②Lit great

column.name: text
column.value: for he had possessions of flocks ①and herds, and a great household, so that the Philistines envied him. ▷ ①Lit and possessions of herds

column.name: text
column.value: Now all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of his father Abraham, the Philistines stopped up ①by filling them with dirt. ▷ ①Lit and filled them

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us, for you are ①too powerful for us.” ▷ ①Lit much mightier than we

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac departed from there and camped in the Valley of Gerar, and ①settled there. ▷ ①Lit dwelt

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac dug again the wells of water which ①had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham; and he ②gave them the same names which his father had ③given them. ▷ ①Lit they had dug ②Lit called their names as the names ③Lit called

column.name: text
column.value: But when Isaac’s servants dug in the valley and found there a well of ①flowing water, ▷ ①Lit living

column.name: text
column.value: the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with the herdsmen of Isaac, saying, “The water is ours!” So he named the well ①Esek, because they argued with him. ▷ ①I.e., argument

column.name: text
column.value: Then they dug another well, and they quarreled over it too, so he named it ①Sitnah. ▷ ①I.e., accusation

column.name: text
column.value: Then he moved away from there and dug another well, and they did not quarrel over it; so he named it ①Rehoboth, for he said, “ ②At last the LORD has made ③room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.” ▷ ①I.e., broad places ②Lit Truly now ③Or broad

column.name: text
column.value: And he went up from there to Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD appeared to him the same night and said, “I am the God of your father Abraham; Do not fear, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your ①descendants, For the sake of My servant Abraham.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: So he built an altar there and called upon the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there; and there Isaac’s servants dug a well.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech came to him from Gerar ①with his adviser Ahuzzath, and Phicol the commander of his army. ▷ ①Lit and his confidential friend

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, since you hate me and have sent me away from you?”

column.name: text
column.value: They said, “We have seen plainly that the LORD has been with you; so we said, ‘An oath must now be taken ①by us,’ that is, ②by you and us. So let us make a covenant with you, ▷ ①Lit between us ②Lit between us and you

column.name: text
column.value: that you will do us no harm, just as we have not touched you ①and have done to you nothing but good, and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit and just as we

column.name: text
column.value: Then he made them a feast, and they ate and drank.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning they got up early and ①exchanged oaths; then Isaac sent them away, and they left him in peace. ▷ ①Lit swore one to another

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about on the same day, that Isaac’s servants came in and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he called it ①Shibah; therefore the name of the city is Beersheba to this day. ▷ ①Meaning uncertain, perhaps oath

column.name: text
column.value: When Esau was forty years old he ①married Judith the daughter of Beeri the Hittite, and Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite; ▷ ①Lit took as wife

column.name: text
column.value: and they ①brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah. ▷ ①Lit were a bitterness of spirit to

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when Isaac was old and his eyes were too dim to see, that he called his older son Esau and said to him, “My son.” And he said to him, “Here I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then ①Isaac said, “Behold now, I am old and I do not know the day of my death. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, please take your gear, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me;

column.name: text
column.value: and prepare a delicious meal for me such as I love, and bring it to me that I may eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to his son Esau. So when Esau went to the field to hunt for game to bring home,

column.name: text
column.value: Rebekah said to her son Jacob, “Behold, I heard your father speak to your brother Esau, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Bring me some game and prepare a delicious meal for me, so that I may eat, and bless you in the presence of the LORD before my death.’

column.name: text
column.value: So now, my son, listen to ①me ②as I command you. ▷ ①Lit my voice ②Lit according to what

column.name: text
column.value: Go now to the flock and ①bring me two choice ②young goats from there, so that I may prepare them as a delicious meal for your father, such as he loves. ▷ ①Lit take ②Lit kids of goats

column.name: text
column.value: Then you shall bring it to your father, that he may eat, so that he may bless you before his death.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, “Behold, my brother Esau is a hairy man and I am a smooth man.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps my father will touch me, then I will be like a ①deceiver in his sight, and I will bring upon myself a curse and not a blessing.” ▷ ①Lit mocker

column.name: text
column.value: But his mother said to him, “Your curse be on me, my son; only obey my voice, and go, get the goats for me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he went and got them, and brought them to his mother; and his mother made a delicious meal such as his father loved.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rebekah took the ①best garments of her elder son Esau, which were with her in the house, and put them on her younger son Jacob. ▷ ①Lit desirable; or choice

column.name: text
column.value: And she put the skins of the ①young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck. ▷ ①Lit kids of the goats

column.name: text
column.value: She also gave the delicious meal and the bread which she had made ①to her son Jacob. ▷ ①Lit into the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: Then he came to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?”

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau your firstborn; I have done as you told me. Come now, sit and eat of my game, so that ①you may bless me.” ▷ ①Lit your soul

column.name: text
column.value: Isaac said to his son, “How is it that you have it so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because the LORD your God made it ①come to me.” ▷ ①Lit meet me

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac said to Jacob, “Please come close, so that I may feel you, my son, whether you are really my son Esau or not.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob came close to his father Isaac, and he touched him and said, “The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Esau’s hands; so he blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he said, “I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “Bring it to me, and I will eat of my son’s game, that ①I may bless you.” And he brought it to him, and he ate; he also brought him wine and he drank. ▷ ①Lit my soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then his father Isaac said to him, “Please come close and kiss me, my son.”

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: May peoples serve you, And nations bow down to you; Be master of your brothers, And may your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be those who curse you, And blessed be those who bless you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had hardly gone out from the presence of his father Isaac, that his brother Esau came in from his hunting.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he also made a delicious meal, and brought it to his father; and he said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat of his son’s game, that ①you may bless me.” ▷ ①Lit your soul

column.name: text
column.value: His father Isaac said to him, “Who are you?” And he said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac ①trembled violently, and said, “Who then was he who hunted game and brought it to me, so that I ate from all of it before you came, and blessed him? Yes, and he shall be blessed.” ▷ ①Lit trembled with a very great trembling

column.name: text
column.value: When Esau heard the words of his father, he cried out with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, me as well, my father!”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Your brother came deceitfully and has taken away your blessing.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau said, “ ①Is he not rightly named ②Jacob, for he has betrayed me these two times? He took away my birthright, and behold, now he has taken away my blessing.” And he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?” ▷ ①Or Was he then named Jacob that he has ②Fr Heb verb meaning to seize someone by the heel, and so to betray

column.name: text
column.value: But Isaac replied to Esau, “Behold, I have made him your master, and I have given to him all his relatives ①as servants; and with grain and new wine I have sustained him. What then can I do for you, my son?” ▷ ①Lit for

column.name: text
column.value: Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me as well, my father.” So Esau raised his voice and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his father Isaac answered and said to him, “Behold, ①away from the ②fertility of the earth shall be your dwelling, And ③away from the dew of heaven from above. ▷ ①Or of ②Lit fatness ③Or of

column.name: text
column.value: And by your sword you shall live, And you shall serve your brother; But it shall come about when you become restless, That you will ①break his yoke from your neck.” ▷ ①Lit tear off

column.name: text
column.value: So Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and Esau said ①to himself, “The days of mourning for my father are near; then I will kill my brother Jacob.” ▷ ①Lit in his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the words of her elder son Esau were reported to Rebekah, she sent word and called her younger son Jacob, and said to him, “Behold your brother Esau is consoling himself concerning you by planning to kill you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, my son, obey my voice, and arise, ①flee to Haran, to my brother Laban! ▷ ①Lit flee for yourself

column.name: text
column.value: Stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury ①subsides, ▷ ①Lit turns away

column.name: text
column.value: until your brother’s anger ①against you subsides and he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send word and get you from there. Why should I lose you both in one day?” ▷ ①Lit turns away from you

column.name: text
column.value: And Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am tired of ①living because of the daughters of Heth; if Jacob takes a wife from the daughters of Heth like these from the daughters of the land, what good will my life be to me?” ▷ ①Lit my life

column.name: text
column.value: So Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and commanded him, ①saying to him, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan. ▷ ①Lit and said to

column.name: text
column.value: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father; and from there take to yourself a wife from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.

column.name: text
column.value: May ①God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a multitude of peoples. ▷ ①Heb El Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: May He also give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your ①descendants with you, so that you may possess the land where you live as a stranger, which God gave to Abraham.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram to Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take to himself a wife from there, and that when he blessed him he commanded him, saying, “You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,”

column.name: text
column.value: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan-aram.

column.name: text
column.value: So Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan displeased ①his father Isaac; ▷ ①Lit in the eyes of his

column.name: text
column.value: and Esau went to Ishmael, and ①married, besides the wives that he had, Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebaioth. ▷ ①Lit took for his wife

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob departed from Beersheba and went toward Haran.

column.name: text
column.value: And he ①happened upon a ②particular place and spent the night there, because the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place and made it a support for his head, and lay down in that place. ▷ ①Lit lighted on ②Lit the place

column.name: text
column.value: And he had a dream, and behold, a ladder was set up on the earth with its top reaching to heaven; and behold, the angels of God were ascending and descending on it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, the LORD was standing ①above it and said, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac; the land on which you lie I will give to you and to your ②descendants. ▷ ①Or beside him ②Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Your ①descendants will also be like the dust of the earth, and you will ②spread out to the west and to the east, and to the north and to the south; and in you and in your ③descendants shall all the families of the earth be blessed. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit break through ③Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have ①promised you.” ▷ ①Lit spoken to

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, “The LORD is certainly in this place, and I did not know it!”

column.name: text
column.value: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob got up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had placed as a support for his head, and set it up as a memorial stone, and poured oil on its top.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he named that place ①Bethel; but ②previously the name of the city had been Luz. ▷ ①I.e., the house of God ②Lit at the first

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob also made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and will keep me on this journey that I ①take, and give me ②food to eat and garments to wear, ▷ ①Lit go ②Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: and I return to my father’s house in ①safety, then the LORD will be my God. ▷ ①Lit peace

column.name: text
column.value: And this stone, which I have set up as a memorial stone, will be God’s house, and of everything that You give me I will assuredly give a tenth to You.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Dinah the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to ①visit the daughters of the land. ▷ ①Lit see

column.name: text
column.value: When Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her, he took her and lay with her and raped her.

column.name: text
column.value: But ①he was deeply attracted to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the girl and ②spoke tenderly to her. ▷ ①Lit His soul clung ②Lit spoke to the heart of the girl

column.name: text
column.value: So Shechem spoke to his father Hamor, saying, “Get me this young woman as a wife.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled his daughter Dinah; but his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Jacob said nothing until they came in.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to speak with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard about it; and the men were grieved, and they were very angry because he had done a ①disgraceful thing in Israel by ②sleeping with Jacob’s daughter, for such a thing ought not to be done. ▷ ①Lit senseless ②I.e., violating her

column.name: text
column.value: But Hamor spoke with them, saying, “The soul of my son Shechem longs for your daughter; please give her to him ①in marriage. ▷ ①Lit for a wife

column.name: text
column.value: And intermarry with us; give your daughters to us and take our daughters for yourselves.

column.name: text
column.value: So you will live with us, and the land shall be ①open to you; live and trade in it and acquire property in it.” ▷ ①Lit before you

column.name: text
column.value: Shechem also said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your sight, and I will give whatever you tell me.

column.name: text
column.value: Demand of me ever so much bridal payment and gift, and I will give whatever you tell me; but give me the girl ①in marriage.” ▷ ①Lit for a wife

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob’s sons answered Shechem and his father Hamor with deceit, because he had defiled their sister Dinah.

column.name: text
column.value: They said to them, “We cannot do this thing, that is, give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised, for that would be a disgrace to us.

column.name: text
column.value: Only on this condition will we consent to you: if you will become like us, in that every male of you will be circumcised,

column.name: text
column.value: then we will give our daughters to you, and we will take your daughters for ourselves, and we will live with you and become one people.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you do not listen to us to be circumcised, then we will take our daughter and go.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now their words seemed ①reasonable to Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son. ▷ ①Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: The young man did not delay to do ①this, because he was delighted with Jacob’s daughter. Now he was more respected than all the household of his father. ▷ ①Lit the thing

column.name: text
column.value: So Hamor and his son Shechem came to the gate of their city and spoke to the people of their city, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “These men are ①friendly to us; therefore let them live in the land and trade in it, for behold, the land is ②large enough for them. We will take their daughters ③in marriage, and give our daughters to them. ▷ ①Lit peaceful ②Lit wide of hands before them ③Lit to us for wives

column.name: text
column.value: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people: that every male among us be circumcised just as they are circumcised.

column.name: text
column.value: Will their livestock and their property and all their animals not be ours? Let’s just consent to them, and they will live with us.”

column.name: text
column.value: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and to his son Shechem, and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of Jacob’s sons—Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers—each took his sword and came upon the city undetected, and killed every male.

column.name: text
column.value: They killed Hamor and his son Shechem with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah from Shechem’s house, and left.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob’s sons came upon those killed and looted the city, because they had defiled their sister.

column.name: text
column.value: They took their flocks, their herds, and their donkeys, and that which was in the city and that which was in the field;

column.name: text
column.value: and they captured and looted all their wealth and all their little ones and their wives, even everything that was in the houses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought trouble on me by making me repulsive among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites; and ①since my men are few in number, they will band together against me and ②attack me, and I will be destroyed, I and my household!” ▷ ①Lit I, few in number ②Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: But they said, “Should he ①treat our sister like a prostitute?” ▷ ①Or make

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob ①set out on his journey, and went to the land of the ②people of the east. ▷ ①Lit lifted up his feet ②Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: He looked, and ①saw a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, because they watered the flocks from that well. Now the stone on the mouth of the well was large. ▷ ①Lit behold

column.name: text
column.value: When all the flocks were gathered there, they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would put the stone back in its place on the mouth of the well.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to them, “My brothers, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Haran.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to them, “Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?” And they said, “We know him.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to them, “Is it well with him?” And they said, “It is well, and here is his daughter Rachel coming with the sheep.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Look, it is still high day; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep, and go, pasture them.”

column.name: text
column.value: But they said, “We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered, and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.”

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, and the sheep of his mother’s brother Laban, Jacob went up and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the flock of his mother’s brother Laban.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and raised his voice and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob told Rachel that he was a relative of her father and that he was Rebekah’s son, and she ran and told her father.

column.name: text
column.value: So when Laban heard the news about Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Then he told Laban all these things.

column.name: text
column.value: And Laban said to him, “You certainly are my bone and my flesh.” And he stayed with him a month.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

column.name: text
column.value: And Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in figure and appearance.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you than to give her to another man; stay with me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him like only a few days because of his love for her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my ①time is completed, that I may have relations with her.” ▷ ①Lit days are

column.name: text
column.value: So Laban gathered all the people of the place and held a feast.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the evening he took his daughter Leah and brought her to him; and Jacob had relations with her.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban also gave his female slave Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a slave.

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about in the morning that, behold, it was Leah! And he said to Laban, “What is this that you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? Why then have you deceived me?”

column.name: text
column.value: But Laban said, “It is not ①the practice in our place to ②marry off the younger before the firstborn. ▷ ①Lit done thus in ②Lit give

column.name: text
column.value: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you shall serve with me, for another seven years.”

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob did so and completed her week, and he gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban also gave his female slave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her slave.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob had relations with Rachel also, and indeed he loved Rachel more than Leah, and he served with ①Laban for another seven years. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD saw that Leah was ①unloved, and He opened her womb, but Rachel was unable to have children. ▷ ①Lit hated

column.name: text
column.value: Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and named him ①Reuben, for she said, “Because the LORD has ②seen my affliction; surely now my husband will love me.” ▷ ①I.e., see, a son ②Lit looked at

column.name: text
column.value: Then she conceived again and gave birth to a son, and said, “Because the LORD has ①heard that I am ②unloved, He has therefore given me this son also.” So she named him Simeon. ▷ ①Heb shama, related to Simeon ②Lit hated

column.name: text
column.value: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son, and said, “Now this time my husband will become ①attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore he was named Levi. ▷ ①Heb lavah, related to Levi

column.name: text
column.value: And she conceived again and gave birth to a son, and said, “This time I will ①praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him ②Judah. Then she stopped having children. ▷ ①Heb Jadah, related to Judah ②Heb Jehudah

column.name: text
column.value: Now ①Jacob heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s, and from what belonged to our father he has made all this ②wealth.” ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit glory

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob saw the ①attitude of Laban, and behold, it was not friendly toward him as it had been before. ▷ ①Lit face

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to his flock in the field,

column.name: text
column.value: and said to them, “I see your father’s ①attitude, that it is not friendly toward me as it was before, but the God of my father has been with me. ▷ ①Lit face

column.name: text
column.value: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times; however, God did not allow him to do me harm.

column.name: text
column.value: If he said this: ‘The speckled shall be your wages,’ then all the flock delivered speckled; and if he said this: ‘The striped shall be your wages,’ then all the flock delivered striped.

column.name: text
column.value: So God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about at the time when the flock was breeding that I raised my eyes and saw in a dream—and behold—the male goats that were ①mating were striped, speckled, or mottled. ▷ ①Lit leaping upon the flock

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob’; and I said, ‘Here I am.’

column.name: text
column.value: He said, ‘Now raise your eyes and see that all the male goats that are ①mating are striped, speckled, or mottled; for I have seen everything that Laban has been doing to you. ▷ ①Lit leaping upon the flock

column.name: text
column.value: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a memorial stone, where you made a vow to Me; now arise, ①leave this land, and return to the land of your birth.’ ” ▷ ①Lit Go out from

column.name: text
column.value: Rachel and Leah said to him, “Do we still have any share or inheritance in our father’s house?

column.name: text
column.value: Are we not regarded by him as foreigners? For he has sold us, and has also ①entirely consumed our ②purchase price. ▷ ①I.e., enjoyed the benefit of ②Lit money

column.name: text
column.value: Surely all the wealth which God has taken away from our father belongs to us and our children; now then, do whatever God has told you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob stood up and put his children and his wives on camels;

column.name: text
column.value: and he drove away all his livestock and all his property which he had acquired, the livestock he possessed which he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to the land of Canaan to his father Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: Laban had gone to shear his flock, and Rachel stole the ①household idols that were her father’s. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob ①deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was fleeing. ▷ ①Lit stole the heart of

column.name: text
column.value: So he fled with all that he had; and he got up and crossed the Euphrates River, and set ①out for the hill country of Gilead. ▷ ①Lit his face

column.name: text
column.value: When Laban was informed on the third day that Jacob had fled,

column.name: text
column.value: he took his kinsmen with him and pursued him a distance of seven days’ journey, and he overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: However, God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream of the night and said to him, “ ①Be careful that you do not speak to Jacob either good or bad.” ▷ ①Lit Take heed to yourself

column.name: text
column.value: And Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban with his kinsmen camped in the hill country of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done ①by deceiving me and carrying away my daughters like captives of the sword? ▷ ①Lit and you have stolen my heart

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you flee secretly and ①deceive me, and did not tell me, so that I might have sent you away with joy and with songs, with tambourine and with lyre; ▷ ①Lit steal me

column.name: text
column.value: and did not allow me to kiss my ①grandchildren and my daughters? Now you have done foolishly. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: It is in ①my power to do you harm, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘ ②Be careful not to speak either good or bad to Jacob.’ ▷ ①Lit the power of my hand ②Lit Take heed to yourself

column.name: text
column.value: Now you have indeed gone away because you longed greatly for your father’s house; but why did you steal my gods?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob replied to Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I thought that you would take your daughters from me by force.

column.name: text
column.value: The one with whom you find your gods shall not live; in the presence of our relatives ①point out what is yours ②among my belongings and take it for yourself.” Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them. ▷ ①Lit recognize ②Lit with me

column.name: text
column.value: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two slave women, but he did not find them. Then he went out of Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Rachel had taken the ①household idols and put them in the camel’s saddlebag, and she sat on them. So Laban searched through all the tent, but did not find them. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her father, “May my lord not be angry that I cannot stand in your presence, because the ①way of women is upon me.” So he searched but did not find the ②household idols. ▷ ①I.e., menstruation ②Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob became angry and argued with Laban; and Jacob said to Laban, “What is my offense? What is my sin that you have hotly pursued me?

column.name: text
column.value: Though you have searched through all my property, what have you found of all your household property? Set it here in front of my relatives and your relatives, so that they may decide between the two of us.

column.name: text
column.value: For these twenty years I have been with you; your ewes and your female goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: I did not even bring to you that which was torn by wild animals; I took the loss myself. You demanded it of my hand whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

column.name: text
column.value: This is how I was: by day the ①heat consumed me and the frost by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes. ▷ ①Or drought

column.name: text
column.value: For these twenty years I have been in your house; I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times.

column.name: text
column.value: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the fear of Isaac, had not been for me, surely now you would have sent me away empty-handed. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, so He rendered judgment last night.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Laban replied to Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the ①children are my ②grandchildren, the flocks are my flocks, and everything that you see is mine. But what can I do this day to these daughters of mine or to their children to whom they have given birth? ▷ ①Lit sons ②Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: So now come, let’s make a covenant, ①you and I, and it shall be a witness between ②you and me.” ▷ ①Lit I and you ②Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob took a stone and set it up as a memorial stone.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” So they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Laban called it ①Jegar-sahadutha, but Jacob called it ②Galeed. ▷ ①I.e., the heap of witness, in Aram ②I.e., the heap of witness, in Heb

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said, “This heap is a witness between ①you and me this day.” Therefore it was named Galeed, ▷ ①Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: and ①Mizpah, for he said, “May the LORD keep watch between ②you and me when we are ③absent one from the other. ▷ ①Lit the Mizpah; i.e., the watchtower ②Lit me and you ③Lit hidden

column.name: text
column.value: If you mistreat my daughters, or if you take wives besides my daughters, although no one is with us, see, God is witness between ①you and me.” ▷ ①Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: Laban also said to Jacob, “Behold this heap and behold the memorial stone which I have set between ①you and me. ▷ ①Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: This heap is a witness, and the memorial stone is a witness, that I will not pass by this heap to you for harm, and you will not pass by this heap and this memorial stone to me, for harm.

column.name: text
column.value: The God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the fear of his father Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain, and called his relatives to ①the meal; and they ate ②the meal and spent the night on the mountain. ▷ ①Lit eat bread ②Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: ①Then early in the morning Laban got up, and kissed his ②grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them. Then Laban departed and returned to his place. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Rachel saw that she had not borne Jacob any children, ①she became jealous of her sister; and she said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I am going to die.” ▷ ①Lit Rachel

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “Here is my female slave Bilhah: have relations with her that she may give birth ①on my knees, so that ②by her I too may obtain a child.” ▷ ①I.e., Prob. referring to a ritual of adoption ②Lit from her I too may be built

column.name: text
column.value: So she gave him her slave Bilhah as a wife, and Jacob had relations with her.

column.name: text
column.value: Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rachel said, “God has ①vindicated me, and has indeed heard my voice and has given me a son.” Therefore she named him ②Dan. ▷ ①Lit judged ②I.e., He judged

column.name: text
column.value: And Rachel’s slave Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

column.name: text
column.value: So Rachel said, “With ①mighty wrestling I have ②wrestled with my sister, and I have indeed prevailed.” And she named him Naphtali. ▷ ①Lit wrestlings of God ②Heb niphtal, related to Naphtali

column.name: text
column.value: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she took her slave Zilpah and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: And Leah’s slave Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, “ ①How fortunate!” So she named him ②Gad. ▷ ①Lit With fortune! Some ancient versions Fortune has come ②I.e., Fortune

column.name: text
column.value: And Leah’s slave Zilpah bore Jacob a second son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, “ ①Happy am I! For women will call me happy.” So she named him ②Asher. ▷ ①Lit With my happiness! ②I.e., happy

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the days of wheat harvest Reuben went and found mandrake fruits in the field, and brought them to his mother Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

column.name: text
column.value: But she said to her, “Is it a small matter for you to take my husband? And would you take my son’s mandrakes also?” So Rachel said, “Therefore he may sleep with you tonight in return for your son’s mandrakes.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob came in from the field in the evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must have relations with me, for I have indeed hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night.

column.name: text
column.value: God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, “God has given me my ①reward, because I gave my slave to my husband.” So she named him Issachar. ▷ ①Heb sachar, related to Issachar

column.name: text
column.value: And Leah conceived again and bore a sixth son to Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Leah said, “God has endowed me with a good gift; finally my husband ①will acknowledge me as his wife, because I have borne him six sons.” So she named him Zebulun. ▷ ①Heb zabal, related to Zebulun

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward she gave birth to a daughter, and named her Dinah.

column.name: text
