column.value: Then God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: So she conceived and gave birth to a son, and said, “God has taken away my disgrace.”

column.name: text
column.value: And she named him Joseph, saying, “May the LORD ①give me another son.” ▷ ①Lit add to me; Heb Joseph

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when Rachel had given birth to Joseph, that Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, so that I may go to my own place and to my own country.

column.name: text
column.value: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you yourself know my service which I have ①rendered you.” ▷ ①Lit served

column.name: text
column.value: But Laban said to him, “If ①it pleases you at all, stay with me; I have determined by divination that the LORD has blessed me on your account.” ▷ ①Lit I have found favor in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: He ①continued, “Name me your wages, and I will give them.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob said to him, “You yourself know how I have served you and how your livestock have ①fared with me. ▷ ①Lit been

column.name: text
column.value: For you had little before ①I came, and it has ②increased to a multitude, and the LORD has blessed you ③wherever I turned. But now, when shall I provide for my own household also?” ▷ ①Lit me ②Lit broken forth ③Lit at my foot

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “What shall I give you?” And Jacob said, “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this one thing for me, I will again pasture and keep your flock:

column.name: text
column.value: let me pass through your entire flock today, removing from there every speckled or spotted sheep and every black sheep among the lambs, and the spotted or speckled among the goats; and those shall be my wages.

column.name: text
column.value: So my ①honesty will answer for me later, when you come concerning my ②wages. Every one that is not speckled or spotted among the goats, or black among the lambs, if found with me, will be considered stolen.” ▷ ①Lit righteousness ②Lit wages which are before you

column.name: text
column.value: Laban said, “ ①Good, let it be according to your word.” ▷ ①Lit Behold, would that it might be

column.name: text
column.value: So he removed on that day the striped or spotted male goats, and all the speckled or spotted female goats, every one with white on it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and put them in the ①care of his sons. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: And he put a distance of three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob ①took fresh rods of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled white stripes in them, exposing the white that was ②in the rods. ▷ ①Lit took to himself ②Lit on

column.name: text
column.value: He set the rods which he had peeled in front of the flocks in the drinking troughs, that is, in the watering channels where the flocks came to drink; and they mated when they came to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: So the flocks mated by the rods, and the flocks delivered striped, speckled, and spotted offspring.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob separated the lambs, and ①made the flocks face toward the striped and all the black in the flock of Laban; and he put his own herds apart, and did not put them with Laban’s flock. ▷ ①Lit set the faces

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, whenever the stronger of the flock were mating, Jacob would place the rods in the sight of the flock in the drinking troughs, so that they would mate by the rods;

column.name: text
column.value: but when the flock was sickly, he did not put them in; so the sickly were Laban’s, and the stronger were Jacob’s.

column.name: text
column.value: So the man ①became exceedingly prosperous, and had large flocks, and female and male servants, and camels and donkeys. ▷ ①Lit broke forth

column.name: text
column.value: Then God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel and live there, and make an altar there to God, who appeared to you when you fled ①from your brother Esau.” ▷ ①Lit from the face of

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him, “Remove the foreign gods which are among you, and purify yourselves and change your garments;

column.name: text
column.value: and let’s arise and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to God, who answered me on the day of my distress and has been with me ①wherever I have gone.” ▷ ①Lit in the way which

column.name: text
column.value: So they gave Jacob all the foreign gods which ①they had and the rings which were in their ears, and Jacob hid them under the ②oak which was near Shechem. ▷ ①Lit were in their hand ②Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: As they journeyed, there was ①a great terror upon the cities which were around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Jacob. ▷ ①Or a terror of God

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he built an altar there, and called the place ①El-bethel, because there God had revealed Himself to him when he fled ②from his brother. ▷ ①I.e., the God of Bethel ②Lit from the face of

column.name: text
column.value: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and it was named ①Allon-bacuth. ▷ ①I.e., oak of weeping

column.name: text
column.value: Then God appeared to Jacob again when he came from Paddan-aram, and He blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob; ①You shall no longer be called Jacob, But Israel shall be your name.” So He called ②him Israel. ▷ ①Lit Your name ②Lit his name

column.name: text
text
column.value: And the land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you, And I will give the land to your ①descendants after you.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then God went up from him at the place where He had spoken with him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob set up a memorial stone in the place where He had spoken with him, a memorial of stone, and he poured out a drink offering on it; he also poured oil on it.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him, ①Bethel. ▷ ①I.e., house of God

column.name: text
column.value: Then they journeyed on from Bethel; but when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth and she suffered severe difficulties in her labor.

column.name: text
column.value: And when she was suffering severe difficulties in her labor, the midwife said to her, “Do not fear, for you have another son!”

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, as her soul was departing (for she died), that she named him ①Ben-oni; but his father called him ②Benjamin. ▷ ①I.e., the son of my sorrow ②I.e., the son of the right hand

column.name: text
column.value: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob set up a memorial stone over her grave; that is the memorial stone of Rachel’s grave to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel journeyed on and pitched his tent beyond the ①tower of ②Eder. ▷ ①Heb Migdal-eder ②Or flock

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, while Israel was living in that land, that Reuben went and slept with his father’s concubine Bilhah, and Israel heard about it. Now there were twelve sons of Jacob—

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of Leah were Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn, then Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun;

column.name: text
column.value: the sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin;

column.name: text
column.value: and the sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s female slave, were Dan and Naphtali;

column.name: text
column.value: and the sons of Zilpah, Leah’s female slave, were Gad and Asher. These were the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob came to his father Isaac at Mamre of Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had resided.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the days of Isaac were 180 years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaac breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, an old man ①of ripe age; and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him. ▷ ①Lit and satisfied with days

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the records of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

column.name: text
column.value: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the ①granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite; ▷ ①Lit daughter; LXX son (referring to Anah)

column.name: text
column.value: also Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, the sister of Nebaioth.

column.name: text
column.value: Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath gave birth to Reuel,

column.name: text
column.value: and Oholibamah gave birth to Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all ①his household, and his livestock and all his cattle, and all his property which he had acquired in the land of Canaan, and went to another land away from his brother Jacob. ▷ ①Lit the souls of his house

column.name: text
column.value: For their possessions had become too great for them to live together, and the land where they resided could not support them because of their livestock.

column.name: text
column.value: So Esau lived in the hill country of Seir; Esau is Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: These then are the records of the generations of Esau the father of ①the Edomites in the hill country of Seir. ▷ ①Lit Edom

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz the son of Esau’s wife Adah, and Reuel the son of Esau’s wife Basemath.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, ①Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 1:36, Zephi

column.name: text
column.value: Timna was a concubine of Esau’s son Eliphaz, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Esau’s wife Adah.

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Esau’s wife Basemath.

column.name: text
column.value: And these were the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the ①granddaughter of Zibeon: ②she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. ▷ ①See note v 2 ②Lit and she

column.name: text
column.value: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, the firstborn of Esau, are chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

column.name: text
column.value: chief Korah, chief Gatam, and chief Amalek. These are the chiefs ①descended from Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah. ▷ ①Lit of Eliphaz

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, and chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs ①descended from Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Esau’s wife Basemath. ▷ ①Lit of Reuel

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of Esau’s wife Oholibamah: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, and chief Korah. These are the chiefs ①descended from Esau’s wife Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah. ▷ ①Lit of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

column.name: text
column.value: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs ①descended from the Horites, the sons of Seir in the land of Edom. ▷ ①Lit of the Horites

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Lotan were Hori and ①Hemam; and Lotan’s sister was Timna. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 1:39, Homam

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of Shobal: ①Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, ②Shepho, and Onam. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 1:40, Alian ②In 1 Chr 1:40, Shephi

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah—he is the Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness when he was pasturing the donkeys of his father Zibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

column.name: text
column.value: And these are the sons of ①Dishon: ②Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. ▷ ①Heb Dishan ②In 1 Chr 1:41, Hamran

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and ①Akan. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 1:42, Jaakan

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the chiefs ①descended from the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah, ▷ ①Lit of the Horites

column.name: text
column.value: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan. These are the chiefs ①descended from the Horites, according to their various chiefs in the land of Seir. ▷ ①Lit of the Horites

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah. ▷ ①Lit And Bela

column.name: text
column.value: Then Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who ①defeated Midian in the field of Moab, became king in his place; and the name of his city was Avith. ▷ ①Or struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shaul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Baal-hanan the son of Achbor died, and ①Hadar became king in his place; and the name of his city was ②Pau; and his wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 1:50, Hadad ②In 1 Chr 1:50, Pai

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the names of the chiefs ①descended from Esau, according to their families and their localities, by their names: chief Timna, chief ②Alvah, chief Jetheth, ▷ ①Lit of Esau ②In 1 Chr 1:51, Aliah

column.name: text
column.value: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

column.name: text
column.value: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

column.name: text
column.value: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom (that is, Esau, the father of ①the Edomites), according to their settlements in the land of their possession. ▷ ①Heb Edom

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob raised his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and four hundred men with him. So he divided the children ①among Leah and Rachel, and the two slave women. ▷ ①Or to

column.name: text
column.value: He put the slave women and their children ①in front, and Leah and her children ②next, and Rachel and Joseph ③last. ▷ ①Lit first ②Lit behind ③Lit behind

column.name: text
column.value: But he himself passed on ahead of them and bowed down to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau ran to meet him and embraced him, and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept.

column.name: text
column.value: He raised his eyes and saw the women and the children, and said, “ ①Who are these with you?” So he said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.” ▷ ①Or What relation are these to you?

column.name: text
column.value: Then the slave women came forward ①with their children, and they bowed down. ▷ ①Lit they and

column.name: text
column.value: And Leah likewise came forward with her children, and they bowed down; and afterward Joseph came forward with Rachel, and they bowed down.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “What do you mean by all this company which I have met?” And he said, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Esau said, “I have plenty, my brother; let what you have be your own.”

column.name: text
column.value: Jacob said, “No, please, if now I have found favor in your sight, then accept my gift from my hand, ①for I see your face as one sees the face of God, and you have received me favorably. ▷ ①Lit for therefore I have seen your face like seeing God’s face

column.name: text
column.value: Please accept my ①gift which has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me and because I have ②plenty.” So he urged him, and he accepted it. ▷ ①Lit blessing ②Lit all

column.name: text
column.value: Then ①Esau said, “Let’s journey on and go, and I will go ahead of you.” ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to him, “My lord knows that the children are frail and that the flocks and herds that are nursing are ①a matter of concern to me. And if they are driven hard just one day, all the flocks will die. ▷ ①Lit upon me

column.name: text
column.value: Please let my lord pass on ahead of his servant, and I will proceed at my leisure, at the pace of the cattle that are ahead of me and at the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esau said, “Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “ ①What need is there? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.” ▷ ①Lit Why this?

column.name: text
column.value: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob journeyed to ①Succoth, and built for himself a house and made booths for his livestock; therefore the place is named Succoth. ▷ ①I.e., booths

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram, and camped before the city.

column.name: text
column.value: He bought the plot of land where he had pitched his tent from the hand of the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for a hundred ①pieces of money. ▷ ①Heb qesitah

column.name: text
column.value: Then he erected there an altar and called it ①El-Elohe-Israel. ▷ ①I.e., God, the God of Israel

column.name: text
column.value: Now as Jacob went on his way, the angels of God met him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s ①camp.” So he named that place ②Mahanaim. ▷ ①Or company ②I.e., Two Camps, or Two Companies

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob sent messengers ahead of himself to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the ①country of Edom. ▷ ①Lit field

column.name: text
column.value: He commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall say to my lord Esau: ‘Your servant Jacob says the following: “I have resided with Laban, and stayed until now;

column.name: text
column.value: and I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants; and I have sent messengers to tell my lord, so that I may find favor in your sight.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau, and furthermore he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed; and he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two companies;

column.name: text
column.value: for he said, “If Esau comes to the one company and ①attacks it, then the company which is left will escape.” ▷ ①Lit strikes

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, LORD, who said to me, ‘Return to your country and to your relatives, and I will ①make you prosper,’ ▷ ①Lit do good with you

column.name: text
column.value: ①I am unworthy of all the ②favor and of all the ③faithfulness, which You have shown to Your servant; for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two companies. ▷ ①Lit I am less than all ②I.e., generosity ③Or truth

column.name: text
column.value: Save me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, that he will come and ①attack me and the mothers with the children. ▷ ①Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: For You said, ‘I will assuredly ①make you prosper and make your ②descendants as the sand of the sea, which is too great to be counted.’ ” ▷ ①Lit do good with you ②Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: So he spent the night there. Then he ①selected from what ②he had with him a gift for his brother Esau: ▷ ①Lit took ②Lit had come to his hand

column.name: text
column.value: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

column.name: text
column.value: thirty milking camels and their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, and twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he placed them in the ①care of his servants, every flock by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass on ahead of me, and put a space between flocks.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: And he commanded the ①one in front, saying, “When my brother Esau meets you and asks you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going, and to whom do these animals in front of you belong?’ ▷ ①Lit first

column.name: text
column.value: then you shall say, ‘These belong to your servant Jacob; it is a gift sent to my lord Esau. And behold, he also is behind us.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he commanded also the second and the third, and all those who followed the flocks, saying, “In this way you shall speak to Esau when you find him;

column.name: text
column.value: and you shall say, ‘Behold, your servant Jacob also is behind us.’ ” For he said, “I will appease him with the gift that goes ahead of me. Then afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the gift passed on ahead of him, while he himself spent that night in the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: Now he got up that same night and took his two wives, his two female slaves, and his eleven children, and crossed the shallow place of the Jabbok.

column.name: text
column.value: He took them and sent them across the stream. And he sent across whatever he had.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

column.name: text
column.value: When the man saw that he had not prevailed against him, he touched the socket of ①Jacob’s hip; and the socket of Jacob’s hip was dislocated while he wrestled with him. ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Let me go, for the dawn is breaking.” But he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be Jacob, but ①Israel; for you have contended with God and with men, and have prevailed.” ▷ ①I.e., he who contends with God; or God contends

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob asked him and said, “Please tell me your name.” But he said, “Why is it that you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob named the place ①Peniel, for he said, “I have seen God face to face, yet my ②life has been ③spared.” ▷ ①I.e., the face of God ②Lit soul ③Lit saved

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sun rose upon him just as he crossed over Penuel, and he was limping on his hip.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, to this day the sons of Israel do not eat the tendon of the hip which is on the socket of the hip, because he touched the socket of Jacob’s hip in the tendon of the hip.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob lived in the land where his father had lived as a stranger, in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the records of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, when he was seventeen years of age, was pasturing the flock with his brothers, while he was still a youth, along with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives. And Joseph brought back a bad report about them to their father.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his other sons, because he was the son of his old age; and he made him a ①multicolored tunic. ▷ ①Or full-length tunic

column.name: text
column.value: And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers; and so they hated him and could not speak to him ①on friendly terms. ▷ ①Lit in peace

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph ①had a dream, and when he told it to his brothers, they hated him even more. ▷ ①Lit dreamed

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, “Please listen to this dream which I have ①had; ▷ ①Lit dreamed

column.name: text
column.value: for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf stood up and also remained standing; and behold, your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then his brothers said to him, “Are you actually going to reign over us? Or are you really going to rule over us?” So they hated him even more for his dreams and for his words.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ①had yet another dream, and informed his brothers of it, and said, “Behold, I have ②had yet another dream; and behold, the sun and the moon, and eleven stars were bowing down to me.” ▷ ①Lit dreamed ②Lit dreamed

column.name: text
column.value: He also told it to his father as well as to his brothers; and his father rebuked him and said to him, “What is this dream that you have ①had? Am I and your mother and your brothers actually going to come to bow down to the ground before you?” ▷ ①Lit dreamed

column.name: text
column.value: And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the matter in mind.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his brothers went to pasture their father’s flock in Shechem.

column.name: text
column.value: And Israel said to Joseph, “Are your brothers not pasturing the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “ ①I will go.” ▷ ①Lit Behold me

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to him, “Go now and see about the welfare of your brothers and the welfare of the flock, and bring word back to me.” So he sent him from the Valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

column.name: text
column.value: A man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field; and the man asked him, “ ①What are you looking for?” ▷ ①Lit saying, “What...?”

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “I am looking for my brothers; please tell me where they are pasturing the flock.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man said, “They have moved from here; for I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’ ” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

column.name: text
column.value: ①When they saw him from a distance, and before he came closer to them, they plotted against him to put him to death. ▷ ①Or And

column.name: text
column.value: They said to one another, “ ①Here comes this dreamer! ▷ ①Lit Behold, this master of dreams comes

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, come and let’s kill him, and throw him into one of the pits; and we will say, ‘A vicious animal devoured him.’ Then we will see what will become of his dreams!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Reuben heard this and rescued him out of their hands ①by saying, “Let’s not ②take his life.” ▷ ①Lit and said ②Lit strike his soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him”—so that later he might rescue him out of their hands, to return him to his father.

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about, when Joseph ①reached his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the ②multicolored tunic that was on him; ▷ ①Lit came to ②Or full-length tunic

column.name: text
column.value: and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, without any water in it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sat down to eat ①a meal. But as they raised their eyes and looked, behold, a caravan of Ishmaelites was coming from Gilead, with their camels carrying labdanum resin, balsam, and ②myrrh, ③on their way to bring them down to Egypt. ▷ ①Lit bread ②Or resinous bark ③Lit going

column.name: text
column.value: And Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it for us to kill our brother and cover up his blood?

column.name: text
column.value: Come, and let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites and not lay our hands on him, for he is our brother, our own flesh.” And his brothers listened to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then some Midianite traders passed by, so they pulled him out and lifted Joseph out of the pit, and sold ①him to the Ishmaelites for ②twenty shekels of silver. So they brought Joseph into Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Joseph ②About 10 oz. or 280 gm

column.name: text
column.value: Now Reuben returned to the pit, and behold, Joseph was not in the pit; so he tore his garments.

column.name: text
column.value: He returned to his brothers and said, “The boy is not there; as for me, where am I to go?”

column.name: text
column.value: So they took Joseph’s tunic, and slaughtered a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood;

column.name: text
column.value: and they sent the ①multicolored tunic and brought it to their father and said, “We found this; please ②examine it to see whether it is your son’s tunic or not.” ▷ ①Or full-length tunic ②Or recognize

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ①examined it and said, “It is my son’s tunic. A vicious animal has devoured him; Joseph has surely been torn to pieces!” ▷ ①Or recognized

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob tore his clothes, and put on a sackcloth undergarment over his waist, and mourned for his son many days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all his sons and all his daughters got up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. And he said, “Surely I will go down to Sheol in mourning for my son.” So his father wept for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the ①Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s officer, the captain of the bodyguard. ▷ ①Lit Medanites

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about at that time, that Judah ①departed from his brothers and ②visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah. ▷ ①Lit went down ②Lit turned aside to

column.name: text
column.value: Judah saw there a daughter of a certain Canaanite whose name was Shua; and he took her as a wife and had relations with her.

column.name: text
column.value: And she conceived and gave birth to a son, and he named him Er.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she conceived again and gave birth to a son, and she named him Onan.

column.name: text
column.value: She gave birth to yet another son and named him Shelah; and it was at Chezib ①that she gave birth to him. ▷ ①Lit when

column.name: text
column.value: Now Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

column.name: text
column.value: But Er, Judah’s firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD took his life.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Judah said to Onan, “Have relations with your brother’s wife and perform your duty as a brother-in-law to her, and raise up a ①child for your brother.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Now Onan knew that the ①child would not be his; so when he had relations with his brother’s wife, he ②wasted his seed on the ground so that he would not give ③a child to his brother. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit spilled on the ground ③Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: But what he did was displeasing in the sight of the LORD; so He took his life also.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Judah said to his daughter-in-law Tamar, “Remain a widow in your father’s house until my son Shelah grows up”; for he ①thought, “I am afraid that he too may die like his brothers.” So Tamar went and lived in her father’s house. ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Now ①after a considerable time Shua’s daughter, the wife of Judah, died; and when ②the time of mourning was ended, Judah went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite. ▷ ①Lit the days became many and ②Lit Judah was comforted, he

column.name: text
column.value: And Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she ①removed her widow’s garments and covered herself with a ②veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gateway of ③Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife. ▷ ①Lit removed from herself ②Or shawl ③In Josh 15:34, Enam

column.name: text
column.value: When Judah saw her, he assumed she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

column.name: text
column.value: So he turned aside to her by the road, and said, “ ①Here now, let me have relations with you”; for he did not know that she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me, that you may have relations with me?” ▷ ①Or Come, now

column.name: text
column.value: He said, therefore, “I will send you a ①young goat from the flock.” She then said, “Will you give a pledge until you send it?” ▷ ①Lit kid of goats

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “What pledge shall I give you?” And she said, “Your seal and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” So he gave them to her and had relations with her, and she conceived by him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she got up and departed, and ①removed her ②veil and put on her widow’s garments. ▷ ①Lit removed from herself ②Or shawl

column.name: text
column.value: When Judah sent the ①young goat by his friend the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand, he did not find her. ▷ ①Lit kid of goats by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: He asked the people of her place, saying, “Where is the temple prostitute who was by the road at Enaim?” But they said, “There has been no temple prostitute here.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he returned to Judah, and said, “I did not find her; and furthermore, the people of the place said, ‘There has been no temple prostitute here.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Judah said, “Let her ①keep them, otherwise we will become a laughingstock. ②After all, I sent this young goat, but you did not find her.” ▷ ①Lit take for herself ②Lit Behold

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was about three months later that Judah was ①informed, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has prostituted herself, and behold, she is also pregnant by prostitution.” Then Judah said, “Bring her out and have her burned!” ▷ ①Lit informed, saying

column.name: text
column.value: It was while she was being brought out that she sent word to her father-in-law, saying, “I am pregnant by the man to whom these things belong.” She also said, “Please examine and see, whose signet ring and cords and staff are these?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Judah recognized them, and said, “She is more righteous than I, since I did not give her to my son Shelah.” And he did not ①have relations with her again. ▷ ①Lit know her yet again

column.name: text
column.value: It came about at the time she was giving birth, that behold, there were twins in her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, it took place while she was giving birth, that one baby put out a hand, and the midwife took and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying, “This one came out first.”

column.name: text
column.value: But it came about as he drew back his hand that behold, his brother came out. Then she said, “What a breach you have made for yourself!” So he was named ①Perez. ▷ ①I.e., a breach

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward his brother came out who had the scarlet thread on his hand; and he was named ①Zerah. ▷ ①I.e., a dawning or brightness

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the bodyguard, bought him ①from the Ishmaelites, who had taken him down there. ▷ ①Lit from the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD was with Joseph, so he became a ①successful man. And he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian. ▷ ①Or prosperous

column.name: text
column.value: Now his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made all that he did prosper in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph found favor in his sight and ①became his personal servant; and he made him overseer over his house, and ②put him in charge of all that he owned. ▷ ①Or ministered to him ②Lit handed over to him

column.name: text
column.value: It came about that from the time he made him overseer in his house and over all that he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house on account of Joseph; so the LORD’S blessing was upon all that he owned, in the house and in the field.

column.name: text
column.value: So he left ①Joseph in charge of everything that he owned; and with him there he did not ②concern himself with anything except the ③food which he ④ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance. ▷ ①Lit in Joseph’s hand ②Lit know ③Lit bread ④Or used to eat

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about after these events that his master’s wife ①had her eyes on Joseph, and she said, “Sleep with me.” ▷ ①Lit lifted up her eyes at

column.name: text
column.value: But he refused and said to his master’s wife, “Look, with me here, my master ①does not concern himself with anything in the house, and he has ②put me in charge of all that he owns. ▷ ①Lit does not know what is in the house ②Lit handed over to me

column.name: text
column.value: ①There is no one greater in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do this great evil, and sin against God?” ▷ ①Or He is not greater

column.name: text
column.value: Though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her to lie beside her or be with her.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened ①one day that he went into the house to do his work, and none of the people of the household was there inside. ▷ ①Lit about this day

column.name: text
column.value: So she grabbed him by his garment, saying, “Sleep with me!” But he left his garment in her hand and fled, and went outside.

column.name: text
column.value: ①When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside, ▷ ①Lit And it came about when

column.name: text
column.value: she called to the men of her household and said to them, “See, he has brought in a ①Hebrew to us to make fun of us; he came in to me to sleep with me, and I ②screamed. ▷ ①Lit Hebrew man ②Lit called with a great voice

column.name: text
column.value: When he heard that I raised my voice and ①screamed, he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside.” ▷ ①Lit called out

column.name: text
column.value: So she ①left his garment beside her until his master came home. ▷ ①Lit let...lie beside

column.name: text
column.value: Then she spoke to him ①with these ②words: “The Hebrew slave, whom you brought to us, came in to me to make fun of me; ▷ ①Lit according to ②Lit words, saying

column.name: text
column.value: but when I raised my voice and ①screamed, he left his garment beside me and fled outside.” ▷ ①Lit called out

column.name: text
column.value: Now when his master heard the words of his wife which she spoke to him, saying, “ ①This is what your slave did to me,” his anger burned. ▷ ①Lit According to these things your slave

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined; and he was there in the prison.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the warden of the prison.

column.name: text
column.value: And the warden of the prison ①put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the prison; so that whatever was done there, he was ②responsible for it. ▷ ①Lit handed over to Joseph all ②Lit the doer

column.name: text
column.value: The warden of the prison did not supervise anything ①under Joseph’s authority, because the LORD was with him; and, the LORD made whatever he did prosper. ▷ ①Lit in his hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about after these things, that the cupbearer and the baker for the king of Egypt offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: And Pharaoh was furious with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker.

column.name: text
column.value: So he put them in confinement in the house of the captain of the bodyguard, in the prison, the same place where Joseph was imprisoned.

column.name: text
column.value: And the captain of the bodyguard put Joseph in charge of them, and he ①took care of them; and they were in confinement for ②some time. ▷ ①Lit ministered to ②Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: Then the cupbearer and the baker for the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison, both had a dream the same night, each man with his own dream and each dream with its own interpretation.

column.name: text
column.value: ①When Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them, ②behold, they were dejected. ▷ ①Or And ②Lit and behold

column.name: text
column.value: So he asked Pharaoh’s officials who were with him in confinement in his master’s house, “ ①Why are your faces so sad today?” ▷ ①Lit saying, Why

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “We have ①had a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.” Then Joseph said to them, “Do interpretations not belong to God? Tell it to me, please.” ▷ ①Lit dreamed

column.name: text
column.value: So the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph, ①saying to him, “In my dream, ②behold, there was a vine in front of me; ▷ ①Lit and said ②Lit and behold

column.name: text
column.value: and on the vine were three branches. And as it was budding, its blossoms came out, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; so I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I put the cup into Pharaoh’s ①hand.” ▷ ①Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph said to him, “This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days;

column.name: text
column.value: within three more days Pharaoh will ①lift up your head and restore you to your office; and you will put Pharaoh’s cup into his hand as in your former practice when you were his cupbearer. ▷ ①I.e., a royal gesture of forgiveness

column.name: text
column.value: Only ①keep me in mind when it goes well for you, and please do me a kindness ②by mentioning me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this ③prison. ▷ ①Lit remember me with yourself ②Lit and mention ③Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: For I was in fact kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and even here I have done nothing that they should have put me into the ①dungeon.” ▷ ①Or pit

column.name: text
column.value: When the chief baker saw that he had interpreted favorably, he said to Joseph, “I also saw in my dream, and behold, there were three baskets of white bread on my head;

column.name: text
column.value: and in the top basket there were some of all ①kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds were eating them out of the basket on my head.” ▷ ①Lit food for Pharaoh made by a baker

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph answered and said, “This is its interpretation: the three baskets are three days;

column.name: text
column.value: within three more days Pharaoh will lift up your head from you and will hang you on a wooden post, and the birds will eat your flesh off you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about on the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, that he held a feast for all his servants; and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

column.name: text
column.value: He restored the chief cupbearer to his ①office, and he put the cup into Pharaoh’s ②hand; ▷ ①Lit wine-pouring ②Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: but he hanged the chief baker, just as Joseph had interpreted to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph, but forgot him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why are you staring at one another?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Look, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt; go down there and buy some for us from ①that place, so that we may live and not die.” ▷ ①Lit there

column.name: text
column.value: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers, for he said, “I am afraid that harm may happen to him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel came to buy grain among those who were coming, because the famine was also in the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph was the ruler over the land; he was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph’s brothers came and bowed down to him with their faces to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joseph saw his brothers, he recognized them, but he disguised himself to them and spoke to them harshly. He said to them, “Where have you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Joseph had recognized his brothers, although they did not recognize him.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he ①had about them, and he said to them, “You are spies; you have come to look at the ②undefended parts of our land.” ▷ ①Lit had dreamed ②Lit nakedness of the land

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

column.name: text
column.value: We are all sons of one man; we are honest men, your servants are not spies.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet he said to them, “No, but you have come to look at the ①undefended parts of our land!” ▷ ①Lit nakedness of the land

column.name: text
column.value: But they said, “Your servants are twelve brothers in all, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is with our father today, and one is no longer alive.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Joseph said to them, “It is as I said ①to you, you are spies; ▷ ①Lit to you, saying

column.name: text
column.value: by this you will be tested: by the life of Pharaoh, you shall not leave this place unless your youngest brother comes here!

column.name: text
column.value: Send one of you and have him get your brother, while you remain confined, so that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you. But if not, by the life of Pharaoh, you are certainly spies!”

column.name: text
column.value: So he put them all together in prison for three days.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph said to them on the third day, “Do this and live, for I fear God:

column.name: text
column.value: if you are honest men, let one of your brothers be confined in ①your prison; but as for the rest of you, go, carry grain for the famine of your households, ▷ ①Lit the house of your prison

column.name: text
column.value: and bring your youngest brother to me, so that your words may be verified, and you will not die.” And they did so.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to one another, “Truly we are guilty concerning our brother, because we saw the distress of his soul when he pleaded with us, yet we would not listen; for that reason this distress has happened to us.”

column.name: text
column.value: Reuben answered them, saying, “Did I not tell ①you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’; and you would not listen? ②Now justice for his blood is required.” ▷ ①Lit you, saying, ②Lit And behold, his blood also is required

column.name: text
column.value: They did not know, however, that Joseph understood, for there was an interpreter between them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he turned away from them and wept. But when he returned to them and spoke to them, he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, but also to return every man’s money in his sack, and to give them provisions for the journey. And that is what was done for them.

column.name: text
column.value: So they loaded their donkeys with their grain and departed from there.

column.name: text
column.value: But when one of them opened his sack to give his donkey feed at the overnight campsite, he saw his money; and behold, it was in the opening of his sack!

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to his brothers, “My money has been returned, and look, it is right in my sack!” Then their hearts ①sank, and they turned ②trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?” ▷ ①Lit went out ②Lit trembled

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to their father Jacob in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly with us, and took us for spies of the country.

column.name: text
column.value: But we said to him, ‘We are honest men; we are not spies.

column.name: text
column.value: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no longer alive, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.’

column.name: text
column.value: But the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me and take grain for the famine of your households, and go.

column.name: text
column.value: But bring your youngest brother to me so that I may know that you are not spies, but ①honest men. I will give your brother to you, and you may trade in the land.’ ” ▷ ①Lit you are honest

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, as they were emptying their sacks, that behold, every man’s bag of money was in his sack; and when they and their father saw their bags of money, they were afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: And their father Jacob said to them, “You have deprived me of my sons: Joseph is gone, and Simeon is gone, and now you would take Benjamin; all these things are against me.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you; put him in my ①care, and I will return him to you.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: But ①Jacob said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm should happen to him on the journey ②you are taking, then you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.” ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit on which you are going

column.name: text
column.value: Now the famine was severe in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about, when they had finished eating the grain which they had brought from Egypt, that their father said to them, “Go back, buy us a little food.”

column.name: text
column.value: Judah spoke to him, however, saying, “The man sternly warned ①us, ‘You shall not see my face unless your brother is with you.’ ▷ ①Lit us, saying

column.name: text
column.value: If you send our brother with us, we will go down and buy you food.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you do not send him, we will not go down; for the man said to us, ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, ①by telling the man whether you still had another brother?” ▷ ①Lit to tell

column.name: text
column.value: But they said, “The man specifically asked about us and our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ So we ①answered his questions. Could we possibly know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?” ▷ ①Lit told him according to these words

column.name: text
column.value: So Judah said to his father Israel, “Send the boy with me and we will arise and go, so that we may live and not die, we as well as you and our little ones.

column.name: text
column.value: I myself will take responsibility for him! You may demand him back from ①me. If I do not bring him back to you and present him to you, then ②you can let me take the blame forever. ▷ ①Lit my hand ②Lit I will be culpable before you all the days

column.name: text
column.value: For if we had not delayed, surely by now we could have returned twice.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then their father Israel said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best products of the land in your ①bags, and carry down to the man as a gift, a little balsam and a little honey, labdanum resin and ②myrrh, pistachio nuts and almonds. ▷ ①Or vessels ②Or resinous bark

column.name: text
column.value: And take double the money in your hand, and take back in your hand the money that was returned in the opening of your sacks; perhaps it was a mistake.

column.name: text
column.value: Take your brother also, and arise, return to the man;

column.name: text
column.value: and may ①God Almighty grant you compassion in the sight of the man, so that he will release to you your other brother and Benjamin. And as for me, if I am bereaved of my sons, I am bereaved!” ▷ ①Heb El Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: So the men took this gift, and they took double the money in their hand, and Benjamin; then they set out and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to his house steward, “Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal and make preparations; for the men are to dine with me at noon.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the man did as Joseph said, and ①brought the men to Joseph’s house. ▷ ①Lit the man brought

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “It is because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time that we are being brought in, so that he may ①attack us and ②overpower us, and take us as slaves with our donkeys.” ▷ ①Lit roll himself upon us ②Lit fall upon

column.name: text
column.value: So they approached Joseph’s house steward, and spoke to him at the entrance of the house,

column.name: text
column.value: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food,

column.name: text
column.value: and it happened when we came to the campsite, that we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the opening of his sack, our money in ①full. So we have brought it back in our hand. ▷ ①Lit its weight

column.name: text
column.value: We have also brought down other money in our hand to buy food; we do not know who put our money in our sacks.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Peace be to you, do not be afraid. Your God and the God of your father has given you treasure in your sacks; your ①money was in my possession.” Then he brought Simeon out to them. ▷ ①Lit your money had come to me

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man brought the men into Joseph’s house and gave them water, and they washed their feet; and he gave their donkeys feed.

column.name: text
column.value: So they prepared the gift ①for Joseph’s arrival at noon; for they had heard that they were to eat ②a meal there. ▷ ①Lit until ②Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: When Joseph came home, they brought into the house to him the gift which was in their hand, and they bowed down to the ground before him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he asked them about their welfare, and said, “Is your old father well, of whom you spoke? Is he still alive?”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “Your servant our father is well; he is still alive.” Then they bowed down again ①in homage. ▷ ①I.e., great respect and honor to a superior

column.name: text
column.value: And as he raised his eyes and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother’s son, he said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” Then he said, “May God be gracious to you, my son.”

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph then hurried out, for ①he was deeply stirred over his brother, and he looked for a place to weep; so he entered his chamber and wept there. ▷ ①Lit his compassion grew warm

column.name: text
column.value: Then he washed his face and came out; and he controlled himself and said, “ ①Serve the meal.” ▷ ①Lit Set on bread

column.name: text
column.value: Then they served him by himself, and ①Joseph’s brothers by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves; because the Egyptians could not eat bread with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians. ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: Now they ①were seated before him, from the firstborn according to his birthright to the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at one another in astonishment. ▷ ①Lit sat

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took portions to them from ①his own table, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. So they drank freely with him. ▷ ①Lit his face

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers and their flocks and their herds and all that they have, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he took five men from among his brothers and presented them to Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What is your occupation?” So they said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers.”

column.name: text
column.value: They also said to Pharaoh, “We have come to reside in the land, for there is no pasture for your servants’ flocks, for the famine is severe in the land of Canaan. Now, therefore, please let your servants live in the land of Goshen.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said to ①Joseph, “Your father and your brothers have come to you. ▷ ①Lit Joseph, saying

column.name: text
column.value: The land of Egypt is ①at your disposal; settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land, let them live in the land of Goshen; and if you know any capable men among them, then ②put them in charge of my livestock.” ▷ ①Lit before you ②Lit appoint them rulers

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and ①presented him to Pharaoh; and Jacob blessed Pharaoh. ▷ ①Lit set him before

column.name: text
column.value: And Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many ①years have you lived?” ▷ ①Lit are the days of the years of your life

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The ①years of my living abroad are ②130; few and ③unpleasant have been the ④years of my life, nor have they ⑤attained the ⑥years ⑦that my fathers lived during the days of their living abroad.” ▷ ①Lit days of the years ②Lit 130 years ③Lit evil ④Lit days of the years ⑤Lit reached ⑥Lit days of the years ⑦Lit of the life of my fathers

column.name: text
column.value: So Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from ①his presence. ▷ ①Lit Pharaoh’s

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them property in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had ordered.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph also provided his father and his brothers and all his father’s household with ①food, according to the ②number of their little ones. ▷ ①Or bread ②Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was no ①food in all the land, because the famine was very severe, so that the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan languished because of the famine. ▷ ①Or bread

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph collected all the money that was found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan in payment for the grain which they bought, and Joseph brought the money into Pharaoh’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: When the money was all spent in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, all the Egyptians came to Joseph saying, “Give us ①food, for why should we die in your presence? For our money is ②gone.” ▷ ①Or bread ②Lit at an end

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph said, “Give up your livestock, and I will give you food for your livestock, since your money is ①gone.” ▷ ①Lit at an end

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them ①food in exchange for the horses and the ②flocks and the herds and the donkeys; and he ③fed them with ④food in exchange for all their livestock ⑤that year. ▷ ①Or bread ②Lit livestock of the flocks and livestock of the herds ③Lit led them as a shepherd ④Or bread ⑤Lit in that year

column.name: text
column.value: But when that year ended, they came to him the ①next year and said to him, “We will not hide from my lord the fact that our money is all spent, and the ②livestock are my lord’s. There is nothing left ③for my lord except our bodies and our lands. ▷ ①Lit second ②Lit livestock of the cattle ③Lit in the presence of

column.name: text
column.value: Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for ①food, and we and our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. So give us seed, so that we may live and not die, and that the land may not be desolate.” ▷ ①Or bread

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, for ①every Egyptian sold his field, because the famine was severe upon them. So the land became Pharaoh’s. ▷ ①Lit Egypt, every man

column.name: text
column.value: As for the people, he relocated them to the cities from one end of Egypt’s border to the other.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the land of the priests he did not buy, because the priests had an allotment from Pharaoh, and they ①lived off the allotment which Pharaoh gave them. Therefore, they did not sell their land. ▷ ①Lit ate their allotment

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph said to the people, “Behold, today I have purchased you and your land for Pharaoh; now, here is seed for you, and you may sow the land.

column.name: text
column.value: ①At the harvest you shall give a fifth to Pharaoh, and ②four-fifths shall be your own for seed of the field and for your food, and for those of your households and as food for your little ones.” ▷ ①Lit It shall come about...that you shall ②Lit four parts

column.name: text
column.value: So they said, “You have saved our lives! Let us find favor in the sight of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh’s slaves.”

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph made it a statute concerning the land of Egypt, valid to this day, that Pharaoh was to have the fifth; only the land of the priests ①did not become Pharaoh’s. ▷ ①Lit alone did

column.name: text
column.value: Now Israel lived in the land of Egypt, in ①Goshen, and they acquired property in it and were fruitful and became very numerous. ▷ ①Lit the land of Goshen

column.name: text
column.value: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt for seventeen years; so the ①length of Jacob’s life was 147 years. ▷ ①Lit days of Jacob, the years of his life

column.name: text
column.value: When ①the time for Israel to die drew near, he called his son Joseph and said to him, “Please, if I have found favor in your sight, place your hand under my thigh now and deal with me in kindness and ②faithfulness: please do not bury me in Egypt, ▷ ①Lit the days of Israel ②Lit truth

column.name: text
column.value: but when I ①lie down with my fathers, you shall carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place.” And he said, “I will do as you have said.” ▷ ①I.e., die

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Swear to me.” So he swore to him. Then Israel bowed in worship at the head of the bed.

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel set out with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac.

column.name: text
column.value: And God spoke to Israel ①in visions of the night and said, “Jacob, Jacob.” And he said, “Here I am.” ▷ ①Lit in the visions

column.name: text
column.value: Then He said, “I am God, the God of your father; do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you into a great nation there.

column.name: text
column.value: I will go down with you to Egypt, and I will also assuredly bring you up again; and Joseph will ①close your eyes.” ▷ ①Lit put his hand on

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob left Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried their father Jacob and their little ones and their wives in the wagons which Pharaoh had sent to carry him.

column.name: text
column.value: They also took their livestock and their possessions, which they had acquired in the land of Canaan, and came to Egypt, Jacob and all his ①descendants with him: ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: his sons and his grandsons with him, his daughters and his granddaughters, and all his ①descendants he brought with him to Egypt. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, Jacob and his sons: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Simeon: ①Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, ②Jachin, ③Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanite woman. ▷ ①In Num

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Levi: ①Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 6:16, Gershom

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah (but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan). And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Issachar: Tola, ①Puvvah, ②Iob, and Shimron. ▷ ①In Num 26:23, Puvah; in 1 Chr 7:1, Puah ②In Num

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, with his daughter Dinah; ①all his sons and his daughters numbered thirty-three. ▷ ①Lit all the souls of

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Gad: ①Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, ②Ezbon, Eri, ③Arodi, and Areli. ▷ ①In Num 26:15, Zephon ②In Num 26:16, Ozni ③In Num 26:17, Arod

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Leah; and she bore to Jacob these sixteen persons.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Jacob’s wife Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: Now to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, ①Ehi, Rosh, ②Muppim, ③Huppim, and Ard. ▷ ①In Num 26:38, Ahiram ②In Num 26:39, Shephupham; in 1 Chr 7:12, Shuppim ③In Num 26:39, Hupham

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Rachel, who were born to Jacob; there were fourteen persons in all.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Dan: ①Hushim. ▷ ①In Num 26:42, Shuham

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Naphtali: ①Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and ②Shillem. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 7:13, Jahziel ②In 1 Chr 7:13, Shallum

column.name: text
column.value: These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel, and she bore these to Jacob; there were seven persons in all.

column.name: text
column.value: All the people belonging to Jacob, who came to Egypt, ①his direct descendants, not including the wives of Jacob’s sons, were sixty-six persons in all, ▷ ①Lit who came out of his loins

column.name: text
column.value: and the sons of Joseph, who were born to him in Egypt, were ①two; all the people of the house of Jacob, who came to Egypt, were seventy. ▷ ①Lit two souls

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jacob sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to ①guide him to Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen. ▷ ①Lit instruct before him

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph ①prepared his chariot and went up to Goshen to meet his father Israel; as soon as he appeared to him, Joseph threw himself on his neck and wept on his neck a long time. ▷ ①Lit harnessed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Now let me die, since I have seen your face, that you are still alive.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Joseph said to his brothers and to his father’s household, “I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and will say to him, ‘My brothers and my father’s household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me;

column.name: text
column.value: and the men are shepherds, for they have been ①keepers of livestock; and they have brought their flocks and their herds and all that they have.’ ▷ ①Lit men

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh calls for you and says, ‘What is your occupation?’

column.name: text
column.value: you shall say, ‘Your servants have been ①keepers of livestock since our youth even until now, both we and our fathers,’ so that you may live in the land of Goshen; for every shepherd is an abomination to the Egyptians.” ▷ ①Lit men

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph could not control himself in front of everyone standing before him, and he shouted, “Have everyone leave me!” So there ①was no one with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers. ▷ ①Lit stood

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ①wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard it, and the household of Pharaoh heard about it. ▷ ①Lit gave forth his voice in weeping

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?” But his brothers could not answer him, for they were terrified in his presence.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph said to his brothers, “Please come ①closer to me.” And they came ②closer. And he said, “I am your brother Joseph, whom you sold to Egypt. ▷ ①Lit near ②Lit near

column.name: text
column.value: Now do not be grieved or angry ①with yourselves because you sold me here, for God sent me ahead of you ②to save lives. ▷ ①Lit in your eyes ②Lit for preservation of life

column.name: text
column.value: For the famine has been in the land these two years, and there are still five years in which there will be neither plowing nor harvesting.

column.name: text
column.value: So God sent me ahead of you to ensure for you a remnant on the earth, and to ①keep you alive by a great deliverance. ▷ ①As in MT; another reading (cf. LXX) keep alive for you a great remnant

column.name: text
column.value: Now, therefore, it was not you who sent me here, but God; and He has made me a father to Pharaoh and lord of all his household, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Hurry and go up to my father, and say to him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: “God has made me lord of all Egypt; come down to me, do not delay.

column.name: text
column.value: For you shall live in the land of Goshen, and you shall be near me, you and your children and your ①grandchildren, and your flocks and your herds and all that you have. ▷ ①Lit children’s children

column.name: text
column.value: There I will also provide for you, for there are still five years of famine to come, and you and your household and all that you have would be impoverished.” ’

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my mouth which is speaking to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you must tell my father of all my splendor in Egypt, and all that you have seen; and you must hurry and bring my father down here.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

column.name: text
column.value: And he kissed all his brothers and wept on them, and afterward his brothers talked with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the ①news was heard in Pharaoh’s house ②that Joseph’s brothers had come, it ③pleased Pharaoh and his servants. ▷ ①Lit voice ②Lit saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come” ③Lit was good in the eyes of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your livestock and ①go to the land of Canaan, ▷ ①Lit come, go

column.name: text
column.value: and take your father and your households and come to me; and I will give you the ①best of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’ ▷ ①Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: Now you are ordered, ‘Do this: ①take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and for your wives, and bring your father and come. ▷ ①Lit take for yourselves

column.name: text
column.value: And do not ①concern yourselves with your property, for the ②best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’ ” ▷ ①Lit let your eye look with regret upon your vessels ②Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel did so; and Joseph gave them wagons according to the ①command of Pharaoh, and gave them provisions for the journey. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: To ①each of them he gave changes of garments, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of garments. ▷ ①Lit all of them he gave each man

column.name: text
column.value: And to his father he sent ①the following: ten male donkeys loaded with the ②best things of Egypt, ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread, and sustenance for his father ③on the journey. ▷ ①Lit like this ②Lit good ③Lit for

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent his brothers away, and ①as they departed, he said to them, “Do not ②quarrel on the journey.” ▷ ①Lit they departed; and he said ②Lit be agitated

column.name: text
column.value: Then they went up from Egypt, and came to the land of Canaan, to their father Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: And they told him, saying, “Joseph is still alive, and indeed he is ruler over all the land of Egypt.” But ①he was stunned, for he did not believe them. ▷ ①Lit his heart grew numb

column.name: text
column.value: When they told him all the words of Joseph that he had spoken to them, and when he saw the wagons that Joseph had sent to carry him, then the spirit of their father Jacob revived.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel said, “It is enough; my son Joseph is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after these things that ①Joseph was told, “Behold, your father is sick.” So he took his two sons Manasseh and Ephraim with him. ▷ ①Lit one said to Joseph

column.name: text
column.value: When ①it was told to Jacob, “Behold, your son Joseph has come to you,” Israel ②collected his strength and sat ③up in the bed. ▷ ①Lit one told Jacob and said ②Lit strengthened himself ③Lit upon the bed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob said to Joseph, “ ①God Almighty appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan and blessed me, ▷ ①Heb El Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: and He said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful and numerous, and I will make you a multitude of peoples, and will give this land to your ①descendants after you as an everlasting possession.’ ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt, are mine; Ephraim and Manasseh shall be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are.

column.name: text
column.value: But your children that you have fathered after them shall be yours; they shall be called by the ①names of their brothers in their inheritance. ▷ ①Lit name

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for me, when I came from Paddan, Rachel died, ①to my sorrow, in the land of Canaan on the journey, when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath. I buried her there on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).” ▷ ①Lit upon me

column.name: text
column.value: When Israel saw Joseph’s sons, he said, “Who are these?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” So he said, “Bring them to me, please, so that I may bless them.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now the eyes of Israel were so ①dim from age that he could not see. And ②Joseph brought them close to him, and he kissed them and embraced them. ▷ ①Lit dull ②Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: And Israel said to Joseph, “I never ①expected to see your face, and behold, God has let me see your ②children as well!” ▷ ①Lit assumed ②Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph ①took them from his knees, and bowed with his face to the ground. ▷ ①Lit made them come out

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph took them both, Ephraim with his right hand toward Israel’s left, and Manasseh with his left hand toward Israel’s right, and brought them close to him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Israel reached out his right hand and placed it on the head of Ephraim, who was the younger, and his left hand on Manasseh’s head, crossing his hands, although Manasseh was the firstborn.

column.name: text
column.value: And he blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, The God who has been my shepherd ①all my life to this day, ▷ ①Lit from the continuance of me

column.name: text
text
column.value: When Joseph saw that his father placed his right hand on Ephraim’s head, it displeased him; and he grasped his father’s hand to move it from Ephraim’s head to Manasseh’s head.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn. Place your right hand on his head.”

column.name: text
column.value: But his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know; he also will become a people and he also will be great. However, his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his ①descendants shall become ②a multitude of nations.” ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit the fullness

column.name: text
column.value: So he blessed them that day, saying, “By you Israel will pronounce blessing, saying, ‘May God make you like Ephraim and Manasseh!’ ” And so he put Ephraim before Manasseh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Israel said to Joseph, “Behold, I am about to die, but God will be with you, and bring you back to the land of your fathers.

column.name: text
