column.value: And I give you one ①portion more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite with my sword and my bow.” ▷ ①Or ridge; lit shoulder; Heb Shechem

column.name: text
column.value: Then he commanded his house steward, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in the opening of his sack.

column.name: text
column.value: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the opening of the sack of the youngest, and his money for the grain.” And he did ①as Joseph had told him. ▷ ①Or according to the word

column.name: text
column.value: ①As soon as it was light, the men were sent away, they with their donkeys. ▷ ①Lit The morning was light

column.name: text
column.value: They had just left the city, and were not far away, when Joseph said to his house steward, “Up, follow the men; and when you overtake them, say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good?

column.name: text
column.value: Is this not that from which my lord drinks, and which he indeed uses for divination? You have done wrong in doing this!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So ①he overtook them and spoke these words to them. ▷ ①I.e., the steward

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “Why does my lord say such words as these? Far be it from your servants to do such a thing!

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, the money which we found in the opening of our sacks we have brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then could we steal silver or gold from your lord’s house?

column.name: text
column.value: With whomever of your servants it is found, he shall die, and we also shall be my lord’s slaves.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “Now let it indeed be according to your words; he with whom it is found shall be my slave, but the rest of you shall be considered innocent.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they hurried, each man lowered his sack to the ground, and each man opened his sack.

column.name: text
column.value: And he searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest; and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they tore their clothes in grief, and when each man had loaded his donkey, they returned to the city.

column.name: text
column.value: When Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, he was still there, and they fell down to the ground before him.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph said to them, “What is this thing that you have done? Do you not know that a man who is like me can indeed practice divination?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Judah said, “What can we say to my lord? What words can we speak? And how can we justify ourselves? God has found out the guilt of your servants; behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and the one in whose ①possession the cup has been found.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Far be it from me to do this. The man in whose ①possession the cup has been found, he shall be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then Judah approached him and said, “Oh my lord, may your servant please speak a word in my lord’s ears, and ①do not be angry with your servant; for you are equal to Pharaoh. ▷ ①Lit let not your anger burn against

column.name: text
column.value: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father or a brother?’

column.name: text
column.value: And we said to my lord, ‘We have an old father and a little boy born in our father’s old age. Now his brother is dead, so he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me so that I may set my eyes on him.’

column.name: text
column.value: But we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father, for if he should leave his father, ①his father would die.’ ▷ ①Lit he would

column.name: text
column.value: You said to your servants, however, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about when we went up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

column.name: text
column.value: And our father said, ‘Go back, buy us a little food.’

column.name: text
column.value: But we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down; for we cannot see the man’s face unless our youngest brother is with us.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons;

column.name: text
column.value: and the one left me, and I said, “Surely he is torn to pieces,” and I have not seen him since.

column.name: text
column.value: If you also take this one from ①me, and harm happens to him, you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in ②sorrow.’ ▷ ①Lit my face ②Lit evil

column.name: text
column.value: So now, when I come to your servant, my father, and the boy is not with us—since ①our father’s life is so attached to the boy’s life— ▷ ①Lit his soul is bound with his soul

column.name: text
column.value: when he sees that the boy is not with us, he will die. So your servants will bring the gray hair of your servant, our father, down to Sheol in sorrow.

column.name: text
column.value: For your servant accepted responsibility for the boy from my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, then ①my father can let me take the blame forever.’ ▷ ①Lit I will be culpable for all the days before my father

column.name: text
column.value: So now, please let your servant remain as a slave to my lord instead of the boy, and let the boy go up with his brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: For how shall I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? I fear that I may see the evil that would ①overtake my father.” ▷ ①Lit find

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jacob summoned his sons and said, “Assemble yourselves, so that I may tell you what will happen to you in the ①days to come. ▷ ①Lit end of the days

column.name: text
column.value: Gather together and listen, sons of Jacob; Yes, listen to Israel your father.

column.name: text
column.value: “Reuben, you are my firstborn, My might and the beginning of my strength, Preeminent in dignity and preeminent in power.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Uncontrollable as water, you shall not have preeminence, Because you went up to your father’s bed; Then you defiled it—he went up to my couch. ▷ ①Or Gushing over

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce; And their wrath, for it is cruel. I will scatter them in Jacob, And disperse them among Israel.

column.name: text
text
column.value: Judah is a lion’s cub; From the prey, my son, you have gone up. He ①crouches, he lies down as a lion, And as a ②lion, who ③dares to stir him up? ▷ ①Lit bows down ②Lit lioness ③Lit shall

column.name: text
column.value: The scepter will not depart from Judah, Nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, ①Until Shiloh comes, And to him shall be the obedience of the peoples. ▷ ①Or Until he comes to Shiloh; or Until he comes to whom it belongs

column.name: text
column.value: He ties his foal to the vine, And his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; He washes his garments in wine, And his robes in the blood of grapes.

column.name: text
column.value: His eyes are ①dull from wine, And his teeth ②white from milk. ▷ ①Or darker than ②Or whiter than

column.name: text
column.value: “Zebulun will reside at the seashore; And he shall be ①a harbor for ships, And his flank shall be toward Sidon. ▷ ①Lit a shore of ships

column.name: text
column.value: “Issachar is a ①strong donkey, Lying down between the sheepfolds. ▷ ①Lit donkey of bone

column.name: text
column.value: When he saw that a resting place was good And that the land was pleasant, He bowed his shoulder to carry burdens, And became a slave at forced labor.

column.name: text
column.value: “Dan shall judge his people, As one of the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Dan shall be a serpent in the way, A horned viper in the path, That bites the horse’s heels, So that its rider falls backward.

column.name: text
column.value: For Your salvation I wait, LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: “As for Gad, a band of raiders shall attack him, But he will attack at their ①heels. ▷ ①Lit heel

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①As for Asher, his ②food shall be ③rich, And he will yield royal delicacies. ▷ ①Lit From ②Or bread ③Lit fat

column.name: text
column.value: “Naphtali is a doe let loose; He utters beautiful words.

column.name: text
column.value: “Joseph is a fruitful ①branch, A fruitful ②branch by a spring; Its ③branches hang over a wall. ▷ ①Lit son ②Lit son ③Lit daughters

column.name: text
column.value: The archers provoked him, And shot at him and were hostile toward him;

column.name: text
column.value: But his bow remained ①firm, And ②his arms were agile, From the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob (From there is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel), ▷ ①I.e., in an unyielding position ②Lit the arms of his hands

column.name: text
column.value: From the God of your father who helps you, And ①by the ②Almighty who blesses you With blessings of heaven above, Blessings of the deep that lies beneath, Blessings of the breasts and of the womb. ▷ ①Or with ②Heb Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: The blessings of your father Have surpassed the blessings of my ancestors Up to the ①furthest boundary of the everlasting hills; May they be on the head of Joseph, And on the top of the head of the one distinguished among his brothers. ▷ ①Lit limit; or desire

column.name: text
column.value: “Benjamin is a ①ravenous wolf; In the morning he devours the prey, And in the evening he divides the spoils.” ▷ ①Lit a wolf that tears

column.name: text
column.value: All these are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is what their father said to them ①when he blessed them. He blessed them, every one ②with the blessing appropriate to him. ▷ ①Lit and ②Lit according to his blessing

column.name: text
column.value: Then he commanded them and said to them, “I am about to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

column.name: text
column.value: in the cave that is in the field of Machpelah, which is opposite Mamre, in the land of Canaan, which Abraham bought along with the field from Ephron the Hittite as a ①burial site. ▷ ①Lit possession of a burial place

column.name: text
column.value: There they buried Abraham and his wife Sarah, there they buried Isaac and his wife Rebekah, and there I buried Leah—

column.name: text
column.value: the field and the cave that is in it, purchased from the sons of Heth.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet into the bed and breathed his last, and was gathered to his people.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened at the end of two full years that Pharaoh had a dream, and behold, he was standing by the Nile.

column.name: text
column.value: And behold, from the Nile seven cows came up, fine-looking and ①fat; and they grazed in the marsh grass. ▷ ①Lit fat of flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, seven other cows came up after them from the Nile, ugly and ①thin, and they stood by the other cows on the bank of the Nile. ▷ ①Lit thin of flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then the ugly and ①thin cows ate the seven fine-looking and fat cows. Then Pharaoh awoke. ▷ ①Lit thin of flesh

column.name: text
column.value: But he fell asleep and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven ears of grain came up on a single stalk, plump and good.

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprouted up after them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the thin ears swallowed the seven plump and full ears. Then Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the morning his spirit was troubled, so he sent messengers and called for all the soothsayer priests of Egypt, and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them his ①dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them for Pharaoh. ▷ ①Lit dream

column.name: text
column.value: Then the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I would make mention today of my own ①offenses. ▷ ①Or sins

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh was furious with his servants, and he put me in confinement in the house of the captain of the bodyguard, both me and the chief baker.

column.name: text
column.value: Then we had a dream one night, ①he and I; each of us dreamed according to the interpretation of his own dream. ▷ ①Lit I and he

column.name: text
column.value: Now a Hebrew youth was there with us, a servant of the captain of the bodyguard, and we told him the dreams, and he interpreted our dreams for us. For each man he interpreted according to his own dream.

column.name: text
column.value: And just as he interpreted for us, so it happened; Pharaoh restored me in my office, but he hanged ①the chief baker.” ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh sent word and called for Joseph, and they hurriedly brought him out of the dungeon; and when he had shaved himself and changed his clothes, he came to Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have had a dream, but no one can interpret it; and I have heard ①it said about you, that ②when you hear a dream you can interpret it.” ▷ ①Lit about you, saying ②Lit you hear a dream to interpret it

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph then answered Pharaoh, saying, “ ①It has nothing to do with me; God will ②give Pharaoh an answer for his own good.” ▷ ①Lit Apart from me ②Lit answer the peace of Pharaoh

column.name: text
column.value: So Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream, there I was, standing on the bank of the Nile;

column.name: text
column.value: and behold, seven cows, ①fat and fine-looking came up out of the Nile, and they grazed in the marsh grass. ▷ ①Lit fat of flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, seven other cows came up after them, poor and very ①ugly and ②thin, such as I had never seen for ③ugliness in all the land of Egypt; ▷ ①Lit bad ②Lit thin of flesh ③Lit badness

column.name: text
column.value: and the thin and ugly cows ate the first seven fat cows.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet when they had ①devoured them, it could not be ②detected that they had ③devoured them, ④for they were just as ugly as ⑤before. Then I awoke. ▷ ①Lit entered their inward parts ②Or known ③Lit entered their inward parts ④Lit and ⑤Lit in the beginning

column.name: text
column.value: I saw also in my dream, and behold, seven ears of grain, full and good, came up on a single stalk;

column.name: text
column.value: and behold, seven ears, withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind sprouted up after them;

column.name: text
column.value: and the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears. Then I told it to the soothsayer priests, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh’s ①dreams are one and the same; God has told to Pharaoh what He is about to do. ▷ ①Lit dream is

column.name: text
column.value: The seven good cows are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years; the ①dreams are one and the same. ▷ ①Lit dream is

column.name: text
column.value: The seven thin and ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and the seven thin ears scorched by the east wind will be seven years of famine.

column.name: text
column.value: ①It is as I have spoken to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do. ▷ ①Lit That is the thing which I spoke

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming in all the land of Egypt;

column.name: text
column.value: and after them seven years of famine will ①come, and all the abundance will be forgotten in the land of Egypt, and the famine will ②ravage the land. ▷ ①Lit arise ②Lit destroy

column.name: text
column.value: So the abundance will be unknown in the land because of that subsequent famine; for it will be very severe.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the repeating of the dream to Pharaoh twice, it means that the matter is confirmed by God, and God will quickly bring it about.

column.name: text
column.value: So now let Pharaoh look for a man discerning and wise, and appoint him over the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Let Pharaoh take action to appoint overseers ①in charge of the land, and let him take a fifth of the produce of the land of Egypt as a tax in the seven years of abundance. ▷ ①Lit over

column.name: text
column.value: Then have them collect all the food of these good years that are coming, and store up the grain for food in the cities under Pharaoh’s authority, and have them guard it.

column.name: text
column.value: Let the food be used as a reserve for the land for the seven years of famine which will occur in the land of Egypt, so that the land will not perish during the famine.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now the ①proposal seemed good ②to Pharaoh and ③to all his servants. ▷ ①Lit word ②Lit in the sight of ③Lit in the sight of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man like this, in whom there is a divine spirit?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has informed you of all this, there is no one as discerning and wise as you are.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall be ①in charge of my house, and all my people shall ②be obedient to you; only regarding the throne will I be greater than you.” ▷ ①Lit over ②Lit kiss your mouth; LXX obey at your command

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh also said to Joseph, “See, I have placed you over all the land of Egypt.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand and put it on Joseph’s hand, and clothed him in garments of fine linen, and put the gold necklace around his neck.

column.name: text
column.value: And he had him ride in ①his second chariot; and they proclaimed ahead of him, “ ②Bow the knee!” And he placed him over all the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit the second...which was his ②Or Make way

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Though I am Pharaoh, yet without ①your permission no one shall raise his hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.” ▷ ①Lit you no one

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh named Joseph ①Zaphenath-paneah; and he gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of ②On, to be his wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Prob. Egyptian for “God speaks; he lives” ②Or Heliopolis

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he ①stood in the presence of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh and went through all the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Or entered the service of

column.name: text
column.value: During the seven years of plenty the land produced ①abundantly. ▷ ①Lit by handfuls

column.name: text
column.value: So he collected all the food of these seven years which occurred in the land of Egypt and put the food in the cities; he put in every city the food from its own surrounding fields.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph stored up grain ①in great abundance like the sand of the sea, until he stopped ②measuring it, for it was ③beyond measure. ▷ ①Lit very much ②Lit numbering ③Or without number

column.name: text
column.value: Now before the year of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, priest of ①On, bore to him. ▷ ①Or Heliopolis

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph named the firstborn ①Manasseh; “For,” he said, “God has made me forget all my trouble and all of my father’s household.” ▷ ①I.e., making to forget

column.name: text
column.value: And he named the second ①Ephraim; “For,” he said, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.” ▷ ①I.e., fruitfulness

column.name: text
column.value: When the seven years of plenty which had taken place in the land of Egypt came to an end,

column.name: text
column.value: and the seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said, then there was famine in all the lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

column.name: text
column.value: So when all the land of Egypt suffered famine, the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread; and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph; whatever he says to you, you shall do.”

column.name: text
column.value: When the famine was spread over the entire face of the earth, then Joseph opened all ①the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; and the famine was severe in the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit that which was in them

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe in all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt with Jacob; they came, each one ①with his household: ▷ ①Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah;

column.name: text
column.value: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin;

column.name: text
column.value: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

column.name: text
column.value: ①All the people who descended from Jacob were seventy ②people, but Joseph was already in Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Every soul ②Lit souls

column.name: text
column.value: And Joseph died, and all his brothers and all that generation.

column.name: text
column.value: But the sons of Israel were fruitful and ①increased greatly, and multiplied, and became exceedingly ②mighty, so that the land was filled with them. ▷ ①Lit swarmed ②Or numerous

column.name: text
column.value: Now a new king arose over Egypt, who did not know Joseph.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his people, “Behold, the people of the sons of Israel are ①too many and too mighty for us. ▷ ①Ormore and mightier than we

column.name: text
column.value: Come, let us deal ①shrewdly with them, otherwise they will multiply, and ②in the event of war, they will also join those who hate us, and fight against us and ③depart from the land.” ▷ ①Or wisely ②Lit it will come about when war occurs that ③Lit go up from

column.name: text
column.value: So they appointed taskmasters over them to oppress them with ①hard labor. And they built for Pharaoh storage cities, Pithom and Raamses. ▷ ①Lit their burdens

column.name: text
column.value: But the more they oppressed them, the more they multiplied and the more they ①spread out, so that they dreaded the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Lit broke forth

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians ①used violence to compel the sons of Israel to labor; ▷ ①Lit with violence compelled

column.name: text
column.value: and they made their lives bitter with hard labor in mortar and bricks and at all kinds of labor in the field, all their labors which they violently had them perform as slaves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, one of whom ①was named Shiphrah, and the other ②was named Puah; ▷ ①Lit the name was ②Lit the name was

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, “When you are helping the Hebrew women to give birth and see them upon the birthstool, if it is a son, then you shall put him to death; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the midwives ①feared God, and did not do as the king of Egypt had ②commanded them, but let the boys live. ▷ ①Or revered ②Lit spoken to

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Egypt called for the midwives and said to them, “Why have you done this thing, and let the boys live?”

column.name: text
column.value: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women are not like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife ①can get to them.” ▷ ①Lit comes to

column.name: text
column.value: So God was good to the midwives, and the people multiplied, and became very ①mighty. ▷ ①Or numerous

column.name: text
column.value: And because the midwives ①feared God, He ②established ③households for them. ▷ ①Or revered ②Lit made ③Or families

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “Every son who is born, ①you are to throw into the Nile, but every daughter, you are to keep alive.” ▷ ①Some ancient versions insert to the Hebrews

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph fell on his father’s face, and wept over him and kissed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father. So the physicians embalmed Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now forty days were ①required for ②it, for ③such is the period required for embalming. And the Egyptians wept for him seventy days. ▷ ①Lit fulfilled ②Or him ③Lit so are fulfilled the days of embalming

column.name: text
column.value: When the days of ①mourning for him were past, Joseph spoke to the household of Pharaoh, saying, “If now I have found favor in your sight, please speak ②to Pharaoh, saying, ▷ ①Lit weeping ②Lit In the ears of

column.name: text
column.value: ‘My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I am about to die; in my grave which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me.” Now then, please let me go up and bury my father; then I will return.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his household and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: and all the household of Joseph and his brothers and his father’s household; they left only their little ones and their flocks and their herds in the land of Goshen.

column.name: text
column.value: Chariots with teams of horses also went up with him; and it was a very great company.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the ①threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, they mourned there with a very great and ②sorrowful lamentation; and he ③observed seven days of mourning for his father. ▷ ①Heb Goren ha-Atad ②Lit heavy ③Lit made a mourning for seven days

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at ①the threshing floor of Atad, they said, “This is a ②grievous ③mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore it was named ④Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan. ▷ ①Heb Goren ha-Atad ②Lit heavy ③Heb ebel ④I.e., the meadow (or mourning) of Egypt

column.name: text
column.value: And so his sons did for him as he had commanded them;

column.name: text
column.value: for his sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah opposite Mamre, which Abraham had bought along with the field as a ①burial site from Ephron the Hittite. ▷ ①Lit possession of a burial place

column.name: text
column.value: And after he had buried his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers, and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joseph’s brothers had seen that their father was dead, they said, “What if Joseph holds a grudge against us and pays us back in full for all the wrong which we did to him!”

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent instructions to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded us before he died, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘This is what you shall say to Joseph: “Please forgive, I beg you, the offense of your brothers and their sin, for they did you wrong.” ’ And now, please forgive the offense of the servants of the God of your father.” And Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Behold, we are your servants.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid, for am I in God’s place?

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good in order to bring about ①this present result, to keep many people alive. ▷ ①Lit as this day

column.name: text
column.value: So therefore, do not be afraid; I will provide for you and your little ones.” So he comforted them and spoke ①kindly to them. ▷ ①Lit to their heart

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joseph stayed in Egypt, he and his father’s household, and Joseph lived 110 years.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph saw the third generation of Ephraim’s sons; also the sons of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.

column.name: text
column.value: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die, but God will assuredly ①take care of you and bring you up from this land to the land which He ②promised on oath to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.” ▷ ①Or visit ②Lit swore

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, “God will assuredly ①take care of you, and you shall carry my bones up from here.” ▷ ①Or visit

column.name: text
column.value: So Joseph died at the age of 110 years; and they embalmed him and placed him in a coffin in Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man from the house of Levi went and ①married a daughter of Levi. ▷ ①Lit took

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman conceived and gave birth to a son; and when she saw ①that he was ②beautiful, she hid him for three months. ▷ ①Lit him that ②Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: But when she could no longer hide him, she got him a papyrus ①basket and covered it with tar and pitch. Then she put the child in it and set it among the reeds by the bank of the Nile. ▷ ①Or chest

column.name: text
column.value: And his sister stood at a distance to ①find out what would ②happen to him. ▷ ①Lit know ②Lit be done

column.name: text
column.value: Now the daughter of Pharaoh came down to bathe at the Nile, with her female attendants walking alongside the Nile; and she saw the ①basket among the reeds and sent her slave woman, and she brought it to her. ▷ ①Or chest

column.name: text
column.value: When she opened it, she ①saw the child, and behold, the boy was crying. And she had pity on him and said, “This is one of the Hebrews’ children.” ▷ ①Heb saw it, the child

column.name: text
column.value: Then his sister said to Pharaoh’s daughter, “Shall I go and call a woman for you who is nursing from the Hebrew women, so that she may nurse the child for you?”

column.name: text
column.value: Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Go ahead.” So the girl went and called the child’s mother.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh’s daughter said to her, “Take this child away and nurse him for me, and I will give you your wages.” So the woman took the child and nursed him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter and he became her son. And she named him ①Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.” ▷ ①Heb Mosheh, from a verb meaning to draw out

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in those days, when Moses had grown up, that he went out to his ①fellow Hebrews and looked at their ②hard labors; and he saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his ③fellow Hebrews. ▷ ①Lit brothers ②Lit burdens ③Lit brothers

column.name: text
column.value: So he ①looked this way and that, and when he saw that there was no one around, he struck and killed the Egyptian, and hid ②his body in the sand. ▷ ①Lit turned ②Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Now he went out the next day, and behold, two Hebrews were ①fighting with each other; and he said to the ②offender, “Why are you striking your companion?” ▷ ①Or quarreling ②Or the guilty one

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Who made you a ①ruler and a judge over us? Do you ②intend to kill me as you killed the Egyptian?” Then Moses was afraid and said, “Surely the matter has become known!” ▷ ①Lit man, a ruler ②Lit say

column.name: text
column.value: When Pharaoh heard about this matter, he tried to kill Moses. But Moses fled from the presence of Pharaoh and ①settled in the land of Midian, and he sat down by a well. ▷ ①Lit dwelt

column.name: text
column.value: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters; and they came to draw water and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the shepherds came and drove them away, but Moses stood up and helped them and watered their flock.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to their father Reuel, he said, “Why have you come back so soon today?”

column.name: text
column.value: They said, “An Egyptian saved us from ①the shepherds, and what is more, he even drew water for us and watered the flock.” ▷ ①Lit the hand of the

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to his daughters, “Where is he then? Why is it that you have left the man behind? Invite him ①to have something to eat.” ▷ ①Lit that he may eat bread

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses was willing to live with the man. And he gave his daughter Zipporah to Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she gave birth to a son, and he named him ①Gershom, for he said, “I have been a stranger in a foreign land.” ▷ ①Cf. Heb ger sham, a stranger there

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in the course of those many days that the king of Egypt died. And the sons of Israel groaned because of the bondage, and they cried out; and their cry for help because of their bondage ascended to God.

column.name: text
column.value: So God heard their groaning; and God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

column.name: text
column.value: And God saw the sons of Israel, and God ①took notice of them. ▷ ①Lit knew them

column.name: text
column.value: And afterward Moses and Aaron came and said to Pharaoh, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘Let My people go so that they may celebrate a feast to Me in the wilderness.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Pharaoh said, “Who is the LORD that I should obey His voice to let Israel go? I do not know the LORD, and besides, I will not let Israel go.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said, “The God of the Hebrews has met with us. Please, let us go a three days’ journey into the wilderness so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God, otherwise He will strike us with plague or with the sword.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the king of Egypt said to them, “Moses and Aaron, why do you let the people neglect their ①work? Get back to your labors!” ▷ ①Lit works

column.name: text
column.value: Again Pharaoh said, “Look, the people of the land are now many, and you would have them cease from their labors!”

column.name: text
column.value: So the same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters over the people and their foremen, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “You are no longer to give the people straw to make bricks as previously; have them go and gather straw for themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: But you shall impose on them the quota of bricks which they were making before; you are not to reduce any of it. Because they are lazy, for that reason they cry ①out, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to our God.’ ▷ ①Lit out, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: Let the labor be heavier on the men, and have them work at it so that they will pay no attention to false words.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the taskmasters of the people and their foremen went out and spoke to the people, saying, “This is what Pharaoh says: ‘I am not going to give you any straw.

column.name: text
column.value: You go, get straw for yourselves wherever you can find it; but none of your labor will be reduced.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So the people scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.

column.name: text
column.value: And the taskmasters pressed them, saying, “Complete your ①work quota, ②your daily amount, just as when ③you had straw.” ▷ ①Lit works ②Lit the matter of a day in its day ③Lit there was

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, the foremen of the sons of Israel, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten ①and asked, “Why have you not completed your required task of making bricks either yesterday or today, as before?” ▷ ①Lit saying

column.name: text
column.value: Then the foremen of the sons of Israel came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you deal this way with your servants?

column.name: text
column.value: There is no straw given to your servants, yet they keep saying to us, ‘Make bricks!’ And behold, your servants are being beaten; but it is the fault of your own people.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “You are lazy, very lazy; for that reason you say, ‘Let us go and sacrifice to the LORD.’

column.name: text
column.value: So go now and work; for you will be given no straw, but you must deliver the quota of bricks.”

column.name: text
column.value: The foremen of the sons of Israel saw that they were in trouble, ①since they were told, “You must not reduce ②your daily amount of bricks.” ▷ ①Lit saying ②Lit from your bricks the matter of a day in its day

column.name: text
column.value: When they left Pharaoh’s presence, they met Moses and Aaron as they were ①waiting for them. ▷ ①Lit standing to meet

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to them, “May the LORD look upon you and judge you, because you have made ①us repulsive in Pharaoh’s sight and in the sight of his servants, to put a sword in their hand to kill us!” ▷ ①Lit our odor stink

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses returned to the LORD and said, “Lord, why have You brought harm to this people? Why did You ever send me?

column.name: text
column.value: Ever since I came to Pharaoh to speak in Your name, he has done harm to this people, and You have not rescued Your people at all.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “What if they will not believe me or listen ①to what I say? For they may say, ‘The LORD has not appeared to you.’ ” ▷ ①Lit to my voice

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to him, “What is that in your hand?” And he said, “A staff.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then He said, “Throw it on the ground.” So he threw it on the ground, and it turned into a serpent; and Moses fled from it.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Moses, “Reach out with your hand and grasp it by its tail”—so he reached out with his hand and caught it, and it turned into a staff in his ①hand— ▷ ①Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: “so that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has appeared to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD furthermore said to him, “Now put your hand inside the fold of your robe.” So he put his hand inside the fold, and when he took it out, behold, his hand was leprous like snow.

column.name: text
column.value: Then He said, “Put your hand inside the fold of your robe again.” So he put his hand into the fold again, and when he took it out of the fold, behold, it was restored like the rest of his flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: “So if they will not believe you nor ①pay attention to the ②evidence of the first ③sign, they may believe the ④evidence of the last ⑤sign. ▷ ①Lit listen to ②Lit voice ③I.e., confirming miracle ④Lit voice ⑤I.e., confirming miracle

column.name: text
column.value: But if they will not believe even these two ①signs nor pay attention to what you say, then you shall take some water from the Nile and pour it on the dry ground; and the water which you take from the Nile will turn into blood on the dry ground.” ▷ ①I.e., confirming miracles

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to the LORD, “Please, Lord, I have never been ①eloquent, neither ②recently nor in time past, nor since You have spoken to Your servant; for I am ③slow of speech and ④slow of tongue.” ▷ ①Lit a man of words ②Lit yesterday ③Lit heavy ④Lit heavy

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to him, “Who has made the human mouth? Or who makes anyone unable to speak or deaf, or able to see or blind? Is it not I, the LORD?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then go, and I Myself will be with your mouth, and instruct you in what you are to say.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Please, Lord, now send the message by ①whomever You will.” ▷ ①Lit the hand You send

column.name: text
column.value: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Moses, and He said, “Is there not your brother Aaron the Levite? I know that ①he speaks fluently. And moreover, behold, he is coming out to meet you; when he sees you, he will be ②overjoyed. ▷ ①Lit speaking he speaks ②Lit joyful in his heart

column.name: text
column.value: So you are to speak to him and put the words in his mouth; and I Myself will be with your mouth and his mouth, and I will instruct you in what you are to do.

column.name: text
column.value: He shall speak for you to the people; and he will be as a mouth for you and you will be as God to him.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall take in your hand this staff, with which you shall perform the signs.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses departed and returned to his father-in-law ①Jethro, and said to him, “Please, let me go, that I may return to my brothers who are in Egypt, and see if they are still alive.” And Jethro said to Moses, “Go in peace.” ▷ ①Heb Jether

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD said to Moses in Midian, “Go ①back to Egypt, for all the men who were seeking your life are dead.” ▷ ①Lit return

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses took his wife and his sons and mounted them on a donkey, and returned to the land of Egypt. Moses also took the staff of God in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses, “When you go ①back to Egypt, see that you perform before Pharaoh all the wonders which I have put in your ②power; but I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go. ▷ ①Lit to return ②Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Israel is My son, My firstborn.

column.name: text
column.value: So I said to you, ‘Let My son go so that he may serve Me’; but you have refused to let him go. Behold, I am going to kill your son, your firstborn.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But it came about at the overnight encampment on the way, that the LORD met ①Moses, and sought to put him to death. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: So Zipporah took a flint and cut off her son’s foreskin and ①threw it at Moses’ feet; and she said, “You are indeed a groom of blood to me!” ▷ ①Lit made it touch at his feet

column.name: text
column.value: So He left him alone. At that time she said, “You are a groom of blood”— ①because of the circumcision. ▷ ①Lit with reference to

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD said to Aaron, “Go to meet Moses in the wilderness.” So he went and met him at the mountain of God and kissed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses told Aaron all the words of the LORD with which He had sent him, and all the signs that He had commanded him to do.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and Aaron went and assembled all the elders of the sons of Israel;

column.name: text
column.value: and Aaron spoke all the words which the LORD had spoken to Moses. He then performed the signs in the sight of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: So the people believed; and when they heard that the LORD ①was concerned about the sons of Israel and that He had seen their affliction, they bowed low and worshiped. ▷ ①Lit had visited

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh; for ①under compulsion he will let them go, and ②under compulsion he will drive them out of his land.” ▷ ①Lit by a strong hand ②Lit by a strong hand

column.name: text
column.value: God spoke further to Moses and said to him, “I am the LORD;

column.name: text
column.value: and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as ①God Almighty, but by My name, ②LORD, I did not make Myself known to them. ▷ ①Heb El Shaddai ②Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
column.value: I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the ①land in which they lived as strangers. ▷ ①Lit land of their sojournings in which...

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore I have heard the groaning of the sons of Israel, because the Egyptians are holding them in bondage, and I have remembered My covenant.

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: Then I will take you ①as My people, and I will be ②your God; and you shall know that I am the LORD your God, who brought you out from under the labors of the Egyptians. ▷ ①Lit to Me for a people ②Lit to you for a God

column.name: text

column.value: But I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, so that I may multiply My signs and My wonders in the land of Egypt.

column.name: text

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron came to Pharaoh, and so they did, just as the LORD had commanded; and Aaron threw his staff down before Pharaoh and ①his servants, and it turned into a serpent. ▷ ①Lit before his

column.name: text

column.name: text

column.value: For if you refuse to let them go and ①continue to hold them, ▷ ①Lit still hold

column.value: behold, the hand of the LORD ①will come with a very severe plague on your livestock which are in the field, on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks. ▷ ①Lit will be

column.value: But the LORD will make a distinction between the livestock of Israel and the livestock of Egypt, so that nothing will die of all that belongs to the sons of Israel.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD set a definite time, saying, “Tomorrow the LORD will do this thing in the land.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD did this thing on the next day, and all the livestock of Egypt died; but not one of the livestock of the sons of Israel died.

column.name: text
column.value: And Pharaoh sent men, and they learned that, behold, not even one of the livestock of Israel was dead. But the heart of Pharaoh was ①hardened, and he did not let the people go. ▷ ①Lit heavy

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Take for yourselves handfuls of soot from a kiln, and Moses shall toss it toward the sky in the sight of Pharaoh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it will become fine dust over all the land of Egypt, and will turn into boils breaking out with sores on every person and animal through all the land of Egypt.”

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: The soothsayer priests could not stand before Moses because of the boils, for the boils were on the soothsayer priests as well as on all the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD ①hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not listen to them, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses. ▷ ①Lit made strong

column.name: text

column.value: For this time I am going to send all My plagues ①on you and your servants and your people, so that you may know that there is no one like Me in all the earth. ▷ ①Lit to your heart

column.value: So now, send word, bring your livestock and whatever you have in the field to safety. Every person and animal that is found in the field and is not brought home, when the hail comes down on them, will die.” ’ ”

column.value: Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, was there no hail.

column.name: text

column.value: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God within the land.”

column.value: But Moses said, “It is not permissible for us to do so, because we will sacrifice to the LORD our God ①that which is an abomination to the Egyptians. If we sacrifice ②that which is an abomination to the Egyptians before their eyes, will they not stone us? ▷ ①Lit the abomination of Egypt ②Lit the abomination of Egypt

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “Behold, I am going to leave you, and I will plead with the LORD that the swarms of flies may depart from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people tomorrow; only do not let Pharaoh deal deceitfully again in not letting the people go to sacrifice to the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses left Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD did ①as Moses asked, and removed the swarms of flies from Pharaoh, from his servants, and from his people; not one remained. ▷ ①Lit according to the word of Moses

column.name: text
column.value: But Pharaoh ①hardened his heart this time also, and he did not let the people go. ▷ ①Lit made heavy

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have ①hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, so that I may ②perform these signs of Mine ③among them, ▷ ①Lit made heavy ②Lit put ③Lit in his midst

column.name: text
column.value: and that you may tell in the ①presence of your son, and of your grandson, how I made a mockery of the Egyptians and how I ②performed My signs among them, so that you may know that I am the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit ears ②Lit put

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may serve Me.

column.name: text
column.value: For if you refuse to let My people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your territory.

column.name: text
column.value: And they will cover the surface of the land, so that no one will be able to see the land. They will also eat the rest of what has survived—what is left to you from the hail—and they will eat every tree of yours which grows ①in the field. ▷ ①Lit from

column.name: text
column.value: Then your houses will be filled with them, ①together with the houses of all your servants and the houses of all the Egyptians, something which neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen, from the day that they ②came upon the earth until this day.’ ” And he turned and left Pharaoh. ▷ ①Lit and the ②Lit were

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long shall this man be a snare to us? Let the ①people go, so that they may serve the LORD their God. Do you not yet ②realize that Egypt is destroyed?” ▷ ①Or men ②Lit know

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go, serve the LORD your God! ①Who specifically are the ones who are going?” ▷ ①Lit Who and who are

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said, “We shall go with our young and our old; with our sons and our daughters, with our flocks and our herds we shall go, for we ①must hold a feast to the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit have a feast

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to them, “So may the LORD be with you, when I let you and your little ones go! Watch out, for evil is ①on your mind! ▷ ①Lit before your face

column.name: text
column.value: Not so! Go now, but only the men among you, and serve the LORD, since ①that is what you desire.” So they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence. ▷ ①Lit you desire it

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Reach out with your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, so that they may come up on the land of Egypt and eat every plant of the land, everything that the hail has left.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses reached out with his staff over the land of Egypt, and the LORD directed an east wind on the land all that day and all that night; and when it was morning, the east wind ①brought the locusts. ▷ ①Lit carried

column.name: text
column.value: The locusts came up over all the land of Egypt and settled in all the territory of Egypt; they were very ①numerous. There had never been so many ②locusts, nor would there be so many ③again. ▷ ①Lit heavy ②Lit locusts like them before them ③Lit after them

column.name: text
column.value: For they covered the surface of the whole land, so that the land was darkened; and they ate every plant of the land and all the fruit of the trees that the hail had left. Therefore nothing green was left on tree or plant of the field throughout the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh hurriedly called for Moses and Aaron, and he said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.

column.name: text
column.value: So now, please forgive my sin only this once, and plead with the LORD your God, that He would only remove this death from me.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he left Pharaoh and pleaded with the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD shifted the wind to a very strong west wind, which picked up the locusts and drove them into the ①Red Sea; not one locust was left in all the territory of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Sea of Reeds

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD ①hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go. ▷ ①Lit made strong

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Reach out with your hand toward the sky, so that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even a darkness which may be felt.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses reached out with his hand toward the sky, and there was thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.

column.name: text
column.value: They did not see one another, nor did anyone rise from his place for three days, but all the sons of Israel had light in their dwellings.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh called for Moses, and said, “Go, serve the LORD; only let your flocks and your herds be left behind. Even your little ones may go with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, “You must also ①let us have sacrifices and burnt offerings, so that we may ②sacrifice them to the LORD our God. ▷ ①Lit hand over ②Lit make them for
