column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD ①hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was not willing to let them go. ▷ ①Lit made strong

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pharaoh said to him, “Get away from me! ①Be careful, do not see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you shall die!” ▷ ①Lit Take care for yourself

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said, “You have spoken correctly; I shall never see your face again!”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Moses was pasturing the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian; and he led the flock to the ①west side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God. ▷ ①Or rear part

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD appeared to him in a blazing fire from the midst of ①a bush; and he looked, and behold, the bush was burning with fire, yet the bush was not being consumed. ▷ ①Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses said, “I must turn aside and see this ①marvelous sight, why the bush is not burning up!” ▷ ①Lit great

column.name: text
column.value: When the LORD saw that he turned aside to look, God called to him from the midst of the bush and said, “Moses, Moses!” And he said, “Here I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then He said, “Do not come near here; remove your sandals from your feet, for the place on which you are standing is holy ground.”

column.name: text
column.value: And He said, “I am the God of your father—the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” Then Moses hid his face, for he was afraid to look at God.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said, “I have certainly seen the oppression of My people who are in Egypt, and have heard their outcry because of their taskmasters, for I am aware of their sufferings.

column.name: text
column.value: So I have come down to rescue them from the ①power of the Egyptians, and to bring them up from that land to a good and spacious land, to a land flowing with milk and honey, to the place of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: And now, behold, the cry of the sons of Israel has come to Me; furthermore, I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians are oppressing them.

column.name: text
column.value: And now come, and I will send you to Pharaoh, so that you may bring My people, the sons of Israel, out of Egypt.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to God, “Who am I, that I should go to Pharaoh, and that I should bring the sons of Israel out of Egypt?”

column.name: text
column.value: And He said, “Assuredly I will be with you, and this shall be the sign to you that it is I who have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall ①worship God at this mountain.” ▷ ①Or serve

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to God, “Behold, I am going to the sons of Israel, and I will say to them, ‘The God of your fathers has sent me to you.’ Now they may say to me, ‘What is His name?’ What shall I say to them?”

column.name: text
column.value: And God said to Moses, “ ①I AM WHO ②I AM”; and He said, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘ ③I AM has sent me to you.’ ” ▷ ①Related to the name of God, YHWH, rendered LORD, which is derived from the verb HAYAH, to be ②Related to the name of God, YHWH, rendered LORD, which is derived from the verb HAYAH, to be ③Related to the name of God, YHWH, rendered LORD, which is derived from the verb HAYAH, to be

column.name: text
column.value: God furthermore said to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, has sent me to you.’ This is My name forever, and this is the ①name for ②all generations to use to call upon Me. ▷ ①I.e., name used in prayer, vows, and ceremony ②Lit generation of generation

column.name: text
column.value: Go and gather the elders of Israel together and say to them, ‘The LORD, the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to me, saying, “ ①I am indeed concerned about you and what has been done to you in Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Visiting I have visited

column.name: text
column.value: So I said, I will bring you up out of the oppression of Egypt to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, to a land flowing with milk and honey.” ’

column.name: text
column.value: Then they will ①pay attention to what you say; and you with the elders of Israel will come to the king of Egypt, and you will say to him, ‘The LORD, the God of the Hebrews, has met with us. So now, please let us go a three days’ journey into the wilderness, so that we may sacrifice to the LORD our God.’ ▷ ①Lit hear your voice

column.name: text
column.value: But I know that the king of Egypt will not permit you to go, except ①under compulsion. ▷ ①Lit by a strong hand

column.name: text
column.value: So I will reach out with My hand and strike Egypt with all My miracles which I shall do in the midst of it; and after that he will let you go.

column.name: text
column.value: I will grant this people favor in the sight of the Egyptians; and it shall be that when you go, you will not go empty-handed.

column.name: text
column.value: But every woman shall ask her neighbor and the woman who lives in her house for articles of silver and articles of gold, and clothing; and you will put them on your sons and daughters. So you will plunder the Egyptians.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Sanctify to Me every firstborn, the firstborn of every womb among the sons of Israel, among people and animals alike; it belongs to Me.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses said to the people, “Remember this day in which you departed from Egypt, from the house of ①slavery; for by ②a powerful hand the LORD brought you out from this place. And nothing with yeast shall be eaten. ▷ ①Lit slaves ②Lit strength of hand

column.name: text
column.value: On this day in the month of Abib, you are about to go out from here.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall be when the LORD brings you to the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall ①perform this rite in this month. ▷ ①Lit serve this service

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day there shall be a feast to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and nothing with yeast shall ①be seen among you, nor shall any dough with yeast ②be seen among you in all your borders. ▷ ①Lit appear to you ②Lit appear to you

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, ‘It is because of what the LORD did for me when I came out of Egypt.’

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall ①serve as a sign to you on your hand, and as a reminder ②on your forehead, that the law of the LORD may be in your mouth; for with a powerful hand the LORD brought you out of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit be for ②Lit between your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, you shall keep this ordinance at its appointed time from ①year to year. ▷ ①Lit days to days

column.name: text
column.value: “Now when the LORD brings you to the land of the Canaanite, as He swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,

column.name: text
column.value: you shall ①devote to the LORD every firstborn of a womb, and every firstborn offspring of an animal that you own; the males belong to the LORD. ▷ ①Lit cause to pass over

column.name: text
column.value: But every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, but if you do not redeem it, then you shall break its neck; and every ①firstborn among your sons you shall redeem. ▷ ①Lit firstborn of a human

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall be when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ then you shall say to him, ‘With ①a powerful hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt, from the house of ②slavery. ▷ ①Lit strength of hand ②Lit slaves

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, when Pharaoh was stubborn about letting us go, that the LORD put to death every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from human firstborns to animal firstborns. Therefore, I sacrifice to the LORD the males, every firstborn of a womb, but every firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

column.name: text
column.value: So it shall ①serve as a sign on your hand and as ②phylacteries ③on your forehead, for with ④a powerful hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.” ▷ ①Lit be for ②Or frontlet-bands ③Lit between your eyes ④Lit strength of hand

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Pharaoh had let the people go, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, even though it was near; for God said, “The people might change their minds when they see war, and return to Egypt.”

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore God led the people around by way of the wilderness to the ①Red Sea; and the sons of Israel went up in battle formation from the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Sea of Reeds

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had made the sons of Israel solemnly swear, saying, “God will certainly ①take care of you, and you shall carry my bones from here with you.” ▷ ①Lit visit

column.name: text
column.value: Then they set out from Succoth and camped in Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD was going before them in a pillar of cloud by day to lead them on the way, and in a pillar of fire by night to give them light, so that they might ①travel by day and by night. ▷ ①Lit go

column.name: text
column.value: ①He did not take away the pillar of cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from the presence of the people. ▷ ①Or The pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night did not depart

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Tell the sons of Israel to turn back and camp in front of Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea; you shall camp in front of Baal-zephon, opposite it, by the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: For Pharaoh will say of the sons of Israel, ‘They are wandering aimlessly in the land; the wilderness has shut them in.’

column.name: text
column.value: And I will ①harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will chase after them; and I will be honored through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” And they did so. ▷ ①Lit make strong

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Egypt was told that the people had fled, ①Pharaoh and his servants had a change of heart toward the people, and they said, “What is this that we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?” ▷ ①Lit the heart of Pharaoh...was changed

column.name: text
column.value: So he had horses harnessed to his chariot and took his people with him;

column.name: text
column.value: and he took six hundred select chariots, and all the other chariots of Egypt with officers over all of them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD ①hardened the heart of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and he chased after the sons of Israel as the sons of Israel were going out ②boldly. ▷ ①Lit made strong ②Lit with a high hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Egyptians chased after them with all the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen and his army, and they overtook them camping by the sea, beside Pi-hahiroth, in front of Baal-zephon.

column.name: text
column.value: As Pharaoh approached, the sons of Israel ①looked, and behold, the Egyptians were coming after them, and they became very frightened; so the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD. ▷ ①Lit lifted up their eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to Moses, “Is it because there were no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why have you dealt with us in this way, ①bringing us out of Egypt? ▷ ①Lit so as to bring

column.name: text
column.value: Is this not the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘ ①Leave us alone so that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness!” ▷ ①Lit Cease from us

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to the people, “Do not fear! ①Stand by and see the salvation of the LORD, which He will perform for you today; for the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you will never see them again, ever. ▷ ①Or Take your stand

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD will fight for you, while you keep silent.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Why are you crying out to Me? Tell the sons of Israel to go forward.

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, lift up your staff and reach out with your hand over the sea and divide it, and the sons of Israel shall ①go through the midst of the sea on dry land. ▷ ①Lit enter the

column.name: text
column.value: And as for Me, behold, I will ①harden the hearts of the Egyptians so that they will go in after them; and I will be honored through Pharaoh and all his army, through his chariots and his horsemen. ▷ ①Lit make strong

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD, when I am honored through Pharaoh, through his chariots, and through his horsemen.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of God, who had been going before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them and stood behind them.

column.name: text
column.value: So it came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel; and there was the cloud ①along with the darkness, yet it gave light at night. Therefore the one did not approach the other all night. ▷ ①Lit and the darkness

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses reached out with his hand over the sea; and the LORD ①swept the sea back by a strong east wind all night, and turned the sea into dry land, and the waters were divided. ▷ ①Lit caused to go

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel ①went through the midst of the sea on the dry land, and the waters were like a wall to them on their right and on their left. ▷ ①Lit entered the

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Egyptians took up the pursuit, and all Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen went in after them into the midst of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: But at the morning watch, the LORD looked down on the ①army of the Egyptians ②through the pillar of fire and cloud, and brought the ③army of the Egyptians into confusion. ▷ ①Lit camp ②Or in ③Lit camp

column.name: text
column.value: He ①caused their chariot wheels to swerve, and He made them drive with difficulty; so the Egyptians each said, “Let me flee from Israel, for the LORD is fighting for them against the Egyptians.” ▷ ①Or removed

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Reach out with your hand over the sea so that the waters may come back over the Egyptians, over their chariots and their horsemen.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses reached out with his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its normal state at daybreak, while the Egyptians were fleeing ①right into it; then the LORD ②overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. ▷ ①Lit to meet it ②Lit shook off

column.name: text
column.value: The waters returned and covered the chariots and the horsemen, Pharaoh’s entire army that had gone into the sea after them; not even one of them remained.

column.name: text
column.value: But the sons of Israel walked on dry land through the midst of the sea, and the waters were like a wall to them on their right and on their left.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD saved Israel that day from the hand of the Egyptians, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.

column.name: text
column.value: When Israel saw the great ①power which the LORD had ②used against the Egyptians, the people ③feared the LORD, and they believed in the LORD and in His servant Moses. ▷ ①Lit hand ②Lit done ③Or revered

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD said to Moses and Aaron in the land of ①Egypt, ▷ ①Lit Egypt, saying

column.name: text
column.value: “This month shall be the beginning of months for you; it is to be the first month of the year for you.

column.name: text
column.value: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth of this month they are, each one, to take a ①lamb for themselves, according to the fathers’ households, a ②lamb for ③each household. ▷ ①Or kid ②Or kid ③Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: Now if the household is too small for a ①lamb, then he and his neighbor nearest to his house are to take one according to the ②number of persons in them; in proportion to ③what each one should eat, you are to ④divide the lamb. ▷ ①Or kid ②Or amount ③Lit each man’s eating ④Lit compute for

column.name: text
column.value: Your ①lamb shall be an unblemished male a year old; you may take it from the sheep or from the goats. ▷ ①Or kid

column.name: text
column.value: ①You shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month, then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel is to slaughter it ②at twilight. ▷ ①Lit It shall be to you for a guarding ②Lit between the two evenings

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, they shall take some of the blood and put it on the two doorposts and on the lintel ①of the houses in which they eat it. ▷ ①Lit upon

column.name: text
column.value: They shall eat the flesh that same night, roasted with fire, and they shall eat it with unleavened bread ①and bitter herbs. ▷ ①Lit in addition to

column.name: text
column.value: Do not eat any of it raw or boiled at all with water, but rather roasted with fire, both its head and its legs along with its entrails.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall not leave any of it over until morning, but whatever is left of it until morning, you shall completely burn with fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you shall eat it in this way: with your garment ①belted around your waist, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in a hurry—it is the LORD’S Passover. ▷ ①I.e., for travel

column.name: text
column.value: For I will go through the land of Egypt on that night, and fatally strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the human firstborn to animals; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgments—I am the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you ①live; and when I see the blood I will pass over you, and no plague will come upon you ②to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit are ②Lit for destruction

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Now this day shall be a memorial to you, and you shall celebrate it as a feast to the LORD; throughout your generations you are to celebrate it as ①a permanent ordinance. ▷ ①Or an eternal

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, but on the first day you shall remove dough with yeast from your houses; for whoever eats anything with yeast from the first day until the seventh day, that ①person shall be cut off from Israel. ▷ ①Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: And on the first day you shall have a holy assembly, and another holy assembly on the seventh day; no work at all shall be done on them, except for what must be eaten by every person—that alone may be ①prepared by you. ▷ ①Lit done

column.name: text
column.value: You shall also keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread, for on this very day I brought your ①multitudes out of the land of Egypt; therefore you shall keep this day throughout your generations as a ②permanent ordinance. ▷ ①Lit armies ②Or eternal

column.name: text
column.value: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty-first day of the month at evening.

column.name: text
column.value: For seven days there shall be no dough with yeast found in your houses; for whoever eats anything with yeast, that ①person shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a stranger or a native of the land. ▷ ①Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: You shall not eat anything with yeast; in all your dwellings you shall eat unleavened bread.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go and take for yourselves ①lambs according to your families, and slaughter the Passover lamb. ▷ ①Lit sheep

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall take a bunch of hyssop and dip it in the blood which is in the basin, and ①apply some of the blood that is in the basin to the lintel and the two doorposts; and none of you shall go outside the door of his house until morning. ▷ ①Lit cause to touch

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD will pass through to strike the Egyptians; but when He sees the blood on the lintel and on the two doorposts, the LORD will pass over the door and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall keep this event as an ordinance for you and your children forever.

column.name: text
column.value: When you enter the land which the LORD will give you, as He has ①promised, you shall keep this ②rite. ▷ ①Lit spoken ②Lit service

column.name: text
column.value: And when your children say to you, ‘ ①What does this rite mean to you?’ ▷ ①Lit What is this service to you?

column.name: text
column.value: then you shall say, ‘It is a Passover sacrifice to the LORD because He passed over the houses of the sons of Israel in Egypt when He struck the Egyptians, but ①spared our homes.’ ” And the people bowed low and worshiped. ▷ ①Lit delivered

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel went and did so; just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about at midnight that the LORD struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of cattle.

column.name: text
column.value: And Pharaoh got up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was no home where there was not someone dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called for Moses and Aaron at night and said, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the sons of Israel; and go, ①worship the LORD, as you have said. ▷ ①Or serve

column.name: text
column.value: Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and go, and bless me also.”

column.name: text
column.value: The Egyptians urged the people, to send them out of the land in a hurry, for they said, “We will all be dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the people took their dough before it was leavened, with their kneading bowls bound up in the clothes on their shoulders.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Israel had done according to the word of Moses, for they had requested from the Egyptians articles of silver and articles of gold, and clothing;

column.name: text
column.value: and the LORD had given the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have their request. Therefore they plundered the Egyptians.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Israel journeyed from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand men on foot, aside from children.

column.name: text
column.value: A mixed multitude also went up with them, ①along with flocks and herds, a very large number of livestock. ▷ ①Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: And they baked the dough which they had brought out of Egypt into cakes of unleavened bread. For it had no yeast, since they were driven out of Egypt and could not delay, nor had they ①prepared any provisions for themselves. ▷ ①Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: Now the time ①that the sons of Israel had lived in Egypt was 430 years. ▷ ①Or of the sons of Israel who lived

column.name: text
column.value: And at the end of 430 years, on this very day, all the ①multitudes of the LORD departed from the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit armies

column.name: text
column.value: It is a night ①to be observed for the LORD, for having brought them out of the land of Egypt; this night is for the LORD, ②to be observed by all the sons of Israel throughout their generations. ▷ ①Or of vigil ②Or of vigil

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover: no ①foreigner is to eat it; ▷ ①Lit son of a stranger

column.name: text
column.value: but as for every slave ①that someone has purchased with money, after you have circumcised him, then he may eat it. ▷ ①Lit of a man, an acquisition of money

column.name: text
column.value: A stranger or a hired worker shall not eat it.

column.name: text
column.value: It is to be eaten in a single house; you are not to bring any of the meat outside of the house, nor are you to break any bone of it.

column.name: text
column.value: All the congregation of Israel are to ①celebrate this. ▷ ①Lit perform

column.name: text
column.value: But if a stranger resides with you and ①celebrates the Passover to the LORD, all of his males are to be circumcised, and then he shall come near to ②celebrate it; and he shall be like a native of the land. But no uncircumcised male may eat it. ▷ ①Lit performs ②Lit perform

column.name: text
column.value: ①The same law shall ②apply to the native as to the stranger who resides among you.” ▷ ①Lit One law ②Lit be

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the sons of Israel did so; they did just as the LORD had commanded Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: And on that very day the LORD brought the sons of Israel out of the land of Egypt according to their ①multitudes. ▷ ①I.e., multitudes in battle formation

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD said to Moses, “One more plague I will bring on Pharaoh and on Egypt; after that he will let you go from here. When he lets you go, he will assuredly drive you out from here completely.

column.name: text
column.value: Speak now ①so that the people hear, that each man is to ask of his neighbor, and each woman of her neighbor, articles of silver and articles of gold.” ▷ ①Lit in the ears of the people that

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Furthermore, the man Moses himself was ①greatly esteemed in the land of Egypt, both in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants and in the sight of the people. ▷ ①Lit very great

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘About midnight I am going out into the midst of Egypt,

column.name: text
column.value: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of the Pharaoh who sits on his throne, to the firstborn of the slave girl who is behind the millstones; all the firstborn of the cattle as well.

column.name: text
column.value: So there shall be a great cry in all the land of Egypt, such as there has not been before and such as shall never be again.

column.name: text
column.value: But not even a dog will ①threaten any of the sons of Israel, nor anything from person to animal, so that you may ②learn how the LORD distinguishes between Egypt and Israel.’ ▷ ①Lit move its tongue ②Lit know

column.name: text
column.value: And all these servants of yours will come down to me and bow themselves ①before me, saying, ‘Go out, you and all the people who ②follow you,’ and after that I will go out.” And he left Pharaoh in the heat of anger. ▷ ①Lit to ②Lit are at your feet

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pharaoh will not listen to you, so that My wonders will be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron performed all these wonders before Pharaoh; yet the LORD ①hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he did not let the sons of Israel go out of his land. ▷ ①Lit made strong

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and the sons of Israel sang this song to the LORD, ①saying: “ ②I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; The horse and its rider He has hurled into the sea. ▷ ①Lit and said, saying ②Or Let me sing

column.name: text
text
text
text
column.value: The waters cover them; They went down into the depths like a stone.

column.name: text
column.value: Your right hand, LORD, is majestic in power; Your right hand, LORD, destroys the enemy.

column.name: text
text
text
text
column.value: You blew with Your wind, the sea covered them; They sank like lead in the mighty waters.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is like You among the gods, LORD? Who is like You, majestic in holiness, Awesome in praises, working wonders?

column.name: text
column.value: You reached out with Your right hand, The earth swallowed them.

column.name: text
text
column.value: The peoples have heard, they tremble; Anguish has gripped the inhabitants of Philistia.

column.name: text
text
column.value: Terror and dread fall upon them; By the greatness of Your arm they are motionless as stone, Until Your people pass over, LORD, Until the people pass over whom You have purchased.

column.name: text
column.value: You will bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, The place, LORD, which You have made as Your dwelling, The sanctuary, Lord, which Your hands have established.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD shall reign forever and ever.”

column.name: text
column.value: For the horses of Pharaoh with his chariots and his horsemen went into the sea, and the LORD brought back the waters of the sea on them, but the sons of Israel walked on dry land through the midst of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Miriam the prophetess, Aaron’s sister, took the tambourine in her hand, and all the women went out after her with tambourines and with ①dancing. ▷ ①Lit dances

column.name: text
column.value: And Miriam answered them, “Sing to the LORD, for He ①is highly exalted; The horse and his rider He has hurled into the sea.” ▷ ①Or has triumphed gloriously

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses ①led Israel from the ②Red Sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness and found no water. ▷ ①Lit caused Israel to journey ②Lit Sea of Reeds

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to Marah, they could not drink the waters ①of Marah, because they were ②bitter; for that reason it was named ③Marah. ▷ ①Lit from ②Heb Marim ③I.e., bitterness

column.name: text
column.value: So the people grumbled at Moses, saying, “What are we to drink?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a tree; and he threw it into the waters, and the waters became sweet. There He made for them a statute and regulation, and there He tested them.

column.name: text
column.value: And He said, “If you will listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God, and do what is right in His sight, and listen to His commandments, and keep all His statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you which I have put on the Egyptians; for I, the LORD, am your healer.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they came to Elim where there were twelve springs of water and seventy date palms, and they camped there beside the waters.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they set out from Elim, and all the congregation of the sons of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departure from the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: But the whole congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel said to them, “If only we had died by the LORD’S hand in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat, when we ate bread until we were full; for you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this entire assembly with hunger!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, so that I may test them, whether or not they will walk in My ①instruction. ▷ ①Or law

column.name: text
column.value: On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather daily.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses and Aaron said to all the sons of Israel, “At evening ①you will know that the LORD has brought you out of the land of Egypt; ▷ ①Lit and you

column.name: text
column.value: and in the morning ①you will see the glory of the LORD, for He hears your grumblings against the LORD; and what are we, that you grumble against us?” ▷ ①Lit and you

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses said, “This will happen when the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening, and bread to the full in the morning; for the LORD hears your grumblings which you grumble against Him. And what are we? Your grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to Aaron, “Say to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, ‘Come forward before the LORD, for He has heard your grumblings.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, as Aaron spoke to the entire congregation of the sons of Israel, that they ①looked toward the wilderness, and behold, the glory of the LORD appeared in the cloud. ▷ ①Lit turned

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “I have heard the grumblings of the sons of Israel; speak to them, saying, ‘ ①At twilight you shall eat meat, and in the morning you shall be filled with bread; and you shall know that I am the LORD your God.’ ” ▷ ①Lit Between the two evenings

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about at evening that the quails came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: When the layer of dew ①evaporated, behold, on the ②surface of the wilderness there was a fine flake-like thing, fine as the frost on the ground. ▷ ①Lit had gone up ②Lit face of

column.name: text
column.value: When the sons of Israel saw it, they said to one another, “ ①What is it?” For they did not know what it was. And Moses said to them, “It is the bread which the LORD has given you to eat. ▷ ①Heb Man hu, cf. v 31

column.name: text
column.value: This is ①what the LORD has commanded: ‘Everyone gather ②as much as he will eat; you shall take ③an omer apiece according to the number of people each of you has in his tent.’ ” ▷ ①Lit the thing which ②Lit according to his eating ③Lit an omer for a head; about 3 qt. or 2.8 liters

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel did so, and some gathered much and some little.

column.name: text
column.value: When they measured it by the ①omer, the one who had gathered much did not have too much, and the one who had gathered little did not have too little; everyone gathered ②as much as he would eat. ▷ ①About 3 qt. or 2.8 liters ②Lit according to his eating

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to them, “No one is to leave any of it until morning.”

column.name: text
column.value: But they did not listen to Moses, and some left part of it until morning, and it bred worms and stank; and Moses was angry with them.

column.name: text
column.value: They gathered it morning by morning, everyone ①as much as he would eat; but when the sun became hot, it would melt. ▷ ①Lit according to his eating

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, ①two omers for each one. When all the leaders of the congregation came and told Moses, ▷ ①About 6 qt. or 5.6 liters

column.name: text
column.value: then he said to them, “This is what the LORD ①meant: Tomorrow is a Sabbath observance, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you will bake and boil what you will boil, and all that is left over ②put aside to be kept until morning.” ▷ ①Lit spoke ②Lit lay up for you

column.name: text
column.value: So they put it aside until morning, as Moses had ordered, and it did not stink nor was there a maggot in it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “Eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to the LORD; today you will not find it in the field.

column.name: text
column.value: Six days you shall gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be ①none.” ▷ ①Lit none on it

column.name: text
column.value: Yet it came about on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, but they found none.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “How long do you refuse to keep My commandments and My ①instructions? ▷ ①Or laws

column.name: text
column.value: See, ①the LORD has given you the Sabbath; for that reason He gives you bread for two days on the sixth day. Remain, everyone, in his place; no one is to leave his place on the seventh day.” ▷ ①Lit for the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: So the people rested on the seventh day.

column.name: text
column.value: And the house of Israel named the bread ①manna, and it was like coriander seed, white, and its taste was like wafers with honey. ▷ ①Heb man, cf. v 15

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “This is ①what the LORD has commanded: ‘A ②full omer of it is to be kept safe throughout your generations, so that they may see the bread that I fed you in the wilderness, when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.’ ” ▷ ①Lit the thing which ②About 3 qt. or 2.8 liters

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take a jar and put a ①full omer of manna in it, and place it before the LORD to be kept safe throughout your generations.” ▷ ①About 3 qt. or 2.8 liters

column.name: text
column.value: As the LORD commanded Moses, so Aaron placed it before the Testimony, to be kept.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel ate the manna for forty years, until they came to an inhabited land; they ate the manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: (Now an ①omer is a tenth of an ephah.) ▷ ①About 3 qt. or 2.8 liters

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the congregation of the sons of Israel journeyed by ①stages from the wilderness of Sin, according to the ②command of the LORD, and camped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink. ▷ ①Lit their journeyings ②Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: So the people quarreled with Moses and said, “Give us water so that we may drink!” And Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test the LORD?”

column.name: text
column.value: But the people were thirsty for water there; and ①they grumbled against Moses and said, “Why is it that you have you brought us up from Egypt, to kill ②us and ③our children and ④our livestock with thirst?” ▷ ①Lit the people ②Lit me ③Lit my ④Lit my

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses cried out to the LORD, saying, “What am I to do with this people? A little more and they will stone me!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Pass before the people and take with you some of the elders of Israel; and take in your hand your staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb; and you shall strike the rock, and water will come out of it, so that the people may drink.” And Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he named the place ①Massah and ②Meribah because of the quarrel of the sons of Israel, and because they tested the LORD, saying, “Is the LORD among us, or not?” ▷ ①I.e., test ②I.e., quarrel

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses said to Joshua, “Choose men for us and go out, fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will station myself on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand.”

column.name: text
column.value: Joshua did just as Moses ①told him, ②and fought against Amalek; and Moses, Aaron, and Hur went up to the top of the hill. ▷ ①Lit said to ②Lit to fight

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about, when Moses held his hand up, that Israel prevailed; but when he let his hand ①down, Amalek prevailed. ▷ ①Lit rest

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses’ hands were heavy. So they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it; and Aaron and Hur supported his hands, one on one side and one on the other. So his hands were steady until the sun set.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joshua ①defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword. ▷ ①Lit weakened

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this in ①a book as a memorial and ②recite it to Joshua, ③that I will utterly wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven.” ▷ ①Lit the book ②Lit place it in the ears of ③Or for

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses built an altar and named it The LORD is My Banner;

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, “ ①Because the LORD has sworn, the LORD will have war against Amalek from generation to generation.” ▷ ①Or Because a hand is against the throne of the LORD; lit Because a hand upon the throne of YAH

column.name: text
column.value: In the third month after the sons of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, ①on that very day they came into the wilderness of Sinai. ▷ ①Lit on this day

column.name: text
column.value: When they set out from Rephidim, they came to the wilderness of Sinai and camped in the wilderness; and there Israel camped in front of the mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying, “This is what you shall say to the house of Jacob and tell the sons of Israel:

column.name: text
column.value: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I carried you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to Myself.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant, then you shall be My ①own possession among all the peoples, for all the earth is Mine; ▷ ①Or special treasure

column.name: text
column.value: and you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.’ These are the words that you shall speak to the sons of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses came and called the elders of the people, and set before them all these words which the LORD had commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people answered together and said, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do!” And Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you and may also trust in you forever.” Then Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD also said to Moses, “Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow, and have them wash their garments;

column.name: text
column.value: and have them ready for the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.

column.name: text
column.value: But you shall set boundaries for the people all around, saying, ‘ ①Beware that you do not go up on the mountain or touch the border of it; whoever touches the mountain shall certainly be put to death. ▷ ①Lit Take heed to yourselves

column.name: text
column.value: No hand shall touch him, but he shall certainly be stoned or ①shot through; whether animal or person, the violator shall not live.’ When the ram’s horn sounds a long blast, they shall come up to the mountain.” ▷ ①I.e., with arrows

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and consecrated the people, and they washed their garments.

column.name: text
column.value: He also said to the people, “Be ready for the third day; do not go near a woman.”

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about on the third day, when it was morning, that there were ①thunder and lightning flashes and a thick cloud over the mountain and a very loud trumpet sound, so that all the people who were in the camp trembled. ▷ ①Lit sounds

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the ①foot of the mountain. ▷ ①Lit lower part

column.name: text
column.value: Now Mount Sinai was all in smoke because the LORD descended upon it in fire; and its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the entire mountain ①quaked violently. ▷ ①Or trembled

column.name: text
column.value: When the sound of the trumpet grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him with ①thunder. ▷ ①Or a voice; lit a sound

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD came down on Mount Sinai, to the top of the mountain; and the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses: “Go down, ①warn the people, so that they do not break through to the LORD to stare, and many of them ②perish. ▷ ①Lit testify to ②Lit fall

column.name: text
column.value: Also have the priests who approach the LORD consecrate themselves, or else the LORD will break out against them.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses said to the LORD, “The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for You ①warned us, saying, ‘Set boundaries around the mountain and consecrate it.’ ” ▷ ①Lit testified to

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to him, “ ①Go down and come up again, you and Aaron with you; but do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, or He will break out against them.” ▷ ①Lit Go, descend

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went down to the people and told them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God spoke all these words, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of ①slavery. ▷ ①Lit slaves

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall have no other gods ①before Me. ▷ ①Or besides Me

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not make for yourself ①an idol, or any likeness of what is in heaven above or on the earth beneath, or in the water under the earth. ▷ ①Or a carved image

column.name: text
column.value: You shall not worship them nor serve them; for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, inflicting the ①punishment of the fathers on the children, on the third and the fourth generations of those who hate Me, ▷ ①I.e., punishment for the wrongdoing

column.name: text
column.value: but showing ①favor to thousands, to those who love Me and keep My commandments. ▷ ①Or faithfulness

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain, for the LORD will not ①leave him unpunished who takes His name in vain. ▷ ①Or hold him guiltless

column.name: text
column.value: “Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.

column.name: text
column.value: For six days you shall labor and do all your work,

column.name: text
column.value: but the seventh day is a Sabbath of the LORD your God; on it you shall not do any work, you, or your son, or your daughter, your male slave or your female slave, or your cattle, or your ①resident who ②stays with you. ▷ ①Lit stranger ②Lit is in your gates

column.name: text
column.value: For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything that is in them, and He rested on the seventh day; for that reason the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.

column.name: text
column.value: “Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be prolonged on the land which the LORD your God gives you.

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not murder.

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not commit adultery.

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not steal.

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not ①give false testimony against your neighbor. ▷ ①Lit answer as a false witness against

column.name: text
column.value: “You shall not covet your neighbor’s house; you shall not covet your neighbor’s wife, or his male slave, or his female slave, or his ox, or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.”

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people were watching and hearing the ①thunder and the lightning flashes, and the sound of the trumpet, and the mountain smoking; and when the people saw it all, they trembled and stood at a distance. ▷ ①Lit sounds

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to Moses, “Speak ①to us yourself and we will listen; but do not have God speak ②to us, or we will die!” ▷ ①Lit with ②Lit with

column.name: text
column.value: However, Moses said to the people, “Do not be afraid; for God has come in order to test you, and in order that the fear of Him may ①remain with you, so that you will not sin.” ▷ ①Lit be before

column.name: text
column.value: So the people stood at a distance, while Moses approached the thick darkness where God was.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “This is what you shall say to the sons of Israel: ‘You yourselves have seen that I have spoken ①to you from heaven. ▷ ①Lit with

column.name: text
column.value: You shall not make other gods besides Me; gods of silver or gods of gold, you shall not make for yourselves.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall make an altar of earth for Me, and you shall sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your peace offerings, your sheep and your oxen; in every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.

column.name: text
column.value: And if you make an altar of stone for Me, you shall not build it of cut stones, for if you wield your chisel on it, you will profane it.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall not go up by steps to My altar, so that your nakedness will not be exposed on it.’

column.name: text
column.value: “Now these are the ordinances which you are to set before them:

column.name: text
column.value: “If you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve for six years; but on the seventh he shall leave as a free man without a payment to you.

column.name: text
column.value: If he comes ①alone, he shall leave ②alone; if he is the husband of a wife, then his wife shall leave with him. ▷ ①Lit by himself ②Lit by himself

column.name: text
column.value: If his master gives him a wife, and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children shall belong to her master, and he shall leave ①alone. ▷ ①Lit by himself

column.name: text
column.value: But if the slave plainly says, ‘I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not leave as a free man,’

column.name: text
column.value: then his master shall bring him to ①God, then he shall bring him to the door or the doorpost. And his master shall pierce his ear with an ②awl; and he shall serve him permanently. ▷ ①Or the judges (who acted in God’s name) ②I.e., a pointed tool

column.name: text
column.value: “Now if a man sells his daughter as a female slave, she is not to ①go free as the male slaves ②do. ▷ ①Lit go out ②Lit go out

column.name: text
column.value: If she is ①displeasing in the eyes of her master ②who designated her for himself, then he shall let her be redeemed. He does not have authority to sell her to a foreign people, because of his ③unfairness to her. ▷ ①Lit bad ②Another reading is so that he did not designate her ③Lit dealing treacherously

column.name: text
column.value: And if he designates her for his son, he shall deal with her according to the custom of daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: If he takes to himself another woman, he may not reduce her ①food, her clothing, or her conjugal rights. ▷ ①Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: But if he will not do these three things for her, then she shall go ①free for nothing, without payment of money. ▷ ①Lit out

column.name: text
column.value: “He who strikes someone so that he dies shall certainly be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet ①if he did not lie in wait for him, but God caused him to fall into his hand, then I will appoint you a place to which he may flee. ▷ ①Lit he who

column.name: text
column.value: If, however, someone is enraged against his neighbor, so as to kill him in a cunning way, you are to take him even from My altar, to be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: “And one who strikes his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: “Now one who ①kidnaps someone, whether he sells him or he is found in his ②possession, shall certainly be put to death. ▷ ①Lit steals ②Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: “And one who curses his father or his mother shall certainly be put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: “Now if people have a quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with a fist, and he does not die but ①is confined to bed, ▷ ①Lit lies in

column.name: text
column.value: if he gets up and walks around outside on his staff, then he who struck him shall go unpunished; he shall only pay for his ①loss of time, and ②shall pay for his care until he is completely healed. ▷ ①Lit his sitting ②Lit healing, he shall cause to be healed

column.name: text
column.value: “And if someone strikes his male or female slave with a rod and the slave dies ①at his hand, he shall ②be punished. ▷ ①Lit under ②Lit suffer vengeance

column.name: text
column.value: If, however, the slave ①survives a day or two, no vengeance shall be taken; for the slave is his ②property. ▷ ①Lit stands ②Lit money

column.name: text
column.value: “Now if people struggle with each other and strike a pregnant woman so that ①she gives birth prematurely, but there is no injury, the guilty person shall certainly be fined as the woman’s husband ②may demand of him, and he shall pay ③as the judges decide. ▷ ①Or an untimely birth occurs; lit her children come out ②Lit lays on him ③Lit by arbitration

column.name: text
column.value: But if there is any further injury, then you shall appoint as a penalty life for life,

column.name: text
column.value: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,

column.name: text
column.value: burn for burn, wound for wound, ①bruise for bruise. ▷ ①Lit welt

column.name: text
column.value: “And if someone strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he shall let ①the slave go free on account of the eye. ▷ ①Lit him go...his eye

column.name: text
column.value: And if he ①knocks out a tooth of his male or female slave, he shall let ②the slave go free on account of the tooth. ▷ ①Lit causes to fall ②Lit him go...his tooth

column.name: text
column.value: “Now if an ox gores a man or a woman ①to death, the ox shall certainly be stoned and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the ox shall go unpunished. ▷ ①Lit so that he dies

column.name: text
column.value: If, however, an ox was previously in the habit of goring and its owner has been warned, yet he does not confine it and it kills a man or a woman, the ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.

column.name: text
