column.value: So Moses said to the LORD, “Why have You ①been so hard on Your servant? And why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have put the burden of all this people on me? ▷ ①Lit treated badly

column.name: text
column.value: Was it I who conceived all this people? Or did I give birth to them, that You should say to me, ‘Carry them ①in your arms, as a ②nurse carries a nursing infant, to the land which You swore to their fathers’? ▷ ①Lit against your chest ②Or foster father

column.name: text
column.value: Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat so that we may eat!’

column.name: text
column.value: I am not able to carry all this people by myself, because it is too ①burdensome for me. ▷ ①Lit heavy

column.name: text
column.value: So if You are going to deal with me this way, please kill me now, if I have found favor in Your sight, and do not let me see my misery.”

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD therefore said to Moses, “Gather for Me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people and their officers, and bring them to the tent of meeting, and have them take their stand there with you.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take away some of the Spirit who is upon you, and put Him upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, so that you will not bear it by yourself.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall say to the people, ‘Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of the LORD, saying, “ ①Oh that someone would give us meat to eat! For we were well-off in Egypt.” Therefore the LORD will give you meat and you shall eat. ▷ ①Or Who will give...?

column.name: text
column.value: You shall eat, not one day, nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days,

column.name: text
column.value: ①but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nose and ②makes you nauseated; because you have rejected the LORD who is among you and have wept before Him, saying, “Why did we ever leave Egypt?” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit until a ②Lit becomes nausea to you

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, “The people, among whom I am included, are six hundred thousand on foot! Yet You have said, ‘I will give them meat, so that they may eat for a whole month.’

column.name: text
column.value: Are flocks and herds to be slaughtered for them, so that it will be sufficient for them? Or are all the fish of the sea to be ①caught for them, so that it will be sufficient for them?” ▷ ①Lit gathered

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Is the LORD’S ①power too little? Now you shall see whether My word will ②come true for you or not.” ▷ ①Lit hand too short ②Lit happen to you

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses went out and told the people the words of the LORD. He also gathered seventy men of the elders of the people, and positioned them around the tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him; and He took away some of the Spirit who was upon him and placed Him upon the seventy elders. And when the Spirit rested upon them, they prophesied. Yet they did not do it again.

column.name: text
column.value: But two men had remained in the camp; the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the ①other, Medad. And the Spirit rested upon them (and they were among those who had been registered, but had not gone out to the tent), and they prophesied in the camp. ▷ ①Lit second

column.name: text
column.value: So a young man ran and informed Moses, and said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joshua the son of Nun, the personal servant of Moses from his youth, responded and said, “My lord Moses, restrain them!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? If only all the LORD’S people were prophets, that the LORD would put His Spirit upon them!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses ①returned to the camp, both he and the elders of Israel. ▷ ①Lit withdrew to

column.name: text
column.value: Now a wind burst forth from the LORD and it brought quail from the sea, and dropped them beside the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on the other side all around the camp, and about ①two cubits deep on the surface of the ground. ▷ ①About 3 ft. or 90 cm

column.name: text
column.value: And the people ①spent all that day, all night, and all the next day, and they gathered the quail (the one who gathered least gathered ②ten homers) and spread them out for themselves all around the camp. ▷ ①Lit arose ②About 77 cubic feet or 2.2 cubic meters

column.name: text
column.value: While the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD was kindled against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very severe plague.

column.name: text
column.value: So that place was named ①Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had been greedy. ▷ ①I.e., the graves of greediness

column.name: text
column.value: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they ①remained at Hazeroth. ▷ ①Lit were

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD spoke further to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Make yourself two trumpets of silver, you shall make them of hammered work; and you shall use them for summoning the congregation and breaking camp.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when both are blown, all the congregation shall meet you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: But if only one is blown, then the leaders, the heads of the ①divisions of Israel, shall meet you. ▷ ①Lit thousands; or clans

column.name: text
column.value: And when you blow an alarm, the camps that are pitched on the east side shall set out.

column.name: text
column.value: Then when you sound an alarm the second time, the camps that are pitched on the south side shall set out; an alarm is to be sounded for them to break camp.

column.name: text
column.value: When convening the assembly, however, you shall blow the trumpets without sounding an alarm.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Aaron, moreover, the priests, shall blow the trumpets; and this shall be a permanent statute for you throughout your generations.

column.name: text
column.value: And when you go to war in your land against the enemy who attacks you, then you shall sound an alarm with the trumpets, so that you will be thought of by the LORD your God, and be saved from your enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: Also on the day of your joy and at your appointed ①feasts, and on the first days of your months, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they shall be as a reminder of you before your God. I am the LORD your God.” ▷ ①Or times

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud was lifted from above the ①tabernacle of the testimony; ▷ ①Lit dwelling place, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: and the sons of Israel set out on their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai. Then the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.

column.name: text
column.value: So they moved on for the first time in accordance with the ①command of the LORD through Moses. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: The ①flag of the camp of the sons of Judah, by their armies, set out first, with Nahshon the son of Amminadab, over its army, ▷ ①Or division, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: and Nethanel the son of Zuar, over the tribal army of the sons of Issachar;

column.name: text
column.value: and Eliab the son of Helon over the tribal army of the sons of Zebulun.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the tabernacle was taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who were carrying the tabernacle, set out.

column.name: text
column.value: Next the flag of the camp of Reuben, by their armies, set out with Elizur the son of Shedeur, over its army,

column.name: text
column.value: and Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai over the tribal army of the sons of Simeon,

column.name: text
column.value: and Eliasaph the son of Deuel was over the tribal army of the sons of Gad.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy objects; and the tabernacle was set up before their arrival.

column.name: text
column.value: Next the flag of the camp of the sons of Ephraim, by their armies, set out, with Elishama the son of Ammihud over its army,

column.name: text
column.value: and Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur over the tribal army of the sons of Manasseh;

column.name: text
column.value: and Abidan the son of Gideoni over the tribal army of the sons of Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the flag of the camp of the sons of Dan, by their armies, which formed the rear guard for all the camps, set out, with Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai over its army,

column.name: text
column.value: and Pagiel the son of Ochran over the tribal army of the sons of Asher;

column.name: text
column.value: and Ahira the son of Enan over the tribal army of the sons of Naphtali.

column.name: text
column.value: ①This was the order of marching for the sons of Israel by their armies as they set out. ▷ ①Lit These were the regulations for the order

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to Hobab the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are setting out to the place of which the LORD said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us and we will do you good, for the LORD has ①promised good concerning Israel.” ▷ ①Lit spoken

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to him, “I will not come, but rather will go to my own land and relatives.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Please do not leave us, since you know ①where we should camp in the wilderness, and you will be as eyes for us. ▷ ①Lit our camping

column.name: text
column.value: So it will be, if you go with us, that ①whatever good the LORD ②does for us, we will ③do for you.” ▷ ①Lit that good which ②Lit does good ③Lit do good

column.name: text
column.value: So they moved on from the mountain of the LORD three days’ journey, with the ark of the covenant of the LORD going on in front of them for the ①three days, to seek out a resting place for them. ▷ ①Lit three days’ journey

column.name: text
column.value: And the cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about when the ark set out that Moses said, “Rise up, LORD! And may Your enemies be scattered, And those who hate You flee from Your presence.”

column.name: text
column.value: And when it came to rest, he said, “Return, LORD, To the myriad thousands of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Send out men for yourself to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am going to give the sons of Israel; you shall send a man from each of their fathers’ tribes, every one a leader among them.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the ①command of the LORD, all of them men who were heads of the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: These then were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Joseph, from the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael;

column.name: text
column.value: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi;

column.name: text
column.value: and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.

column.name: text
column.value: These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land; but Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun, ①Joshua. ▷ ①In Heb Yehoshua

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, he said to them, “Go up there into the ①Negev; then go up into the hill country. ▷ ①I.e., South country, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, whether they are few or many.

column.name: text
column.value: And how is the land in which they live, is it good or bad? And how are the cities in which they live, are the people in open camps or in fortifications?

column.name: text
column.value: And how is the land, is it ①productive or unproductive? Are there trees in it or not? And show yourselves courageous and get some of the fruit of the land.” Now the time was the season of the first ripe grapes. ▷ ①Lit fat or gaunt

column.name: text
column.value: So they went up and spied out the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, ①at Lebo-hamath. ▷ ①Or to the entrance of Hamath

column.name: text
column.value: When they had gone up into the Negev, ①they came to Hebron where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the ②descendants of Anak were. (Hebron was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.) ▷ ①Most mss one came ②Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: Then they came to the ①Valley of ②Eshcol, and from there they cut off a branch with a single cluster of grapes; and they carried it on a pole between two men, with some of the pomegranates and the figs. ▷ ①Or wadi ②I.e., cluster (of grapes)

column.name: text
column.value: That place was called the Valley of ①Eshcol, because of the cluster which the sons of Israel cut off from there. ▷ ①I.e., cluster

column.name: text
column.value: When they returned from spying out the land, at the end of forty days,

column.name: text
column.value: they went on and came to Moses and Aaron and to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, ①in the wilderness of Paran at Kadesh; and they brought back word to them and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: So they reported to him and said, “We came into the land where you sent us, and it certainly does flow with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, the people who live in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. And indeed, we saw the ①descendants of Anak there! ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: Amalek is living in the land of the Negev, the Hittites, the Jebusites, and the Amorites are living in the hill country, and the Canaanites are living by the sea and by the side of the Jordan.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Caleb quieted the people ①before Moses and said, “We should by all means go up and take possession of it, for we will certainly prevail over it.” ▷ ①Lit toward

column.name: text
column.value: But the men who had gone up with him said, “We are not able to go up against the people, because they are too strong for us.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought a bad report of the land which they had spied out to the sons of Israel, saying, “The land through which we have gone to spy out is a land that devours its inhabitants; and all the people whom we saw in it are people of great stature.

column.name: text
column.value: We also saw the ①Nephilim there (the sons of Anak are part of the Nephilim); and we were like ②grasshoppers in our own sight, and so we were in their sight.” ▷ ①Lit fallen ones; LXX giants ②Or locusts

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘When you enter the land ①where you are going to live, which I am giving you, ▷ ①Lit of your dwellings

column.name: text
column.value: and you make an offering by fire to the LORD, a burnt offering or a sacrifice to ①fulfill a special vow, or as a ②voluntary offering or at your appointed times, to make a soothing aroma to the LORD from the herd or from the flock, ▷ ①Or make a special votive offering ②Or freewill offering

column.name: text
column.value: then the one who presents his offering shall present to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ①ephah of fine flour mixed with a fourth of a ②hin of oil, ▷ ①An ephah was about 7.4 gallons or 28 liters ②A hin also was about 1 gallon or 3.8 liters

column.name: text
column.value: and you shall prepare wine for the drink offering, a fourth of a hin, with the burnt offering or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.

column.name: text
column.value: Or for a ram you shall prepare as a grain offering two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil;

column.name: text
column.value: and for the drink offering you shall offer a third of a hin of wine as a soothing aroma to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And when you prepare a bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to ①fulfill a special vow, or for peace offerings to the LORD, ▷ ①Or make a special votive offering

column.name: text
column.value: then you shall offer with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil;

column.name: text
column.value: and you shall offer as the drink offering half a hin of wine as an offering by fire, as a soothing aroma to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘This is how it shall be done for each ox, or for each ram, or for each of the male lambs, or of the goats.

column.name: text
column.value: According to the number that you prepare, so you shall do for each one according to their number.

column.name: text
column.value: Everyone who is a native shall do these things in this way, in presenting an offering by fire as a soothing aroma to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if a stranger resides among you, or one who may be among you throughout your generations, and he wants to make an offering by fire, as a soothing aroma to the LORD, just as you do so shall he do.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the assembly, there shall be one statute for you and for the stranger who resides among you, a permanent statute throughout your generations; as you are, so shall the stranger be before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: There is to be one law and one ordinance for you and for the stranger who resides with you.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, ‘When you enter the land where I am bringing you,

column.name: text
column.value: then it shall be, that when you eat from the ①food of the land, you shall lift up an ②offering to the LORD. ▷ ①Lit bread ②Or uplifted offering

column.name: text
column.value: Of the first of your ①dough you shall lift up a loaf as an ②offering; as an ③offering of the threshing floor, so you shall lift it up. ▷ ①Or coarse meal ②Or uplifted offering ③Or uplifted offering

column.name: text
column.value: From the first of your ①dough you shall give to the LORD an ②offering throughout your generations. ▷ ①Or coarse meal ②Or uplifted offering

column.name: text
column.value: ‘But when you unintentionally do wrong and fail to ①comply with all these commandments which the LORD has spoken to Moses, ▷ ①Lit perform all

column.name: text
column.value: that is, all that the LORD has commanded you ①through Moses from the day that the LORD gave commandments and onward, throughout your generations, ▷ ①Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: then it shall be, if it is done unintentionally, ①without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation shall offer one bull as a burnt offering, as a soothing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering, according to the ordinance, and one male goat as a sin offering. ▷ ①Lit away from the eyes of the congregation

column.name: text
column.value: Then the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the sons of Israel, and they will be forgiven; for it was an unintentional wrong, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD, for their unintentional wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the congregation of the sons of Israel will be forgiven, as well as the stranger who resides among them, for guilt was attributed to all the people through an unintentional wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Also, if one person sins unintentionally, then he shall offer a one-year-old female goat as a sin offering.

column.name: text
column.value: And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD for the person who goes astray by an unintentional sin, making atonement for him ①so that he may be forgiven. ▷ ①Or and he shall

column.name: text
column.value: You shall have one law for the native among the sons of Israel and for the stranger who resides among them, for one who does anything wrong unintentionally.

column.name: text
column.value: But the person who does wrong ①defiantly, whether he is a native or a stranger, that one is blaspheming the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from among his people. ▷ ①Lit with upraised hand

column.name: text
column.value: Since he has despised the word of the LORD and has broken His commandment, that person shall be completely cut off; his ①guilt will be on him.’ ” ▷ ①Or wrongdoing

column.name: text
column.value: Now while the sons of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.

column.name: text
column.value: And those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation;

column.name: text
column.value: and they placed him in custody, because it had not been decided what should be done to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.”

column.name: text
column.value: So all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him ①to death with stones, just as the LORD had commanded Moses. ▷ ①Lit with stones and he died

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD also spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak to the sons of Israel and tell them that they shall make for themselves tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and that they shall put on the tassel of each corner a ①violet thread. ▷ ①Or bluish; LXX hyacinth in color, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: It shall be a tassel for you ①to look at and remember all the commandments of the LORD, so that you will do them and not ②follow your own heart and your own eyes, ③which led you to prostitute yourselves, ▷ ①Lit and you shall look at it ②Lit seek ③Lit after which you played

column.name: text
column.value: so that you will remember and do all My commandments and be holy to your God.

column.name: text
column.value: I am the LORD your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt to be your God; I am the LORD your God.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Korah the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, took men,

column.name: text
column.value: and they stood before Moses, ①together with some of the sons of Israel, 250 leaders of the congregation ②chosen in the assembly, men of renown. ▷ ①Lit and men from ②Lit called ones of

column.name: text
column.value: They assembled together against Moses and Aaron, and said to them, “ ①You have gone far enough! For all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the LORD is in their midst; so why do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?” ▷ ①Lit Much for you

column.name: text
column.value: When Moses heard this, he fell on his face;

column.name: text
column.value: and he spoke to Korah and all his group, saying, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will make known who is His, and who is holy, and will bring that one near to Himself; indeed, the one whom He will choose, He will bring near to Himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and ①your whole group, ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: and put fire in them, and place incense upon them in the presence of the LORD tomorrow; and the man whom the LORD chooses shall be the one who is holy. ①You have gone far enough, you sons of Levi!” ▷ ①Lit Much for you

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi:

column.name: text
column.value: Is it too small an honor for you that the God of Israel has singled you out from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to Himself, to perform the service of the tabernacle of the LORD, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them;

column.name: text
column.value: and that He has brought you near, Korah, and all your brothers, sons of Levi, with you? But are you seeking the priesthood as well?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore you and your whole group are the ones gathered together against the LORD; but as for Aaron, ①who is he, that you grumble against him?” ▷ ①Lit what

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses sent ①a summons to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; but they said, “We will not come up. ▷ ①Lit to call to

column.name: text
column.value: Is it ①not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to have us die in the wilderness, but you would also appoint yourself as master over us? ▷ ①Lit a little thing

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor have you given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Would you gouge out the eyes of ①these men? We will not come up!” ▷ ①Lit those

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Pay no attention to their offering! I have not taken a single donkey from them, nor have I done harm to any of them.”

column.name: text
column.value: Moses said to Korah, “You and all your group be present before the LORD tomorrow, you and they along with Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: And each of you take his censer and put incense on ①it, and each of you bring his censer before the LORD, 250 censers; also you and Aaron shall each bring his censer.” ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: So they took, each one his own censer, and put fire on ①it, and placed incense on ②it; and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, with Moses and Aaron. ▷ ①Lit them ②Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: So Korah assembled all the congregation against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting. And the glory of the LORD appeared to all the congregation.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Separate yourselves from among this congregation, so that I may consume them instantly.”

column.name: text
column.value: But they fell on their faces and said, “God, the God of the spirits of ①humanity, when one person sins, will You be angry with the entire congregation?” ▷ ①Lit all flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from the areas around the ①tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.’ ” ▷ ①Lit residence

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses arose and went to Dathan and Abiram, with the elders of Israel following him,

column.name: text
column.value: and he spoke to the congregation, saying, “Get away now from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away in all their sin!”

column.name: text
column.value: So they moved away from the areas around the ①tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram; and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents, along with their wives, their sons, and their little ones. ▷ ①Lit dwelling place

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses said, “By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me to do all these deeds; for it is not ①my doing. ▷ ①Lit from my heart

column.name: text
column.value: If these men die ①the death of all mankind, or ②if they suffer the fate of all mankind, then the LORD has not sent me. ▷ ①Lit like the death ②Lit the visitation of all men is visited upon them

column.name: text
column.value: But if the LORD ①brings about an entirely new thing and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them with everything that is theirs, and they descend alive into ②Sheol, then you will know that these men have been disrespectful to the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit creates ②I.e., the netherworld

column.name: text
column.value: And as he finished speaking all these words, the ground that was under them split open;

column.name: text
column.value: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, their households, and all the people who belonged to Korah with all their possessions.

column.name: text
column.value: So they and all that belonged to them went down alive to ①Sheol; and the earth closed over them, and they perished from the midst of the assembly. ▷ ①I.e., the netherworld

column.name: text
column.value: Then all Israel who were around them fled at their ①outcry, for they said, “The earth might swallow us!” ▷ ①Or voice

column.name: text
column.value: Fire also came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: “Tell Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, that he shall pick up the censers from the midst of the burned area, because they are holy; and you are to scatter the ①burning coals further away. ▷ ①Lit the fire

column.name: text
column.value: As for the censers of these ①men who have sinned at the cost of their own lives, have them made into hammered sheets as plating for the altar, since they did present them before the LORD and they are holy; and they shall ②serve as a sign to the sons of Israel.” ▷ ①Lit sinners against their lives ②Lit be for a

column.name: text
column.value: So the priest Eleazar took the bronze censers which the men who were burned had offered, and they hammered them out as plating for the altar,

column.name: text
column.value: as a reminder to the sons of Israel so that no ①layman, anyone who was not of the ②descendants of Aaron, would approach to burn incense before the LORD; then he would not become like Korah and his group—just as the LORD had spoken to him ③through Moses. ▷ ①Lit stranger ②Lit seed ③Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: But on the next day all the congregation of the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You are the ones who have caused the death of the LORD’S people!”

column.name: text
column.value: It came about, however, when the congregation had assembled against Moses and Aaron, that they turned toward the tent of meeting, and behold, the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and Aaron came to the front of the tent of meeting,

column.name: text
column.value: and the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Get away from among this congregation so that I may consume them instantly.” Then they fell on their faces.

column.name: text
column.value: And Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer and put fire in it from the altar, and place incense on it; then bring it quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the LORD, the plague has begun!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Aaron took it just as Moses had spoken, and he ran into the midst of the assembly; and behold, the plague had begun among the people. So he put on the incense and made atonement for the people.

column.name: text
column.value: And he took his stand between the dead and the living, so that the plague was brought to a halt.

column.name: text
column.value: But those who died by the plague were 14,700 in number, besides those who died on account of Korah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, for the plague had been brought to a halt.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the congregation ①raised their voices and cried out, and the people wept ②that night. ▷ ①Lit raised and gave their voice ②Lit in that

column.name: text
column.value: And all the sons of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron; and the entire congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or even if we had died in this wilderness!

column.name: text
column.value: So why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will become plunder! Would it not be better for us to return to Egypt?”

column.name: text
column.value: So they said to one another, “Let’s appoint a leader and return to Egypt!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces in the presence of all the assembly of the congregation of the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, of those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes;

column.name: text
column.value: and they spoke to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying, “The land which we passed through to spy out is an exceedingly good land.

column.name: text
column.value: If the LORD is pleased with us, then He will bring us into this land and give it to us—a land which flows with milk and honey.

column.name: text
column.value: Only do not rebel against the LORD; and do not fear the people of the land, for they will be our ①prey. Their ②protection is gone from them, and the LORD is with us; do not fear them.” ▷ ①Lit food ②Lit shadow

column.name: text
column.value: But all the congregation said to stone them with stones. Then the glory of the LORD appeared in the tent of meeting to all the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people be disrespectful to Me? And how long will they not ①believe in Me, despite all the signs that I have performed in their midst? ▷ ①Or trust in

column.name: text
column.value: I will strike them with ①plague and dispossess them, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they.” ▷ ①Lit the plague

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said to the LORD, “Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people up from their midst,

column.name: text
column.value: and they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that You, LORD, are in the midst of this people, because You, LORD, are seen eye to eye, while Your cloud stands over them; and You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night.

column.name: text
column.value: Now if You put this people to death ①all at once, then the nations who have heard of Your fame will ②say, ▷ ①Lit as one man ②Lit say, saying

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Since the LORD could not bring this people into the land which He promised them by oath, He slaughtered them in the wilderness.’

column.name: text
column.value: So now, please, let the power of the Lord be great, just as You have declared, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abundant in mercy, forgiving wrongdoing and violation of His Law; but He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished, inflicting the ①punishment of the fathers on the children ②to the third and the fourth generations.’ ▷ ①I.e., punishment for the wrongdoing ②Lit on

column.name: text
column.value: Please forgive the guilt of this people in accordance with the greatness of Your mercy, just as You also have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said, “I have forgiven them in accordance with your word;

column.name: text
column.value: however, as I live, ①all the earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit and all

column.name: text
column.value: Certainly all the people who have seen My glory and My signs which I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have put Me to the test these ten times and have not listened to My voice,

column.name: text
column.value: shall by no means see the land which I swore to their fathers, nor shall any of those who were disrespectful to Me see it.

column.name: text
column.value: But as for My servant Caleb, because he has had a different spirit and has followed Me fully, I will bring him into the land which he ①entered, and his ②descendants shall take possession of it. ▷ ①Lit entered there ②Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valleys; turn tomorrow and set out for the wilderness by the way of the ①Red Sea.” ▷ ①Lit Sea of Reeds

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron again, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “How long shall I put up with this evil congregation who are grumbling against Me? I have heard the complaints of the sons of Israel which they are ①voicing against Me. ▷ ①Lit complaining

column.name: text
column.value: Say to them, ‘As I live,’ declares the LORD, ‘just as you have spoken in My hearing, so I will do to you;

column.name: text
column.value: your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness, all your ①numbered men according to your complete number from twenty years old and upward, who have grumbled against Me. ▷ ①Lit mustered

column.name: text
column.value: By no means will you come into the land where I ①swore to settle you, except for Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. ▷ ①Lit raised My hand

column.name: text
column.value: Your children, however, whom you said would become plunder—I will bring them in, and they will know the land which you have rejected.

column.name: text
column.value: But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, your sons will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will ①suffer for your unfaithfulness, until your bodies perish in the wilderness. ▷ ①Lit bear

column.name: text
column.value: In accordance with the number of days that you spied out the land, forty days, for every day you shall suffer the punishment for your ①guilt a year, that is, forty years, and you will know My opposition. ▷ ①Or wrongdoings

column.name: text
column.value: I, the LORD, have spoken, I certainly will do this to all this evil congregation who are gathered together against Me. They shall be worn out in this wilderness, and there they shall die.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: As for the men whom Moses sent to spy out the land, and who returned and led all the congregation to grumble against him by bringing a bad report about the land,

column.name: text
column.value: those men who brought the bad report of the land also died by a plague in the presence of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh remained alive out of those men who went to spy out the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Moses spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, the people mourned greatly.

column.name: text
column.value: In the morning, however, they got up early and went up to the ①ridge of the hill country, saying, “Here we are; and we will go up to the place which the LORD has ②promised, for ③we have sinned.” ▷ ①Or top of the mountain ②Lit said ③I.e., by lacking faith to go

column.name: text
column.value: But Moses said, “Why then are you violating the ①command of the LORD, when doing so will not succeed? ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Do not go up, for the LORD is not among you, ①to prevent you from being defeated ②by your enemies. ▷ ①Lit so that you are not ②Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: For the Amalekites and the Canaanites will be there ①to confront you, and you will fall by the sword, since you have turned back from following the LORD. And the LORD will not be with you.” ▷ ①Lit before you

column.name: text
column.value: But they foolishly dared to go up to the ①ridge of the hill country; neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses left the camp. ▷ ①Or top of the mountain

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down, and struck them and scattered them as far as Hormah.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying, ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: in Heb

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak to the sons of Israel, and obtain from them a staff for each father’s household: twelve staffs, from all their leaders for their fathers’ households. You shall write each man’s name on his staff,

column.name: text
column.value: and write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi; for there is to be one staff for the head of each of their fathers’ households.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall then leave them in the tent of meeting in front of the testimony, where I meet with you.

column.name: text
column.value: And it will come about that the staff of the man whom I choose will sprout. So I will relieve Myself of the grumblings of the sons of Israel, who are grumbling against you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses spoke to the sons of Israel, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader, for their fathers’ households, twelve staffs in all, with the staff of Aaron among their staffs.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses left the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony; and behold, Aaron’s staff for the house of Levi had sprouted and produced buds and bloomed with blossoms, and it yielded ripe almonds.

column.name: text
column.value: Moses then brought out all the staffs from the presence of the LORD to all the sons of Israel; and they looked, and each man took his staff.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Moses, “Put the staff of Aaron back in front of the testimony ①to be kept as a sign against the ②rebels, so that you may put an end to their grumblings against Me and they do not die.” ▷ ①Lit for preserving ②Lit sons of rebellion

column.name: text
column.value: Moses did so; just as the LORD had commanded him, so he did.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel spoke to Moses, saying, “Behold, we are passing away, we are perishing, we are all perishing!

column.name: text
column.value: Everyone who comes near, who comes near to the tabernacle of the LORD, must die. Are we to perish completely?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “This is the statute of the law which the LORD has commanded, saying, ‘Speak to the sons of Israel that they bring you an unblemished red heifer in which there is no defect and on which a yoke has never ①been mounted. ▷ ①Lit gone up

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall give it to Eleazar the priest, and it shall be brought outside the camp and be slaughtered in his presence.

column.name: text
column.value: And Eleazar the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and sprinkle some of its blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the heifer shall be burned in his sight; its hide, its flesh, and its blood, with its refuse, shall be burned.

column.name: text
column.value: And the priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet material, and throw it into the midst of the ①burning heifer. ▷ ①Lit burning of the heifer

column.name: text
column.value: The priest shall then wash his clothes and bathe his ①body in water, and afterward come into the camp; but the priest will be ②unclean until evening. ▷ ①Lit flesh ②I.e., ritually unclean, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: The one who burns ①the heifer shall also wash his clothes in water and bathe his ②body in water, and will be unclean until evening. ▷ ①Lit it ②Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them outside the camp in a clean place, and ①the congregation of the sons of Israel shall keep them for water to remove impurity; it is ②purification from sin. ▷ ①Lit it shall be to the congregation...Israel, for a guarding as water of impurity ②Or a sin offering

column.name: text
column.value: And the one who gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening; and it shall be a permanent statute for the sons of Israel and for the stranger who resides among them.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘The one who touches the dead body of any ①person will also be unclean for seven days. ▷ ①Lit soul of mankind

column.name: text
column.value: That one shall purify himself with ①the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean; but if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean. ▷ ①Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: Anyone who touches a dead body, the ①body of a person who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the ②tabernacle of the LORD; and that person shall be cut off from Israel. Since the water for impurity was not sprinkled on him, he will be unclean; his uncleanness is still on him. ▷ ①Lit soul ②Lit dwelling place

column.name: text
column.value: ‘This is the law when a person dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent will be unclean for seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: And every open container, which has no cover tied down on it, will be unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, anyone who in the open field touches one who has been killed with a sword or one who has died naturally, or touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then for the unclean person they shall take some of the ①ashes of the ②burnt ③purification from sin and ④running water shall be ⑤added to them in a container. ▷ ①Lit dust ②Lit burning of the ③Or sin offering ④Lit living ⑤Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: And a clean person shall take hyssop and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the furnishings, on the persons who were there, and on the one who touched the bone or the one who was killed or the one who died naturally, or the grave.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he shall purify him, and he shall wash his clothes and bathe himself in water and will be clean by evening.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘But the person who is unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD; the water for impurity has not been sprinkled on him, so he is unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: So it shall be a permanent statute for them. And the one who sprinkles the water for impurity shall wash his clothes, and the one who touches the water for impurity will be unclean until evening.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, anything that the unclean person touches will be unclean; and the person who touches it will be unclean until evening.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said to Aaron, “You, your sons, and your father’s household with you shall bear the guilt ①in connection with the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you shall bear the guilt ②in connection with your priesthood. ▷ ①Lit of the sanctuary ②Lit of your priesthood

column.name: text
column.value: But also bring your brothers with you, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, so that they may join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you are before the tent of the testimony.

column.name: text
column.value: And they shall perform duties for you and the duties of the whole tent, but they shall not come near the furnishings of the sanctuary and the altar, or both they and you will die.

column.name: text
column.value: They shall join you and perform the duties of the tent of meeting, for all the service of the tent; but ①an unauthorized person shall not come near you. ▷ ①Lit a stranger

column.name: text
column.value: So you shall perform the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the altar, so that there will no longer be wrath on the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I Myself have taken your ①fellow Levites from among the sons of Israel; they are a gift to you, ②dedicated to the LORD, to perform the service for the tent of meeting. ▷ ①Lit brothers the ②Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: But you and your sons with you shall attend to your priesthood for everything that concerns the altar and inside the veil, and you are to perform service. I am giving you the priesthood as a ①service that is a gift, and the ②unauthorized person who comes near shall be put to death.” ▷ ①Lit service of a gift ②Lit stranger

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Aaron, “Now behold, I Myself have put you in charge of My ①offerings, all the holy gifts of the sons of Israel I have given to you as a portion and to your sons as a permanent allotment. ▷ ①Or uplifted offerings, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: This shall be yours from the most holy gifts reserved from the fire; every offering of theirs, namely every grain offering, every sin offering, and every guilt offering, with which they shall make restitution to Me, shall be most holy for you and for your sons.

column.name: text
column.value: As the most holy gifts you shall eat it; every male shall eat it. It shall be holy to you.

column.name: text
column.value: This also is yours, the offering of their gift, that is, all the wave offerings of the sons of Israel; I have given them to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a permanent allotment. Everyone of your household who is clean may eat it.

column.name: text
column.value: All the ①best of the fresh oil and all the ②best of the fresh wine and of the grain, the first fruits of what they give to the LORD, I have given them to you. ▷ ①Lit fat ②Lit fat

column.name: text
column.value: The first ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the LORD, shall be yours; everyone of your household who is clean may eat it.

column.name: text
column.value: Everything banned from secular use in Israel shall be yours.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Every firstborn of the womb of all flesh, whether human or animal, which they offer to the LORD, shall be yours; however you must redeem the human firstborn, and the firstborn of unclean animals you shall redeem. ▷ ①Lit Everything that opens

column.name: text
column.value: As to ①their redemption price, from a month old you shall redeem them, by your assessment, five ②shekels in silver by the ③shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs. ▷ ①Lit his being redeemed ②A shekel is about 0.5 oz. or 14 gm ③A shekel is about 0.5 oz. or 14 gm

column.name: text
column.value: But the firstborn of an ox, the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy. You shall sprinkle their blood on the altar and offer up their fat in smoke as an offering by fire, for a soothing aroma to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: However, their ①meat shall be yours; it shall be yours like the breast of a wave offering and like the right thigh. ▷ ①Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: All the offerings of the holy gifts, which the sons of Israel offer to the LORD, I have given to you and your sons and your daughters with you, as a permanent allotment. It is a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD to you and your ①descendants with you.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You shall have no inheritance in their land nor own any portion among them; I am your portion and your inheritance among the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: “To the sons of Levi, behold, I have given all the tithe in Israel as an inheritance, in return for their service which they perform, the service of the tent of meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel shall not come near the tent of meeting again, or they will bring sin on themselves and die.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the Levites shall perform the service of the tent of meeting, and they shall bear their own guilt; it shall be a permanent statute throughout your generations, and among the sons of Israel they shall have no inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: For the tithe of the sons of Israel, which they offer as an offering to the LORD, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance; therefore I have said concerning them, ‘They shall have no inheritance among the sons of Israel.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Moreover, you shall speak to the Levites and say to them, ‘When you take from the sons of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then you shall present an offering from it to the LORD, a tithe of the tithe.

column.name: text
column.value: Your offering shall be credited to you like the grain from the threshing floor or the full produce from the wine vat.

column.name: text
column.value: So you shall also present an offering to the LORD from all your tithes, which you receive from the sons of Israel; and from it you shall give the LORD’S offering to Aaron the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Out of all your gifts you shall present every offering due to the LORD, from all the ①best of them, ②the sacred part from them.’ ▷ ①Lit fat ②Lit its

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall say to them, ‘When you have ①offered from it the best of it, then the rest shall be credited to the Levites like the product of the threshing floor, and like the product of the wine vat. ▷ ①Lit lifted

column.name: text
column.value: You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, for it is your compensation in return for your service in the tent of meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: And you will bring on yourselves no sin by reason of it when you have ①offered the ②best of it. But you shall not profane the sacred gifts of the sons of Israel, so that you do not die.’ ” ▷ ①Lit lifted ②Lit fat

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month; and the people stayed at Kadesh. Now Miriam died there and was buried there.

column.name: text
column.value: There was no water for the congregation, and they assembled against Moses and Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people argued with Moses and spoke, saying, “If only we had perished when our brothers perished before the LORD!

column.name: text
column.value: Why then have you brought the LORD’S assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die ①here? ▷ ①Lit there

column.name: text
column.value: Why did you make us come up from Egypt, to bring us into this wretched place? It is not a place of ①grain or figs or vines or pomegranates, nor is there water to drink!” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses and Aaron came in from the presence of the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell on their faces. And the glory of the LORD appeared to them;

column.name: text
column.value: then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Take the staff; and you and your brother Aaron assemble the congregation and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it shall yield its water. So you shall bring water for them out of the rock, and have the congregation and their livestock drink.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, just as He had commanded him;

column.name: text
column.value: and Moses and Aaron summoned the assembly in front of the rock. And he said to them, “Listen now, you rebels; shall we bring water for you out of this rock?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff; and water came out abundantly, and the congregation and their livestock drank.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Since you did not trust in Me, to treat Me as holy in the sight of the sons of Israel, for that reason you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”

column.name: text
column.value: Those were called the waters of ①Meribah, ②because the sons of Israel argued with the LORD, and He proved Himself holy among them. ▷ ①I.e., contention ②Or where

column.name: text
column.value: From Kadesh Moses then sent messengers to the king of Edom to say, “This is what your brother Israel has said: ‘You know all the hardship that has ①overtaken us; ▷ ①Lit found

column.name: text
column.value: that our fathers went down to Egypt, and we stayed in Egypt a long time, and the Egyptians treated us and our fathers badly.

column.name: text
column.value: But when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice and sent an angel, and brought us out from Egypt; now behold, we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.

column.name: text
column.value: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard; we will not even drink water from a well. We will go along the king’s road, not turning to the right or left, until we pass through your territory.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Edom, however, said to him, “You shall not pass through ①us, or I will come out with the sword against you.” ▷ ①Lit me

column.name: text
column.value: Again, the sons of Israel said to him, “We will go up by the road, and if I and my livestock do drink any of your water, then I will ①pay its price. Let me only pass through on my feet, ②nothing more.” ▷ ①Lit give ②Or no great thing

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “You shall not pass through.” And Edom came out against him with a heavy ①force and a strong hand. ▷ ①Lit people

column.name: text
column.value: So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory; then Israel turned away from him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when they set out from Kadesh, the sons of Israel, the whole congregation, came to Mount Hor.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor by the border of the land of Edom, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Aaron will be gathered to his people; for he shall not enter the land which I have given to the sons of Israel, because you rebelled against My ①command at the waters of Meribah. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar, and bring them up to Mount Hor.

column.name: text
column.value: Then strip Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar. So Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses did just as the LORD had commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.

column.name: text
column.value: And after Moses stripped Aaron of his garments and put them on his son Eleazar, Aaron died there on the mountain top. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the congregation saw that Aaron had died, the whole house of Israel wept for Aaron for thirty days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel journeyed on, and camped in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan opposite Jericho.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Balak the son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.

column.name: text
column.value: So Moab was in great fear because of the people, for they were numerous; and Moab was in dread of the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this ①horde will eat up all that is around us, as the ox eats up the grass of the field!” And Balak the son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time. ▷ ①Lit assembly

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, at Pethor, which is near the Euphrates River, in the land of the sons of his people, to call for him, saying, “Behold, a people came out of Egypt; behold, they have covered the surface of the land, and they are living opposite me.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, therefore, please come, curse this people for me since they are too ①mighty for me; perhaps I will be able to ②defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.” ▷ ①Or numerous ②Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian left with the fees for divination in their hands; and they came to Balaam and ①repeated Balak’s words to him. ▷ ①Lit spoke

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to them, “Spend the night here, and I will bring word back to you just as the LORD may speak to me.” And the leaders of Moab stayed with Balaam.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”

column.name: text
column.value: Balaam said to God, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent word to me:

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Behold, there is a people who came out of Egypt, and they cover the surface of the land; now come, curse them for me; perhaps I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them; you shall not curse the people, for they are blessed.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak’s representatives, “Go back to your land, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the representatives from Moab got up and went to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak sent representatives once again, more numerous and more distinguished than ①the previous. ▷ ①Lit these

column.name: text
column.value: They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak the son of Zippor says: ‘I beg you, let nothing keep you from coming to me;

column.name: text
column.value: for I will indeed honor you richly, and I will do whatever you tell me. Please come then, curse this people for me.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “Even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything, either small or great, contrary to the ①command of the LORD my God. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Now please, you also stay here tonight, and I will find out what else the LORD will say to me.”

column.name: text
column.value: And God came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If the men have come to call you, rise and go with them; but you shall do only the thing that I tell you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Balaam arose in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the leaders of Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: But God was angry that he was going, and the angel of the LORD took his stand in the road as an adversary against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, the donkey turned off from the road and went into the field; and Balaam struck the donkey to guide her back onto the road.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path of the vineyards, with a stone wall on this side and on that side.

column.name: text
column.value: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed herself against the wall and pressed Balaam’s foot against the wall, so he struck her again.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD went further, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn to the right or to the left.

column.name: text
column.value: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam; so Balaam was angry and struck the donkey with his staff.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Balaam said to the donkey, “It is because you have made a mockery of me! If only there had been a sword in my hand! For I would have killed you by now!”

column.name: text
column.value: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey on which you have ridden all your life to this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing such a thing to you?” And he said, “No.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed ①all the way to the ground. ▷ ①Lit and prostrated himself to his face

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out as an adversary, because your way was reckless and contrary to me.

column.name: text
column.value: But the donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away from me, I certainly would have killed you just now, and let her live.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “I have sinned, for I did not know that you were standing in the way against me. Now then, if it is displeasing to you, I will turn back.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you shall speak only the word that I ①tell you.” So Balaam went along with the representatives of Balak. ▷ ①Or speak to

column.name: text
column.value: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the city of Moab, which is on the Arnon border, ①at the extreme end of the border. ▷ ①Lit which is at

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not urgently send word to you to call for you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really unable to honor you?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Balaam said to Balak, “Behold, I have come to you now! Am I really able to speak anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that only shall I speak.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.

column.name: text
column.value: Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and the leaders who were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about in the morning that Balak took Balaam and brought him up to ①the high places of Baal, and he saw from there ②a portion of the people. ▷ ①Or Bamoth-baal ②Lit the extremity of the people

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”

column.name: text
column.value: Balak did just as Balaam had spoken, and Balak and Balaam offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps the LORD will come to meet me, and whatever He shows me I will tell you.” So he went to a bare hill.

column.name: text
column.value: Now God met with Balaam, and he said to Him, “I have set up the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD put a word in Balaam’s mouth and said, “Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he returned to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the leaders of Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: And he took up his discourse and said, “From Aram Balak has brought me, Moab’s king from the mountains of the East, saying, ‘Come, declare Jacob cursed for me, And come, curse Israel!’

column.name: text
column.value: How am I to put a curse on him upon whom God has not put a curse? And how am I to curse him whom the LORD has not cursed?

column.name: text
column.value: For I see him from the top of the rocks, And I look at him from the hills; Behold, a people that lives in isolation, And does not consider itself to be among the nations.

column.name: text
column.value: Who has counted the dust of Jacob, Or the number of the fourth part of Israel? May ①I die the death of the upright, And may my end be like his!” ▷ ①Lit my soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to put a curse on my enemies, but behold, you have actually blessed them!”

column.name: text
column.value: He replied, “Must I not be careful to speak what the LORD puts in my mouth?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place from where you may see them, although you will only see the extreme end of them and will not see all of them; and put a curse on them for me from there.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to Balak, “Stand here beside your burnt offering while I myself meet the LORD over there.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, and said, “Return to Balak, and this is what you shall speak.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he came to him, and behold, he was standing beside his burnt offering, and the leaders of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, “What has the LORD spoken?”

column.name: text
text
column.value: God is not a man, that He would lie, Nor a son of man, that He would change His mind; Has He said, and will He not do it? Or has He spoken, and will He not make it good?

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I have received a command to bless; When He has blessed, I cannot revoke it.

column.name: text
text
column.value: God brings them out of Egypt, He is for them like the horns of the wild ox.

column.name: text
column.value: For there is no magic curse against Jacob, Nor is there any divination against Israel; At the proper time it shall be said to Jacob And to Israel, what God has done!

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, a people rises like a lioness, And like a lion it raises itself; It will not lie down until it devours the prey, And drinks the blood of those slain.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Do not curse them at all nor bless them at all!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Balaam replied to Balak, “Did I not tell you, ‘ ①Whatever the LORD speaks, I must do’?” ▷ ①Lit saying, Whatever

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak said to Balaam, “Please come, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will be ①agreeable with God that you curse them for me from there.” ▷ ①Lit right in the sight of God

column.name: text
column.value: So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the ①desert. ▷ ①Or Jeshimon

column.name: text
column.value: And Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”

column.name: text
column.value: Balak did just as Balaam had said, and offered up a bull and a ram on each altar.

column.name: text
column.value: When Balaam saw that it ①pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as at other times to ②seek omens, rather he turned his ③attention toward the wilderness. ▷ ①Lit was good in the eyes of ②Lit encounter ③Lit face

column.name: text
column.value: And Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel ①camping tribe by tribe; and the Spirit of God came upon him. ▷ ①Lit dwelling

column.name: text
text
column.value: The declaration of him who hears the ①words of God, Who sees the vision of ②the Almighty, Falling down, yet having his eyes uncovered, ▷ ①Lit sayings ②Heb Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: How pleasant are your tents, Jacob, Your dwelling places, Israel!

column.name: text
column.value: Like ①valleys that stretch out, Like gardens beside a river, Like aloes planted by the LORD, Like cedars beside the waters. ▷ ①Or possibly palm trees

column.name: text
column.value: Water will flow from his buckets, And his seed will be by many waters, And his king shall be higher than Agag, And his kingdom shall be exalted.

column.name: text
column.value: God brings him out of Egypt, He is for him like the horns of the wild ox. He will devour the nations who are his adversaries, And will crush their bones, And smash them with his arrows.

column.name: text
column.value: He ①crouches, he lies down like a lion, And like a lioness, who ②dares to rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, And cursed is everyone who curses you.” ▷ ①Lit bows down ②Lit will

column.name: text
column.value: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his ①hands together; and Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times! ▷ ①Lit palms

column.name: text
column.value: So ①flee to your place now. I said I would honor you greatly, but behold, the LORD has held you back from honor.” ▷ ①Lit flee for yourself

column.name: text
column.value: And Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not in fact tell your messengers whom you had sent to me, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything contrary to the ①command of the LORD, either good or bad, of my own ②accord. What the LORD speaks, I will ③speak’? ▷ ①Lit mouth ②Lit heart ③Lit speak it

column.name: text
column.value: So now, behold, I am going to my people; come, and I will advise you of what this people will do to your people in the ①days to come.” ▷ ①Lit end of the days

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took up his discourse and said, “The declaration of Balaam the son of Beor, And the declaration of the man whose eye is opened,

column.name: text
column.value: The declaration of him who hears the ①words of God, And knows the knowledge of the ②Most High, Who sees the vision of ③the Almighty, Falling down, yet having his eyes uncovered: ▷ ①Lit sayings ②Heb Elyon ③Heb Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: I see him, but not now; I look at him, but not near; A star shall appear from Jacob, A scepter shall rise from Israel, And shall smash the ①forehead of Moab, And overcome all the sons of Sheth. ▷ ①Lit corners

column.name: text
column.value: And Edom shall be a possession, Seir, its enemies, also will be a possession, While Israel performs valiantly.

column.name: text
column.value: One from Jacob shall rule, And will eliminate the survivors from the city.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he looked at Amalek and took up his discourse and said, “Amalek was the first of the nations, But his end shall be ①destruction.” ▷ ①Lit to destruction

column.name: text
column.value: And he looked at the Kenite, and took up his discourse and said, “Your dwelling place is enduring, And your nest is set in the cliff.

column.name: text
text
column.value: Then he took up his discourse and said, “Oh, who can live unless God has ordained it?

column.name: text
text
column.value: Then Balaam arose, and he departed and returned to his place, and Balak also went on his way.

column.name: text
column.value: While Israel remained at Shittim, the people began to commit infidelity with the daughters of Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: For they invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel ①became followers of ②Baal of Peor, and the LORD was angry with Israel. ▷ ①Lit bound themselves to ②Or Baal-peor

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and ①execute them ②in broad daylight before the LORD, so that the fierce anger of the LORD may turn away from Israel.” ▷ ①Lit display them (dead) with broken limbs ②Lit in front of the sun

column.name: text
column.value: So Moses said to the judges of Israel, “Each of you kill his men who have ①become followers of ②Baal of Peor.” ▷ ①Lit bound themselves to ②Or Baal-peor

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, one of the sons of Israel came and brought to his relatives a Midianite woman, in the sight of Moses and in the sight of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from the midst of the congregation and took a spear in his hand,

column.name: text
column.value: and he went after the man of Israel into the inner room of the tent and pierced both of them, the man of Israel and the woman, through the abdomen. So the plague on the sons of Israel was brought to a halt.

column.name: text
column.value: But those who died from the plague were twenty-four thousand in number.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has averted My wrath from the sons of Israel in that he was ①jealous with My ②jealousy among them, so that I did not destroy the sons of Israel in My ③jealousy. ▷ ①Or possibly zealous; i.e., impassioned ②Or possibly anger ③Or possibly anger

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore say, ‘Behold, I am giving him My covenant of peace;

column.name: text
column.value: and it shall be for him and for his ①descendants after him, a covenant of a permanent priesthood, because he was ②jealous for his God and made atonement for the sons of Israel.’ ” ▷ ①Lit seed ②Or possibly zealous; i.e., impassioned

column.name: text
column.value: Now the name of the ①dead man of Israel who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri the son of Salu, a leader of a father’s household among the Simeonites. ▷ ①Lit killed

column.name: text
column.value: And the name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, ①who was head of the people of a father’s household in Midian. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Be hostile to the Midianites and attack them;

column.name: text
