column.value: Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, from the sons of Hobab the ①father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far away as the ②oak in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh. ▷ ①Another reading is brother-in-law ②Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: Then they told Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.

column.name: text
column.value: Sisera summoned all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the river Kishon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Deborah said to Barak, “Arise! For this is the day on which the LORD has handed Sisera over to you; ①behold, the LORD has gone out before you.” So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him. ▷ ①Lit has the LORD not gone...?

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD ①routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot. ▷ ①Lit confused

column.name: text
column.value: But Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not even one was left.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, “Turn aside, my master, turn aside to me! Do not be afraid.” So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a ①rug. ▷ ①Or blanket

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to her, “Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty.” So she opened a leather bottle of milk and gave him a drink; then she covered him.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to her, “Stand in the doorway of the tent, and it shall be if anyone comes and inquires of you, and says, ‘Is there anyone here?’ that you shall say, ‘No.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg and ①a hammer in her hand, and went secretly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went through into the ground; for he was sound asleep and exhausted. So he died. ▷ ①Lit put a hammer

column.name: text
column.value: And behold, while Barak was pursuing Sisera, Jael came out to meet him and said to him, “Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking.” So he entered ①with her, and behold, Sisera was lying dead with the tent peg in his temple. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: So God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan on that day before the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the hand of the sons of Israel pressed harder and harder upon Jabin the king of Canaan, until they had eliminated Jabin the king of Canaan.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the nations that the LORD left, to test Israel by them (that is, all the Israelites who had not ①experienced any of the wars of Canaan; ▷ ①Lit known

column.name: text
column.value: only in order that the generations of the sons of Israel might ①be taught war, ②those who had not ③experienced it previously). ▷ ①Lit know, to teach them ②Lit only those ③Lit known

column.name: text
column.value: These nations are: the five governors of the Philistines and all the Canaanites and the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as ①Lebo-hamath. ▷ ①Or the entrance of Hamath

column.name: text
column.value: They were left to test Israel by them, to find out if they would ①obey the commandments of the LORD, which He had commanded their fathers ②through Moses. ▷ ①Lit listen to ②Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites;

column.name: text
column.value: and they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the ①Asheroth. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah)

column.name: text
column.value: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, so that He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of ①Mesopotamia; and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years. ▷ ①Heb Aram-naharaim

column.name: text
column.value: But the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the sons of Israel to set them free, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. When he went to war, the LORD handed over to him Cushan-rishathaim king of ①Mesopotamia, so that ②he prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim. ▷ ①Heb Aram ②Lit his hand was strong

column.name: text
column.value: Then the land was at rest for forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And he gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek; and he went and ①defeated Israel, and they took possession of the city of the palm trees. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab for eighteen years.

column.name: text
column.value: But when the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. And the sons of Israel sent tribute by ①him to Eglon the king of Moab. ▷ ①Lit his hand

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length, and he strapped it on his right thigh under his cloak.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, when he had finished presenting the tribute, that Ehud sent away the people who had carried the tribute.

column.name: text
column.value: But he himself turned back from the idols which were at Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” And the king said, “Silence!” And all who were attending him left him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ehud came to him while he was sitting in his cool roof chamber alone. And Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.” And he got up from his seat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ehud reached out with his left hand and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.

column.name: text
column.value: The hilt of the sword also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade because he did not pull the sword out of his belly; and ①the refuse came out. ▷ ①Meaning of the Heb uncertain, but perhaps excrement

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ehud went out into the ①vestibule, and shut the doors of the roof chamber behind him, and locked them. ▷ ①Meaning uncertain

column.name: text
column.value: When he had left, ①the king’s servants came and looked, and behold, the doors of the roof chamber were locked; and they said, “Undoubtedly he is ②relieving himself in the cool room.” ▷ ①Lit his ②Lit covering his feet; a euphemism referring to a squatting position

column.name: text
column.value: So they waited ①until it would have been shameful to wait longer; but behold, he did not open the doors of the roof chamber. So they took the key and opened them, and behold, their master had fallen to the ②floor dead. ▷ ①Lit until shaming ②Lit earth

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ehud escaped while they were hesitating, and he passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.

column.name: text
column.value: And ①when he arrived, he blew the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he was ②leading them. ▷ ①Lit it happened ②Lit before them

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to them, “Pursue them, for the LORD has handed your enemies the Moabites over to you.” So they went down after him and took control of the crossing places of the Jordan opposite Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross.

column.name: text
column.value: They struck and killed about ten thousand Moabites at that time, all robust and valiant men; and no one escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land was at rest for eighty years.

column.name: text
column.value: Now after him came Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck and killed six hundred Philistines with an ①oxgoad; and he also saved Israel. ▷ ①I.e., a spiked stick for driving livestock

column.name: text
column.value: Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “For ①the leaders leading in Israel, For the people volunteering, Bless the LORD! ▷ ①Or the hair hanging free in

column.name: text
column.value: Hear, you kings; listen, you dignitaries! I myself—to the LORD, I myself will sing, I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel!

column.name: text
column.value: LORD, when You went out from Seir, When You marched from the field of Edom, The earth quaked, the heavens also dripped, The clouds also dripped water.

column.name: text
column.value: The mountains ①flowed with water at the presence of the LORD, This Sinai, at the presence of the LORD, the God of Israel. ▷ ①As in MT; LXX quaked

column.name: text
column.value: “In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, In the days of Jael, the roads ①were deserted, And travelers went by ②roundabout ways. ▷ ①Lit had ceased ②Lit twisting

column.name: text
column.value: The ①peasantry came to an end, they came to an end in Israel, Until I, Deborah, arose, Until I arose, a mother in Israel. ▷ ①Or rural dwellers

column.name: text
column.value: New gods were chosen; Then war was in the gates. Not a shield or a spear was seen Among forty thousand in Israel.

column.name: text
text
column.value: You who ride on ①white donkeys, You who sit on rich carpets, And you who travel on the road—shout in praise! ▷ ①Or tawny

column.name: text
column.value: At the sound of those who distribute water among the watering places, There they will recount the righteous deeds of the LORD, The righteous deeds for His ①peasantry in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates. ▷ ①Or rural dwellers

column.name: text
column.value: “Awake, awake, Deborah; Awake, awake, ①sing a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, son of Abinoam. ▷ ①Lit speak

column.name: text
column.value: Then survivors came down to the nobles; The people of the LORD came down to me as warriors.

column.name: text
column.value: From Ephraim those whose root is in Amalek came down, Following you, Benjamin, with your peoples; From Machir commanders came down, And from Zebulun those who wield the staff of ①office. ▷ ①Lit a scribe

column.name: text
text
column.value: Why did you sit among the ①sheepfolds, To hear the piping for the flocks? Among the divisions of Reuben There were great searchings of heart. ▷ ①Or saddlebags

column.name: text
column.value: Gilead ①remained across the Jordan; And why did Dan stay on ships? Asher sat at the seashore, And ②remained by its landings. ▷ ①Or dwelt ②Or dwelt

column.name: text
column.value: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives, And Naphtali too, on the high places of the field.

column.name: text
text
column.value: The stars fought from heaven, From their paths they fought against Sisera.

column.name: text
column.value: The torrent of Kishon swept them away, The ancient torrent, the torrent Kishon. My soul, march on with strength!

column.name: text
column.value: Then the horses’ hoofs beat From the galloping, the galloping of his mighty stallions.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Curse Meroz,’ said the angel of the LORD, ‘Utterly curse its inhabitants, Because they did not come to the help of the LORD, To the help of the LORD against the warriors.’

column.name: text
text
column.value: He asked for water, she gave him milk; In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.

column.name: text
column.value: She reached out her hand for the tent peg, And her right hand for the workmen’s hammer. Then she struck Sisera, she smashed his head; And she shattered and pierced his temple.

column.name: text
text
column.value: “Out of the window she looked and wailed, The mother of Sisera through the ①lattice, ‘Why does his chariot delay in coming? Why do the ②hoofbeats of his chariots delay?’ ▷ ①Or window ②Lit steps

column.name: text
column.value: Her wise princesses would answer her, Indeed she repeats her words to herself,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Are they not finding, are they not dividing the spoils? A concubine, two concubines for every warrior; To Sisera a spoil of dyed cloth, A spoil of dyed cloth embroidered, Dyed cloth of double embroidery on the ①neck of the plunderer?’ ▷ ①Lit necks of the spoil

column.name: text
column.value: May all Your enemies perish in this way, LORD; But may those who love Him be like the rising of the sun in its might.” And the land was at rest for forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD handed them over to Midian for seven years.

column.name: text
column.value: The ①power of Midian prevailed against Israel. Because of Midian the sons of Israel made for themselves the dens which were in the mountains and the caves and the strongholds. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: For whenever Israel had sown, the Midianites would come up with the Amalekites and the ①people of the east and ②march against them. ▷ ①Lit sons ②Lit go up against

column.name: text
column.value: So they would camp against them and destroy the produce of the earth ①as far as Gaza, and leave no sustenance in Israel, nor a sheep, ox, or donkey. ▷ ①Lit until your coming to

column.name: text
column.value: For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, they would come in like locusts in number, and both they and their camels were innumerable; and they came into the land to ruin it.

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,

column.name: text
column.value: that the LORD sent a prophet to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘It was I who brought you up from Egypt, and brought you out of the house of ①slavery. ▷ ①Lit slaves

column.name: text
column.value: And I rescued you from the hands of the Egyptians, and from the hands of all your oppressors, and I drove them out from you and gave you their land,

column.name: text
column.value: and I said to you, “I am the LORD your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live.” But you have not ①obeyed Me.’ ” ▷ ①Lit listened to My voice

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat under the ①oak that was in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, as his son Gideon was beating out wheat in the wine press in order to save it from the Midianites. ▷ ①Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: And the angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, “The LORD is with you, valiant warrior.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon said to him, “O my lord, if the LORD is with us, why then has all this happened to us? And where are all His miracles which our fathers told us about, saying, ‘Did the LORD not bring us up from Egypt?’ But now the LORD has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD ①looked at him and said, “Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?” ▷ ①Or turned toward

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to Him, “O Lord, ①how am I to save Israel? Behold, my family is the least in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father’s house.” ▷ ①Lit with what

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD said to him, “I will certainly be with you, and you will ①defeat Midian as one man.” ▷ ①Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: So ①Gideon said to Him, “If now I have found favor in Your sight, then perform for me a sign that it is You speaking with me. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Please do not depart from here until I come back to You, and bring out my offering and lay it before You.” And He said, “I will remain until you return.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon went in and prepared a young goat and unleavened bread from an ①ephah of flour; he put the meat in a basket ②and the broth in a pot, and brought them out to him under the ③oak and presented them. ▷ ①About 1 cubic foot or 0.03 cubic meters ②Lit and he put ③Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: And the angel of God said to him, “Take the meat and the unleavened bread and lay them on this rock, and pour out the broth.” And he did so.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD put out the end of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread; and fire came up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread. Then the angel of the LORD ①vanished from his sight. ▷ ①Lit departed

column.name: text
column.value: When Gideon perceived that he was the angel of the LORD, ①he said, “Oh, Lord ②GOD! For I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!” ▷ ①Lit Gideon ②Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to him, “Peace to you, do not be afraid; you shall not die.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and named it ①The LORD is Peace. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites. ▷ ①Heb Yahweh-shalom

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the same night the LORD said to him, “Take your father’s bull ①and a second bull seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal which belongs to your father, and cut down the ②Asherah that is beside it; ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbol of a female deity; also vv 26, 28, 30 ②Or even

column.name: text
column.value: and build an altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold in an orderly way, and take a second bull and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon took ten men from his servants and did as the LORD had spoken to him; and because he was too afraid of his father’s household and the men of the city to do it by day, he did it by night.

column.name: text
column.value: When the people of the city got up early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal had been torn down, and the Asherah which had been beside it had been cut down, and the second bull had been offered on the altar which had been built.

column.name: text
column.value: So they said to one another, “Who did this thing?” And when they searched and inquired, they said, “Gideon the son of Joash did this thing.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of the city said to Joash, “Bring out your son, that he may die, for he has torn down the altar of Baal, and indeed, he has cut down the Asherah which was beside it.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Joash said to all who stood against him, “Will you contend for Baal, or will you save him? Whoever will contend for him shall be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, since someone has torn down his altar!”

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore on that day he named ①Gideon Jerubbaal, that is to say, “Let Baal contend against him,” because he had torn down his altar. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the ①people of the east assembled together; and they crossed over and camped in the Valley of Jezreel. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: So the Spirit of the LORD ①covered Gideon like clothing; and he blew a trumpet, and the Abiezrites were called together to follow him. ▷ ①Lit clothed

column.name: text
column.value: And he sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they also were called together to follow him; and he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon said to God, “If You are going to save Israel ①through me, as You have spoken, ▷ ①Lit by my hand

column.name: text
column.value: behold, I am putting a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the ground, then I will know that You will save Israel ①through me, as You have spoken.” ▷ ①Lit by my hand

column.name: text
column.value: And it was so. When he got up early the next morning and wrung out the fleece, he wrung the dew from the fleece, a bowl full of water.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon said to God, “Do not let Your anger burn against me, so that I may speak only one more time; please let me put You to the test only one more time with the fleece: let it now be dry only on the fleece, and let there be dew on all the ground.”

column.name: text
column.value: And God did so that night; for it was dry only on the fleece, and dew was on all the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Ephraim said to ①Gideon, “What is this thing that you have done to us, not calling upon us when you went to fight against Midian?” And they quarreled with him vehemently. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to them, “What have I done now in comparison with you? Is the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim not better than the vintage of Abiezer?

column.name: text
column.value: God has handed over to you the leaders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what was I able to do in comparison with you?” Then their ①anger toward him subsided when he said ②that. ▷ ①Lit spirit ②Lit this thing

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon and the three hundred men who were with him came to the Jordan and crossed over, exhausted yet still pursuing.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who are ①following me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.” ▷ ①Lit at my feet

column.name: text
column.value: But the leaders of Succoth said, “ ①Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?” ▷ ①Lit Is the palm of...; i.e., are you so sure of victory that

column.name: text
column.value: So Gideon said, “For this answer, when the LORD has handed over to me Zebah and Zalmunna, I will ①thrash your ②bodies with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.” ▷ ①Or trample ②Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went up from there to ①Penuel and spoke similarly to them; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered. ▷ ①In Gen 32:30, Peniel

column.name: text
column.value: So he said also to the men of ①Penuel, “When I return safely, I will tear down this tower.” ▷ ①Lit Penuel, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their ①armies with them, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of the entire ②army of the ③people of the east; for the fallen were 120,000 ④swordsmen. ▷ ①Or camps ②Or camp ③Lit sons ④Lit men who drew the sword

column.name: text
column.value: Gideon went up by the way of those who lived in tents to the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he ①attacked the camp when the camp was unsuspecting. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and routed the entire ①army. ▷ ①Or camp

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle ①by the ascent of Heres. ▷ ①Or from

column.name: text
column.value: And he captured a youth from ①Succoth and questioned him. Then the youth wrote down for him the leaders of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men. ▷ ①Lit the men of

column.name: text
column.value: And he came to the men of Succoth and said, “Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, ‘ ①Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are weary?’ ” ▷ ①Lit Is the palm of...; i.e., are you so sure of victory

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and he ①disciplined the men of Succoth with them. ▷ ①Lit taught

column.name: text
column.value: And he tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “Where were the men whom you killed at Tabor?” But they said, “You and they were alike, each one ①resembling the son of a king.” ▷ ①Lit like the form of the sons

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if only you had let them live, I would not kill you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to Jether his firstborn, “Rise, kill them.” But the youth did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a youth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “Rise up yourself, and attack us; for as the man, so is his strength.” So Gideon arose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent amulets which were on their camels’ necks.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, “Rule over us, both you and your son, your son’s son as well, for you have saved us from the hand of Midian!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Gideon said to them, “I will not rule over you, nor shall my son rule over you; the LORD shall rule over you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet Gideon said to them, “I would ①request of you, that each of you give me ②an earring from his plunder.” (For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.) ▷ ①Lit request a request ②Or a nose ring

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “We will certainly give them to you.” So they spread out a garment, and every one of them tossed an earring there from his plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: The weight of the gold earrings that he requested was 1,700 shekels of gold, apart from the crescent amulets, the ear pendants, and the purple robes which were on the kings of Midian, and apart from the neck chains that were on their camels’ necks.

column.name: text
column.value: Gideon made it into an ephod, and placed it in his city, Ophrah; but all Israel ①committed infidelity with it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his household. ▷ ①I.e., against God

column.name: text
column.value: So Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they did not lift up their heads anymore. And the land was undisturbed for forty years in the days of Gideon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and lived in his own house.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Gideon had seventy sons who ①were his direct descendants, for he had many wives. ▷ ①Lit came from his loins

column.name: text
column.value: And his concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he ①named him Abimelech. ▷ ①Lit appointed his name

column.name: text
column.value: And Gideon the son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the sons of Israel again ①committed infidelity with the Baals, and made Baal-berith their god. ▷ ①I.e., against God

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had saved them from the hands of all their enemies on every side;

column.name: text
column.value: nor did they show kindness to the household of Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) in accordance with all the good that he had done for Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abimelech the son of ①Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother’s relatives, and spoke to them and to the entire family of the household of his mother’s father, saying, ▷ ①I.e., Gideon

column.name: text
column.value: “Speak, now, in the hearing of all the ①leaders of Shechem, ‘Which is better for you: for seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, to rule over you, or for one man to rule over you?’ Also, remember that I am your bone and your flesh.” ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: So his mother’s relatives spoke all these words on his behalf in the hearing of all the ①leaders of Shechem; and ②they were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our relative.” ▷ ①Or landowners ②Lit their hearts inclined after

column.name: text
column.value: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-berith, with which Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, and they followed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went to his father’s house in Ophrah and killed his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, ①on one stone. But Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, because he hid himself. ▷ ①Perhaps a mass human sacrifice

column.name: text
column.value: All the ①leaders of Shechem and all ②Beth-millo assembled together, and they went and made Abimelech king, by the ③oak of the memorial stone which was in Shechem. ▷ ①Or landowners ②Or the house of Millo ③Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: Now when they told Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and raised his voice and called out. And he said to them, “Listen to me, you ①leaders of Shechem, that God may listen to you. ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: Once the trees went to anoint a king over them, and they said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us!’

column.name: text
column.value: But the olive tree said to them, ‘Shall I give up my fatness with ①which God and mankind are honored, and go to wave over the trees?’ ▷ ①Lit which by me

column.name: text
column.value: Then the trees said to the fig tree, ‘You, come, reign over us!’

column.name: text
column.value: But the fig tree said to them, ‘Shall I give up my sweetness and my good ①fruit, and go to wave over the trees?’ ▷ ①Lit produce

column.name: text
column.value: Then the trees said to the vine, ‘You, come, reign over us!’

column.name: text
column.value: But the vine said to them, ‘Shall I give up my new wine, which cheers God and mankind, and go to wave over the trees?’

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘You, come, reign over us!’

column.name: text
column.value: And the bramble said to the trees, ‘If you ①really are anointing me as king over you, come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, may fire come out of the bramble and consume the cedars of Lebanon.’ ▷ ①Or sincerely

column.name: text
column.value: “Now then, if you have acted with ①honesty and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and ②have dealt with him ③as he deserved— ▷ ①Or sincerity ②Lit if you have ③Lit according to the accomplishment of his hands

column.name: text
column.value: for my father fought for you, and ①risked his life and saved you from the hand of Midian; ▷ ①Lit threw his soul away

column.name: text
column.value: but in fact you have risen against my father’s house today and have killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his female slave, king over the ①leaders of Shechem, because he is your relative— ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: so if you have acted with ①honesty and integrity toward Jerubbaal and his house this day, be joyful about Abimelech, and may he also be joyful about you. ▷ ①Or sincerity

column.name: text
column.value: But if not, may fire come out of Abimelech and consume the ①leaders of Shechem and ②Beth-millo; and may fire come out of the ③leaders of Shechem and from ④Beth-millo, and consume Abimelech.” ▷ ①Or landowners ②Or the house of Millo ③Or landowners ④Or the house of Millo

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jotham escaped and fled, and went to Beer; and he stayed there because of his brother Abimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the ①leaders of Shechem; and the ②leaders of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech, ▷ ①Or landowners ②Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: so that the violence ①done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come, and the responsibility for their blood would be placed on their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and on the ②leaders of Shechem, who ③encouraged him to kill his brothers. ▷ ①Lit of the seventy ②Or landowners ③Lit strengthened his hands

column.name: text
column.value: The ①leaders of Shechem set up men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed everyone who would pass by them on the road; and it was reported to Abimelech. ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: Now Gaal the son of Ebed came with his relatives, and crossed over into Shechem; and the ①leaders of Shechem trusted him. ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: So they went out to the field and gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trampled them, and held a festival; and they went into the house of their god, and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gaal the son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is Zebul not his governor? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem; but why should we serve him?

column.name: text
column.value: ①If only this people were under my authority! Then I would do away with Abimelech.” And he said to Abimelech, “Enlarge your army and come out!” ▷ ①Lit And who will hand this people over to me

column.name: text
column.value: When Zebul the leader of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.

column.name: text
column.value: So using deception, he successfully sent messengers to Abimelech, saying, “Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem; and behold, they are ①stirring up the city against you. ▷ ①Or besieging

column.name: text
column.value: So now, arise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, you shall rise early and attack the city; and behold, when he and the people who are with him come out against you, you shall do to them ①whatever you can.” ▷ ①Lit as your hand finds

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech and all the people who were with him got up at night, and lay in wait against Shechem, in four ①units. ▷ ①Lit heads

column.name: text
column.value: Now Gaal the son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate; and Abimelech and the people who were with him arose from the ambush.

column.name: text
column.value: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “ ①Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains.” But Zebul said to him, “You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as if they were people.” ▷ ①Lit Behold

column.name: text
column.value: And Gaal spoke yet again and said, “Look, people are coming down from the ①highest part of the land, and one ②unit is coming by way of ③the diviners’ ④oak.” ▷ ①Lit center ②Lit head ③Heb Elon-meonenim ④Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zebul said to him, “Where then is your ①boasting with which you said, ‘Who is Abimelech that we should serve him?’ Is this not the people whom you rejected? Go out now and fight them!” ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: So Gaal went out ①in the sight of the ②leaders of Shechem and fought Abimelech. ▷ ①Or at the head of ②Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: But Abimelech chased him, and he fled from him; and many fell wounded up to the entrance of the gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech stayed in Arumah, but Zebul drove out Gaal and his relatives so that they could not stay in Shechem.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about the next day, that the people went out to the field, and it was reported to Abimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: So he took ①his people and divided them into three ②units, and lay in wait in the field; when he looked and ③saw the people coming out from the city, he ④attacked them and killed them. ▷ ①Lit the ②Lit heads ③Lit behold, the ④Lit rose against

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech and the ①company who was with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the city gate; the other two ②companies then attacked all who were in the field and killed them. ▷ ①Lit heads ②Lit heads

column.name: text
column.value: Abimelech fought against the city that whole day, and he captured the city and killed the people who were in it; then he tore down the city and sowed it with salt.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the ①leaders of the tower of Shechem heard about it, they entered the inner chamber of the ②temple of El-berith. ▷ ①Or landowners ②Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: And it was reported to Abimelech that all the ①leaders of the tower of Shechem were gathered together. ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took ①an axe in his hand and cut down a branch from the trees, and lifted it and put it on his shoulder. Then he said to the people who were with him, “What you saw me do, hurry and do ②likewise.” ▷ ①Lit the axes ②Lit like me

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people also cut down, each one, his branch and followed Abimelech, and put them on top of the inner chamber and set the inner chamber on fire over those inside, so that all the people of the tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, and he camped against Thebez and captured it.

column.name: text
column.value: But there was a strong tower in the center of the city, and all the men and women with all the ①leaders of the city fled there and shut themselves in; and they went up on the roof of the tower. ▷ ①Or landowners

column.name: text
column.value: So Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and approached the entrance of the tower to burn it down with fire.

column.name: text
column.value: But a woman threw an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, crushing his skull.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called quickly to the young man, his armor bearer, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, so that it will not be said of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ ” So ①the young man pierced him through, and he died. ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, each left for his ①home. ▷ ①Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: So God repaid the wickedness of Abimelech, which he had done to his father in killing his seventy brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: God also returned all the wickedness of the men of Shechem on their heads, and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came ①upon them. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: Now after Abimelech died, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, rose up to save Israel; and he lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: He judged Israel for twenty-three years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.

column.name: text
column.value: After him, Jair the Gileadite rose up and judged Israel for twenty-two years.

column.name: text
column.value: And he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys, and they had thirty cities ①in the land of Gilead that are called ②Havvoth-jair to this day. ▷ ①Lit which are in ②I.e., the towns of Jair

column.name: text
column.value: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the sons of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; so they abandoned the LORD and did not serve Him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the sons of Ammon.

column.name: text
column.value: And they ①afflicted and oppressed the sons of Israel ②that year; for eighteen years they oppressed all the sons of Israel who were beyond the Jordan, ③in Gilead in the land of the Amorites. ▷ ①Lit destroyed ②Lit in that ③Lit which is in

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight also against Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was in great difficulty.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, “We have sinned against You, for indeed, we have abandoned our God and served the Baals.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to the sons of Israel, “Did I not save you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the sons of Ammon, and the Philistines?

column.name: text
column.value: And when the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites oppressed you, you cried out to Me, and I saved you from their hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet you abandoned Me and served other gods; therefore I will no longer save you.

column.name: text
column.value: Go and cry out to the gods which you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel said to the LORD, “We have sinned, do to us whatever ①seems good to You; only please save us this day.” ▷ ①Lit the good in Your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: So they removed the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD; and ①He could no longer endure the misery of Israel. ▷ ①Lit His soul became impatient with the misery

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Ammon were summoned, and they camped in Gilead. And the sons of Israel gathered together and camped in Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the sons of Ammon? He shall become head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men of Ephraim were summoned, and they crossed ①to Zaphon; and they said to Jephthah, “Why did you cross over to fight against the sons of Ammon without calling us to go with you? We will burn your house down on you!” ▷ ①Or northward

column.name: text
column.value: So Jephthah said to them, “I and my people were in a major dispute with the sons of Ammon; and I did call you, but you did not save me from their hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When I saw that you were no deliverer, I ①took my life in my hands and crossed over against the sons of Ammon, and the LORD handed them over to me. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?” ▷ ①Lit put my soul in my palm

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim; and the men of Gilead ①defeated Ephraim, because they said, “You are survivors of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasseh.” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And the Gileadites took control of the crossing places of the Jordan opposite Ephraim. And it happened whenever any of the survivors of Ephraim said, “Let me cross over,” that the men of Gilead would say to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he said, “No,”

column.name: text
column.value: then they would say to him, “Just say, ‘Shibboleth.’ ” But he said, “Sibboleth,” for he was not ①prepared to ②pronounce it correctly. Then they seized him and slaughtered him at the crossing places of the Jordan. So at that time forty-two thousand from Ephraim fell. ▷ ①Some Heb mss read able to ②Lit speak

column.name: text
column.value: Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel after him.

column.name: text
column.value: He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters whom he ①gave in marriage outside the family, and he brought in thirty daughters from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel for seven years. ▷ ①Lit sent outside

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel after him; he judged Israel for ten years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel after him.

column.name: text
column.value: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys; and he judged Israel for eight years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jerubbaal (that is, Gideon) and all the people who were with him got up early, and camped beside ①the spring of Harod; and the camp of Midian was on the north side of ②them by the hill of Moreh in the valley. ▷ ①Or En-Harod ②Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Gideon, “The people who are with you are too many for Me to hand Midian over to them, otherwise Israel would ①become boastful, saying, ‘My own ②power has saved me.’ ▷ ①Lit boast against me ②Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore come, proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is afraid and worried, is to return and leave Mount Gilead.’ ” So twenty-two thousand from the people returned, but ten thousand remained.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Gideon, “The people are still too many; bring them down to the water and I will test them for you there. So it shall be that he of whom I say to you, ‘This one shall go with you,’ he shall go with you; but everyone of whom I say to you, ‘This one shall not go with you,’ he shall not go.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he brought the people down to the water. Then the LORD said to Gideon, “You shall put everyone who laps the water with his tongue as a dog laps ①in one group, and everyone who kneels down to drink in another.” ▷ ①Lit by himself

column.name: text
column.value: Now the number of those who lapped, ①putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people kneeled down to drink water. ▷ ①Lit with their

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Gideon, “I will save you with the three hundred men who lapped, and will hand the Midianites over to you; so have all the other people go, each man to his ①home.” ▷ ①Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: So ①the three hundred men took the people’s provisions and their trumpets in their hands. And ②Gideon dismissed all the other men of Israel, each to his tent, but retained the three hundred men; and the camp of Midian was below him in the valley. ▷ ①Lit they took ②Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the same night it came about that the LORD said to him, “Arise, go down against the camp, for I have handed it over to you.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you are afraid to go down, go with Purah your servant down to the camp,

column.name: text
column.value: so that you will hear what they say; and afterward ①you will have the courage to go down against the camp.” So he went down with Purah his servant to the ②outposts of the army that was in the camp. ▷ ①Lit your hand will be strengthened ②Lit extremity of the battle formation

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Midianites, the Amalekites, and all the ①people of the east were lying in the valley as numerous as locusts; and their camels were without number, as numerous as the sand on the seashore. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: When Gideon came, behold, a man was relating a dream to his friend. And he said, “Behold, I ①had a dream; ②a loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian, and it came to the tent and struck it so that it fell, and turned it ③upside down so that the tent collapsed.” ▷ ①Lit dreamed ②Lit and behold, a loaf ③Lit upward

column.name: text
column.value: And his friend replied, “This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel; God has handed over to him Midian and all the camp.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Gideon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed in worship. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, “Arise, for the LORD has handed over to you the camp of Midian!”

column.name: text
column.value: And he divided the three hundred men into three ①units, and he put trumpets and empty pitchers into the hands of all of them, with torches inside the pitchers. ▷ ①Lit heads

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to them, “Look at me and do likewise. And behold, when I come to the outskirts of the camp, ①do as I do. ▷ ①Lit it shall come about that just as I do, so you shall do

column.name: text
column.value: When I and all who are with me blow the trumpet, then you also blow the trumpets around the entire camp and say, ‘For the LORD and for Gideon!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the outskirts of the camp at the beginning of the middle night watch, when they had just posted the watch; and they blew the trumpets and smashed the pitchers that were in their hands.

column.name: text
column.value: When the three ①units blew the trumpets and broke the pitchers, they held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands for blowing, and shouted, “A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!” ▷ ①Lit heads

column.name: text
column.value: And each stood in his place around the camp; and all the ①army ran, crying out as they fled. ▷ ①Or camp

column.name: text
column.value: And when they blew the three hundred trumpets, the LORD set the sword of one against another even throughout the entire ①army; and the ②army fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath. ▷ ①Or camp ②Or camp

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Israel were summoned from Naphtali, Asher, and all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down ①against Midian and take control of the waters ahead of them, as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan.” So all the men of Ephraim were summoned, and they took control of the waters as far as Beth-barah and the Jordan. ▷ ①Lit to meet

column.name: text
column.value: And they captured the two leaders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, and they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and they killed Zeeb at the wine press of Zeeb, while they pursued Midian; and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon from across the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD handed them over to the Philistines for forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was a man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was infertile and had not given birth to any children.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, “Behold now, you are infertile and have not given birth; but you will conceive and give birth to a son.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, be careful not to drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any ①unclean thing. ▷ ①I.e., ritually unclean

column.name: text
column.value: For behold, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and no razor shall come upon his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb; and he will begin to save Israel from the hands of the Philistines.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the angel of God, very awesome. So I did not ask him where he came from, nor did he tell me his name.

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall conceive and give birth to a son, and now you shall not drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any ①unclean thing, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’ ” ▷ ①I.e., ritually unclean

column.name: text
column.value: Then Manoah pleaded with the LORD and said, “Lord, please let the man of God whom You have sent come to us again so that he may teach us what we are to do for the boy who is to be born.”

column.name: text
column.value: And God listened to the voice of Manoah; and the angel of God came again to the woman as she was sitting in the field, but Manoah her husband was not with her.

column.name: text
column.value: So the woman hurried and ran, and told her ①husband, “Behold, the man who ②came the other day has appeared to me!” ▷ ①Lit husband, and said to him ②Lit came to me

column.name: text
column.value: So Manoah got up and followed his wife, and when he came to the man he said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to the woman?” And he said, “I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Manoah said, “Now when your words ①are fulfilled, what shall be the boy’s way of life and his vocation?” ▷ ①Lit come

column.name: text
column.value: And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, “The woman shall pay attention ①to all that I said. ▷ ①Lit from

column.name: text
column.value: She shall not eat anything that comes from the vine nor drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing; she shall keep all that I commanded.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “Please let us detain you so that we may prepare a young goat for you.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I will not eat your ①food, but if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD.” For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, “What is your name, so that when your words ①are fulfilled, we may honor you?” ▷ ①Lit come

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD said to him, “Why do you ask my name, for it is ①wonderful?” ▷ ①I.e., incomprehensible

column.name: text
column.value: So Manoah took the young goat along with the grain offering and offered it on the rock to the LORD; and He performed wonders while Manoah and his wife looked on.

column.name: text
column.value: For it came about when the flame went up from the altar toward heaven, that the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. When Manoah and his wife saw this, they fell on their faces to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the angel of the LORD did not appear to Manoah or his wife again. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So Manoah said to his wife, “We will certainly die, for we have seen God.”

column.name: text
column.value: But his wife said to him, “If the LORD had desired to kill us, He would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hands, nor would He have shown us all these things, nor would He have let us hear things like this at this time.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the woman gave birth to a son, and named him Samson; and the child grew up and the LORD blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him when he was in ①Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. ▷ ①I.e., the camp of Dan

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: So he came ①back and told his father and ②mother, “I saw a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines; so now, get her for me as a wife.” ▷ ①Lit up ②Lit mother, and said,

column.name: text
column.value: But his father and his mother said to him, “Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives, or among all ①our people, that you go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” Yet Samson said to his father, “Get her for me, because she is right ②for me.” ▷ ①Lit my ②Lit in my eyes

column.name: text
column.value: However, his father and mother did not know that this was of the LORD, for He was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. And at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother, and came as far as the vineyards of Timnah; and behold, a young lion came roaring toward him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, so that he tore it apart as one tears apart a young goat, though he had nothing in his hand; but he did not tell his father or mother what he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: So he went down and talked to the woman; and she ①looked pleasing to Samson. ▷ ①Lit was right in Samson’s eyes

column.name: text
column.value: When he returned later to take her, he turned aside to look at the carcass of the lion; and behold, a swarm of bees and honey were in the body of the lion.

column.name: text
column.value: So he took out ①the honey on his ②hands and went on, eating as he went. When he came to his father and mother, he gave some to them and they ate it; but he did not tell them that he had took the honey out of the body of the lion. ▷ ①Lit it ②Lit palms

column.name: text
column.value: Then his father went down to the woman; and Samson held a feast there, for the young men customarily did this.

column.name: text
column.value: When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson said to them, “Let me now propose a riddle for you; if you actually tell me ①the answer within the seven days of the feast, and solve it, then I will give you thirty linen wraps and thirty outfits of clothes. ▷ ①Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: But if you are unable to tell me, then you shall give me thirty linen wraps and thirty outfits of clothes.” And they said to him, “Propose your riddle, so that we may hear it.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to them, “Out of the eater came something to eat, And out of the strong came something sweet.” But they could not tell the answer to the riddle in three days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about on the ①fourth day that they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband, so that he will tell us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us to impoverish us? Is this not so?” ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT seventh

column.name: text
column.value: So Samson’s wife wept in front of him and said, “You only hate me, and you do not love me; you have proposed a riddle to the sons of my people, and have not told it to me.” And he said to her, “Behold, I have not told it to my father or mother; so should I tell you?”

column.name: text
column.value: However she wept before him for seven days while their feast lasted. And on the seventh day he told her because she pressed him so hard. She then told the riddle to the sons of her people.

column.name: text
column.value: So the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” And he said to them, “If you had not plowed with my heifer, You would not have found out my riddle.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and killed thirty men of them and took what they were wearing and gave the outfits of clothes to those who told the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: But Samson’s wife was given to his companion who had been his ①friend. ▷ ①Or best man

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a ①valiant warrior, but he was the son of a prostitute. And Gilead had fathered Jephthah. ▷ ①Or mighty man of valor

column.name: text
column.value: Gilead’s wife bore him sons; and when his wife’s sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, “You shall not have an inheritance in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob; and worthless men gathered ①around Jephthah, and they went ②wherever he did. ▷ ①Lit to ②Lit out with him

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, after a while, that the sons of Ammon fought against Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: When the sons of Ammon fought against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from the land of Tob;

column.name: text
column.value: and they said to Jephthah, “Come and be our leader, that we may fight against the sons of Ammon.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Did you not hate me and drive me from my father’s house? So why have you come to me now when you are in trouble?”

column.name: text
column.value: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “For this reason we have now returned to you, that you may go with us and fight the sons of Ammon, and become our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me back to fight against the sons of Ammon and the LORD gives them up ①to me, will I become your head?” ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “The LORD is ①witness between us; be assured we will do ②as you have said.” ▷ ①Lit listener ②Lit according to your word

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and leader over them; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, “What conflict do you and I have, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthah, “It is because Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and the Jordan; so return them peaceably now.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jephthah sent messengers once again to the king of the sons of Ammon,

column.name: text
column.value: and they said to him, “This is what Jephthah says: ‘Israel did not take the land of Moab nor the land of the sons of Ammon.

column.name: text
column.value: For when they came up from Egypt, and Israel went through the wilderness to the ①Red Sea, and came to Kadesh, ▷ ①Lit Sea of Reeds

column.name: text
column.value: then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, “Please let us pass through your land”; but the king of Edom would not listen. And they also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel remained at Kadesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they went through the wilderness and around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east side of the land of Moab, and they camped beyond the Arnon; but they did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.

column.name: text
column.value: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, “Please let us pass through your land to our place.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; so Sihon gathered all his people and camped in Jahaz, and fought with Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD, the God of Israel, handed Sihon and all his people over to Israel, and they ①defeated them; so Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: So they possessed all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: And now the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites from His people Israel; so should you possess it?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you not possess what Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So whatever the LORD our God has dispossessed before us, we will possess it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, are you any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

column.name: text
column.value: While Israel was living in Heshbon and its villages, and in Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities that are on the banks of the Arnon, three hundred years, why did you not recover them within that time?

column.name: text
column.value: So I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by making war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But the king of the sons of Ammon ①disregarded the message which Jephthah sent him. ▷ ①Lit did not listen to the words

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh; then he passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he went on to the sons of Ammon.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD and said, “If You will indeed hand over to me the sons of Ammon,

column.name: text
column.value: then whatever comes out the doors of my house to meet me when I return ①safely from the sons of Ammon, it shall be the LORD’S, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering.” ▷ ①Or with success; lit in well-being

column.name: text
column.value: So Jephthah crossed over to the sons of Ammon to fight against them; and the LORD handed them over to him.

column.name: text
column.value: He ①inflicted a very great defeat on them from Aroer ②to the entrance of Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-keramim. So the sons of Ammon were subdued before the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Lit struck a...blow ②Lit even until you are coming to

column.name: text
column.value: But Jephthah came to his house at Mizpah, and behold, his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dancing. And she was his one and only child; besides her he had no son or daughter.

column.name: text
column.value: So when he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, “Oh, my daughter! You have brought me disaster, and you are among those who trouble me; for I have ①given my word to the LORD, and I cannot take it back.” ▷ ①Lit opened my mouth wide

column.name: text
column.value: So she said to him, “My father, you have ①given your word to the LORD; do to me just as ②you have said, since the LORD has brought you vengeance on your enemies, the sons of Ammon.” ▷ ①Lit opened your mouth wide ②Lit has gone out of your mouth

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her father, “Let this thing be done for me; allow me two months, so that I may ①go to the mountains and weep because of my virginity, I and my friends.” ▷ ①Lit go and go down on

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Go.” So he let her go for two months; and she left with her friends, and wept on the mountains because of her virginity.

column.name: text
column.value: And at the end of two months she returned to her father, who did to her ①what he had vowed; and she ②had no relations with a man. And it became a custom in Israel, ▷ ①Lit his vow which he had vowed ②Lit knew no man

column.name: text
column.value: that the ①daughters of Israel went annually to ②commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days in the year. ▷ ①I.e., women ②Lit recount; some ancient versions, lament

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samson went to Gaza and saw a prostitute there, and had relations with her.

column.name: text
column.value: When it was reported to the Gazites, saying, “Samson has come here,” they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city. And they kept silent all night, saying, “Let’s wait until the morning light, then we will kill him.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samson lay asleep until midnight, and at midnight he got up and took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two doorposts, and pulled them up along with the bars; then he put them on his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of the mountain which is opposite Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: After this it came about that he was in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

column.name: text
column.value: So the governors of the Philistines came up to her and said to her, “Entice him, and see where his great strength lies and ①how we can overpower him so that we may bind him to humble him. Then we will each give you 1,100 pieces of silver.” ▷ ①Lit by what

column.name: text
column.value: So Delilah said to Samson, “Please tell me where your great strength lies, and ①how you can be bound to humble you.” ▷ ①Lit by what

column.name: text
column.value: And Samson said to her, “If they bind me with seven fresh ①animal tendons that have not been dried, then I will become weak and be like any other man.” ▷ ①I.e., of a butchered animal, that shrink and hold when drying

column.name: text
column.value: Then the governors of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh ①animal tendons that had not been dried, and she bound him with them. ▷ ①See note v 7

column.name: text
column.value: Now she had men prepared for an ambush in an inner room. And she said to him, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” But he tore the tendons to pieces just like a thread of flax is torn apart when it ①comes too close to fire. So his strength was not discovered. ▷ ①Lit smells

column.name: text
column.value: Then Delilah said to Samson, “Behold, you have toyed with me and told me lies; now please tell me ①how you may be bound.” ▷ ①Lit by what

column.name: text
column.value: Then He said to her, “If they bind me tightly with new ropes ①which have not been used, then I will become weak and be like any other man.” ▷ ①Lit with which work has not been done

column.name: text
column.value: So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them and said to him, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” For the men in the ambush were waiting in the inner room. But he tore ①the ropes from his arms like thread. ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: Then Delilah said to Samson, “Up to now you have toyed with me and told me lies; tell me ①how you may be bound.” And he said to her, “If you weave the seven locks of my ②hair with the ③web ④[and fasten it with the pin, then I will be weak like any other man.” ▷ ①Lit by what ②Lit head ③I.e., in weaving, the warp of a loom ④The passage in brackets is found in LXX but not in any Heb mss

column.name: text
column.value: So while he slept, Delilah wove the seven locks of his ①hair with the web]. And she fastened it with the pin and said to him, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” But he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom and the web. ▷ ①Lit head

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me? You have toyed with me these three times and have not told me where your great strength is.”

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, when she pressed him daily with her words and urged him, that his soul was ①annoyed to death. ▷ ①Lit impatient to the point of

column.name: text
column.value: So he told her all that was in his heart and said to her, “A razor has never come on my head, for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother’s womb. If I am shaved, then my strength will leave me and I will become weak and be like any other man.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Delilah saw that he had told her all that was in his heart, she sent word and called the governors of the Philistines, saying, “Come up once more, for he has told me all that is in his heart.” Then the governors of the Philistines came up to her and brought up the money in their hands.

column.name: text
column.value: And she made him sleep on her knees, and called for a man and had him shave off the seven locks of his head. Then she began to humble him, and his strength left him.

column.name: text
column.value: She said, “The Philistines are upon you, Samson!” And he awoke from his sleep and said, “I will go out as at other times and shake myself free.” But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza and restrained him with bronze chains, and he became a grinder in the prison.

column.name: text
column.value: However, the hair of his head began to grow again after it was shaved off.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the governors of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to celebrate, for they said, “Our god has handed Samson our enemy over to us.”

column.name: text
column.value: When the people saw him, they praised their god, for they said, “Our god has handed our enemy over to us, Even the destroyer of our country, Who has killed many of us.”

column.name: text
column.value: It so happened when ①they were in high spirits, that they said, “Call for Samson, that he may amuse us.” So they called for Samson from the prison, and he ②entertained them. And they made him stand between the pillars. ▷ ①Lit their heart was pleasant ②Lit made sport before them

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson said to the boy who was holding his hand, “ ①Let me feel the pillars on which the house rests, so that I may lean against them.” ▷ ①Or Let go of me, and let me feel

column.name: text
column.value: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the governors of the Philistines were there. And about three thousand men and women were on the roof looking on while Samson was entertaining them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson called to the LORD and said, “Lord ①GOD, please remember me and please strengthen me just this time, O God, that I may at once take vengeance on the Philistines for my two eyes.” ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house rested, and braced himself against them, the one with his right hand and the other with his left.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samson said, “Let ①me die with the Philistines!” And he pushed outwards powerfully, so that the house fell on the governors and all the people who were in it. And the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those whom he killed during his lifetime. ▷ ①Lit my soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then his brothers and all his father’s household came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah. So he had judged Israel for twenty years.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a man of the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his mother, “The 1,100 pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse and also spoke it in my hearing, behold, the silver is with me; I took it.” And his mother said, “Blessed be my son by the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: He then returned the 1,100 pieces of silver to his mother, and his mother said, “I wholly consecrate the silver from my hand to the LORD for my son to make a carved image and a cast metal image; so now I will return ①them to you.” ▷ ①Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: So when he returned the silver to his mother, his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to the silversmith, who made ①them into a carved image and a cast metal image, and ②they were in the house of Micah. ▷ ①Lit it ②Lit it was

column.name: text
column.value: And the man Micah had a ①shrine and he made an ephod and ②household idols, and ③consecrated one of his sons, so that he might become his priest. ▷ ①Lit house of gods ②Heb teraphim ③Lit filled the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the family of Judah, who was a Levite; and he was ①staying there. ▷ ①Or sojourning

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man left the city, Bethlehem in Judah, to ①stay wherever he would find a place; and as he made his journey, he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah. ▷ ①Or sojourn

column.name: text
column.value: Micah said to him, “Where do you come from?” And he said to him, “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to ①stay wherever I may find a place.” ▷ ①Or sojourn

column.name: text
column.value: Micah then said to him, “Stay with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, a supply of clothing, and your sustenance.” So the Levite went in.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levite agreed to live with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.

column.name: text
column.value: So Micah ①consecrated the Levite, and the young man became his priest and ②lived in the house of Micah. ▷ ①Lit filled the hand of ②Lit was

column.name: text
column.value: Then Micah said, “Now I know that the LORD will prosper me, because I have a Levite as a priest.”

column.name: text
column.value: But after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat, and said, “I will go in to my wife in her room.” But her father did not let him enter.

column.name: text
column.value: Her father said, “I really thought that you hated her intensely; so I gave her to your companion. Is her younger sister not ①more beautiful than she? Please let her be yours ②instead.” ▷ ①Lit better ②Lit instead of her

column.name: text
column.value: Samson then said to them, “This time I will have been blameless regarding the Philistines when I do them harm.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Samson went and caught three hundred jackals, and took torches, and turned the jackals tail to tail and put one torch in the middle between two tails.

column.name: text
