column.value: When he had set fire to the torches, he released the jackals into the standing grain of the Philistines and set fire to both the bundled heaps and the standing grain, along with the vineyards and olive groves.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistines said, “Who did this?” And some said, “Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because ①he took his wife and gave her to his companion.” So the Philistines came up and burned her and her father to death with fire. ▷ ①I.e., the Timnite

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samson said to them, “If this is how you act, I will certainly take revenge on you, and only after that will I stop.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he struck them ①ruthlessly with a great slaughter; and afterward he went down and lived in the cleft of the rock of Etam. ▷ ①Lit thigh on loin

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistines went up and camped in Judah, and spread out in Lehi.

column.name: text
column.value: So the men of Judah said, “Why have you come up against us?” And they said, “We have come up to bind Samson in order to do to him as he did to us.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, “Do you not know that the Philistines are rulers over us? What then is this that you have done to us?” And he said to them, “Just as they did to me, so I have done to them.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to him, “We have come down to bind you so that we may hand you over to the Philistines.” And Samson said to them, “Swear to me that you will not ①kill me.” ▷ ①Lit fall upon me yourselves

column.name: text
column.value: So they said to ①him, “No, but we will bind you tightly and give you into their hands; but we certainly will not kill you.” Then they bound him with two new ropes, and brought him up from the rock. ▷ ①Lit him, saying

column.name: text
column.value: When he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they met him. And the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon him so that the ropes that were on his arms were like flax that has burned with fire, and his restraints ①dropped from his hands. ▷ ①Lit melted

column.name: text
column.value: Then he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, so he reached out with his hand and took it, and ①killed a thousand men with it. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And Samson said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, ①Heaps upon heaps, With the jawbone of a donkey I have ②killed a thousand men.” ▷ ①Lit Heap, two heaps; Heb is same root as donkey ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand; and he named that place ①Ramath-lehi. ▷ ①I.e., the high place of the jawbone

column.name: text
column.value: Then he became very thirsty, and he called to the LORD and said, “You have ①handed this great ②victory over to Your servant, and now ③am I to die of thirst ④and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised?” ▷ ①Or given...victory by the hand of Your ②Lit deliverance ③Or I shall...uncircumcised ④Or or

column.name: text
column.value: But God split the hollow place that is in Lehi so that water came out of it. When he drank, his ①strength returned and he revived. Therefore he named it ②En-hakkore, which is in Lehi to this day. ▷ ①Lit spirit ②I.e., the spring of him who called

column.name: text
column.value: So he judged Israel for twenty years in the days of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days there was no king of Israel; and in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance for themselves to live in, for until that day ①an inheritance had not ②been allotted to them as a possession among the tribes of Israel. ▷ ①Lit it ②Lit fallen

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Dan sent from their family five men out of their whole number, ①valiant men from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it; and they said to them, “Go, explore the land.” And they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and stayed overnight there. ▷ ①Lit men, sons of valor

column.name: text
column.value: When they were near the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young man, the Levite; and they turned aside there and said to him, “Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what do you have here?”

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, “Micah has done this and that for me, and he has hired me and I have become his priest.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to him, “Inquire of God, please, that we may know whether our way on which we are going will be successful.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the priest said to them, “Go in peace; your way in which you are going ①has the LORD’S approval.” ▷ ①Lit is before the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: So the five men departed and came to Laish, and saw the people who were in it living in security, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting; for there was no ①oppressive ruler humiliating them for anything in the land, and they were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone. ▷ ①Or oppressive conqueror; lit possessor of oppression

column.name: text
column.value: When they came back to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, their brothers said to them, “What do you say?”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “Arise, and let’s go up against them; for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good. And will you ①sit still? Do not hesitate to go, to enter, to take possession of the land. ▷ ①Lit be

column.name: text
column.value: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people with a spacious land; for God has handed it over to you, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then from the family of the Danites, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men armed with weapons of war set out.

column.name: text
column.value: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they called that place ①Mahaneh-dan to this day; behold, it is ②west of Kiriath-jearim. ▷ ①I.e., the camp of Dan ②Lit behind

column.name: text
column.value: And they passed from there to the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the five men who went to spy out the country of Laish ①said to their kinsmen, “Do you know that there are in these houses an ephod and ②household idols, and a carved image and a cast metal image? Now then, consider what you should do.” ▷ ①Lit answered and said ②Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young man, the Levite, to the house of Micah, and asked ①him how he was doing. ▷ ①Lit his well-being

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, the six hundred men armed with their weapons of war, who were of the sons of Dan, were positioned at the entrance of the gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the five men who went to spy out the land went up and entered there; they took the carved image, the ephod, the ①household idols, and the cast metal image, while the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: When these men entered Micah’s house and took the carved image, the ephod, ①household idols, and the cast metal image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?” ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “Be silent, put your hand over your mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be a priest to the house of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a family in Israel?”

column.name: text
column.value: The priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the ①household idols, and the carved image, and went among the people. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: Then they turned and left, and put the children, the livestock, and the valuables in front of them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had distanced themselves from Micah’s house, the men who were in the houses near Micah’s house assembled by command and overtook the sons of Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they called out to the sons of Dan, who turned ①around and said to Micah, “What is the matter with you, that you have assembled together?” ▷ ①Lit their faces

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “You have taken my gods which I made, and the priest, and have gone away; what more do I have? So how can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Dan said to him, “Do not let your voice be heard among us, or else ①fierce men will attack you, and you will ②lose your life and the lives of your household.” ▷ ①Lit bitter of soul ②Lit take away

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Dan went on their way; and when Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they took what Micah had made and the priest who had belonged to him, and came to Laish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting, and struck them with the edge of the sword; and they burned the city with fire.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was no one to save them, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone, and it was in the valley which is near Beth-rehob. So they rebuilt the city and lived in it.

column.name: text
column.value: And they named the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father who was born to Israel; however, the name of the city was previously Laish.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Dan set up for themselves the carved image; and Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of ①Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day of the captivity of the land. ▷ ①Some ancient versions Moses

column.name: text
column.value: So they set up for themselves Micah’s carved image which he had made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite ①staying in the remote part of the hill country of Ephraim, who took a concubine for himself from Bethlehem in Judah. ▷ ①Or sojourning

column.name: text
column.value: But his concubine ①found him repugnant, and she left him and went to her father’s house in Bethlehem in Judah, and remained there for a period of four months. ▷ ①Or was unfaithful to him (a Hebrew homonym); LXX became angry at him

column.name: text
column.value: Then her husband set out and went after her to speak ①gently to her in order to bring her back, ②taking with him his servant and a pair of donkeys. And she brought him into her father’s house, and when the girl’s father saw him, he was glad to meet him. ▷ ①Lit to her heart ②Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: His father-in-law, the girl’s father, prevailed upon him, and he remained with him for three days. So they ate and drank and stayed there.

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the fourth day they got up early in the morning, and he ①prepared to go; but the girl’s father said to his son-in-law, “Strengthen ②yourself with a piece of bread, and afterward you may go.” ▷ ①Lit arose ②Lit your heart

column.name: text
column.value: So both of them sat down and ate and drank together; and the girl’s father said to the man, “Please ①be so kind as to spend the night, and let your heart be cheerful.” ▷ ①Lit be willing to

column.name: text
column.value: However, the man got up to go; but his father-in-law urged him, and he spent the night there again.

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the fifth day he got up to go early in the morning, but the girl’s father said, “Please strengthen ①yourself, and wait until ②late afternoon”; so both of them ate. ▷ ①Lit your heart ②Lit the day declines

column.name: text
column.value: When the man got up to go, along with his concubine and servant, his father-in-law, the girl’s father, said to him, “Behold now, the day has drawn ①to a close; please spend the night. Behold, the day is ②coming to an end; spend the night here so that your heart may be cheerful. Then tomorrow you may arise early for your journey and go ③home.” ▷ ①Lit toward evening ②Lit declining ③Lit to your tent

column.name: text
column.value: But the man was unwilling to spend the night, so he got up and left, and came to a place opposite Jebus (that is, Jerusalem). And with him was a pair of saddled donkeys; his concubine also was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: When they were near Jebus, the day was almost gone; and the servant said to his master, “Please come, and let’s turn aside into this city of the Jebusites and spend the night in it.”

column.name: text
column.value: However, his master said to him, “We will not turn aside into a city of foreigners who are not of the sons of Israel; instead, we will go on as far as Gibeah.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his servant, “Come, and let’s approach one of these places; and we will spend the night in Gibeah or Ramah.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they passed along and went their way, and the sun set on them near Gibeah which belongs to Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: They turned aside there to enter and spend the night in Gibeah. When ①they entered, ②they sat down in the public square of the city, for no one took them into his house to spend the night. ▷ ①As in LXX; MT he ②As in LXX; MT he

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, an old man was coming out of the field from his work at evening. Now the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he was ①staying in Gibeah, but the men of the place were Benjaminites. ▷ ①Or sojourning

column.name: text
column.value: And he raised his eyes and saw the traveler in the public square of the city; and the old man said, “Where are you going, and where do you come from?”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to him, “We are passing from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote part of the hill country of Ephraim, for I am from there, and I went to Bethlehem in Judah. But I am now going to ①my house, and no one will take me into his house. ▷ ①MT; LXX the house of the LORD, cf. v 29

column.name: text
column.value: Yet there is both straw and feed for our donkeys, and also bread and wine for me, and ①your female slave, and the young man who is with your servants; there is no lack of anything.” ▷ ①I.e., the concubine

column.name: text
column.value: Then the old man said, “Peace to you. Only let me take care of all your needs; however, do not spend the night in the public square.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he took him into his house and fed the donkeys, and they washed their feet and ate and drank.

column.name: text
column.value: While they were ①celebrating, behold, the men of the city, certain ②worthless men, surrounded the house, pushing one another at the door; and they spoke to the owner of the house, the old man, saying, “Bring out the man who entered your house that we may ③have relations with him.” ▷ ①Lit making their hearts glad ②Lit sons of Belial ③Lit know him

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man, the owner of the house, went out to them and said to them, “No, my brothers, please do not act so wickedly. Since this man has come into my house, do not commit this vile sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is my virgin daughter and ①the man’s concubine. Please let me bring them out, then rape them and do to them ②whatever you wish. But do not commit this act of vile sin against this man.” ▷ ①Lit his ②Lit the good in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: But the men would not listen to him. So the man seized his concubine and brought her outside to them; and they ①raped her and abused her all night until morning, then let her go at the approach of dawn. ▷ ①Lit knew her (carnally)

column.name: text
column.value: ①As the day began to dawn, the woman came and fell down at the doorway of the man’s house where her master was, until full daylight. ▷ ①Lit At the turning of the morning

column.name: text
column.value: When her master got up in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way, then behold, his concubine was lying at the doorway of the house with her hands on the threshold.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to her, “Get up and let’s go,” but there was no answer. Then he put her on the donkey; and the man set out and went to his ①home. ▷ ①Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: When he entered his house, he took a knife and seized his concubine, and cut her in twelve pieces, limb by limb. Then he sent her throughout the territory of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: All who saw it said, “Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen from the day when the sons of Israel came up from the land of Egypt to this day. Consider it, ①make a plan, and speak up!” ▷ ①Or take counsel

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, “None of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin ①in marriage.” ▷ ①Lit as a wife

column.name: text
column.value: So the people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, and raised their voices and wept ①profusely. ▷ ①Lit with great weeping

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, that one tribe is missing today from Israel?”

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about the next day that the people got up early and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel said, “Who is there among all the tribes of Israel who did not go up to the LORD in the assembly?” For ①they had taken a solemn oath concerning anyone who did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, “He shall certainly be put to death.” ▷ ①Lit there was a great oath

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel were sorry for their brother Benjamin, and said, “Today one tribe is cut off from Israel!

column.name: text
column.value: What are we to do for wives for those who are left, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters as wives?”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “What one is there of the tribes of Israel that did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah?” And behold, no one had come to the camp from Jabesh-gilead to the assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: For when the people were ①counted, behold, not one of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was there. ▷ ①Or mustered

column.name: text
column.value: And the congregation sent twelve thousand ①of the valiant warriors there, and commanded them, saying, “Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the edge of the sword, along with the women and the children. ▷ ①Lit men from the sons of valor

column.name: text
column.value: And this is the thing that you shall do: you shall utterly destroy every male, and every woman who has ①slept with a male.” ▷ ①Lit known the bed of

column.name: text
column.value: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by ①sleeping with him; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan. ▷ ①Lit the bed of a male

column.name: text
column.value: Then the whole congregation sent word and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the tribe of Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had allowed to live from the women of Jabesh-gilead; but they ①were not enough for them. ▷ ①Lit did not find it so

column.name: text
column.value: And the people were sorry for Benjamin, because the LORD had created a gap in the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the elders of the congregation said, “What are we to do for wives for those who are left, since the women have been eliminated from Benjamin?”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe will not be wiped out from Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: But we cannot give them wives from our daughters.” For the sons of Israel had sworn, saying, “Cursed is he who gives a wife to Benjamin!”

column.name: text
column.value: So they said, “Behold, there is a feast of the LORD from year to year in Shiloh, which is on the north side of Bethel, on the east side of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south side of Lebonah.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, “Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

column.name: text
column.value: and watch; and behold, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to ①take part in the dances, then you shall come out of the vineyards, and each of you shall seize his wife from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin. ▷ ①Lit dance

column.name: text
column.value: And when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, we shall say to them, ‘ ①Give them to us voluntarily, because we did not take for each man of Benjamin ②a wife in battle, ③nor did you give them to them, ④otherwise you would now be guilty.’ ” ▷ ①Lit Favor us with them ②Lit his ③Lit because you did not ④Lit as

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Benjamin did so, and took wives according to their number from those who danced, whom they seized. And they went and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and lived in them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel departed from there at that time, every man to his tribe and family, and each one departed from there to his inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the sons of Israel from Dan to Beersheba, including the land of Gilead, came out, and the congregation assembled as one person to the LORD at Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: And the ①leaders of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, took their stand in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand foot ②soldiers who drew the sword. ▷ ①Lit cornerstones ②Lit men

column.name: text
column.value: (Now the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) And the sons of Israel said, “Tell us, how did this wickedness take place?”

column.name: text
column.value: So the Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, “I came with my concubine to spend the night at Gibeah which belongs to Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: But the ①citizens of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house at night, ②threatening me. They intended to kill me; instead, they raped my concubine so that she died. ▷ ①Or landowners ②Lit against me

column.name: text
column.value: And I took hold of my concubine and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout the land of Israel’s inheritance; for they have committed an outrageous sin and vile act in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, all you sons of Israel, give your ①response and advice here.” ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people rose up as one person, saying, “Not one of us will go to his tent, nor will any of us go home.

column.name: text
column.value: But now this is the thing which we will do to Gibeah; we will go up against it by lot.

column.name: text
column.value: And we will take ten men out of a hundred throughout the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand to ①supply provisions for the people, so that when they come to ②Gibeah of Benjamin, they may ③punish them for all the vile sin that they have committed in Israel.” ▷ ①Lit take ②Heb Geba ③Lit do

column.name: text
column.value: So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, ①united as one man. ▷ ①Lit companions as

column.name: text
column.value: Then the tribes of Israel sent men through the entire ①tribe of Benjamin, saying, “What is this wickedness that has taken place among you? ▷ ①Lit tribes

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, turn over the men, the ①worthless men who are in Gibeah, so that we may put them to death and remove this wickedness from Israel.” But the sons of Benjamin would not listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Lit sons of Belial

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, the sons of Benjamin gathered from the cities to Gibeah, to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: From the cities on that day the sons of Benjamin were ①counted, twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah who were ②counted, seven hundred choice men. ▷ ①Or mustered ②Or mustered

column.name: text
column.value: Out of all these people seven hundred choice men were left-handed; each one could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel besides Benjamin were ①counted, four hundred thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were men of war. ▷ ①Or mustered

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Israel set out, went up to Bethel, and inquired of God and said, “Who shall go up first for us to battle against the sons of Benjamin?” Then the LORD said, “Judah shall go up first.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel got up in the morning and camped against Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel went to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel lined up for battle against them at Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and ①struck to the ground on that day twenty-two thousand men of Israel. ▷ ①Lit destroyed

column.name: text
column.value: But the people, the men of Israel, showed themselves courageous and lined up for battle again in the place where they had lined themselves up on the first day.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall we again advance for battle against the sons of my brother Benjamin?” And the LORD said, “Go up against him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel ①came against the sons of Benjamin on the second day. ▷ ①Lit approached

column.name: text
column.value: And Benjamin went out against them from Gibeah the second day and struck to the ground again eighteen thousand men of the sons of Israel; all of these drew the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept and remained there before the LORD, and fasted that day until evening. And they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel inquired of the LORD (for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,

column.name: text
column.value: and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, Aaron’s son, stood before it to minister in those days), saying, “Shall I yet again go out to battle against the sons of my brother Benjamin, or shall I stop?” And the LORD said, “Go up, for tomorrow I will hand them over to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Israel set men in ambush around Gibeah.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and lined up against Gibeah as at other times.

column.name: text
column.value: When the sons of Benjamin went out against the people, they were lured away from the city, and they began to strike and kill some of the people as at other times, on the roads (one of which goes up to Bethel, and the other to Gibeah), and in the field, about thirty men of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Benjamin said, “They are defeated before us, like the first time.” But the sons of Israel said, “Let’s flee, so that we may draw them away from the city to the roads.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the men of Israel rose from their place and lined up at Baal-tamar; and the men of Israel in ambush charged from their place, from Maareh-geba.

column.name: text
column.value: When ten thousand choice men from all Israel came against Gibeah, the battle became ①fierce; but ②Benjamin did not know that disaster was ③close to them. ▷ ①Lit heavy ②Lit they ③Lit touching

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD struck Benjamin before Israel, so that the sons of Israel destroyed 25,100 men of Benjamin that ①day, all who drew the sword. ▷ ①Lit day; all these drew

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Benjamin saw that they were ①defeated. When the men of Israel gave ②ground to Benjamin because they relied on the men in ambush whom they had set against Gibeah, ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: the men in ambush hurried and rushed against Gibeah; the men in ambush also deployed and struck all the city with the edge of the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the agreed sign between the men of Israel and the men in ambush was that they would make a great cloud of smoke rise from the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin began to strike and kill about thirty men of Israel, for they said, “Undoubtedly they are ①defeated before us, as in the first battle.” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: But when the cloud began to rise from the city in a column of smoke, Benjamin looked behind them; and behold, the entire city was going up in smoke to heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified; for they saw that disaster was ①close to them. ▷ ①Lit touching

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, they turned their backs before the men of Israel to flee in the direction of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them while those who attacked from the cities were annihilating them in the midst of them.

column.name: text
column.value: They surrounded Benjamin, pursued them without rest, and trampled them down opposite Gibeah toward the ①east. ▷ ①Lit sunrise

column.name: text
column.value: So eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all of these were valiant men.

column.name: text
column.value: ①The rest turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, but they ②caught five thousand of them on the roads and overtook them ③at Gidom, and ④killed two thousand of them. ▷ ①As in LXX; Heb And they ②Lit gleaned ③Lit as far as ④Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: So all those of Benjamin who fell that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were valiant men.

column.name: text
column.value: But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon; and they remained at the rock of Rimmon for four months.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Israel then turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, both the entire city with the cattle and all that they found; they also set on fire all the cities which they found.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there, and behold, the redeemer of whom Boaz spoke was passing by, so he said, “Come over here, ①friend, sit down here.” And he came over and sat down. ▷ ①Lit a certain one

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took ten men of the elders of the city and said, “Sit down here.” So they sat down.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to the redeemer, “Naomi, who has returned from the land of Moab, has to sell the plot of land which belonged to our brother Elimelech.

column.name: text
column.value: So I thought that I would ①inform you, saying, ‘Buy it before those who are sitting here, and before the elders of my people. If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if ②not, tell me so that I may know; for there is no one except you to redeem it, and I am after you.’ ” And he said, “I will redeem it.” ▷ ①Lit uncover your ear ②Lit no one will redeem

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must also acquire Ruth the Moabitess, the widow of the deceased, in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the redeemer said, “I cannot redeem it for myself, otherwise I would ①jeopardize my own inheritance. Redeem it for yourself; you may have my right of redemption, since I cannot redeem it.” ▷ ①Lit damage

column.name: text
column.value: Now this was the custom in former times in Israel concerning the redemption and the exchange of land to confirm any matter: a man removed his sandal and gave it to another; and this was the way of confirmation in Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So the redeemer said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself.” And he removed his sandal.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz said to the elders and all the people, “You are witnesses today that I have bought from the hand of Naomi all that belonged to Elimelech and all that belonged to Chilion and Mahlon.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, I have acquired Ruth the Moabitess, the widow of Mahlon, to be my wife in order to raise up the name of the deceased on his inheritance, so that the name of the deceased will not be eliminated from his brothers or from the ①court of his birth place; you are witnesses today.” ▷ ①Lit gate

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people who were ①in the court, and the elders, said, “We are witnesses. May the LORD make the woman who is coming into your home like Rachel and Leah, both of whom built the house of Israel; and may you achieve ②wealth in Ephrathah and ③become famous in Bethlehem. ▷ ①Lit at the gate ②Or power ③Lit call the name in

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, may your house be like the house of Perez whom Tamar bore to Judah, through the ①descendants whom the LORD will give you by this young woman.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: So Boaz took Ruth, and she became his wife, and he had relations with her. And the LORD ①enabled her to conceive, and she gave birth to a son. ▷ ①Lit gave her conception

column.name: text
column.value: Then the women said to Naomi, “Blessed is the LORD who has not left you without a redeemer today, and may his name ①become famous in Israel. ▷ ①Lit be called in

column.name: text
column.value: May he also be to you one who restores life and sustains your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you ①and is better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.” ▷ ①Lit who

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naomi took the child and ①laid him in her lap, and became his nurse. ▷ ①I.e., as her own

column.name: text
column.value: And the neighbor women gave him a name, saying, “A son has been born to Naomi!” So they named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the generations of Perez: Perez fathered Hezron,

column.name: text
column.value: Hezron fathered Ram, and Ram fathered Amminadab,

column.name: text
column.value: and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,

column.name: text
column.value: and Salmon fathered Boaz, and Boaz fathered Obed,

column.name: text
column.value: and Obed fathered Jesse, and Jesse fathered David.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in the days when the judges ①governed, that there was a famine in the land. And a man of Bethlehem in Judah went to reside in the land of Moab ②with his wife and his two sons. ▷ ①Or judged ②Lit he, and

column.name: text
column.value: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife, Naomi; and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem in Judah. So they entered the land of Moab and remained there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left with her two sons.

column.name: text
column.value: And they took for themselves Moabite women as wives; the name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other, Ruth. And they lived there about ten years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then ①both Mahlon and Chilion also died, and the woman was left without her two sons and her husband. ▷ ①Lit both of them

column.name: text
column.value: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law to return from the land of Moab, because she had heard in the land of Moab that the LORD had visited His people by giving them food.

column.name: text
column.value: So she departed from the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the way to return to the land of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: But Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to ①your mother’s house. May the LORD deal kindly with you as you have dealt with the dead and with me. ▷ ①Lit her

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD grant that you may find a place of rest, each one in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they raised their voices and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: However, they said to her, “No, but we will return with you to your people.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. Why should you go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?

column.name: text
column.value: Return, my daughters! Go, for I am too old to have a husband. If I said I have hope, if I were even to have a husband tonight and also give birth to sons,

column.name: text
column.value: would you therefore wait until they were grown? Would you therefore refrain from marrying? No, my daughters; for it is much more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has come out against me.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they raised their voices and wept again; and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “Behold, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; return after your sister-in-law.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Ruth said, “Do not plead with me to leave you or to turn back from following you; for where you go, I will go, and where you sleep, I will sleep. Your people shall be my people, and your God, my God.

column.name: text
column.value: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the LORD do so to me, and worse, if anything but death separates ①me from you.” ▷ ①Lit between me and you

column.name: text
column.value: When she saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped speaking to her about it.

column.name: text
column.value: So they both went on until they came to Bethlehem. And when they had come to Bethlehem, all the city was stirred because of them, and ①the women said, “Is this Naomi?” ▷ ①Lit they

column.name: text
column.value: But she said to them, “Do not call me ①Naomi; call me ②Mara, for ③the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me. ▷ ①I.e., pleasant ②I.e., bitter ③Heb Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since the LORD has testified against me and ①the Almighty has afflicted me?” ▷ ①Heb Shaddai

column.name: text
column.value: So Naomi returned, and with her Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, who returned from the land of Moab. And they came to Bethlehem at the beginning of barley harvest.

column.name: text
column.value: Then her mother-in-law Naomi said to her, “My daughter, shall I not seek ①security for you, that it may go well for you? ▷ ①Lit a resting place

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, is Boaz not our relative, with whose young women you were? Behold, he is winnowing barley at the threshing floor tonight.

column.name: text
column.value: Wash yourself therefore, and anoint yourself, and put on your best clothes, and go down to the threshing floor; but do not reveal yourself to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall be when he lies down, that you shall ①take notice of the place where he lies, and you shall go and uncover his feet and lie down; then he will tell you what you should do.” ▷ ①Lit know

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her, “All that you say I will do.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she went down to the threshing floor and did according to all that her mother-in-law had commanded her.

column.name: text
column.value: When Boaz had eaten and drunk and his heart was cheerful, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain; and she came secretly, and uncovered his feet and lay down.

column.name: text
column.value: And it happened in the middle of the night that the man was startled and ①bent forward; and behold, a woman was lying at his feet. ▷ ①Or tossed around

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “Who are you?” And she answered, “I am Ruth your slave. Now spread your garment over your slave, for you are a redeemer.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “May you be blessed of the LORD, my daughter. You have shown your last kindness to be better than the first, by not going after young men, whether poor or rich.

column.name: text
column.value: So now, my daughter, do not fear. I will do for you whatever you say, for all ①my people in the city know that you are a woman of excellence. ▷ ①Lit the gate of my people know

column.name: text
column.value: But now, although it is true that I am a redeemer, yet there is also a redeemer more closely related than I.

column.name: text
column.value: Remain this night, and when morning comes, if he will ①redeem you, good; let him redeem you. But if he does not wish to ②redeem you, then I will redeem you, as the LORD lives. Lie down until morning.” ▷ ①Or act as close relative to ②Or act as close relative to

column.name: text
column.value: So she lay at his feet until morning, and got up before one person could recognize another; and he said, “Do not let it be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”

column.name: text
column.value: Again he said, “Give me the shawl that is on you and hold it.” So she held it, and he measured six measures of barley and laid it on her. Then ①she went into the city. ▷ ①Many mss; MT he

column.name: text
column.value: When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “ ①How did it go, my daughter?” And she told her all that the man had done for her. ▷ ①Lit Who are you?

column.name: text
column.value: She also said, “These six measures of barley he gave to me, for he said, ‘Do not go to your mother-in-law empty-handed.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “Wait, my daughter, until you know how the matter ①turns out; for the man will not rest until he has ②settled it today.” ▷ ①Lit falls ②Lit finished the matter

column.name: text
column.value: Now Naomi had ①a relative of her husband, a ②man of great wealth, of the family of Elimelech, whose name was Boaz. ▷ ①Another reading is an acquaintance ②Or mighty, valiant man

column.name: text
column.value: And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Please let me go to the field and glean among the ears of grain following one in whose eyes I may find favor.” And she said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she left and went and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and ①she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech. ▷ ①Lit her chance chanced upon

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem and said to the reapers, “May the LORD be with you.” And they said to him, “May the LORD bless you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz said to his servant who was ①in charge of the reapers, “Whose young woman is this?” ▷ ①Lit appointed over

column.name: text
column.value: And the servant ①in charge of the reapers replied, “She is the young Moabite woman who returned with Naomi from the land of Moab. ▷ ①Lit who was appointed over

column.name: text
column.value: And she said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came and has remained from the morning until now; she has been sitting in the house for a little while.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “ ①Listen carefully, my daughter. Do not go to glean in another field; furthermore, do not go on from this one, but join my young women here. ▷ ①Lit Have you not heard

column.name: text
column.value: Keep your eyes on the field which they reap, and go after them. Indeed, I have ordered the servants not to touch you. When you are thirsty, go to the ①water jars and drink from what the servants draw.” ▷ ①Lit vessels

column.name: text
column.value: Then she fell on her face, bowing to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your sight that you should take notice of me, since I am a foreigner?”

column.name: text
column.value: Boaz replied to her, “All that you have done for your mother-in-law after the death of your husband has been fully reported to me, and how you left your father and your mother and the land of your birth, and came to a people that you did not previously know.

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD reward your ①work, and may your wages be full from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.” ▷ ①Or behavior

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “I have found favor in your sight, my lord, for you have comforted me and indeed have spoken ①kindly to your servant, though I am not like one of your female servants.” ▷ ①Lit to the heart of your

column.name: text
column.value: And at mealtime Boaz said to her, “ ①Come here, that you may eat of the bread and dip your piece of bread in the vinegar.” So she sat beside the reapers; and he served her roasted grain, and she ate and was satisfied and had some left. ▷ ①Lit Come near here

column.name: text
column.value: When she got up to glean, Boaz commanded his servants, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and do not ①insult her. ▷ ①Or harm

column.name: text
column.value: Also you are to purposely slip out for her some grain from the bundles and leave it so that she may glean, and do not rebuke her.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she gleaned in the field until evening. Then she beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an ①ephah of barley. ▷ ①About 1 cubic foot or 0.03 cubic meters

column.name: text
column.value: And she picked it up and went into the city, and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned. She also took some out and gave ①Naomi what she had left after ②she was satisfied. ▷ ①Lit her ②Lit her satiety

column.name: text
column.value: Her mother-in-law then said to her, “Where did you glean today and where did you work? May he who took notice of you be blessed.” So she told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, “The name of the man with whom I worked today is Boaz.”

column.name: text
column.value: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed of the LORD who has not withdrawn His kindness from the living and from the dead.” Again Naomi said to her, “The man is our relative; he is one of our redeemers.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ruth the Moabitess said, “ ①Furthermore, he said to me, ‘You are to stay close to my servants until they have finished all my harvest.’ ” ▷ ①Lit Also that

column.name: text
column.value: And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law Ruth, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that others do not assault you in another field.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she stayed close by the young women of Boaz in order to glean until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest. And she lived with her mother-in-law.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a man from Ramathaim-zophim from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

column.name: text
column.value: And he had two wives: the name of one was Hannah and the name of the ①other Peninnah; and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children. ▷ ①Or second

column.name: text
column.value: Now this man would go up from his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of armies in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD there.

column.name: text
column.value: When the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to his wife Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters;

column.name: text
column.value: but to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved Hannah, but the LORD had closed her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: Her rival, moreover, would provoke her bitterly to irritate her, because the LORD had closed her womb.

column.name: text
column.value: And it happened year after year, as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, that she would provoke her; so she wept and would not eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elkanah her husband would say to her, “Hannah, why do you weep, and why do you not eat, and why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hannah got up after eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the ①temple of the LORD. ▷ ①I.e., tabernacle

column.name: text
column.value: She, ①greatly distressed, prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly. ▷ ①Lit bitter of soul

column.name: text
column.value: And she made a vow and said, “LORD of armies, if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your bond-servant and remember me, and not forget Your bond-servant, but will give Your bond-servant a ①son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and a razor shall never come on his head.” ▷ ①Lit seed of men

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, as she ①continued praying before the LORD, that Eli was watching her mouth. ▷ ①Lit multiplied

column.name: text
column.value: As for Hannah, she was speaking in her heart, only her lips were quivering, but her voice was not heard. So Eli thought that she was drunk.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eli said to her, “How long will you behave like a drunk? Get rid of your wine!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Hannah answered and said, “No, my lord, I am a woman ①despairing in spirit; I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD. ▷ ①Lit hard

column.name: text
column.value: Do not ①consider your bond-servant a useless woman, for I have spoken until now out of my great concern and provocation.” ▷ ①Lit give

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eli answered and said, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your request that you have asked of Him.”

column.name: text
column.value: She said, “Let your bond-servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they got up early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD, and returned again to their house in Ramah. And Elkanah ①had relations with Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her. ▷ ①Lit knew Hannah

column.name: text
column.value: It came about ①in due time, after Hannah had conceived, that she gave birth to a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked for him of the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit at the circuit of the days

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man Elkanah went up with all his household to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and to pay his vow.

column.name: text
column.value: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “I will not go until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, so that he may appear before the LORD and stay there for life.”

column.name: text
column.value: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do ①what seems best to you. Stay until you have weaned him; only may the LORD confirm His word.” So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him. ▷ ①Lit the good in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Now when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with a three-year-old bull, one ephah of flour, and a jug of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD in Shiloh, although the child was young.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they ①slaughtered the bull, and brought the boy to Eli. ▷ ①I.e., for sacrifice

column.name: text
column.value: And she said, “Pardon me, my lord! As your soul lives, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you, praying to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: For this boy I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my request which I asked of Him.

column.name: text
column.value: So I have also ①dedicated him to the LORD; as long as he lives he is ②dedicated to the LORD.” And he worshiped the LORD there. ▷ ①Or lent ②Or lent

column.name: text
column.value: So the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out to meet the Philistines in battle, and they camped beside Ebenezer, while the Philistines camped in Aphek.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistines drew up in battle formation to meet Israel. When the battle ①spread, Israel was ②defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men on the battlefield. ▷ ①Or was over ②Lit struck before

column.name: text
column.value: When the people came into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has the LORD defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s take the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that He may come among us and save us from the power of our enemies.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the people sent men to Shiloh, and from there they carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD of armies who is enthroned above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

column.name: text
column.value: And as the ark of the covenant of the LORD was coming into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth resounded.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” Then they understood that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God has come into the camp!” And they said, “Woe to us! For nothing like this has happened before.

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to us! Who will save us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.

column.name: text
column.value: Take courage and be men, Philistines, or you will become slaves to the Hebrews, as they have been slaves to you; so be men and fight!”

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines fought and Israel was defeated, and every man fled to his tent; and the defeat was very great, for thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh the same day with his clothes torn, and ①dust on his head. ▷ ①Lit soil

column.name: text
column.value: When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat ①by the road keeping watch, because his heart was anxious about the ark of God. And the man came to give a report in the city, and all the city cried out. ▷ ①LXX beside the gate watching the road

column.name: text
column.value: When Eli heard the noise of the outcry, he said, “What does the noise of this commotion mean?” Then the man came hurriedly and told Eli.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were ①fixed and he could not see. ▷ ①I.e., possibly unable to focus

column.name: text
column.value: The man said to Eli, “I am the one who came from the battle line. Indeed, I escaped from the battle line today.” And he said, “How are things, my son?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the one who brought the news replied, “Israel has fled before the Philistines and there has also been a great defeat among the people, and your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas are also dead; and the ark of God has been taken.”

column.name: text
column.value: When he mentioned the ark of God, ①Eli fell off the seat backward beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for ②he was old and heavy. And so he judged Israel for forty years. ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit the man

column.name: text
column.value: Now his daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was pregnant and about to give birth; and when she heard the news that the ark of God had been taken and that her father-in-law and her husband had died, she kneeled down and gave birth, because her pains came upon her.

column.name: text
column.value: And about the time of her death the women who were standing by her said to her, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son.” But she did not answer or pay attention.

column.name: text
column.value: And she named the boy ①Ichabod, saying, “The glory has departed from Israel,” because the ark of God had been taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband. ▷ ①I.e., no glory, or where is the glory?

column.name: text
column.value: So she said, “The glory has departed from Israel, because the ark of God has been taken.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hannah prayed and said, “My heart rejoices in the LORD; My ①horn is exalted in the LORD, My mouth ②speaks boldly against my enemies, Because I rejoice in Your salvation. ▷ ①I.e., strength ②Lit is enlarged

column.name: text
column.value: There is no one holy like the LORD, Indeed, there is no one besides You, Nor is there any rock like our God.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not go on ①boasting so very proudly, Do not let arrogance come out of your mouth; For the LORD is a God of knowledge, And ②with Him actions are weighed. ▷ ①Lit talk much ②Or disgraceful actions have no place

column.name: text
column.value: The bows of the mighty are broken to pieces, But those who have stumbled strap on strength.

column.name: text
column.value: Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, But those who were hungry cease to be hungry. Even the infertile woman gives birth to seven, But she who has many children languishes.

column.name: text
text
column.value: The LORD makes poor and rich; He humbles, He also exalts.

column.name: text
column.value: He raises the poor from the dust, He lifts the needy from the garbage heap To seat them with nobles, And He gives them a seat of honor as an inheritance; For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’S, And He set the world on them.

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: Then Elkanah went to his home at Ramah. But the boy continued to attend to the service of the LORD before Eli the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Eli were ①useless men; they did not know the LORD. ▷ ①Lit sons of Belial

column.name: text
column.value: And this was the custom of the priests with the people: when anyone was offering a sacrifice, the priest’s servant would come while the meat was cooking, with a three-pronged fork in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And he would thrust it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; everything that the fork brought up, the priest would take for himself. They did so in Shiloh to all the Israelites who came there.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, before they ①burned the fat, the priest’s servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, “Give the priest meat for roasting, as he will not take cooked meat from you, only raw.” ▷ ①Lit offered up in smoke

column.name: text
column.value: And if the man said to him, “They must ①burn the fat ②first, then take as much as ③you desire,” then he would say, “No, but you must give it to me now; and if not, I am taking it by force!” ▷ ①Lit offer up in smoke ②Lit as the day ③Lit your soul desires

column.name: text
column.value: And so the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD disrespectfully.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel was ministering before the LORD, as a boy wearing a linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: And his mother would make for him a little robe and bring it up to him from year to year when she would come up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, and say, “May the LORD give you ①children from this woman in place of the ②one she requested of the LORD.” And they went to their own ③home. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit request ③Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: ①The LORD indeed visited Hannah, and she conceived and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up ②before the LORD. ▷ ①Or When the LORD visited...then she; DSS And the LORD visited ②Lit with

column.name: text
column.value: Now Eli was very old; and he heard about everything that his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they slept with the women who served at the doorway of the tent of meeting.

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to them, “Why are you doing such things as these, the evil things that I hear from all these people?

column.name: text
column.value: No, my sons; for the report is not good which I hear the LORD’S people circulating.

column.name: text
column.value: If one person sins against another, God will mediate for him; but if a person sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?” But they would not listen to the voice of their father, for the LORD desired to put them to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the boy Samuel was continuing to grow and to be in favor both with the LORD and with people.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a man of God came to Eli and said to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Did I not indeed reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?

column.name: text
column.value: Did I not choose them from all the tribes of Israel to be My priests, to go up to My altar, to burn incense, to carry an ephod before Me? And did I not give to the house of your father all the fire offerings of the sons of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Why are you ①showing contempt for My sacrifice and My offering which I have commanded for My dwelling, and why are you honoring your sons above Me, by making yourselves fat with the ②choicest of every offering of My people Israel?’ ▷ ①Lit giving a kick to ②Or first

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the LORD God of Israel declares, ‘I did indeed say that your house and the house of your father was to walk before Me forever’; but now the LORD declares, ‘Far be it from Me—for those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me will be insignificant.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, the days are coming when I will eliminate your ①strength and the ②strength of your father’s house, so that there will not be an old man in your house. ▷ ①Lit arm ②Lit arm

column.name: text
column.value: And you will look at the distress of My dwelling, in spite of all the good that ①I do for Israel; and there will never be an old man in your house. ▷ ①Lit He does

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I will not cut off every man of yours from My altar, ①so that your eyes will fail from weeping and your soul grieve, and all the ②increase of your house will die ③in the prime of life. ▷ ①Lit to make your eyes fail and to grieve your soul ②I.e., new children ③Lit as men

column.name: text
column.value: And this will be the sign to you which will come in regard to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: on the same day both of them will die.

column.name: text
column.value: But I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest who will do according to what is in My heart and My soul; and I will build him an enduring house, and he will walk before My anointed always.

column.name: text
column.value: And everyone who is left in your house will come to bow down to him for a ①silver coin or a loaf of bread and say, “Please ②assign me to one of the priest’s offices so that I may eat a piece of bread.” ’ ” ▷ ①Or payment ②Lit attach

column.name: text
column.value: Now the boy Samuel was attending to the service of the LORD before Eli. And word from the LORD was rare in those days; ①visions were infrequent. ▷ ①Lit there was no vision spreading

column.name: text
column.value: But it happened at that time as Eli was lying down in his place (now his eyesight had begun to be ①poor and he could not see well), ▷ ①Lit dim

column.name: text
column.value: and the lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD where the ark of God was,

column.name: text
column.value: that the LORD called Samuel; and he said, “Here I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call, go back and lie down.” So he went and lay down.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD called yet again, “Samuel!” So Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call, my son, go back and lie down.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel did not yet know the LORD, nor had the word of the LORD yet been revealed to him.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD called Samuel again for the third time. And he got up and went to Eli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” Then Eli realized that the LORD was calling the boy.

column.name: text
column.value: And Eli said to Samuel, “Go lie down, and it shall be if He calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.’ ” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD came and stood, and called as at the other times: “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for Your servant is listening.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Samuel, “Behold, I am going to do a thing in Israel, and both ears of everyone who hears about it will ring.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day I will carry out against Eli everything that I have spoken in regard to his house, from beginning to end.

column.name: text
column.value: For I have told him that I am going to judge his house forever for the wrongdoing that he knew, because his sons were bringing a curse on themselves and he did not rebuke them.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the wrongdoing of Eli’s house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel lay down until morning. Then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. But Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son.” And he said, “Here I am.”

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do the same to you, and more so, if you hide a single word from me of all the words that He spoke to you!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel told him ①everything and hid nothing from him. And he said, “He is the LORD; let Him do ②what seems good to Him.” ▷ ①Lit all the words ②Lit the good in His eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him, and He let none of his words ①fail. ▷ ①Lit fall to the ground

column.name: text
column.value: And all Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD appeared again at Shiloh, because the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon, and placed it beside Dagon.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Ashdodites got up early the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and set him back in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: But when they got up early the next morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. And the head of Dagon and both palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold; ①only the torso of Dagon was left. ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT only Dagon

column.name: text
column.value: For that reason neither the priests of Dagon nor any who enter Dagon’s house step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the hand of the LORD was heavy on the Ashdodites, and He made them feel devastated and struck them with tumors, both Ashdod and its territories.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God of Israel must not remain with us, because His hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent word and gathered all the governors of the Philistines to them, and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?” And they said, “Have the ark of the God of Israel ①brought to Gath.” So they took the ark of the God of Israel away. ▷ ①Lit turn to

column.name: text
column.value: After they had taken it away, the hand of the LORD was against the city, creating a very great panic; and He struck the people of the city, from the young to the old, so that tumors broke out on them.

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And as the ark of God came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought the ark of the God of Israel to ①us, to kill ②us and ③our people!” ▷ ①Lit me ②Lit me ③Lit my

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore they sent word and gathered all the governors of the Philistines, and said, “Send away the ark of the God of Israel and let it return to its own place, so that it will not kill ①us and ②our people!” For there was a deadly panic throughout the city; the hand of God was very heavy there. ▷ ①Lit me ②Lit my

column.name: text
column.value: And the people who did not die were struck with tumors, and the outcry of the city went up to heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the ark of the LORD had been in the territory of the Philistines for seven months.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What are we to do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us ①how we may send it to its place.” ▷ ①Or what...send with it

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “If you are going to send the ark of the God of Israel away, do not send it empty; but you shall certainly return to Him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be revealed to you why His hand does not leave you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said, “What is to be the guilt offering that we shall return to Him?” And they said, “Five gold tumors and five gold mice corresponding to the number of the governors of the Philistines, since one plague was on all of ①you and on your governors. ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: So you shall make likenesses of your tumors and likenesses of your mice that are ruining the land, and you shall give glory to the God of Israel; perhaps He will lighten His hand from you, your gods, and your land.

column.name: text
column.value: Why then do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When He had severely dealt with them, did they not let ①the people go, and they left? ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, take and prepare a new cart and two milk cows on which there has never been a yoke; and hitch the cows to the cart and take their calves back home, away from them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then take the ark of the LORD and place it on the cart; and put the articles of gold which you return to Him as a guilt offering in a saddlebag by its side. Then send it away that it may go.

column.name: text
column.value: But watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory to Beth-shemesh, then He has done this great evil to us. But if not, then we will know that it was not His hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men did so: they took two milk cows and hitched them to the cart, and shut in their calves at home.

column.name: text
column.value: And they put the ark of the LORD on the cart, and the saddlebag with the gold mice and the likenesses of their tumors.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the cows went straight in the ①direction of Beth-shemesh; they went on the same road, bellowing as they went, and did not turn off to the right or to the left. And the governors of the Philistines followed them to the border of Beth-shemesh. ▷ ①Lit way

column.name: text
column.value: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were gathering in their wheat harvest in the valley, and they raised their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced at seeing it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite and stopped there where there was a large stone; and they split the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the saddlebag that was with it, in which were the articles of gold, and put them on the large stone; and the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices that day to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: When the five governors of the Philistines saw it, they returned to Ekron that day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the gold tumors which the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, and one for Ekron;

column.name: text
column.value: and the gold mice, corresponding to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five governors, both of fortified cities and of country villages. The large ①stone on which they placed the ark of the LORD is a witness to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemite. ▷ ①As in some mss and ancient versions; MT Abel

column.name: text
column.value: Now He fatally struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck 50,070 men among the people, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom will He go up from us?”

column.name: text
column.value: So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back the ark of the LORD; come down and take it up to yourselves.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Kiriath-jearim came and took the ark of the LORD and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill, and they ①consecrated his son Eleazar to watch over the ark of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit made holy; i.e., ordained

column.name: text
column.value: From the day that the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim, the ①time was long, for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel ②mourned after the LORD. ▷ ①Lit days increased ②Or followed after

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, then remove the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to the LORD and serve Him alone; and He will save you from the hand of the Philistines.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD alone.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah and I will pray to the LORD for you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they gathered to Mizpah, and drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day and said there, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the governors of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the sons of Israel heard about it, they were afraid of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Israel said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that He will save us from the hand of the Philistines!”

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel took a nursing lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD; and Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, and the Philistines advanced to battle Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great ①thunder on that day against the Philistines and confused them, so that they were struck down before Israel. ▷ ①Lit voice

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Israel came out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and killed them as far as below Beth-car.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took a stone and placed it between Mizpah and Shen, and named it ①Ebenezer, saying, “ ②So far the LORD has helped us.” ▷ ①I.e., the stone of help ②Lit As far as here

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines were subdued, and they did not come anymore within the border of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

column.name: text
column.value: The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel ①recovered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. So there was peace between Israel and the Amorites. ▷ ①Lit saved

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

column.name: text
column.value: And he used to go annually on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and he judged Israel in all these places.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he would make his return to Ramah, because his house was there, and there he also judged Israel; and there he built an altar to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when Samuel was old, that he appointed his sons as judges over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: The name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah; they were judging in Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: His sons, however, did not walk in his ways but turned aside after dishonest gain, and they took bribes and perverted justice.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah;

column.name: text
column.value: and they said to him, “Behold, you have grown old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

column.name: text
