column.value: But the matter was ①displeasing in the sight of Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” And Samuel prayed to the LORD. ▷ ①Or evil

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people regarding all that they say to you, because they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me from being King over them.

column.name: text
column.value: Like all the deeds which they have done since the day that I brought them up from Egypt even to this day—in that they have abandoned Me and served other gods—so they are doing to you as well.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, listen to their voice; however, you shall warn them strongly and tell them of the ①practice of the king who will reign over them.” ▷ ①Lit custom

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel spoke all the words of the LORD to the people who had asked him for a king.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “This will be the ①practice of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and put them in his chariots for himself and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots. ▷ ①Lit custom

column.name: text
column.value: He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and some to ①do his plowing and to gather in his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and equipment for his chariots. ▷ ①Lit plow his plowing

column.name: text
column.value: He will also take your daughters and use them as perfumers, cooks, and bakers.

column.name: text
column.value: He will take the best of your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, and give them to his servants.

column.name: text
column.value: And he will take a tenth of your seed and your vineyards and give it to his high officials and his servants.

column.name: text
column.value: He will also take your male servants and your female servants, and your best young men, and your donkeys, and ①use them for his work. ▷ ①Lit make

column.name: text
column.value: He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will become his servants.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you will cry out on that day because of your king whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you on that day.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel, and they said, “No, but there shall be a king over us,

column.name: text
column.value: so that we also may be like all the nations, and our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now after Samuel had heard all the words of the people, he ①repeated them in the LORD’S hearing. ▷ ①Lit spoke

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice and appoint a king for them.” So Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Go, every man to his city.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish the son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, son of a Benjaminite, a ①valiant mighty man. ▷ ①Or man of wealth and influence

column.name: text
column.value: He had a son whose name was Saul, a young and handsome man, and there was not a more handsome man than he among the sons of Israel; from his shoulders and up he was taller than any of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the donkeys of Kish, Saul’s father, had wandered off. So Kish said to his son Saul, “Now take with you one of the servants and arise, go search for the donkeys.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he passed through the hill country of Ephraim and passed through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjaminites, but they did not find them.

column.name: text
column.value: When they came to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, “Come, and let’s return, or else my father will stop being concerned about the donkeys and will become anxious about us.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to him, “Behold now, there is a man of God in this city, and the man is held in honor; everything that he says definitely comes true. Now let’s go there, perhaps he can tell us about our journey on which we have set out.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to his servant, “But look, if we go, what shall we bring the man? For the bread is gone from our sacks and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What do we have?”

column.name: text
column.value: The servant answered Saul again and said, “Look, I have in my hand a fourth of a shekel of silver; I will give it to the man of God and he will tell us our way.”

column.name: text
column.value: (Previously in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he used to say, “Come, and let’s go to the seer”; for he who is called a prophet now was previously called a seer.)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to his servant, “ ①Good idea; come, let’s go.” So they went to the city where the man of God was. ▷ ①Lit Your word is good

column.name: text
column.value: As they went up the slope to the city, they found young women going out to draw water, and they said to them, “Is the seer here?”

column.name: text
column.value: They answered them and said, “He is; ①see, he is ahead of you. Hurry now, for he has come into the city today, because the people have a sacrifice on the high place today. ▷ ①Or behold

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as you enter the city you will find him before he goes up to the high place to eat, for the people will not eat until he comes, because he must bless the sacrifice; afterward those who are invited will eat. Now then, go up, for you will find him about this time.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they went up to the city. As they came into the city, behold, Samuel was coming out toward them to go up to the high place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a day before Saul’s coming, the LORD had ①revealed this to Samuel, saying, ▷ ①Lit opened Samuel’s ear

column.name: text
column.value: “About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him as ruler over My people Israel; and he will save My people from the hand of the Philistines. For I have considered My people, because their outcry has come to Me.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD ①said to him, “Behold, the man of whom I spoke to you! This one shall rule over My people.” ▷ ①Lit answered

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul approached Samuel at the gateway and said, “Please tell me where the seer’s house is.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel answered Saul and said, “I am the seer. Go up ahead of me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today; and in the morning I will let you go, and will tell you everything that is on your mind.

column.name: text
column.value: And as for your donkeys that wandered off three days ago, do not be concerned about them, for they have been found. And for whom is everything that is desirable in Israel? Is it not for you and for all your father’s household?”

column.name: text
column.value: Saul replied, “Am I not a Benjaminite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel, and my family the least of all the families of the ①tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me in this way?” ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT tribes

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the hall, and gave them a place at the head of those who were invited, who were about thirty men.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel said to the cook, “ ①Serve the portion that I gave you about which I said to you, ‘Set it ②aside.’ ” ▷ ①Lit Give ②Lit with you

column.name: text
column.value: Then the cook took up the leg with what was on it and placed it before Saul. And Samuel said, “Here is what has been reserved! Place it before you and eat, because it has been kept for you until the appointed time, ①since I said I have invited the people.” So Saul ate with Samuel that day. ▷ ①Lit saying

column.name: text
column.value: When they came down from the high place into the city, ①Samuel spoke with Saul on the roof. ▷ ①LXX they spread a bed for Saul on the roof

column.name: text
column.value: And they got up early; and at daybreak Samuel called to Saul on the roof, saying, “Get up, so that I may send you on your way.” So Saul got up, and both he and Samuel went out into the street.

column.name: text
column.value: As they were going down to the edge of the city, Samuel said to Saul, “Speak to the servant and have him go on ahead of us and pass by; but you stand here now, so that I may proclaim the word of God to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel took the flask of oil, poured it on ①Saul’s head, kissed him, and said, “Has the LORD not anointed you as ruler over His inheritance? ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: When you leave me today, then you will find two men close to Rachel’s tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say to you, ‘The donkeys which you went to look for have been found. Now behold, your father has stopped talking about the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, “What am I to do about my son?” ’

column.name: text
column.value: Then you will go on further from there, and you will come as far as the ①oak of Tabor, and there three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you: one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a jug of wine. ▷ ①Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: And they will ①greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you will accept from their hand. ▷ ①Lit inquire of your welfare

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward you will come to ①the hill of God where the Philistine garrison is; and it shall be as soon as you have come there to the city, that you will meet a group of prophets coming down from the high place with harp, tambourine, flute, and a lyre in front of them, and they will be prophesying. ▷ ①Or Gibeath-haelohim

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush upon you, and you will prophesy with them and be changed into a different man.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall be when these signs come to you, do for yourself what ①the occasion requires, because God is with you. ▷ ①Lit your hand finds

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall go down ahead of me to Gilgal; and behold, I will be coming down to you to offer burnt offerings and sacrifice peace offerings. You shall wait seven days until I come to you and inform you of what you should do.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened, when he turned his back to leave Samuel, that God changed ①his heart; and all those signs came about on that day. ▷ ①Lit for him another heart

column.name: text
column.value: When they came there to ①the hill, behold, a group of prophets met him; and the Spirit of God rushed upon him, so that he prophesied among them. ▷ ①Or Gibeath

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, when all who previously knew him saw that he was indeed prophesying with the prophets, that the people said to one another, “What is this that has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?”

column.name: text
column.value: And a man from there responded and said, “And who is their father?” Therefore it became a saying: “Is Saul also among the prophets?”

column.name: text
column.value: When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul’s uncle said to him and his servant, “Where did you go?” And he said, “To look for the donkeys. When we saw that they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Saul’s uncle said, “Please tell me what Samuel said to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to his uncle, “He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found.” But he did not tell him about the matter of the kingdom which Samuel had mentioned.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah;

column.name: text
column.value: and he said to the sons of Israel, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the ①power of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you.’ ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your catastrophes and your distresses; yet you have ①said, ‘No, but put a king over us!’ Now then, present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your ②groups of thousands.” ▷ ①As in several mss and ancient versions; MT said to Him ②Or clans

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel forward; and the tribe of Benjamin was selected by lot.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he brought the tribe of Benjamin forward by its families, and the Matrite family was selected by lot. And Saul the son of Kish was selected by lot; but when they looked for him, he could not be found.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore they inquired further of the LORD: “Has the man come here yet?” And the LORD said, “Behold, he is hiding himself among the baggage.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they ran and took him from there, and when he stood among the people, he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upward.

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to all the people, “Do you see him whom the LORD has chosen? Surely there is no one like him among all the people.” So all the people shouted and said, “ ①Long live the king!” ▷ ①Lit May the king live

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel told the people the ordinances of the kingdom, and wrote them in the book, and placed it before the LORD. And Samuel sent all the people away, each one to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul also went to his house in Gibeah; and the valiant men whose hearts God had touched went with him.

column.name: text
column.value: But certain ①useless men said, “How can this one save us?” And they despised him and did not bring him a gift. But ②he kept silent about it. ▷ ①A mutilated DSS fragment of uncertain reliability (4QSama) adds here that Nahash (11:1) gouged out the right eyes of Israelites ②Or wicked; lit sons of Belial

column.name: text
column.value: Now Nahash the Ammonite went up and besieged Jabesh-gilead; and all the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, “Make a covenant with us and we will serve you.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, “I will make it with you on this condition, that I will gouge out the right eye of every one of you, and thereby I will inflict a disgrace on all Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the elders of Jabesh said to him, “Allow us seven days to send messengers throughout the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul and spoke these words in the hearing of the people, and all the people raised their voices and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, Saul was coming from the field behind the oxen, and Saul said, “What is the matter with the people that they weep?” So they reported to him the words of the men of Jabesh.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit of God rushed upon Saul when he heard these words, and ①he became very angry. ▷ ①Lit his anger burned exceedingly

column.name: text
column.value: He then took a yoke of oxen and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout the territory of Israel by the hand of messengers, saying, “Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, the same shall be done to his oxen.” Then the dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one person.

column.name: text
column.value: He ①counted them in Bezek; and the sons of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah, thirty thousand. ▷ ①Lit mustered

column.name: text
column.value: They said to the messengers who had come, “This is what you shall say to the men of Jabesh-gilead: ‘Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you will be saved.’ ” So the messengers went and told the men of Jabesh; and they rejoiced.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Jabesh said, “Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good ①to you.” ▷ ①Lit in your sight

column.name: text
column.value: The next morning Saul put the people in three companies; and they came into the midst of the camp at the morning watch, and struck and killed the Ammonites until the heat of the day. And those who survived scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people said to Samuel, “Who is he that said, ‘Shall Saul reign over us?’ ①Bring the men, so that we may put them to death!” ▷ ①Lit Give

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul said, “Not a single person shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has brought about ①victory in Israel.” ▷ ①Or deliverance in

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to the people, “Come, and let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there.”

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they also offered sacrifices of peace offerings before the LORD; and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to all Israel, “Behold, I have listened to your voice for all that you said to me, and I have appointed a king over you.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, here is the king walking before you, but as for me, I am old and gray, and my sons are here with you. And I have walked before you since my youth to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Here I am; testify against me before the LORD and His anointed. Whose ox have I taken, or whose donkey have I taken, or whom have I exploited? Whom have I oppressed, or from whose hand have I taken a bribe to close my eyes with it? I will return it to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “You have not exploited us or oppressed us, or taken anything from anyone’s hand.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to them, “The LORD is witness against you, and His anointed is witness this day that you have found nothing in my hand.” And they said, “He is witness.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to the people, “It is the LORD who ①appointed Moses and Aaron and who brought your fathers up from the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, take your stand, so that I may enter into judgment with you before the LORD concerning all the righteous acts of the LORD that He did for you and your fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jacob went into Egypt and your fathers cried out to the LORD, then the LORD sent Moses and Aaron ①who brought your fathers out of Egypt and settled them in this place. ▷ ①Lit and they brought

column.name: text
column.value: But they forgot the LORD their God, so He sold them into the hand of Sisera, commander of the army of Hazor, and into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the king of Moab, and they fought against them.

column.name: text
column.value: They cried out to the LORD and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have abandoned the LORD and have served the Baals and the Ashtaroth; but now save us from the hands of our enemies, and we will serve You.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD sent Jerubbaal, ①Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel, and saved you from the hands of your enemies all around, so that you lived in security. ▷ ①LXX and Syriac Barak

column.name: text
column.value: But when you saw that Nahash the king of the sons of Ammon was coming against you, you said to me, ‘No, but a king shall reign over us!’ Yet the LORD your God was your king.

column.name: text
column.value: And now, behold, the king whom you have chosen, whom you have asked for, and behold, the LORD has ①put a king over you. ▷ ①Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: If you will fear the LORD and serve Him, and listen to His voice and not rebel against the ①command of the LORD, then both you and the king who reigns over you will follow the LORD your God. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD, but rebel against the ①command of the LORD, then the hand of the LORD will be against you, even as it was against your fathers. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Even now, take your stand and see this great thing which the LORD is going to do before your eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: Is it not the wheat harvest today? I will call to the LORD, that He will send ①thunder and rain. Then you will know and see that your wickedness is great which you have done in the sight of the LORD, by asking for yourselves a king.” ▷ ①Lit sounds

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel called to the LORD, and the LORD sent ①thunder and rain that day; and all the people greatly feared the LORD and Samuel. ▷ ①Lit sounds

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the people said to Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for your servants, so that we do not die; for we have added to all our sins this evil, by asking for ourselves a king.”

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said to the people, “Do not fear. You have committed all this evil, yet do not turn aside from following the LORD, but serve the LORD with all your heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, you must not turn aside, for then you would go after useless things which cannot benefit or save, because they are useless.

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD will not abandon His people on account of His great name, because the LORD has been pleased to make you a people for Himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, as for me, far be it from me that I would sin against the LORD by ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and right way.

column.name: text
column.value: Only ①fear the LORD and serve Him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things He has done for you. ▷ ①Or revere

column.name: text
column.value: But if you still do evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was ①thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for ②forty-two years over Israel. ▷ ①As in some LXX mss, but very uncertain; MT one year old ②See Acts 13:21; Heb two years

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul chose for himself three thousand men of Israel, of whom two thousand were with Saul in Michmash and in the hill country of Bethel, while a thousand were with Jonathan at Gibeah of Benjamin. But he sent the rest of the people away, each to his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan attacked the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Then Saul blew the trumpet throughout the land, saying, “Let the Hebrews hear!”

column.name: text
column.value: And all Israel heard ①the news that Saul had attacked the garrison of the Philistines, and also that Israel had become repulsive to the Philistines. Then the people were summoned ②to Saul at Gilgal. ▷ ①Lit saying ②Lit after

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines assembled to fight with Israel, thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen, and people like the sand which is on the seashore in abundance; and they came up and camped in Michmash, east of Beth-aven.

column.name: text
column.value: When the men of Israel saw that they were in trouble (for the people were hard-pressed), then the people kept themselves hidden in caves, in crevices, in cliffs, in crypts, and in pits.

column.name: text
column.value: And some of the Hebrews crossed the Jordan into the land of Gad and Gilead. But as for Saul, he was still in Gilgal, and all the people followed him, trembling.

column.name: text
column.value: Now he waited for seven days, until the appointed time that Samuel had set, but Samuel did not come to Gilgal; and the people were scattering from him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said, “Bring me the burnt offering and the peace offerings.” And he offered the burnt offering.

column.name: text
column.value: But as soon as he finished offering the burnt offering, behold, Samuel came; and Saul went out to meet him and to ①greet him. ▷ ①Lit bless

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, “What have you done?” And Saul said, “Since I saw that the people were scattering from me, and that you did not come at the appointed ①time, and that the Philistines were assembling at Michmash, ▷ ①Lit time of days

column.name: text
column.value: I ①thought, ‘Now the Philistines will come down against me at Gilgal, and I have not ②asked the favor of the LORD.’ So I worked up the courage and offered the burnt offering.” ▷ ①Lit said ②Or appeased

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said to Saul, “You have acted foolishly! You have not kept the commandment of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, for the LORD would now have established your kingdom ①over Israel forever. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: But now your kingdom shall not endure. The LORD has sought for Himself a man ①after His own heart, and the LORD has appointed him ruler over His people, because you have not kept what the LORD commanded you.” ▷ ①Lit like His

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel set out and went up from Gilgal to Gibeah of Benjamin. And Saul ①counted the people who were ②present with him, about six hundred men. ▷ ①Lit mustered ②Lit found

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul, his son Jonathan, and the people who were ①present with them were staying in Geba of Benjamin while the Philistines camped at Michmash. ▷ ①Lit found

column.name: text
column.value: Then ①raiders came from the camp of the Philistines in three ②companies: one ③company turned ④toward Ophrah, to the land of Shual, ▷ ①Lit destroyers ②Lit heads ③Lit head ④Lit to the way of

column.name: text
column.value: and another ①company turned ②toward Beth-horon, and another ③company turned ④toward the border that overlooks the Valley of Zeboim toward the wilderness. ▷ ①Lit head ②Lit the way of ③Lit head ④Lit the way of

column.name: text
column.value: Now no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines said, “Otherwise the Hebrews will make ①swords or spears.” ▷ ①Lit sword or spear

column.name: text
column.value: So all Israel went down to the Philistines, each to sharpen his plowshare, his mattock, his axe, and his hoe.

column.name: text
column.value: The charge was ①two-thirds of a shekel for the plowshares, the mattocks, the forks, and the axes, and to fix the ②cattle goads. ▷ ①Heb pim ②I.e., spiked sticks for driving cattle

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about on the day of battle that neither sword nor spear was found in the hands of any of the people who were with Saul and Jonathan, but they were found with Saul and his son Jonathan.

column.name: text
column.value: And the garrison of the Philistines went out to the gorge of Michmash.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD said to Samuel, “How long are you going to mourn for ①Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and go; I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite, because I have chosen a king for Myself among his sons.” ▷ ①I.e., God’s rejection of Saul

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, “How can I go? When Saul hears about it, he will kill me.” But the LORD said, “Take a heifer ①with you and say, ‘I have come to sacrifice to the LORD.’ ▷ ①Lit by your hand

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will let you know what you shall do; and you shall anoint for Me the one whom I ①designate to you.” ▷ ①Lit say to you

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel did what the LORD told him, and he came to Bethlehem. Then the elders of the city came trembling to meet him and said, “Do you come in peace?”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “In peace; I have come to sacrifice to the LORD. Consecrate yourselves and come with me to the sacrifice.” He also consecrated Jesse and his sons and invited them to the sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: When they entered, he looked at Eliab and thought, “Surely the LORD’S anointed is standing before Him.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Do not look at his appearance or at the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for ①God does not see as man sees, since man looks at ②the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.” ▷ ①As in LXX; MT, He does not see what man sees ②Lit the eyes; or what is before the eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him pass before Samuel. But he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.”

column.name: text
column.value: Next Jesse had ①Shammah pass by. And he said, “The LORD has not chosen this one, either.” ▷ ①In 2 Sam 13:3, Shimeah; in 1 Chr 2:13, Shimea

column.name: text
column.value: So Jesse had seven of his sons pass before Samuel. But Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen these.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to Jesse, “Are these all the boys?” And he said, “The youngest is still left, but behold, he is tending the sheep.” So Samuel said to Jesse, “Send word and bring him; for we will not take our places at the table until he comes here.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent word and brought him in. Now he was ①reddish, with beautiful eyes and a handsome appearance. And the LORD said, “Arise, anoint him; for this is he.” ▷ ①I.e., of reddish hair or skin

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the midst of his brothers; and the Spirit of the LORD rushed upon David from that day forward. And Samuel set out and went to Ramah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Spirit of the LORD left Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD terrified him.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul’s servants then said to him, “Behold now, an evil spirit from God is terrifying you.

column.name: text
column.value: May our lord now command your servants who are before you. Have them search for a man who is a skillful musician on the harp; and it shall come about whenever the evil spirit from God is upon you, that he shall play the harp with his hand, and you will become well.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to his servants, “Now select for me a man who can play well, and bring him to me.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of the young men responded and said, “Behold, I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite who is a skillful musician, a valiant mighty man, a warrior, skillful in speech, and a handsome man; and the LORD is with him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse ①to say, “Send me your son David, who is with the flock.” ▷ ①Lit and said

column.name: text
column.value: And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread and a jug of wine, and he took a young goat, and sent them to Saul by his son David.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David came to Saul and ①attended him; and Saul greatly loved him, and he became his armor bearer. ▷ ①Lit stood before him

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul sent word to Jesse, saying, “Let David now ①be my attendant for he has found favor in my sight.” ▷ ①Lit stand before me

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about whenever the evil spirit from God came to Saul, David would take the harp and play it with his hand; and Saul would feel relieved and become well, and the evil spirit would leave him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to Saul, “The LORD sent me to anoint you as king over His people, over Israel; now therefore, listen to the ①words of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit sound of the words

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD of armies says: ‘I will ①punish Amalek for what he did to Israel, in that he obstructed him on the way while he was coming up from Egypt. ▷ ①Or visit

column.name: text
column.value: Now go and strike Amalek and completely destroy everything that he has, and do not spare him; but put to death both man and woman, child and infant, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul summoned the people and ①counted them in Telaim: two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah. ▷ ①Lit mustered

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul came to the city of Amalek and set an ambush in the ①wadi. ▷ ①Or valley

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul said to the Kenites, “Go, get away, go down from among the Amalekites, so that I do not destroy you along with them; for you showed kindness to all the sons of Israel when they went up from Egypt.” So the Kenites got away from among the Amalekites.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul ①defeated the Amalekites, from Havilah ②going toward Shur, which is ③east of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit as you go ③Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: He captured Agag the king of the Amalekites alive, and completely destroyed all the people with the edge of the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep, the oxen, the more valuable animals, the lambs, and everything that was good, and were unwilling to destroy them completely; but everything despicable and weak, that they completely destroyed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “I regret that I have made Saul king, because he has turned back from ①following Me and has not carried out My commands.” And Samuel was furious and cried out to the LORD all night. ▷ ①Lit after

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel got up early in the morning to meet Saul; and it was reported to Samuel, saying, “Saul came to Carmel, and behold, he set up a monument for himself, then turned and proceeded on ①down to Gilgal.” ▷ ①Lit and went down

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel came to Saul, and Saul said to him, “Blessed are you of the LORD! I have carried out the command of the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, “What then is this ①bleating of the sheep in my ears, and the ②bellowing of the oxen which I hear?” ▷ ①Lit sound ②Lit sound

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, “They have brought them from the Amalekites, for the people spared the best of the sheep and oxen to sacrifice to the LORD your God; but the rest we have completely destroyed.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said to Saul, “Stop, and let me inform you of what the LORD said to me last night.” And he said to him, “Speak!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel said, “ ①Is it not true, though you were ②insignificant in your own eyes, that you became the head of the tribes of Israel? For the LORD anointed you as king over Israel. ▷ ①Or Though you were..., did you not become ②Lit small

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD sent you on a ①mission, and said, ‘Go and completely destroy the sinners, the Amalekites, and fight against them until they are eliminated.’ ▷ ①Lit way

column.name: text
column.value: Why then did you not obey the voice of the LORD? Instead, you loudly rushed upon the spoils and did what was evil in the sight of the LORD!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I did obey the voice of the LORD, for I went on the ①mission on which the LORD sent me; and I have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have completely destroyed the Amalekites. ▷ ①Lit way

column.name: text
column.value: But the people took some of the spoils, sheep and oxen, the choicest of the things designated for destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said, “Does the LORD have as much delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices As in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than a sacrifice, And to pay attention is better than the fat of rams.

column.name: text
column.value: For rebellion is as reprehensible as the sin of divination, And insubordination is as reprehensible as false religion and idolatry. Since you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has also rejected you from being king.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned, for I have violated the ①command of the LORD and your words, because I feared the people and listened to their voice. ▷ ①Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, please pardon my sin and return with me, so that I may worship the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said to Saul, “I will not return with you; for you have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you from being king over Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel turned to go, but Saul grasped the edge of his robe, and it tore off.

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel said to him, “The LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel from you today and has given it to your neighbor, who is better than you.

column.name: text
column.value: Also the ①Glory of Israel will not lie nor change His mind; for He is not a man, that He would change His mind.” ▷ ①Or Splendor

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “I have sinned; but please honor me now before the elders of my people and before all Israel, and go back with me, so that I may worship the LORD your God.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Samuel went back following Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel said, “Bring me Agag, the king of the Amalekites.” And Agag came to him ①cheerfully. And Agag said, “Surely the bitterness of death is gone!” ▷ ①Or in chains

column.name: text
column.value: But Samuel said, “As your sword has made women childless, so shall your mother be childless among women.” And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel went to Ramah, but Saul went up to his house at Gibeah of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel did not see Saul again until the day of his death, though Samuel mourned for ①Saul. And the LORD regretted that He had made Saul king over Israel. ▷ ①I.e., God’s rejection of Saul

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines gathered their armies for battle; and they were gathered at Socoh which belongs to Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and the men of Israel were assembled and camped in the Valley of Elah, and they drew up in battle formation to confront the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines were standing on the mountain on one side, while Israel was standing on the mountain on the other side, with the valley between them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a champion came forward from the army encampment of the Philistines, named Goliath, from Gath. His height was ①six cubits and a ②span. ▷ ①About 9 ft. or 2.7 m ②About 9 in. or 23 cm

column.name: text
column.value: And he had a bronze helmet on his head, and he wore scale-armor ①which weighed ②five thousand shekels of bronze. ▷ ①Lit and the weight of the armor was ②Possibly 75-125 lb. (shekel weight varied)

column.name: text
column.value: He also had bronze ①greaves on his legs and a bronze ②saber slung between his shoulders. ▷ ①I.e., shin guards ②Lit scimitar was

column.name: text
column.value: The shaft of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the head of his spear weighed ①six hundred shekels of iron; and his shield-carrier walked in front of him. ▷ ①Possibly 8-14 lb.

column.name: text
column.value: He stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel and said to them, “Why do you come out to draw up in battle formation? Am I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul? Choose a man as your representative and have him come down to me.

column.name: text
column.value: If he is able to fight me and ①kill me, then we will become your servants; but if I prevail against him and ②kill him, then you shall become our servants and serve us.” ▷ ①Lit strike ②Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistine said, “I have defied the ranks of Israel this day! Give me a man, so that we may fight together.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, they were dismayed and very fearful.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David was the son of ①the Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah, the man whose name was Jesse, and he had eight sons. And ②Jesse was old in the days of Saul, advanced in years among men. ▷ ①Lit this ②Lit the man

column.name: text
column.value: The three older sons of Jesse had ①followed Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who had gone into the battle were Eliab the firstborn, and second to him, Abinadab, and the third, Shammah. ▷ ①Lit gone; they went after

column.name: text
column.value: So David was the youngest. Now the three oldest followed Saul,

column.name: text
column.value: but David went back and forth from Saul to tend his father’s flock at Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistine came forward morning and evening, and took his stand for forty days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jesse said to his son David, “Take now for your brothers an ephah of this roasted grain and these ten loaves, and run to the camp to your brothers.

column.name: text
column.value: Bring also these ten slices of cheese to the commander of their thousand, and look into the well-being of your brothers and bring back ①confirmation from them. ▷ ①Lit their pledge

column.name: text
column.value: For Saul and they and all the men of Israel are in the Valley of Elah, fighting the Philistines.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David got up early in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and took the supplies and went as Jesse had commanded him. And he came to the entrenchment encircling the camp while the army was going out in battle formation, shouting the war cry.

column.name: text
column.value: Israel and the Philistines drew up in battle formation, army against army.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David left the baggage in the ①care of the baggage keeper and ran to the battle line. And he entered and ②greeted his brothers. ▷ ①Lit hand ②Lit inquired about his brothers’ well-being

column.name: text
column.value: As he was speaking with them, behold, the champion, the Philistine from Gath named Goliath, was coming up from the army of the Philistines, and he spoke these same words; and David heard him.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the men of Israel saw the man, they fled from him and were very fearful.

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of Israel said, “Have you seen this man who is coming up? Surely he is coming up to defy Israel. And it will be that the king will make the man who kills him wealthy with great riches, and will give him his daughter and make his father’s house ①free in Israel.” ▷ ①I.e., exempt from taxes and public service

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the men who were standing by him, “What will be done for the man who kills this Philistine and rids Israel of the disgrace? For who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has dared to defy the armies of the living God?”

column.name: text
column.value: The people ①answered him in agreement with this statement, saying, “This is what will be done for the man who kills him.” ▷ ①Lit said to

column.name: text
column.value: Now Eliab his oldest brother heard him when he spoke to the men; and Eliab’s anger burned against David and he said, “Why is it that you have come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I myself know your insolence and the wickedness of your heart; for you have come down in order to see the battle.”

column.name: text
column.value: But David said, “What have I done now? Was it not just a ①question?” ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: Then he turned ①away from him to another and said the same thing; and the people replied with the same words as ②before. ▷ ①Lit from beside him ②Lit the former word

column.name: text
column.value: When the words that David spoke were heard, they informed ①Saul, and he ②sent for him. ▷ ①Lit before Saul ②Lit took him

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Saul, “May no one’s heart fail on account of him; your servant will go and fight this Philistine!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul said to David, “You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight him; for you are only a youth, while he has been a warrior since his youth.”

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Saul, “Your servant was tending his father’s sheep. When a lion or a bear came and took a sheep from the flock,

column.name: text
column.value: I went out after it and ①attacked it, and rescued the sheep from its mouth; and when it rose up against me, I grabbed it by its mane and struck it and killed it. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant has ①killed both the lion and the bear; and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, since he has defied the armies of the living God.” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And David said, “The LORD who saved me from the paw of the lion and the paw of the bear, He will save me from the hand of this Philistine.” So Saul said to David, “Go, and may the LORD be with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul clothed David with his military attire and put a bronze helmet on his head, and outfitted him with armor.

column.name: text
column.value: And David strapped on his sword over his military attire and struggled at walking, for he had not trained with the armor. So David said to Saul, “I cannot go with these, because I have not trained with them.” And David took them ①off. ▷ ①Lit off from himself

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the brook, and put them in the shepherd’s bag which he had, that is, in his shepherd’s pouch, and his sling was in his hand; and he approached the Philistine.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Philistine came and approached David, with the shield-bearer in front of him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Philistine looked and saw David, he was contemptuous of him; for he was only a youth, and ①reddish, with a handsome appearance. ▷ ①I.e., of reddish hair or complexion

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistine said to David, “Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?” And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistine also said to David, “Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the sky and the ①wild animals.” ▷ ①Lit beast of the field

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, a spear, and a ①saber, but I come to you in the name of the LORD of armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied. ▷ ①Lit scimitar

column.name: text
column.value: This day the LORD will hand you over to me, and I will strike you and remove your head from you. Then I will give the dead bodies of the army of the Philistines this day to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: and that this entire assembly may know that the LORD does not save by sword or by spear; for the battle is the LORD’S, and He will hand you over to us!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened, when the Philistine ①came closer to meet David, that David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet the Philistine. ▷ ①Lit arose and came

column.name: text
column.value: And David put his hand into his bag and took from it a stone and slung it, and struck the Philistine on his forehead. And the stone penetrated his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: So David prevailed over the Philistine with the sling and the stone: he struck the Philistine and killed him, and there was no sword in David’s hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David ran and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and finished him, and cut off his head with it. When the Philistines saw that their champion was dead, they fled.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up and shouted, and they pursued the Philistines ①as far as the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the Philistine dead ②lay along the way to Shaaraim, even to Gath and Ekron. ▷ ①Lit until your coming to ②Lit fell

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of Israel returned from their close pursuit of the Philistines, and plundered their camps.

column.name: text
column.value: And David took the Philistine’s head and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his weapons in his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Saul had seen David going out against the Philistine, he said to Abner the commander of the army, “Abner, whose son is this young man?” And Abner said, “By your life, O king, I do not know.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said, “You then, ask whose son the youth is.”

column.name: text
column.value: So when David returned from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul with the Philistine’s head in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to him, “Whose son are you, young man?” And David answered, “I am the son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when he had finished speaking to Saul, that ①Jonathan committed himself to David, and Jonathan loved him as himself. ▷ ①Lit the soul of Jonathan was joined to the soul of

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul took him that day and did not let him return to his father’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan made a covenant with David because he loved him as himself.

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him and gave it to David, with his military gear, including his sword, his bow, and his belt.

column.name: text
column.value: And David went into battle wherever Saul sent him, and always ①achieved success; so Saul put him in charge of the men of war. And it was pleasing in the sight of all the people, and also in the sight of Saul’s servants. ▷ ①Or acted wisely

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened as they were coming, when David returned from killing the Philistine, that the women came out of all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet King Saul, with tambourines, with joy and with other ①musical instruments. ▷ ①Possibly three-stringed lutes

column.name: text
column.value: The women sang as they ①played, and said, “Saul has slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands.” ▷ ①Or danced

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul became very angry, for this lyric ①displeased him; and he said, “They have given David credit for ten thousands, but to me they have given credit for only thousands! Now what more can he have but the kingdom?” ▷ ①Lit was evil in his eyes

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul eyed David with suspicion from that day on.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about on the next day that an evil spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved in the midst of the house while David was playing the harp with his hand, ①as usual; and ②a spear was in Saul’s hand. ▷ ①Lit day by day ②Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul hurled the spear, for he thought, “I will ①pin David to the wall.” But David ②escaped from his presence, twice. ▷ ①Lit strike David and the wall ②Lit turned about

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul was afraid of David, because the LORD was with him but had left Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul removed him from ①his presence and appointed him as his commander of a thousand; and he went out and came in before the people. ▷ ①Lit with him

column.name: text
column.value: David was ①successful in all his ways, for the LORD was with him. ▷ ①Or acting wisely

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul saw that he was ①very successful, he was afraid of him. ▷ ①Or acting very wisely

column.name: text
column.value: But all Israel and Judah loved David, for he would go out to battle and ①return ②before them. ▷ ①Lit come in ②Or leading them

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to David, “Here is my older daughter Merab; I will give her to you as a wife, only be a valiant man for me and fight the LORD’S battles.” For Saul thought, “My hand shall not be against him, but let the hand of the Philistines be against him.”

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Saul, “Who am I, and who is my family, or my father’s family in Israel, that I should be the king’s son-in-law?”

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about at the time that Merab, Saul’s daughter, was to be given to David, that she was given instead to Adriel the Meholathite as a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David. When they informed Saul, the thing was pleasing ①to him. ▷ ①Lit in his sight

column.name: text
column.value: For Saul thought, “I will give her to him so that she may become a trap for him, and that the hand of the Philistines may be against him.” Therefore Saul said to David, “For a second time you may become my son-in-law, today.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul commanded his servants, “Speak to David in secret, saying, ‘Behold, the king delights in you, and all his servants love you; now then, become the king’s son-in-law.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul’s servants spoke these words ①to David. But David said, “Is it trivial in your sight to become the king’s son-in-law, since I am only a poor man and insignificant?” ▷ ①Lit in the ears of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul’s servants reported to him, saying, “ ①These are the words David spoke.” ▷ ①Lit According to these words David

column.name: text
column.value: Saul then said, “This is what you shall say to David: ‘The king does not desire any dowry except a hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to take vengeance on the king’s enemies.’ ” But Saul plotted to have David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: When his servants told David these words, ①it pleased David to become the king’s son-in-law. So ②before the time had expired, ▷ ①Lit the thing was pleasing in the sight of ②Lit the days were not fulfilled, and

column.name: text
column.value: David set out and went, he and his men, and fatally struck two hundred men among the Philistines. Then David brought their foreskins, and they presented all two hundred of them to the king, so that he might become the king’s son-in-law. And Saul gave him his daughter Michal as a wife.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul saw and realized that the LORD was with David, and that Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved him,

column.name: text
column.value: then Saul was even more afraid of David. So Saul was David’s enemy continually.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commanders of the Philistines went to battle, and it happened as often as they went out, that David was more ①successful than all the servants of Saul. So his name was held in high esteem. ▷ ①Or wise

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul told his son Jonathan and all his servants to put David to death. But Jonathan, Saul’s son, greatly delighted in David.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jonathan informed David, saying, “My father Saul is seeking to put you to death. Now then, please be on your guard in the morning, and stay in a hiding place and conceal yourself.

column.name: text
column.value: And as for me, I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where you are hiding, and I will speak with my father about you; and whatever I ①find out, I will tell you.” ▷ ①Lit see

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul and said to him, “May the king not sin against his servant David, since he has not sinned against you, and since his deeds have been very ①beneficial to you. ▷ ①Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: For he took his life in his hand and struck the Philistine, and the LORD brought about a great ①victory for all Israel; you saw it and rejoiced. Why then would you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death ②for no reason?” ▷ ①Lit deliverance ②Or undeservedly

column.name: text
column.value: Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan, and Saul vowed, “As the LORD lives, David shall not be put to death.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan called David, and Jonathan told him all these words. And Jonathan brought David to Saul, and he was in his presence as before.

column.name: text
column.value: When there was war again, David went out and fought the Philistines and ①defeated them with great slaughter, so that they fled from him. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was an evil spirit from the LORD on Saul as he was sitting in his house with his spear in his hand, and David was playing the harp with his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul tried to ①pin David to the wall with the spear, but he escaped from Saul’s presence, so that he stuck the spear into the wall. And David fled and escaped that night. ▷ ①Lit strike David and the wall

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent messengers to David’s house to watch him, in order to put him to death in the morning. But Michal, David’s wife, informed him, saying, “If you do not save your life tonight, tomorrow you will be put to death!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Michal let David down through a window, and he went and fled, and escaped.

column.name: text
column.value: And Michal took the ①household idol and laid it on the bed, and put a quilt of goats’ hair at its head, and covered it with clothing. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul sent messengers to take David, she said, “He is sick.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent messengers to see David, saying, “Bring him up to me on ①his bed, so that I may put him to death.” ▷ ①Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: When the messengers entered, behold, the ①household idol was on the bed with the quilt of goats’ hair at its head. ▷ ①Heb teraphim

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to Michal, “Why have you betrayed me like this and let my enemy go, so that he has escaped?” And Michal said to Saul, “He said to me, ‘Let me go! Why should I put you to death?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So David fled and escaped, and came to Samuel at Ramah; and he informed him of everything that Saul had done to him. And he and Samuel went and stayed in Naioth.

column.name: text
column.value: But it was reported to Saul, saying, “Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul sent messengers to take David, but when they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing and presiding over them, the Spirit of God came upon the messengers of Saul; and they also prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul was informed of this, he sent other messengers, but they also prophesied. So Saul sent messengers again the third time, yet they prophesied.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went to Ramah himself and came as far as the large well that is in Secu; and he ①asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” And someone said, “Behold, they are at Naioth in Ramah.” ▷ ①Lit asked and said

column.name: text
column.value: So he ①proceeded there to Naioth in Ramah; but the Spirit of God came upon him also, so that he went along prophesying continually until he came to Naioth in Ramah. ▷ ①Lit went

column.name: text
column.value: He also stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied before Samuel and ①lay down ②naked all that day and all night. Therefore they say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?” ▷ ①Lit fell ②I.e., without outward garments

column.name: text
column.value: Then David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and he came and said ①to Jonathan, “What have I done? What is my guilt? And what is my sin before your father, that he is seeking my life?” ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: He said to him, “Far from it, you shall not die! Behold, my father does nothing either great or small ①without informing me. So why would my father hide this thing from me? It is not so!” ▷ ①Lit and he does not uncover my ear

column.name: text
column.value: Yet David vowed again, ①saying, “Your father is well aware that I have found favor in your sight, and he has said, ‘Jonathan is not to know this, otherwise he will be worried.’ But indeed as the LORD lives and as your soul lives, there is ②just a step between me and death.” ▷ ①Lit and said ②Lit about

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to David, “Whatever ①you say, I will do for you.” ▷ ①Lit your soul says

column.name: text
column.value: So David said to Jonathan, “Behold, tomorrow is the new moon, and I am obligated to sit down to eat with the king. But let me go so that I may hide myself in the field until the third evening.

column.name: text
column.value: If your father misses me at all, then say, ‘David earnestly requested leave of me to run to Bethlehem, his city, because it is the yearly sacrifice there for the whole family.’

column.name: text
column.value: If he ①says, ‘That is good,’ your servant will be safe; but if he is very angry, be aware that he has decided on evil. ▷ ①Lit says thus

column.name: text
column.value: So deal kindly with your servant, for you have brought your servant into a covenant of the LORD with you. But if ①I am guilty of wrongdoing, kill me yourself; for why then should you bring me to your father?” ▷ ①Lit guilt exists in me

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said, “Far be it from you! For if I in fact learn that my father has decided ①to inflict harm on you, would I not inform you?” ▷ ①Lit evil to come on

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Jonathan, “Who will inform me ①if your father answers you harshly?” ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT or what your father

column.name: text
column.value: Jonathan said to David, “Come, and let’s go out to the field.” So both of them went out to the field.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to David, “The LORD, the God of Israel, is my witness! When I have sounded out my father about this time tomorrow or the third day, behold, if he has a good feeling toward ①you, shall I not then send word to you and ②inform you? ▷ ①Lit David ②Lit uncover your ear

column.name: text
column.value: If it pleases my father to do you harm, may the LORD do so to ①me and more so, if I fail to ②inform you and send you away, so that you may go in safety. And may the LORD be with you as He has been with my father. ▷ ①Lit Jonathan ②Lit uncover your ear

column.name: text
column.value: And if I am still alive, will you not show me the faithfulness of the LORD, so that I do not die?

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall never cut off your loyalty to my house, not even when the LORD cuts off every one of the enemies of David from the face of the earth.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jonathan made a covenant with the house of David, saying, “May the LORD demand it from the hands of David’s enemies.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan made David vow again because of his love for him, because he loved him as he loved his own life.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon, and you will be missed since your seat will be empty.

column.name: text
column.value: When you have stayed for three days, you shall go down quickly and come to the place where you hid yourself on that eventful day, and you shall remain beside the stone Ezel.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will shoot three arrows to the side, as though I shot at a target.

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, I will send the boy, telling him, ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I specifically say to the boy, ‘Behold, the arrows are on this side of you, get them,’ then come, because it is safe for you and there is nothing to harm you, as the LORD lives.

column.name: text
column.value: But if I ①say to the youth, ‘Behold, the arrows are beyond you,’ go, because the LORD has sent you away. ▷ ①Lit say thus

column.name: text
column.value: As for the ①agreement of which you and I have spoken, behold, the LORD is between you and me forever.” ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: So David hid himself in the field; and when the new moon came, the king sat down to eat food.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king sat on his seat as usual, the seat by the wall; then Jonathan stood up and Abner sat down by Saul’s side; but David’s place was empty.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless Saul did not say anything that day, because he thought, “It must have been an ①accident; he is not clean, undoubtedly he is not clean.” ▷ ①I.e., accident of ritual pollution

column.name: text
column.value: But it came about the next day, the second day of the new moon, that David’s place was empty again; so Saul said to his son Jonathan, “Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan answered Saul, “David earnestly requested leave of me to go to Bethlehem.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, ‘Please let me go, because our family has a sacrifice in the city, and my brother has ordered me to attend. So now, if I have found favor in your sight, please let me slip away so that I may see my brothers.’ For this reason he has not come to the king’s table.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul’s anger burned against Jonathan, and he said to him, “You son of a perverse, rebellious woman! Do I not know that you are choosing the son of Jesse to your own shame, and to the shame of your mother’s nakedness?

column.name: text
column.value: For, ①as long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be established. Now then, send men and bring him to me, for he is ②doomed to die!” ▷ ①Lit all the days which ②Lit a son of death

column.name: text
column.value: But Jonathan replied to his father Saul and said to him, “Why must he be put to death? What has he done?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul hurled his spear at him to strike and kill him; so Jonathan knew that his father had decided to put David to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan got up from the table in the heat of anger, and did not eat food on the second day of the new moon, because he was worried about David since his father had insulted him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in the morning that Jonathan went out to the field at the time agreed upon with David, and a little boy was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to his boy, “Run, find now the arrows which I am about to shoot.” The boy ran, and he shot ①an arrow past him. ▷ ①Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: When the boy reached the location of the arrow which Jonathan had shot, Jonathan called after the boy and said, “Is the arrow not beyond you?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan called after the boy, “Hurry, be quick, do not stay!” And Jonathan’s boy picked up the arrow and came to his master.

column.name: text
column.value: But the boy was not aware of anything; only Jonathan and David knew about the matter.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan gave his weapons to his boy and said to him, “Go, bring them to the city.”

column.name: text
column.value: When the boy was gone, David got up from the south side, then he fell on his face to the ground and bowed three times. And they kissed each other and wept together, until David wept immeasurably.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to David, “Go ①in safety, since we have sworn to each other in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘The LORD will be between me and you, and between my ②descendants and your ③descendants forever.’ ” ④So David set out and went on his way, while Jonathan went into the city. ▷ ①Lit to peace ②Lit seed ③Lit seed ④Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Now the day came that Jonathan, the son of Saul, said to the young man who was carrying his armor, “Come, and let’s cross over to the Philistines’ garrison that is on the other side.” But he did not tell his father.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul was staying on the outskirts of Gibeah under the pomegranate tree that is in Migron. And the people who were with him numbered about six hundred men;

column.name: text
column.value: and Ahijah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod’s brother, the son of Phinehas, the son of Eli, the priest of the LORD at Shiloh, was ①wearing an ephod. And the people did not know that Jonathan had gone. ▷ ①Lit carrying

column.name: text
column.value: Now between the gorges by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistines’ garrison there was a rocky crag on the one side, and a rocky crag on the other side; and the name of the one was Bozez, and the name of the other, Seneh.

column.name: text
column.value: The one crag rose on the north opposite Michmash, and the other on the south opposite Geba.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said to the young man who was carrying his armor, “Come, and let’s cross over to the garrison of these uncircumcised men; perhaps the LORD will work for us, because the LORD is not limited to saving by many or by few!”

column.name: text
column.value: His armor bearer said to him, “Do everything that is in your heart; turn yourself to it, and here I am with you, as your heart desires.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said, “Behold, we are going to cross over to the men and reveal ourselves to them.

column.name: text
column.value: If they ①say to us, ‘Wait until we come to you’; then we will stand in our place and not go up to them. ▷ ①Lit say thus

column.name: text
column.value: But if they ①say, ‘Come up to us,’ then we will go up, for the LORD has handed them over to us; and this shall be the sign to us.” ▷ ①Lit say thus

column.name: text
column.value: When the two of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Philistines, the Philistines said, “Behold, Hebrews are coming out of the holes where they have kept themselves hidden.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the men of the garrison responded to Jonathan and his armor bearer and said, “Come up to us and we will inform you of something.” And Jonathan said to his armor bearer, “Come up after me, for the LORD has handed them over to Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan climbed up on his hands and feet, with his armor bearer behind him; and the men fell before Jonathan, and his armor bearer put some to death after him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now that first slaughter which Jonathan and his armor bearer inflicted was about twenty men within about half a furrow in an acre of land.

column.name: text
column.value: And there was a trembling in the camp, in the field, and among all the people. Even the garrison and the raiders trembled, and the earth quaked so that it became a ①great trembling. ▷ ①Lit trembling of God

column.name: text
column.value: Now Saul’s watchmen in Gibeah of Benjamin looked, and behold, the multitude dissolved; they went here and there.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to the people who were with him, “Look carefully now and see who has left us.” And when they had looked, behold, Jonathan and his armor bearer were not there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to Ahijah, “Bring the ark of God here.” For at that time the ark of God was with the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: While Saul talked to the priest, the commotion in the camp of the Philistines continued and increased; so Saul said to the priest, “Withdraw your hand.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul and all the people who were with him rallied and came to the battle; and behold, every man’s sword was against his fellow Philistine, and there was very great confusion.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Hebrews who were with the Philistines previously, who went up with them all around in the camp, even they also returned to be with the Israelites who were with Saul and Jonathan.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the men of Israel who had kept themselves hidden in the hill country of Ephraim heard that the Philistines had fled, they also closely pursued them in the battle.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD saved Israel that day, and the battle ①spread beyond Beth-aven. ▷ ①Lit passed over

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men of Israel were hard-pressed on that day, for Saul had put the people under oath, saying, “Cursed be the man who eats food ①before evening, and before I have avenged myself on my enemies.” So none of the people tasted food. ▷ ①Lit until

column.name: text
column.value: All the people of the land entered the forest, and there was honey on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: When the people entered the forest, behold, there was honey dripping; but no man put his hand to his mouth, because the people feared the oath.

column.name: text
column.value: However, Jonathan had not heard it when his father put the people under oath; so he put out the end of the staff that was in his hand and dipped it in the honeycomb, and put his hand to his mouth, and his eyes ①brightened. ▷ ①As in some mss and ancient versions; MT saw

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of the people responded and said, “Your father strictly put the people under oath, saying, ‘Cursed be the man who eats food today.’ ” And the people were weary.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jonathan said, “My father has troubled the land. See now that my eyes have brightened because I tasted a little of this honey.

column.name: text
column.value: How much more, if only the people had freely eaten today of the spoils of their enemies which they found! For now the defeat among the Philistines has not been great.”

column.name: text
column.value: They attacked the Philistines that day from Michmash to Aijalon. But the people were very tired.

column.name: text
column.value: So the people loudly rushed upon the spoils, and took sheep, oxen, and calves, and slaughtered them on the ground; and the people ate them with the blood.

column.name: text
column.value: Then observers informed Saul, saying, “Look, the people are sinning against the LORD by eating meat with the blood.” And he said, “You have acted treacherously; roll a large rock to me today.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “Disperse yourselves among the people and say to them, ‘Each one of you bring me his ox or his sheep, and slaughter it here and eat; and do not sin against the LORD by eating it with the blood.’ ” So all the people brought them that night, each one his ox ①with him, and they slaughtered them there. ▷ ①Lit with his hand

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul built an altar to the LORD; it was the first altar that he built to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “Let’s go down after the Philistines by night and take plunder among them until the morning light, and let’s not leave a man among them alive.” And they said, “Do whatever seems good ①to you.” So the priest said, “Let’s approach God here.” ▷ ①Lit in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul inquired of God: “Shall I go down after the Philistines? Will You hand them over to Israel?” But He did not answer him on that day.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “ ①Come here, all you ②leaders of the people, and investigate and see how this sin has happened today. ▷ ①Lit Approach here ②Lit cornerstones

column.name: text
column.value: For as the LORD lives, who saves Israel, even if it is in my son Jonathan, he shall assuredly die!” But not one of all the people answered him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to all Israel, “You shall be on one side, and I and my son Jonathan will be on the other side.” And the people said to Saul, “Do what seems good ①to you.” ▷ ①Lit in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, Saul said to the LORD, the God of Israel, “Give a ①perfect lot.” And Jonathan and Saul were selected by lot, but the people ②were exonerated. ▷ ①I.e., a clear answer ②Lit got out

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “Cast lots between me and my son Jonathan.” And Jonathan was selected by lot.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul said to Jonathan, “Tell me what you have done.” And Jonathan told him, and said, “I did indeed taste a little honey with the end of the staff that was in my hand. Here I am, I must die!”

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul said, “May God do the same to me and more also, for you shall certainly die, Jonathan!”

column.name: text
column.value: But the people said to Saul, “Must Jonathan die, he who has ①brought about this great ②victory in Israel? Far from it! As the LORD lives, not even a hair of his head shall fall to the ground, because he has worked with God this day.” So the people ③rescued Jonathan and he did not die. ▷ ①Lit worked ②Lit deliverance ③Lit ransomed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul went up from ①pursuing the Philistines, and the Philistines went to their own place. ▷ ①Lit after

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Saul had taken control of the kingdom over Israel, he fought against all his enemies on every side, against Moab, the sons of Ammon, Edom, the kings of Zobah, and the Philistines; and wherever he turned, he ①inflicted punishment. ▷ ①Or condemned

column.name: text
column.value: And he acted valiantly and ①defeated the Amalekites, and saved Israel from the hands of ②those who plundered them. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit its plunderer

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, Ishvi, and Malchi-shua; and the names of his two daughters were these: the name of the firstborn was Merab, and the name of the younger, Michal.

column.name: text
column.value: And the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam the daughter of Ahimaaz. And the name of the commander of his army was Abner the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle.

column.name: text
column.value: Kish was the father of Saul, and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the war against the Philistines was severe all the days of Saul; and when Saul saw any warrior or any valiant man, he ①attached him to his staff. ▷ ①Lit brought him in to himself

column.name: text
column.value: Then David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest; and Ahimelech came trembling to meet David and said to him, “Why are you alone, and no one with you?”

column.name: text
