column.value: David said to Ahimelech the priest, “The king has commissioned me with a matter and has said to me, ‘No one is to know anything about the matter on which I am sending you and with which I have commissioned you; and I have directed the young men to a certain place.’

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, what ①do you have on hand? Give ②me five loaves of bread, or whatever can be found.” ▷ ①Lit is there under your hand? ②Lit into my hand

column.name: text
column.value: The priest answered David and said, “There is no ordinary bread ①on hand, but there is consecrated bread, if only the young men have kept themselves from women.” ▷ ①Lit under my hand

column.name: text
column.value: David answered the priest and said to him, “Be assured, women have been denied to us as previously when I left and the ①bodies of the young men were consecrated, though it was an ordinary journey; how much more then will ②their bodies be consecrated today?” ▷ ①Lit vessels ②Lit it be holy in the vessel

column.name: text
column.value: So the priest gave him consecrated bread; for there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence which was removed from its place before the LORD, in order to put hot bread in its place on the day it was taken away.

column.name: text
column.value: Now one of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the LORD; and his name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul’s shepherds.

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Ahimelech, “Now is there no spear or sword ①on hand? For I brought neither my sword nor my weapons ②with me, because the king’s matter was urgent.” ▷ ①Lit under your hand ②Lit in my hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then the priest said, “The sword of Goliath the Philistine, whom you ①killed in the Valley of Elah, behold, it is wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod; if you would take it for yourself, take it. For there is no other except it here.” And David said, “There is none like it; give it to me.” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then David set out and fled that day from Saul, and went to Achish king of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: But the servants of Achish said to him, “Is this not David, the king of the land? Did they not sing of this one as they danced, saying, ‘Saul has slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands’?”

column.name: text
column.value: David took these words ①to heart and greatly feared Achish king of Gath. ▷ ①Lit in his

column.name: text
column.value: So he disguised his sanity while in their sight and acted insanely in their ①custody, and he scribbled on the doors of the gate, and drooled on his beard. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then Achish said to his servants, “Look, you see the man is behaving like an insane person. Why do you bring him to me?

column.name: text
column.value: Do I lack insane people, that you have brought this one to behave like an insane person in my presence? Shall this one come into my house?”

column.name: text
column.value: So David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam; and when his brothers and all his father’s household heard about it, they went down there to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then everyone who was in distress, and everyone who ①was in debt, and everyone who was ②discontented gathered to him; and he became captain over them. Now there were about four hundred men with him. ▷ ①Lit had a creditor ②Lit bitter of soul

column.name: text
column.value: And David went from there to Mizpah of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and my mother come and stay with you until I know what God will do for me.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he ①left them with the king of Moab; and they stayed with him all the time that David was in the stronghold. ▷ ①Probable reading of the Heb; MT brought them before

column.name: text
column.value: But Gad the prophet said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold; leave, and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went into the forest of Hereth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the height with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing in front of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said to his servants who were standing in front of him, “Hear now, you Benjaminites! Will the son of Jesse really give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make you all commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

column.name: text
column.value: For all of you have conspired against me so that there is no one who ①informs me when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you who cares about me or ②informs me that my son has stirred up my servant against me to lie in ambush, as it is this day.” ▷ ①Lit uncovers my ear ②Lit uncovers my ear

column.name: text
column.value: Then Doeg the Edomite, who was ①standing in front of the servants of Saul, responded and said, “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub. ▷ ①Or set over

column.name: text
column.value: And he inquired of the LORD for him, gave him provisions, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent a messenger to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s household, the priests who were in Nob; and all of them came to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, “Listen now, son of Ahitub.” And he ①replied, “Here I am, my lord.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Saul then said to him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me, in that you have given him bread and a sword, and have inquired of God for him, so that he would rise up against me by lying in ambush as it is this day?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahimelech answered the king and said, “And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s own son-in-law, who ①is commander over your bodyguard, and is honored in your house? ▷ ①As in LXX; MT turns aside to

column.name: text
column.value: Did I just begin to inquire of God for him today? Far be it from me! Do not let the king impute anything against his servant or against any of the household of my father, because your servant knows nothing ①at all of this whole affair.” ▷ ①Lit small or great

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, “You shall certainly die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s household!”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to the ①guards who were attending him, “Turn around and put the priests of the LORD to death, because their hand also is with David and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not ②inform me.” But the servants of the king were unwilling to reach out with their hands to ③attack the priests of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit runners ②Lit uncover my ear ③Lit fall upon

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Doeg, “You, turn around and ①attack the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned around and ②attacked the priests, and he killed on that day eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod. ▷ ①Lit fall upon ②Lit fell upon

column.name: text
column.value: He also struck Nob the city of the priests with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and infants; he also struck oxen, donkeys, and sheep with the edge of the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: But one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped and fled ①to David. ▷ ①Lit after

column.name: text
column.value: Abiathar informed David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would certainly tell Saul. I myself ①have turned against every person in your father’s household. ▷ ①LXX am responsible for

column.name: text
column.value: Stay with me; do not be afraid, ①even though he who is seeking my life is seeking your life. For you are safe with me.” ▷ ①Or because he

column.name: text
column.value: ①Now when Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, it was reported to him, saying, “Behold, David is in the wilderness of Engedi.” ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to search for David and his men in front of the Rocks of the Mountain Goats.

column.name: text
column.value: And he came to the sheepfolds on the way, where there was a cave; and Saul went in to ①relieve himself. Now David and his men were sitting in the inner recesses of the cave. ▷ ①Lit cover his feet

column.name: text
column.value: Then David’s men said to him, “Behold, this is the day of which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold; I am about to hand your enemy over to you, and you shall do to him as it seems good ①to you.’ ” Then David got up and cut off the edge of Saul’s robe secretly. ▷ ①Lit in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: But it came about afterward that David’s ①conscience bothered him because he had cut off the edge of Saul’s robe. ▷ ①Lit heart struck

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to his men, “Far be it from me because of the LORD that I would do this thing to my lord, the LORD’S anointed, to reach out with my hand against him, since he is the LORD’S anointed.”

column.name: text
column.value: And David rebuked his men with these words and did not allow them to rise up against Saul. And Saul got up, ①left the cave, and went on his way. ▷ ①Lit from

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward, however, David got up and went out of the cave, and called after Saul, saying, “My lord the king!” And when Saul looked behind him, David bowed with his face to the ground and prostrated himself.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men ①who say, ‘Behold, David is seeking ②to harm you’? ▷ ①Lit saying ②Lit your harm

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, this day your eyes have seen that the LORD had handed you over to me today in the cave, and someone said to kill you, but ①I spared you; and I said, ‘I will not reach out with my hand against my lord, because he is the LORD’S anointed.’ ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT, my eye had pity on

column.name: text
column.value: So, my father, look! Indeed, look at the edge of your robe in my hand! For by the fact that I cut off the edge of your robe but did not kill you, know and understand that there is no evil or ①rebellion in my hands, and I have not sinned against you, though you are lying in wait for my life, to take it. ▷ ①Lit offense

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD judge between ①you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you for me; but my hand shall not be against you. ▷ ①Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Out of the wicked comes wickedness’; but my hand shall not be against you.

column.name: text
column.value: After whom has the king of Israel gone out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog, a single flea?

column.name: text
column.value: May the LORD therefore be judge and decide between ①you and me; and may He see and plead my cause and save me from your hand.” ▷ ①Lit me and you

column.name: text
column.value: When David had finished speaking these words to Saul, Saul said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” Then Saul raised his voice and wept.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to David, “You are more righteous than I; for you have dealt well with me, while I have dealt maliciously with you.

column.name: text
column.value: You have declared today that you have done good to me, that the LORD handed me over to you and yet you did not kill me.

column.name: text
column.value: Though if a man finds his enemy, will he let him go away ①unharmed? May the LORD therefore reward you with good in return for what you have done to me this day. ▷ ①Lit on a good road

column.name: text
column.value: Now, behold, I know that you will certainly be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: So now swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my ①descendants after me, and that you will not eliminate my name from my father’s household.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: And David swore an oath to Saul. Then Saul went to his home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Samuel died; and all Israel assembled and mourned for him, and they buried him at his house in Ramah. And David set out and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel; and the man was very ①rich, and he had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats. And it came about while he was shearing his sheep in Carmel ▷ ①Lit great

column.name: text
column.value: (now the man’s name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. And the woman was ①intelligent and beautiful in appearance, but the man was harsh and evil in his dealings, and he was a Calebite), ▷ ①Lit of good understanding

column.name: text
column.value: that David heard in the wilderness that Nabal was shearing his sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: So David sent ten young men; and David said to the young men, “Go up to Carmel and ①visit Nabal, and greet him in my name; ▷ ①Lit come to

column.name: text
column.value: and this is what you shall say: ‘ ①Have a long life, peace to you, and peace to your house, and peace to all that you have! ▷ ①Lit To life

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, I have heard that you have shearers. Now, your shepherds have been with us; we have not harmed them, nor has anything of theirs gone missing all the days they were in Carmel.

column.name: text
column.value: Ask your young men and they will tell you. Therefore let my young men find favor in your eyes, for we have come on a ①festive day. Please give whatever you find at hand to your servants and to your son David.’ ” ▷ ①Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: When David’s young men came, they spoke to Nabal in accordance with all these words in David’s name; then they waited.

column.name: text
column.value: But Nabal answered David’s servants and said, “Who is David? And who is the son of Jesse? There are many servants today who are each breaking away from his master.

column.name: text
column.value: Shall I then take my bread and my water and my meat that I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men ①whose origin I do not know?” ▷ ①Lit from where they are

column.name: text
column.value: So David’s young men made their way back and returned; and they came and informed him in accordance with all these words.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to his men, “Each of you strap on his sword.” So each man strapped on his sword. And David also strapped on his sword, and about four hundred men went up behind David, while two hundred stayed with the baggage.

column.name: text
column.value: Now one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, saying, “Behold, David sent messengers from the wilderness to ①greet our master, and he spoke to them in anger. ▷ ①Lit bless

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the men were very good to us, and we were not harmed, nor did anything go missing ①as long as we went with them, while we were in the fields. ▷ ①Lit all the days

column.name: text
column.value: They were a wall to us both by night and by day, all the time we were with them tending the sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, be aware and ①consider what you should do, because harm is plotted against our master and against all his household; and he is such a ②worthless man that no one can speak to him.” ▷ ①Lit see ②Lit son of Belial

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread and two jugs of wine, and five sheep already prepared and five measures of roasted grain, and a hundred cakes of raisins and two hundred cakes of figs, and she loaded them on donkeys.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said to her young men, “Go on ahead of me; behold, I am coming after you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.

column.name: text
column.value: And it happened as she was riding on her donkey and coming down by the hidden part of the mountain, that behold, David and his men were coming down toward her; so she met them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David had said, “It is certainly for nothing that I have guarded everything that this man has in the wilderness, so that nothing has gone missing of all that belonged to him! For he has returned me evil for good.

column.name: text
column.value: May God do so to the enemies of David, and more so, if by morning I leave alive as much as one ①male of any who belong to him.” ▷ ①Lit who urinates against the wall

column.name: text
column.value: When Abigail saw David, she hurried and dismounted from her donkey, and fell on her face in front of David and bowed herself to the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: She fell at his feet and said, “On me ①alone, my lord, be the blame. And please let your slave speak ②to you, and listen to the words of your slave. ▷ ①Lit myself ②Lit in your ears

column.name: text
column.value: Please do not let my lord ①pay attention to this ②worthless man, Nabal, for as his name is, so is he. ③Nabal is his name, and stupidity is with him; but I your slave did not see the young men of my lord whom you sent. ▷ ①Lit set his heart to ②Lit man of Belial ③I.e., fool

column.name: text
column.value: “Now then, my lord, as the LORD lives, and as your soul lives, since the LORD has restrained you from ①shedding blood, and from ②avenging yourself by your own hand, now then, may your enemies and those who seek evil against my lord, be like Nabal. ▷ ①Lit coming in with blood ②Lit helping

column.name: text
column.value: And now let this ①gift which your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who ②accompany my lord. ▷ ①Lit blessing ②Lit walk at the feet of

column.name: text
column.value: Please forgive the offense of your slave; for the LORD will certainly make for my lord an ①enduring house, because my lord is fighting the battles of the LORD, and evil will not be found in you all your days. ▷ ①Or permanent

column.name: text
column.value: Should anyone rise up to pursue you and to seek your ①life, then the ②life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living with the LORD your God; but the ③lives of your enemies He will sling out ④as from the hollow of a sling. ▷ ①Lit soul ②Lit soul ③Lit soul ④Lit in the midst of

column.name: text
column.value: And when the LORD does for my lord in accordance with all the good that He has spoken concerning you, and appoints you ruler over Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: this will not become an obstacle to you, or a ①troubled heart to my lord, both by having shed blood without cause and by my lord’s having ②avenged himself. When the LORD deals well with my lord, then remember your slave.” ▷ ①Lit stumbling of heart ②Lit helped

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who sent you this day to meet me,

column.name: text
column.value: and blessed be your discernment, and blessed be you, who have kept me this day from ①bloodshed and from ②avenging myself by my own hand. ▷ ①Lit coming into blood ②Lit helping

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, as the LORD God of Israel lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, there certainly would not have been left to Nabal until the morning light as much as one ①male.” ▷ ①Lit who urinates against the wall

column.name: text
column.value: So David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and said to her, “Go up to your house in peace. See, I have listened to ①you and ②granted your request.” ▷ ①Lit your voice ②Lit lifted up your face

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abigail came to Nabal, and behold, he was having a feast in his house, like the feast of a king. And Nabal’s heart was cheerful within him, for he was very drunk; so she did not tell him anything ①at all until the morning light. ▷ ①Lit small or large

column.name: text
column.value: But in the morning, when the wine had gone out of Nabal, his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him so that he became like a stone.

column.name: text
column.value: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: When David heard that Nabal was dead, he said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has pleaded the cause of the shame inflicted on me by the hand of Nabal, and has kept back His servant from evil. The LORD has also returned the evildoing of Nabal on his own head.” Then David sent ①a proposal to Abigail, to take her as his wife. ▷ ①Lit and spoke

column.name: text
column.value: When the servants of David came to Abigail at Carmel, they spoke to her, saying, “David has sent us to you to take you to him as his wife.”

column.name: text
column.value: And she got up and bowed with her face to the ground, and said, “Behold, your slave is a servant to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abigail got up quickly, and rode on a donkey, with her five female attendants who ①accompanied her; and she followed the messengers of David and became his wife. ▷ ①Lit walked at her feet

column.name: text
column.value: David had also taken Ahinoam of Jezreel, and they both became his wives.

column.name: text
column.value: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti the son of Laish, who was from Gallim.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to ①himself, “Now I will ②perish one day by the hand of Saul. There is nothing better for me than to safely escape into the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will despair of searching for me anymore in all the territory of Israel, and I will escape from his hand.” ▷ ①Lit his heart ②Lit be carried away

column.name: text
column.value: So David set out and went over, he and the six hundred men who were with him, to Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath.

column.name: text
column.value: And David lived with Achish in Gath, he and his men, each with his own household—David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal’s ①widow. ▷ ①Lit wife

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was reported to Saul that David had fled to Gath, so he no longer searched for him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Achish, “If now I have found favor in your sight, have them give me a place in one of the cities in the country, so that I may live there; for why should your servant live in the royal city with you?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; therefore Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: The number of days that David lived in the country of the Philistines was a year and four months.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David and his men went up and attacked the Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites; for they were the inhabitants of the land from ancient times, as you come to Shur even as far as the land of Egypt.

column.name: text
column.value: David ①attacked the land and did not leave a man or a woman alive, and he took the sheep, the cattle, the donkeys, the camels, and the clothing. Then he returned and came to Achish. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Now Achish said, “ ①Where did you carry out an attack today?” And David said, “Against the ②Negev of Judah, against the ③Negev of the Jerahmeelites, and against the ④Negev of the Kenites.” ▷ ①DSS indicate Against whom ②I.e., South country ③I.e., South country ④I.e., South country

column.name: text
column.value: And David did not leave a man or a woman alive to bring to Gath, saying, “Otherwise they will tell about us, saying, ‘This is what David has done, and this has been his practice all the time that he has lived in the country of the Philistines.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So Achish believed David, saying, “He has undoubtedly made himself repulsive among his people Israel; therefore he will become my servant forever.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not keeping himself hidden on the hill of Hachilah, which is opposite ①Jeshimon?” ▷ ①Or the desert

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul set out and went down to the wilderness of Ziph, ①taking with him three thousand chosen men of Israel, to search for David in the wilderness of Ziph. ▷ ①Lit and with him

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul camped on the hill of Hachilah, which is opposite ①Jeshimon, beside the road, and David was staying in the wilderness. When he saw that Saul had come after him into the wilderness, ▷ ①Or the desert

column.name: text
column.value: David sent out spies, and he learned that Saul was definitely coming.

column.name: text
column.value: David then set out and came to the place where Saul had camped. And David saw the place where Saul lay, and Abner the son of Ner, the commander of his army; and Saul was lying in the circle of the camp, and the people were camped around him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, saying, “Who will go down with me to Saul in the camp?” And Abishai said, “I will go down with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David and Abishai came to the people by night, and behold, Saul lay sleeping inside the circle of the camp with his spear stuck in the ground at his head; and Abner and the people were lying around him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abishai said to David, “Today God has handed your enemy over to you; now then, please let me ①pin him with the spear to the ground with one thrust, and I will not ②do it to him a second time.” ▷ ①Lit strike him...even into ②Lit repeat it to him

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Abishai, “Do not ①kill him, for who can reach out with his hand against the LORD’S anointed and remain innocent?” ▷ ①Lit destroy

column.name: text
column.value: David also said, “As the LORD lives, the LORD certainly will strike him, or his day will come that he dies, or he will go down in battle and ①perish. ▷ ①Lit be carried away

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD forbid that I would reach out with my hand against the LORD’S anointed! But now please take the spear that is at his head and the jug of water, and let’s go.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David took the spear and the jug of water that were at Saul’s head, and they left; and no one saw or knew about it, nor did anyone awaken, for they were all asleep, because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the mountain at a distance with a large area between them.

column.name: text
column.value: And David called to the people and to Abner the son of Ner, saying, “Will you not answer, Abner?” Then Abner replied, “Who are you who calls to the king?”

column.name: text
column.value: So David said to Abner, “Are you not a man? And who is like you in Israel? Why then have you not guarded your lord the king? For one of the people came to ①kill the king your lord! ▷ ①Lit destroy

column.name: text
column.value: This thing that you have done is not good. As the LORD lives, all of you undoubtedly ①must die, because you did not guard your lord, the LORD’S anointed. And now, see where the king’s spear is and the jug of water that was at his head!” ▷ ①Lit are sons of death

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is this your voice, my son David?” And David said, “It is my voice, my lord the king.”

column.name: text
column.value: He also said, “Why then is my lord pursuing his servant? For what have I done? Or what evil is in my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, please let my lord the king listen to the words of his servant. If the LORD has incited you against me, may He ①accept an offering; but if it is ②people, cursed ③are they before the LORD, because they have driven me out today so that I would have no share in the inheritance of the LORD, saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’ ▷ ①Lit smell ②Lit the sons of mankind ③Or may they be

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the presence of the LORD; for the king of Israel has come out to search for a single flea, just as one hunts a partridge in the mountains.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said, “I have sinned. Return, my son David, for I will not harm you again since my life was precious in your sight this day. Behold, I have played the fool and have made a very great mistake.”

column.name: text
column.value: David replied, “Behold, the spear of the king! Now have one of the young men come over and take it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD will repay each man for his righteousness and his faithfulness; for the LORD handed you over to me today, but I refused to reach out with my hand against the LORD’S anointed.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore behold, just as your life was highly valued in my sight this day, so may my life be highly valued in the sight of the LORD, and may He rescue me from all distress.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, my son David; you will both accomplish much and assuredly prevail.” So David went on his way, and Saul returned to his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in those days that the Philistines gathered their armed camps for war, to fight against Israel. And Achish said to David, “Know for certain that you will go out with me in the camp, you and your men.”

column.name: text
column.value: David said to Achish, “Very well, you will learn what your servant can do.” So Achish said to David, “Then I will assuredly make you ①my bodyguard for ②life!” ▷ ①Lit guardian of my head ②Lit all the days

column.name: text
column.value: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had mourned him and buried him in Ramah, his own city. And Saul had removed the mediums and spiritists from the land.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Philistines assembled and came and camped in Shunem; and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they camped in Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul saw the camp of the Philistines, he was afraid and his heart trembled greatly.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, either in dreams, or by the Urim, or by the prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to his servants, “Find for me a woman who is a medium, so that I may go to her and inquire of her.” And his servants said to him, “Behold, there is a woman who is a medium at En-dor.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul disguised himself by putting on different clothes, and went, he and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night; and he said, “Consult the spirit for me, please, and bring up for me the one whom I shall ①name for you.” ▷ ①Lit say

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman said to him, “Behold, you know what Saul has done, that he has eliminated the mediums and spiritists from the land. Why are you then setting a trap for my life, to bring about my death?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul swore an oath to her by the LORD, saying, “As the LORD lives, no punishment shall come upon you for this thing.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman said, “Whom shall I bring up for you?” And he said, “Bring up Samuel for me.”

column.name: text
column.value: When the woman saw Samuel, she cried out with a loud voice; and the woman spoke to Saul, saying, “Why have you deceived me? For you are Saul!”

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said to her, “Do not be afraid; but what do you see?” And the woman said to Saul, “I see a ①divine being coming up from the earth.” ▷ ①Or god

column.name: text
column.value: He said to her, “ ①How does he appear?” And she said, “An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe.” Then Saul knew that it was Samuel, and he bowed with his face to the ground and paid ②homage. ▷ ①Lit What is his form ②I.e., great respect and honor to a superior

column.name: text
column.value: And Samuel said to Saul, “Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?” Saul replied, “I am very distressed, for the Philistines are waging war against me, and God has abandoned me and no longer answers me, either through prophets or in dreams; therefore I have called you, so that you may let me know what I should do.”

column.name: text
column.value: Samuel said, “But why ask me, since the LORD has abandoned you and has become your enemy?

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD has done ①just as He spoke through me; for the LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David. ▷ ①Lit for Himself just; another reading is to you just

column.name: text
column.value: Just as you did not ①obey the LORD and did not execute His fierce wrath on Amalek, so the LORD has done this thing to you this day. ▷ ①Lit listen to the voice of

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, the LORD will also hand Israel along with you over to the Philistines; so tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. Indeed, the LORD will hand the army of Israel over to the Philistines!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul immediately fell full length to the ground and was very afraid because of Samuel’s words; there was no strength in him either, because he had eaten no ①food all day and all night. ▷ ①Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: The woman came to Saul and saw that he was utterly horrified, and she said to him, “Behold, your servant has ①obeyed you, and I have ②taken my life in my hand and have listened to your words which you spoke to me. ▷ ①Lit listened to your voice ②Lit put

column.name: text
column.value: So now you too, please listen to the voice of your servant, and let me serve you a piece of bread, and eat it, so that you will have strength when you go on your way.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he refused and said, “I will not eat.” However, his servants together with the woman urged him, and he listened to ①them. So he got up from the ground and sat on the bed. ▷ ①Lit their voice

column.name: text
column.value: Now the woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it; then she took flour, kneaded it and baked unleavened bread from it.

column.name: text
column.value: She then served it to Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and left that night.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines gathered together all their armies to Aphek, while the Israelites were camping by the spring which is in Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: And the governors of the Philistines were proceeding on, leading hundreds and thousands, and David and his men were proceeding in the back with Achish.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commanders of the Philistines said, “What are these Hebrews doing here?” And Achish said to the commanders of the Philistines, “Is this not David, the servant of Saul the king of Israel, who has been with me these days, or rather these years, and I have found nothing at all suspicious in him since the day he ①deserted to me to this day?” ▷ ①Lit fell

column.name: text
column.value: But the commanders of the Philistines were angry with him, and the commanders of the Philistines said to him, “Make the man go back, so that he will return to his place where you have assigned him, and do not let him go down to battle with us, or in the battle he may become an adversary to us. For how could this man find favor with his lord? Would it not be with the heads of ①these men? ▷ ①Lit those

column.name: text
column.value: Is this not David, of whom they sing in the dances, saying, ‘Saul has slain his thousands, And David his ten thousands’?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Achish called David and said to him, “As the LORD lives, you have indeed been honest, and your ①going out and your coming in with me in the army are pleasing in my sight; for I have not found evil in you since the day of your coming to me to this day. Nevertheless, you are not pleasing in the sight of the governors. ▷ ①I.e., performance of duties

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, return and go in peace, so that you will not do anything wrong in the sight of the governors of the Philistines.”

column.name: text
column.value: However, David said to Achish, “But what have I done? And what have you found in your servant since the day that I came before you, to this day, that I cannot go and fight against the enemies of my lord the king?”

column.name: text
column.value: But Achish replied to David, “I know that you are pleasing in my sight, like an angel of God; nevertheless the commanders of the Philistines have said, ‘He must not go up with us into the battle.’

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, rise early in the morning with the servants of your lord who have come with you, and as soon as you have risen early in the morning and have light, leave.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David got up early, he and his men, to leave in the morning to return to the land of the Philistines. And the Philistines went up to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel, and the men of Israel fled from the Philistines but fell fatally wounded on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines also overtook Saul and his sons, and the Philistines ①killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, the sons of Saul. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: The battle went heavily against Saul, and the archers found him; and he was gravely wounded by the archers.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Saul said to his armor bearer, “Draw your sword and pierce me through with it, otherwise these uncircumcised Philistines will come and pierce me through, and abuse me.” But his armor bearer was unwilling, because he was very fearful. So Saul took ①his sword and fell on it. ▷ ①Lit the sword

column.name: text
column.value: When his armor bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell on his sword and died with him.

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul died with his three sons, his armor bearer, and all his men on that day together.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the people of Israel who were on the other side of the valley, with those who were beyond the Jordan, saw that the men of Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned the cities and fled; then the Philistines came and settled in them.

column.name: text
column.value: It came about on the next day, when the Philistines came to strip those killed, that they found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa.

column.name: text
column.value: They cut off his head and stripped off his weapons, and sent them ①throughout the land of the Philistines, to bring the good news to the house of their idols and to the people. ▷ ①Lit into...Philistines on all sides

column.name: text
column.value: They put his weapons in the ①temple of Ashtaroth, and they nailed his body to the wall of Beth-shan. ▷ ①Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead heard ①what the Philistines had done to Saul, ▷ ①Lit about him, what

column.name: text
column.value: all the valiant men got up and walked all night, and they took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons from the wall of Beth-shan, and they came to Jabesh and burned them there.

column.name: text
column.value: And they took their bones and buried them under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted for seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they informed David, saying, “Behold, the Philistines are fighting against Keilah and are plundering the threshing floors.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go and ①attack these Philistines?” And the LORD said to David, “Go and ②attack the Philistines and save Keilah.” ▷ ①Lit strike ②Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: But David’s men said to him, “Behold, we are fearful here in Judah. How much more then if we go to Keilah against the ranks of the Philistines?”

column.name: text
column.value: So David inquired of the LORD once more. And the LORD answered him and said, “Arise, go down to Keilah, for I am going to hand the Philistines over to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines; and he drove away their livestock and struck them with a great slaughter. So David saved the inhabitants of Keilah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when Abiathar the son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, that he came down with an ephod in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: When it was reported to Saul that David had come to Keilah, Saul said, “God has handed him over to me, for he shut himself in by entering a city with double gates and bars.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul summoned all the people for war, to go down to Keilah to besiege David and his men.

column.name: text
column.value: But David knew that Saul was plotting evil against him; so he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, “LORD God of Israel, Your servant has heard for certain that Saul is seeking to come to Keilah to destroy the city on my account.

column.name: text
column.value: Will the citizens of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down just as Your servant has heard? LORD God of Israel, please, tell Your servant.” And the LORD said, “He will come down.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, “Will the citizens of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?” And the LORD said, “They will hand you over.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and his men, about six hundred, rose up and departed from Keilah, and they went wherever they could go. When it was reported to Saul that David had escaped from Keilah, he gave up ①the pursuit. ▷ ①Lit going out

column.name: text
column.value: David stayed in the wilderness in the strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph. And Saul searched for him every day, but God did not hand him over to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David saw that Saul had come out to seek his life while David was in the wilderness of Ziph, at Horesh.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonathan, Saul’s son, set out and went to David at Horesh, and ①encouraged him in God. ▷ ①Lit strengthened his hand

column.name: text
column.value: He said to him, “Do not be afraid, because the hand of Saul my father will not find you, and you will be king over Israel, and I will be second in command to you; and Saul my father knows that as well.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the two of them made a covenant before the LORD; and David stayed at Horesh, while Jonathan went to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ziphites came up to Saul at Gibeah, saying, “Is David not keeping himself hidden with us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, which is south of ①Jeshimon? ▷ ①Or the desert

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, O king, come down, ①since you fully desire to ②do so; and our part shall be to hand him over to the king.” ▷ ①Lit according to all your soul’s desire ②Lit come down

column.name: text
column.value: Saul said, “May you be blessed of the LORD, since you have had compassion on me.

column.name: text
column.value: Go now, be more persistent, and investigate and see his place where ①he is hiding, and who has seen him there; for I am told that he is very cunning. ▷ ①Lit his foot is

column.name: text
column.value: So look, and learn about all the hiding places where he keeps himself hidden, and return to me with certainty, and I will go with you; and if he is in the land, I will search him out among all the thousands of Judah.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they set out and went to Ziph ahead of Saul. Now David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah to the south of ①Jeshimon. ▷ ①Or the desert

column.name: text
column.value: When Saul and his men went to seek him, they informed David, and he came down to the rock and stayed in the wilderness of Maon. And when Saul heard about it, he pursued David in the wilderness of Maon.

column.name: text
column.value: Saul went on one side of the mountain, and David and his men on the other side of the mountain; and David was hurrying to get away from Saul, while Saul and his men were surrounding David and his men to apprehend them.

column.name: text
column.value: But a messenger came to Saul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have launched an attack against the land!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Saul returned from pursuing David and went to confront the Philistines; therefore they called that place ①the Rock of Division. ▷ ①Heb Sela-hammahlekoth; meaning uncertain, possibly Rock of Smoothness (i.e., “Slippery Rock”)

column.name: text
column.value: ①And David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of Engedi. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, that David stayed two days in Ziklag.

column.name: text
column.value: And on the third day, behold, a man came from ①Saul’s camp with his clothes torn and ②dust on his head. And it happened when he came to David, he fell to the ground and prostrated himself. ▷ ①Lit the camp connected with Saul ②Lit earth

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to him, “From where do you come?” And he said to him, “I have escaped from the camp of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: David said to him, “How did things go? Please tell me.” And he said, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead; and Saul and his son Jonathan are also dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and his son Jonathan are dead?”

column.name: text
column.value: The young man who told him said, “By chance I happened to be on Mount Gilboa, and behold, Saul was leaning on his spear. And behold, the chariots and the horsemen had overtaken him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he looked behind himself, he saw me, and called to me. And I said, ‘Here I am.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to me, ‘Who are you?’ And I ①answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’ ▷ ①Lit said to

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to me, ‘Please stand next to me and finish me off, for ①agony has seized me because my ②life still lingers in me.’ ▷ ①Or dizziness ②Lit whole life is still in me

column.name: text
column.value: So I stood next to him and finished him off, because I knew that he could not live after he had fallen. And I took the crown which was on his head and the band which was on his arm, and I have brought them here to my lord.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them, and so also did all the men who were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: And they mourned and wept and fasted until evening for Saul and his son Jonathan, and for the people of the LORD and the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the young man who informed him, “Where are you from?” And he ①answered, “I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, “How is it you were not afraid to reach out with your hand to destroy the LORD’S anointed?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David called one of the young men and said, “Come forward, ①put him to death.” So he struck him and he died. ▷ ①Lit fall on him

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, “ ①Your blood is on your head, because your own mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have finished off the LORD’S anointed.’ ” ▷ ①I.e., his death was his own responsibility

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sang this song of mourning over Saul and his son Jonathan,

column.name: text
column.value: and he told them to teach the sons of Judah the mourning song of the bow; behold, it is written in the Book of Jashar.

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①Your beauty, Israel, is ②slaughtered on your high places! How the mighty have fallen! ▷ ①Lit pierced ②Lit The

column.name: text
column.value: Tell it not in Gath, Proclaim it not in the streets of Ashkelon, Or the daughters of the Philistines will rejoice, The daughters of the uncircumcised will celebrate.

column.name: text
column.value: Mountains of Gilboa, May there be no dew nor rain on you, or fields of offerings! For there the shield of the mighty was defiled, The shield of Saul, not anointed with oil.

column.name: text
column.value: From the blood of those ①slaughtered, from the fat of the mighty, The bow of Jonathan did not turn back, And the sword of Saul did not return ②unstained. ▷ ①Lit pierced ②Or without success

column.name: text
column.value: Saul and Jonathan, beloved and delightful in ①life, And in their deaths they were not separated; They were swifter than eagles, They were mightier than lions. ▷ ①Lit their lives

column.name: text
column.value: Daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, Who clothed you in scarlet, with jewelry, Who put gold jewelry on your apparel.

column.name: text
column.value: How the mighty have fallen in the midst of the battle! Jonathan is ①slaughtered on your high places. ▷ ①Lit pierced

column.name: text
column.value: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan; You have been ①a close friend to me. Your love for me was more wonderful Than the love of women. ▷ ①Lit very friendly to

column.name: text
column.value: How the mighty have fallen, And the weapons of war have perished!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened, when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had carried out an attack on the ①Negev and on Ziklag, and had ②overthrown Ziklag and burned it with fire; ▷ ①I.e., South country ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: and they took captive the women and all who were in it, from the small to the great, ①without killing anyone, and drove them off and went their way. ▷ ①Lit they did not kill

column.name: text
column.value: When David and his men came to the city, behold, it was burned with fire, and their wives, their sons, and their daughters had been taken captive.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David’s two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the ①widow of Nabal the Carmelite. ▷ ①Lit wife

column.name: text
column.value: Also, David was in great distress because the people spoke of stoning him, for all the people were ①embittered, each one because of his sons and his daughters. But David felt strengthened in the LORD his God. ▷ ①Lit bitter of soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Please bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.

column.name: text
column.value: And David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I pursue this band of raiders? Will I overtake them?” And He said to him, “Pursue, for you will certainly overtake them, and you will certainly rescue everyone.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David left, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the brook Besor, where some who were left behind stayed.

column.name: text
column.value: But David pursued, he and four hundred men, for two hundred who were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor stayed behind.

column.name: text
column.value: Now they found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David, and gave him bread and he ate, and they provided him water to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: They also gave him a slice of fig cake and two cakes of raisins, and he ate; then his spirit ①revived. For he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights. ▷ ①Lit returned to him

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to him, “To whom do you belong? And where are you from?” And he said, “I am a young man of Egypt, a servant of an Amalekite; and my master abandoned me when I became sick three days ago.

column.name: text
column.value: We carried out an attack on the ①Negev of the Cherethites, and on that which belongs to Judah, and on the ②Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.” ▷ ①I.e., South country ②I.e., South country

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to him, “Will you bring me down to this band of raiders?” And he said, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or hand me over to my master, and I will bring you down to this band.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now when he had brought him down, behold, they were dispersed over all the land, eating and drinking and celebrating because of all the great plunder that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And David ①slaughtered them from the twilight ②until the evening of ③the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit even until ③Lit their

column.name: text
column.value: So David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and ①rescued his two wives. ▷ ①Lit David rescued

column.name: text
column.value: And nothing of theirs was missing, whether small or great, sons or daughters, plunder, or anything that they had taken for themselves; David brought it all back.

column.name: text
column.value: So David had ①captured all the sheep and the cattle which the people drove ahead of ②the other livestock, and they said, “This is David’s plunder.” ▷ ①Lit taken ②Lit those livestock

column.name: text
column.value: When David came to the two hundred men who were too exhausted to follow David and ①had been left behind at the brook Besor, and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him, then David approached the people and greeted them. ▷ ①Lit they left them

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the wicked and ①worthless men among those who went with David said, “Since they did not go with ②us, we will not give them any of the spoils that we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his children, so that they may lead them away and leave.” ▷ ①Lit sons of Belial ②Lit me

column.name: text
column.value: But David said, “You must not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us, for He has protected us and handed over to us the band of raiders that came against us.

column.name: text
column.value: And who will listen to you in this matter? For as is the share of the one who goes down into the battle, so shall be the share of the one who stays by the baggage; they shall share alike.”

column.name: text
column.value: So it has been from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the spoils to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, “Behold, a ①gift for you from the spoils of the enemies of the LORD: ▷ ①Lit blessing

column.name: text
column.value: to those who were in Bethel, to those who were in Ramoth of the ①Negev, to those who were in Jattir, ▷ ①I.e., South country

column.name: text
column.value: to those who were in Aroer, to those who were in Siphmoth, to those who were in Eshtemoa,

column.name: text
column.value: to those who were in Racal, to those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, to those who were in the cities of the Kenites,

column.name: text
column.value: to those who were in Hormah, to those who were in Bor-ashan, to those who were in Athach,

column.name: text
column.value: to those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men walked.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a long war between the house of Saul and the house of David; and David became steadily stronger, while the house of Saul became steadily weaker.

column.name: text
column.value: Sons were born to David in Hebron: his firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess;

column.name: text
column.value: and his second, Chileab, by Abigail the ①widow of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur; ▷ ①Lit wife

column.name: text
column.value: and the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital;

column.name: text
column.value: and the sixth, Ithream, by David’s wife Eglah. These sons were born to David in Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened that while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, Abner was ①strengthening himself in the house of Saul. ▷ ①Or remaining faithful to

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul had a concubine whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah; and ①Ish-bosheth said to Abner, “Why have you gone in to my father’s concubine?” ▷ ①As in some mss and ancient versions; MT he

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner became very angry over Ish-bosheth’s ①question and said, “Am I a dog’s head that belongs to Judah? Today I show kindness to the house of Saul your father, to his brothers and to his friends, and have not let you fall into the hands of David; yet today you call me to account for wrongdoing with ②that woman? ▷ ①Lit words ②Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: May God do so to ①me, and more so, if as the LORD has sworn to David, I do not accomplish this for him: ▷ ①Lit Abner

column.name: text
column.value: to transfer the kingdom from the house of Saul, and to establish the throne of David over Israel and over Judah, from Dan even to Beersheba!”

column.name: text
column.value: And Ish-bosheth could no longer say a word in response to Abner, because he was afraid of him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner sent messengers to David at his place, saying, “Whose is the land? Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand shall be with you to bring all Israel over to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Good! I will make a covenant with you, only I require one thing of you, ①namely, that you shall not see my face unless you first bring Michal, Saul’s daughter, when you come to see ②me.” ▷ ①Lit saying ②Lit my face

column.name: text
column.value: So David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, saying, “Give me my wife Michal, to whom I was betrothed for a hundred foreskins of the Philistines.”

column.name: text
column.value: Ish-bosheth sent men and ①had her taken from her husband, from ②Paltiel the son of Laish. ▷ ①Lit took her ②In 1 Sam 25:44, Palti

column.name: text
column.value: And her husband went with her, weeping as he went, ①following her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, “Go, return.” So he returned. ▷ ①Lit after her

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abner had a ①consultation with the elders of Israel, saying, “In times past you were seeking for David to be king over you. ▷ ①Lit a word

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, do it! For the LORD has spoken regarding David, saying, ‘By the hand of My servant David ①I will save My people Israel from the hand of the Philistines, and from the hands of all their enemies.’ ” ▷ ①As in many mss and ancient versions; MT he

column.name: text
column.value: Abner also spoke ①to Benjamin; and in addition Abner went to speak ②to David in Hebron everything that seemed good to Israel and to the entire house of Benjamin. ▷ ①Lit in the ears of ②Lit in the ears of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner and twenty men with him came to David at Hebron. And David held a feast for Abner and the men who were with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner said to David, “Let me set out and go and gather all Israel to my lord the king, so that they may make a covenant with you, and that you may be king over all that your soul desires.” So David let Abner go, and he went in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: And behold, the servants of David and Joab came from a raid and brought a large amount of plunder with them; but Abner was not with David in Hebron, since he had let him go, and he had gone in peace.

column.name: text
column.value: When Joab and all the army that was with him arrived, they informed Joab, saying, “Abner the son of Ner came to the king, and he has let him go on his way, and he has gone in peace.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab came to the king and said, “What have you done? Behold, Abner came to you; why then have you let him go, so that he is already gone?

column.name: text
column.value: You know Abner the son of Ner, that he came to gain your confidence, and to learn of your ①going out and coming in and to find out everything that you are doing.” ▷ ①I.e., daily business

column.name: text
column.value: When Joab left David’s presence, he sent messengers after Abner, and they brought him back from the well of Sirah; but David did not know about it.

column.name: text
column.value: So when Abner returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside into the middle of the gate to speak with him privately, and there he struck him in the belly, so that he died on account of the blood of his brother Asahel.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward, when David heard about this, he said, “I and my kingdom are innocent before the LORD forever of the blood of Abner the son of Ner.

column.name: text
column.value: May it turn upon the head of Joab and on all his father’s house; and may there not be eliminated from the house of Joab someone who suffers a discharge, or has leprosy, or ①holds the spindle, or falls by the sword, or lacks bread.” ▷ ①I.e., an effeminate man; LXX holds on to a staff (prob. a crutch)

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had put their brother Asahel to death in the battle at Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Joab and to all the people who were with him, “Tear your clothes and put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And King David walked behind the bier.

column.name: text
column.value: And they buried Abner in Hebron; and the king raised his voice and wept at the grave of Abner, and all the people wept.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king sang a song of mourning for Abner and said, “Should Abner die as a fool dies?

column.name: text
text
column.value: Then all the people came to provide ①food for David in his distress while it was still day; but David vowed, saying, “May God do so to me, and more so, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down.” ▷ ①Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: Now all the people took note of David’s vow, and it ①pleased them, just as everything that the king did ②pleased all the people. ▷ ①Lit was good in their eyes ②Lit was good in the eyes of all

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people and all Israel understood on that day that it had not been the desire of the king to put Abner the son of Ner to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to his servants, “Do you not know that a leader and a great man has fallen in Israel this day?

column.name: text
column.value: And I am weak today, though anointed king; and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too difficult for me. May the LORD repay the evildoer in proportion to his evil.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now when ①Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, heard that Abner had died in Hebron, ②his courage failed, and all Israel was horrified. ▷ ①As in some mss; MT he ②Lit his hands dropped

column.name: text
column.value: And Saul’s son had two men who were commanders of troops: the name of the one was Baanah, and the name of the other Rechab, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, of the sons of Benjamin (for Beeroth is also considered part of Benjamin,

column.name: text
column.value: and the Beerothites fled to Gittaim and have lived there as strangers until this day).

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was disabled in both feet. He was five years old when the news of Saul and Jonathan came from Jezreel, and his nurse picked him up and fled. But it happened that in her hurry to flee, he fell and could no longer walk. And his name was ①Mephibosheth. ▷ ①In 1 Chr

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, Rechab and Baanah, departed and came to the house of Ish-bosheth in the heat of the day, while he was taking his midday rest.

column.name: text
column.value: ①And they came to the interior of the house as if ②to get wheat, and they struck him in the belly; and Rechab and his brother Baanah escaped. ▷ ①Lit And here they ②Lit takers of wheat

column.name: text
column.value: Now when they had come into the house, as he was lying on his bed in his bedroom, they struck him and killed him, and they beheaded him. And they took his head and ①traveled by way of the Arabah all night. ▷ ①Lit went

column.name: text
column.value: Then they brought the head of Ish-bosheth to David at Hebron, and said to the king, “Behold, the head of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, your enemy, who sought your life; so the LORD has given my lord the king vengeance this day on Saul and his ①descendants.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: But David replied to Rechab and his brother Baanah, sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said to them, “As the LORD lives, who has redeemed my life from all distress,

column.name: text
column.value: when the one who informed me, saying, ‘Behold, Saul is dead,’ also ①viewed himself as the bearer of good news, I seized him and killed him in Ziklag, which was the reward I gave him for his news. ▷ ①Lit was as a bearer of good news in his own eyes

column.name: text
column.value: How much more, when wicked men have killed a righteous man in his own house on his bed, shall I not now require his blood from your hands and eliminate you both from the earth?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David commanded the young men, and they killed them and cut off their hands and feet, and hung them up beside the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish-bosheth and buried it in the grave of Abner in Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about afterward that David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up to one of the cities of Judah?” And the LORD said to him, “Go up.” So David said, “Where shall I go up?” And He said, “To Hebron.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David went up there, and his two wives also, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the ①widow of Nabal the Carmelite. ▷ ①Lit wife

column.name: text
column.value: And David brought up his men who were with him, each with his household; and they settled in the cities of Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, “It was the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead, and said to them, “May you be blessed of the LORD because you have ①shown this kindness to Saul your lord, and have buried him. ▷ ①Lit done

column.name: text
column.value: And now may the LORD ①show kindness and truth to you; and I also will ②show this goodness to you, because you have done this thing. ▷ ①Lit do ②Lit do

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, let your hands be strong and be ①valiant, since Saul your lord is dead, and also the house of Judah has anointed me king over them.” ▷ ①Lit sons of valor

column.name: text
column.value: But Abner the son of Ner, commander of Saul’s army, had taken ①Ish-bosheth the son of Saul and brought him over to Mahanaim. ▷ ①I.e., man of shame; cf. 1 Chr 8:33, Eshbaal

column.name: text
column.value: And he made him king over Gilead, over the Ashurites, over Jezreel, over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, even over all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Ish-bosheth, Saul’s son, was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he was king for two years. The house of Judah, however, followed David.

column.name: text
column.value: And the ①time that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months. ▷ ①Lit number of days

column.name: text
column.value: Now Abner the son of Ner, went from Mahanaim to Gibeon with the servants of Ish-bosheth the son of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab the son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out and met ①them by the pool of Gibeon; and they sat down, ②Abner’s men on the one side of the pool and ③Joab’s men on the other side of the pool. ▷ ①Lit them together ②Lit these on ③Lit these on

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner said to Joab, “Now have the young men arise and hold a martial skills match in our presence.” And Joab said, “Have them arise!”

column.name: text
column.value: So they got up and went over by count, twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and twelve from the servants of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And each one of them seized his ①opponent by the head and thrust his sword in his ②opponent’s side; so they fell down together. Therefore that place was called ③Helkath-hazzurim, which is in Gibeon. ▷ ①Lit fellow ②Lit fellow’s ③I.e., the field of sword-edges

column.name: text
column.value: That day the battle was very severe, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated ①by the servants of David. ▷ ①Lit in front of

column.name: text
column.value: Now the three sons of Zeruiah were there, Joab, Abishai, and Asahel; and Asahel was as ①swift-footed as one of the gazelles that is in the field. ▷ ①Lit light in his feet

column.name: text
column.value: Asahel pursued Abner and did not turn ①to the right or to the left from following Abner. ▷ ①Lit to go to

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner looked behind himself and said, “Is that you, Asahel?” And he said, “It is I!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Abner said to him, “Turn aside for your own good to your right or to your left, and take hold of one of the young men for yourself, and take for yourself his equipment.” But Asahel was unwilling to turn aside from following him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner repeated again to Asahel, “Turn aside for your own good from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? How then could I ①show my face to your brother Joab?” ▷ ①Lit lift up

column.name: text
column.value: However, he refused to turn aside; so Abner struck him in the belly with the butt end of the spear, so that the spear came out at his back. And he fell there and died on the spot. And it happened that all who came thereafter to the place where Asahel had fallen and died, stood still.

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab and Abishai pursued Abner, and when the sun was going down, they came to the hill of Ammah, which is opposite Giah by way of the wilderness of Gibeon.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Benjamin gathered together behind Abner and became one troop, and they stood on the top of a hill.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abner called to Joab and said, “Should the sword devour forever? Do you not realize that it will be bitter in the end? So how long will you ①refrain from telling the people to turn back from pursuing their kinsmen?” ▷ ①Lit not tell the people

column.name: text
column.value: Joab said, “As God lives, if you had not spoken, then the people of Judah certainly would have withdrawn in the morning, each from pursuing his brother.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab blew the trumpet, and all the people halted and no longer pursued Israel, nor did they continue to fight anymore.

column.name: text
column.value: Abner and his men then went through the Arabah all that night; so they crossed the Jordan, walked all morning, and came to Mahanaim.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab returned from pursuing Abner; but he gathered all the people together, and ①nineteen of David’s servants were missing, besides Asahel. ▷ ①Lit nineteen men

column.name: text
column.value: However, the servants of David had struck and killed many of Benjamin and Abner’s men; 360 men were dead.

column.name: text
column.value: And they carried Asahel away and buried him in his father’s tomb, which was in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men traveled all night until the day ①dawned at Hebron. ▷ ①Lit dawned for them

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and ①said, “Behold, we are your bone and your flesh. ▷ ①Lit said, saying

column.name: text
column.value: Previously, when Saul was king over us, you were the one who led Israel ①out and in. And the LORD said to you, ‘You will shepherd My people Israel, and you will be a leader over Israel.’ ” ▷ ①I.e., to battle and in (returning) from battle

column.name: text
column.value: So all the elders of Israel came to the king at Hebron, and King David made a covenant with them before the LORD in Hebron; then they anointed David king over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: David was thirty years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty years.

column.name: text
column.value: At Hebron he reigned over Judah for seven years and six months, and in Jerusalem he reigned for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land; and they said to ①David, “You shall not come in here, but even those who are blind and those who limp will turn you away,” ②thinking, “David cannot enter here.” ▷ ①Lit David, saying ②Lit saying

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, David captured the stronghold of Zion, that is, the city of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites is to reach those who limp and those who are blind, who are hated by David’s soul, through the water tunnel.” For that reason they say, “People who are blind and people who limp shall not come into the house.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David lived in the stronghold, and called it the city of David. And David built all around from the ①Millo and inward. ▷ ①I.e., terraced structure

column.name: text
column.value: David became greater and greater, for the LORD God of armies was with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David with cedar trees, carpenters, and ①stonemasons; and they built a house for David. ▷ ①Lit stone wall craftsmen

column.name: text
column.value: And David realized that the LORD had appointed him as king over Israel, and that He had exalted his kingdom for the sake of His people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile David took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, after he came from Hebron; and more sons and daughters were born to David.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

column.name: text
column.value: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

column.name: text
column.value: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the Philistines heard that they had anointed David king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek out David; and when David heard about it, he went down to the stronghold.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines came and overran the Valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I go up against the Philistines? Will You hand them over to me?” And the LORD said to David, “Go up, for I will certainly hand the Philistines over to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David came to Baal-perazim and ①defeated them there; and he said, “The LORD has broken through my enemies before me like the breakthrough of waters.” Therefore he named that place ②Baal-perazim. ▷ ①Lit David struck ②I.e., the master of breakthroughs

column.name: text
column.value: And the Philistines abandoned their idols there, so David and his men carried them away.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Philistines came up once again and overran the Valley of Rephaim.

column.name: text
column.value: So David inquired of the LORD, but He said, “You shall not go directly up; circle around behind them and come at them in front of the baka-shrubs.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall be, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the baka-shrubs, then you shall ①act promptly, for then the LORD will have gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.” ▷ ①Or pay attention

column.name: text
column.value: Then David did so, just as the LORD had commanded him; he struck and killed the Philistines from ①Geba ②as far as Gezer. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 14:16, Gibeon ②Lit until you come to

column.name: text
column.value: Now David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: And David ①departed from ②Baale-judah, with all the people who were with him, to bring up from there the ark of God which is called by the Name, the very name of the LORD of armies who is ③enthroned above the cherubim. ▷ ①Lit arose and went ②I.e., Kiriath-jearim ③Lit sitting

column.name: text
column.value: They had mounted the ark of God on a new cart and moved it from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, were leading the new cart.

column.name: text
column.value: So they brought it with the ark of God from the house of Abinadab, which was on the hill; and Ahio was walking ahead of the ark.

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile, David and all the house of Israel were celebrating before the LORD with all kinds of instruments made of juniper wood, and with ①lyres, harps, tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. ▷ ①Or zithers

column.name: text
column.value: But when they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached out toward the ark of God and took hold of it, because the oxen nearly overturned it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for ①his irreverence; and he died there by the ark of God. ▷ ①Lit the

column.name: text
column.value: Then David became angry because ①of the LORD’S outburst against Uzzah; and that place has been called ②Perez-uzzah to this day. ▷ ①Lit the LORD broke through a breakthrough ②I.e., outburst against Uzzah

column.name: text
column.value: So David was afraid of the LORD that day; and he said, “How can the ark of the LORD come to me?”

column.name: text
column.value: And David was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD into the city of David with him; but David took it aside to the house of Obed-edom, the Gittite.

column.name: text
