column.value: The ark of the LORD remained in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and all his household.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was reported to King David, saying, “The LORD has blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that belongs to him, on account of the ark of God.” So David went and brought the ark of God up from the house of Obed-edom to the city of David with joy.

column.name: text
column.value: And so it was, that ①when those carrying the ark of the LORD marched six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened steer. ▷ ①Or each time those

column.name: text
column.value: And David was dancing before the LORD with all his strength, and David was wearing a linen ephod.

column.name: text
column.value: So David and all the house of Israel were bringing up the ark of the LORD with joyful shouting and the sound of the trumpet.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened, as the ark of the LORD was coming into the city of David, that Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD; and she was contemptuous of him in her heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Now they brought in the ark of the LORD and set it in its place inside the tent which David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of armies.

column.name: text
column.value: Further, he distributed to all the people, to all the multitude of Israel, both to men and women, a cake of bread, one of dates, and one of raisins to each one. Then all the people left, each to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: But when David returned to bless his own household, Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, “How the king of Israel dignified himself today! For he exposed himself today in the sight of his servants’ female slaves, as one of the rabble shamelessly exposes himself!”

column.name: text
column.value: But David said to Michal, “I was before the LORD, who preferred me to your father and to all his house, to appoint me as ruler over the people of the LORD, over Israel. So I will ①celebrate before the LORD! ▷ ①Or dance

column.name: text
column.value: And I might demean myself even more than this and be lowly in my own sight, but with the female slaves of whom you have spoken, with them I am to be held in honor!”

column.name: text
column.value: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when the king lived in his house, and the LORD had given him rest on every side from all his enemies,

column.name: text
column.value: that the king said to Nathan the prophet, “See now, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of God remains within the tent.”

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan said to the king, “Go, do all that is in your mind, for the LORD is with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: But in the same night, the word of the LORD came to Nathan, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Go and say to My servant David, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Should you build Me a house for My dwelling?

column.name: text
column.value: For I have not dwelt in a house since the day I brought up the sons of Israel from Egypt, even to this day; rather, I have been moving about in a tent, that is, in a dwelling place.

column.name: text
column.value: Wherever I have gone with all the sons of Israel, did I speak a word with one of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to shepherd My people Israel, saying, ‘Why have you not built Me a house of cedar?’ ” ’

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, this is what you shall say to My servant David: ‘This is what the LORD of armies says: “I Myself took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be leader over My people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have eliminated all your enemies from you; I will also make a great name for you, like the names of the great men who ①are on the earth. ▷ ①Or were

column.name: text
column.value: And I will establish a place for My people Israel, and will plant them, so that they may live in their own place and not be disturbed again, nor will ①malicious people oppress them anymore as previously, ▷ ①Lit sons of malice

column.name: text
column.value: even from the day that I appointed judges over My people Israel; and I will give you rest from all your enemies. The LORD also declares to you that the LORD will make a house for you.

column.name: text
column.value: When your days are finished and you ①lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your ②descendant after you, who will come from ③you, and I will establish his kingdom. ▷ ①I.e., die ②Lit seed ③Lit your bowels

column.name: text
column.value: He shall build a house for My name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.

column.name: text
column.value: I will be a father to him and he will be a son to Me; when he does wrong, I will discipline him with a rod of men and with strokes of sons of mankind,

column.name: text
column.value: but My favor shall not depart from him, as I took it away from Saul, whom I removed from you.

column.name: text
column.value: Your house and your kingdom shall endure before ①Me forever; your throne shall be established forever.” ’ ” ▷ ①As in LXX and some ancient mss; MT you

column.name: text
column.value: In accordance with all these words and all of this vision, so Nathan spoke to David.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David the king came in and sat before the LORD, and he said, “Who am I, Lord ①GOD, and who are the members of my household, that You have brought me this far? ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: And yet this was insignificant in Your eyes, Lord GOD, for You have spoken also of the house of Your servant regarding the distant future. And this is the ①custom of mankind, Lord GOD. ▷ ①Or law

column.name: text
column.value: Again what more can David say to You? For You know Your servant, Lord GOD!

column.name: text
column.value: For the sake of Your word, and according to Your heart, You have done all this greatness, to let Your servant know.

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason You are great, Lord GOD; for there is no one like You, and there is no God except You, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

column.name: text
column.value: And what one nation on the earth is like Your people Israel, whom God went to redeem for Himself as a people, and to make a name for Himself, and to do a great thing for You and awesome things for Your land, ①because of Your people whom You have redeemed for Yourself from Egypt, from other nations and their gods? ▷ ①Or before Your

column.name: text
column.value: For You have established for Yourself Your people Israel as Your own people forever, and You, LORD, have become their God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, LORD God, the word that You have spoken about Your servant and his house, confirm it forever, and do just as You have spoken,

column.name: text
column.value: so that Your name may be great forever, by saying, ‘The LORD of armies is God over Israel’; and may the house of Your servant David be established before You.

column.name: text
column.value: For You, LORD of armies, God of Israel, have ①given a revelation to Your servant, saying, ‘I will build you a house’; therefore Your servant has found ②courage to pray this prayer to You. ▷ ①Lit uncovered the ear of ②Lit his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, Lord GOD, You are God, and Your words are truth; and You have ①promised this good thing to Your servant. ▷ ①Lit spoken

column.name: text
column.value: And now, may ①it please You to bless the house of Your servant, so that it may continue forever before You. For You, Lord GOD, have spoken; and ②with Your blessing may the house of Your servant be blessed forever.” ▷ ①Lit You be resolved and bless ②Lit from

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD sent Nathan to David. And he came to him and ①said, “There were two men in a city, the one wealthy and the other poor. ▷ ①Lit said to him

column.name: text
column.value: The wealthy man had a great many flocks and herds.

column.name: text
column.value: But the poor man had nothing at all except one little ewe lamb Which he bought and nurtured; And it grew up together with him and his children. It would eat ①scraps from him and drink from his cup and lie ②in his lap, And was like a daughter to him. ▷ ①Lit his piece ②Or on his chest

column.name: text
column.value: Now a visitor came to the wealthy man, And he could not bring himself to take any animal from his own flock or his own herd, To prepare for the traveler who had come to him; So he took the poor man’s ewe lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David’s anger burned greatly against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As the LORD lives, the man who has done this certainly ①deserves to die! ▷ ①Lit is a son of death

column.name: text
column.value: So he must make restitution for the lamb four times over, since he did this thing and ①had no compassion.” ▷ ①Or showed no consideration

column.name: text
column.value: Nathan then said to David, “You yourself are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘It is I who anointed you as king over Israel, and it is I who rescued you from the hand of Saul.

column.name: text
column.value: I also gave you your master’s house and put your master’s wives ①into your care, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah; and if that had been too little, I would have added to you ②many more things like these! ▷ ①Lit on your lap; or chest ②Lit like these and like these

column.name: text
column.value: Why have you despised the word of the LORD, by doing evil in His sight? You have struck and killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, you have taken his wife as your wife, and you have slaughtered him with the sword of the sons of Ammon.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, the sword shall never leave your house, because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be your wife.’

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the LORD says: ‘Behold, I am going to raise up evil against you from your own household; I will even take your wives before your eyes and give them to your companion, and he will sleep with your wives in ①broad daylight. ▷ ①Lit the sight of this sun

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and ①in open daylight.’ ” ▷ ①Lit before the sun

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.” And Nathan said to David, “The LORD also has allowed your sin to pass; you shall not die.

column.name: text
column.value: However, since by this deed you have shown utter disrespect for the ①LORD, the child himself who is born to you shall certainly die.” ▷ ①Lit enemies of the LORD (a euphemistic reference to God); DSS word of the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nathan went to his house. L ater the LORD struck the child that Uriah’s ①widow bore to David, so that he was very sick. ▷ ①Lit wife

column.name: text
column.value: David therefore pleaded with God for the child; and David fasted and went and lay all night on the ground.

column.name: text
column.value: The elders of his household stood beside him in order to help him up from the ground, but he was unwilling and would not eat food with them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened on the seventh day that the child died. And David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Behold, while the child was still alive, we spoke to him and he did not listen to ①us. How then can we tell him that the child is dead, since he might do himself harm?” ▷ ①Lit our voice

column.name: text
column.value: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; so David said to his servants, “Is the child dead?” And they said, “He is dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David got up from the ground, washed, anointed himself, and changed his clothes; and he went into the house of the LORD and worshiped. Then he went to his own house, and when he asked, they served him food, and he ate.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his servants said to him, “What is this thing that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while he was ①alive; but when the child died, you got up and ate food.” ▷ ①Some ancient versions still alive

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, ‘Who knows, the LORD may be gracious to me, and the child may live.’

column.name: text
column.value: But now he has died; why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I am going to him, but he will not return to me.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David comforted his wife Bathsheba, and went in to her and slept with her; and she gave birth to a son, and ①he named him Solomon. Now the LORD loved him, ▷ ①Some mss she

column.name: text
column.value: and sent word through Nathan the prophet, and he named him ①Jedidiah for the LORD’S sake. ▷ ①I.e., beloved of the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, and captured the royal city.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab sent messengers to David and said, “I have fought against Rabbah, I have even captured the city of waters.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, gather the rest of the people and camp opposite the city and capture it, or I will capture the city myself and it will be named after me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So David gathered all the people and went to Rabbah, and he fought against it and captured it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took the crown of ①their king from his head; and its weight was a ②talent of gold, and it had a precious stone; and it was placed on David’s head. And he brought out the plunder of the city in great amounts. ▷ ①Or Milcom; MT Malcam, prob. a variant spelling of Milcom; cf. Zeph

column.name: text
column.value: He also brought out the people who were in it, and put some to work at saws, iron picks, and iron axes, and made ①others ②serve at the brick ③works. And he did the same to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit them ②Another reading of MT lit pass through ③Lit mold; i.e., for molding bricks

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was after this that Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister whose name was Tamar, and Amnon the son of David was in love with her.

column.name: text
column.value: But Amnon was so frustrated on account of his sister Tamar that he made himself ill, for she was a virgin, and it ①seemed too difficult to Amnon to do anything to her. ▷ ①Lit was too difficult in Amnon’s eyes

column.name: text
column.value: But Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab, the son of ①Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab was a very clever man. ▷ ①In 1 Sam 16:9, Shammah; in 1 Chr 2:13, Shimea

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to him, “Why are you, the king’s son, so depressed morning after morning? Will you not tell me?” So Amnon said to him, “I am in love with Tamar, the sister of my brother Absalom.”

column.name: text
column.value: Jonadab then said to him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be ill; when your father comes to see you, say to him, ‘Please have my sister Tamar come and give me food to eat, and have her prepare the ①food in my sight, so that I may see it and eat from her hand.’ ” ▷ ①I.e., food for the sick

column.name: text
column.value: So Amnon lay down and pretended to be ill; when the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, “Please have my sister Tamar come and make me a couple of pastries in my sight, so that I may eat from her hand.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sent a messenger to the house for Tamar, saying, “Go now to your brother Amnon’s house, and prepare ①food for him.” ▷ ①I.e., food for the sick

column.name: text
column.value: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house, and he was lying in bed. And she took dough, kneaded it, made pastries in his sight, and baked the pastries.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she took the tray and served them to him, but he refused to eat. And Amnon said, “Have everyone leave me.” So everyone left him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the ①bedroom, so that I may eat from your hand.” So Tamar took the pastries which she had made and brought them into the bedroom to her brother Amnon. ▷ ①Or inner room

column.name: text
column.value: When she brought them to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, sleep with me, my sister.”

column.name: text
column.value: But she said to him, “No, my brother, do not violate me, for such a thing is not done in Israel; do not do this disgraceful sin!

column.name: text
column.value: As for me, where could I ①get rid of my shame? And as for you, you will be like one of the ②fools in Israel. Now then, please speak to the king, for he will not ③withhold me from you.” ▷ ①Lit take away ②Or worthless ones ③I.e., refuse a marriage

column.name: text
column.value: However, he would not listen to ①her; since he was stronger than she, he violated her and slept with her. ▷ ①Lit her voice

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amnon hated her with a very great hatred; indeed, the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. And Amnon said to her, “Get up, go away!”

column.name: text
column.value: But she said to him, “No, because this wrong in sending me away is greater than the other that you have done to me!” Yet he would not listen to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he called his young man who attended him and said, “Now throw this woman out of my presence, and lock the door behind her!”

column.name: text
column.value: Now she had on a ①long-sleeved garment; for this is how the virgin daughters of the king dressed themselves in robes. Then his attendant took her out and locked the door behind her. ▷ ①Or varicolored tunic

column.name: text
column.value: Tamar took ashes and put them on her head, and tore her ①long-sleeved garment which was on her; and she put her hand on her head and went on her way, crying out as she went. ▷ ①Or varicolored tunic

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now keep silent, my sister, he is your brother; do not take this matter to heart.” So Tamar remained and was isolated in her brother Absalom’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when King David heard about all these matters, he became very angry.

column.name: text
column.value: But Absalom did not speak with Amnon either good or bad; for Absalom hated Amnon because he had violated his sister Tamar.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after two full years that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is near Ephraim, and Absalom invited all the king’s sons to celebrate.

column.name: text
column.value: And Absalom came to the king and said, “Behold now, your servant has sheepshearers; may the king and his servants please go with your servant.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said to Absalom, “No, my son, we should not all go, so that we will not be a burden to you.” Though he urged him, he would not go; but he blessed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom said, “If not, please have my brother Amnon go with us.” But the king said to him, “Why should he go with you?”

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless Absalom urged him, so he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom commanded his servants, saying, “See now, when Amnon’s heart is cheerful with wine, and I say to you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ then put him to death. Do not fear; have I not commanded you myself? Be courageous and be ①valiant.” ▷ ①Lit sons of valor

column.name: text
column.value: And the servants of Absalom did to Amnon just as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons got up and each mounted his mule and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was while they were on the way that the report came to David, saying, “Absalom has struck and killed all the king’s sons, and not one of them is left.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay on the ground; and all his servants were standing by with clothes torn.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonadab, the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, ①responded, “Let my lord not ②assume that they have put to death all the young men, the king’s sons, for only Amnon is dead; because this has been set up by the ③intent of Absalom since the day that he violated his sister Tamar. ▷ ①Lit answered and said ②Lit say ③Lit mouth

column.name: text
column.value: So now, may my lord the king not take the report to ①heart, ②claiming, ‘all the king’s sons are dead’; but only Amnon is dead.” ▷ ①Lit his heart ②Lit saying

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom had fled. And the young man who was the watchman raised his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming from the road behind him by the side of the mountain.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jonadab said to the king, “Behold, the king’s sons have come; so it has happened according to your servant’s word.”

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king’s sons came and raised their voices and wept; and the king and all his servants also wept ①very profusely. ▷ ①Lit with a very great weeping

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom had fled and gone to Talmai the son of Ammihud, the king of Geshur. And David mourned for his son every day.

column.name: text
column.value: So Absalom had fled and gone to Geshur, and was there for three years.

column.name: text
column.value: And the heart of King David longed to go out to Absalom; for he was comforted regarding Amnon, since he was dead.

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened ①in the spring, at the time when kings go out to battle, that David sent Joab and his servants with him and all Israel, and they brought destruction on the sons of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed in Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit at the return of the year

column.name: text
column.value: Now at evening time David got up from his bed and walked around on the roof of the king’s house, and from the roof he saw a woman bathing; and the woman was very beautiful in appearance.

column.name: text
column.value: So David sent servants and inquired about the woman. And someone said, “Is this not Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sent messengers and ①had her brought, and when she came to him, he slept with her; and when she had purified herself from her uncleanness, she returned to her house. ▷ ①Lit took her

column.name: text
column.value: But the woman conceived; so she sent word and informed David, and said, “I am pregnant.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David sent word to Joab: “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” So Joab sent Uriah to David.

column.name: text
column.value: When Uriah came to him, David asked about Joab’s well-being and ①that of the people, and the condition of the war. ▷ ①Lit welfare of

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house, and wash your feet.” So Uriah left the king’s house, and a gift from the king ①was sent after him. ▷ ①Lit went out

column.name: text
column.value: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and did not go down to his house.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when they informed David, saying, “Uriah did not go down to his house,” David said to Uriah, “Did you not come from a journey? Why did you not go down to your house?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Uriah said to David, “The ark and Israel and Judah are staying in ①temporary shelters, and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are camping in the open field. Should I then go to my house to eat and drink and to sleep with my wife? By your life and the life of your soul, I will not do this thing.” ▷ ①Or huts

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Uriah, “Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you go back.” So Uriah remained in Jerusalem that day and the day after.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David summoned ①Uriah, and he ate and drank in his presence, and he made ②Uriah drunk; and in the evening Uriah went out to lie on his bed with his lord’s servants, and he still did not go down to his house. ▷ ①Lit him ②Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: So in the morning David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

column.name: text
column.value: He had written in the letter ①the following: “ ②Station Uriah on the front line of the ③fiercest battle and pull back from him, so that he may be struck and killed.” ▷ ①Lit saying ②Lit Give ③Lit severe

column.name: text
column.value: So it was as Joab kept watch on the city, that he ①stationed Uriah at the place where he knew there were valiant men. ▷ ①Lit gave

column.name: text
column.value: And the men of the city went out and fought against Joab, and some of the people among David’s servants fell; and Uriah the Hittite also died.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab sent a messenger and reported to David all the events of the war.

column.name: text
column.value: He ordered the messenger, saying, “When you have finished telling all the events of the war to the king,

column.name: text
column.value: then it shall be that if the king’s wrath rises and he says to you, ‘Why did you move against the city to fight? Did you not know that they would shoot from the wall?

column.name: text
column.value: Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Did a woman not throw an upper millstone on him from the wall so that he died at Thebez? Why did you move against the wall?’—then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So the messenger departed and came and reported to David everything that Joab had sent him to tell.

column.name: text
column.value: The messenger said to David, “The men prevailed against us and came out against us in the field, but we ①pressed them as far as the entrance of the gate. ▷ ①Lit were upon

column.name: text
column.value: Also, the archers shot at your servants from the wall; so some of the king’s servants died, and your servant Uriah the Hittite also died.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to the messenger, “This is what you shall say to Joab: ‘Do not let this thing ①displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another; ②fight with determination against the city and overthrow it’; and thereby encourage him.” ▷ ①Lit be evil in your sight ②Lit seize your battle against

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Uriah’s wife heard that her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for her husband.

column.name: text
column.value: When the time of mourning was over, David sent servants and ①had her brought to his house and she became his wife; then she bore him a son. But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit brought her

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened afterward that David ①defeated the Philistines and subdued them; and David took ②control of the chief city from the hand of the Philistines. ▷ ①Lit the bridle of the mother city ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And He ①defeated Moab, and measured them with the line, making them lie down on the ground; and he measured two lines to put to death, and a full line to keep alive. And the Moabites became servants to David, bringing tribute. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then David ①defeated Hadadezer, the son of Rehob king of Zobah, as he went to restore his ②power at the Euphrates River. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: And David captured from him ①1,700 horsemen and twenty thousand foot soldiers; and David hamstrung almost all the chariot horses, but left enough of them for a hundred chariots. ▷ ①Here LXX reads as 1 Chr 18:4; partial DSS text appears to also

column.name: text
column.value: When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, king of Zobah, David ①killed twenty-two thousand men among the Arameans. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then David put garrisons among the Arameans of Damascus, and the Arameans became servants to David, bringing tribute. And the LORD helped David wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: David took the shields of gold which were ①carried by the servants of Hadadezer, and brought them to Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit on

column.name: text
column.value: And from ①Betah and Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took a very large amount of bronze. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 18:8, Tibhath

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Toi king of Hamath heard that David had ①defeated the whole army of Hadadezer, ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Toi sent his son ①Joram to King David to ②greet him and bless him, because he had fought Hadadezer and ③defeated him; for Hadadezer ④had been at war with Toi. And ⑤Joram brought with him articles of silver, gold, and bronze. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 18:10, Hadoram ②Lit ask him of his welfare ③Lit struck ④Lit was a man of wars ⑤Lit there were in his hand

column.name: text
column.value: King David also consecrated these gifts to the LORD, with the silver and gold that he had consecrated from all the nations which he had subdued:

column.name: text
column.value: from ①Aram, Moab, the sons of Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and from the spoils of Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah. ▷ ①Some mss Edom

column.name: text
column.value: So David made a name for himself when he returned from ①killing eighteen thousand ②Arameans in the Valley of Salt. ▷ ①Lit striking ②Some mss Edom

column.name: text
column.value: He also put garrisons in Edom. In all Edom he put garrisons, and all the Edomites became servants to David. And the LORD helped David wherever he went.

column.name: text
column.value: So David reigned over all Israel; and David ①administered justice and righteousness for all his people. ▷ ①Lit was doing

column.name: text
column.value: Joab the son of Zeruiah was commander over the army, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was secretary.

column.name: text
column.value: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were priests, and Seraiah was scribe.

column.name: text
column.value: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada ①was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were ②chief ministers. ▷ ①See 1 Chr 18:17; MT and the Cherethites ②Lit priests

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, “Is there ①anyone still left of the house of Saul, so that I could show him kindness for Jonathan’s sake?” ▷ ①Lit he who is

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a servant of the house of Saul whose name was Ziba, and they summoned him to David; and the king said to him, “Are you Ziba?” And he said, “I am your servant.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, “Is there no one remaining of the house of Saul to whom I could show the kindness of God?” And Ziba said to the king, “There is still a son of Jonathan, one who is disabled in both feet.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to him, “Where is he?” And Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, in Lo-debar.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David sent ①messengers who brought him from the house of Machir the son of Ammiel, from Lo-debar. ▷ ①Lit and he brought

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, came to David and fell on his face and prostrated himself. And David said, “Mephibosheth.” And he said, “Here is your servant!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to him, “Do not be afraid, for I will assuredly show kindness to you for the sake of your father Jonathan, and I will restore to you all the ①land of your ②grandfather Saul; and you yourself shall ③eat at my table regularly.” ▷ ①Lit field ②Lit father ③Lit eat bread

column.name: text
column.value: Again he prostrated himself, and said, “What is your servant, that you should be concerned about a dead dog like me?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king summoned Saul’s servant Ziba and said to him, “Everything that belonged to Saul and to all his house I have given to your master’s ①grandson. ▷ ①Lit son

column.name: text
column.value: You and your sons and your servants shall cultivate the land for him, and you shall bring in the produce so that your master’s grandson will have food ①to eat; nevertheless Mephibosheth, your master’s grandson, shall ②eat at my table regularly.” Now Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants. ▷ ①Lit and eat it ②Lit eat bread

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ziba said to the king, “In accordance with everything that my lord the king commands his servant, so your servant will do.” So Mephibosheth ate at ①David’s table as one of the king’s sons. ▷ ①Lit my

column.name: text
column.value: Mephibosheth had a young son whose name was Mica. And all who lived in the house of Ziba were servants to Mephibosheth.

column.name: text
column.value: So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he ate at the king’s table regularly. And he was disabled in his two feet.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was drawn toward Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab sent a messenger to Tekoa and ①brought a wise woman from there, and said to her, “Please follow mourning rites, and put on mourning garments now, and do not anoint yourself with oil but be like a woman who has been mourning for the dead for many days. ▷ ①Lit took

column.name: text
column.value: Then go to the king and speak to him in this way.” So Joab put the words in her mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the woman of Tekoa ①spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground and prostrated herself, and said, “Help, O king!” ▷ ①Many mss and ancient versions came

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to her, “What is troubling you?” And she ①answered, “Truly I am a widow, for my husband is dead. ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: And your servant had two sons, but the two of them fought in the field, and there was no ①one to save ②them from each other, so one struck the other and killed him. ▷ ①Lit deliverer between ②Lit between them

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, the entire family has risen against your servant, and they have said, ‘Hand over the one who struck his brother, so that we may put him to death for the life of his brother whom he killed, and eliminate the heir as well.’ So they will extinguish my coal which is left, so as to ①leave my husband neither name nor remnant on the face of the earth.” ▷ ①Lit establish for

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to the woman, “Go to your home, and I will issue orders concerning you.”

column.name: text
column.value: The woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord, the king, the guilt is on me and my father’s house, but the king and his throne are guiltless.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said, “Whoever speaks to you, bring him to me, and he will not touch you anymore.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “May the king please remember the LORD your God, so that the avenger of blood will not continue to destroy, otherwise they will destroy my son.” And he said, “As the LORD lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the ground.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the woman said, “Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” And he said, “Speak.”

column.name: text
column.value: The woman said, “Why then have you planned such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is like one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring back his banished one.

column.name: text
column.value: For we will surely die and are like water spilled on the ground, which cannot be gathered up. Yet God does not take away life, but makes plans so that the banished one will not be cast out from Him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, ①the reason I have come to speak this word to my lord the king is that the people have made me afraid; so your servant said, ‘Let me now speak to the king, perhaps the king will perform the ②request of his slave. ▷ ①Lit that I ②Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: For the king will listen, to save his slave from the ①hand of the man who would eliminate ②both me and my son from the inheritance of God.’ ▷ ①Lit palm ②Lit together

column.name: text
column.value: Then your servant said, ‘Please let the word of my lord the king be ①comforting, for as the angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and evil. And may the LORD your God be with you.’ ” ▷ ①Lit for rest

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king answered and said to the woman, “Please do not hide anything from me that I am about to ask you.” And the woman said, “Let my lord the king please speak.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?” And the woman replied, “As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken. Indeed, it was your servant Joab who commanded me, and it was he who put all these words in the mouth of your servant.

column.name: text
column.value: In order to change the appearance of things your servant Joab has done this thing. But my lord is wise, like the wisdom of the angel of God, to know all that is on the earth.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Joab, “Behold now, I ①will certainly do this thing; go then, bring back the young man Absalom.” ▷ ①Lit have done

column.name: text
column.value: And Joab fell on his face to the ground, prostrated himself, and blessed the king; then Joab said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord the king, in that the king has performed the ①request of his servant.” ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: However, the king said, “He shall return to his own house, but he shall not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house and did not see the king’s face.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in all Israel there was no one as handsome as Absalom, so highly praised; from the sole of his foot to the top of his head there was no impairment in him.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he cut the hair of his head (and it was at the end of every year that he cut it, because it was heavy on him, so he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head at ①two hundred shekels by the king’s weight. ▷ ①About 4 lb. or 1.8 kg

column.name: text
column.value: And to Absalom there were born three sons, and one daughter whose name was Tamar; she was a woman of beautiful appearance.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, yet he did not see the king’s face.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. So he sent word again a second time, but he would not come.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore he said to his servants, “See, Joab’s plot is next to mine, and he has barley there; go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the plot on fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab got up, came to Absalom at his house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my plot on fire?”

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom ①answered Joab, “Behold, I sent for you, saying, ‘Come here, so that I may send you to the king, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me still to be there.” ’ Now then, let me see the king’s face, and if there is guilt in me, he can have me executed.” ▷ ①Lit said to

column.name: text
column.value: So when Joab came to the king and told him, he summoned Absalom. Then Absalom came to the king and prostrated himself ①with his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom. ▷ ①Lit on his

column.name: text
column.value: Now when David had gone on a little beyond the summit, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a team of saddled donkeys, and on them were two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred cakes of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a jug of wine.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Ziba, “Why do you have these?” And Ziba said, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride, the bread and summer fruit are for the young men to eat, and the wine, for whoever is weary in the wilderness to drink.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, “And where is your master’s son?” And Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore the kingdom of my father to me.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to Ziba, “Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” And Ziba said, “I prostrate myself; may I find favor in your sight, my lord, the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man was coming out from there from the family of the house of Saul, and his name was Shimei, the son of Gera; he was coming out, cursing as he came.

column.name: text
column.value: He also threw stones at David and all the servants of King David; and all the people and all the warriors were on his right and on his left.

column.name: text
column.value: This is what Shimei said when he cursed: “Go away, go away, you man of bloodshed and worthless man!

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has brought back upon you all the bloodshed of the house of Saul, in whose place you have become king; and the LORD has handed the kingdom over to your son Absalom. And behold, you are caught in your own evil, for you are a man of bloodshed!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Now let me go over and ①cut off his head.” ▷ ①Lit take off

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, “ ①What business of mine is yours, you sons of Zeruiah? If he curses, and if the LORD has told him, ‘Curse David,’ then who should say, ‘Why have you done so?’ ” ▷ ①Lit What to me and to you, an ancient idiom

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Abishai and to all his servants, “Behold, my son who came out of my own body seeks my life; how much more now this Benjaminite? Leave him alone and let him curse, for the LORD has told him.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps the LORD will look on my ①misery and ②return good to me instead of his cursing this day.” ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT wrongdoing ②Lit the LORD will return

column.name: text
column.value: So David and his men went on the road; and Shimei kept going on the hillside close beside him, and as he went he cursed and threw stones and dirt at him.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king and all the people who were with him arrived exhausted, and he refreshed himself there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, entered Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when Hushai the Archite, David’s friend, came to Absalom, that Hushai said to Absalom, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Absalom said to Hushai, “Is this your ①loyalty to your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?” ▷ ①Or faithfulness

column.name: text
column.value: So Hushai said to Absalom, “No! For whomever the LORD, this people, and all the men of Israel have chosen, his I shall be, and with him I shall remain.

column.name: text
column.value: Besides, whom should I serve? Should I not serve in the presence of his son? Just as I have served in your father’s presence, so I shall be in your presence.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom said to Ahithophel, “Give your advice. What should we do?”

column.name: text
column.value: Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Have relations with your father’s concubines, whom he has left behind to take care of the house; then all Israel will hear that you have made yourself repulsive to your father. The hands of all who are with you will also be strengthened.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom had relations with his father’s concubines in the sight of all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the advice of Ahithophel, which he ①gave in those days, was taken as though one inquired of the word of God; so was all the advice of Ahithophel regarded by both David and Absalom. ▷ ①Lit advised

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened afterward that the king of the Ammonites died, and his son Hanun became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, just as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent ①some of his servants to console him about his father. But when David’s servants came to the land of the Ammonites, ▷ ①Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: the commanders of the Ammonites said to their lord Hanun, “ ①Do you think that David is simply honoring your father since he has sent you servants ②to console you? Has David not sent his servants to you in order to explore the city, to spy it out and overthrow it?” ▷ ①Lit In your eyes is David honoring ②Lit consoling

column.name: text
column.value: So Hanun took David’s servants and shaved off half of their beards, and cut off their robes in the middle as far as their buttocks, and sent them away.

column.name: text
column.value: When messengers informed David, he sent servants to meet them, because the men were extremely humiliated. And the king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back, and then you shall return.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the sons of Ammon saw that they had become repulsive to David, the sons of Ammon sent messengers and hired the Arameans of Beth-rehob and the Arameans of Zobah, twenty thousand foot soldiers, and the king of Maacah with a thousand men, and the men of Tob with twelve thousand men.

column.name: text
column.value: When David heard about this, he sent Joab and all the army, the warriors.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Ammon came out and lined up for battle at the entrance of the ①city, while the Arameans of Zobah and of Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were stationed by themselves in the field. ▷ ①Lit gate

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Joab saw that ①the battle was set against him at the front and at the rear, he selected warriors from all the choice men in Israel, and lined them up against the Arameans. ▷ ①Lit the faces of the battle were against

column.name: text
column.value: But the remainder of the people he placed ①under the command of his brother Abishai, and he lined them up against the sons of Ammon. ▷ ①Lit in the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the sons of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come to help you.

column.name: text
column.value: Be strong, and let’s show ourselves courageous for the sake of our people and the cities of our God; and may the LORD do what is good in His sight.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Joab and the people who were with him advanced to the battle against the Arameans, and they fled from him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the sons of Ammon saw that the Arameans had fled, they also fled from Abishai and entered the city. Then Joab returned from fighting against the sons of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: When the Arameans saw that they had been ①defeated by Israel, they assembled together. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: And Hadadezer sent word and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the Euphrates River, and they came to Helam; and Shobach the commander of the army of Hadadezer ①led them. ▷ ①Lit was before them

column.name: text
column.value: Now when it was reported to David, he gathered all Israel together and crossed the Jordan, and came to Helam. And the Arameans lined up against David and fought him.

column.name: text
column.value: But the Arameans fled from Israel, and David killed seven hundred charioteers of the Arameans and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the commander of their army, and he died there.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the kings, servants of Hadadezer, saw that they had been ①defeated by Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Arameans were afraid to help the sons of Ammon anymore. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then David ①took a count of the people who were with him and appointed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds. ▷ ①Lit mustered

column.name: text
column.value: And David sent the people out, a third ①under the command of Joab, a third ②under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third ③under the command of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said to the people, “I myself will certainly go out with you also.” ▷ ①Lit by the hand of ②Lit by the hand of ③Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: But the people said, “You should not go out; for if in fact we flee, they will not care about us; and if half of us die, they will not care about us. But ①you are ②worth ten thousand of us; so now it is better that you will be ready to help us from the city.” ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT for now there are 10,000 like us ②Lit like us by 10,000

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to them, “Whatever seems best to you I will do.” So the king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and thousands.

column.name: text
column.value: But the king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, “Deal gently with the young man Absalom for my sake.” And all the people heard when the king commanded all the commanders regarding Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people went out to the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: The people of Israel were ①defeated there by the servants of David, and the slaughter there that day was great, twenty thousand men. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: For the battle there was spread over the whole countryside, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom encountered the servants of David. Absalom was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the branches of a massive oak. Then his head caught firmly in the oak, and he was ①left hanging between the sky and earth, while the mule that was under him kept going. ▷ ①Lit placed

column.name: text
column.value: When a certain man saw him, he informed Joab and said, “Behold, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab said to the man who had informed him, “So behold, you saw him! Why then did you not strike him there to the ground? And it would have been ①my duty to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt.” ▷ ①Lit And upon me

column.name: text
column.value: But the man said to Joab, “Even if I were to ①receive a thousand pieces of silver in my hand, I would not put out my hand against the king’s son; for in our hearing the king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, ‘ ②Protect the young man Absalom for me!’ ▷ ①Lit weigh ②As in some mss and ancient versions; MT Protect, whoever you are, the

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise, if I had dealt treacherously against ①his life (and there is nothing hidden from the king), then you yourself would have ②avoided me.” ▷ ①Another reading is my life; i.e., at the risk of my own life ②Lit stood aloof

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab said, “I will not ①waste time here with you.” So he took three spears in his hand and thrust them through the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the ②midst of the oak. ▷ ①Lit wait so with ②Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: And ten young men who carried Joab’s armor gathered around and struck Absalom and killed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing Israel, for Joab restrained the people.

column.name: text
column.value: And they took Absalom and threw him into ①a deep pit in the forest, and erected over him a very large pile of stones. And all Israel fled, each to his own tent. ▷ ①Lit the great

column.name: text
column.value: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and set up for himself a memorial stone, which is in the King’s Valley, for he said, “I have no son to ①continue my name.” So he named the memorial stone after his own name, and it is called Absalom’s Monument to this day. ▷ ①Lit bring to remembrance

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Please let me run and bring the king news that the LORD has ①freed him from the hand of his enemies!” ▷ ①Lit vindicated

column.name: text
column.value: But Joab said to him, “You are not the man to bring news this day, but you shall bring news another day; however, you shall bring no news this day, because the king’s son is dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab said to the Cushite, “Go, tell the king what you have seen.” So the Cushite bowed to Joab and ran.

column.name: text
column.value: However, Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said once more to Joab, “But whatever happens, please let me also run after the Cushite.” And Joab said, “Why would you run, my son, since you will have no messenger’s reward for going?”

column.name: text
column.value: “But whatever happens,” he said, “I will run.” So he said to him, “Run.” Then Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and passed by the Cushite.

column.name: text
column.value: Now David was sitting between the two gates; and the watchman went to the roof of the gate by the wall, and raised his eyes and looked; and behold, a man was running by himself.

column.name: text
column.value: So the watchman called out and told the king. And the king said, “If he is by himself there is good news in his mouth.” And he came nearer and nearer.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the watchman saw another man running; and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, “Behold, another man is running by himself.” And the king said, “This one also is bringing good news.”

column.name: text
column.value: The watchman said, “I ①think the running form of the first one is like the running form of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” And the king said, “This is a good man, and he is coming with good news.” ▷ ①Lit see

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, “ ①All is well.” And he prostrated himself before the king with his face to the ground. And he said, “Blessed is the LORD your God, who has turned over the men who raised their hands against my lord the king.” ▷ ①Lit Peace; Heb Shalom

column.name: text
column.value: But the king said, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” And Ahimaaz answered, “When Joab sent the king’s servant, and your servant, I saw a great commotion, but I did not know what it was.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, “Turn aside and stand here.” So he turned aside and stood still.

column.name: text
column.value: Then behold, the Cushite arrived, and the Cushite said, “Let my lord the king receive good news, for the LORD has ①freed you this day from the hand of all those who rose up against you.” ▷ ①Lit vindicated

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to the Cushite, “Is it well with the young man Absalom?” And the Cushite answered, “May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise up against you for evil, be like that young man!”

column.name: text
column.value: ①Then the king trembled and went up to the chamber over the gate and wept. And this is what he said as he walked: “My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you, Absalom, my son, my son!” ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, Ahithophel said to Absalom, “Please let me choose twelve thousand men and let me set out and pursue David tonight.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will ①attack him while he is weary and ②exhausted and startle him, so that all the people who are with him will flee. Then I will strike and kill the king when he is alone, ▷ ①Lit come upon ②Lit slack of hands

column.name: text
column.value: and I will bring all the people back to you. ①The return of everyone depends on the man whom you are seeking; then all the people will be at peace.” ▷ ①Lit As the return of the whole is the man whom you seek

column.name: text
column.value: And the ①plan pleased Absalom and all the elders of Israel. ▷ ①Lit word was pleasing in the sight of

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, Absalom said, “Now call Hushai the Archite also, and let’s hear what ①he has to say.” ▷ ①Lit is in his mouth—even he

column.name: text
column.value: When Hushai had come to Absalom, Absalom said to ①him, “Ahithophel has ②proposed this plan. Should we ③carry out his plan? If not, say so yourself.” ▷ ①Lit him, saying ②Lit spoken according to this word ③Lit do his word

column.name: text
column.value: So Hushai said to Absalom, “This time the advice that Ahithophel has ①given is not good.” ▷ ①Lit advised

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hushai said, “You yourself know your father and his men, that they are warriors and they are ①fierce, like a bear deprived of her cubs in the field. And your father is an ②expert in warfare, and he will not spend the night with the people. ▷ ①Lit bitter of soul ②Lit man of war

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, he has now hidden himself in one of the ravines, or in another place; and it will be that when he falls on them at the first attack, whoever hears it will say, ‘There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom!’

column.name: text
column.value: And even the one who is valiant, whose heart is like the heart of a lion, will completely despair; for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty man, and those who are with him are valiant men.

column.name: text
column.value: But I advise that all Israel be fully gathered to you, from Dan even to Beersheba, like the sand that is by the sea in abundance; and that ①you personally go into battle. ▷ ①Lit your face goes

column.name: text
column.value: Then we will come to him in one of the places where he can be found, and we will ①fall on him just as the dew falls on the ground; and of him and of all the men who are with him, not even one will be left. ▷ ①Lit settle down

column.name: text
column.value: And if he withdraws into a city, then all Israel shall bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it into the ①valley until not even a pebble is found there.” ▷ ①Or wadi; i.e., a dry stream bed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom and all the men of Israel said, “The advice of Hushai the Archite is better than the advice of Ahithophel.” For the LORD had ordained to foil the good advice of Ahithophel, in order for the LORD to bring disaster on Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hushai said to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, “ ①This is what Ahithophel advised Absalom and the elders of Israel to do, and ②this is what I have advised. ▷ ①Lit According to this and this ②Lit According to this and this

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, send a messenger quickly and tell David, saying, ‘Do not spend the night at the river crossing places of the wilderness, but by all means cross over, or else the king and all the people who are with him will be ①destroyed.’ ” ▷ ①Lit swallowed up

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jonathan and Ahimaaz were staying at En-rogel, and a female servant would go and inform them, and they would go and inform King David, for they could not allow themselves to be seen entering the city.

column.name: text
column.value: But a boy did see them, and he told Absalom; so the two of them left quickly and came to the house of a man in Bahurim, who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down ①into it. ▷ ①Lit there

column.name: text
column.value: And the woman ①took a cover and spread it over the well’s mouth and scattered barley meal on it, so that nothing was known. ▷ ①Lit took and spread the covering

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom’s servants came to the woman at the house and said, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” And the woman said to them, “They have crossed the brook of water.” And when they searched and did not find them, they returned to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: It came about after they had departed, that they came up out of the well and went and reported to King David; and they said to David, “Set out and cross over the water quickly, because this is what Ahithophel has advised against you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David and all the people who were with him set out and crossed the Jordan; by ①dawn not even one remained who had not crossed the Jordan. ▷ ①Lit the light of the morning

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been ①followed, he saddled his donkey and set out and went to his home, to his city, and ②set his house in order, and hanged himself; so he died and was buried in his father’s grave. ▷ ①Lit done ②Lit ordered in regard to

column.name: text
column.value: Then David came to Mahanaim. And Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom put Amasa ①in command of the army in place of Joab. Now Amasa was the son of a man whose name was ②Ithra the Israelite, who ③had relations with Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother. ▷ ①Lit over the army ②In 1 Chr 2:17, Jether the Ishmaelite ③Lit came in to

column.name: text
column.value: And Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when David had come to Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash from Rabbah of the sons of Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim,

column.name: text
column.value: brought beds, basins, pottery, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, roasted seeds,

column.name: text
column.value: honey, curds, sheep, and cheese of the herd, for David and the people who were with him, to eat. For they said, “The people are hungry and exhausted and thirsty in the wilderness.”

column.name: text
column.value: ①Then it was reported to Joab, “Behold, the king is weeping and he mourns for Absalom.” ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: So the ①victory that day was turned into mourning for all the people, because the people heard it said that day, “The king is in mourning over his son.” ▷ ①Lit salvation

column.name: text
column.value: And the people entered the city surreptitiously that day, just as people who are humiliated surreptitiously flee in battle.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king covered his face and ①cried out with a loud voice, “My son Absalom, Absalom, my son, my son!” ▷ ①Lit the king cried

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joab came into the house to the king and said, “Today you have shamed ①all your servants, who have saved your life today and the lives of your sons and daughters, the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines, ▷ ①Lit the faces of all

column.name: text
column.value: by loving those who hate you, and by hating those who love you. For you have revealed today that ①commanders and servants are nothing to you; for I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then it would be right ②as far as you are concerned. ▷ ①Or princes ②Lit in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore arise, go out and speak ①kindly to your servants, for I swear by the LORD, if you do not go out, no man will stay the night with you, and this will be worse for you than all the misfortune that has ②happened to you from your youth until now!” ▷ ①Lit to the heart of your ②Lit come upon

column.name: text
column.value: So the king got up and sat at the gate. When they told all the people, saying, “Behold, the king is sitting at the gate,” then all the people came before the king. Now Israel had fled, each to his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people were quarreling throughout the tribes of Israel, saying, “The king rescued us from the ①hands of our enemies and saved us from the ②hands of the Philistines, but now he has fled out of the land from Absalom. ▷ ①Lit palm ②Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: However, Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now then, why are you silent about bringing the king back?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, “Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, ‘Why are you the last to bring the king back to his house, since the word of all Israel has come to the king, even to his house?

column.name: text
column.value: You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why then should you be the last to bring back the king?’

column.name: text
column.value: And say to Amasa, ‘Are you not my bone and my flesh? May God do so to me, and more so, if you will not be commander of the army ①for me continually, in place of Joab.’ ” ▷ ①Lit before me

column.name: text
column.value: So he turned the hearts of all the men of Judah as one man, so that they sent word to the king, saying, “Return, you and all your servants.”

column.name: text
column.value: The king then returned and came as far as the Jordan. And the men of Judah came to Gilgal in order to go to meet the king, to escort the king across the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shimei the son of Gera, the Benjaminite who was from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

column.name: text
column.value: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they rushed to the Jordan before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they crossed the shallow places repeatedly to bring over the king’s household, and to do what was good in his sight. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king as he was about to cross the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to the king, “May my lord not consider me guilty, nor call to mind what your servant did wrong on the day when my lord the king went out from Jerusalem, so that the king would ①take it to heart. ▷ ①Lit set

column.name: text
column.value: For your servant knows that I have sinned; so behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah responded, “Should Shimei not be put to death for this, the fact that he cursed the LORD’S anointed?”

column.name: text
column.value: David then said, “What ①is there between you and me, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should be an adversary to me today? Should anyone be put to death in Israel today? For do I not know that I am king over Israel today?” ▷ ①Lit to me and to you; an ancient idiom

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” The king also swore to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Mephibosheth the ①grandson of Saul came down to meet the king; but he had neither ②tended to his feet, nor ③trimmed his mustache, nor washed his clothes since the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace. ▷ ①Lit son ②Lit done ③Lit done

column.name: text
column.value: And it was when he came from Jerusalem to meet the king, that the king said to him, “Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “My lord the king, my servant betrayed me; for your servant said, ‘I will ①saddle the donkey for myself so that I may ride on it and go with the king,’ since your servant cannot walk. ▷ ①I.e., have the donkey saddled

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, he has slandered your servant to my lord the king; but my lord the king is like the angel of God, therefore do what is good in your sight.

column.name: text
column.value: For all my father’s household was only people worthy of death to my lord the king; yet you placed your servant among those who ate at your own table. So what right do I still have, that I should ①complain anymore to the king?” ▷ ①Lit cry out

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to him, “Why do you still speak of your affairs? I have ①decided, ‘You and Ziba shall divide the land.’ ” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Let him even take it all, since my lord the king has come safely to his own house.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim; and he went on to the Jordan with the king to ①escort him over the Jordan. ▷ ①Lit send

column.name: text
column.value: Barzillai was very old: eighty years old; and he had provided the king food while he stayed in Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said to Barzillai, “You cross over with me, and I will provide you food in Jerusalem with me.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Barzillai said to the king, “How long ①do I still have to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem? ▷ ①Lit are the days of the years of my life

column.name: text
column.value: I am ①now eighty years old. Can I distinguish between good and bad? Or can your servant taste what I eat or what I drink? Or can I still hear the voice of men and women singing? Why then should your servant be an added burden to my lord the king? ▷ ①Lit today

column.name: text
column.value: Your servant would merely cross over the Jordan with the king. So why should the king compensate me with this reward?

column.name: text
column.value: Please let your servant return, so that I may die in my own city near the grave of my father and my mother. However, here is your servant Chimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your sight.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king answered, “Chimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your sight; and whatever you ①require of me, I will do for you.” ▷ ①Lit choose

column.name: text
column.value: All the people crossed over the Jordan and the king crossed too. The king then kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him; and all the people of Judah and also half the people of Israel ①accompanied the king. ▷ ①Lit crossed over with

column.name: text
column.value: And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, “Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, abducted you and brought the king and his household and all David’s men with him, over the Jordan?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “Because the king is a close relative to ①us. Why then are you angry about this matter? Have we eaten at all ②at the king’s expense, or has anything been taken for us?” ▷ ①Lit me ②Lit from the king

column.name: text
column.value: But the men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, “ ①We have ten parts in the king, therefore ②we also have more claim on David than you. Why then did you treat ③us with contempt? Was it not ④our ⑤advice first to bring back ⑥our king?” Yet the words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel. ▷ ①Singular in Heb ②Singular in Heb ③Singular in Heb ④Singular in Heb ⑤Lit word ⑥Singular in Heb

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after this that Absalom provided for himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men ①to run ahead of him. ▷ ①Lit as runners ahead

column.name: text
column.value: And Absalom used to rise early and stand beside the road to the gate; and when any man who had a lawsuit was to come before the king for judgment, Absalom would call out to him and say, “From what city are you?” And he would say, “Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Absalom would say to him, “See, your ①claims are good and right, but you have no one to listen to you on the part of the king.” ▷ ①Lit words

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Absalom would say, “Oh that someone would appoint me judge in the land, then every man who has a lawsuit or claim could come to me, and I would give him justice!”

column.name: text
column.value: And whenever a man approached to prostrate himself before him, he would put out his hand and take hold of him and kiss him.

column.name: text
column.value: Absalom dealt this way with all Israel who came to the king for judgment; so Absalom stole the hearts of the people of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about at the end of ①four years that Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow which I have made to the LORD, in Hebron. ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT forty

column.name: text
column.value: For your servant made a vow while I was living in Geshur in Aram, saying, ‘If the LORD will indeed bring me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve the LORD.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he got up and went to Hebron.

column.name: text
column.value: But Absalom sent spies throughout the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then two hundred men went with Absalom from Jerusalem, who were invited and went ①innocently, for they did not know anything. ▷ ①Lit in their integrity

column.name: text
column.value: And Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. And the conspiracy was strong, for the people continually increased with Absalom.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the people of Israel are ①with Absalom.” ▷ ①Lit after

column.name: text
column.value: So David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, “Arise and let’s flee, for otherwise none of us will escape from Absalom. Go quickly, or he will hurry and overtake us, and bring disaster on us and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king’s servants said to the king, “Behold, your servants will do whatever my lord the king chooses.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king left, and all his household ①with him; but the king left ten concubines behind to take care of the house. ▷ ①Lit at his feet

column.name: text
column.value: The king left, and all the people ①with him, and they stopped at the last house. ▷ ①Lit at his feet

column.name: text
column.value: Now all of his servants passed by beside him, and all the Cherethites, all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had come ①with him from Gath, passed by before the king. ▷ ①Lit at his feet

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you go with us too? Return and stay with ①your king, since you are a foreigner and an exile as well; return to your own place. ▷ ①Lit the king

column.name: text
column.value: You came only yesterday, so should I make you wander with us today, while I go wherever I go? Return and take your brothers back; mercy and ①truth be with you.” ▷ ①Or faithfulness

column.name: text
column.value: But Ittai answered the king and said, “As the LORD lives, and as my lord the king lives, wherever my lord the king may be, whether for death or for life, there assuredly shall your servant be!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then David said to Ittai, “Go and cross over the brook Kidron.” So Ittai the Gittite crossed over with all his men and all the ①little ones who were with him. ▷ ①I.e., children; here, families of the men

column.name: text
column.value: While all the country was weeping with a loud voice, all the people were crossing over. The king was also crossing over the brook Kidron, and all the people were crossing over toward the way of the wilderness.

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. And they set down the ark of God, and Abiathar came up until all the people had finished crossing over from the city.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Zadok, “Return the ark of God to the city. If I find favor in the sight of the LORD, then He will bring me back and show me both it and His habitation.

column.name: text
column.value: But if He says this: ‘I have no delight in you,’ then here I am, let Him do to me as seems good ①to Him.” ▷ ①Lit in His sight

column.name: text
column.value: The king also said to Zadok the priest, “Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, your son Ahimaaz and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

column.name: text
column.value: See, I am going to wait at the river crossing places of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Zadok and Abiathar returned the ark of God to Jerusalem and remained there.

column.name: text
column.value: And David was going up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went, and his head was covered, and he was walking barefoot. Then all the people who were with him each covered his own head, and they were going up, weeping as they went.

column.name: text
column.value: Now someone informed David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” And David said, “LORD, please make the advice of Ahithophel foolish.”

column.name: text
column.value: It happened as David was coming to the summit, where God was worshiped, that behold, Hushai the Archite met him with his ①coat torn, and ②dust on his head. ▷ ①Or tunic ②Lit earth

column.name: text
column.value: And David said to him, “If you go over with me, then you will become a burden to me.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king; even as I was your father’s servant in time past, so now I will also be your servant,’ then you can foil the advice of Ahithophel for me.

column.name: text
