column.value: Answer me, LORD, answer me, so that this people may know that You, LORD, are God, and that You have turned their heart back.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering and the wood, and the stones and the dust; and it licked up the water that was in the trench.

column.name: text
column.value: When all the people saw this, they fell on their faces; and they said, “The LORD, He is God; the LORD, He is God!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elijah said to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal; do not let one of them escape.” So they seized them; and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slaughtered them there.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elijah said to Ahab, “Go up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of the roar of a heavy shower.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab went up to eat and drink. But Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he bent down to the earth and put his face between his knees.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his servant, “Go up now, look toward the sea.” So he went up and looked, but he said, “There is nothing.” Yet Elijah said, “Go back” seven times.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he returned the seventh time, he said, “Behold, a cloud as small as a person’s hand is coming up from the sea.” And Elijah said, “Go up, say to Ahab, ‘Harness your chariot horses and go down, so that the heavy shower does not stop you.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Meanwhile the sky became dark with clouds and wind came up, and there was a heavy shower. And Ahab rode and went to Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the hand of the LORD was on Elijah, and he ①belted his cloak around his waist and ②outran Ahab ③to Jezreel. ▷ ①I.e., for travel ②Lit ran ahead of ③Lit until your coming to

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ahab told Jezebel everything that Elijah had done, and ①how he had killed all the prophets with the sword. ▷ ①Lit all that he had

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah, saying, “So may the gods do to me and more so, if by about this time tomorrow I do not make your ①life like the ②life of one of them.” ▷ ①Lit soul ②Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: And he ①was afraid, and got up and ran for his ②life and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah; and he left his servant there. ▷ ①Reading of many mss; MT may read saw ②Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a broom tree; and he asked for himself to die, and said, “Enough! Now, LORD, take my ①life, for I am no better than my fathers.” ▷ ①Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then he lay down and fell asleep under a broom tree; but behold, there was an angel touching him, and he said to him, “Arise, eat!”

column.name: text
column.value: And he looked, and behold, there was at his head a round loaf of bread baked on hot coals, and a pitcher of water. So he ate and drank, and lay down again.

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD came back a second time and touched him, and said, “Arise, eat; because the journey is too long for you.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he arose and ate and drank, and he journeyed in the strength of that food for forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he came there to a cave and spent the night there; and behold, the word of the LORD came to him, and He said to him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of armies; for the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. And I alone am left; and they have sought to take my life.”

column.name: text
column.value: So He said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.” And behold, the LORD was passing by! And a great and powerful wind was tearing out the mountains and breaking the rocks in pieces before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind. And after the wind there was an earthquake, but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

column.name: text
column.value: And after the earthquake, a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire; and after the fire, a sound of a gentle blowing.

column.name: text
column.value: When Elijah heard it, he wrapped his face in his cloak and went out and stood in the entrance of the cave. And behold, a voice came to him and said, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “I have been very zealous for the LORD, the God of armies; for the sons of Israel have abandoned Your covenant, torn down Your altars, and killed Your prophets with the sword. And I alone am left; and they have sought to take my life.”

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to him, “Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus; and when you have arrived, you shall anoint Hazael king over Aram.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall also anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi king over Israel; and you shall anoint Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah as prophet in your place.

column.name: text
column.value: And it shall come about that the one who escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu shall put to death, and the one who escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha shall put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet I will leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal and every mouth that has not kissed him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he departed from there and found Elisha the son of Shaphat while he was plowing, with twelve yoke of oxen in front of him, and he with the twelfth. And Elijah came over to him and threw his cloak on him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he left the oxen behind and ran after Elijah, and said, “Please let me kiss my father and my mother, then I will follow you.” And he said to him, “Go back, for ①what have I done to you?” ▷ ①I.e., so as to influence Elisha’s decision

column.name: text
column.value: So he returned from following him, and took the pair of oxen and sacrificed them, and cooked their meat with the implements of the oxen, and gave it to the people and they ate. Then he got up and followed Elijah and served him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after these things that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which was in Jezreel beside the palace of Ahab, the king of Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: And Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard so that I may have it for a vegetable garden, because it is close beside my house, and I will give you a better vineyard in place of it; if ①you prefer, I will give you what ②it is worth in money.” ▷ ①Lit it is good in your eyes ②Lit this

column.name: text
column.value: But Naboth said to Ahab, “The LORD forbid me that I would give you the inheritance of my fathers!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab entered his house sullen and furious because of the ①answer that Naboth the Jezreelite had given to him, since he said, “I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.” And he lay down on his bed and turned his face away, and ate no ②food. ▷ ①Lit word...had spoken to him ②Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: But Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, “How is it that your spirit is so sullen that you are not eating ①food?” ▷ ①Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to her, “It is because I was speaking to Naboth the Jezreelite and saying to him, ‘Give me your vineyard for money; or else, if it pleases you, I will give you a vineyard in place of it.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Jezebel his wife said to him, “Do you now ①reign over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be joyful; I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” ▷ ①Lit exercise kingship

column.name: text
column.value: So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and to the nobles who were living with Naboth in his city.

column.name: text
column.value: Now she had written in the letters, saying, “Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people;

column.name: text
column.value: and seat two worthless men opposite him, and have them testify against him, saying, ‘You ①cursed God and the king.’ Then take him out and stone him ②to death.” ▷ ①Lit blessed, an ancient euphemism to avoid any mention of the cursing of God ②Lit so that he dies

column.name: text
column.value: So the men of his city, the elders and the nobles who lived in his city, did just as Jezebel had sent word to them, just as it was written in the letters which she had sent them.

column.name: text
column.value: They proclaimed a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the two worthless men came in and sat opposite him; and the worthless men testified against him, against Naboth, before the people, saying, “Naboth ①cursed God and the king.” So they took him outside the city and stoned him ②to death with stones. ▷ ①See note 1 v 10 ②Lit with stones so that he died

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sent word to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: And when Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth, the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money; for Naboth is not alive, but dead.”

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab got up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria; behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall speak to him, saying, ‘This is what the LORD says: “Have you murdered and also taken possession?” ’ And you shall speak to him, saying, ‘The LORD says this: “In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, the dogs will lick up your blood, yours as well.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahab said to Elijah, “Have you found me, enemy of mine?” And he ①answered, “I have found you, because you have given yourself over to do evil in the sight of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I am bringing disaster upon you, and I will utterly sweep you away, and will eliminate from Ahab every male, both ①bond and free in Israel; ▷ ①Or child and adult

column.name: text
column.value: and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked Me to anger, and because you have misled Israel into sin.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD has also spoken of Jezebel, saying, ‘The dogs will eat Jezebel in the ①territory of Jezreel.’ ▷ ①As in some mss and ancient versions; MT rampart

column.name: text
column.value: The one belonging to Ahab, who dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and the one who dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.”

column.name: text
column.value: There certainly was no one like Ahab who gave himself over to do evil in the sight of the LORD, ①because Jezebel his wife incited him. ▷ ①Or whom Jezebel his wife

column.name: text
column.value: He also acted very despicably in following idols, conforming to everything that the Amorites had done, whom the LORD drove out from the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet it came about, when Ahab heard these words, that he tore his clothes and put ①on sackcloth and fasted, and he lay in sackcloth and went about despondently. ▷ ①Lit sackcloth on his flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Do you see how Ahab has humbled himself before Me? Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; I will bring the disaster upon his house in his son’s days.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now ①three years passed without war between Aram and Israel. ▷ ①Lit they sat for three years

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year, Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Israel said to his servants, “Are you aware that Ramoth-gilead belongs to us, yet we are hesitant to take it out of the hand of the king of Aram?”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go to battle with me at Ramoth-gilead?” And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “ ①Consider me yours, my people yours, and my horses yours!” ▷ ①Lit As me as you, as my people...as my horses, as your horses, an ancient idiom

column.name: text
column.value: However, Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, “Please request the word of the LORD ①first.” ▷ ①Lit today

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel assembled the ①prophets, about four hundred men, and said to them, “Should I go to battle against Ramoth-gilead or should I refrain?” And they said, “Go up, for the Lord will hand it over to the king.” ▷ ①I.e., official prophets who at that time were false

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no longer a prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of him?”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man by whom we may inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy anything good regarding me, but only bad. He is Micaiah the son of Imlah.” But Jehoshaphat said, “May the king not say so.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel summoned an officer and said, “Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, dressed in their robes, at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah made horns of iron for himself and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: All the prophets were prophesying this as well, saying, “Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, for the LORD will hand it over to the king.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the messenger who went to summon Micaiah spoke to him saying, “Behold now, the words of the prophets are ①unanimously favorable to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak favorably.” ▷ ①Lit of one mouth

column.name: text
column.value: But Micaiah said, “As the LORD lives, whatever the LORD says to me, I shall speak it.”

column.name: text
column.value: When he came to the king, the king said to him, “Micaiah, should we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain?” And he said, “Go up and succeed, for the LORD will hand it over to the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to him, “How many times must I make you swear that you will tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “I saw all Israel Scattered on the mountains, Like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, ‘These people have no master. Each of them is to return to his house in peace.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy anything good regarding me, but only bad?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Micaiah said, “Therefore, hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the ①angels of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left. ▷ ①Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said, ‘Who will ①entice Ahab to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?’ And one spirit said this, while another said that. ▷ ①Or persuade

column.name: text
column.value: Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD, and said, ‘I will ①entice him.’ ▷ ①Or persuade

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD said to him, ‘How?’ And he said, ‘I will go out and be a deceiving spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ Then He said, ‘You shall ①entice him, and you will also prevail. Go and do so.’ ▷ ①Or persuade

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, behold, the LORD has put a deceiving spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours; and the LORD has declared disaster against you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek; and he said, “How did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Micaiah said, “Behold, you are going to see how on that day when you go from one inner room to ①another trying to hide yourself.” ▷ ①Lit inner room

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

column.name: text
column.value: and say, ‘This is what the king says: “Put this man in prison, and feed him enough bread and water to survive until I ①return safely.” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit come in peace

column.name: text
column.value: But Micaiah said, “If you actually return ①safely, the LORD has not spoken by me.” And he said, “Listen, all you people!” ▷ ①Lit in peace

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up against Ramoth-gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you put on your robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram had commanded the thirty-two commanders of his chariots, saying, “Do not fight with the small or great, but only with the king of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “Surely he is the king of Israel!” And they turned aside to fight against him, and Jehoshaphat cried out.

column.name: text
column.value: Then, when the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now one man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel ①in a joint of the armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn ②around and take me out of the battle, for I am severely wounded.” ▷ ①Lit between the scales and the scale armor ②Lit your hand

column.name: text
column.value: The battle ①raged on that day, and the king was propped up in his chariot in front of the Arameans, and he died at evening, and the blood from the wound ran into the bottom of the chariot. ▷ ①Lit went up

column.name: text
column.value: Then the word passed throughout the army close to sunset, saying, “Every man to his city, and every man to his ①country!” ▷ ①Lit land

column.name: text
column.value: So the king died and was brought to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: They washed out the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood (it was there that the prostitutes bathed themselves) in accordance with the word of the LORD which He had spoken.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Ahab and everything that he did, and the ivory house which he built and all the cities which he built, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahab ①lay down with his fathers, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoshaphat the son of Asa became king over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-five years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked ①entirely in the way of his father Asa; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the sight of the LORD. However, the high places were not taken away; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. ▷ ①Lit in all the way of

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat also made peace with the king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might which he showed and how he made war, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: And the remnant of the cult prostitutes who remained in the days of his father Asa, he eliminated from the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was no king in Edom; a governor served as king.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, because the ships were destroyed at Ezion-geber.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.” But Jehoshaphat was not willing.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehoshaphat ①lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David, and his son Jehoram became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah the son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned over Israel for two years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD and walked in the way of his father and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who misled Israel into sin.

column.name: text
column.value: So he served Baal and worshiped him, and provoked the LORD God of Israel to anger, according to all that his father had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Moab broke with Israel after the death of Ahab.

column.name: text
column.value: And Ahaziah fell through the window lattice in his upper chamber which was in Samaria, and became ill. So he sent messengers and said to them, “Go, inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this sickness.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, “Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria and say to them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?’

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, this is what the LORD says: ‘ ①You will not get down from the bed upon which you have lain, but you shall certainly die.’ ” Then Elijah departed. ▷ ①Lit The bed where you went up, you will not come down from it

column.name: text
column.value: When the messengers returned to ①Ahaziah, he said to them, “ ②Why have you returned?” ▷ ①Lit him ②Lit What is this that you have returned?

column.name: text
column.value: They said to him, “A man came up to meet us and said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you and say to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore ①you will not get down from the bed upon which you have lain, but you shall certainly die.’ ” ’ ” ▷ ①See note v 4

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to them, “What ①did the man look like, who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?” ▷ ①Lit was the appearance of

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “He was a hairy man with a leather ①belt worn around his waist.” And he said, “It is Elijah the Tishbite.” ▷ ①Lit loincloth

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent to him a captain of fifty with his fifty men. And he went up to him, and behold, he was sitting on the top of the hill. And he said to him, “You man of God, the king says, ‘Come down.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Elijah replied to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty.” Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king again sent to him another captain of fifty with his fifty men. And he said to him, “You man of God, this is what the king says: ‘Come down quickly!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Elijah replied to them, “If I am a man of God, may fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty.” Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty men.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king again sent the captain of a third fifty with his fifty men. When the third captain of fifty went up, he came and bowed down on his knees before Elijah, and begged him and said to him, “You man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty with their fifties; but now let my ①life be precious in your sight.” ▷ ①Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: And the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, “Go down with him; do not be afraid of him.” So he got up and went down with him to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Since you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron—is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of His word? Therefore ①you will not get down from the bed upon which you have lain, but you shall certainly die.’ ” ▷ ①See note v 4

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahaziah died in accordance with the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken. And since he had no son, Jehoram became king in his place in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ben-hadad, king of Aram, gathered all his army, and there were thirty-two kings with him, and horses and chariots. And he went up and besieged Samaria, and fought against it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent messengers to the city to Ahab, king of Israel, and said to him, “This is what Ben-hadad says:

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Your silver and your gold are mine; your most beautiful wives and children are also mine.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of Israel replied, “As ①you say, my lord, O king; I am yours, as well as all that I have.” ▷ ①Lit your word

column.name: text
column.value: Then the messengers returned and said, “Ben-hadad says ①this: ‘I did indeed send word to you, saying, “You shall give me your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children”; ▷ ①Lit this, saying

column.name: text
column.value: but about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants; and they will take in their hands everything that is pleasing to your eyes, and take it all away.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, “Please be aware and see that this man is looking for trouble; for he sent me his demand for my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, and I did not refuse him.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen nor consent.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said to the messengers of Ben-hadad, “Tell my lord the king, ‘Everything that you sent as a demand to your servant at the first, I will do; but this thing I cannot do.’ ” Then the messengers departed, and brought him word again.

column.name: text
column.value: Ben-hadad sent word to him and said, “May the gods do so to me and more so, ①if the dust of Samaria will be enough for handfuls for all the people who ②follow me.” ▷ ①I.e., what is left of Samaria after it is destroyed ②Lit are at my feet

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel replied, “Tell him, ‘He who straps on his weapons had better not boast like one who takes them off.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: And when Ben-hadad heard this message, while he was drinking ①with the kings in the ②temporary shelters, he said to his servants, “Take your positions.” So they took their positions against the city. ▷ ①Lit he and ②Or huts

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, a prophet approached Ahab king of Israel, and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold, I am going to hand them over to you today, and you shall know that I am the LORD.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Ahab said, “By whom?” So he said, “The LORD says this: ‘By the young men of the leaders of the provinces.’ ” Then he said, “Who will begin the battle?” And he said, “You will.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he mustered the young men of the leaders of the provinces, and there were 232; and after them he mustered all the people, all the sons of Israel: seven thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: They went out at noon, while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in the ①temporary shelters ②with the thirty-two kings who were helping him. ▷ ①Or huts ②Lit he and the 32 kings

column.name: text
column.value: The young men of the leaders of the provinces went out first; and Ben-hadad sent out scouts, and they reported to him, saying, “Men have come out from Samaria.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “If they have come out ①for peace, take them alive; or if they have come out for war, take them alive as well.” ▷ ①I.e., to seek terms for surrender

column.name: text
column.value: So these men went out from the city, the young men of the leaders of the provinces, and the army which followed them.

column.name: text
column.value: And they ①killed, each one, his man; and the Arameans fled and Israel pursued them, and Ben-hadad the king of Aram escaped on a horse with horsemen. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Israel also went out and struck the horses and chariots, and ①killed the Arameans in a great slaughter. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then the prophet approached the king of Israel and said to him, “Go, show yourself courageous and be aware and see what you have to do; for at ①the turn of the year the king of Aram will march against you.” ▷ ①I.e., spring

column.name: text
column.value: Now the servants of the king of Aram said to him, “Their gods are gods of the mountains; for that reason they were stronger than we. But let us fight them in the plain, and we will certainly be stronger than they.

column.name: text
column.value: Carry out this ①plan: remove the kings, each from his place, and put governors in their place, ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: and ①muster an army like the army that you have lost, horse for horse and chariot for chariot. Then we will fight against them in the plain, and we will certainly be stronger than they.” And he listened to their voice and did so. ▷ ①Lit count

column.name: text
column.value: So at ①the turn of the year Ben-hadad mustered the Arameans and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel. ▷ ①I.e., spring

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel were mustered and given provisions, and they went to meet them; and the sons of Israel camped opposite them like two little flocks of goats, while the Arameans filled the country.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a man of God approached and spoke to the king of Israel, and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Since the Arameans have said, “The LORD is a god of mountains, but He is not a god of valleys,” therefore I will hand over to you all this great multitude, and you shall know that I am the LORD.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So they camped, one opposite the other, for seven days. And on the seventh day the battle was joined, and the sons of Israel ①killed of the Arameans a hundred thousand foot soldiers in a single day. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: But the rest fled to Aphek into the city, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand men who were left. And Ben-hadad fled and came into the city, going from one inner room to another.

column.name: text
column.value: But his servants said to him, “Behold now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Please let’s put sackcloth ①around our waists and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will let ②you live.” ▷ ①Lit on ②Lit your soul

column.name: text
column.value: So they put sackcloth ①around their waists and ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said, “Your servant Ben-hadad says, ‘Please let ②me live.’ ” And Ahab said, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.” ▷ ①Lit on ②Lit my soul

column.name: text
column.value: Now the men took this as a good omen, and quickly ①accepting it from him, they said, “Your brother Ben-hadad.” Then he said, “Go, bring him.” Then Ben-hadad came out to him, and he had him mount the chariot. ▷ ①Lit accepted

column.name: text
column.value: And Ben-hadad said to him, “The cities which my father took from your father I will restore, and you can make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria.” Ahab said, “And I will let you go with this covenant.” So he made a covenant with him and let him go.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man from the sons of the prophets said to ①another by the word of the LORD, “Please strike me.” But the man refused to strike him. ▷ ①Lit his neighbor

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to him, “Because you have not listened to the voice of the LORD, behold, as soon as you leave me, a lion will ①kill you.” And as soon as he left him a lion found him and ②killed him. ▷ ①Lit strike ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then he found another man and said, “Please strike me.” And the man struck him, ①injuring him. ▷ ①Lit striking and injuring

column.name: text
column.value: So the prophet departed and waited for the king by the road, and disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: And as the king passed by, he cried out to the king and said, “Your servant went out into the midst of the battle; and behold, a man turned aside and brought a man to me and said, ‘Guard this man; if for any reason he goes missing, then your life shall be forfeited in place of his life, or else you shall pay a ①talent of silver.’ ▷ ①About 75 lb. or 34 kg

column.name: text
column.value: Now while your servant was busy here and there, he disappeared.” And the king of Israel said to him, “So shall your judgment be; you yourself determined it.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he quickly took the bandage away from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: And the prophet said to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Since you have let go from your hand the man I had designated for destruction, your ①life shall be forfeited in place of his ②life, and your people in place of his people.’ ” ▷ ①Lit soul ②Lit soul

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel went to his house sullen and furious, and came to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, when the LORD was about to bring Elijah up by a ①whirlwind to heaven, that Elijah left Gilgal with Elisha. ▷ ①Or windstorm

column.name: text
column.value: And Elijah said to Elisha, “Stay here please, for the LORD has sent me as far as Bethel.” But Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So they went down to Bethel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of the prophets who were at Bethel went out to Elisha and said to him, “Are you aware that the LORD will take away your master from over ①you today?” And he said, “Yes, I am aware; say nothing about it.” ▷ ①Lit your head

column.name: text
column.value: And Elijah said to him, “Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to Jericho.” But he said, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So they came to Jericho.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho approached Elisha and said to him, “Do you know that the LORD will take away your master from over ①you today?” And he ②answered, “Yes, I know; say nothing about it.” ▷ ①Lit your head ②Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: And Elijah said to him, “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me to the Jordan.” But he said, “As surely as the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So the two of them went on.

column.name: text
column.value: Now fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: And Elijah took his coat, folded it, and struck the waters, and they were divided here and there, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had crossed over, Elijah said to Elisha, “Ask me what I should do for you before I am taken from you.” And Elisha said, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be upon me.”

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “You have asked a hard thing. Nevertheless, if you see me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so.”

column.name: text
column.value: And as they were walking along and talking, behold, a chariot of fire appeared with horses of fire, and they separated the two of them. Then Elijah went up by a ①whirlwind to heaven. ▷ ①Or windstorm

column.name: text
column.value: And Elisha was watching it and he was crying out, “My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!” And he did not see ①Elijah again. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two pieces. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: He also took up the coat of Elijah that had fallen from him, and he went back and stood by the bank of the Jordan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he took the coat of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the waters, and said, “Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?” And when he also had struck the waters, they were divided here and there; and Elisha crossed over.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho opposite him saw him, they said, “The spirit of Elijah has settled on Elisha.” And they came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to him, “Behold now, there are with your servants fifty strong men; please let them go and search for your master, in case the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and cast him on some mountain or into some valley.” But he said, “You shall not send anyone.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet when they urged him until he was ashamed to refuse, he said, “Send them.” So they sent fifty men; and they searched for three days, but did not find him.

column.name: text
column.value: They returned to him while he was staying in Jericho; and he said to them, “Did I not say to you, ‘Do not go’?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men of the city said to Elisha, “Behold now, the site of the city is pleasant, as my lord sees; but the water is bad and the land ①is unfruitful.” ▷ ①Lit causes miscarriages

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Bring me a new jar, and put salt ①in it.” So they brought it to him. ▷ ①Lit there

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went out to the spring of water and threw salt ①in it and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘I have ②purified these waters; there shall not come from there death or ③unfruitfulness any longer.’ ” ▷ ①Lit there ②Lit healed ③Lit anything causing miscarriages

column.name: text
column.value: So the waters have been ①purified to this day, in accordance with the word of Elisha which he spoke. ▷ ①Lit healed

column.name: text
column.value: Now he went up from there to Bethel; and as he was going up by the road, some young boys came out from the city and ridiculed him and said to him, “Go up, you baldhead; go up, you baldhead!”

column.name: text
column.value: When he looked behind him and saw them, he cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two female bears came out of the woods and tore up forty-two ①of the boys. ▷ ①Lit boys from them

column.name: text
column.value: He then went on from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab became king over Israel at Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned for twelve years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, though not like his father and his mother; for he removed the memorial stone of Baal which his father had made.

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, he clung to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; he did not abandon them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Mesha the king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to make tribute payments to the king of Israel of a hundred thousand lambs, and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.

column.name: text
column.value: However, when King Ahab died, the king of Moab broke with the ①king of Israel. ▷ ①I.e., Jehoram, the new king

column.name: text
column.value: So King Jehoram left Samaria for battle ①at that time and mustered all Israel. ▷ ①Lit in that day

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went and sent word to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has broken away from me. Will you go with me to fight against Moab?” And he said, “I will go up. ①Consider me yours, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.” ▷ ①Lit As I, as you, as my people...

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Which way shall we go up?” And he ①answered, “The way of the wilderness of Edom.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel went with the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they made a circuit of seven days’ journey. But there was no water for the army or for the cattle that ①followed them. ▷ ①Lit were in their footsteps

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel said, “It is hopeless! For the LORD has called these three kings to hand them over to Moab!”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshaphat said, “Is there no prophet of the LORD here, that we may inquire of the LORD by him?” And one of the king of Israel’s servants answered and said, “Elisha the son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehoshaphat said, “The word of the LORD is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha said to the king of Israel, “ ①What business do you have with me? Go to your father’s prophets and your mother’s prophets.” But the king of Israel said to him, “No, for the LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab.” ▷ ①Lit What to me and to you, an ancient idiom

column.name: text
column.value: Elisha said, “As surely as the LORD of armies lives, before whom I stand, if I did not respect Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look at you nor see you.

column.name: text
column.value: But now bring me a ①musician.” And it came about, when the ②musician played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him. ▷ ①Lit string player ②Lit string player

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Make this valley ①full of trenches.’ ▷ ①Lit trenches, trenches

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD says this: ‘You will not see wind, nor will you see rain; yet that valley shall be filled with water, so that you will drink, you, your livestock, and your other animals.

column.name: text
column.value: And this is an insignificant thing in the sight of the LORD; He will also give the Moabites into your hand.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you shall strike every fortified city and every choice city, and ①cut down every good tree and stop up all the springs of water, and spoil every good plot of land with stones.’ ” ▷ ①Lit fell

column.name: text
column.value: And it happened in the morning about the time of offering the sacrifice, that behold, water came from the direction of Edom, and the country was filled with water.

column.name: text
column.value: Now all the Moabites heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. And all who were able to ①put on armor and older were summoned and they took their positions on the border. ▷ ①Lit strap on a belt (for weapons)

column.name: text
column.value: Then they got up early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite them as red as blood.

column.name: text
column.value: So they said, “This is blood; the kings must have fought each other, and they have killed one another. Now then, Moab, to the spoils!”

column.name: text
column.value: But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck the Moabites, so that they fled from them; and the Israelites invaded ①the land, ②killing the Moabites. ▷ ①Lit it ②Lit striking

column.name: text
column.value: So they destroyed the cities; and each one threw a stone on every plot of good land and filled it. So they stopped up every spring of water and ①cut down every good tree, until in Kir-hareseth only they left its stones; however, the rock slingers surrounded it and struck it. ▷ ①Lit felled

column.name: text
column.value: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew swords, to break through to the king of Edom; but they could not.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Moab took his oldest son who was to reign in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And great anger came upon Israel, and they departed from him and returned to their own land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD; and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” And she said, “Your servant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Go, ①borrow containers ②elsewhere for yourself, empty containers from all your neighbors—do not get too few. ▷ ①Lit request ②Lit from outside

column.name: text
column.value: Then you shall come in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour into all these containers; and you shall set aside what is full.”

column.name: text
column.value: So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they began bringing the containers to her, and she poured the oil.

column.name: text
column.value: When the containers were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another container.” But he said to her, “There ①are no more containers.” Then the oil stopped. ▷ ①Lit is...container

column.name: text
column.value: So she came and told the man of God. And he said, “Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons can live on the rest.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now a day came when Elisha went over to Shunem, where there was a ①prominent woman, and she urged him to eat ②food. And so it was, as often as he passed by, that he turned in there to eat ③food. ▷ ①Lit great ②Lit bread ③Lit bread

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her husband, “Behold now, I am aware that this is a holy man of God passing by us repeatedly.

column.name: text
column.value: Please, let’s make a little walled upper room, and let’s set up a bed for him there, and a table, a chair, and a lampstand; then it shall be, when he comes to us, that he can turn in there.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now ①one day he came there, and turned in to the upper room and ②rested. ▷ ①Lit the day came that ②Lit lay there

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to his servant Gehazi, “Call this Shunammite.” And when he had called her, she stood before him.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to him, “Say now to her, ‘Behold, you have taken trouble for us with all this ①care; what can I do for you? ②Would you like me to speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’ ” But she ③answered, “I live among my own people.” ▷ ①Lit fear ②Lit Is it to speak ③Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “What then is to be done for her?” And Gehazi ①answered, “It is a fact that she has no son, and her husband is old.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: He then said, “Call her.” When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “At this season ①next year, you are going to embrace a son.” And she said, “No, my lord, you man of God, do not lie to your servant.” ▷ ①Lit when the time revives

column.name: text
column.value: Now the woman conceived and gave birth to a son at that season ①the next year, as Elisha had told her. ▷ ①Lit when the time revived

column.name: text
column.value: When the child was grown, the day came that he went out to his father, to the reapers.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to his father, “My head, my head!” And his father said to his servant, “Carry him to his mother.”

column.name: text
column.value: When he had carried him and brought him to his mother, he sat on her ①lap until noon, and then he died. ▷ ①Lit knees

column.name: text
column.value: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and shut the door behind him and left.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she called to her husband and said, “Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may run to the man of God and return.”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath.” So she just said, “It will be fine.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Drive the donkey and go on; do not slow down ①the pace for me unless I tell you.” ▷ ①Lit riding

column.name: text
column.value: So she went on and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her at a distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Behold, that person there is the Shunammite.

column.name: text
column.value: Please run now to meet her and say to her, ‘Is it going well for you? Is it going well for your husband? Is it going well for the child?’ ” Then she ①answered, “It is going well.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: But she came to the man of God at the hill and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi came up to push her away, but the man of God said, “Leave her alone, for her soul is ①troubled within her; and the LORD has concealed it from me and has not informed me.” ▷ ①Lit bitter

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, ‘Do not give me false hope’?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to Gehazi, “ ①Get ready and take my staff in your hand, and go; if you meet anyone, do not ②greet him, and if anyone ③greets you, do not reply to him. And lay my staff on the boy’s face.” ▷ ①Lit Belt up your waist ②Lit bless ③Lit blesses

column.name: text
column.value: The mother of the boy said, “As surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, I will not leave you.” So he got up and followed her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy’s face, but there was no sound or ①response. So he returned to meet him and informed him, saying, “The boy has not awakened.” ▷ ①Lit attentiveness

column.name: text
column.value: When Elisha entered the house, behold the boy was dead, laid on his bed.

column.name: text
column.value: So he entered and shut the door behind them both, and he prayed to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he got up on the bed and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, his hands on his hands, and he bent down on him; and the flesh of the child became warm.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he returned and walked in the house back and forth once, and went up and bent down on him; and the boy sneezed seven times, then the boy opened his eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: And he called Gehazi and said, “Call this Shunammite.” So he called her. And when she came to him, he said, “Pick up your son.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then she came in and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, and she picked up her son and left.

column.name: text
column.value: When Elisha returned to Gilgal, there was a famine in the land. ①As the sons of the prophets were sitting in front of him, he said to his servant, “Put on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.” ▷ ①Lit And

column.name: text
column.value: Then one went out into the field to gather mallow, and found a wild vine and gathered from it his lap full of wild gourds; and he came and sliced them into the pot of stew, because they did not know what they were.

column.name: text
column.value: So they poured it out for the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out and said, “You man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they were unable to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Bring flour.” And he threw it into the pot, and said, “Pour it out for the people that they may eat.” Then there was nothing harmful in the pot.

column.name: text
column.value: Now a man came from Baal-shalishah, and brought the man of God bread of the first fruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. And Elisha said, “Give them to the people that they may eat.”

column.name: text
column.value: But his attendant said, “How am I to serve this to a hundred men?” Nevertheless he said, “Give them to the people that they may eat, for this is what the LORD says: ‘They shall eat and have some left over.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So he served it to them, and they ate and had some left over, in accordance with the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man ①in the view of his master, and eminent, because by him the LORD had given victory to Aram. The man was also a valiant warrior, but afflicted with leprosy. ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: Now the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken captive a little girl from the land of Israel; and she ①waited on Naaman’s wife. ▷ ①Lit was before

column.name: text
column.value: And she said to her mistress, “If only my master were ①with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his leprosy.” ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: And ①Naaman went in and told his master, saying, “The girl who is from the land of Israel spoke such and such.” ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Aram said, “Go ①now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.” So he departed and took with him ten ②talents of silver, six thousand ③shekels of gold, and ten changes of clothes. ▷ ①Lit enter ②A talent was about 75 lb. or 34 kg ③A shekel was about 0.5 oz. or 14 gm

column.name: text
column.value: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, ①which said, “And now as this letter comes to you, behold, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy.” ▷ ①Lit saying

column.name: text
column.value: But when the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, “Am I God, to kill and to keep alive, that this man is sending word to me to cure a man of his leprosy? But consider now, and see how he is seeking ①a quarrel against me.” ▷ ①Lit an opportunity

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened, when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, that he sent word to the king, saying, “Why did you tear your clothes? Just have him come to me, and he shall learn that there is a prophet in Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots, and stood at the doorway of Elisha’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: And Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh will be restored to you and you will be clean.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Naaman was furious and went away, and he said, “Behold, I ①thought, ‘He will certainly come out to me, and stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the site and cure the ②leprosy.’ ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit one with leprosy

column.name: text
column.value: Are ①Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, not better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?” So he turned and went away in a rage. ▷ ①Another reading is Amanah

column.name: text
column.value: Then his servants approached and spoke to him, ①saying, “My father, had the prophet told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean’?” ▷ ①Lit and said

column.name: text
column.value: So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, in accordance with the word of the man of God; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he returned to the man of God ①with all his company, and came and stood before him. And he said, “Behold now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, except in Israel; so please accept a ②gift from your servant now.” ▷ ①Lit he and ②Lit blessing

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing.” And he urged him to accept it, but he refused.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Naaman said, “If not, please let your servant be given two mules’ load of earth; for your servant will no longer offer a burnt offering nor a sacrifice to other gods, but to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Regarding this matter may the LORD forgive your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand and I bow down in the house of Rimmon, when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may the LORD please forgive your servant in this matter.”

column.name: text
column.value: He said to him, “Go in peace.” So he went some distance from him.

column.name: text
column.value: But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, ①thought, “Behold, my master has spared this Naaman the Aramean, ②by not accepting from his hand what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him.” ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit from

column.name: text
column.value: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he came down from the chariot to meet him and said, “Is everything well?”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Everything is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, just now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Naaman said, “Be sure to take two talents.” And he urged him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags with two changes of clothes, and gave them to two of his servants; and they carried them before him.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came to the ①hill, he took them from their hand and deposited them in the house, and he sent the men away, and they departed. ▷ ①Lit Ophel

column.name: text
column.value: But he went in and stood before his master. And Elisha said to him, “Where have you been, Gehazi?” And he said, “Your servant went nowhere.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to him, “Did my heart not go with you, when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to accept money and to accept clothes, olive groves, vineyards, sheep, oxen, and male and female slaves?

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you and to your ①descendants forever.” So he went out from his presence afflicted with leprosy, as white as snow. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Now the sons of the prophets said to Elisha, “Behold now, the place ①before you where we are living is too cramped for us. ▷ ①Or where we sit in your presence

column.name: text
column.value: Please let us go to the Jordan, and let us each take from there a beam, and let us construct a place there for ourselves, to live there.” So he said, “Go.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then one of them said, “Please agree and go with your servants.” And he said, “I will go.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he went with them; and when they came to the Jordan, they cut down trees.

column.name: text
column.value: But it happened that as one of them was ①cutting down a beam, ②the axe head fell into the water; and he cried out and said, “Oh, my master! It was borrowed!” ▷ ①Or dropping; lit felling ②Lit as for the iron, it fell

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man of God said, “Where did it fall?” And when he showed him the place, he cut off a stick and threw it in there, and made the iron float.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Pick it up for yourself.” So he reached out his hand and took it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram was making war against Israel; and he consulted with his servants, saying, “In such and such a place shall be my camp.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel, saying, “Be careful that you do not pass this place, because the Arameans are coming down there.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of Israel sent scouts to the place about which the man of God had told him; so he warned him, so that he was on his guard there, ①more than once or twice. ▷ ①Lit not once or twice

column.name: text
column.value: Now the heart of the king of Aram was enraged over this matter; and he called his servants and said to them, “Will you not tell me which of us is for the king of Israel?”

column.name: text
column.value: One of his servants said, “No, my lord, the king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he said, “Go and see where he is, so that I may send men and take him.” And it was told to him, saying, “Behold, he is in Dothan.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent horses and chariots and a substantial army there, and they came by night and surrounded the city.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the attendant of the man of God had risen early and gone out, behold, an army with horses and chariots was circling the city. And his servant said to him, “This is hopeless, my master! ①What are we to do?” ▷ ①Lit How

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are ①greater than those who are with them.” ▷ ①Or more

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha prayed and said, “LORD, please, open his eyes so that he may see.” And the LORD opened the servant’s eyes, and he saw; and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, “Please strike this ①people with blindness.” So He struck them with blindness in accordance with the word of Elisha. ▷ ①Lit nation

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, nor is this the city; follow me and I will bring you to the man whom you seek.” And he brought them to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had come into Samaria, Elisha said, “LORD, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see.” So the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw; and behold, they were in the midst of Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel when he saw them, said to Elisha, “My father, shall I ①kill them? Shall I ②kill them?” ▷ ①Lit strike ②Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: But he ①answered, “You shall not ②kill them. Would you ③kill those whom you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.” ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit strike ③Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: So he provided a large feast for them; and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. And the marauding bands of Arameans did not come again into the land of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after this, that Ben-hadad the king of Aram gathered all his army, and went up and besieged Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: So there was a severe famine in Samaria; and behold, they kept besieging it until a donkey’s head was sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a fourth of a ①kab of dove’s dung for five shekels of silver. ▷ ①One kab equals about 2 qt. or 1.9 liters

column.name: text
column.value: And as the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, “Help, my lord the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said, “ ①If the LORD does not help you, from where am I to help you? From the threshing floor, or from the wine press?” ▷ ①Or No! Let the LORD help you

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to her, “What ①is on your mind?” And she said, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.’ ▷ ①Lit to you

column.name: text
column.value: So we cooked my son and ate him; and I said to her on the next day, ‘Give your son, so that we may eat him’; but she has hidden her son.”

column.name: text
column.value: When the king heard the woman’s words, he tore his clothes—and he was passing by on the wall—and the people looked, and behold, he had sackcloth ①underneath on his ②body. ▷ ①Lit within ②Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “May God do so to me and more so, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat ①remains on him today.” ▷ ①Lit stands

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. And the king sent a man from his presence; but before the messenger came to him, he said to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent a man to cut off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and ①hold the door shut against him. Is the sound of his master’s feet not behind him?” ▷ ①Lit press him with the door

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still talking with them, behold, the messenger came down to him and he said, “Behold, this evil is from the LORD; why should I wait for the LORD any longer?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha said, “Listen to the word of the LORD; this is what the LORD says: ‘About this time tomorrow a ①measure of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.’ ” ▷ ①Heb seah

column.name: text
column.value: The royal officer on whose hand the king was leaning responded to the man of God and said, “Even if the LORD were to make ①windows in heaven, could this thing happen?” Then he said, “Behold, you are going to see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat ②any of it.” ▷ ①Or hatches ②Lit from there

column.name: text
column.value: Now there were four leprous men at the entrance of the gate; and they said to one another, “Why are we sitting here until we die?

column.name: text
column.value: If we say, ‘We will enter the city,’ then the famine is in the city and we will die there; but if we sit here, we will also die. Now then come, and let’s go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they spare us, we will live; and if they kill us, then we will die.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they got up at twilight to go to the camp of the Arameans; when they came to the outskirts of the camp of the Arameans, behold, there was no one there.

column.name: text
column.value: For the Lord had made the army of the Arameans hear a sound of chariots, a sound of horses, that is, the sound of a great army; and they said to one another, “Behold, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Egyptians against us, to ①attack us!” ▷ ①Lit come against

column.name: text
column.value: So they got up and fled at twilight, and abandoned their tents, their horses, and their donkeys—indeed the camp itself, just as it was; and they fled for their lives.

column.name: text
column.value: When these men with leprosy came to the outskirts of the camp, they entered one tent and ate and drank, and carried from there silver, gold, and clothes, and they went and hid them; then they returned and entered another tent, and carried valuables from there also, and went and hid them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they said to one another, “We are not doing the right thing. This day is a day of good news, but we are keeping silent about it; if we wait until the morning light, punishment will ①overtake us. Now then come, let’s go and inform the king’s household.” ▷ ①Lit find

column.name: text
column.value: So they came and called to the gatekeepers of the city, and told them, saying, “We came to the camp of the Arameans, and behold, there was no one there, nor a human voice; only the horses tied and the donkeys tied, and the tents just as they were.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the gatekeepers called and announced it inside the king’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king got up in the night and said to his servants, “I will now tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry; so they have left the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, ‘When they come out of the city, we will capture them alive and get into the city.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: One of his servants responded and said, “Please, have some men take five of the horses that remain, which are left ①in the city. Behold, they will be in any case like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it; behold, they will be like all the multitude of Israel who have already perished, so let us send them and see.” ▷ ①Lit in it

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the army of the Arameans, saying, “Go and see.”

column.name: text
column.value: They went after them to the Jordan, and behold, all the way was full of clothes and equipment which the Arameans had thrown away when they fled in a hurry. Then the messengers returned and informed the king.

column.name: text
column.value: So the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. Then a ①measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and two ②measures of barley for a shekel, in accordance with the word of the LORD. ▷ ①Heb seah ②Heb seah

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king appointed the royal officer on whose hand he leaned ①to be in charge of the gate; but the people trampled on him at the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had said, who spoke when the king came down to him. ▷ ①Lit over the gate

column.name: text
column.value: So it happened just as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, “Two ①measures of barley for a shekel and a ②measure of fine flour for a shekel, will be sold about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria.” ▷ ①Heb seahs ②Heb seahs

column.name: text
column.value: At that time the royal officer had responded to the man of God and said, “Now even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven, could such a thing as this happen?” And he had said, “Behold, you are going to see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat ①any of it.” ▷ ①Lit from there

column.name: text
column.value: And this is what happened to him, for the people trampled on him at the gate and he died.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha spoke to the woman whose son he had restored to life, saying, “Arise and go ①with your household, and live wherever you can live; for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will indeed come on the land for seven years.” ▷ ①Lit you and your

column.name: text
column.value: So the woman arose and acted in accordance with the word of the man of God: she went with her household and resided in the land of the Philistines for seven years.

column.name: text
column.value: Then at the end of seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines; and she went to ①appeal to the king for her house and for her field. ▷ ①Lit cry out

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king was speaking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please report to me all the great things that Elisha has done.”

column.name: text
column.value: And as he was reporting to the king how he had restored to life the one who was dead, behold, the woman whose son he had restored to life ①appealed to the king for her house and for her field. And Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.” ▷ ①Lit cried out

column.name: text
column.value: When the king asked the woman, she told everything to him. So the king appointed an officer for her, saying, “Restore all that was hers and all the produce of the field from the day that she left the land even until now.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha came to Damascus. Now Ben-hadad, the king of Aram, was sick, and it was told to him, saying, “The man of God has come here.”

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD by him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: So Hazael went to meet him and took a gift in his hand, even every kind of good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ loads; and he came and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha said to him, “Go, say to him, ‘You will certainly recover’; but the LORD has shown me that he will certainly die.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he ①stared steadily at him until Hazael was embarrassed, and then the man of God wept. ▷ ①Lit made his face stand fast and he set

column.name: text
column.value: And Hazael said, “Why is my lord weeping?” And he ①answered, “Because I know the evil that you will do to the sons of Israel: you will set their fortified cities on fire, you will kill their young men with the sword, their little ones you will smash to pieces, and you will rip up their pregnant women.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hazael said, “But what is your servant—a lowly dog—that he could do this great thing?” And Elisha ①answered, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: So he left Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, “What did Elisha say to you?” And he ①answered, “He told me that you would certainly recover.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: But on the following day, he took the ①cover and dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, so that he died. And Hazael became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., item of woven material

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, when Jehoshaphat was the king of Judah, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.

column.name: text
column.value: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: However, the LORD did not want to destroy Judah, for the sake of David His servant, since He had ①promised him to give him a ②lamp through his sons always. ▷ ①Lit said to him ②I.e., descendant on the throne

column.name: text
column.value: In his days Edom broke away from the ①rule of Judah, and appointed a king over themselves. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joram crossed over to Zair, and all his chariots with him. And he got up at night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the captains of the chariots; but ①his army fled to their tents. ▷ ①Lit the people

column.name: text
column.value: So Edom has broken away from ①Judah to this day. Then Libnah broke away at the same time. ▷ ①Lit under the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Joram and everything that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: So Joram ①lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and his son Ahaziah became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD, like the house of Ahab, because he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he went with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans ①wounded Joram. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: So King Joram returned to have himself healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Arameans had ①inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel because he was sick. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Now Elisha the prophet summoned one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, “ ①Get ready and take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead. ▷ ①Lit Belt up your waist

column.name: text
column.value: When you arrive there, then look there for Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in and have him get up from among his brothers, and bring him to an inner room.

column.name: text
column.value: Then take the flask of oil and pour it on his head, and say, ‘This is what the LORD says: “I have anointed you king over Israel.” ’ Then open the door and flee, and do not wait.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the young man, the servant of the prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
