column.name: text
column.value: When he arrived, behold, the commanders of the army were sitting, and he said, “I have a word for you, commander.” And Jehu said, “ ①For which one of us?” And he said, “For you, commander.” ▷ ①Lit To whom of us all?

column.name: text
column.value: He then got up and went into the house, and the prophet’s servant poured the oil on his head and said to him, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘I have anointed you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall strike the house of Ahab your master, so that I may avenge the blood of My servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of the LORD, at the hand of Jezebel.

column.name: text
column.value: For the entire house of Ahab shall perish, and I will eliminate from Ahab every male person both ①slave and free in Israel. ▷ ①Or child and adult

column.name: text
column.value: I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah.

column.name: text
column.value: The dogs will eat Jezebel in the territory of Jezreel, and no one will bury her.’ ” Then he opened the door and fled.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehu went out to the servants of his master, and one said to him, “Is everything well? Why did this crazy fellow come to you?” And he said to them, “You know very well the man and his talk.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they said, “It is a lie; tell us now.” And he said, “Such and such he said to me, saying, ‘This is what the LORD says: “I have anointed you king over Israel.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they hurried, and each man took his garment and put it under him on the bare steps, and blew the trumpet, saying, “Jehu is king!”

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram ①with all Israel was ②defending Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram, ▷ ①Lit he and ②Lit protecting

column.name: text
column.value: but King ①Joram had returned to Jezreel to have himself healed of the wounds which the Arameans had ②inflicted on him when he fought Hazael king of Aram. So Jehu said to the other men, “If this is your ③intent, then let no ④one escape from the city to go tell about it in Jezreel.” ▷ ①Heb Jehoram ②Lit struck ③Lit soul ④Lit escapee leave

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu rode in a chariot and went to Jezreel, since Joram was lying there recovering. And Ahaziah the king of Judah had come down to see Joram.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the watchman was standing on the tower in Jezreel and he saw the ①company of Jehu as he came, and he said, “I see a ②company.” And ③Joram said, “Take a horseman and send him to meet them and have him ④ask, ‘Is your intention peace?’ ” ▷ ①Lit crowd ②Lit crowd ③Heb Jehoram ④Lit say

column.name: text
column.value: So a horseman went to meet him and said, “This is what the king says: ‘Is your intention peace?’ ” But Jehu said, “ ①How is peace any business of yours? Turn and follow me.” And the watchman ②reported, “The messenger came to them, but he did not return.” ▷ ①Lit What to you and to peace ②Lit reported, saying

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent a second horseman, and he came to them and said, “This is what the king says: ‘Is your intention peace?’ ” And Jehu ①answered, “ ②How is peace any business of yours? Turn and follow me.” ▷ ①Lit said ②See note 1 v 18

column.name: text
column.value: And the watchman ①reported, “He came up to them, but he did not return; and the ②driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.” ▷ ①Lit reported, saying ②I.e., of the chariot

column.name: text
column.value: Then ①Joram said, “ ②Get ready.” And they ③made his chariot ready. Then ④Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot, and they went out to meet Jehu and found him on the ⑤property of Naboth the Jezreelite. ▷ ①Heb Jehoram ②Lit Harness the chariot ③Lit harnessed ④Heb Jehoram ⑤Lit portion

column.name: text
column.value: When ①Joram saw Jehu, he said, “Is your intention peace, Jehu?” And he ②answered, “What ‘peace,’ so long as your mother Jezebel’s acts of prostitution and witchcraft are so many?” ▷ ①Heb Jehoram ②Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: So ①Joram ②turned back and fled, and he said to Ahaziah, “There is treachery, Ahaziah!” ▷ ①Heb Jehoram ②Lit turned his hands

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu ①drew his bow with his full strength and ②shot ③Joram between his arms; and the arrow went ④through his heart, and he sank in his chariot. ▷ ①Lit filled his hand with the bow ②Lit struck ③Heb Jehoram ④Lit out from

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, “Pick him up and throw him on the ①property of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember, when ②you and I were riding together after his father Ahab, that the LORD brought this pronouncement against him: ▷ ①Lit portion ②Lit I and you

column.name: text
column.value: ‘I have certainly seen yesterday the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons,’ declares the LORD, ‘and I will repay you on this ①property,’ declares the LORD. Now then, pick him up and throw him on the ②property, in accordance with the word of the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit portion ②Lit portion

column.name: text
column.value: When Ahaziah the king of Judah saw this, he fled by way of the garden house. But Jehu pursued him and said, “ ①Shoot him too, in the chariot.” So they shot him at the ascent of Gur, which is at Ibleam. But he fled to Megiddo and died there. ▷ ①Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: Then his servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and buried him in his grave with his fathers in the city of David.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the eleventh year of Joram, the son of Ahab, Ahaziah became king over Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jehu came to Jezreel, Jezebel heard about it, and she put makeup on her eyes and adorned her head, and looked down through the window.

column.name: text
column.value: As Jehu entered the gate, she said, “Is your intention peace, Zimri, his master’s murderer?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he raised his face toward the window and said, “Who is with me, who?” And two or three officials looked down at him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Throw her down.” So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her underfoot.

column.name: text
column.value: When he came in, he ate and drank; and he said, “See now to this cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king’s daughter.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore they returned and informed him. And he said, “This is the word of the LORD, which He spoke by His servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘On the ①property of Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel; ▷ ①Lit portion

column.name: text
column.value: and the corpse of Jezebel will be like dung on the face of the field in the ①property of Jezreel, so they cannot say, “This is Jezebel.” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit portion

column.name: text
column.value: In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel, Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah became king.

column.name: text
column.value: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, yet not like his father David; he acted in accordance with everything that his father Joash had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the high places were not eliminated; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, as soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, that he ①killed his servants who had ②killed the king, his father. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: But he did not put the sons of ①the murderers to death, in ②obedience to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses, as the LORD commanded, saying, “The fathers shall not be put to death for the sons, nor the sons be put to death for the fathers; but each shall be put to death for his own sin.” ▷ ①Lit those who struck ②Lit accordance with what

column.name: text
column.value: He ①killed ten thousand of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and took Sela by war, and named it Joktheel, as it is to this day. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amaziah sent messengers to ①Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let’s face each other in combat.” ▷ ①In Heb Jehoash is another spelling of Joash

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoash king of Israel sent messengers to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thorn bush that was in Lebanon sent word to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son ①in marriage.’ But a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thorn bush. ▷ ①Lit as a wife

column.name: text
column.value: You have indeed ①defeated Edom, and your heart ②is elated. Enjoy the glory and stay home; for why should you get involved in trouble so that you would fall, you and Judah with you?” ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit has lifted you up

column.name: text
column.value: But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up; and they faced each other, he and Amaziah king of Judah, at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And Judah was defeated by Israel, and they fled, every man to his tent.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh, and came to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, ①four hundred cubits. ▷ ①About 600 ft. or 183 m

column.name: text
column.value: And he took all the gold and silver and all the utensils which were found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasuries of the king’s house, the hostages as well, and returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jehoash that he did, and his might and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoash ①lay down with his fathers and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and his son Jeroboam became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lived for fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: They formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent men to Lachish after him and they killed him there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they carried him on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his fathers in the city of David.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people of Judah took ①Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah. ▷ ①In 2 Chr 26:1, Uzziah

column.name: text
column.value: He built Elath and restored it to Judah after the king ①lay down with his fathers. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and reigned for forty-one years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not abandon all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He restored the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath as far as the Sea of the Arabah, in accordance with the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which He spoke ①through His servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher. ▷ ①Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD saw the misery of Israel, which was very bitter; for there was neither ①bond nor free spared, nor was there any helper for Israel. ▷ ①Or child nor adult

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD did not say that He would wipe out the name of Israel from under heaven, but He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam and all that he did and his might, how he fought and how he recovered for Israel Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: And Jeroboam ①lay down with his fathers, with the kings of Israel, and his son Zechariah became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.

column.name: text
column.value: He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was ①Jecoliah of Jerusalem. ▷ ①In 2 Chr 26:3, Jechiliah

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with everything that his father Amaziah had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the high places were not eliminated; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD afflicted the king, so that he had leprosy to the day of his death. And he lived in a separate house, ①while Jotham the king’s son was in charge of the household, judging the people of the land. ▷ ①Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Azariah and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: And Azariah ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jotham became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria for six months.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his fathers had done; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him in the presence of the people and ①killed him, and reigned in his place. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the word of the LORD which He spoke to Jehu, saying, “Your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” And so it was.

column.name: text
column.value: Shallum the son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned for ①one month in Samaria. ▷ ①Lit a month of days

column.name: text
column.value: Then Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria, and struck Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria, and killed him and became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Shallum and his conspiracy which he formed, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah and all who were in it and its borders from Tirzah, because they did not open up to him; so he attacked it and ripped up all its women who were pregnant.

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi became king over Israel and reigned for ten years in Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD; for all his days he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Pul, the king of Assyria, came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a ①thousand talents of silver so that his hand might be with him to strengthen the ②kingdom ③under his rule. ▷ ①About 38 tons or 34 metric tons ②Or royal power ③Lit in his hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then Menahem collected the money from Israel, from all the ①mighty men of wealth, from each man fifty shekels of silver to pay the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria returned and did not stay there in the land. ▷ ①I.e., landowners

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Menahem and all that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: And Menahem ①lay down with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned for two years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Pekah the son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him and struck him in Samaria, in the castle of the king’s house with Argob and Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites, and he killed him and became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Pekahiah and everything that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for twenty years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, ①Tiglath-pileser the king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he led ②their populations into exile to Assyria. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 5:6, 26, Tilgath-pilneser ②Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: And Hoshea the son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, and struck him and put him to death, and he became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Pekah and all that he did, behold, they are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of ①Uzziah king of Judah became king. ▷ ①I.e., Azariah

column.name: text
column.value: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD; he acted in accordance with everything that his father Uzziah had done.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the high places were not eliminated; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places. He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jotham which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: In those days the LORD began to send Rezin the king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jotham ①lay down with his fathers, and he was buried with his fathers in the city of his father David; and his son Ahaz became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu became king over Israel at Samaria, and he reigned for seventeen years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, and followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; he did not turn from them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He continually handed them over to Hazael king of Aram, and to Ben-hadad, the son of Hazael.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoahaz appeased the LORD, and the LORD listened to him; for He saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD gave Israel a ①savior, so that they ②escaped from under the hand of the Arameans; and the sons of Israel lived in their tents as previously. ▷ ①Or deliverer ②Lit went out

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless they did not abandon the sins of the house of Jeroboam, into which he misled Israel; rather, they walked in ①them; and the ②Asherah also remained standing in Samaria. ▷ ①Lit it ②I.e., wooden symbol of a female deity

column.name: text
column.value: For he left to Jehoahaz no more of the ①army than fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand infantry, because the king of Aram had eliminated them and made them like the dust at threshing. ▷ ①Lit people

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did and his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehoahaz ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria; and his son Joash became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, ①Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned for sixteen years. ▷ ①In Heb Jehoash is another spelling of Joash

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD; he did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel; rather, he walked in ①them. ▷ ①Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Joash and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: So Joash ①lay down with his fathers, and Jeroboam sat on his throne; and Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: When Elisha ①became sick with the illness of which he was to die, Joash the king of Israel came down to him, and wept over ②him and said, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!” ▷ ①Lit was sick with his sickness ②Lit his face

column.name: text
column.value: And Elisha said to him, “Take a bow and arrows.” So he ①took a bow and arrows. ▷ ①Lit took to himself

column.name: text
column.value: Then Elisha said to the king of Israel, “Lay your hand on the bow.” And he laid his hand on it, then Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Open the window toward the east,” and he opened it. Then Elisha said, “Shoot!” So he shot. And he said, “The LORD’S arrow of victory, and the arrow of victory over Aram; for you will ①defeat the Arameans at Aphek until you have put an end to them.” ▷ ①Lit strike

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Take the arrows,” and he took them. And he said to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground,” and he struck it three times and ①stopped. ▷ ①Lit stood still

column.name: text
column.value: Then the man of God became angry at him and said, “You should have struck five or six times, then you would have struck Aram until you put an end to it. But now you shall strike Aram only three times.”

column.name: text
column.value: And Elisha died, and they buried him. Now the marauding bands of the Moabites would invade the land ①in the spring of the year. ▷ ①Lit at the coming of

column.name: text
column.value: And as they were burying a man, behold, they saw a marauding band; and they threw the man into the grave of Elisha. And when the man ①touched the bones of Elisha he revived and stood up on his feet. ▷ ①Lit went and touched

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hazael king of Aram had oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them and turned to them because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; and He was unwilling to eliminate them or cast them away from His presence until now.

column.name: text
column.value: When Hazael king of Aram died, his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz again took from the hand of Ben-hadad the son of Hazael the cities which he had taken in war from the hand of his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash ①defeated him and recovered the cities of Israel. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham, king of Judah, became king.

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem; and he did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD his God, as his father David had done.

column.name: text
column.value: But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and he even made his son pass through the fire, in accordance with the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had ①driven out before the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Or dispossessed

column.name: text
column.value: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rezin the king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem for war; and they besieged Ahaz, but ①were not capable of fighting him. ▷ ①Or did not prevail in fighting

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram, and drove the Judeans away from ①Elath; and the ②Arameans came to Elath and have lived there to this day. ▷ ①Heb Eloth ②As in some ancient versions; MT Edomites

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son; come up and save me from the ①hand of the king of Aram, and from the ②hand of the king of Israel, who are rising up against me.” ▷ ①Lit palm ②Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: And Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king’s house, and sent a gift to the king of Assyria.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Assyria listened to him; and the king of Assyria went up against Damascus and captured it, and led the people of it into exile to Kir, and put Rezin to death.

column.name: text
column.value: Now King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and he saw the altar which was at Damascus; and King Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the ①pattern of the altar and its model, according to all its workmanship. ▷ ①Lit likeness

column.name: text
column.value: So Urijah the priest built an altar; according to everything that King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, in that way Urijah the priest made it, ①before the coming of King Ahaz from Damascus. ▷ ①Lit until

column.name: text
column.value: And when the king came from Damascus, the king saw the altar; then the king approached the altar and ①went up to it, ▷ ①Or offered on it

column.name: text
column.value: and ①burned his burnt offering and his meal offering, and poured out his ②drink offering and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar. ▷ ①Lit offered up in smoke ②I.e., libation

column.name: text
column.value: And the bronze altar, which was before the LORD, ①he brought from the front of the house, from between his altar and the house of the LORD, and he put it on the north side of his altar. ▷ ①Lit he also

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, “Upon the great altar ①burn the morning burnt offering, the evening meal offering, the king’s burnt offering and his meal offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their meal offering, and their ②drink offerings; and sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offering and all the blood of the sacrifice. But the bronze altar shall be for me, for making inquiries.” ▷ ①Lit offer up in smoke ②I.e., libations

column.name: text
column.value: So Urijah the priest acted in accordance with everything that King Ahaz commanded.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Ahaz cut off the borders of the stands, and removed the wash basin from them; he also took down the ①Sea from the bronze oxen which were under it and put it on a pavement of stone. ▷ ①I.e., a very large basin

column.name: text
column.value: And the covered way for the Sabbath which they had built in the house, and the outer entry of the king, he removed from the house of the LORD because of the king of Assyria.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahaz ①lay down with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David; and his son Hezekiah reigned in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of the children of Ahab, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “And now, when this letter comes to you, since your master’s sons are with you, ①as well as the chariots and horses, and a fortified city and the weapons, ▷ ①Lit and with you the

column.name: text
column.value: select the best and most capable of your master’s sons and seat him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house.”

column.name: text
column.value: But they feared greatly and said, “Behold, the two kings did not stand firm before him; how then can we stand?”

column.name: text
column.value: And the one who was in charge of the household, and the one who was in charge of the city, and the elders, and the guardians of the children, sent word to Jehu, saying, “We are your servants, and everything that you tell us we will do. We will not appoint any man king; do what is good in your sight.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then he wrote them a letter a second time, saying, “If you are on my side, and will listen to my voice, take the heads of the men, your master’s sons, and come to me at Jezreel about this time tomorrow.” Now the king’s sons, seventy men, were with the great people of the city, who were raising them.

column.name: text
column.value: When the letter came to them, they took the king’s sons and slaughtered them, seventy men, and put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.

column.name: text
column.value: When the messenger came and informed him, saying, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons,” he said, “Put them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the morning he went out and stood and said to all the people, “You are ①innocent; behold, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who ②killed all these? ▷ ①Lit righteous ②Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Know then that nothing of the word of the LORD, which the LORD spoke concerning the house of Ahab, shall ①fall to the earth, for the LORD has done what He spoke ②through His servant Elijah.” ▷ ①I.e., fail to come true ②Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehu ①killed all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great men, his acquaintances, and his priests, until he left him without a survivor. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Then he set out and ①went to Samaria. On the way while he was at ②Beth-eked of the shepherds, ▷ ①Lit came in and went ②I.e., house of binding

column.name: text
column.value: Jehu ①encountered the relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, “Who are you?” And they ②answered, “We are the relatives of Ahaziah; and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother.” ▷ ①Lit found ②Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Take them alive.” So they took them alive, and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men; and he left none of them.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when he had gone from there, he ①encountered Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him; and he ②greeted him and said to him, “Is your heart right, just as my heart is with your heart?” And Jehonadab ③answered, “It is.” Jehu said, “If it is, give me your hand.” And he gave him his hand, and he pulled him up to him into the chariot. ▷ ①Lit found ②Lit blessed ③Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said, “Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD.” So ①he had him ride in his chariot. ▷ ①Lit they

column.name: text
column.value: When he came to Samaria, he ①killed all who remained to Ahab in Samaria, until he had eliminated ②them, in accordance with the word of the LORD which He spoke to Elijah. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, “Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

column.name: text
column.value: Now, summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers and all his priests; let no one go missing, because I have a great sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing shall not live.” But Jehu did it in deception, in order to eliminate the worshipers of Baal.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehu said, “Proclaim a holy assembly for Baal.” And they proclaimed it.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu sent word ①throughout Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came, so that there was not a person left who did not come. And when they entered the house of Baal, the house of Baal was filled from one end to the other. ▷ ①Lit in all

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to the one who was ①in charge of the wardrobe, “Bring out garments for all the worshipers of Baal.” So he brought out the garments for them. ▷ ①Lit over the

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehu entered the house of Baal with Jehonadab the son of Rechab; and he said to the worshipers of Baal, “Search carefully and see to it that there is here with you none of the servants of the LORD, but only the worshipers of Baal.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then they entered to ①offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed for himself eighty men outside, and he had said, “The one who allows any of the men whom I bring into your hands to escape ②shall give up his life in exchange.” ▷ ①Lit make ②Lit his soul for his soul

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about, as soon as he had finished ①offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the ②guard and to the royal officers, “Go in, ③kill them; let none come out.” So they ④killed them with the edge of the sword; and the ⑤guard and the royal officers threw them out, and went to the ⑥sanctuary of the house of Baal. ▷ ①Lit making ②Lit runners ③Lit strike ④Lit struck ⑤Lit runners ⑥Lit city

column.name: text
column.value: They brought out the memorial stones of the house of Baal and burned them.

column.name: text
column.value: They also tore down the memorial stone of Baal and tore down the house of Baal, and made it a latrine as it is to this day.

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehu eradicated Baal from Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: However, as for the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, into which he misled Israel, from these Jehu did not desist, including the golden calves that were at Bethel and at Dan.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD said to Jehu, “Because you have done well in performing what is right in My eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab in accordance with everything that was in My heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehu was not careful to walk in the Law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart; he did not desist from the sins of Jeroboam, into which he misled Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days the LORD began to cut off pieces from Israel; and Hazael ①defeated them throughout the territory of Israel: ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites; from Aroer, which is by the Valley of the Arnon, that is, Gilead and Bashan.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Jehu and everything that he did and all his might, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehu ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. And his son Jehoahaz became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: So the ①time which Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years. ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: In the seventh year of Jehu, ①Jehoash became king, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Zibiah of Beersheba. ▷ ①Jehoash is another spelling of Joash in Heb

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all his days that Jehoiada the priest instructed him.

column.name: text
column.value: Only the high places did not end; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoash said to the priests, “All the money of the sacred offerings which is brought into the house of the LORD, in current money, both the money of each man’s assessment and all the money ①which anyone’s heart prompts him to bring into the house of the LORD, ▷ ①Lit which it comes into...to bring

column.name: text
column.value: The priests are to take it for themselves, each from his ①acquaintance; and they shall repair ②damage to the house wherever ③any damage is found.” ▷ ①Or perhaps assessor ②Lit a breach, and so through v 12 ③Lit a breach, and so through v 12

column.name: text
column.value: But it came about that in the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had not repaired any damage to the house.

column.name: text
column.value: So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest, and the other priests, and said to them, “Why do you not repair damage to the house? Now then, you are not to take any more money from your ①acquaintances, but give it up for the damage to the house.” ▷ ①See note 1 v 5

column.name: text
column.value: The priests then agreed that they would not take any more money from the people, nor would they ①repair damage to the house. ▷ ①I.e., do or oversee repairs themselves

column.name: text
column.value: Instead, Jehoiada the priest ①took a chest and drilled a hole in its lid and put it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the house of the LORD; and the priests who guarded the threshold put in it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD. ▷ ①I.e., at the king’s command; see 2 Chr

column.name: text
column.value: When they saw that there was a great amount of money in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest went up and tied it up in bags, and counted the money that was found in the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And they handed the money which was assessed over to those who did the work, who had the oversight of the house of the LORD; and they ①paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of the LORD; ▷ ①Lit brought

column.name: text
column.value: and to the masons and the stonecutters, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and for everything that ①was laid out for the house to repair it. ▷ ①Lit went out

column.name: text
column.value: However there were not made for the house of the LORD silver cups, shears, bowls, trumpets, any receptacles of gold, or receptacles of silver from the money which was brought into the house of the LORD;

column.name: text
column.value: for they gave that to those who did the work, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, they did not require an accounting from the men into whose hands they gave the money to pay to those who did the work, because they acted faithfully.

column.name: text
column.value: The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD; it belonged to the priests.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hazael the king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it, and Hazael ①was intent on going up against Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit set his face to go

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoash king of Judah took all the sacred offerings that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had consecrated, and his own sacred offerings, and all the gold that was found among the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king’s house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then he withdrew from Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the rest of the acts of Joash and everything that he did, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: And his servants rose up and formed a conspiracy; and they struck and killed Joash at the house of Millo as he was going down to Silla.

column.name: text
column.value: For Jozacar the son of Shimeath and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, struck him and he died; and they buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Amaziah became king in his place.

column.name: text
column.value: When Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and eliminated all the royal ①children. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehosheba, the daughter of King Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah and abducted him from among the king’s sons who were being put to death, and put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.

column.name: text
column.value: So he was kept hidden with her in the house of the LORD for six years, while Athaliah was reigning over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the seventh year Jehoiada sent orders and brought the captains of hundreds of the Carites and of the ①guards, and brought them to himself at the house of the LORD. Then he made a covenant with them and put them under oath at the house of the LORD, and showed them the king’s son. ▷ ①Lit runners

column.name: text
column.value: And he commanded them, saying, “This is the thing that you shall do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath and keep watch over the king’s house

column.name: text
column.value: (a third also shall be at the gate Sur, and a third at the gate behind the ①guards), ②shall keep watch over the house ③for defense. ▷ ①Lit runners ②Lit and shall ③Or possibly in shifts

column.name: text
column.value: And two parts of you, all who go out on the Sabbath, shall also keep watch over the house of the LORD for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then you shall surround the king, each with his weapons in his hand; and whoever comes within the ranks shall be put to death. And you are to be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the captains of hundreds acted in accordance with everything that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And each one of them took his men who were to come in on the Sabbath, along with those who were to go out on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the priest gave the captains of hundreds the spears and shields that had been King David’s, which were in the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The ①guards stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king. ▷ ①Lit runners

column.name: text
column.value: Then he brought the king’s son out, and put the crown on him and gave him the testimony; and they made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, “Long live the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and of the people, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And she looked, and behold, the king was standing by the pillar according to the custom, with the captains and the ①trumpeters beside the king; and all the people of the land were joyful and were blowing trumpets. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!” ▷ ①Lit trumpets

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehoiada the priest commanded the captains of hundreds who were appointed over the army and said to them, “Bring her out between the ranks, and whoever follows her, put to death with the sword!” For the priest said, “She is not to be put to death at the house of the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: So they ①seized her, and when ②they brought her to the horses’ entrance of the king’s house, she was put to death there. ▷ ①Lit laid hands on her ②Lit she entered

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD, the king, and the people, that they would be the LORD’S people, and between the king and the people.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people of the land came to the house of Baal and tore it down; they thoroughly smashed his altars and his images in pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Then the priest appointed sentries over the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And he took the captains of hundreds and the Carites, and the ①guards and all the people of the land; and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD, and came by way of the gate of the ②guards to the king’s house. And he sat on the throne of the kings. ▷ ①Lit runners ②Lit runners

column.name: text
column.value: So all the people of the land rejoiced and the city was ①peaceful. For they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king’s house. ▷ ①Or quiet

column.name: text
column.value: ①Jehoash was seven years old when he became king. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and reigned for nine years.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, only not as the kings of Israel who preceded him.

column.name: text
column.value: Shalmaneser the king of Assyria marched against him, and Hoshea became his servant and paid him tribute.

column.name: text
column.value: But the king of Assyria uncovered a conspiracy by Hoshea, who had sent messengers to So, king of Egypt, and had then brought no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he had done year by year; so the king of Assyria arrested him and confined him in prison.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Assyria invaded the entire land, and went up to Samaria and besieged it for three years.

column.name: text
column.value: In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and led the people of Israel into exile to Assyria, and settled them in Halah and Habor, on the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

column.name: text
column.value: Now this came about because the sons of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up from the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt; and they had ①feared other gods. ▷ ①Or revered, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: They also ①followed the ②customs of the nations whom the LORD had driven out from the sons of Israel, and in the customs of the kings of Israel which they had ③introduced. ▷ ①Lit walked in ②Lit statutes ③Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel ①did things secretly against the LORD their God which were not right. Moreover, they built for themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city. ▷ ①Or ascribed words to

column.name: text
column.value: And they set up for themselves memorial stones and ①Asherim on every high hill and under every green tree, ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah)

column.name: text
column.value: and there they burned incense on all the high places as the nations did that the LORD had taken into exile before them; and they did evil things, provoking the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: They served idols, concerning which the LORD had said to them, “You shall not do this thing.”

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD warned Israel and Judah ①through all His prophets and every seer, saying, “Turn back from your evil ways and keep My commandments and My statutes in accordance with all the Law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you ②through My servants the prophets.” ▷ ①Lit by the hand of ②Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: However, they did not listen, but stiffened their neck ①like their fathers, who did not believe in the LORD their God. ▷ ①Lit like the neck of

column.name: text
column.value: They rejected His statutes and His covenant which He made with their fathers, and His warnings which He ①gave them. And they followed ②idols and became empty, and followed the nations that surrounded them, about which the LORD had commanded them not to do as they did. ▷ ①Lit warned ②Lit the non-existent

column.name: text
column.value: And they abandoned all the commandments of the LORD their God and made for themselves cast metal images: two calves. And they made an ①Asherah, and worshiped all the heavenly ②lights, and served Baal. ▷ ①I.e., a wooden symbol of a female deity ②Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: Then they made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire, and they practiced divination and interpreting omens, and gave themselves over to do evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD was very angry with Israel, and He removed them from His ①sight; no one was left except the tribe of Judah. ▷ ①Lit face

column.name: text
column.value: Judah did not keep the commandments of the LORD their God either, but they ①followed the ②customs ③which Israel had ④introduced. ▷ ①Lit walked in ②Lit statutes ③Lit of Israel which they ④Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD rejected all the ①descendants of Israel and afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until He had cast them ②out of His sight. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Lit from His face

column.name: text
column.value: When He had torn Israel from the house of David, they made Jeroboam the son of Nebat king. Then Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and misled them into a great sin.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel walked in all the sins of Jeroboam which he committed; they did not desist from them

column.name: text
column.value: until the LORD removed Israel from His sight, just as He had spoken through all His servants the prophets. So Israel went into exile from their own land to Assyria until this day.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, ①Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and settled them in the cities of Samaria in place of the sons of Israel. So they took possession of Samaria and lived in its cities. ▷ ①In 2 Kin 18:34; 19:13; Is 37:13, Ivvah

column.name: text
column.value: And at the beginning of their living there, they did not fear the LORD; therefore the LORD sent lions among them that were killing some of them.

column.name: text
column.value: So they spoke to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations whom you have taken into exile and settled in the cities of Samaria do not know the custom of the God of the land; so He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them because they do not know the custom of the God of the land.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Assyria issued commands, saying, “Take one of the priests there whom you led into ①exile, and have ②him go and live there; and have him teach them the custom of the God of the land.” ▷ ①Lit exile from there ②Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: So one of the priests whom they had led into exile from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and taught them how they were to fear the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But every nation was still making gods of its own, and they put them in the houses of the high places which the people of Samaria had made, every nation in their cities in which they lived.

column.name: text
column.value: The men of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the men of Cuth made Nergal, the men of Hamath made Ashima,

column.name: text
column.value: and the Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites were burning their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.

column.name: text
column.value: They also feared the LORD and ①appointed from their entire population priests of the high places, who acted for them in the houses of the high places. ▷ ①Lit made for themselves

column.name: text
column.value: They feared the LORD, yet they were serving their own gods in accordance with the custom of the nations from among whom they had been taken into exile.

column.name: text
column.value: To this day they act in accordance with the earlier customs: they do not fear the LORD, nor do they ①follow their statutes, their ordinances, the Law, or the commandments which the LORD commanded the sons of Jacob, whom He named Israel. ▷ ①Lit do according to

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD made a covenant with them and commanded them, saying, “You shall not fear other gods, nor bow down to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them.

column.name: text
column.value: But the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm, Him you shall fear, and to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.

column.name: text
column.value: And the statutes, the ordinances, the Law, and the commandment which He wrote for you, you shall take care to do always; and you shall not fear other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: The covenant that I have made with you, you shall not forget, nor shall you fear other gods.

column.name: text
column.value: But you shall fear the LORD your God; and He will save you from the hand of all your enemies.”

column.name: text
column.value: However, they did not listen, but they kept acting in accordance with their earlier custom.

column.name: text
column.value: So while these nations feared the LORD, they also served their ①idols; their children likewise and their grandchildren, just as their fathers did, they do to this day. ▷ ①Or carved images

column.name: text
column.value: Now when King Hezekiah heard the report, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and entered the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he sent Eliakim, who was in charge of the household, with Shebna the scribe and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz.

column.name: text
column.value: And they said to him, “This is what Hezekiah says: ‘This day is a day of distress, rebuke, and humiliation; for children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to deliver them.

column.name: text
column.value: Perhaps the LORD your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to taunt the living God, and will avenge the words which the LORD your God has heard. Therefore, offer a prayer for the remnant that is ①left.’ ” ▷ ①Lit found

column.name: text
column.value: So the servants of King Hezekiah came to Isaiah.

column.name: text
column.value: And Isaiah said to them, “This is what you shall say to your master: ‘The LORD says this: “Do not be fearful because of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed Me.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I am going to put a spirit in him so that he will hear news and return to his own land. And I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.” ’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rabshakeh returned and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.

column.name: text
column.value: When he heard them say about Tirhakah king of ①Cush, “Behold, he has come out to fight you,” he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying, ▷ ①Or Ethiopia

column.name: text
column.value: “This is what you shall say to Hezekiah king of ①Judah: ‘Do not let your God in whom you trust deceive you by saying, “Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.” ▷ ①Lit Judah, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, you yourself have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them completely. So will you be saved?

column.name: text
column.value: Did the gods of the nations which my fathers destroyed save them: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the sons of Eden who were in Telassar?

column.name: text
column.value: Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, the king of the city of Sepharvaim, and of Hena and Ivvah?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah took the ①letter from the hand of the messengers and read it, and he went up to the house of the LORD and ②spread it out before the LORD. ▷ ①Lit letters...read them ②Lit Hezekiah spread

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah prayed before the LORD and said, “LORD, God of Israel, ①enthroned above the cherubim, You are the God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. ▷ ①Lit sitting

column.name: text
column.value: Incline Your ear, LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, LORD, and see; and listen to the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to taunt the living God.

column.name: text
column.value: It is true, LORD; the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands,

column.name: text
column.value: and have ①hurled their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but only the work of human hands, wood and stone. So they have destroyed them. ▷ ①Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: But now, LORD our God, please, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, LORD, are God.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent word to Hezekiah, saying, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘Because you have prayed to Me about Sennacherib king of Assyria, I have heard you.’

column.name: text
text
column.value: Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? And against whom have you raised your voice, And ①haughtily raised your eyes? Against the Holy One of Israel! ▷ ①Lit on high

column.name: text
column.value: Through your messengers you have taunted the Lord, And you have said, “With my many chariots I went up to the heights of the mountains, To the remotest parts of Lebanon; And I cut down its tall cedars and its choicest junipers. And I entered its farthest resting place, its thickest forest.

column.name: text
column.value: I dug wells and drank foreign waters, And with the soles of my feet I dried up All the streams of Egypt.”

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Have you not heard? Long ago I did it; From ancient times I planned it. Now I have brought it about, That you would turn fortified cities into ruined heaps.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore their inhabitants were ①powerless, They were shattered and put to shame. They were like the vegetation of the field and the green grass, Like grass on the housetops that is scorched before it has grown. ▷ ①Lit short of hand

column.name: text
column.value: But I know your sitting down, Your going out, your coming in, And your raging against Me.

column.name: text
column.value: Because of your raging against Me, And because your complacency has come up to My ears, I will put My hook in your nose, And My bridle in your lips, And I will turn you back by the way by which you came.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Then this shall be the sign for you: ①you will eat this year what grows of itself, in the second year what grows by itself, and in the third year sow, harvest, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit. ▷ ①Lit to eat

column.name: text
column.value: The survivors that are left of the house of Judah will again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

column.name: text
column.value: For out of Jerusalem will go a remnant, and survivors out of Mount Zion. The zeal of ①the LORD will perform this. ▷ ①Some ancient mss the LORD of armies

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Therefore this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: “He will not come to this city nor shoot an arrow there; and he will not come before it with a shield nor heap up an assault ramp against it.

column.name: text
column.value: By the way that he came, by ①the same he will return, and he shall not come to this city,” ’ declares the LORD. ▷ ①Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: ‘For I will protect this city to save it for My own sake, and for My servant David’s sake.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then it happened that night that the angel of the LORD went out and struck 185,000 in the camp of the Assyrians; and when the rest got up early in the morning, behold, all of ①the 185,000 were ②dead. ▷ ①Lit them ②Lit dead bodies

column.name: text
column.value: So Sennacherib the king of Assyria departed and ①returned home, and lived at Nineveh. ▷ ①Lit went and returned

column.name: text
column.value: Then it came about, as he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, that ①Adrammelech and Sharezer killed him with the sword; and they escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon became king in his place. ▷ ①Some ancient mss his sons Adrammelech

column.name: text
column.value: In those days Hezekiah became ①mortally ill. And Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, came to him and said to him, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Set your house in order, for you are going to die and not live.’ ” ▷ ①Lit sick to death

column.name: text
column.value: Then he turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Please, LORD, just remember how I have walked before You wholeheartedly and in truth, and have done what is good in Your sight!” And Hezekiah wept ①profusely. ▷ ①Lit great weeping

column.name: text
column.value: And even before Isaiah had left the middle courtyard, the word of the LORD came to him, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Return and say to Hezekiah the leader of My people, ‘This is what the LORD, the God of your father David says: “I have heard your prayer, I have seen your tears; behold, I am going to heal you. On the third day you shall go up to the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will add fifteen years to your ①life, and I will save you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria; and I will protect this city for My own sake and for My servant David’s sake.” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaiah said, “Take a cake of figs.” And they took it and placed it on the inflamed spot, and he recovered.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “What will be the sign that the LORD will heal me, and that I will go up to the house of the LORD on the third day?”

column.name: text
column.value: Isaiah said, “This shall be the sign to you from the LORD, that the LORD will perform the word that He has spoken: shall the shadow go forward ten steps or go back ten steps?”

column.name: text
column.value: So Hezekiah said, “It is easy for the shadow to decline ten steps; no, but have the shadow turn backward ten steps.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaiah the prophet called out to the LORD, and He brought the shadow on the ①stairway back ten steps by which it had gone down on the ②stairway of Ahaz. ▷ ①Lit steps ②Lit steps

column.name: text
column.value: At that time ①Berodach-baladan, a son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, because he heard that Hezekiah had been sick. ▷ ①Some mss and ancient versions Merodach-baladan; cf. Is

column.name: text
column.value: And Hezekiah listened to ①them, and showed them all his treasure house, the silver, the gold, the balsam oil, the ②scented oil, the house of his armor, and everything that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house nor in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them. ▷ ①I.e., messengers ②Lit good

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said to him, “What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?” And Hezekiah said, “They have come from a far country, from Babylon.”

column.name: text
column.value: Isaiah said, “What have they seen in your house?” So Hezekiah ①answered, “They have seen everything that is in my house; there is nothing among my treasuries that I have not shown them.” ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, “Hear the word of the LORD:

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Behold, the days are coming when everything that is in your house, and what your fathers have stored up to this day, will be carried to Babylon; nothing will be left,’ says the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘And some of your sons who will come from you, whom you will father, will be taken away; and they will become officials in the palace of the king of Babylon.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah said to Isaiah, “The word of the LORD which you have spoken is good.” For he ①thought, “Is it not good, if there will be peace and ②security in my days?” ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit trustworthiness

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and all his might, and how he constructed the pool and the conduit and brought water into the city, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

column.name: text
column.value: So Hezekiah ①lay down with his fathers, and his son Manasseh became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in the third year of Hoshea, the son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.

column.name: text
column.value: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Abi the daughter of Zechariah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with everything that his father David had done.

column.name: text
column.value: He removed the high places and smashed the memorial stones to pieces, and cut down the ①Asherah. He also crushed to pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for until those days the sons of Israel had been burning incense to it; and it was called ②Nehushtan. ▷ ①I.e., a wooden symbol of a female deity ②I.e., a bronze sculpture

column.name: text
column.value: He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel; and after him there was no one like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among those who came before him.

column.name: text
column.value: For he clung to the LORD; he did not desist from following Him, but kept His commandments, which the LORD had commanded Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD was with him; wherever he went he was successful. And he revolted against the king of Assyria and did not serve him.

column.name: text
column.value: He ①defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria marched against Samaria and besieged it.

column.name: text
column.value: And at the end of three years they captured it; in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Assyria led Israel into exile to Assyria, and put them in Halah and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.

column.name: text
column.value: This happened because they did not obey the voice of the LORD their God, but violated His covenant, all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded; they would neither listen nor do it.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria marched against all the fortified cities of Judah and seized them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, “I have done wrong. ①Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me I will endure.” So the king of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah the payment of three hundred ②talents of silver and thirty talents of gold. ▷ ①Lit Turn back ②A talent was about 75 lb. or 34 kg

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah then gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasuries of the king’s house.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD, and from the doorposts, which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and he gave it to the king of Assyria.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Assyria sent Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to King Hezekiah with a large army to Jerusalem. So they went up and came to Jerusalem. And when they went up, they came and stood by the conduit of the upper pool, which is on the road of the ①fuller’s field. ▷ ①I.e., launderer’s

column.name: text
column.value: Then they called to the king, and Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the household, Shebnah the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the secretary, went out to them.

column.name: text
column.value: And Rabshakeh said to them, “Say now to Hezekiah, ‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria says: “What is this confidence that you ①have? ▷ ①Lit trust

column.name: text
column.value: You say—but they are only ①empty words—‘I have a plan and strength for the war.’ Now on whom have you relied, that you have revolted against me? ▷ ①Lit a word of lips

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, you have ①relied on the ②support of this broken reed, on Egypt; on which if a man leans, it will go into his ③hand and pierce it. That is how Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who rely on him. ▷ ①Lit relied for yourself ②Or staff ③Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: However, if you say to me, ‘We have trusted in the LORD our God,’ is it not He whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has removed, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem’?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, ①come make a wager with my master the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to put riders on them! ▷ ①Lit please exchange pledges

column.name: text
column.value: How then can you drive back even ①one ②official of the least of my master’s servants, and ③rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen? ▷ ①Lit the face of one ②Or governor ③Lit rely for yourself

column.name: text
column.value: Have I now come up without ①the LORD’S approval against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, ‘Go up against this land and destroy it.’ ” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah, said to Rabshakeh, “Speak now to your servants in Aramaic, because we ①understand it; and do not speak with us in ②Judean ③so that the people who are on the wall hear you.” ▷ ①Lit hear ②I.e., Hebrew ③Lit in the ears of...wall

column.name: text
column.value: But Rabshakeh said to them, “Has my master sent me only to your master and to you to speak these words? Has he not also sent me to the men who sit on the wall, doomed to eat their own dung and drink their own urine with you?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Rabshakeh stood up and shouted with a loud voice in Judean, ①saying, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria! ▷ ①Lit and spoke, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the king says: ‘Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to save you from ①my hand. ▷ ①MT his

column.name: text
column.value: And do not let Hezekiah lead you to trust in the LORD by saying, “The LORD will certainly save us, and this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”

column.name: text
column.value: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: “Make ①your peace with me and come out to me, and eat, each one, from his vine and each from his fig tree, and drink, each one, the waters of his own cistern, ▷ ①Lit with me a blessing

column.name: text
column.value: until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees producing oil, and of honey, so that you will live and not die.” But do not listen to Hezekiah, because he misleads you by saying, “The LORD will save us.”

column.name: text
column.value: Has any of the gods of the nations actually saved his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?

column.name: text
column.value: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and ①Ivvah? Have they saved Samaria from my hand? ▷ ①In 2 Kin 17:24, Avva

column.name: text
column.value: Who among all the gods of the lands are there who have saved their land from my hand, that the LORD would save Jerusalem from my hand?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But the people were silent and did not answer him with even a word, because it was the king’s ①command: “Do not answer him.” ▷ ①Lit command, saying

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was in charge of the household, and Shebna the scribe and Joah the son of Asaph, the secretary, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they reported to him the words of Rabshakeh.

column.name: text
column.value: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Hephzibah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with the abominations of the nations whom the LORD ①dispossessed before the sons of Israel. ▷ ①Or drove out

column.name: text
column.value: For he rebuilt the high places which his father Hezekiah had destroyed; and he erected altars for Baal and made an ①Asherah, just as Ahab king of Israel had done, and he worshiped all the heavenly ②lights and served them. ▷ ①I.e., a wooden symbol of a female deity ②Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: And he built altars in the house of the LORD, of which the LORD had said, “In Jerusalem I will put My name.”

column.name: text
column.value: He built altars for all the heavenly ①lights in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: And he made his son pass through the fire, interpreted signs, practiced divination, and used mediums and spiritists. He did great evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he put the carved image of Asherah that he had made in the house of which the LORD had said to David and to his son Solomon, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will not make the feet of Israel wander anymore from the land which I gave their fathers, if only they will take care to act in accordance with everything that I have commanded them, and with all the Law that My servant Moses commanded them.”

column.name: text
column.value: But they did not listen, and Manasseh encouraged them to do evil, more than the nations whom the LORD eliminated from the presence of the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the LORD spoke through His servants the prophets, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “Since Manasseh king of Judah has committed these abominations, having done more evil than all that the Amorites did who were before him, and has also misled Judah into sin with his idols,

column.name: text
column.value: therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘Behold, I am bringing such a disaster on Jerusalem and Judah that whoever hears about it, both of his ears will ring.

column.name: text
column.value: I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and the plummet of the house of Ahab, and I will wipe Jerusalem clean just as one wipes a bowl, wiping it and turning it upside down.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will abandon the remnant of My inheritance and hand them over to their enemies, and they will become as plunder and spoils to all their enemies,

column.name: text
column.value: because they have done evil in My sight, and have been provoking Me to anger since the day their fathers came from Egypt, even to this day.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, Manasseh shed very much innocent blood until he had filled Jerusalem ①from one end to another, besides his sin into which he misled Judah, in doing evil in the sight of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit mouth to mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh and all that he did, and his sin which he ①committed, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? ▷ ①Lit sinned

column.name: text
column.value: And Manasseh ①lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza, and his son Amon became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done.

column.name: text
column.value: For he walked ①entirely in the way that his father had walked, and served the idols that his father had served, and worshiped them. ▷ ①Lit in all the way that

column.name: text
column.value: So he abandoned the LORD, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the way of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the servants of Amon conspired against him and killed the king in his own house.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of the land ①killed all those who had conspired against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place. ▷ ①Lit struck
