column.value: Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, ‘I will ①entice him.’ And the LORD said to him, ‘How?’ ▷ ①Or persuade

column.name: text
column.value: He said, ‘I will go out and be a deceiving spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ Then He said, ‘You shall ①entice him, and you will also prevail. Go out and do so.’ ▷ ①Or persuade

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, behold, the LORD has put a deceiving spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours, for the LORD has declared disaster against you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah approached and struck Micaiah on the cheek; and he said, “ ①How did the Spirit of the LORD pass from me to speak to you?” ▷ ①Lit Which way

column.name: text
column.value: And Micaiah said, “Behold, you are going to see how on that day when you go from one inner room to ①another trying to hide yourself.” ▷ ①Lit inner room

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son;

column.name: text
column.value: and say, ‘This is what the king says: “Put this man in prison, and feed him enough bread and water to survive until I ①return safely.” ’ ” ▷ ①Lit come in peace

column.name: text
column.value: But Micaiah said, “If you actually return ①safely, the LORD has not spoken by me.” And he said, “ ②Listen, all you people!” ▷ ①Lit in peace ②Heb shema

column.name: text
column.value: So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up against Ramoth-gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you put on your robes.” So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king of Aram had commanded the commanders of his chariots, saying, “Do not fight with the small or great, but only with the king of Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So when the commanders of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “He is the king of Israel!” And they turned aside to fight against him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him, and God diverted them from him.

column.name: text
column.value: When the commanders of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now one man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel ①in a joint of the armor. So he said to the driver of his chariot, “Turn ②around and take me out of the battle, for I am severely wounded.” ▷ ①Lit between the scales and the scale armor ②Lit your hand

column.name: text
column.value: The battle raged on that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot in front of the Arameans until the evening; and at sunset he died.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returned in safety to his house in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehu the son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD, and ①by doing so bring wrath on yourself from the LORD? ▷ ①Lit by this

column.name: text
column.value: But ①there is some good in you, for you have removed the ②Asheroth from the land and you have set your heart to seek God.” ▷ ①Lit good things are found ②I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity

column.name: text
column.value: So Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem and went out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed judges in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to the judges, “Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for mankind but for the LORD who is with you ①when you render judgment. ▷ ①Lit in the word of judgment

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, let the fear of the LORD be upon you; be careful ①about what you do, for ②the LORD our God will have no part in injustice or partiality, or in the taking of a bribe.” ▷ ①Lit and do ②Lit it is not with the LORD our God

column.name: text
column.value: In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat also appointed some of the Levites and priests, and some of the heads of the fathers’ households of Israel, for the judgment of the LORD, and ①to judge disputes among the inhabitants of Jerusalem. ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT for the dispute. And they returned to Jerusalem; or And they lived in Jerusalem

column.name: text
column.value: Then he commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall do in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and wholeheartedly.

column.name: text
column.value: Whenever any dispute comes to you from your countrymen who live in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, you shall warn them so that they will not be guilty before the LORD, and wrath will not come on you and your countrymen. This you shall do and you will not be guilty.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, Amariah the chief priest will be over you in every matter ①that pertains to the LORD, and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in all that pertains to the king. Also the Levites shall be officers before you. ②Act resolutely, and may the LORD be with the upright.” ▷ ①Lit of ②Lit Be strong and do

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after this, that the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon, together with some of the ①Meunites, came to make war against Jehoshaphat. ▷ ①As in LXX; MT Ammonites

column.name: text
column.value: Then some came and reported to Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from ①Aram; and behold, they are in Hazazon-tamar (that is Engedi).” ▷ ①Another reading is Edom

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat was afraid and ①turned his attention to seek the LORD; and he proclaimed a period of fasting throughout Judah. ▷ ①Lit set his face

column.name: text
column.value: So Judah gathered together to seek help from the LORD; they even came from all the cities of Judah to seek the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD in front of the new courtyard;

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, “LORD, God of our fathers, are You not God in the heavens? And are You not ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in Your hand so that no one can stand against You.

column.name: text
column.value: Did You not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land from Your people Israel, and give it to the descendants of Your friend Abraham forever?

column.name: text
column.value: They have lived in it, and have built You a sanctuary in it for Your name, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: ‘If disaster comes upon us, the sword, or judgment, or plague, or famine, we will stand before this house and before You (for Your name is in this house), and cry out to You in our distress, and You will hear and save us.’

column.name: text
column.value: Now behold, the sons of Ammon, Moab, and ①Mount Seir, whom You did not allow Israel to invade when they came out of the land of Egypt (for they turned aside from them and did not destroy them), ▷ ①I.e., Edom

column.name: text
column.value: see how they are rewarding us by coming to drive us out from Your possession which You have given us as an inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: Our God, will You not judge them? For we are powerless before this great multitude that is coming against us; nor do we know what to do, but our eyes are on You.”

column.name: text
column.value: All Judah was standing before the LORD, with their infants, their wives, and their children.

column.name: text
column.value: Then in the midst of the assembly the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite of the sons of Asaph;

column.name: text
column.value: and he said, “Listen, all you of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat: This is what the LORD says to you: ‘Do not fear or be dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God’s.

column.name: text
column.value: Tomorrow, go down against them. Behold, they will come up by the ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley in front of the wilderness of Jeruel.

column.name: text
column.value: You need not fight in this battle; take your position, stand and watch the salvation of the LORD in your behalf, Judah and Jerusalem.’ Do not fear or be dismayed; tomorrow, go out to face them, for the LORD is with you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD, worshiping the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites, from the sons of the Kohathites and from the sons of the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

column.name: text
column.value: They rose early in the morning and went out to the wilderness of Tekoa; and when they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, “Listen to me, Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem: Put your trust in the LORD your God and you will endure. Put your trust in His prophets, and succeed.”

column.name: text
column.value: When he had consulted with the people, he appointed those who sang to the LORD and those who praised Him in holy attire, as they went out before the army and said, “Give thanks to the LORD, for His faithfulness is everlasting.”

column.name: text
column.value: When they began singing and praising, the LORD set ambushes against the sons of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah; so they were struck down.

column.name: text
column.value: For the sons of Ammon and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir, completely destroying them; and when they had finished with the inhabitants of Seir, they helped to destroy one another.

column.name: text
column.value: When Judah came to the watchtower of the wilderness, they turned toward the multitude, and behold, they were corpses lying on the ground, and there was no survivor.

column.name: text
column.value: When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their spoils, they found much among them, including goods, ①garments, and valuable things which they took for themselves, more than they could carry. And they were taking the spoils for three days because there was so much. ▷ ①As in several ancient mss; others corpses

column.name: text
column.value: Then on the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for they blessed the LORD there. Therefore they have named that place “The Valley of ①Beracah” until today. ▷ ①I.e., blessing

column.name: text
column.value: Every man of Judah and Jerusalem returned, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returning to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had helped them to rejoice over their enemies.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres, and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And the dread of God was on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God gave him rest on all sides.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for twenty-five years. And his mother’s name was Azubah the daughter of Shilhi.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not deviate from it, doing right in the sight of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The high places, however, were not removed; the people had not yet directed their hearts to the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first ①to last, behold, they are written in the annals of Jehu the son of Hanani, which is ②recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel. ▷ ①Lit and ②Lit taken up

column.name: text
column.value: After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel. He acted wickedly ①in so doing. ▷ ①Lit to do

column.name: text
column.value: So he allied himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish, and they made the ships in Ezion-geber.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed your works.” So the ships were wrecked and could not go to Tarshish.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoshaphat ①lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Jehoram became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, ①Azaryahu, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these were the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel. ▷ ①Or Azariah

column.name: text
column.value: Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold, and precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Jehoram had ①taken over the kingdom of his father and gathered courage, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the leaders of Israel as well. ▷ ①Lit risen

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for eight years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab’s daughter was his wife; and he did evil in the sight of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David because of the covenant which He had made with David, and because He had promised to give a lamp to him and his sons forever.

column.name: text
column.value: In his days Edom broke away ①from the rule of Judah, and appointed a king over themselves. ▷ ①Lit from under the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots with him. And he got up at night and struck and killed the Edomites who were surrounding him, and the commanders of the chariots.

column.name: text
column.value: So Edom revolted ①against Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolted at the same time ②against his rule because he had abandoned the LORD God of his fathers. ▷ ①Lit from under the hand of ②Lit from under his hand

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful, and led Judah astray.

column.name: text
column.value: Then a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “This is what the LORD, the God of your father David says: ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat and the ways of Asa king of Judah,

column.name: text
column.value: but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful as the house of Ahab was unfaithful, and you have also killed your brothers, ①your own family, who were better than you, ▷ ①Lit your father’s house

column.name: text
column.value: behold, the LORD is going to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and all your possessions with a great plague;

column.name: text
column.value: and you will suffer ①severe sickness, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the sickness, day by day.’ ” ▷ ①Lit in many sicknesses

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who ①bordered the Ethiopians; ▷ ①Lit were at the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: and they came against Judah and invaded it, and carried away all the possessions found in the king’s house together with his sons and his wives, so that no son was left to him except ①Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons. ▷ ①In 2 Chr 22:1, Ahaziah

column.name: text
column.value: So after all this the LORD struck him in his intestines with an incurable sickness.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about in the course of time, at the end of two years, that his bowels came out because of his sickness, and he died in great pain. And his people did not make a funeral fire for him like the fire for his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for eight years; and he departed ①with no one’s regret, and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the tombs of the kings. ▷ ①Lit without desire

column.name: text
column.value: Then the inhabitants of Jerusalem made ①Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the band of men who came with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah began to reign. ▷ ①In 2 Chr 21:17, Jehoahaz

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaziah was ①twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for one year in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Athaliah, the ②granddaughter of Omri. ▷ ①As in some ancient versions and 2 Kin 8:26; MT 42 years ②Lit daughter

column.name: text
column.value: He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor to act wickedly.

column.name: text
column.value: So he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his own destruction.

column.name: text
column.value: He also walked by their counsel, and went with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to wage war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead. But the Arameans ①wounded ②Joram. ▷ ①Lit struck ②I.e., Jehoram

column.name: text
column.value: So he returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds ①which they had inflicted on him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And ②Ahaziah, the son of Jehoram king of Judah, went down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was sick. ▷ ①Lit with which...struck ②As in 2 Kin 8:29; MT Azariah

column.name: text
column.value: Now the destruction of Ahaziah was from God, in that ①he went to Joram. For when he arrived, he went out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to eliminate the house of Ahab. ▷ ①Lit to go

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about, when Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, that he found the princes of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah’s brothers attending to Ahaziah, and killed them.

column.name: text
column.value: He also searched for Ahaziah, and they caught him while he was hiding in Samaria; they brought him to Jehu, put him to death, and buried him. For they said, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart.” So there was no one of the house of Ahaziah to retain the power of the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she rose and eliminated all the royal ①children of the house of Judah. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: But Jehoshabeath the king’s daughter took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons who were being put to death, and placed him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she was the sister of Ahaziah), hid him from Athaliah so that she would not put him to death.

column.name: text
column.value: He kept himself hidden with them in the house of God for six years while Athaliah reigned over the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the seventh year, Jehoiada gathered his courage, and took captains of hundreds: Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Johanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, and they entered into a covenant with him.

column.name: text
column.value: And they went throughout Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the fathers’ households of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. And ①Jehoiada said to them, “Behold, the king’s son shall reign, as the LORD has spoken concerning the sons of David. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: This is the thing which you shall do: a third of you, of the priests and Levites who come in on the Sabbath, shall be gatekeepers,

column.name: text
column.value: and a third shall be at the king’s house, and a third at the Gate of the Foundation; and all the people shall be in the courtyards of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: But no one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and the ministering Levites; they may enter, for they are holy. And all the people are to keep the command of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites will surround the king, each man with his weapons in his hand; and whoever enters the house is to be put to death. Therefore be with the king when he comes in and when he goes out.”

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites and all Judah did according to all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. And each one of them took his men who were to come in on the Sabbath, with those who were to go out on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest did not dismiss any of the divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoiada the priest gave the captains of hundreds the spears and the shields and quivers which had been King David’s, which were in the house of God.

column.name: text
column.value: He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the right ①side of the house to the left ②side of the house, by the altar and by the house, around the king. ▷ ①Lit shoulder ②Lit shoulder

column.name: text
column.value: Then they brought out the king’s son and put the crown on him, and gave him the testimony and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him and said, “Long live the king!”

column.name: text
column.value: When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she went into the house of the LORD to the people.

column.name: text
column.value: She looked, and behold, the king was standing by his pillar at the entrance, and the captains and the ①trumpeters were beside the king. And all the people of the land rejoiced and blew trumpets, the singers with their musical instruments ②leading the praise. Then Athaliah tore her clothes and said, “Conspiracy! Conspiracy!” ▷ ①Lit trumpets ②Lit and leading for praising

column.name: text
column.value: And Jehoiada the priest brought out the captains of hundreds who were appointed over the army, and said to them, “Bring her out ①between the ranks, and whoever follows her is to be put to death with the sword.” For the priest said, “You shall not put her to death in the house of the LORD.” ▷ ①Lit from within

column.name: text
column.value: So they ①seized her, and when she arrived at the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king’s house, they put her to death there. ▷ ①Lit put hands to her

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they would be the LORD’S people.

column.name: text
column.value: And all the people went to the house of Baal and tore it down, and they broke in pieces his altars and his images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Jehoiada placed the offices of the house of the LORD under the ①authority of the Levitical priests, whom David had assigned over the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD, as it is written in the Law of Moses—with rejoicing and singing according to the ②order of David. ▷ ①Lit hand ②Lit hands of

column.name: text
column.value: He stationed the gatekeepers of the house of the LORD, so that no one would enter who was in any way unclean.

column.name: text
column.value: He took the captains of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people, and all the people of the land, and brought the king down from the house of the LORD, and went through the upper gate to the king’s house. And they seated the king upon the royal throne.

column.name: text
column.value: So all of the people of the land rejoiced and the city was at rest. For they had put Athaliah to death with the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: Now all the people of Judah took ①Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah. ▷ ①In 2 Kin 14:21, Azariah

column.name: text
column.value: He built Eloth and restored it to Judah after the king ①lay down with his fathers. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned for fifty-two years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was ①Jechiliah of Jerusalem. ▷ ①In 2 Kin 15:2, Jecoliah

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with everything that his father Amaziah had done.

column.name: text
column.value: He continued to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding ①through the vision of God; and ②as long as he sought the LORD, God made him successful. ▷ ①Many mss in the fear of God ②Lit in the days of his seeking

column.name: text
column.value: Now he went out and fought against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he built cities in the area of Ashdod and among the Philistines.

column.name: text
column.value: God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.

column.name: text
column.value: The Ammonites gave tribute to Uzziah, and his ①fame extended to the border of Egypt, for he became very strong. ▷ ①Lit name went to the entering of Egypt

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, the Valley Gate, and at the corner buttress, and he fortified them.

column.name: text
column.value: He also built towers in the wilderness and carved out many cisterns, for he had much livestock, both in the ①lowland and in the plain. He also had plowmen and vinedressers in the hill country and the fertile fields, for he loved the soil. ▷ ①Heb shephelah

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Uzziah had an army ready for battle, which ①entered combat by divisions according to the number of their muster, ②recorded by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the official, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king’s officers. ▷ ①Lit was going out to ②Lit by the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: The total number of the heads of the ①households, of valiant warriors, was 2,600. ▷ ①Lit fathers

column.name: text
column.value: Under their direction was an army of 307,500, who could wage war with great power, to help the king against the enemy.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Uzziah prepared ①for all the army shields, spears, helmets, body armor, bows, and slingstones. ▷ ①Lit for them, for all

column.name: text
column.value: In Jerusalem he made machines of war invented by skillful workmen to be on the towers and the corners, for the purpose of shooting arrows and great stones. So his ①fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped until he was strong. ▷ ①Lit name

column.name: text
column.value: But when he became strong, his heart was so ①proud that he acted corruptly, and he was untrue to the LORD his God, for he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense. ▷ ①Lit high

column.name: text
column.value: Then Azariah the priest entered after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, valiant men.

column.name: text
column.value: They opposed Uzziah the king and said to him, “It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron who have been consecrated to burn incense. Leave the sanctuary, for you have been untrue and will have no honor from the LORD God.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Uzziah, with a censer in his hand for burning incense, was enraged; and while he was enraged with the priests, leprosy broke out on his forehead in the presence of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, and behold, he was leprous on his forehead; and they quickly removed him from there, and he himself also hurried to get out because the LORD had stricken him.

column.name: text
column.value: King Uzziah had leprosy to the day of his death; and he lived in a separate house, afflicted as he was with leprosy, for he was cut off from the house of the LORD. And his son Jotham was over the king’s house, judging the people of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, the first to the last, the prophet Isaiah, the son of Amoz, has written.

column.name: text
column.value: So Uzziah ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him with his fathers in the field of the grave which belonged to the kings, for they said, “He had leprosy.” And his son Jotham became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned for forty years in Jerusalem; and his mother’s name was Zibiah from Beersheba.

column.name: text
column.value: Joash did what was right in the sight of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about after this that Joash ①decided to restore the house of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit was with a heart

column.name: text
column.value: He gathered the priests and Levites and said to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah and collect money from all Israel to ①repair the house of your God annually, and you shall ②do the work quickly.” But the Levites did not act quickly. ▷ ①Lit strengthen ②Lit hasten to the thing

column.name: text
column.value: So the king summoned Jehoiada, the chief priest, and said to him, “Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and from Jerusalem the ①contribution of Moses, the servant of the LORD, and the congregation of Israel, for the tent of the testimony?” ▷ ①Or mandatory offering

column.name: text
column.value: For the sons of the wicked Athaliah had broken into the house of God, and even ①used the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals. ▷ ①Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: So the king commanded, and they made a chest and set it outside by the gate of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: And they made a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the ①contribution commanded by Moses the servant of God on Israel in the wilderness. ▷ ①Or mandatory offering

column.name: text
column.value: All the officers and all the people rejoiced, and they brought in their contribution and ①dropped it into the chest until they had finished. ▷ ①Lit threw

column.name: text
column.value: It happened that whenever the chest was brought to the king’s officer by the Levites, and they saw that the money was substantial, the king’s scribe and the chief priest’s officer would come and empty the chest, and pick it up and return it to its place. They did this daily and collected a large amount of money.

column.name: text
column.value: The king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD; and they hired masons and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So the workmen labored, and the repair work progressed in their hands, and they ①restored the house of God according to its ②specifications and strengthened it. ▷ ①Lit set up ②Lit measurement

column.name: text
column.value: When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada; and it was made into utensils for the house of the LORD, utensils for the service and the burnt offerings, and pans and utensils of gold and silver. And they offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually, all the days of Jehoiada.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Jehoiada ①reached a good old age and he died; he was 130 years old at his death. ▷ ①Lit became old and satisfied with days

column.name: text
column.value: And they buried him in the city of David with the kings, because he had done well in Israel and ①for God and His house. ▷ ①Lit with

column.name: text
column.value: But after the death of Jehoiada the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king, and the king listened to them.

column.name: text
column.value: And they abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the ①Asherim and the idols; so wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah)

column.name: text
column.value: Yet He sent prophets to them to bring them back to the LORD; and they testified against them, but they would not listen.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Spirit of God ①covered Zechariah, the son of Jehoiada the priest like clothing; and he stood above the people and said to them, “This is what God has said, ‘Why do you break the commandments of the LORD and do not prosper? Because you have abandoned the LORD, He has also abandoned you.’ ” ▷ ①Lit clothed

column.name: text
column.value: So they conspired against him, and at the command of the king they stoned him ①to death in the courtyard of the house of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit with stones

column.name: text
column.value: So Joash the king did not remember the kindness which Zechariah’s father Jehoiada had shown him, but he murdered his son. And as Zechariah died he said, “May the LORD see and ①avenge!” ▷ ①Lit seek; or require

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened at the turn of the year that the army of the Arameans came up against Joash; and they came to Judah and Jerusalem, destroyed all the officials of the people from among the people, and sent all their spoils to the king of Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, the army of the Arameans came with a small number of men; yet the LORD handed a very great army over to them, because ①Judah and Joash had abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers. So they executed judgment on Joash. ▷ ①Lit they

column.name: text
column.value: When they left him (for they left him very sick), his own servants conspired against him because of the blood of the ①son of Jehoiada the priest, and they murdered him on his bed. So he died, and they buried him in the city of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings. ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT sons

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the men who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.

column.name: text
column.value: As to his sons and the many pronouncements against him and the ①rebuilding of the house of God, behold, they are written in the ②treatise of the Book of the Kings. Then his son Amaziah became king in his place. ▷ ①Lit founding ②Heb midrash

column.name: text
column.value: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for sixteen years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jerushah the daughter of Zadok.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that his father Uzziah had done; however he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people continued acting corruptly.

column.name: text
column.value: He built the upper gate of the house of the LORD, and he built the wall of Ophel extensively.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, he built cities in the hill country of Judah, and he built fortresses and towers on the wooded hills.

column.name: text
column.value: He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them so that during that year the Ammonites gave him ①a hundred talents of silver, ②ten thousand kors of wheat, and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites also paid him this amount in the second year and in the third. ▷ ①About 3.75 tons or 3.4 metric tons ②About 77,000 cubic feet or 2,180 cubic meters

column.name: text
column.value: So Jotham became powerful because he directed his ways before the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and his ways, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years.

column.name: text
column.value: And Jotham ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David; and his son Ahaz became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. He did not do what was right in the sight of the LORD as his father David had done.

column.name: text
column.value: But he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; he also made cast metal images for the Baals.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, he burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, and burned his sons in fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD had driven out from the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram; and they ①defeated him and carried from him a great number of captives, and brought them to Damascus. And he was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him with heavy casualties. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: For Pekah the son of Remaliah killed 120,000 in Judah in one day, all valiant men, because they had abandoned the LORD God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: And Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king’s son, Azrikam the ruler of the house, and Elkanah the second to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel led away captive two hundred thousand of their relatives, women, sons, and daughters; and they also ①took a great deal of spoils from them, and brought the spoils to Samaria. ▷ ①Lit plundered

column.name: text
column.value: But a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded; and he went out to meet the army which came to Samaria and said to them, “Behold, because the LORD, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, He has handed them over to you, and you have killed them in a rage which has even reached heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you are proposing to subjugate the people of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for yourselves. Are you not, however guilty yourselves of offenses against the LORD your God?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, listen to me and return the captives whom you captured from your brothers, for the burning anger of the LORD is against you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then some of the leading men of the sons of Ephraim—Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai—rose up against those who were coming from the battle,

column.name: text
column.value: and said to them, “You must not bring the captives in here, for you are proposing to bring guilt upon us before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt; for our guilt is great, and His burning anger is against Israel.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the armed men left the captives and the spoils before the officers and all the assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the men who were designated by name got up, took the captives, and they clothed all their naked people from the spoils; they gave them clothes and sandals, fed them and gave them drink, anointed them with oil, led all their feeble ones on donkeys, and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers; then they returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: At that time King Ahaz sent word to the ①kings of Assyria for help. ▷ ①Ancient versions king

column.name: text
column.value: For the Edomites had come again and attacked Judah, and led away captives.

column.name: text
column.value: The Philistines had also invaded the cities of the ①lowland and of the Negev of Judah, and had taken Beth-shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, and Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and Gimzo with its villages; and they had settled there. ▷ ①Heb shephelah

column.name: text
column.value: For the LORD had humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had brought about a lack of restraint in Judah and was very unfaithful to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and afflicted him instead of strengthening him.

column.name: text
column.value: Although Ahaz took a portion out of the house of the LORD and out of the palace of the king and of the princes, and gave it to the king of Assyria, it did not help him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now during the time of his distress, this same King Ahaz became even more unfaithful to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: For he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who had ①defeated him, and said, “Because the gods of the kings of Aram helped them, I will sacrifice to them so that they may help me.” But they became the ②downfall of him and all Israel. ▷ ①Lit struck ②Lit stumbling

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, when Ahaz gathered together the utensils of the house of God, he cut the utensils of the house of God in pieces; and he closed the doors of the house of the LORD, and made altars for himself in every corner of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and provoked the LORD, the God of his fathers, to anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of his acts and all his ways, from the first to the last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So Ahaz ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, for they did not bring him to the tombs of the kings of Israel; and his son Hezekiah reigned in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Jehoaddan of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, only not wholeheartedly.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about, as soon as the kingdom was ①firmly in his grasp, that he killed his servants who had killed his father the king. ▷ ①Lit firm upon him

column.name: text
column.value: However, he did not put their children to death, but did as it is written in the Law in the Book of Moses, which the LORD commanded, saying, “Fathers shall not be put to death for sons, nor sons be put to death for fathers; but each shall be put to death for his own sin.”

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Amaziah assembled Judah and appointed them according to their fathers’ households under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds throughout Judah and Benjamin; and he ①took a census of those from twenty years old and upward and found them to be three hundred thousand choice men, able to go to war and handle spear and shield. ▷ ①Lit mustered

column.name: text
column.value: He also hired a hundred thousand valiant warriors from Israel for ①a hundred talents of silver. ▷ ①About 3.75 tons or 3.4 metric tons

column.name: text
column.value: But a man of God came to him saying, “O king, do not let the army of Israel come with you, for the LORD is not with Israel nor with any of the sons of Ephraim.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you do go, do it, be strong for the battle; yet God will ①bring you down before the enemy, for God has the power to help and to ②bring down.” ▷ ①Lit cause you to stumble ②Lit cause to stumble

column.name: text
column.value: Amaziah said to the man of God, “But what are we to do about the ①hundred talents which I have given to the troops of Israel?” And the man of God answered, “The LORD has much more to give you than this.” ▷ ①About 3.75 tons or 3.4 metric tons

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amaziah ①dismissed the troops which came to him from Ephraim, to go home; so their anger burned against Judah, and they returned ②home in fierce anger. ▷ ①Lit separated ②Lit to their own place

column.name: text
column.value: Now Amaziah gathered his courage and led his people out, and went to the Valley of Salt, and struck and killed ten thousand of the sons of Seir.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Judah also captured ten thousand alive and brought them to the top of the cliff, and threw them down from the top of the cliff so that they were all dashed to pieces.

column.name: text
column.value: But the ①troops whom Amaziah sent back, those not going with him to battle, raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon, and struck and killed three thousand of them, and plundered a large amount of spoils. ▷ ①Lit sons of the troops

column.name: text
column.value: Now after Amaziah came from slaughtering the Edomites, he brought the gods of the sons of Seir and set them up as his gods. Then he bowed down before them and burned incense to them.

column.name: text
column.value: So the anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and He sent him a prophet who said to him, “Why have you sought the gods of the people who have not saved their own people from your hand?”

column.name: text
column.value: As he was talking with him, ①the king said to him, “Have we appointed you to be a royal counselor? Stop! Why should ②you be put to death?” Then the prophet stopped and said, “I know that God has planned to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel.” ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit they strike and kill you

column.name: text
column.value: Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent word to Joash the son of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, the king of Israel, saying, “Come, let’s face each other.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Joash the king of Israel sent a reply to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thorn bush that was in Lebanon sent word to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son in marriage.’ But a wild beast that was in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thorn bush.

column.name: text
column.value: You said, ‘Behold, you have ①defeated Edom.’ And your heart has lifted you up in boasting. Now stay home; why should you provoke trouble so that you, would fall, you and Judah with you?” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: But Amaziah would not listen, for it was from God, so that He might hand them over to Joash, because they had sought the gods of Edom.

column.name: text
column.value: So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belonged to Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: And Judah was defeated ①by Israel, and they fled, every man to his tent. ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: Then Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh, and brought him to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, ①four hundred cubits. ▷ ①About 600 ft. or 183 m

column.name: text
column.value: He took all the gold and silver and all the utensils which were found in the house of God with Obed-edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages too, and returned to Samaria.

column.name: text
column.value: And Amaziah, the son of Joash king of Judah, lived fifteen years after the death of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, from the first to the last, behold, are they not written in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel?

column.name: text
column.value: From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD they conspired against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish; but they sent men after him to Lachish, and they killed him there.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they brought him on horses and buried him with his fathers in the city of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: After these ①acts of faithfulness Sennacherib king of Assyria came and invaded Judah and besieged the fortified cities, and ②intended to break into them for himself. ▷ ①Lit things and this faithfulness ②Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Hezekiah saw that Sennacherib had come and that ①he intended to wage war against Jerusalem, ▷ ①Lit he set his face for war

column.name: text
column.value: he decided with his officers and his warriors to cut off the supply of water from the springs which were outside the city, and they helped him.

column.name: text
column.value: So many people assembled and stopped up all the springs and the stream which flowed ①through the region, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come and find abundant water?” ▷ ①Lit in the midst of

column.name: text
column.value: And he resolutely set to work and rebuilt all of the wall that had been broken down and ①erected towers on it, and built another outside wall and strengthened the ②Millo in the city of David, and made weapons and shields in great numbers. ▷ ①Lit raised on the towers ②I.e., terraced structure

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed military officers over the people and gathered them to him in the public square at the city gate, and spoke ①encouragingly to them, saying, ▷ ①Lit upon their hearts

column.name: text
column.value: “Be strong and courageous, do not fear or be dismayed because of the king of Assyria nor because of all the horde that is with him; for the One with us is greater than the one with him.

column.name: text
column.value: With him is only an arm of flesh, but with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles.” And the people relied on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: After this Sennacherib king of Assyria sent his servants to Jerusalem while he was ①besieging Lachish with all his forces with him, against Hezekiah king of Judah and against all of Judah who were in Jerusalem, saying, ▷ ①Lit against

column.name: text
column.value: “This is what Sennacherib king of Assyria says: ‘On what are you trusting that you are staying in Jerusalem under siege?

column.name: text
column.value: Is Hezekiah not misleading you to give yourselves over to die by hunger and by thirst, saying, “The LORD our God will save us from the ①hand of the king of Assyria”? ▷ ①Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: Is it not the same Hezekiah who removed His high places and His altars, and said to Judah and ①Jerusalem, “You shall worship before one altar, and on it you shall ②burn incense”? ▷ ①Lit Jerusalem, saying, ②Lit offer up in smoke

column.name: text
column.value: Do you not know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of those lands at all able to save their land from my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Who was there among all the gods of those nations which my fathers utterly destroyed who could save his people from my hand, that your God would be able to save you from my hand?

column.name: text
column.value: Now then, do not let Hezekiah deceive you or mislead you like this, and do not believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to save his people from my hand or from the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God save you from my hand?’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: His servants spoke further against the LORD God and against His servant Hezekiah.

column.name: text
column.value: He also wrote letters to insult the LORD God of Israel, and to speak against Him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands ①have not saved their people from my hand, so the God of Hezekiah will not save His people from my hand.” ▷ ①Lit who have

column.name: text
column.value: They called this out with a loud voice in the language of Judah to the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall, to frighten and terrify them, so that they might take the city.

column.name: text
column.value: They spoke ①of the God of Jerusalem as they did against the gods of the peoples of the earth, the work of human hands. ▷ ①Lit to

column.name: text
column.value: But King Hezekiah and Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, prayed about this and called out to heaven for help.

column.name: text
column.value: And the LORD sent an angel who destroyed every warrior, commander, and officer in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returned ①in shame to his own land. And when he had entered the temple of his god, some of his own sons killed him there with the sword. ▷ ①Lit in shame of face

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD saved Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and ①guided them on every side. ▷ ①Another reading is gave them rest

column.name: text
column.value: And many were bringing gifts to the LORD at Jerusalem and valuable presents to Hezekiah king of Judah; so thereafter he rose in the sight of all nations.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days Hezekiah became ①mortally ill; and he prayed to the LORD, and ②the LORD spoke to him and gave him a sign. ▷ ①Lit sick to the point of death ②Lit He

column.name: text
column.value: But Hezekiah did nothing in return for the benefit ①he received, because his heart was ②proud; therefore wrath came upon him and upon Judah and Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit to Him ②Lit high

column.name: text
column.value: However, Hezekiah ①humbled the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the wrath of the LORD did not come on them in the days of Hezekiah. ▷ ①Lit humbled himself in

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hezekiah had immense riches and honor; and he made for himself treasuries for silver, gold, precious stones, spices, shields, and all kinds of valuable articles,

column.name: text
column.value: also storehouses for the produce of grain, wine, and oil; stalls for all kinds of cattle, and ①sheepfolds for the flocks. ▷ ①As in ancient versions; MT herds for the stables

column.name: text
column.value: He made cities for himself and acquired flocks and herds in abundance, because God had given him very great ①wealth. ▷ ①Lit possessions; or property

column.name: text
column.value: It was Hezekiah who stopped the upper outlet of the waters of Gihon and directed them to the west side of the city of David. And Hezekiah was successful in everything that he did.

column.name: text
column.value: Even in the matter of the messengers of the rulers of Babylon, who were sent to him to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land; God left him alone only to test him, so that He might know everything that was in his heart.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah and his deeds of devotion, behold, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So Hezekiah ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the ②upper section of the tombs of the sons of David; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honored him at his death. And his son Manasseh became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died ②Or ascent to

column.name: text
column.value: Now when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah, broke the memorial stones in pieces, cut down the ①Asherim and pulled down the high places and the altars throughout Judah and Benjamin, as well as in Ephraim and Manasseh, until ②they had destroyed them all. Then all the sons of Israel returned to their cities, each to his possession. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah) ②Lit to completion

column.name: text
column.value: And Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites by their divisions, each according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to serve and to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camp of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He also appointed the king’s portion of his property for the burnt offerings, namely, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths and for the new moons and for the appointed festivals, as it is written in the Law of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Also he told the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion due to the priests and the Levites, so that they might devote themselves to the Law of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: As soon as the ①order spread, the sons of Israel abundantly provided the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the produce of the field; and they brought in abundantly the tithe of everything. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought in the tithe of oxen and sheep, and the tithe of ①sacred gifts which were consecrated to the LORD their God, and placed them in heaps. ▷ ①Lit consecrated things

column.name: text
column.value: In the third month they began to ①make the heaps, and they finished them by the seventh month. ▷ ①Lit lay

column.name: text
column.value: When Hezekiah and the rulers came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and His people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah questioned the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps.

column.name: text
column.value: Azariah, the chief priest of the house of Zadok, said to ①him, “Since the contributions started coming into the house of the LORD, we have had enough to eat with plenty left over, for the LORD has blessed His people, and this great quantity is left over.” ▷ ①Lit him, and he said

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare rooms in the house of the LORD, and they prepared them.

column.name: text
column.value: They faithfully brought in the contributions, the tithes, and the consecrated things; and Conaniah the Levite was the officer in charge of them, and his brother Shimei was second.

column.name: text
column.value: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers ①under the authority of Conaniah and his brother Shimei by the appointment of King Hezekiah, and Azariah was the chief officer of the house of God. ▷ ①Lit from the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the keeper of the eastern gate, was in charge of the ①voluntary offerings for God, to distribute the contributions for the LORD and the most holy things. ▷ ①Or freewill offerings

column.name: text
column.value: ①Under his authority were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, to distribute their portions faithfully to their brothers by divisions, whether great or small, ▷ ①Lit On his hand

column.name: text
column.value: without regard to their genealogical enrollment, to the males from ①thirty years old and upward—everyone who entered the house of the LORD for his daily obligations—for their work in their duties according to their divisions; ▷ ①Heb three

column.name: text
column.value: as well as the priests who were enrolled genealogically according to their fathers’ households, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, by their duties and their divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: The genealogical enrollment included ①all their little children, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, for the whole assembly, for they consecrated themselves ②faithfully in holiness. ▷ ①Lit with all ②Lit in their faithfulness

column.name: text
column.value: Also for the sons of Aaron, the priests, who were in the pasture lands of their cities, or in each and every city, there were men who were designated by name to distribute portions to every male among the priests and to everyone genealogically enrolled among the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah did this throughout Judah; and he did what was good, right, and true before the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: Every work which he began in the service of the house of God in the Law and in the commandment, seeking his God, he did with all his heart and prospered.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah and also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to ①celebrate the Passover to the LORD God of Israel. ▷ ①Lit do, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: For the king and his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem had decided to celebrate the Passover in the second month,

column.name: text
column.value: since they could not celebrate it at that time, because the priests had not consecrated themselves in sufficient numbers, nor had the people been gathered to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: So the ①decision was right in the sight of the king and all the assembly. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: So they established a decree to circulate a ①proclamation throughout Israel from Beersheba to Dan, that they are to come to celebrate the Passover to the LORD God of Israel in Jerusalem. For they had not celebrated it in great numbers as was written. ▷ ①Lit voice

column.name: text
column.value: The ①couriers went throughout Israel and Judah with the letters from the hand of the king and his princes, even according to the command of the king, saying, “Sons of Israel, return to the LORD God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that He may return to those of you who escaped and are left from the ②hand of the kings of Assyria. ▷ ①Lit runners ②Lit palm

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be like your fathers and your brothers, who were untrue to the LORD God of their fathers, so that He made them an object of horror, just as you see.

column.name: text
column.value: Now do not stiffen your neck like your fathers, but ①yield to the LORD and enter His sanctuary which He has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, that His burning anger may turn away from you. ▷ ①Lit give a hand

column.name: text
column.value: For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your sons will find compassion in the presence of those who led them captive, and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and will not turn His face away from you if you return to Him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the ①couriers passed from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, and as far as Zebulun, but they laughed at them with scorn and mocked them. ▷ ①Lit runners

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless, some men of Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The hand of God was also on Judah to give them one heart to do what the king and the princes commanded by the word of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Now many people were gathered at Jerusalem to celebrate the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very large assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: They got up and removed the altars which were in Jerusalem; they also removed all the incense altars and threw them into the brook Kidron.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they slaughtered the Passover lambs on the fourteenth of the second month. And the priests and Levites were ashamed of themselves, and consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: They stood at their stations following their custom, according to the Law of Moses the man of God; the priests sprinkled the blood which they received from the hand of the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: For there were many in the assembly who had not consecrated themselves; therefore, the Levites were in charge of the slaughter of the Passover lambs for everyone who was unclean, in order to consecrate them to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: For a multitude of the people, many from Ephraim and Manasseh, and Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover contrary to what was written. For Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, “May the good LORD pardon

column.name: text
column.value: everyone who prepares his heart to seek God, the LORD God of his fathers, though not according to the purification rules of the sanctuary.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Israel present in Jerusalem celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy, and the Levites and the priests were praising the LORD day after day with loud instruments to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah spoke ①encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good insight in the things of the LORD. So they ate for the appointed seven days, sacrificing peace offerings and giving thanks to the LORD God of their fathers. ▷ ①Lit to the heart of

column.name: text
column.value: Then the whole assembly decided to celebrate the feast another seven days, so they celebrated the seven days with joy.

column.name: text
column.value: For Hezekiah king of Judah had contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep, and the princes had contributed to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep; and a large number of priests consecrated themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: All the assembly of Judah rejoiced, with the priests and the Levites and all the assembly that came from Israel, both the strangers who came from the land of Israel and those living in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: So there was great joy in Jerusalem, because there was nothing like this in Jerusalem since the days of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Levitical priests stood and blessed the people; and their voice was heard and their prayer came to His holy dwelling place, to heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old; and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. And his mother’s name was Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, in accordance with everything that his father David had done.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them into the public square on the east.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to them, “Listen to me, you Levites. Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and carry the uncleanness out of the holy place.

column.name: text
column.value: For our fathers have been unfaithful and have done evil in the sight of the LORD our God, and they have abandoned Him and turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD, and have ①turned their backs. ▷ ①Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: They have also shut the doors of the porch and extinguished the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the wrath of the LORD was against Judah and Jerusalem, and He has made them an object of terror, of horror, and of hissing, as you see with your own eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: For behold, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters, and our wives are in captivity because of this.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD God of Israel, so that His burning anger may turn away from us.

column.name: text
column.value: My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before Him, to serve Him, and to be His ministers and burn incense.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Levites arose: Mahath the son of Amasai and Joel the son of Azariah, from the sons of the Kohathites; and from the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and from the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah and Eden the son of Joah;

column.name: text
column.value: and from the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and ①Jeiel; and from the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah; ▷ ①Or Jeuel

column.name: text
column.value: and from the sons of Heman, ①Jehiel and Shimei; and from the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel. ▷ ①Another reading is Jehuel

column.name: text
column.value: They assembled their brothers, consecrated themselves, and went in to cleanse the house of the LORD, according to the commandment of the king by the words of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So the priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to cleanse it, and they brought every unclean thing which they found in the temple of the LORD out to the courtyard of the house of the LORD. Then the Levites received it to carry out to the Kidron ①Valley. ▷ ①Or wadi

column.name: text
column.value: Now they began ①the consecration on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they entered the porch of the LORD. Then they consecrated the house of the LORD in eight days, and finished on the sixteenth day of the first month. ▷ ①Lit to consecrate

column.name: text
column.value: Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, “We have cleansed the whole house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table of the showbread with all of its utensils.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, all the utensils which King Ahaz had discarded during his reign in his unfaithfulness, we have prepared and consecrated; and behold, they are before the altar of the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Hezekiah got up early and assembled the princes of the city, and went up to the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, the sanctuary, and Judah. And he ordered the priests, the sons of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests took the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. They also slaughtered the rams and sprinkled the blood on the altar; they slaughtered the lambs as well, and sprinkled the blood on the altar.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they brought the male goats of the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests slaughtered them and purified the altar with their blood to atone for all Israel, because the king ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: He then stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps, and lyres, according to the command of David and of Gad, the king’s seer, and of Nathan the prophet; for the command was from the LORD through His prophets.

column.name: text
column.value: The Levites stood with the musical instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song to the LORD also began with the trumpets, ①accompanied by the instruments of David, king of Israel. ▷ ①Lit and on the hands of

column.name: text
column.value: While the whole assembly worshiped, the singers also sang and the trumpets sounded; all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.

column.name: text
column.value: Now at the completion of the burnt offerings, the king and all who were present with him bowed down and worshiped.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, King Hezekiah and the officials ordered the Levites to sing praises to the LORD with the words of David and Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with joy, and bowed down and worshiped.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah said, “Now that you have ①consecrated yourselves to the LORD, come forward and bring sacrifices and thanksgiving offerings to the house of the LORD.” So the assembly brought sacrifices and thanksgiving offerings, and everyone who was ②willing brought burnt offerings. ▷ ①Lit filled your hands ②Lit willing of heart

column.name: text
column.value: The number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams, and two hundred lambs; all of these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: The consecrated offerings were six hundred bulls and three thousand sheep.

column.name: text
column.value: But the priests were too few, so that they were unable to skin all the burnt offerings; therefore their brothers the Levites helped them until the work was finished and the other priests had consecrated themselves. For the Levites were more ①conscientious to consecrate themselves than the priests. ▷ ①Lit upright of heart

column.name: text
column.value: There were also ①many burnt offerings with the fat of the peace offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of the LORD was established again. ▷ ①Lit the burnt offerings to an abundance

column.name: text
column.value: Then Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, because the thing came about suddenly.

column.name: text
column.value: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned for fifty-five years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD according to the abominations of the nations whom the LORD dispossessed before the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: For he rebuilt the high places which his father Hezekiah had torn down; he also set up altars for the Baals and made ①Asherim, and he worshiped all the heavenly ②lights and served them. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah) ②Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: He built altars in the house of the LORD of which the LORD had said, “My name shall be in Jerusalem forever.”

column.name: text
column.value: He built altars for all the heavenly ①lights in the two courtyards of the house of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit host

column.name: text
column.value: He also made his sons pass through the fire in the Valley of Ben-hinnom; and he practiced witchcraft, used divination, practiced sorcery, and dealt with mediums and spiritists. He did much evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he put the carved image of the idol which he had made in the house of God, of which God had said to David and his son Solomon, “In this house and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen from all the tribes of Israel, I will put My name forever;

column.name: text
column.value: and I will not remove the foot of Israel again from the land which I have appointed for your fathers, if only they will take care to do everything that I have commanded them according to all the Law, the statutes, and the ordinances given through Moses.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Manasseh encouraged Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to do more evil than the nations whom the LORD destroyed before the sons of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD spoke to Manasseh and his people, but they paid no attention.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the LORD brought the commanders of the army of the king of Assyria against them, and they captured Manasseh with hooks, bound him with bronze chains, and led him to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: When he was in distress, he appeased the LORD his God and humbled himself greatly before the God of his fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: When he prayed to Him, He was moved by him and heard his pleading, and brought him back to Jerusalem to his kingdom. Then Manasseh knew that the LORD alone is God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now after this he built the outer wall of the city of David on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, up to the entrance of the Fish Gate; and he encircled the Ophel with it and made it very high. Then he put army commanders in all the fortified cities in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: He also removed the foreign gods and the idol from the house of the LORD, as well as all the altars which he had built on the mountain of the house of the LORD and in Jerusalem, and he threw them outside the city.

column.name: text
column.value: He set up the altar of the LORD and sacrificed peace offerings and thanksgiving offerings on it; and he ordered Judah to serve the LORD God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: However, the people still sacrificed on the high places, although only to the LORD their God.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who spoke to him in the name of the LORD God of Israel, behold, they are among the records of the kings of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: His prayer also and how God was moved by him, and all his sin, his unfaithfulness, and the sites on which he built high places and erected the ①Asherim and the carved images, before he humbled himself, behold, they are written in the records of ②Hozai. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah) ②LXX seers

column.name: text
column.value: So Manasseh ①lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in his own house. And his son Amon became king in his place. ▷ ①I.e., died

column.name: text
column.value: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned for two years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as his father Manasseh had done, and Amon sacrificed to all the carved images which his father Manasseh had made, and he served them.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, he did not humble himself before the LORD as his father Manasseh had ①done, but Amon multiplied his guilt. ▷ ①Lit humbled himself

column.name: text
column.value: Finally, his servants conspired against him and put him to death in his own house.

column.name: text
