column.value: But the people of the land ①killed all the conspirators against King Amon, and the people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place. ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, and walked in the ways of his father David and did not turn aside to the right or the left.

column.name: text
column.value: For in the eighth year of his reign while he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, the ①Asherim, the carved images, and the cast metal images. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah)

column.name: text
column.value: They tore down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and he chopped down the incense altars that were high above them; also he broke in pieces the Asherim, the carved images, and the cast metal images, and ground them to powder, and scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he burned the bones of the priests on their altars and purged Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, and as far as Naphtali, in their surrounding spaces,

column.name: text
column.value: he also tore down the altars and crushed the ①Asherim and the carved images into powder, and chopped down all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem. ▷ ①I.e., wooden symbols of a female deity (Asherah)

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah an official of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the secretary, to repair the house of the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the money that was brought into the house of God, which the Levites, the ①doorkeepers, had collected ②from Manasseh and Ephraim, and from all the remnant of Israel, from all Judah and Benjamin and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit guardians of the threshold ②Lit from the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: Then they handed it over to the workmen who had the oversight of the house of the LORD, and the workmen who were working in the house of the LORD ①used it to restore and repair the house. ▷ ①Lit gave

column.name: text
column.value: They in turn gave it to the carpenters and the builders to buy quarried stone and timber for couplings, and to make beams for the houses which the kings of Judah had let go to ruin.

column.name: text
column.value: The men did the work faithfully with foremen over them to supervise: Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites of the sons of Merari, Zechariah and Meshullam of the sons of the Kohathites, and the Levites, all who were skillful with musical instruments.

column.name: text
column.value: They were also in charge of the burden bearers, and supervised all the workmen from job to job; and some of the Levites were scribes, and officials, and gatekeepers.

column.name: text
column.value: When they were bringing out the money which had been brought into the house of the LORD, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law of the LORD given by Moses.

column.name: text
column.value: Hilkiah responded and said to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the Book of the Law in the house of the LORD.” And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Shaphan brought the book to the king and ①reported further word to the king, saying, “Everything that was ②entrusted to your servants, they are doing. ▷ ①Lit returned ②Lit given into the hand of

column.name: text
column.value: They have also emptied out the money which was found in the house of the LORD, and have handed it over to the supervisors and the workmen.”

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, Shaphan the scribe informed the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest gave me a book.” And Shaphan read from it in the presence of the king.

column.name: text
column.value: When the king heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king commanded Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, ①Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying, ▷ ①In 2 Kin 22:12, Achbor, son of Micaiah

column.name: text
column.value: “Go, inquire of the LORD for me and for those who are left in Israel and Judah, concerning the words of the book which has been found; for the wrath of the LORD which has poured out on us is great, because our fathers have not kept the word of the LORD, to act in accordance with everything that is written in this book.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Hilkiah and those ①whom the king had told went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of ②Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, the keeper of the wardrobe (she lived in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter); and they spoke to her regarding this. ▷ ①As in LXX; MT who were the king’s men ②In 2 Kin 22:14, Tikvah, son of Harhas

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said to them, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: ‘Tell the man who sent you to Me,

column.name: text
column.value: this is what the LORD says: “Behold, I am bringing ①evil on this place and on its inhabitants, all the curses written in the book which they have read in the presence of the king of Judah. ▷ ①Or disaster

column.name: text
column.value: Since they have abandoned Me and have burned incense to other gods, so that they may provoke Me to anger with all the works of their hands, My wrath will be poured out on this place and it will not be quenched.” ’

column.name: text
column.value: But to the king of Judah who sent you to inquire of the LORD, this is what you shall say to him: ‘This is what the LORD, the God of Israel says: In regard to the words which you have heard,

column.name: text
column.value: “Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before God when you heard His words against this place and its inhabitants, and because you humbled yourself before Me, tore your clothes, and wept before Me, I have indeed heard you,” declares the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: “Behold, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace, so your eyes will not see all the evil which I am bringing on this place and its inhabitants.” ’ ” And they brought back word to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent word and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The king went up to the house of the LORD ①with all the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, from the greatest to the least; and he read in their ②presence all the words of the Book of the Covenant which was found in the house of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit and ②Lit ears

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king stood ①in his place and made a covenant before the LORD to walk after the LORD, and to keep His commandments, His testimonies, and His statutes with all his heart and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that are written in this book. ▷ ①LXX by a pillar

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, he made all who were present in Jerusalem and Benjamin stand with him. So the inhabitants of Jerusalem acted in accordance with the covenant of God, the God of their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: Josiah removed all the abominations from all the lands belonging to the sons of Israel, and made all who were present in Israel serve the LORD their God. Throughout his ①lifetime they did not turn from following the LORD God of their fathers. ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the seventh month came, and the sons of Israel were in the cities, the people gathered together as one person to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeshua the son of Jozadak and his brothers the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and his brothers, rose up and built the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it, as it is written in the Law of Moses, the man of God.

column.name: text
column.value: So they set up the altar on its foundation, because ①they were terrified of the peoples of the lands; and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, burnt offerings morning and evening. ▷ ①Lit terror was upon them from

column.name: text
column.value: They also celebrated the Feast of ①Booths, as it is written, and offered ②the prescribed number of burnt offerings daily, according to the ordinance, ③as each day required; ▷ ①Or Tabernacles ②Lit by number ③Lit a day’s word on its day

column.name: text
column.value: and afterward there was a continual burnt offering, also for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of the LORD that were consecrated, and from everyone who offered a ①voluntary offering to the LORD. ▷ ①Or freewill offering

column.name: text
column.value: From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, but the foundation of the temple of the LORD had not been laid.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they gave money to the masons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the Sidonians and the Tyrians to bring cedar wood from Lebanon to the sea at Joppa, according to the permission they had ①from Cyrus king of Persia. ▷ ①Lit of

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the second year of their coming to the house of God at Jerusalem, in the second month, Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and the rest of their brothers the priests and the Levites, and all who came from the captivity to Jerusalem, began the work and appointed the Levites who were twenty years old and upward to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeshua with his sons and brothers stood united with Kadmiel and his sons, the sons of ①Judah and the sons of Henadad with their sons and brothers the Levites, to oversee the workmen in the temple of God. ▷ ①In Ezra 2:40, Hodaviah; in Neh 7:43, Hodevah

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, ①the priests stood in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the ②directions of King David of Israel. ▷ ①As in LXX and some mss; MT they set the priests ②Lit hands

column.name: text
column.value: And they sang, praising and giving thanks to the LORD, saying, “For He is good, for His favor is upon Israel forever.” And all the people shouted with a great shout of joy when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ households, the old men who had seen the first ①temple, wept with a loud voice when the foundation of this house was laid before their eyes, while many shouted aloud for joy, ▷ ①Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: so that the people could not distinguish the sound of the shout of joy from the sound of the weeping of the people, because the people were shouting with a loud shout, and the sound was heard far away.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, in order to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he sent a proclamation throughout his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: “This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has appointed me to rebuild for Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Whoever there is among you of all His people, may his God be with him! ①Go up to Jerusalem which is in Judah and rebuild the house of the LORD, the God of Israel; He is the God who is in Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit he is to go up

column.name: text
column.value: And every survivor, at whatever place he may ①live, the people of ②that place are to support him with silver and gold, with equipment and cattle, together with a ③voluntary offering for the house of God which is in Jerusalem.’ ” ▷ ①Or reside as a stranger ②Lit his ③Or freewill offering

column.name: text
column.value: Then the heads of fathers’ households of Judah and Benjamin and the priests and the Levites rose up, everyone whose spirit God had stirred to go up to rebuild the house of the LORD which is in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And all of those around them ①encouraged them with articles of silver, with gold, with equipment, cattle, and with valuables, aside from everything that was given as a ②voluntary offering. ▷ ①Lit strengthened their hands ②Or freewill offering

column.name: text
column.value: Also King Cyrus brought out the articles of the house of the LORD, which Nebuchadnezzar had carried away from Jerusalem and put in the house of his gods;

column.name: text
column.value: and Cyrus, king of Persia, had them brought out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and he counted them out to Sheshbazzar, the leader of Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now this was their number: thirty gold dishes, a thousand silver dishes, twenty nine ①duplicates; ▷ ①Heb obscure; other possible meanings are knives, censers

column.name: text
column.value: thirty gold bowls, 410 silver bowls of a second kind, and a thousand other articles.

column.name: text
column.value: All the articles of gold and silver totaled 5,400. Sheshbazzar brought them all up with the exiles who went up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Josiah celebrated the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and they slaughtered the Passover animals on the fourteenth day of the first month.

column.name: text
column.value: He appointed the priests to their offices and encouraged them in the service of the house of the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: He also said to the Levites who taught all Israel and who were holy to the LORD, “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built; it will not be a burden on your shoulders. Now serve the LORD your God and His people Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Prepare yourselves by your fathers’ households in your divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel and according to the writing of his son Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, stand in the holy place according to the sections of the fathers’ households of your countrymen, the ①lay people, and according to the Levites, by division of a father’s household. ▷ ①Lit sons of the people, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: Now slaughter the Passover animals, keep one another consecrated, and prepare for your countrymen to act in accordance with the word of the LORD by Moses.”

column.name: text
column.value: Josiah contributed to the lay people, to all who were present, flocks of lambs and young goats, all for the Passover offerings, numbering thirty thousand, plus three thousand bulls; these were from the king’s property.

column.name: text
column.value: His officers also contributed a ①voluntary offering to the people, the priests, and the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the officials of the house of God, gave the priests 2,600 from the flocks and three hundred bulls, for the Passover offerings. ▷ ①Or freewill offering

column.name: text
column.value: Conaniah also, and his brothers Shemaiah and Nethanel, and Hashabiah and Jeiel and Jozabad, the officers of the Levites, contributed five thousand from the flocks and five hundred bulls to the Levites for the Passover offerings.

column.name: text
column.value: So the service was prepared, and the priests stood at their positions and the Levites by their divisions according to the king’s command.

column.name: text
column.value: ①They slaughtered the Passover animals, and while the priests ②sprinkled the blood received from their hand, the Levites skinned the animals. ▷ ①I.e., the Levites ②As in LXX; MT sprinkled from their hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then they removed the burnt offerings so that they might give them to the sections of the fathers’ households of the lay people to present to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses. They did this with the bulls as well.

column.name: text
column.value: So they roasted the Passover animals on the fire according to the ordinance, and they boiled the holy things in pots, in kettles, and in pans and carried them quickly to all the lay people.

column.name: text
column.value: Afterward they prepared for themselves and for the priests, because the priests, the sons of Aaron, were offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night; so the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, the sons of Aaron.

column.name: text
column.value: The singers, the sons of Asaph, were also at their positions according to the command of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer; and the gatekeepers at each gate did not have to leave their service, because their kinsmen the Levites prepared for them.

column.name: text
column.value: So all the service of the LORD was prepared on that day to celebrate the Passover, and to offer burnt offerings on the altar of the LORD according to the command of King Josiah.

column.name: text
column.value: And the sons of Israel who were present celebrated the Passover at that time, and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.

column.name: text
column.value: There had not been a Passover celebrated like it in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet; nor had any of the kings of Israel celebrated such a Passover as Josiah did with the priests, the Levites, all Judah and Israel who were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: In the eighteenth year of Josiah’s reign this Passover was celebrated.

column.name: text
column.value: After all this, when Josiah had set the ①temple in order, Neco king of Egypt came up to wage war at Carchemish on the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to engage him. ▷ ①Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: But ①Neco sent messengers to him, saying, “ ②What business do you have with me, King of Judah? I am not coming against you today, but against the house with which I am at war, and God has told me to hurry. For your own sake, stop interfering with God who is with me, so that He does not destroy you.” ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit What to me and to you, an ancient idiom

column.name: text
column.value: However, Josiah would not turn ①away from him, but disguised himself in order to fight against him; nor did he listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, but he came to wage war on the plain of Megiddo. ▷ ①Lit his face

column.name: text
column.value: The archers shot King Josiah, and the king said to his servants, “Take me away, for I am badly wounded.”

column.name: text
column.value: So his servants took him out of the chariot and carried him on the second chariot which he had, and brought him to Jerusalem ①where he died and was buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah. ▷ ①Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: Then Jeremiah chanted a song of mourning for Josiah. And all the male and female singers speak about Josiah in their songs of mourning to this day. And they made them an ordinance in Israel; behold, they are also written in the Lamentations.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Josiah and his deeds of devotion as written in the Law of the LORD,

column.name: text
column.value: and his acts, the first to the last, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the people of the exile were building a temple to the LORD God of Israel,

column.name: text
column.value: they approached Zerubbabel and the heads of fathers’ households, and said to them, “Let us build with you, for like you, we seek your God; and we have been sacrificing to Him since the days of Esarhaddon king of Assyria, who brought us up here.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Zerubbabel and Jeshua and the rest of the heads of fathers’ households of Israel said to them, “You have nothing in common with us in building a house to our God; but we ourselves will together build for the LORD God of Israel, just as King Cyrus, the king of Persia, has commanded us.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of the land ①discouraged the people of Judah, and frightened them from building, ▷ ①Lit slackened the hands of

column.name: text
column.value: and bribed advisers against them to frustrate their advice all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the reign of ①Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. ▷ ①Or Xerxes; Heb Ahash-verosh

column.name: text
column.value: And in the days of ①Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabeel, and the rest of his colleagues wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia; and the ②text of the letter was written in Aramaic and translated from Aramaic. ▷ ①Heb Artah-shashta ②Lit writing

column.name: text
column.value: ①Rehum the commander and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes, as follows— ▷ ①Chs 4:8-

column.name: text
column.value: ①Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and the rest of their colleagues, the judges and the lesser governors, the officials, the secretaries, the men of Erech, the Babylonians, the men of Susa, that is, the Elamites, ▷ ①Uncertain, MT Then Rehum

column.name: text
column.value: and the rest of the nations which the great and honorable ①Osnappar deported and settled in the city of Samaria, and in the rest of the region beyond the Euphrates River. And now ▷ ①I.e., prob. Ashurbanipal

column.name: text
column.value: this is a copy of the letter which they sent to him: “To King Artaxerxes: Your servants, the men of the region beyond the Euphrates River; and now

column.name: text
column.value: let it be known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us at Jerusalem; they are rebuilding the rebellious and evil city and are finishing the walls and repairing the foundations.

column.name: text
column.value: Now let it be known to the king, that if that city is rebuilt and the walls are finished, they will not pay tribute, custom tax, or toll, and it will ①be detrimental to the revenue of the kings. ▷ ①Or certainly be...to the kings

column.name: text
column.value: Now because we ①are in the service of the palace, and it is not fitting for us to see the king’s shame, for this reason we have sent word and informed the king, ▷ ①Lit eat the salt of

column.name: text
column.value: so that a search may be conducted in the record books of your fathers. And you will discover in the record books and learn that that city is a rebellious city and detrimental to kings and provinces, and that they have revolted within it in past days; for this reason that city was laid waste.

column.name: text
column.value: We are informing the king that if that city is rebuilt and the walls finished, then as a result of this you will have no possession in the province beyond the Euphrates River.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king sent a response to Rehum the commander, Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their colleagues who live in Samaria and in the rest of the provinces beyond the Euphrates River: “Peace. And now,

column.name: text
column.value: the document which you sent to us has been ①translated and read before me. ▷ ①Lit clearly read

column.name: text
column.value: And a decree has been ①issued by me, and a search has been conducted and it has been discovered that that city has risen up against the kings in past days, and that rebellion and revolt have been perpetrated in it, ▷ ①Lit put forth

column.name: text
column.value: that mighty kings have ①ruled over Jerusalem, governing all the provinces beyond the Euphrates River, and that tribute, custom tax, and toll were paid to them. ▷ ①Lit been

column.name: text
column.value: Now issue a decree to make those men stop work, so that this city will not be rebuilt until a decree is issued by me.

column.name: text
column.value: And beware of being negligent in carrying out this matter; why should there be great damage, to the detriment of the kings?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then as soon as the copy of King Artaxerxes’ decree was read before Rehum and Shimshai the scribe and their colleagues, they went in a hurry to Jerusalem to the Jews and stopped them by military force.

column.name: text
column.value: Then work on the house of God in Jerusalem was discontinued, and it was stopped until the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the people of the land took ①Joahaz the son of Josiah and made him king in place of his father in Jerusalem. ▷ ①I.e., short form of Jehoahaz

column.name: text
column.value: Joahaz was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned for three months in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of Egypt deposed him in Jerusalem, and imposed a fine on the land of ①a hundred talents of silver and ②one talent of gold. ▷ ①About 3.75 tons or 3.4 metric tons ②About 75 lb. or 34 kg

column.name: text
column.value: The king of Egypt made ①Joahaz’s brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. But Neco took his brother Joahaz and brought him to Egypt. ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiakim was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem; and he did evil in the sight of the LORD his God.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against him and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar also brought some of the articles of the house of the LORD to Babylon, and he put them in his temple in Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim and ①the abominations which he committed, and what was found against him, behold, they are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. And his son Jehoiachin became king in his place. ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: Jehoiachin was ①eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned for three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did evil in the sight of the LORD. ▷ ①As in LXX and some Heb mss; MT eight years

column.name: text
column.value: At the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent men and had him brought to Babylon with the valuable articles of the house of the LORD; and he made his relative Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned for eleven years in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: He did evil in the sight of the LORD his God; he did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet ①who spoke for the LORD. ▷ ①Lit from the mouth of the LORD

column.name: text
column.value: He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear allegiance by God. But he stiffened his neck and hardened his heart against turning to the LORD God of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, all the officials of the priests and the people were very unfaithful, following all the abominations of the nations; and they defiled the house of the LORD which He had sanctified in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent word to them again and again by His messengers, because He had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place;

column.name: text
column.value: but they continually mocked the messengers of God, despised His words, and scoffed at His prophets, until the wrath of the LORD rose against His people, until there was no remedy.

column.name: text
column.value: So He brought up against them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or frail; He handed them all over to him.

column.name: text
column.value: He brought all the articles of the house of God, great and small, and the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the king and his officers, to Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then they burned the house of God and broke down the wall of Jerusalem, and burned all its fortified buildings with fire and destroyed all its valuable articles.

column.name: text
column.value: He took into exile those who had escaped from the sword to Babylon; and they were servants to him and to his sons until the rule of the kingdom of Persia,

column.name: text
column.value: to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths. All the days of its desolation it kept the Sabbath ①until seventy years were complete. ▷ ①Lit to fulfill seventy years

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia—in order to fulfill the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah—the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia so that he sent a proclamation throughout his kingdom, and also put it in writing, saying,

column.name: text
column.value: “This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: ‘The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has appointed me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever there is among you of all His people, may the LORD his God be with him; ①go up then!’ ” ▷ ①Lit and he is to go up; i.e., go to Jerusalem

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the ①people of the province who came up out of the captivity of the exiles whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had taken into exile to Babylon, and they returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his city. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: ①These came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, ②Seraiah, ③Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, ④Mispar, Bigvai, ⑤Rehum, and Baanah. T his is the number of the men of the people of Israel: ▷ ①In Neh 7:7, Azariah ②In Neh 7:7, Raamiah ③In Neh 7:7, Mispereth ④In Neh 7:7, Nehum ⑤Lit who
