column.name: text
column.value: And of the priests: the sons of Hobaiah, the sons of Hakkoz, the sons of Barzillai, who took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai, the Gileadite, and was named after them.

column.name: text
column.value: These searched among their ancestral registration, but it could not be located; therefore they were considered unclean and disqualified from the priesthood.

column.name: text
column.value: And the ①governor said to them that they were not to eat from the most holy things until a priest arose with Urim and Thummim. ▷ ①Heb Tirshatha, a Persian title

column.name: text
column.value: The whole assembly together totaled 42,360,

column.name: text
column.value: besides their male slaves and their female slaves, ①of whom there were 7,337; and they had 245 male and female singers. ▷ ①Lit these

column.name: text
column.value: ①Their horses were 736; their mules, 245; ▷ ①As in some ancient mss and LXX; verse not in MT

column.name: text
column.value: their camels, 435; their donkeys, 6,720.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the heads of fathers’ households gave to the work. The ①governor gave to the treasury a thousand gold drachmas, fifty basins, and 530 priests’ garments. ▷ ①Heb Tirshatha, a Persian title

column.name: text
column.value: And some of the heads of fathers’ households gave to the treasury for the work twenty thousand gold drachmas and 2,200 silver minas.

column.name: text
column.value: What the rest of the people gave was twenty thousand gold drachmas, two thousand silver minas, and sixty-seven priests’ garments.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, some of the people, the temple servants, and all Israel lived in their cities. And when the seventh month came, the sons of Israel were in their cities.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem, but the rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while nine-tenths remained in the other cities.

column.name: text
column.value: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the heads of the provinces who lived in Jerusalem, but in the cities of Judah each lived on his own property in their cities—the ①Israelites, the priests, the Levites, the ②temple servants, and the ③descendants of Solomon’s servants. ▷ ①Lit Israel ②Heb Nethinim ③Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From the sons of Judah: Athaiah the son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;

column.name: text
column.value: and Maaseiah the son of Baruch, the son of Col-hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, the son of the Shilonite.

column.name: text
column.value: All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were 468 able men.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the sons of Benjamin: Sallu the son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah;

column.name: text
column.value: and after him Gabbai and Sallai, 928.

column.name: text
column.value: Joel the son of Zichri was their overseer, and Judah the son of Hassenuah was second ①in command of the city. ▷ ①Lit over

column.name: text
column.value: From the priests: Jedaiah the son of Joiarib, Jachin,

column.name: text
column.value: Seraiah the son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the overseer of the house of God,

column.name: text
column.value: and their kinsmen who did the work of the ①temple, 822; and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malchijah, ▷ ①Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: and his kinsmen, heads of fathers’ households, 242; and Amashsai the son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,

column.name: text
column.value: and their brothers, valiant warriors, 128. And their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of ①Haggedolim. ▷ ①Or the great ones

column.name: text
column.value: Now from the Levites: Shemaiah the son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni;

column.name: text
column.value: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, from the ①leaders of the Levites, who were ②in charge of the outside work of the house of God; ▷ ①Lit heads ②Lit over

column.name: text
column.value: and Mattaniah the son of Mica, the son of ①Zabdi, the son of Asaph, who was the ②leader in beginning the thanksgiving at prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his kinsmen; and ③Abda the son of ④Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun. ▷ ①In 1 Chr 9:15, Zichri ②Lit head ③In 1 Chr 9:16, Obadiah ④In 1 Chr 9:16, Shemaiah

column.name: text
column.value: All the Levites in the holy city were 284.

column.name: text
column.value: Also the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon, and their kinsmen who kept watch at the gates, were 172.

column.name: text
column.value: The rest of Israel, of the priests and of the Levites, were in all the cities of Judah, each on his own inheritance.

column.name: text
column.value: But the temple servants were living in Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were ①in charge of the temple servants. ▷ ①Lit over

column.name: text
column.value: Now the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi the son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica, from the sons of Asaph, who were the singers for the ①service of the house of God. ▷ ①Or work

column.name: text
column.value: For there was a commandment from the king concerning them and a royal command for the singers day by day.

column.name: text
column.value: And Pethahiah the son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah the son of Judah, was the king’s ①representative for every matter concerning the people. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Now as for the villages with their fields, some of the sons of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its ①towns, in Dibon and its ②towns, and in Jekabzeel and its villages, ▷ ①Lit daughters, and so throughout the ch ②Lit daughters, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: and in Jeshua, in Moladah, and Beth-pelet,

column.name: text
column.value: and in Hazar-shual, in Beersheba and its towns,

column.name: text
column.value: and in Ziklag, in Meconah and in its towns,

column.name: text
column.value: and in En-rimmon, in Zorah, and in Jarmuth,

column.name: text
column.value: Zanoah, Adullam, and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its towns. So they camped from Beersheba as far as the Valley of Hinnom.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Benjamin also lived from Geba onward, at Michmash and Aija, at Bethel and its towns,

column.name: text
column.value: at Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,

column.name: text
column.value: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,

column.name: text
column.value: Lod, and Ono, the Valley of Craftsmen.

column.name: text
column.value: And from the Levites, some divisions in Judah belonged to Benjamin.

column.name: text
column.value: Now it came about on the third day that Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner courtyard of the king’s palace in front of the king’s ①rooms, and the king was sitting on his royal throne in the ②throne room, opposite the entrance to the palace. ▷ ①Lit house ②Lit royal house

column.name: text
column.value: When the king saw Esther the queen standing in the courtyard, she obtained favor in his sight; and the king extended to Esther the golden scepter which was in his hand. So Esther approached and touched the top of the scepter.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to her, “What is troubling you, Queen Esther? And what is your request? Up to half of the kingdom it shall be given to you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Esther said, “If it pleases the king, may the king and Haman come this day to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, “Bring Haman quickly so that we may do ①as Esther desires.” So the king and Haman came to the banquet which Esther had prepared. ▷ ①Lit the word of Esther

column.name: text
column.value: ①As they drank their wine at the banquet, the king said to Esther, “What is your request, for it shall be granted to you. And what is your wish? Up to half of the kingdom it shall be done.” ▷ ①Lit At the banquet of wine

column.name: text
column.value: So Esther replied, “My request and my wish is:

column.name: text
column.value: if I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my request and do ①what I wish, may the king and Haman come to the banquet which I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do ②as the king says.” ▷ ①Lit my wish ②Lit according to the word of the king

column.name: text
column.value: Then Haman went out that day joyful and pleased of heart; but when Haman saw Mordecai at the king’s gate and that he did not stand up or tremble before him, Haman was filled with anger against Mordecai.

column.name: text
column.value: Haman controlled himself, however, and went to his house. But he ①sent for his friends and his wife Zeresh. ▷ ①Lit sent and brought

column.name: text
column.value: Then Haman told them of the glory of his riches, and his many sons, and every occasion on which the king had honored him and how he had ①promoted him above the officials and servants of the king. ▷ ①Lit lifted

column.name: text
column.value: Haman also said, “Even Esther the queen let no one except me come with the king to the banquet which she had prepared; and tomorrow also I am invited by her with the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet all of this ①does not satisfy me every time I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.” ▷ ①Lit is not suitable to me

column.name: text
column.value: Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, “Have a wooden gallows ①fifty cubits high made, and in the morning ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on it; then go joyfully with the king to the banquet.” And the ②advice pleased Haman, so he had the wooden gallows made. ▷ ①About 75 ft. or 23 m ②Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened in the days of Ahasuerus, the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to ①Cush over 127 provinces, ▷ ①Or Ethiopia

column.name: text
column.value: in those days as King Ahasuerus sat on his royal throne which was at the citadel in Susa,

column.name: text
column.value: in the third year of his reign he held a banquet for all his officials and attendants, the army officers of Persia and Media, the nobles and the officials of his provinces, in his presence.

column.name: text
column.value: ①At that time he displayed the riches of his royal glory and the splendor of his great majesty for many days, 180 days. ▷ ①Lit When

column.name: text
column.value: When these days were finished, the king held a banquet lasting seven days for all the people who were present at the citadel in Susa, from the greatest to the least, in the courtyard of the garden of the king’s palace.

column.name: text
column.value: There were curtains of fine white and violet linen held by cords of fine purple linen on silver rings and marble columns, and couches of gold and silver on a mosaic floor of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl, and mineral stones.

column.name: text
column.value: Drinks were served in golden vessels of various kinds, and the royal wine was plentiful in proportion to the king’s ①bounty. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: But the drinking was done according to the royal law; there was no compulsion, for so the king had given orders to each official of his household, that he was to do as each person pleased.

column.name: text
column.value: Queen Vashti also held a banquet for the women in the ①palace which belonged to King Ahasuerus. ▷ ①Lit royal house

column.name: text
column.value: On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was cheerful with wine, he ordered Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas, the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus,

column.name: text
column.value: to bring Queen Vashti before the king with her royal turban in order to display her beauty to the people and the officials, for she was beautiful.

column.name: text
column.value: But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king’s order ①delivered by the eunuchs. So the king became very angry, and his wrath burned within him. ▷ ①Lit by the hand of the

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to the wise men who understood the times—for it was the custom of the king to speak this way before all who knew Persian law and justice

column.name: text
column.value: and were close to him, namely, Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who ①had access to the king’s presence and sat in the first place in the kingdom— ▷ ①Lit saw the face of the king

column.name: text
column.value: “According to law, what is to be done with Queen Vashti, since she did not ①obey the command of King Ahasuerus ②delivered by the eunuchs?” ▷ ①Lit do ②Lit by the hand of the

column.name: text
column.value: And in the presence of the king and the other officials, Memucan said, “Queen Vashti has wronged not only the king but also all the officials and all the peoples who are in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

column.name: text
column.value: For the queen’s conduct will ①become known to all the women so as to make their own husbands despicable in their sight, when they say, ‘King Ahasuerus ②commanded that Queen Vashti be brought in to his presence, but she did not come.’ ▷ ①Lit said to bring ②Lit go forth

column.name: text
column.value: And this day the wives of the officials of Persia and Media who have heard about the queen’s conduct will talk about it to all the king’s officials, and there will be plenty of contempt and anger.

column.name: text
column.value: If it pleases the king, let a royal ①edict be issued by him and let it be written in the laws of Persia and Media so that it cannot ②be repealed, that Vashti may not come into the presence of King Ahasuerus, and let the king give her royal position to ③another who is more worthy than she. ▷ ①Lit word go forth from ②Lit pass by ③Lit her neighbor

column.name: text
column.value: When the king’s edict which he will make is heard throughout his kingdom, ①great as it is, then all women will give honor to their husbands, great and small.” ▷ ①Lit for great is it

column.name: text
column.value: Now this word pleased the king and the officials, and the king did ①as Memucan proposed. ▷ ①Lit according to the word of

column.name: text
column.value: So he sent letters to all the king’s provinces, to each province according to its script and to every people according to their language, that every man was to be the ruler in his own house and the one who speaks in the language of his own people.

column.name: text
column.value: Now these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,

column.name: text
column.value: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,

column.name: text
column.value: Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,

column.name: text
column.value: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,

column.name: text
column.value: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,

column.name: text
column.value: Shemaiah and Joiarib, Jedaiah,

column.name: text
column.value: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their kinsmen in the days of Jeshua.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Levites were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah who was ①in charge of the songs of thanksgiving, he and his brothers. ▷ ①Lit over

column.name: text
column.value: Also Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood opposite them in their service divisions.

column.name: text
column.value: Jeshua fathered Joiakim, Joiakim fathered Eliashib, Eliashib fathered Joiada,

column.name: text
column.value: Joiada fathered Jonathan, and Jonathan fathered Jaddua.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the days of Joiakim, the priests, the heads of fathers’ households were: of Seraiah, Meraiah; of Jeremiah, Hananiah;

column.name: text
column.value: of Ezra, Meshullam; of Amariah, Jehohanan;

column.name: text
column.value: of ①Malluchi, Jonathan; of Shebaniah, Joseph; ▷ ①In v 2, Malluch

column.name: text
column.value: of Harim, Adna; of Meraioth, Helkai;

column.name: text
column.value: of Iddo, Zechariah; of Ginnethon, Meshullam;

column.name: text
column.value: of Abijah, Zichri; of Miniamin, of Moadiah, Piltai;

column.name: text
column.value: of Bilgah, Shammua; of Shemaiah, Jehonathan;

column.name: text
column.value: of Joiarib, Mattenai; of Jedaiah, Uzzi;

column.name: text
column.value: of Sallai, Kallai; of Amok, Eber;

column.name: text
column.value: of Hilkiah, Hashabiah; and of Jedaiah, Nethanel.

column.name: text
column.value: As for the Levites, the heads of fathers’ households were registered in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, and Johanan, and Jaddua; so were the priests in the reign of Darius the Persian.

column.name: text
column.value: The sons of Levi, the heads of fathers’ households, were registered in the Book of the Chronicles up to the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib.

column.name: text
column.value: And the heads of the Levites were Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brothers opposite them, to praise and give thanks, ①as prescribed by David the man of God, division corresponding to division. ▷ ①Lit by the commandment of

column.name: text
column.value: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers keeping watch at the storerooms of the gates.

column.name: text
column.value: These men served in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

column.name: text
column.value: Now at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought out the Levites from all their places, to bring them to Jerusalem so that they could celebrate the dedication with joy, with songs of thanksgiving and with songs to the accompaniment of cymbals, harps, and lyres.

column.name: text
column.value: So the sons of the singers were assembled from the territory around Jerusalem, and from the villages of the Netophathites,

column.name: text
column.value: from Beth-gilgal and from their fields in Geba and Azmaveth, because the singers had built themselves villages around Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: The priests and the Levites purified themselves; they also purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I had the leaders of Judah come up on top of the wall, and I appointed two large ①choirs, ②the first proceeding to the right on top of the wall toward the Dung Gate. ▷ ①Lit thanksgiving choirs ②Heb and processions to the right

column.name: text
column.value: Hoshaiah and half of the leaders of Judah followed them,

column.name: text
column.value: with Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam,

column.name: text
column.value: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah,

column.name: text
column.value: and some of the sons of the priests with trumpets; and Zechariah the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Micaiah, the son of Zaccur, the son of Asaph,

column.name: text
column.value: and his kinsmen, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani, with the musical instruments of David the man of God. And Ezra the scribe went before them.

column.name: text
column.value: At the Fountain Gate they went directly up the steps of the city of David by the stairway of the wall, above the house of David to the Water Gate on the east.

column.name: text
column.value: The second ①choir proceeded to the ②left, while I followed them with half of the people on the wall, above the Tower of Furnaces, to the Broad Wall, ▷ ①Lit thanksgiving choir ②Heb uncertain, perhaps opposite

column.name: text
column.value: and above the Gate of Ephraim, by the Ancient Gate, by the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of the Hundred, as far as the Sheep Gate; and they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the two choirs took their positions in the house of God. So did I and half of the officials with me;

column.name: text
column.value: and the priests, Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, with the trumpets;

column.name: text
column.value: and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. And the singers ①sang, with Jezrahiah their leader, ▷ ①Lit made themselves heard

column.name: text
column.value: and on that day they offered great sacrifices and rejoiced because God had given them great joy, and the women and children rejoiced as well, so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard from far away.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day men were also appointed over the chambers for the supplies, the contributions, the first fruits, and the tithes, to gather into them from the fields of the cities the portions required by the Law for the priests and Levites; for Judah rejoiced over the priests and the Levites who ①served. ▷ ①Lit stood

column.name: text
column.value: For they performed the ①worship of their God and the service of purification, together with the singers and the gatekeepers in accordance with the command of David and of his son Solomon. ▷ ①Lit service

column.name: text
column.value: For in the days of David and Asaph, in ancient times, there were ①leaders of the singers, songs of praise and songs of thanksgiving to God. ▷ ①Lit heads

column.name: text
column.value: So all Israel in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah gave the portions due the singers and the gatekeepers as each day required, and they ①set apart the consecrated portion for the Levites, and the Levites ②set apart the consecrated portion for the sons of Aaron. ▷ ①Or gave votive offerings to ②Or gave votive offerings to

column.name: text
column.value: After these things, when the anger of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done, and what had been decided regarding her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king’s attendants, who served him, said, “Let beautiful young virgins be sought for the king.

column.name: text
column.value: And may the king appoint overseers in all the provinces of his kingdom, and have them ①bring every beautiful young virgin to the citadel of Susa, to the harem, into the custody of Hegai, the king’s eunuch, who is in charge of the women; and let their cosmetics be given to them. ▷ ①Lit gather

column.name: text
column.value: Then let the young woman who pleases the king be queen in place of Vashti.” And the ①suggestion pleased the king, and he did accordingly. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: There was a Jew at the citadel in Susa whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

column.name: text
column.value: who had been taken from Jerusalem with the exiles who had been deported with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had deported.

column.name: text
column.value: He was the guardian to Hadassah, that is Esther, his uncle’s daughter, for she had no father or mother. Now the young woman was beautiful of form and ①face, and when her father and her mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter. ▷ ①Lit good of appearance

column.name: text
column.value: So it came about, when the command and decree of the king were heard and many young ladies were gathered to the citadel of Susa into the ①custody of Hegai, that Esther was taken to the king’s ②palace into the custody of Hegai, who was in charge of the women. ▷ ①Lit hand ②Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: Now the young lady pleased him and found favor with him. So he quickly provided her with her cosmetics and ①food, gave her seven choice female attendants from the king’s palace, and transferred her and her attendants to the best place in the harem. ▷ ①Lit portions

column.name: text
column.value: Esther did not reveal her people or her kindred, because Mordecai had instructed her that she was not to reveal them.

column.name: text
column.value: And every day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the courtyard of the harem to learn how Esther was and what was happening to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the turn came for each young woman to go in to King Ahasuerus, after the end of her twelve months under the regulations for the women—for the days of their beauty treatment were completed as follows: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with balsam oil and the cosmetics for women—

column.name: text
column.value: the young woman would go in to the king in this way: anything that she ①desired was given her to ②take with her from the harem to the king’s palace. ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit come

column.name: text
column.value: In the evening she would enter and in the morning she would return to the second harem, to the ①custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch who was in charge of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again, unless the king delighted in her and she was summoned by name. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who had taken her as his daughter, came to go in to the king, she did not request anything except what Hegai, the king’s eunuch who was in charge of the women, ①advised. And Esther was finding favor in the eyes of all who saw her. ▷ ①Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

column.name: text
column.value: The king loved Esther more than all the women, and she found favor and kindness with him more than all the virgins, so that he set the royal turban on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king held a great banquet, Esther’s banquet, for all his officials and his servants; he also made a holiday for the provinces and gave gifts in proportion to the king’s bounty.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the virgins were gathered together for the second time, then Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Esther still had not revealed her relatives or her people, just as Mordecai had instructed her; for Esther did ①what Mordecai told her just as she had when under his care. ▷ ①Lit the command of Mordecai

column.name: text
column.value: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king’s gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king’s officials from those who guarded the door, became angry and sought to ①attack King Ahasuerus. ▷ ①Or kill; lit put out a hand against

column.name: text
column.value: But the ①plot became known to Mordecai and he informed Queen Esther, and Esther told the king in Mordecai’s name. ▷ ①Lit matter, so also v 23

column.name: text
column.value: Then when the plot was investigated and found to be so, they were both hanged on a wooden gallows; and it was written in the Book of the Chronicles in the king’s presence.

column.name: text
column.value: When Mordecai learned of everything that had been done, ①he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the midst of the city and wailed loudly and bitterly. ▷ ①Lit Mordecai

column.name: text
column.value: And he came as far as the king’s gate, for no one was to enter the king’s gate clothed in sackcloth.

column.name: text
column.value: In each and every province where the command and decree of the king came, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping, and mourning rites; and many had sackcloth and ashes spread out as a bed.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther’s attendants and her eunuchs came and informed her, and the queen was seized by great fear. And she sent garments to clothe Mordecai so that he would remove his sackcloth from him, but he did not accept them.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther summoned Hathach from the king’s eunuchs, whom ①the king had appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to learn what this mourning was and why it was happening. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: So Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square, in front of the king’s gate.

column.name: text
column.value: Mordecai told him everything that had happened to him, and the exact amount of money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the elimination of the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: He also gave him a copy of the text of the edict which had been issued in Susa for their annihilation, so that he might show Esther and inform her, and to order her to go in to the king to implore his favor and plead with him for her people.

column.name: text
column.value: So Hathach came back and reported Mordecai’s words to Esther.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther spoke to Hathach and ordered him to reply to Mordecai:

column.name: text
column.value: “All the king’s servants and the people of the king’s provinces know that for any man or woman who comes to the king in the inner courtyard, who is not summoned, he has only one law, that he be put to death, unless the king holds out to him the golden scepter so that he may live. And I have not been summoned to come to the king for these thirty days.”

column.name: text
column.value: And they reported Esther’s words to Mordecai.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Mordecai told them to reply to Esther, “Do not imagine that you in the king’s palace can escape any more than all the other Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: For if you keep silent at this time, liberation and rescue will arise for the Jews from another place, and you and your father’s house will perish. And who knows whether you have not attained royalty for such a time as this?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther told them to reply to Mordecai,

column.name: text
column.value: “Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me; do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my attendants also will fast in the same way. And then I will go in to the king, which is not in accordance with the law; and if I perish, I perish.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Mordecai went away and did just as Esther had commanded him.

column.name: text
column.value: After these events King Ahasuerus honored Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and promoted him and ①established his authority over all the officials who were with him. ▷ ①Lit set his seat

column.name: text
column.value: All the king’s servants who were at the king’s gate bowed down and paid ①homage to Haman; for so the king had commanded regarding him. But Mordecai neither bowed down nor paid ②homage. ▷ ①I.e., great respect and honor to a superior ②I.e., great respect and honor to a superior

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king’s servants who were at the king’s gate said to Mordecai, “Why are you violating the king’s command?”

column.name: text
column.value: Now it was when they had spoken daily to him and he would not listen to them, that they told Haman to see whether Mordecai’s reason would ①stand; for he had told them that he was a Jew. ▷ ①I.e., as valid

column.name: text
column.value: When Haman saw that Mordecai neither bowed down nor paid ①homage to him, Haman was filled with rage. ▷ ①I.e., great respect and honor to a superior

column.name: text
column.value: But he ①considered it beneath his dignity to ②kill Mordecai alone, for they had told him who the people of Mordecai were; so Haman sought to annihilate all the Jews, the people of Mordecai, who were found throughout the kingdom of Ahasuerus. ▷ ①Lit despised in his eyes ②Lit send a hand against

column.name: text
column.value: In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, ①Pur, that is the lot, was cast before Haman from day to day and from month to month, ②until the twelfth month, that is the month Adar. ▷ ①Lit he cast Pur...before ②LXX and the lot fell on the thirteenth day of

column.name: text
column.value: Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom; their laws are different from those of all other people and they do not ①comply with the king’s laws, so it is not in the king’s interest to let them remain. ▷ ①Lit do the

column.name: text
column.value: If it is pleasing to the king, let it be ①decreed that they be eliminated, and I will pay ②ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who carry out the king’s business, to put into the king’s treasuries.” ▷ ①Lit written ②About 375 tons or 340 metric tons

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king took his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Haman, “The silver is ①yours, and the people also, to do with them as you please.” ▷ ①Lit given to you

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king’s scribes were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and it was written just as Haman commanded to the king’s satraps, to the governors who were over each province and to the officials of each people, each province according to its script, each people according to its language, being written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king’s signet ring.

column.name: text
column.value: Letters were sent by couriers to all the king’s provinces to annihilate, kill, and destroy all the Jews, both young and old, women and children, in one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to seize their possessions as plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: A copy of the edict to be ①issued as law in every province was published to all the peoples so that they would be ready for this day. ▷ ①Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: The couriers went out, speeded by the king’s ①order while the decree was ②issued at the citadel in Susa; and while the king and Haman sat down to drink, the city of Susa was agitated. ▷ ①Lit word ②Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: On that day the Book of Moses was read aloud ①as the people listened; and there was found written in it that no Ammonite or Moabite was ever to enter the assembly of God, ▷ ①Lit in the ears of the people

column.name: text
column.value: because they did not meet the sons of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.

column.name: text
column.value: So when they heard the Law, they excluded all foreigners from Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: Now prior to this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the chambers of the house of our God, being ①related to Tobiah, ▷ ①Lit close to

column.name: text
column.value: had prepared a large ①room for him, where previously they used to put the grain offerings, the frankincense, the utensils and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, the singers, and the gatekeepers, and the ②contributions for the priests. ▷ ①Or chamber ②Or uplifted offerings

column.name: text
column.value: But during all this time I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had come to the king. After some time, however, I requested a leave of absence from the king,

column.name: text
column.value: and I came to Jerusalem and ①learned about the evil that Eliashib had committed for ②Tobiah, by preparing a ③room for him in the courtyards of the house of God. ▷ ①Or understood ②An Ammonite, banned from the temple ③Or chamber, and so in vv 8, 9

column.name: text
column.value: It was very displeasing to me, so I threw all of Tobiah’s household articles out of the room.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I gave an order, and they cleansed the rooms; and I returned the utensils of the house of God there with the grain offering and the frankincense.

column.name: text
column.value: I also ①discovered that the portions of the Levites had not been given to them, so the Levites and the singers who performed the service had ②gone away, each to his own field. ▷ ①Or knew ②Lit fled

column.name: text
column.value: So I ①reprimanded the officials and said, “Why has the house of God been neglected?” Then I gathered them together and stationed them at their posts. ▷ ①Or contended with

column.name: text
column.value: All Judah then brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.

column.name: text
column.value: To be in charge of the storehouses, I appointed Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah from the Levites, and in addition to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah; for they were considered reliable, and it was ①their task to distribute to their kinsmen. ▷ ①Lit on them to

column.name: text
column.value: Remember me for this, my God, and do not wipe out my loyal deeds which I have performed for the house of my God and its services.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days I saw in Judah people who were treading wine presses on the Sabbath, and bringing in sacks of grain and loading them on donkeys, as well as wine, grapes, figs, and every kind of load, and they were bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. So I admonished them on the day they sold food.

column.name: text
column.value: Also people of Tyre were living ①there who imported fish and all kinds of merchandise, and sold them to the sons of Judah on the Sabbath, even in Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit in it

column.name: text
column.value: Then I ①reprimanded the nobles of Judah and said to them, “What is this evil thing that you are doing, ②by profaning the Sabbath day? ▷ ①Or contended with ②Lit and

column.name: text
column.value: Did your fathers not do the same, so that our God brought on us and on this city all this trouble? Yet you are adding to the wrath against Israel by profaning the Sabbath.”

column.name: text
column.value: And it came about that just as it became dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I ordered that the doors be shut, ①and that they were not to open them until after the Sabbath. Then I stationed some of my servants at the gates so that no load would enter on the Sabbath day. ▷ ①Lit and commanded

column.name: text
column.value: Once or twice the traders and merchants of every kind of merchandise spent the night outside Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I warned them and said to them, “Why do you spend the night in front of the wall? If you do so again, I will ①use force against you.” From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath. ▷ ①Lit send a hand against

column.name: text
column.value: And I ordered the Levites that they were to purify themselves and come as gatekeepers to sanctify the Sabbath day. For this also remember me, my God, and have compassion on me according to the greatness of Your mercy.

column.name: text
column.value: In those days I also saw that the Jews had ①married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab. ▷ ①Lit given dwelling to

column.name: text
column.value: As for their children, half spoke in the language of Ashdod, and none of them knew how to speak the language of Judah, but ①only the language of his own people. ▷ ①Lit according to the tongue of people and people

column.name: text
column.value: So I quarreled with them and cursed them, and struck some of them and pulled out their hair, and made them swear by God, “You shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Did Solomon the king of Israel not sin regarding these things? Yet among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet the foreign women caused even him to sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Has it not then been reported about you that you have committed all this great evil by acting unfaithfully against our God, by ①marrying foreign women?” ▷ ①Lit giving dwelling to

column.name: text
column.value: Even one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, became a son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, so I chased him away from me.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember them, my God, ①because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites. ▷ ①Lit for the defilements of

column.name: text
column.value: So I purified them from everything foreign, and assigned duties to the priests and the Levites, each in his work,

column.name: text
column.value: and I arranged for the delivery of wood at appointed times and for the first fruits. Remember me, my God, for good.

column.name: text
column.value: During that night ①the king could not sleep, so he gave an order to bring the book of records, the chronicles, and they were read before the king. ▷ ①Lit the king’s sleep fled

column.name: text
column.value: And it was found written what Mordecai had reported about Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs who were doorkeepers, that they had sought to ①attack King Ahasuerus. ▷ ①Or kill; lit put out a hand against

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said, “What honor or dignity has been bestowed on Mordecai for this?” And the king’s servants who attended him said, “Nothing has been done for him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king said, “Who is in the courtyard?” Now Haman had just entered the outer courtyard of the king’s palace in order to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the wooden gallows which he had prepared for him.

column.name: text
column.value: So the king’s servants said to him, “Behold, Haman is standing in the courtyard.” And the king said, “Have him come in.”

column.name: text
column.value: Haman then came in and the king said to him, “What is to be done for the man whom the king desires to honor?” And Haman said ①to himself, “Whom would the king desire to honor more than me?” ▷ ①Lit in his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore Haman said to the king, “For the man whom the king desires to honor,

column.name: text
column.value: have them bring a royal robe which the king has worn, and the horse on which the king has ridden, and on whose head a royal turban has been placed;

column.name: text
column.value: then order them to hand the robe and the horse over to one of the king’s noble officials, and have them dress the man whom the king desires to honor, and lead him on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, ‘So it shall be done for the man whom the king desires to honor.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king said to Haman, “Quickly, take the robe and the horse just as you have said, and do so for Mordecai the Jew, who is sitting at the king’s gate; do not fail to do anything of all that you have said.”

column.name: text
column.value: So Haman took the robe and the horse, and dressed Mordecai, and led him on horseback through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “So it shall be done for the man whom the king desires to honor.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Mordecai returned to the king’s gate, while Haman hurried home, mourning, with his head covered.

column.name: text
column.value: And Haman informed Zeresh his wife and all his friends of everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is ①of Jewish origin, you will not prevail over him, but will certainly fall before him.” ▷ ①Lit from the seed of the Jews

column.name: text
column.value: While they were still talking with him, the king’s eunuchs arrived and quickly brought Haman to the banquet which Esther had prepared.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the king and Haman came to drink wine with Esther the queen.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Esther on the second day also ①as they drank their wine at the banquet, “What is your request, Queen Esther? It shall be granted you. And what is your wish? Up to half of the kingdom it shall be done.” ▷ ①Lit at the banquet of wine

column.name: text
column.value: Then Queen Esther replied, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me as my request, and my people as my wish;

column.name: text
column.value: for we have been sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, killed, and eliminated. Now if we had only been sold as slaves, men and women, I would have kept silent, because the distress would not be sufficient reason to burden the king.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Ahasuerus ①asked Queen Esther, “Who is he, and where is he, ②who would presume to do such a thing?” ▷ ①Lit said and said to ②Lit whose heart has filled him

column.name: text
column.value: And Esther said, “A foe and an enemy is this wicked Haman!” Then Haman became terrified before the king and queen.

column.name: text
column.value: The king then got up in his anger from ①drinking wine and went into the palace garden; but Haman stayed to beg for his life from Queen Esther, for he saw that harm had been determined against him by the king. ▷ ①Lit the banquet of wine

column.name: text
column.value: Now when the king returned from the palace garden into the ①place where they had been drinking wine, Haman was falling on the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen with me in the house?” As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face. ▷ ①Lit house of the banquet of wine

column.name: text
column.value: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who stood before the king, said, “Indeed, behold, the wooden gallows standing at Haman’s house ①fifty cubits high, which Haman made for Mordecai who spoke good in behalf of the king!” And the king said, “Hang him on it.” ▷ ①About 75 ft. or 23 m

column.name: text
column.value: So they hanged Haman on the wooden gallows which he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king’s anger subsided.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, to Queen Esther; and Mordecai came before the king, because Esther had disclosed what he was to her.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king took off his signet ring, which he had taken away from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther spoke again ①to the king, fell at his feet, wept, and pleaded for his compassion to avert the evil scheme of Haman the Agagite and his plot which he had devised against the Jews. ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: And the king extended the golden scepter to Esther. So Esther got up and stood before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then she said, “If it pleases the king and if I have found favor before him, and the matter seems proper to the king and I am pleasing in his sight, let it be written to revoke the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to eliminate the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces.

column.name: text
column.value: For how can I endure to see the disaster which will happen to my people, and how can I endure to see the destruction of my kindred?”

column.name: text
column.value: So King Ahasuerus said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai the Jew, “Behold, I have given the house of Haman to Esther, and they have hanged him on the wooden gallows because he had reached out with his hand against the Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: Now you write to the Jews ①as you see fit, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s signet ring; for a decree which is written in the name of the king and sealed with the king’s signet ring may not be revoked.” ▷ ①Lit according to the good in your eyes

column.name: text
column.value: So the king’s scribes were summoned at that time in the third month (that is, the month Sivan), on the twenty-third ①day; and it was written in accordance with everything that Mordecai commanded the Jews, the satraps, the governors, and the officials of the provinces which extended from India to ②Cush, 127 provinces, to every province according to its script, and to every people according to their language, as well as to the Jews according to their script and their language. ▷ ①Lit in it ②Or Ethiopia

column.name: text
column.value: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and sent letters by couriers on horses, riding on royal relay horses, offspring of racing mares.

column.name: text
column.value: ①In the letters the king granted the Jews who were in each and every city the right to assemble and to defend their lives, to destroy, kill, and eliminate the entire army of any people or province which was going to attack them, including children and women, and to plunder their spoils, ▷ ①Lit Which the king

column.name: text
column.value: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month (that is, the month Adar).

column.name: text
column.value: A copy of the edict to be ①issued as law in each and every province was published to all the peoples, so that the Jews would be ready for this day to avenge themselves on their enemies. ▷ ①Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: The couriers, hurrying and speeded by the king’s command, left, riding on the royal relay horses; and the decree was issued at the citadel in Susa.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in a royal robe of violet and white, with a large crown of gold and a garment of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.

column.name: text
column.value: For the Jews there was light, joy, jubilation, and honor.

column.name: text
column.value: In each and every province and in each and every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree arrived, there was joy and jubilation for the Jews, a feast and a ①holiday. And many among the peoples of the land ②became Jews, because the dread of the Jews had fallen on them. ▷ ①Lit good day ②Or posed as Jews

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the twelfth month (that is, the month Adar), on the thirteenth ①day, when the king’s command and edict were to be put into effect, on the day when the enemies of the Jews hoped to gain the mastery over them, it turned out to the contrary so that the Jews themselves gained mastery over those who hated them. ▷ ①Lit day in it

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews assembled in their cities throughout the provinces of King Ahasuerus to ①attack those who sought ②to harm them; and no one could stand against them, because the dread of them had fallen on all the peoples. ▷ ①Lit put out a hand against ②Lit their harm

column.name: text
column.value: Even all the officials of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who were doing the king’s business were supporting the Jews, because the dread of Mordecai had fallen on them.

column.name: text
column.value: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and the news about him spread throughout the provinces; for the man Mordecai became greater and greater.

column.name: text
column.value: So the Jews struck all their enemies with ①the sword, killing and destroying; and they did as they pleased to those who hated them. ▷ ①Lit the stroke of the

column.name: text
column.value: At the citadel in Susa the Jews killed and eliminated five hundred men,

column.name: text
column.value: and they killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

column.name: text
column.value: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

column.name: text
column.value: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,

column.name: text
column.value: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy; but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: On that day the number of those who were killed at the citadel in Susa ①was reported to the king. ▷ ①Lit came before

column.name: text
column.value: And the king said to Queen Esther, “The Jews have killed and eliminated five hundred men and the ten sons of Haman at the citadel in Susa. What have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces! Now what is your request? It shall also be granted you. And what is your further wish? It shall also be done.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Esther said, “If it pleases the king, let tomorrow also be granted to the Jews who are in Susa to do according to the edict of today; and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the wooden gallows.”

column.name: text
column.value: So the king commanded that it was to be done so; and an edict was issued in Susa, and Haman’s ten sons were hanged.

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews who were in Susa assembled also on the fourteenth day of the month Adar and killed three hundred men in Susa, but they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

column.name: text
column.value: Now the rest of the Jews who were in the king’s provinces assembled, to defend their lives and ①rid themselves of their enemies, and to kill seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; but they did not lay their hands on the plunder. ▷ ①Lit have rest from

column.name: text
column.value: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar, and on the fourteenth ①day they rested and made it a day of feasting and rejoicing. ▷ ①Lit in it

column.name: text
column.value: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled on the thirteenth and the fourteenth ①of the same month, and they rested on the fifteenth ②day and made it a day of feasting and rejoicing. ▷ ①Lit in it ②Lit in it

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the Jews of the rural areas, who live in the rural towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a ①holiday for rejoicing and feasting and sending portions of food to one another. ▷ ①Lit rejoicing and feasting and a good day and sending

column.name: text
column.value: Then Mordecai recorded these events, and he sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, both near and far,

column.name: text
column.value: obliging them to celebrate the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day ①of the same month, annually, ▷ ①Lit in it

column.name: text
column.value: because on those days the Jews ①rid themselves of their enemies, and it was a month which was turned for them from grief into joy, and from mourning into a ②holiday; that they were to make them days of feasting and rejoicing, and sending portions of food to one another, and gifts to the poor. ▷ ①Lit had rest from ②Lit good day

column.name: text
column.value: So the Jews undertook what they had started to do, and what Mordecai had written to them.

column.name: text
column.value: For Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the adversary of all the Jews, had schemed against the Jews to eliminate them, and had cast Pur, that is the lot, to disturb them and eliminate them.

column.name: text
column.value: But when it came ①to the king’s attention, he commanded by letter that his wicked scheme which he had devised against the Jews was to return on his own head, and that he and his sons were to be hanged on the wooden gallows. ▷ ①Lit before the king, he

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore they called these days Purim after the name of ①Pur. ②And because of the instructions in this letter, both what they had seen in this regard and what had happened to them, ▷ ①Akkadian for lot ②Lit Therefore because of all the words

column.name: text
column.value: the Jews established and ①made a custom for themselves, their ②descendants, and for all those who allied themselves with them, so that ③they would not fail to celebrate these two days according to their ④regulation and according to their appointed time annually. ▷ ①Lit received ②Lit seed ③Lit it would not pass away ④Lit writing

column.name: text
column.value: So these days were to be remembered and celebrated throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and these days of Purim were not to ①be neglected by the Jews, or their memory ②fade from their ③descendants. ▷ ①Lit pass from the midst of ②Lit end ③Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter about Purim.

column.name: text
column.value: He sent letters to all the Jews, to the 127 provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus, namely, words of peace and truth,

column.name: text
column.value: to establish these days of Purim at their appointed times, just as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had established for them, and just as they had established for themselves and for their ①descendants, with ②instructions for their times of fasting and their mourning. ▷ ①Lit words ②Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: The command of Esther established these ①customs for Purim, and it was written in the book. ▷ ①Lit words

column.name: text
column.value: Now King Ahasuerus imposed a tax on the land and the coastlands of the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: And every accomplishment of his authority and power, and the full account of the greatness of Mordecai with which the king honored him, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Media and Persia?

column.name: text
column.value: For Mordecai the Jew was second only to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and in favor with his many kinsmen, one who sought the good of his people and one who spoke for the welfare of his entire ①nation. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Again, there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and ①Satan also came among them to present himself before the LORD. ▷ ①Heb ha-satan; i.e., the adversary, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered the LORD and said, “From roaming about on the earth and walking around on it.”

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD said to Satan, “Have you ①considered My servant Job? For there is no one like him on the earth, a blameless and upright man ②fearing God and turning away from evil. And he still holds firm to his integrity, although you incited Me against him to ③ruin him without cause.” ▷ ①Lit set your heart to ②Or revering ③Lit swallow him up

column.name: text
column.value: Satan answered the LORD and said, “Skin for skin! Yes, all that a man has, he will give for his life.

column.name: text
column.value: However, reach out with Your hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh; he will curse You to Your face!”

column.name: text
column.value: So the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, he is in your ①power, only spare his life.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then Satan went out from the presence of the LORD and struck Job with severe boils from the sole of his foot to the top of his head.

column.name: text
column.value: And Job took a piece of pottery to scrape himself while he was sitting in the ashes.

column.name: text
column.value: Then his wife said to him, “Do you still hold firm your integrity? Curse God and die!”

column.name: text
column.value: But he said to her, “You are speaking as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we actually accept good from God but not accept adversity?” Despite all this, Job did not sin with his lips.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Job’s three friends heard about all this adversity that had come upon him, they came, each one from his own place—Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite; and they made an appointment together to come to sympathize with him and comfort him.

column.name: text
column.value: When they ①looked from a distance and did not recognize him, they raised their voices and wept. And each of them tore his robe, and they threw dust over their heads toward the sky. ▷ ①Lit raised their eyes

column.name: text
column.value: Then they sat down on the ground with him for seven days and seven nights, with no one speaking a word to him, for they saw that his pain was very great.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Eliphaz the Temanite responded,

column.name: text
column.value: “If one ventures a word with you, will you become impatient? But who can refrain ①from speaking? ▷ ①Lit in words

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, you have taught many, And you have strengthened weak hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Your words have helped the stumbling to stand, And you have strengthened ①feeble knees. ▷ ①Lit knees giving way

column.name: text
column.value: But now it comes to you, and you are impatient; It touches you, and you are horrified.

column.name: text
column.value: Is your ①fear of God not your confidence, And the integrity of your ways your hope? ▷ ①Or reverence for

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: The roaring of the lion and the voice of the fierce lion, And the teeth of the young lions are broken out.

column.name: text
column.value: The lion perishes for lack of prey, And the cubs of the lioness are scattered.

column.name: text
column.value: “Now a word was brought to me secretly, And my ear received a whisper of it.

column.name: text
column.value: Amid disquieting thoughts from visions of the night, When deep sleep falls on people,

column.name: text

text
column.value: ‘Can mankind be righteous ①before God? Can a man be pure ②before his Maker? ▷ ①Lit from ②Lit from

column.value: He puts no trust even in His servants; And He accuses His angels of error.

column.name: text
column.value: How much more those who live in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust, Who are crushed before the moth!

column.name: text
column.value: Between morning and evening they are broken in pieces; Unregarded, they perish forever.

column.name: text
column.value: Is their tent-cord not pulled out within them? They die, yet without wisdom.’

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job responded,

column.name: text
column.value: “Oh if only my grief were actually weighed And laid in the balances together with my disaster!

column.name: text
column.value: For then it would be heavier than the sand of the seas; For that reason my words have been rash.

column.name: text
column.value: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me, ①My spirit drinks their poison; The terrors of God line up against me. ▷ ①Lit Whose poison my spirit drinks

column.name: text
column.value: Does the wild donkey bray over his grass, Or does the ox low over his feed?

column.name: text
column.value: Can something tasteless be eaten without salt, Or is there any taste in the ①juice of an alkanet plant? ▷ ①Heb hallamuth, meaning uncertain

column.name: text
column.value: My soul refuses to touch them; They are like loathsome food to me.

column.name: text
column.value: “Oh, that my request might come to pass, And that God would grant my hope!

column.name: text
column.value: Oh, that God would decide to crush me, That He would let loose His hand and cut me off!

column.name: text
column.value: But it is still my comfort, And I rejoice in unsparing pain, That I have not ①denied the words of the Holy One. ▷ ①Lit hidden

column.name: text
column.value: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should ①endure? ▷ ①Lit prolong my soul

column.name: text
column.value: Is my strength the strength of stones, Or is my flesh bronze?

column.name: text
column.value: Is it that my help is not within me, And that a good outcome is driven away from me?

column.name: text
text
column.value: My brothers have acted deceitfully like a ①wadi, Like the torrents of ②wadis which drain away, ▷ ①I.e., dry stream bed(s), except in the rainy season ②I.e., dry stream bed(s), except in the rainy season

column.name: text
column.value: Which are darkened because of ice, And into which the snow ①melts. ▷ ①Lit hides itself

column.name: text

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: The caravans of Tema looked, The travelers of Sheba hoped for them.

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, you have now become such, You see terrors and are afraid.

column.name: text
column.value: Have I said, ‘Give me something,’ Or, ‘Offer a bribe for me from your wealth,’

column.name: text
column.value: Or, ‘Save me from the hand of the enemy,’ Or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the tyrants’?

column.name: text
column.value: “Teach me, and I will be silent; And show me how I have done wrong.

column.name: text
column.value: How painful are honest words! But what does your argument prove?

column.name: text
column.value: Do you intend to rebuke my words, When the words of one in despair belong to the wind?

column.name: text
column.value: You would even cast lots for the orphans, And barter over your friend.

column.name: text
column.value: Now please look at me, And see if I am lying to your face.

column.name: text
column.value: Please turn away, let there be no injustice; Turn away, my righteousness is still in it.

column.name: text
column.value: Is there injustice on my tongue? Does my palate not discern disasters?

column.name: text
column.value: There was a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job; and that man was blameless, upright, fearing God and turning away from evil.

column.name: text
column.value: Seven sons and three daughters were born to him.

column.name: text
column.value: His possessions were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and very many servants; and that man was the greatest of all the ①men of the east. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: His sons used to go and hold a feast in the house of each one on his day, and they would send word and invite their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

column.name: text
column.value: When the days of feasting had completed their cycle, Job would send word to them and consecrate them, getting up early in the morning and offering burnt offerings according to the number of them all; for Job said, “Perhaps my sons have sinned and cursed God in their hearts.” Job did so continually.

column.name: text
column.value: Now there was a day when the ①sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and ②Satan also came among them. ▷ ①I.e., prob. angels ②Heb ha-satan; i.e., the adversary, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: Then Satan answered the ①LORD, “Does Job fear God for nothing? ▷ ①Lit LORD and said

column.name: text
column.value: Have You not made a fence around him and his house and all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the work of his hands, and his possessions have increased in the land.

column.name: text
column.value: But reach out with Your hand now and touch all that he has; he will certainly curse You to Your face.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the LORD said to Satan, “Behold, all that he has is in your ①power; only do not reach out and put your hand on him.” So Satan departed from the presence of the LORD. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, another came and said, “The fire of God fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and the servants and consumed them, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, another came and said, “The Chaldeans formed three units and made a raid on the camels and took them, and ①killed the servants with the edge of the sword, and I alone have escaped to tell you.” ▷ ①Lit struck

column.name: text
column.value: While he was still speaking, another also came and said, “Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in their oldest brother’s house,

column.name: text
column.value: and behold, a great wind came from across the wilderness and struck the four corners of the house, and it fell on the young people and they died, and I alone have escaped to tell you.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job got up, tore his robe, and shaved his head; then he fell to the ground and worshiped.

column.name: text
column.value: He said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, And naked I shall return there. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the name of the LORD.”

column.name: text
column.value: Despite all this, Job did not sin, nor did he ①blame God. ▷ ①Lit ascribe unseemliness to

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: For ①what I fear comes upon me, And what I dread ②encounters me. ▷ ①Lit I fear a fear, and it comes ②Lit comes to me

column.value: I am not at ease, nor am I quiet, And I am not at rest, but turmoil comes.”

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①Is a person not forced to labor on earth, And are his days not like the days of a hired worker? ▷ ①Lit Has not man compulsory labor

column.name: text
column.value: As a slave pants for the shade, And as a hired worker who eagerly waits for his wages,

column.name: text
column.value: So I am allotted worthless months, And nights of trouble are apportioned to me.

column.name: text
column.value: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise?’ But the night continues, And I am continually tossing until dawn.

column.name: text

column.value: He will not return to his house again, Nor will his place know about him anymore.

column.name: text
text

column.name: text
column.value: I ①waste away; I will not live forever. Leave me alone, for my days are only a breath. ▷ ①Or loathe

column.name: text
column.value: “Please inquire of past generations, And consider the things searched out by their fathers.

column.name: text
column.value: For we are only of yesterday and know nothing, Because our days on earth are as a shadow.

column.name: text
column.value: Will they not teach you and tell you, And bring forth words from their minds?

column.value: “Can papyrus grow tall without a marsh? Can the rushes grow without water?

column.name: text
column.value: While it is still green and not cut down, Yet it withers before any other ①plant. ▷ ①Lit reed

column.name: text
column.value: So are the paths of all who forget God; And the hope of the godless will perish,

column.name: text

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: “In truth I know that this is so; But how can a person be in the right with God?

column.value: If one wished to dispute with Him, He could not answer Him once in a thousand times.

column.name: text
column.value: Wise in heart and mighty in strength, Who has ①defied Him ②without harm? ▷ ①Lit stiffened his neck against ②Lit and remained safe

column.name: text
column.value: It is God who removes the mountains, and they do not know how, When He overturns them in His anger.

column.name: text

text
text

column.name: text
column.value: If He were to pass by me, I would not see Him; Were He to move past me, I would not perceive Him.

column.value: If He were to snatch away, who could restrain Him? Who could say to Him, ‘What are You doing?’

column.name: text
text
column.value: How then can I ①answer Him, And choose my words ②before Him? ▷ ①Or plead my case ②Lit with

column.value: If I called and He answered me, I could not believe that He was listening to my voice.

column.value: For He bruises me with a storm And multiplies my wounds without cause.

column.name: text
column.value: He will not allow me to get my breath, But He saturates me with bitterness.

column.name: text
column.value: If it is a matter of power, behold, He is the strong one! And if it is a matter of justice, who can summon ①Him? ▷ ①As in LXX; Heb me

column.name: text
column.value: Though I am righteous, my mouth will condemn me; Though I am guiltless, He will declare me guilty.

column.name: text
text

column.name: text
column.value: If the whip kills suddenly, He mocks the despair of the innocent.

column.name: text
text
column.value: “Now my days are swifter than a runner; They flee away, they see no good.

column.name: text
column.value: They slip by like reed boats, Like an eagle that swoops on ①its prey. ▷ ①Lit food

column.name: text
column.value: Though I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will ①put my face in order and be cheerful,’ ▷ ①I.e., improve the look

column.name: text
text
column.value: Yet You have concealed these things in Your heart; I know that this is within You:

column.name: text
column.value: If I have sinned, You will take note of me, And will not acquit me of my guilt.

column.name: text
column.value: If I am wicked, woe to me! But if I am righteous, I dare not lift up my head. I am full of shame, and ①conscious of my misery. ▷ ①Lit see

column.name: text
column.value: And should my head be high, You would hunt me like a lion; And You would show Your power against me again.

column.name: text
column.value: You renew Your witnesses against me And increase Your anger toward me; ①Hardship after hardship is with me. ▷ ①Lit Changes and warfare are with me

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Why then did You bring me out of the womb? If only I had died and no eye had seen me!

column.name: text
column.value: I should have been as though I had not been, Brought from womb to tomb.’

column.name: text
column.value: Would He not leave my few days alone? ①Withdraw from me so that I may have a little cheerfulness ▷ ①Lit Put

column.name: text
column.value: Before I go—and I shall not return— To the land of darkness and deep shadow,

column.name: text
column.value: The land of utter gloom like darkness itself, Of deep shadow without order, And it shines like darkness.”

column.name: text
column.value: “Call now, is there anyone who will answer you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?

column.name: text
column.value: For irritation kills the fool, And jealousy brings death to the simple.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen the fool taking root, And I cursed his home immediately.

column.name: text
column.value: His sons are far from safety, They are also ①oppressed at the gate, And there is no one to save them. ▷ ①Lit crushed

column.name: text
column.value: ①The hungry devour his harvest And take it to a place of thorns, And the ②schemer is eager for their wealth. ▷ ①Lit Whose harvest the hungry devour ②Ancient versions thirsty

column.name: text
column.value: For disaster does not come from the dust, Nor does trouble sprout from the ground,

column.name: text
column.value: For man is born for trouble, As sparks fly upward.

column.name: text
column.value: “But as for me, I would seek God, And I would make my plea before God,

column.name: text
column.value: Who does great and unsearchable things, ①Wonders without number. ▷ ①Or Miracles

column.name: text
column.value: He gives rain on the earth, And sends water on the fields,

column.name: text
column.value: So that He sets on high those who are lowly, And those who mourn are lifted to safety.

column.name: text
column.value: He frustrates the schemes of the shrewd, So that their hands cannot attain success.

column.name: text
column.value: He captures the wise by their own cleverness, And the advice of the cunning is quickly thwarted.

column.name: text
column.value: By day they meet with darkness, And grope at noon as in the night.

column.name: text
column.value: But He saves from the sword of their mouth, And the poor from the hand of the strong.

column.name: text
column.value: So the helpless has hope, And injustice has shut its mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: “Behold, happy is the person whom God disciplines, So do not reject the discipline of ①the Almighty. ▷ ①Heb Shaddai, and so throughout ch 6

column.name: text
text
column.value: In six troubles He will save you; Even in seven, evil will not touch you.

column.name: text
column.value: In famine He will redeem you from death, And in war, from the power of the sword.

column.name: text
column.value: You will be hidden ①from the scourge of the tongue, And you will not be afraid of violence when it comes. ▷ ①Lit at

column.name: text
column.value: You will laugh at violence and hunger, And you will not be afraid of ①wild animals. ▷ ①Lit animals of the earth

column.name: text
column.value: For you will be in league with the stones of the field, And the animals of the field will be at peace with you.

column.name: text
column.value: You will know that your tent is secure, For you will visit your home and ①have nothing missing. ▷ ①Lit not miss

column.name: text
column.value: You will also know that your ①descendants will be many, And your offspring as the grass of the earth. ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: You will come to the grave at a ripe age, Like the stacking of grain in its season.

column.name: text
column.value: Behold this; we have investigated it, and so it is. Hear it, and know for yourself.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Job responded,

column.name: text
column.value: “Truly then you are the people, And with you wisdom will die!

column.name: text
column.value: But I have intelligence as well as you; I am not inferior to you. And ①who does not know such things as these? ▷ ①Lit with whom is there not like these?

column.name: text
column.value: I am a joke to ①my friends, The one who called on God and He answered him; The just and blameless man is a joke. ▷ ①Lit his

column.name: text
column.value: ①He who is at ease holds disaster in contempt, As prepared for those whose feet slip. ▷ ①Lit Contempt for calamity is the thought of him who is at ease

column.name: text
column.value: The tents of the destroyers prosper, And those who provoke God are secure, ①Whom God brings into their power. ▷ ①Or He who brings God into his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: “But just ask the animals, and have them teach you; And the birds of the sky, and have them tell you.

column.name: text
column.value: Or speak to the earth, and have it teach you; And have the fish of the sea tell you.

column.name: text
column.value: Who among all these does not know That the hand of the LORD has done this,

column.name: text
column.value: In whose hand is the life of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?

column.name: text
column.value: Does the ear not put words to the test, As the palate ①tastes its food? ▷ ①Lit tastes food for itself

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom is with the aged, And with ①long life comes understanding. ▷ ①Lit length of days

column.name: text
column.value: “Wisdom and might are with Him; Advice and understanding belong to Him.

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: Strength and sound wisdom are with Him. One who goes astray and one who leads astray belong to Him.

column.name: text
column.value: He makes advisers walk ①barefoot And makes fools of judges. ▷ ①Or stripped

column.name: text
column.value: He undoes the binding of kings, And ties a loincloth around their waist.

column.name: text
column.value: He makes priests walk ①barefoot, And overthrows the secure ones. ▷ ①Or stripped

column.name: text
