column.value: The wicked flee when no one is pursuing, But the righteous are ①bold as a lion. ▷ ①Lit confident

column.name: text
column.value: Due to a ①wrongdoing of ②a land its leaders are many, But by a person of understanding and knowledge, so it endures. ▷ ①Or rebellion ②I.e., the people of a land

column.name: text
column.value: A poor man who oppresses the helpless Is like a driving rain ①which leaves no food. ▷ ①Lit and there is no bread

column.name: text
column.value: Those who abandon the Law praise the wicked, But those who keep the Law strive against them.

column.name: text
column.value: Evil people do not understand justice, But those who seek the LORD understand everything.

column.name: text
column.value: Better is a poor person who walks in his integrity, Than a person who is ①crooked, though he is rich. ▷ ①Lit perverse of two ways

column.name: text
column.value: He who keeps the Law is a discerning son, But he who is a companion of gluttons humiliates his father.

column.name: text
column.value: One who increases his wealth by ①interest of any kind, Collects it for one who is gracious to the poor. ▷ ①Possibly interest on money and food loans

column.name: text
column.value: One who turns his ear away from listening to the Law, Even his prayer is an abomination.

column.name: text
column.value: One who leads the upright astray in an evil way Will himself fall into his own pit, But the blameless will inherit good.

column.name: text
column.value: The rich person is wise in his own eyes, But the poor who has understanding ①sees through him. ▷ ①Lit examines him

column.name: text
column.value: When the righteous triumph, there is great glory, But when the wicked rise, people ①hide themselves. ▷ ①Lit will be searched for

column.name: text
column.value: One who conceals his wrongdoings will not prosper, But one who confesses and abandons them will find compassion.

column.name: text
column.value: How blessed is the person who fears always, But one who hardens his heart will fall into disaster.

column.name: text
column.value: Like a roaring lion and a rushing bear Is a wicked ruler over a poor people.

column.name: text
column.value: A leader who is a great oppressor lacks understanding, But a person who hates unjust gain will prolong his days.

column.name: text
column.value: A person who is burdened with the guilt of human blood Will ①be a fugitive until death; no one is to support him! ▷ ①Lit flee to the pit

column.name: text
column.value: One who walks blamelessly will receive help, But one who is ①crooked will fall all at once. ▷ ①Lit perverse of two ways

column.name: text
column.value: One who works his land will have plenty of food, But one who follows empty pursuits will have plenty of poverty.

column.name: text
column.value: A faithful person will abound with blessings, But one who hurries to be rich will not go unpunished.

column.name: text
column.value: To ①show partiality is not good, Because for a piece of bread a man will do wrong. ▷ ①Lit regard the face

column.name: text
column.value: A person with an evil eye hurries after wealth And does not know that poverty will come upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: One who rebukes a person will afterward find more favor Than one who flatters with the tongue.

column.name: text
column.value: He who robs his father or his mother And says, “There is no wrong done,” Is the companion of a person who destroys.

column.name: text
column.value: An ①arrogant person stirs up strife, But one who trusts in the LORD will ②prosper. ▷ ①Lit broad soul ②Lit be made fat

column.name: text
column.value: One who trusts in his own heart is a fool, But one who walks wisely will flee to safety.

column.name: text
column.value: One who gives to the poor will never lack anything, But one who ①shuts his eyes will have many curses. ▷ ①Lit hides

column.name: text
column.value: When the wicked rise, people hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase.

column.name: text
column.value: A person ①often rebuked who ②becomes obstinate Will suddenly be broken ③beyond remedy. ▷ ①Lit of rebukes who ②Lit hardens his neck ③Lit and there is no remedy

column.name: text
column.value: When the righteous ①increase, the people rejoice, But when a wicked person rules, people groan. ▷ ①Or become great

column.name: text
column.value: A man who loves wisdom makes his father glad, But he who involves himself with prostitutes wastes his wealth.

column.name: text
column.value: The king gives stability to the land by justice, But a person who takes bribes ruins it.

column.name: text
column.value: A man who flatters his neighbor Is spreading a net for his steps.

column.name: text
column.value: By wrongdoing an evil person is ensnared, But the righteous sings and rejoices.

column.name: text
text
column.value: Arrogant people inflame a city, But wise people turn away anger.

column.name: text
column.value: When a wise person has a controversy with a foolish person, ①The foolish person either rages or laughs, and there is no rest. ▷ ①Lit He

column.name: text
column.value: People of bloodshed hate the blameless person, But the upright ①are concerned for his life. ▷ ①Lit seek his soul

column.name: text
column.value: A fool ①always loses his temper, But a wise person holds it back. ▷ ①Lit sends forth all his spirit

column.name: text
column.value: If a ruler pays attention to falsehood, All his ministers become wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: The poor person and the oppressor ①have this in common: The LORD gives light to the eyes of both. ▷ ①Lit meet together

column.name: text
column.value: If a king judges the poor with truth, His throne will be established forever.

column.name: text
column.value: The rod and a rebuke give wisdom, But a child ①who gets his own way brings shame to his mother. ▷ ①Lit left to himself

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: Where there is no ①vision, the people are unrestrained, But happy is one who keeps the Law. ▷ ①Or revelation

column.name: text
column.value: A slave will not be instructed by words alone; For though he understands, there will be no response.

column.name: text
column.value: Do you see a person who is hasty with his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.

column.name: text
column.value: One who pampers his slave from childhood Will in the end find him to be rebellious.

column.name: text
column.value: An angry person stirs up strife, And a hot-tempered person abounds in wrongdoing.

column.name: text
column.value: A person’s pride will bring him low, But a humble spirit will obtain honor.

column.name: text
column.value: One who is a partner with a thief hates his own life; He hears the oath but tells nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: The fear of man ①brings a snare, But one who trusts in the LORD will be protected. ▷ ①Lit gives

column.name: text
column.value: Many seek the ruler’s ①favor, But justice for mankind comes from the LORD. ▷ ①Lit face

column.name: text
column.value: An unjust person is an abomination to the righteous, And one who is upright in the way is an abomination to the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh, the pronouncement. The man declares to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:

column.name: text
column.value: I am certainly more stupid than any man, And I do not have the understanding of a man;

column.name: text
column.value: Nor have I learned wisdom, Nor do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.

column.name: text
column.value: Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has gathered the wind in His fists? Who has wrapped the waters in ①His garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is His name or His ②Son’s name? Surely you know! ▷ ①Lit the ②Or son’s

column.name: text
text
column.value: Do not add to His words Or He will rebuke you, and you will be proved a liar.

column.name: text
column.value: Two things I have asked of You; Do not refuse me before I die:

column.name: text
column.value: Keep deception and ①lies far from me, Give me neither poverty nor riches; Feed me with the food that is my portion, ▷ ①Lit words of falsehood

column.name: text
column.value: So that I will not be full and deny You and say, “Who is the LORD?” And that I will not become impoverished and steal, And profane the name of my God.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not slander a slave to his master, Or he will curse you and you will be found guilty.

column.name: text
column.value: There is a ①kind of person who curses his father And does not bless his mother. ▷ ①Or generation

column.name: text
column.value: There is a ①kind who is pure in his own eyes, Yet is not washed from his filthiness. ▷ ①Or generation

column.name: text
column.value: There is a ①kind—oh how lofty are his eyes! And his eyelids are raised in arrogance. ▷ ①Or generation

column.name: text
column.value: There is a ①kind of person whose teeth are like swords And his jaw teeth like knives, To devour the poor from the earth And the needy from among mankind. ▷ ①Or generation

column.name: text
column.value: The leech has two daughters: “Give” and “Give.” There are three things that will not be satisfied, Four that will not say, “Enough”:

column.name: text
column.value: ①Sheol, the infertile womb, Earth that is never satisfied with water, And fire that never says, “Enough.” ▷ ①I.e., The netherworld

column.name: text
column.value: The eye that mocks a father And ①scorns a mother, The ravens of the valley will pick it out, And the young eagles will eat it. ▷ ①Lit despises to obey

column.name: text
column.value: There are three things which are too wonderful for me, Four which I do not understand:

column.name: text
column.value: The way of the eagle in the sky, The way of a snake on a rock, The way of a ship in the middle of the sea, And the way of a man with a ①virgin. ▷ ①Lit young unmarried woman

column.name: text
column.value: This is the way of an adulterous woman: She eats and wipes her mouth, And says, “I have done no wrong.”

column.name: text
column.value: Under three things the earth quakes, And under four, it cannot endure:

column.name: text
column.value: Under a slave when he becomes king, And a fool when he is satisfied with food,

column.name: text
column.value: Under an unloved woman when she gets a husband, And a female servant when she dispossesses her mistress.

column.name: text
column.value: Four things are small on the earth, But they are exceedingly wise:

column.name: text
column.value: The ants are not a strong people, But they prepare their food in the summer;

column.name: text
column.value: The rock hyraxes are not a mighty people, Yet they make their houses in the rocks;

column.name: text
column.value: The locusts have no king, Yet all of them go out in ranks;

column.name: text
column.value: The lizard you may grasp with the hands, Yet it is in kings’ palaces.

column.name: text
column.value: There are three things which are stately in their march, Even four which are stately when they walk:

column.name: text
column.value: The lion, which is mighty among animals And does not ①retreat from anything, ▷ ①Lit turn back

column.name: text
column.value: The ①strutting rooster or the male goat, And a king when his army is with him. ▷ ①Lit girt in the loins

column.name: text
column.value: If you have been foolish in exalting yourself, Or if you have plotted evil, put your hand on your mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: For the ①churning of milk produces butter, And pressing the nose produces blood; So the ②churning of anger produces strife. ▷ ①Lit pressing ②Lit pressing

column.name: text
column.value: The words of King Lemuel, the pronouncement which his mother taught him:

column.name: text
column.value: What, my son? And what, son of my womb? And what, son of my vows?

column.name: text
column.value: Do not give your strength to women, Or your ways to that which destroys kings.

column.name: text
column.value: It is not for kings, Lemuel, It is not for kings to drink wine, Or for rulers to desire intoxicating drink,

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise they will drink and forget what is decreed, And pervert the ①rights of all the ②needy. ▷ ①Lit judgment ②Lit sons of affliction

column.name: text
column.value: Give intoxicating drink to one who is perishing, And wine to one ①whose life is bitter. ▷ ①Lit bitter of soul

column.name: text
column.value: Let him drink and forget his poverty, And remember his trouble no more.

column.name: text
column.value: Open your mouth for the people who cannot speak, For the ①rights of all the ②unfortunate. ▷ ①Lit judgment ②Lit sons of passing away

column.name: text
column.value: Open your mouth, judge righteously, And ①defend the rights of the poor and needy. ▷ ①Lit judge the afflicted

column.name: text
column.value: An excellent wife, who can find her? For her worth is far above jewels.

column.name: text
column.value: The heart of her husband trusts in her, And he will have no lack of gain.

column.name: text
column.value: She does him good and not evil All the days of her life.

column.name: text
column.value: She looks for wool and linen, And works with her ①hands ②in delight. ▷ ①Lit palms ②Or willingly

column.name: text
column.value: She is like merchant ships; She brings her food from afar.

column.name: text
column.value: And she rises while it is still night And gives food to her household, And ①portions to her attendants. ▷ ①Or prescribed tasks

column.name: text
text
column.value: She surrounds her waist with strength And makes her arms strong.

column.name: text
column.value: She senses that her profit is good; Her lamp does not go out at night.

column.name: text
column.value: She stretches out her hands to the ①distaff, And her ②hands grasp the spindle. ▷ ①I.e., the staff that holds the textile fibers for spinning ②Lit palms

column.name: text
column.value: She ①extends her hand to the poor, And she stretches out her hands to the needy. ▷ ①Lit spreads out her palm

column.name: text
column.value: She is not afraid of the snow for her household, For all her household are clothed with scarlet.

column.name: text
column.value: She makes coverings for herself; Her clothing is fine linen and purple.

column.name: text
column.value: Her husband is known in the gates, When he sits among the elders of the land.

column.name: text
column.value: She makes linen garments and sells them, And ①supplies belts to the ②tradesmen. ▷ ①Lit gives ②Lit Canaanite

column.name: text
column.value: Strength and dignity are her clothing, And she smiles at the ①future. ▷ ①Lit latter days

column.name: text
column.value: She opens her mouth in wisdom, And the ①teaching of kindness is on her tongue. ▷ ①Or law

column.name: text
column.value: She watches over the activities of her household, And does not eat the bread of idleness.

column.name: text
column.value: Her children rise up and bless her; Her husband also, and he praises her, saying:

column.name: text
column.value: “Many daughters have done nobly, But you excel them all.”

column.name: text
column.value: Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, But a woman who ①fears the LORD, she shall be praised. ▷ ①Or reveres

column.name: text
column.value: Give her the ①product of her hands, And let her works praise her in the gates. ▷ ①Lit fruit

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: “Futility of futilities,” says the Preacher, “Futility of futilities! All is futility.”

column.name: text
column.value: What advantage does a person have in all his work Which he does under the sun?

column.name: text
column.value: A generation goes and a generation comes, But the earth ①remains forever. ▷ ①Lit stands

column.name: text
text
column.value: ①Blowing toward the south, Then turning toward the north, The wind continues ②swirling along; And on its circular courses the wind returns. ▷ ①Lit Going ②Lit turning

column.name: text
column.value: All the rivers ①flow into the sea, Yet the sea is not full. To the place where the rivers ②flow, There they ③flow again. ▷ ①Lit go ②Lit go ③Lit go

column.name: text
column.value: All things are wearisome; No one can tell it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, Nor is the ear filled with hearing.

column.name: text
column.value: What has been, it is what will be, And what has been done, it is what will be done. So there is nothing new under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Is there anything of which one might say, “See this, it is new”? It has already existed for ages Which were before us.

column.name: text
column.value: There is no remembrance of the ①earlier things, And of the later things as well, which will occur, There will be no remembrance of them Among those who will come later still. ▷ ①Lit first; or former

column.name: text
column.value: I, the Preacher, have been king over Israel in Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: And I set my ①mind to seek and explore by wisdom about everything that has been done under heaven. It is a ②sorry task with which God has given the sons of mankind to be troubled. ▷ ①Lit evil ②Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen all the works which have been done under the sun, and behold, all is futility and striving after wind.

column.name: text
column.value: What is crooked cannot be straightened, and what is lacking cannot be counted.

column.name: text
column.value: I ①said to myself, “Behold, I have magnified and increased wisdom more than all who were over Jerusalem before me; and my ②mind has observed ③a wealth of wisdom and knowledge.” ▷ ①Lit spoke with my heart, saying ②Lit heart ③Lit an abundance

column.name: text
column.value: And I applied my ①mind to know wisdom and to know insanity and foolishness; I realized that this also is striving after wind. ▷ ①Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: Because in much wisdom there is much grief; and increasing knowledge results in increasing pain.

column.name: text
column.value: There is an appointed time for everything. And there is a time for every matter under heaven—

column.name: text
column.value: A time to give birth and a time to die; A time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to kill and a time to heal; A time to tear down and a time to build up.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to weep and a time to laugh; A time to mourn and a time to dance.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; A time to embrace and a time to shun embracing.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to search and a time to give up as lost; A time to keep and a time to throw away.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to tear apart and a time to sew together; A time to be silent and a time to speak.

column.name: text
column.value: A time to love and a time to hate; A time for war and a time for peace.

column.name: text
column.value: What benefit is there for the worker from that in which he labors?

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen the task which God has given the sons of mankind with which to ①occupy themselves. ▷ ①Or trouble

column.name: text
column.value: He has made everything appropriate in its time. He has also set eternity in their heart, without the possibility that mankind will find out the work which God has done from the beginning even to the end.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good in one’s lifetime;

column.name: text
column.value: moreover, that every person who eats and drinks sees good in all his labor—this is the gift of God.

column.name: text
column.value: I know that everything God does will remain forever; there is nothing to add to it and there is nothing to take from it. And God has so worked, that people will ①fear Him. ▷ ①Or be in awe before Him

column.name: text
column.value: That which is, is what has already been, and that which will be has already been; and God ①seeks what has passed by. ▷ ①Or finds

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, I have seen under the sun that in the place of justice there is wickedness and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.

column.name: text
column.value: I said ①to myself, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked,” for a time for every matter and for every deed ②is there. ▷ ①Lit in my heart ②I.e., exists with God

column.name: text
column.value: I said ①to myself regarding the sons of mankind, “God is testing them in order for them to see that they are as animals, they to themselves.” ▷ ①Lit in my heart

column.name: text
column.value: For the fate of the sons of mankind and the fate of animals ①is the same. As one dies, so dies the other; indeed, they all have the same breath, and there is no advantage for mankind over animals, for all is futility. ▷ ①Lit and they have one fate

column.name: text
column.value: All go to the same place. All came from the dust and all return to the dust.

column.name: text
column.value: Who knows that the spirit of the sons of mankind ascends upward and the spirit of the animal descends downward to the earth?

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen that nothing is better than when a person is happy in his activities, for that is his ①lot. For who will bring him to see what will occur after him? ▷ ①Or reward

column.name: text
column.value: I said ①to myself, “Come now, I will test you with pleasure. So ②enjoy yourself.” And behold, it too was futility. ▷ ①Lit in my heart ②Lit consider with goodness

column.name: text
column.value: I said of laughter, “It is senseless,” and of pleasure, “What does this accomplish?”

column.name: text
column.value: I explored with my ①mind how to refresh my body with wine while my ②mind was guiding me wisely; and how to seize foolishness, until I could see what good there is for the sons of mankind ③to do under heaven for the few ④years of their lives. ▷ ①Lit heart ②Lit heart ③Lit which they do ④Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: I enlarged my works: I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself;

column.name: text
column.value: I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted in them all kinds of fruit trees;

column.name: text
column.value: I made ponds of water for myself from which to irrigate a forest of growing trees.

column.name: text
column.value: I bought male and female slaves, and I had ①slaves born at home. I also possessed flocks and herds larger than all who preceded me in Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit sons

column.name: text
column.value: I also amassed for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I provided for myself male and female singers, and the pleasures of the sons of mankind: many concubines.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I became great and increased more than all who preceded me in Jerusalem. My wisdom also stood by me.

column.name: text
column.value: All that my eyes desired, I did not refuse them. I did not restrain my heart from any pleasure, for my heart was pleased because of all my labor; and this was my reward for all my labor.

column.name: text
column.value: So I considered all my activities which my hands had done and the labor which I had ①exerted, and behold, all was futility and striving after wind, and there was no benefit under the sun. ▷ ①Lit labored to do

column.name: text
column.value: So I turned to consider wisdom, insanity, and foolishness; for what will the man do who will come after the king, except what has already been done?

column.name: text
column.value: Then I saw that wisdom surpasses foolishness as light surpasses darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: The wise person’s eyes are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. And yet I know that one and the same fate happens to ①both of them. ▷ ①Lit all of

column.name: text
column.value: Then I said ①to myself, “As is the fate of the fool, it will also happen to me. Why then have I been extremely wise?” So ②I said to myself, “This too is futility.” ▷ ①Lit in my heart ②Lit I spoke in my heart

column.name: text
column.value: For there is no ①lasting remembrance of the wise, along with the fool, since in the coming days everything will ②soon be forgotten. And how the wise and the fool alike die! ▷ ①Lit forever ②Lit already

column.name: text
column.value: So I hated life, for the work which had been done under the sun was ①unhappy to me; because everything is futility and striving after wind. ▷ ①Lit evil

column.name: text
column.value: So I hated all the fruit of my labor for which I had labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.

column.name: text
column.value: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will have control over all the fruit of my labor for which I have labored by acting wisely under the sun. This too is futility.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I ①completely despaired over all the fruit of my labor for which I had labored under the sun. ▷ ①Lit turned aside my heart to despair

column.name: text
column.value: When there is a person who has labored with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, and then gives his ①legacy to one who has not labored for it; this too is futility and a great evil. ▷ ①Lit share

column.name: text
column.value: For what does a person get in all his labor and in ①his striving with which he labors under the sun? ▷ ①Lit the striving of his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Because all his days his activity is painful and irritating; even at night his ①mind does not rest. This too is futility. ▷ ①Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: There is nothing better for a person than to eat and drink, and show ①himself some good in his trouble. This too I have seen, that it is from the hand of God. ▷ ①Lit his soul

column.name: text
column.value: For who can eat and who can have enjoyment without ①Him? ▷ ①As in LXX; Heb me

column.name: text
column.value: For to a person who is good in His sight, He has given wisdom and knowledge and joy, while to the sinner He has given the task of gathering and collecting so that he may give to one who is good in God’s sight. This too is futility and striving after wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I looked again at all the acts of oppression which were being done under the sun. And behold, I saw the tears of the oppressed and that they had no one to comfort them; and power was on the side of their oppressors, but they had no one to comfort them.

column.name: text
column.value: So I congratulated the dead who are already dead, more than the living who are still living.

column.name: text
column.value: But better off than both of them is the one who has never existed, who has never seen the evil activity that is done under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen that every labor and every skill which is done is the result of rivalry between a person and his neighbor. This too is futility and striving after wind.

column.name: text
column.value: The fool folds his hands and consumes his own flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: One hand full of rest is better than two fists full of labor and striving after wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I looked again at futility under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: There was a man without a ①dependent, having neither a son nor a brother, yet there was no end to all his labor. Indeed, his eyes were not satisfied with riches, and he never asked, “And for whom do I labor and deprive myself of pleasure?” This too is futility, and it is an unhappy task. ▷ ①Lit second

column.name: text
column.value: Two are better than one because they have a good return for their labor;

column.name: text
column.value: for if ①either of them falls, the one will lift up his companion. But woe to the one who falls when there is not ②another to lift him up! ▷ ①Lit they fall ②Lit a second

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, if two lie down together they ①keep warm, but how can one be warm alone? ▷ ①Lit have warmth

column.name: text
column.value: And if ①one can overpower him who is alone, two can resist him. A cord of three strands is not quickly torn apart. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: A poor yet wise youth is better than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to receive ①instruction— ▷ ①Or warning

column.name: text
column.value: for he has come out of prison to become king, even though he was born poor in his kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen all those living under the sun move to the side of the second youth who ①replaces him. ▷ ①Lit stands in his place

column.name: text
column.value: There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them. Even the ones who will come later will not be happy with him; for this too is futility and striving after wind.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Do not be quick with your mouth or ②impulsive in thought to bring up a matter in the presence of God. For God is in heaven and you are on the earth; therefore let your words be few. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: in Heb ②Lit hurry your heart

column.name: text
column.value: For the dream comes through much ①effort, and the voice of a fool through many words. ▷ ①Lit task

column.name: text
column.value: When you make a vow to God, do not be late in paying it; for He takes no delight in fools. Pay what you vow!

column.name: text
column.value: It is better that you not vow, than vow and not pay.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not let your ①speech cause ②you to sin, and do not say in the presence of the messenger of God that it was a mistake. Why should God be angry on account of your voice, and destroy the work of your hands? ▷ ①Lit mouth ②Lit your body

column.name: text
column.value: For in many dreams and in many words there is futility. Rather, ①fear God. ▷ ①Or revere

column.name: text
column.value: If you see oppression of the poor and denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be shocked at the ①sight; for one ②official watches over another ③official, and there are higher ④officials over them. ▷ ①Lit delight ②Lit high one ③Lit high one ④Lit ones

column.name: text
column.value: After all, a king who cultivates the field is beneficial to the land.

column.name: text
column.value: One who loves money will not be satisfied with money, nor one who loves abundance with its income. This too is futility.

column.name: text
column.value: When good things increase, those who consume them increase. So what is the advantage to their owners except to ①look at them? ▷ ①Lit see with their eyes

column.name: text
column.value: The sleep of the laborer is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the ①full stomach of the rich person does not allow him to sleep. ▷ ①Lit satiety

column.name: text
column.value: There is a sickening evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth being ①hoarded by its owner to his detriment. ▷ ①Lit guarded

column.name: text
column.value: When that wealth was lost through bad business and he had fathered a son, then there was nothing ①to support him. ▷ ①Lit in his hand

column.name: text
column.value: As he came naked from his mother’s womb, so he will return as he came. He will take nothing from the fruit of his labor that he can carry in his hand.

column.name: text
column.value: This also is a sickening evil: exactly as a person ①is born, so will he ②die. What then is the advantage for him who labors for the wind? ▷ ①Lit comes ②Lit go

column.name: text
column.value: All his life he also eats in darkness with great irritation, sickness, and anger.

column.name: text
column.value: Here is what I have seen to be good and ①fitting: to eat, to drink, and ②enjoy oneself in all one’s labor in which he labors under the sun during the few ③years of his life which God has given him; for this is his ④reward. ▷ ①Lit beautiful ②Lit see good ③Or days ④Or share

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, as for every person to whom God has given riches and wealth, He has also given him the opportunity to ①enjoy them and to receive his ②reward and rejoice in his labor; this is the gift of God. ▷ ①Lit eat from it ②Or share

column.name: text
column.value: For he will not often call to mind the ①years of his life, because God keeps ②him busy with the joy of his heart. ▷ ①Or days ②As in LXX

column.name: text
column.value: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is widespread ①among mankind: ▷ ①Lit upon

column.name: text
column.value: a person to whom God has given riches, wealth, and honor, so that his soul lacks nothing of all that he desires, yet God has not given him the opportunity to ①enjoy these things, but a foreigner ②enjoys them. This is futility and a severe affliction. ▷ ①Lit eat from it ②Lit eats it

column.name: text
column.value: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years, however many ①they may be, but his soul is not satisfied with good things and he does not even have a proper burial, then I say, “Better the miscarriage than he, ▷ ①Lit the days of his years

column.name: text
column.value: for a miscarriage comes in futility and goes into darkness; and its name is covered in darkness.

column.name: text
column.value: It has not even seen the sun nor does it know it; yet ①it is better off than that man. ▷ ①Lit more rest has this one than that

column.name: text
column.value: Even if the man lives a thousand years twice, but does not see good things—do not all go to one and the same place?”

column.name: text
column.value: All a person’s labor is for his mouth, and yet ①his appetite is not ②satisfied. ▷ ①Lit the soul ②Lit filled

column.name: text
column.value: For what advantage does the wise person have over the fool? What does the poor person have, knowing how to walk before the living?

column.name: text
column.value: What the eyes see is better than what the soul ①desires. This too is futility and striving after wind. ▷ ①Lit goes after

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever exists has already been named, and it is known what man is; for he cannot dispute with the ①one who is mightier than he is. ▷ ①Or Him who

column.name: text
column.value: For there are many words which increase futility. What then is the advantage to a person?

column.name: text
column.value: For who knows what is good for a person during his lifetime, during the few ①years of his futile life? He will ②spend them like a shadow. For who can tell a person what will happen after him under the sun? ▷ ①Lit days ②Lit do

column.name: text
column.value: A good name is better than good ①oil, And the day of one’s death is better than the day of one’s birth. ▷ ①I.e., olive oil

column.name: text
column.value: It is better to go to a house of mourning Than to go to a house of feasting, Because ①that is the end of every person, And the living ②takes it to ③heart. ▷ ①I.e., death ②Lit gives ③Lit his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Sorrow is better than laughter, For when a face is sad a heart may be happy.

column.name: text
column.value: The ①mind of the wise is in the house of mourning, While the ②mind of fools is in the house of pleasure. ▷ ①Lit heart ②Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: It is better to listen to the rebuke of a wise person Than for one to listen to the song of fools.

column.name: text
column.value: For as the ①crackling of thorn bushes under a pot, So is the laughter of the fool; And this too is futility. ▷ ①Lit voice

column.name: text
column.value: For oppression makes a wise person look foolish, And a bribe ①corrupts the heart. ▷ ①Lit destroys

column.name: text
column.value: The end of a matter is better than its beginning; Patience of spirit is better than arrogance of spirit.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be ①eager in your spirit to be angry, For anger resides in the ②heart of fools. ▷ ①Lit hasty ②Lit chest

column.name: text
column.value: Do not say, “Why is it that the former days were better than these?” For it is not from wisdom that you ask about this.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom along with an inheritance is good, And an advantage to those who see the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: For wisdom is ①protection just as money is ②protection, But the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom keeps its possessors alive. ▷ ①Lit in a shadow ②Lit in a shadow

column.name: text
column.value: Consider the work of God, For who is able to straighten what He has bent?

column.name: text
column.value: On the day of prosperity be happy, But on the day of adversity consider: God has made the one as well as the other So that a person will not discover anything that will come after him.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen everything during my ①lifetime of futility; there is a righteous person who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked person who prolongs his life in his wickedness. ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be excessively righteous, and do not be overly wise. Why should you ruin yourself?

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be excessively wicked, and do not be foolish. Why should you die ①before your time? ▷ ①Lit when not your time

column.name: text
column.value: It is good that you grasp one thing while not ①letting go of the other; for one who fears God comes out with ②both of them. ▷ ①Lit resting your hand ②Lit all of them

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom strengthens a wise person more than ten rulers who are in a city.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, there is not a righteous person on earth who always does good and does not ever sin.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, do not ①take seriously all the words which are spoken, so that you do not hear your servant cursing you, ▷ ①Lit give your heart to

column.name: text
column.value: for ①you know that even you have cursed others many times as well. ▷ ①Lit your heart knows

column.name: text
column.value: I tested all this with wisdom, and I said, “I will be wise,” but wisdom was far from me.

column.name: text
column.value: What has been is remote and very ①mysterious. Who can discover it? ▷ ①Lit deep

column.name: text
column.value: I ①directed my ②mind to know and to investigate, and to seek wisdom and an explanation, and to know the evil of foolishness and the foolishness of insanity. ▷ ①Lit turned about ②Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: And I discovered as more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and nets, whose hands are chains. One who is pleasing to God will escape from her, but the sinner will be captured by her.

column.name: text
column.value: “Behold, I have discovered this,” says the Preacher, “by adding one thing to another to find an explanation,

column.name: text
column.value: which ①I am still seeking but have not found. I have found one man among a thousand, but I have not found a woman among all these. ▷ ①Lit my soul still seeks

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, I have found only this, that God made people upright, but they have sought out many schemes.”

column.name: text
column.value: Dead flies turn a perfumer’s oil rancid, so a little foolishness is more ①potent than wisdom and honor. ▷ ①Lit costly

column.name: text
column.value: A wise person’s heart directs him toward the right, but the foolish person’s heart directs him toward the left.

column.name: text
column.value: Even when the fool walks along the road, his ①sense is lacking, and he ②demonstrates to everyone that he is a fool. ▷ ①Lit heart ②Lit says

column.name: text
column.value: If the ruler’s ①temper rises against you, do not abandon your place, because composure puts great offenses to rest. ▷ ①Lit spirit

column.name: text
column.value: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, like a mistake that proceeds from the ruler:

column.name: text
column.value: foolishness is set in many exalted places while the rich sit in humble places.

column.name: text
column.value: I have seen slaves riding on horses and princes walking like slaves on the land.

column.name: text
column.value: One who digs a pit may fall into it, and a serpent may bite one who breaks through a wall.

column.name: text
column.value: One who quarries stones may be hurt by them, and one who splits logs may be endangered by them.

column.name: text
column.value: If the ①axe is dull and he does not sharpen its ②edge, then he must exert more strength. Wisdom has the advantage of bringing success. ▷ ①Lit iron ②Lit faces

column.name: text
column.value: If the serpent bites ①before being charmed, there is no benefit for the charmer. ▷ ①Lit with no incantation

column.name: text
column.value: Words from the mouth of a wise person are gracious, while the lips of a fool consume him;

column.name: text
column.value: the beginning of ①his talking is foolishness, and the end of ②it is evil insanity. ▷ ①Lit the words of his mouth ②Lit his mouth

column.name: text
column.value: Yet the fool multiplies words. No person knows what will happen, and who can tell him what will come after him?

column.name: text
column.value: The labor of ①a fool makes him so weary that he does not even know how to go to a city. ▷ ①Lit fools make

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to you, land whose king is a boy, and whose princes ①feast in the morning. ▷ ①Lit eat

column.name: text
column.value: Blessed are you, land whose king is of nobility, and whose princes eat at the appropriate time—for strength and not for drunkenness.

column.name: text
column.value: Through extreme laziness the rafters sag, and through idleness the house leaks.

column.name: text
column.value: People prepare a meal for enjoyment, wine makes life joyful, and money ①is the answer to everything. ▷ ①Lit answers all

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, in your bedroom do not curse a king, and in your sleeping rooms do not curse a rich person; for a bird of the sky will bring the sound, and the winged one will make your word known.

column.name: text
column.value: For I have taken all this to my heart, even to ①examine ②it all, that righteous people, wise people, and their deeds are in the hand of God. People do not know whether it will be love or hatred; anything ③awaits them. ▷ ①Or explain ②Lit all this ③Lit is before them

column.name: text
column.value: It is the same for all. There is one fate for the righteous and for the wicked; for the good, for the clean and the unclean; for the person who offers a sacrifice and for the one who does not sacrifice. As the good person is, so is the sinner; the one who swears an oath is just as the one who ①is afraid to swear an oath. ▷ ①Lit fears an oath

column.name: text
column.value: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun, that there is one fate for everyone. Furthermore, the hearts of the sons of mankind are full of evil, and insanity is in their hearts throughout their lives. Afterward they go to the dead.

column.name: text
column.value: For whoever is joined to all the living, there is hope; for better a live dog, than a dead lion.

column.name: text
column.value: For the living know that they will die; but the dead do not know anything, nor do they have a reward any longer, for their memory is forgotten.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed their love, their hate, and their zeal have already perished, and they will no longer have a share in all that is done under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Go then, eat your bread in happiness, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart; for God has already approved your works.

column.name: text
column.value: See that your clothes are white all the time, and that there is no lack of oil on your head.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Enjoy life with the wife whom you love all the days of your futile life which He has given you under the sun, ②all the days of your futility; for this is your reward in life and in your work which you have labored under the sun. ▷ ①Lit See ②all...your futility not found in some ancient versions

column.name: text
column.value: Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with all your might; for there is no activity, planning, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol where you are going.

column.name: text
column.value: I again saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift and the battle is not to the warriors, and neither is bread to the wise nor wealth to the discerning, nor favor to the skillful; for time and chance overtake them all.

column.name: text
column.value: For indeed, a person does not know his time: like fish that are caught in a treacherous net and birds caught in a snare, so the sons of mankind are ensnared at an evil time when it suddenly falls on them.

column.name: text
column.value: This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and ①it impressed me: ▷ ①Lit it was great to me

column.name: text
column.value: there was a small city with few men in it, and a great king came to it, surrounded it, and constructed large siegeworks against it.

column.name: text
column.value: But there was found in it a poor wise man, and he ①saved the city by his wisdom. Yet no one remembered that poor man. ▷ ①Or might have saved

column.name: text
column.value: So I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” But the wisdom of the poor man is despised, and his words are ①ignored. ▷ ①Lit not listened to

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the wise heard in calm are better than the shouting of a ruler among fools.

column.name: text
column.value: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good.

column.name: text
column.value: Who is like the wise person and who knows the meaning of a matter? A person’s wisdom illuminates his face and makes his stern face ①brighten up. ▷ ①Or change

column.name: text
column.value: I say, “Keep the ①command of the king because of the oath ②before God. ▷ ①Lit mouth ②Lit of

column.name: text
column.value: Do not be in a hurry ①to leave him. Do not join in an evil matter, for he will do whatever he pleases.” ▷ ①Lit to go out from his presence

column.name: text
column.value: Since the word of the king is authoritative, who will say to him, “What are you doing?”

column.name: text
column.value: One who keeps a royal command experiences no ①trouble, for a wise heart knows the proper time and procedure. ▷ ①Lit evil thing

column.name: text
column.value: For there is a proper time and procedure for every delight, though a person’s trouble is heavy upon him.

column.name: text
column.value: If no one knows what will happen, who can tell him when it will happen?

column.name: text
column.value: No one has authority over the wind to restrain the wind, nor authority over the day of death; and there is no military discharge in the time of war, and evil will not save ①those who practice it. ▷ ①Lit its possessors

column.name: text
column.value: All this I have seen, and have applied my ①mind to every deed that has been done under the sun at a time when one person has exercised authority over another person to his detriment. ▷ ①Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: So then, I have seen the wicked buried, those who used to go in and out of the holy place, and they are soon forgotten in the city where they did such things. This too is futility.

column.name: text
column.value: Because the sentence against an evil deed is not executed quickly, therefore the hearts of the sons of mankind among them are ①fully given to do evil. ▷ ①Lit full to do

column.name: text
column.value: Although a sinner does evil a hundred times and may lengthen his life, still I know that it will go well for those who fear God, who fear ①Him openly. ▷ ①Lit before Him

column.name: text
column.value: But it will not go well for the evil person and he will not lengthen his days like a shadow, because he does not fear God.

column.name: text
column.value: There is futility which is done on the earth, that is, there are righteous people to whom it ①happens according to the deeds of the wicked. On the other hand, there are evil people to whom it ②happens according to the deeds of the righteous. I say that this too is futility. ▷ ①Lit strikes ②Lit strikes

column.name: text
column.value: So I commended pleasure, for there is nothing good for a person under the sun except to eat, drink, and be joyful, and this will stand by him in his labor throughout the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: When I devoted my ①mind to know wisdom and to see the business which has been done on the earth (even though one should ②never sleep day or night), ▷ ①Lit heart ②Lit see no sleep in his eyes

column.name: text
column.value: and I saw every work of God, I concluded that one cannot discover the work which has been done under the sun. Even though a person laboriously seeks, he will not discover; and even if the wise person claims to know, he cannot discover.

column.name: text
column.value: Cast your bread on the surface of the waters, for you will find it ①after many days. ▷ ①Lit in, within

column.name: text
column.value: Divide your portion to seven, or even to eight, for you do not know what misfortune may occur on the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: If the clouds are full, they pour out rain on the earth; and whether a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, wherever the tree falls, there it ①lies. ▷ ①Lit is

column.name: text
column.value: One who watches the wind will not sow and one who looks at the clouds will not harvest.

column.name: text
column.value: Just as you do not know the path of the ①wind, and how bones are formed in the womb of the ②pregnant woman, so you do not know the activity of God who makes everything. ▷ ①Or with many mss spirit into the bones in the womb ②Lit full

column.name: text
column.value: Sow your seed in the morning and do not ①be idle in the evening, for you do not know whether ②one or the other will succeed, or whether both of them alike will be good. ▷ ①Lit let down your hand ②Lit this or that

column.name: text
column.value: The light is pleasant, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.

column.name: text
column.value: Indeed, if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything that is to come will be futility.

column.name: text
column.value: Rejoice, young man, during your childhood, and let your heart be pleasant during the days of young manhood. And follow the ①impulses of your heart and the ②desires of your eyes. Yet know that God will bring you to judgment for all these things. ▷ ①Lit ways ②Lit sights

column.name: text
column.value: So remove ①sorrow from your heart and keep ②pain away from your body, because childhood and the prime of life are ③fleeting. ▷ ①Or anger ②Lit evil ③Lit futility

column.name: text
column.value: Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth, before the evil days come and the years approach when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them”;

column.name: text
column.value: before the sun and the light, the moon and the stars are darkened, and clouds return after the rain;

column.name: text
column.value: on the day that the watchmen of the house tremble, and strong men are bent over, the grinders stop working because they are few, and those who look through ①windows grow ②dim; ▷ ①Or holes ②I.e., in their eyesight

column.name: text
column.value: and the doors on the street are shut as the sound of the grinding mill is low, and one will arise at the sound of the bird, and all the daughters of song will ①sing softly. ▷ ①Lit be low

column.name: text
column.value: Furthermore, people are afraid of a high place and of terrors on the road; the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry is ineffective. For man goes to his eternal home while the mourners move around in the street.

column.name: text
column.value: Remember your Creator before the silver cord is ①broken and the golden bowl is crushed, the pitcher by the spring is shattered and the wheel at the cistern is crushed; ▷ ①As in LXX; Heb removed

column.name: text
column.value: then the dust will return to the earth as it was, and the ①spirit will return to God who gave it. ▷ ①Or breath

column.name: text
column.value: “Futility of futilities,” says the Preacher, “all is futility!”

column.name: text
column.value: In addition to being wise, the Preacher also taught the people knowledge; and he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.

column.name: text
column.value: The Preacher sought to find delightful words and to write words of truth correctly.

column.name: text
column.value: The words of the wise are like ①goads, and masters of these collections are like driven nails; they are given by one Shepherd. ▷ ①I.e., spiked sticks for driving cattle

column.name: text
column.value: But beyond this, my son, be warned: the ①writing of many books is endless, and excessive study is ②wearying to the body. ▷ ①Lit making ②Lit weariness

column.name: text
column.value: The conclusion, when everything has been heard, is: fear God and keep His commandments, because this applies to every person.

column.name: text
column.value: For God will bring every act to judgment, everything which is hidden, whether it is good or evil.

column.name: text
column.value: The ①Song of Songs, which is Solomon’s. ▷ ①Or Best of the Songs ②The speaker identifications are not from the Hebrew text nor the Septuagint, but reflect an ancient tradition which appears in some manuscripts.

column.name: text
column.value: ①“May he kiss me with the kisses of his mouth! For your love is ②sweeter than wine. ▷ ①Lit more pleasant

column.name: text
column.value: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance, Your name is like ①purified oil; Therefore the ②young women love you. ▷ ①Lit oil poured from one vessel to another ②Or virgins

column.name: text
column.value: Draw me after you and let’s run together! The king has brought me into his chambers.” “We will rejoice in you and be joyful; We will praise your love more than wine. Rightly do they love you.”

column.name: text
column.value: “I am black and beautiful, You daughters of Jerusalem, Like the tents of Kedar, Like the curtains of Solomon.

column.name: text
column.value: Do not stare at me because I am ①dark, For the sun has tanned me. My mother’s sons were angry with me; They made me caretaker of the vineyards, But I have not taken care of my own vineyard. ▷ ①Or swarthy, blackish

column.name: text
column.value: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, Where do you pasture your flock, Where do you have it lie down at noon? For why should I be like one who ①veils herself Beside the flocks of your companions?” ▷ ①Some ancient versions wanders

column.name: text
column.value: “If you yourself do not know, Most beautiful among women, Go out on the trail of the flock, And pasture your young goats By the tents of the shepherds.

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①To me, my darling, you are like My mare among the chariots of Pharaoh. ▷ ①Lit I have compared you to

column.name: text
column.value: Your cheeks are delightful with jewelry, Your neck with strings of beads.”

column.name: text
column.value: “We will make for you jewelry of gold With beads of silver.”

column.name: text
column.value: “While the king was at his table, My ①perfume gave forth its fragrance. ▷ ①Lit nard

column.name: text
column.value: My beloved is to me a pouch of myrrh Which lies all night between my breasts.

column.name: text
column.value: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms In the vineyards of Engedi.”

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①How beautiful you are, my darling, ②How beautiful you are! Your eyes are like doves.” ▷ ①Lit Behold ②Lit Behold

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①How handsome you are, my beloved, And so delightful! Indeed, our bed is luxuriant! ▷ ①Lit Behold

column.name: text
column.value: The beams of our house are cedars, Our rafters, junipers.

column.name: text
text
column.value: ‘ ①I must arise now and ②go around in the city; In the streets and in the public squares ③I must seek him whom my soul loves.’ I sought him but did not find him. ▷ ①Or Let me arise ②Or Let me go about ③Or Let me seek

column.name: text
column.value: The watchmen who make the rounds in the city found me, And I said, ‘Have you seen him whom my soul loves?’

column.name: text
column.value: Hardly had I ①left them When I found him whom my soul loves; I held on to him and would not let him go Until I had brought him to my mother’s house, And into the room of her who conceived me.” ▷ ①Lit passed

column.name: text
column.value: “Swear to me, you daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles or by the does of the field, That you will not disturb or awaken my love Until she pleases.”

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①What is this coming up from the wilderness Like columns of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all the scented powders of the merchant? ▷ ①Lit Who

column.name: text
column.value: Behold, it is ①the traveling couch of Solomon; Sixty warriors around it, Of the warriors of Israel. ▷ ①I.e., an elegant couch designed to be carried with poles by servants

column.name: text
column.value: All of them are wielders of the sword, Expert in war; Each man has his sword at his side, Guarding against the ①terrors of the night. ▷ ①Lit terror in the nights

column.name: text
column.value: King Solomon has made for himself a ①sedan chair From the timber of Lebanon. ▷ ①I.e., an elegant throne with poles, carried by servants

column.name: text
column.value: He made its posts of silver, Its ①back of gold And its seat of purple fabric, With its interior lovingly inlaid By the daughters of Jerusalem. ▷ ①Or support

column.name: text
column.value: Go out, you daughters of Zion, And look at King Solomon with the ①crown With which his mother has crowned him On the day of his wedding, And on the day of the joy of his heart.” ▷ ①Or wreath

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①How beautiful you are, my darling, ②How beautiful you are! Your eyes are like doves behind your veil; Your hair is like a flock of goats That have descended from Mount Gilead. ▷ ①Lit Behold ②Lit Behold

column.name: text
column.value: Your teeth are like a flock of newly shorn sheep Which have come up from their watering place, All of which bear twins, And not one among them has lost her young.

column.name: text
column.value: Your lips are like a scarlet thread, And your mouth is beautiful. Your temples are like a slice of a pomegranate Behind your veil.

column.name: text
column.value: Your neck is like the tower of David, Built with layers of stones On which are hung a thousand shields, All the round shields of the warriors.

column.name: text
column.value: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle That graze among the lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: Until ①the cool of the day When the shadows flee, I will go my way to the mountain of myrrh And to the hill of frankincense. ▷ ①Lit the day blows

column.name: text
column.value: “You are altogether beautiful, my darling, And there is no blemish on you.

column.name: text
column.value: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, You shall come with me from Lebanon. You shall ①come down from the summit of Amana, From the summit of Senir and Hermon, From the dens of lions, From the mountains of leopards. ▷ ①Or look

column.name: text
column.value: You have ①enchanted my heart, my sister, my bride; You have ②enchanted my heart with a single glance of your eyes, With a single strand of your necklace. ▷ ①Or stolen ②Or stolen

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much ①sweeter is your love than wine, And the fragrance of your oils Than that of all kinds of balsam oils! ▷ ①Lit better

column.name: text
text
column.value: A locked garden is my sister, my bride, A locked spring, a sealed fountain.

column.name: text
column.value: Your branches are an ①orchard of pomegranates With delicious fruits, henna with nard plants, ▷ ①Or park; or garden

column.name: text
column.value: Nard and saffron, spice reed and cinnamon, With all the trees of frankincense, Myrrh, and aloes, along with all the finest balsam oils.

column.name: text
column.value: You are a garden spring, A well of ①fresh water, And flowing streams from Lebanon.” ▷ ①Lit living; i.e., running

column.name: text
column.value: “Awake, north wind, And come, wind of the south; ①Make my garden breathe out fragrance, May its balsam oils flow. May my beloved come into his garden And eat its delicious fruits!” ▷ ①Or Drift through my

column.name: text
column.value: “I am the ①rose of Sharon, The lily of the valleys.” ▷ ①Lit asphodel

column.name: text
column.value: “Like a lily among the thorns, So is my darling among the ①young women.” ▷ ①Lit daughters

column.name: text
column.value: “Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, So is my beloved among the ①young men. In his shade I took great delight and sat down, And his fruit was sweet to my ②taste. ▷ ①Lit sons ②Lit palate

column.name: text
column.value: He has brought me to his ①banquet hall, And his banner over me is love. ▷ ①Lit house of wine

column.name: text
column.value: Refresh me with raisin cakes, Sustain me with apples, Because I am lovesick.

column.name: text
column.value: His left hand is under my head, And his right hand embraces me.”

column.name: text
column.value: “Swear to me, you daughters of Jerusalem, By the gazelles or by the does of the field, That you will not disturb or awaken my love Until she pleases.”

column.name: text
column.value: “Listen! My beloved! Behold, he is coming, Leaping on the mountains, Jumping on the hills!

column.name: text
column.value: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young ①stag. Behold, he is standing behind our wall, He is looking through the windows, He is peering through the lattice. ▷ ①Lit of the stags

column.name: text
column.value: “My beloved responded and said to me, ‘Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, And come along.

column.name: text
column.value: For behold, the winter is past, The rain is over and gone.

column.name: text
column.value: The blossoms have already appeared in the land; The time has arrived for ①pruning the vines, And the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land. ▷ ①Or singing

column.name: text
column.value: The fig tree has ripened its fruit, And the vines in blossom have given forth their fragrance. Arise, my darling, my beautiful one, And come along!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: “My dove, in the clefts of the ①rock, In the hiding place of the mountain pathway, Let me see ②how you look, Let me hear your voice; For your voice is pleasant, And ③you look delightful.” ▷ ①Or crag ②Lit your appearance ③Lit your appearance

column.name: text
column.value: “Catch the ①foxes for us, The ②little ③foxes that are ruining the vineyards, While our vineyards are in blossom.” ▷ ①Or jackals ②Or young ③Or jackals

column.name: text
column.value: “My beloved is mine, and I am his; He pastures his flock among the lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: Until the cool of the day, when the shadows flee, Turn, my beloved, and be like a gazelle Or a young stag on the mountains of ①Bether.” ▷ ①Or ravines; or perfumes

column.name: text
text
column.value: “I was asleep but my heart was awake. A voice! My beloved was knocking: ‘Open to me, my sister, my darling, My dove, my perfect one! For my head is ①drenched with dew, My locks with the dew drops of the night.’ ▷ ①Lit filled

column.name: text
column.value: I have taken off my dress, How can I put it on again? I have washed my feet, How can I dirty them again?

column.name: text
column.value: My beloved extended his hand through the opening, And my feelings were stirred for him.

column.name: text
column.value: I arose to open to my beloved; And my hands dripped with myrrh, And my fingers with drops of myrrh, On the handles of the bolt.

column.name: text
column.value: I opened to my beloved, But my beloved had turned away and had gone! My ①heart went out to him as he spoke. I searched for him but I did not find him; I called him but he did not answer me. ▷ ①Lit soul

column.name: text
text
column.value: Swear to me, you daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, As to what you will tell him: For I am lovesick.”

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①What kind of beloved is your beloved, O most beautiful among women? ②What kind of beloved is your beloved, That you make us swear in this way?” ▷ ①Or What is your beloved more than another beloved ②Or What is your beloved more than another beloved

column.name: text
column.value: “My beloved is dazzling and ①reddish, Outstanding among ten thousand. ▷ ①I.e., of reddish hair or skin

column.name: text
text
column.value: His eyes are like doves Beside streams of water, Bathed in milk, And perched in their setting.

column.name: text
column.value: His cheeks are like a bed of balsam, ①Banks of herbal spices; His lips are lilies Dripping with drops of myrrh. ▷ ①Lit Towers

column.name: text
column.value: His hands are rods of gold Set with topaz; His abdomen is panels of ivory Covered with ①sapphires. ▷ ①Lit lapis lazuli

column.name: text
column.value: His thighs are pillars of alabaster Set on pedestals of pure gold; His appearance is like Lebanon, Choice as the cedars.

column.name: text
column.value: His ①mouth is full of sweetness. And he is wholly desirable. This is my beloved and this is my friend, You daughters of Jerusalem.” ▷ ①Lit palate

column.name: text
column.value: “Where has your beloved gone, O most beautiful among women? Where has your beloved turned, That we may seek him with you?”

column.name: text
column.value: “My beloved has gone down to his garden, To the beds of balsam, To pasture his flock in the gardens And gather lilies.

column.name: text
column.value: I am my beloved’s and my beloved is mine, He who pastures his flock among the lilies.”

column.name: text
column.value: “You are as beautiful as Tirzah, my darling, As lovely as Jerusalem, As awesome as an army with banners.

column.name: text
column.value: Turn your eyes away from me, For they have confused me; Your hair is like a flock of goats That have descended from Gilead.

column.name: text
column.value: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes That have come up from their watering place, All of which bear twins, And not one among them has lost her young.

column.name: text
column.value: Your temples are like a slice of a pomegranate Behind your veil.

column.name: text
text
column.value: But my dove, my perfect one, is ①unique: She is her mother’s ②only daughter; She is the pure child of the one who gave birth to her. The ③young women saw her and called her ④blessed, The queens and the concubines also, and they praised her, saying, ▷ ①Lit one ②Lit one ③Lit daughters ④Or happy

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Who is this who looks down like the dawn, As beautiful as the full moon, As pure as the sun, As awesome as an army with banners?’

column.name: text
column.value: I went down to the orchard of nut trees To see the plants of the valley, To see whether the vine had grown Or the pomegranates had bloomed.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Before I was aware, my soul set me Over the chariots of ②my noble people.” ▷ ①Lit I was not aware, my soul ②Or Ammi-nadib

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①Come back, come back, O Shulammite; Come back, come back, so that we may look at you!” “Why should you look at the Shulammite, As at the dance of ②the two armies? ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①How beautiful are your feet in sandals, ②Prince’s daughter! The curves of your hips are like jewels, The work of the hands of an artist. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: Your navel is like a round goblet That never lacks mixed wine; Your belly is like a heap of wheat, ①Surrounded with lilies. ▷ ①Lit Fenced around

column.name: text
column.value: Your two breasts are like two fawns, Twins of a gazelle.

column.name: text
column.value: Your neck is like a tower of ivory, Your eyes like the pools in Heshbon By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, Which looks toward Damascus.

column.name: text
column.value: Your head ①crowns you like Carmel, And the flowing hair of your head is like purple threads; The king is captivated by your tresses. ▷ ①Lit is upon

column.name: text
column.value: How beautiful and how delightful you are, ①My love, with all your delights! ▷ ①Or With love among your charms

column.name: text
column.value: ①Your stature is like a palm tree, And your breasts are like its clusters. ▷ ①Lit This stature of yours

column.name: text
column.value: I said, ‘I will climb the palm tree, I will grasp its fruit stalks.’ Oh, may your breasts be like clusters of the vine, And the fragrance of your ①breath like apples, ▷ ①Lit nose

column.name: text
column.value: And your ①mouth like the best wine!” “It goes down smoothly for my beloved, Flowing gently through the lips of those who are asleep. ▷ ①Lit palate

column.name: text
column.value: “I am my beloved’s, And his desire is for me.

column.name: text
column.value: Come, my beloved, let’s go out to the ①country, Let’s spend the night in the villages. ▷ ①Lit field

column.name: text
column.value: Let’s rise early and go to the vineyards; Let’s see whether the vine has grown And its buds have opened, And whether the pomegranates have bloomed. There I will give you my love.

column.name: text
column.value: The mandrakes have given forth fragrance; And over our doors are all delicious fruits, New as well as old, Which I have saved for you, my beloved.

column.name: text
column.value: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz concerning Judah and Jerusalem, which he saw during the ①reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: Listen, heavens, and hear, earth; For the LORD has spoken: “Sons I have raised and brought up, But they have revolted against Me.

column.name: text
column.value: An ox knows its owner, And a donkey its master’s manger, But Israel does not know, My people do not understand.”

column.name: text
column.value: Oh, sinful nation, People weighed down with guilt, ①Offspring of evildoers, Sons who act corruptly! They have abandoned the LORD, They have despised the Holy One of Israel, They have turned away ②from Him. ▷ ①Lit Seed ②Lit backward

column.name: text
column.value: Where will you be stricken again, As you continue in your rebellion? The entire head is sick And the entire heart is faint.

column.name: text
column.value: From the sole of the foot even to the head There is nothing healthy in it, Only bruises, slashes, and raw wounds; Not pressed out nor bandaged, Nor softened with oil.

column.name: text
text
column.value: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, Like a watchman’s hut in a cucumber field, like a city under watch.

column.name: text
column.value: If the LORD of armies Had not left us a few survivors, We would be like Sodom, We would be like Gomorrah.

column.name: text
column.value: Hear the word of the LORD, You rulers of Sodom; Listen to the instruction of our God, You people of Gomorrah!

column.name: text
column.value: “What are your many sacrifices to Me?” Says the LORD. “I ①have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fattened cattle; And I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, or goats. ▷ ①Or am sated with

column.name: text
column.value: When you come to appear before Me, Who requires ①of you this trampling of My courtyards? ▷ ①Lit of your hand

column.name: text
column.value: Do not go on bringing your worthless offerings, Incense is an abomination to Me. New moon and Sabbath, the proclamation of an assembly— I cannot endure wrongdoing and the festive assembly.

column.name: text
column.value: ①I hate your new moon festivals and your appointed feasts, They have become a burden to Me; I am tired of bearing them. ▷ ①Lit My soul hates

column.name: text
column.value: So when you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide My eyes from you; Yes, even though you offer many prayers, I will not be listening. Your hands are ①covered with blood. ▷ ①Lit full of

column.name: text
text
column.value: Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor, Obtain justice for the orphan, Plead for the widow’s case.

column.name: text
column.value: “Come now, and let us ①debate your case,” Says the LORD, “Though your sins are as scarlet, They shall become as white as snow; Though they are red like crimson, They shall be like wool. ▷ ①Or argue

column.name: text
column.value: If you are willing and obedient, You will eat the best of the land;

column.name: text
column.value: But if you refuse and rebel, You will be devoured by the sword.” For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.

column.name: text
column.value: How the faithful city has become a prostitute, She who was full of justice! Righteousness once dwelt in her, But now murderers.

column.name: text
column.value: Your silver has become ①waste matter, Your drink diluted with water. ▷ ①Lit dross

column.name: text
column.value: Your rulers are rebels And companions of thieves; Everyone loves a bribe And chases after gifts. They do not obtain justice for the ①orphan, Nor does the widow’s case come before them. ▷ ①Or fatherless

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore the Lord ①GOD of armies, The Mighty One of Israel, declares, “Ah, I will have satisfaction against My adversaries, And avenge Myself on My enemies. ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
text
column.value: Then I will restore your judges as at first, And your counselors as at the beginning; After that you will be called the city of righteousness, A faithful city.”

column.name: text
column.value: Zion will be redeemed with justice And her ①repentant ones with righteousness. ▷ ①Or returning

column.name: text
column.value: But ①wrongdoers and sinners together will be broken, And those who abandon the LORD will come to an end. ▷ ①Lit a breaking of wrongdoers and sinners together

column.name: text
column.value: ①You certainly will be ashamed of the ②oaks which you have desired, And you will be embarrassed by the gardens which you have chosen. ▷ ①As in some mss; MT They ②Or terebinths

column.name: text
column.value: For you will be like an ①oak whose leaf withers away, Or like a garden that has no water. ▷ ①Or terebinth

column.name: text
column.value: The strong man will become like ①flax fiber, And his work a spark. So they shall both burn together And there will be no one to extinguish them. ▷ ①Lit tow

column.name: text
column.value: “Oh that you were like a brother to me Who nursed at my mother’s breasts. If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you; No one would despise me, either.

column.name: text
text
column.value: Let his left hand be under my head, And his right hand embrace me.”

column.name: text
column.value: “Swear to me, you daughters of Jerusalem: ①Do not disturb or awaken my love Until she pleases.” ▷ ①Lit Why should you disturb or

column.name: text
column.value: “Who is this coming up from the wilderness, Leaning on her beloved?” “Beneath the apple tree I awakened you; There your mother went into labor with you, There she was in labor and gave birth to you.

column.name: text
column.value: Put me like a seal over your heart, Like a seal on your arm. For love is as strong as death, ①Jealousy is as severe as Sheol; Its flames are flames of fire, ②The flame of the LORD. ▷ ①Or Its passion is as inflexible ②Another reading is A vehement flame

column.name: text
column.value: Many waters cannot quench love, Nor will rivers flood over it; If a man were to give all the riches of his house for love, It would be utterly despised.”

column.name: text
column.value: “We have a little sister, And she has no breasts; What shall we do for our sister On the day when she is spoken for?

column.name: text
column.value: If she is a wall, We will build on her a battlement of silver; But if she is a door, We will barricade her with planks of cedar.”

column.name: text
column.value: “I was a wall, and my breasts were like towers; Then I became in his eyes as one who finds peace.

column.name: text
text
column.value: My very own vineyard is ①at my disposal; The thousand shekels are for you, Solomon, And two hundred are for those who take care of its fruit.” ▷ ①Lit before me

column.name: text
column.value: “You who sit in the gardens: My companions are listening for your voice— Let me hear it!”

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①Hurry, my beloved, And be like a gazelle or a young ②stag On the mountains of balsam trees!” ▷ ①Lit Flee ②Lit of the stags

column.name: text
column.value: For behold, the Lord ①GOD of armies is going to remove from Jerusalem and Judah Both supply and support, the entire supply of bread And the entire supply of water; ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
column.value: The mighty man and the warrior, The judge and the prophet, The diviner and the elder,

column.name: text
column.value: The captain of fifty and the esteemed person, The counselor and the expert artisan, And the skillful enchanter.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will make mere boys their leaders, And ①mischievous children will rule over them, ▷ ①Orarbitrary power will rule

column.name: text
column.value: And the people will be oppressed, Each one by another, and each one by his neighbor; The youth will assault the elder, And the contemptible person will assault the one honored.

column.name: text
column.value: When a man lays hold of his brother in his father’s house, saying, “You have a cloak, you shall be our ruler! And these ruins will be under your ①authority,” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: He will ①protest on that day, saying, “I will not be your ②healer, For in my house there is neither bread nor cloak; You should not appoint me ruler of the people.” ▷ ①Lit lift up his voice ②Lit binder of wounds

column.name: text
column.value: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, Because their ①speech and their actions are against the LORD, To rebel against ②His glorious presence. ▷ ①Lit tongue ②Lit the eyes of His glory

column.name: text
column.value: ①The expression of their faces testifies against them, And they ②display their sin like Sodom; They do not even conceal it. Woe to ③them! For they have done evil to themselves. ▷ ①Or Their partiality testifies ②Lit proclaim ③Lit their soul

column.name: text
column.value: Say to the righteous that it will go well for them, For they will eat the fruit of their actions.

column.name: text
column.value: Woe to the wicked! It will go badly for him, For ①what he deserves will be done to him. ▷ ①Lit the accomplishment of his hands

column.name: text
column.value: My people! Their oppressors treat them violently, And women rule over them. My people! Those who guide you lead you astray And confuse the direction of your paths.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD arises to contend, And stands to judge the people.

column.name: text
column.value: The LORD enters into judgment with the elders and leaders of His people, “It is you who have ①devoured the vineyard; The goods stolen from the poor are in your houses. ▷ ①Lit grazed over

column.name: text
column.value: What do you mean by crushing My people And ①oppressing the face of the poor?” Declares the Lord ②GOD of armies. ▷ ①Lit grinding the face of ②Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
