column.value: Again he measured a thousand and led me through the water, water reaching the knees. Again he measured a thousand and led me through the water, water reaching the ①hips. ▷ ①Lit loins

column.name: text
column.value: Again he measured a thousand; and it was a river that I could not ①wade across, because the water had risen, enough water to swim in, a river that could not be crossed by wading. ▷ ①Lit cross

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen this?” Then he brought me ①back to the bank of the river. ▷ ①Lit and caused me to return

column.name: text
column.value: Now when I had returned, behold, on the bank of the river there were very many trees on the one side and on the other.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he said to me, “These waters go out toward the eastern region and go down into the Arabah; then they go toward the ①sea, being made to flow into the sea, and the waters of the sea become ②fresh. ▷ ①I.e., Dead Sea ②Lit healed

column.name: text
column.value: And it will come about that every living creature which swarms in every place where the ①river goes, will live. And there will be very many fish, for these waters go there and the others ②become fresh; so everything will live where the river goes. ▷ ①Lit two rivers ②Lit are healed

column.name: text
column.value: And it will come about that fishermen will stand beside it; from Engedi to Eneglaim there will be a place for the spreading of nets. Their fish will be according to their kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.

column.name: text
column.value: But its swamps and marshes will not become ①fresh; they will be ②left for salt. ▷ ①Lit healed ②Lit given

column.name: text
column.value: And by the river on its bank, on one side and on the other, will grow all kinds of trees for food. Their leaves will not wither and their fruit will not fail. They will bear fruit every month because their water flows from the sanctuary, and their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing.”

column.name: text
column.value: This is what the Lord ①GOD says: “This shall be the boundary by which you shall divide the land for an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel; Joseph shall have two portions. ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: And you shall divide it for an inheritance, each one ①equally with the other; for I ②swore to give it to your forefathers, and this land shall fall to you ③as an inheritance. ▷ ①Lit like his brother ②Lit lifted up My hand ③Lit in

column.name: text
column.value: “And this shall be the boundary of the land: on the north side, from the Great Sea by the way of Hethlon, to the entrance of ①Zedad; ▷ ①As in MT; LXX Hamath, Zedad; cf.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazer-hatticon, which is by the border of Hauran. ▷ ①Or LXX Berothah

column.name: text
column.value: The boundary shall ①extend from the sea to Hazar-enan at the border of Damascus, and on the north toward the north is the border of Hamath. This is the north side. ▷ ①Lit be

column.name: text
column.value: “The east side, from between Hauran, Damascus, Gilead, and the land of Israel, shall be the Jordan; from the north border to the eastern sea you shall measure. This is the east side.

column.name: text
column.value: “The south side toward the south shall extend from Tamar as far as the waters of Meribath-kadesh, to the brook of Egypt and to the Great Sea. This is the south side toward the south.

column.name: text
column.value: “And the west side shall be the Great Sea, from the south border to a point opposite ①Lebo-hamath. This is the west side. ▷ ①Or the entrance of Hamath

column.name: text
column.value: “So you shall divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: You shall divide it by lot for an inheritance among yourselves and among the strangers who stay in your midst, who bring forth sons in your midst. And they shall be to you as the native-born among the sons of Israel; they shall be allotted an inheritance with you among the tribes of Israel.

column.name: text
column.value: And in the tribe with which the stranger resides, there you shall give him his inheritance,” declares the Lord GOD.

column.name: text
column.value: “Now these are the names of the tribes: from the northern extremity, ①beside the way of Hethlon to ②Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan at the border of Damascus, toward the north ③beside Hamath, ④running from east to west, Dan, one portion. ▷ ①Lit at the hand of ②Or the entrance of Hamath ③Lit at the hand of ④Lit and there shall be to it an east and the west side

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Asher, from the east side to the west side, Naphtali, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Ephraim, from the east side to the west side, Reuben, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: “And beside the border of Judah, from the east side to the west side, shall be the ①allotment which you shall ②set apart, twenty-five thousand ③cubits in width, and in length like one of the portions, from the east side to the west side; and the sanctuary shall be in the middle of it. ▷ ①Or contribution, and so throughout the ch ②Lit raise ③Each of these cubits equals about 21 in. or 53 cm

column.name: text
column.value: The allotment that you shall set apart to the LORD shall be twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width.

column.name: text
column.value: The holy allotment shall be for these, namely for the priests, toward the north twenty-five thousand cubits in length, toward the west ten thousand in width, toward the east ten thousand in width, and toward the south twenty-five thousand in length; and the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in its midst.

column.name: text
column.value: It shall be for the priests who are sanctified of the sons of Zadok, who have ①taken the responsibility I gave them, who did not go astray when the sons of Israel went astray as the Levites went astray. ▷ ①Lit kept the duty to Me

column.name: text
column.value: It shall be an allotment to them from the allotment of the land, a most holy reserve, by the border of the Levites.

column.name: text
column.value: And alongside the border of the priests, the Levites shall have twenty-five thousand cubits in length and ten thousand in width. The entire length shall be twenty-five thousand cubits and the width ten thousand.

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, they shall not sell or exchange any of it, or allow this ①choice portion of land to pass to others; for it is holy to the LORD. ▷ ①Lit first; or first fruits

column.name: text
column.value: “The remainder, five thousand cubits in width and twenty-five thousand ①in length, shall be for common use for the city, for homes and for ②open spaces; and the city shall be in its midst. ▷ ①Lit in front ②Or pasture land

column.name: text
column.value: And these shall be its measurements: the north side, 4,500 cubits, the south side 4,500 cubits, the east side 4,500 cubits, and the west side, 4,500 cubits.

column.name: text
column.value: The city shall have ①open spaces: on the north 250 cubits, on the south 250 cubits, on the east 250 cubits, and on the west 250 cubits. ▷ ①Or pasture land

column.name: text
column.value: The remainder of the length alongside the holy allotment shall be ten thousand cubits toward the east and ten thousand toward the west; and it shall be ①alongside the holy allotment. And its produce shall be food for the workers of the city. ▷ ①Or exactly as

column.name: text
column.value: And the workers of the city, out of all the tribes of Israel, shall cultivate it.

column.name: text
column.value: The whole allotment shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand cubits; you shall ①set apart the holy allotment, a ②square, with the ③property of the city. ▷ ①Lit raise ②Lit fourth ③Or possession

column.name: text
column.value: “The remainder shall be for the prince, on the one side and on the other of the holy allotment and of the ①property of the city; in front of the twenty-five thousand cubits of the allotment toward the east border and westward in front of the twenty-five thousand toward the west border, alongside the portions, it shall be for the prince. And the holy allotment and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the middle of it. ▷ ①Or possession

column.name: text
column.value: And exclusive of the ①property of the Levites and the ②property of the city, which are in the middle of that which belongs to the prince, everything between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin shall belong to the prince. ▷ ①Or possession ②Or possession

column.name: text
column.value: “As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: Beside the border of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad, one portion.

column.name: text
column.value: And beside the border of Gad, at the south side toward the south, the border shall be from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, to the brook of Egypt, to the Great Sea.

column.name: text
column.value: This is the land which you shall divide by lot to the tribes of Israel for an inheritance, and these are their several portions,” declares the Lord ①GOD. ▷ ①Heb YHWH, usually rendered LORD

column.name: text
column.value: “Now these are the exits of the city: on the north side, 4,500 cubits by measurement,

column.name: text
column.value: ①shall be the gates of the city, ②named for the tribes of Israel, three gates toward the north: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; and the gate of Levi, one. ▷ ①Litand the gates ②Lit according to the names of

column.name: text
column.value: On the east side, 4,500 cubits, ①shall be three gates: the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; and the gate of Dan, one. ▷ ①Lit and three gates

column.name: text
column.value: On the south side, 4,500 cubits by measurement, ①shall be three gates: the gate of Simeon, one; the gate of Issachar, one; and the gate of Zebulun, one. ▷ ①Lit and three gates

column.name: text
column.value: On the west side, 4,500 cubits, shall be three gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Asher, one; and the gate of Naphtali, one.

column.name: text
column.value: The city shall be eighteen thousand cubits all around; and the name of the city from that day shall be, ‘ ①The LORD is there.’ ” ▷ ①Heb YHWH-shammah

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

column.name: text
column.value: And the Lord handed Jehoiakim king of Judah over to him, along with some of the vessels of the house of God; and he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his ①god, and he brought the vessels into the treasury of his ②god. ▷ ①Or gods ②Or gods

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king told Ashpenaz, the chief of his ①officials, to bring in some of the sons of Israel, including some of the ②royal family and of the nobles, ▷ ①Or eunuchs, and so throughout the ch ②Lit seed of the monarchy

column.name: text
column.value: youths in whom there was no impairment, who were good-looking, suitable for instruction in every kind of expertise, endowed with understanding and discerning knowledge, and who had ability to ①serve in the king’s ②court; and he ordered Ashpenaz to teach them the ③literature and language of the Chaldeans. ▷ ①Lit stand ②Lit palace ③Or writing

column.name: text
column.value: The king also allotted for them a daily ration from the king’s choice food and from the wine which he drank, and ordered that they be educated for three years, at the end of which they were to ①enter the king’s personal service. ▷ ①Lit stand before the king

column.name: text
column.value: Now among them from the sons of Judah were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commander of the officials assigned new names to them; and to Daniel he assigned the name Belteshazzar, to Hananiah Shadrach, to Mishael Meshach, and to Azariah Abed-nego.

column.name: text
column.value: But Daniel ①made up his mind that he would not defile himself with the king’s choice food or with the wine which he drank; so he sought permission from the commander of the officials that he might not defile himself. ▷ ①Lit set upon his heart

column.name: text
column.value: Now God granted Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the commander of the officials.

column.name: text
column.value: The commander of the officials said to Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who has allotted your food and your drink; for why should he see your faces looking gaunt in comparison to the youths who are your own age? Then you would ①make me forfeit my head to the king.” ▷ ①Lit make my head guilty

column.name: text
column.value: But Daniel said to the overseer whom the commander of the officials had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

column.name: text
column.value: “Please put your servants to the test for ten days, and let us be given some vegetables to eat and water to drink.

column.name: text
column.value: Then let our appearance be ①examined in your presence and the appearance of the youths who are eating the king’s choice food; and deal with your servants according to what you see.” ▷ ①Lit seen

column.name: text
column.value: So he listened to them in this matter, and put them to the test for ten days.

column.name: text
column.value: And at the end of ten days their appearance seemed better, and ①they were fatter than all the youths who had been eating the king’s choice food. ▷ ①Lit fat of flesh

column.name: text
column.value: So the overseer continued to ①withhold their choice food and the wine they were to drink, and kept giving them vegetables. ▷ ①Lit take away

column.name: text
column.value: And as for these four youths, God gave them knowledge and intelligence in every kind of ①literature and expertise; Daniel even understood all kinds of visions and dreams. ▷ ①Or writing

column.name: text
column.value: Then at the end of the days which the king had ①specified ②for presenting them, the commander of the officials ③presented them before Nebuchadnezzar. ▷ ①Lit said ②Lit to bring them in ③Lit brought them in

column.name: text
column.value: And the king talked with them, and out of them all not one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah; so they ①entered the king’s personal service. ▷ ①Lit stood before the king

column.name: text
column.value: As for every matter of expertise ①and understanding about which the king consulted them, he found them ten times better than all the soothsayer priests and conjurers who were in all his realm. ▷ ①Lit of

column.name: text
column.value: And Daniel ①continued until the first year of Cyrus the king. ▷ ①Lit was until

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar ①had dreams; and his spirit was troubled and his sleep ②left him. ▷ ①Lit dreamed dreams ②Lit was gone upon him

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king ①gave orders to call in the soothsayer priests, the conjurers, the sorcerers, and the ②Chaldeans, to ③tell the king his dreams. So they came in and stood before the king. ▷ ①Lit said to call ②Probably master astrologers, diviners, etc., and so throughout the ch ③Lit explain to

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to them, “I ①had a dream, and my spirit ②is anxious to ③understand the dream.” ▷ ①Lit dreamed ②Lit was troubled ③Lit know

column.name: text
column.value: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in ①Aramaic: “O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.” ▷ ①The text is in Aramaic from here through

column.name: text
column.value: The king replied to the Chaldeans, “The command ①from me is firm: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be ②torn limb from limb and your houses will be turned into a rubbish heap. ▷ ①Another reading is is issued by me ②Lit turned into limbs

column.name: text
column.value: But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts and a reward and great honor; therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation.”

column.name: text
column.value: They answered a second time and said, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare the interpretation.”

column.name: text
column.value: The king replied, “I know for certain that you are trying to buy time, because you have perceived that the command ①from me is firm, ▷ ①See note 1 v 5

column.name: text
column.value: that if you do not make the dream known to me, there is only one ①decree for you. For you have agreed together to speak lying and corrupt ②words before me until the ③situation is changed; therefore tell me the dream, so that I may know that you can declare to me its interpretation.” ▷ ①Or verdict ②Lit word ③Lit time

column.name: text
column.value: The Chaldeans answered ①the king and said, “There is no person on earth who could declare the matter ②to the king, because no great king or ruler has ever asked anything like this of any soothsayer priest, sorcerer, or Chaldean. ▷ ①Lit before the ②Lit of

column.name: text
column.value: Moreover, the thing which the king demands is difficult, and there is no one else who could declare it ①to the king except gods, whose dwelling place is not with mortal flesh.” ▷ ①Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: Because of this, the king became angry and extremely furious, and he gave orders to kill all the wise men of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: So the ①decree was issued that the wise men be killed; and they looked for Daniel and his friends, to ②kill them. ▷ ①Or law ②Lit be killed

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel replied with discretion and discernment to Arioch, the captain of the king’s ①bodyguard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon; ▷ ①Or executioners

column.name: text
column.value: he said to Arioch, the king’s officer, “For what reason is the decree from the king so harsh?” Then Arioch informed Daniel of the matter.

column.name: text
column.value: So Daniel went in and requested of the king that he would give him a grace period, so that he might declare the interpretation to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel went to his house and informed his friends, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, about the matter,

column.name: text
column.value: so that they might request compassion from the God of heaven concerning this secret, so that Daniel and his friends would not be killed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in a night vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven;

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel said, “May the name of God be blessed forever and ever, For wisdom and power belong to Him.

column.name: text
text
text
column.value: To You, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, For You have given me wisdom and power; Even now You have made known to me what we requested of You, For You have made known to us the king’s matter.”

column.name: text
column.value: Thereupon, Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to kill the wise men of Babylon; he went and said this to him: “Do not kill the wise men of Babylon! Take me ①into the king’s presence, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.” ▷ ①Lit in before the king

column.name: text
column.value: Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel ①into the king’s presence and spoke to him as follows: “I have found a man among the ②exiles from Judah who can make the interpretation known to the king!” ▷ ①Lit in before the king ②Lit sons of the exile of

column.name: text
column.value: The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen and its interpretation?”

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel answered before the king and said, “As for the secret about which the king has inquired, neither wise men, sorcerers, soothsayer priests, nor diviners are able to declare it to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: However, there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets, and He has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will take place in the ①latter days. This was your dream and the visions ②in your mind while on your bed. ▷ ①Lit end of the days ②Lit of your head

column.name: text
column.value: As for you, O king, while on your bed your thoughts ①turned to what would take place ②in the future; and He who reveals secrets has made known to you what will take place. ▷ ①Lit came up ②Lit after this

column.name: text
column.value: But as for me, this secret has not been revealed to me ①for any wisdom ②residing in me more than in any other living person, but for the purpose of making the interpretation known to the king, and that you may understand the thoughts of your ③mind. ▷ ①Or through ②Lit which is ③Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: “You, O king, were watching and behold, there was a single great statue; that statue, which was large and ①of extraordinary radiance, was standing in front of you, and its appearance was ②awesome. ▷ ①Lit its radiance was extraordinary ②Or dreadful

column.name: text
column.value: The head of that statue was made of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,

column.name: text
column.value: its legs of iron, and its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.

column.name: text
column.value: You ①continued watching until a stone was broken off without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay, and crushed them. ▷ ①Lit were

column.name: text
column.value: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed to pieces ①all at the same time, and they were like chaff from the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away so that not a trace of them was found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the entire earth. ▷ ①Lit as one

column.name: text
column.value: “This was the dream; and now we will tell its interpretation before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the ①kingdom, the power, the strength, and the honor; ▷ ①Or sovereignty

column.name: text
column.value: and wherever the sons of mankind live, or the animals of the field, or the birds of the sky, He has handed them over to you and has made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.

column.name: text
column.value: And after you another kingdom will arise inferior to you, then another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then there will be a fourth kingdom as strong as iron; just as iron smashes and crushes everything, so, like iron that crushes, it will smash and crush all these things.

column.name: text
column.value: And in that you saw the feet and toes, partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but it will have within it some of the toughness of iron, since you saw the iron mixed with ①common clay. ▷ ①Lit wet clay

column.name: text
column.value: And just as the toes of the feet were partly of iron and partly of pottery, so some of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be fragile.

column.name: text
column.value: In that you saw the iron mixed with ①common clay, they will combine with one another ②in ③their descendants; but they will not adhere to one another, just as iron does not combine with pottery. ▷ ①Lit wet clay ②Or with ③Lit the seed of men

column.name: text
column.value: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be ①left for another people; it will crush and put an end to all these kingdoms, but it will itself endure forever. ▷ ①Or passed on to

column.name: text
column.value: Just as you saw that a stone was broken off from the mountain without hands, and that it crushed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver, and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what will take place ①in the future; so the dream is certain and its interpretation is trustworthy.” ▷ ①Lit after this

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid humble respect to Daniel, and gave orders to present to him an offering and incense.

column.name: text
column.value: The king responded to Daniel and said, “Your God truly is a God of gods and a Lord of kings and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king ①promoted Daniel and gave him many great gifts, and he made him ruler over the entire province of Babylon, and chief ②prefect over all the wise men of Babylon. ▷ ①Lit made Daniel great ②Lit of the prefects

column.name: text
column.value: And Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego over the administration of the province of Babylon, while Daniel was at the king’s ①court. ▷ ①Lit gate

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar the king made a statue of gold, the height of which was ①sixty cubits, and its width six cubits; he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon. ▷ ①About 90 ft. high and 9 ft. wide or 27 m and 2.7 m

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar the king also sent word to assemble the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counselors, the chief treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the administrators of the provinces to come to the dedication of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the satraps, the prefects and the governors, the counselors, the chief treasurers, the judges, the magistrates, and all the administrators of the provinces were assembled for the dedication of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up; and they stood before the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the herald loudly proclaimed: “To you ①the command is given, you peoples, nations, and populations of all ②languages, ▷ ①Lit they command ②Lit tongues

column.name: text
column.value: that at the moment you hear the sound of the horn, flute, ①lyre, ②trigon, ③psaltery, bagpipe, and all kinds of musical instruments, you are to fall down and worship the golden statue that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up. ▷ ①Or zither ②I.e., triangular lyre ③Or a type of harp

column.name: text
column.value: But whoever does not fall down and worship shall immediately be thrown into the middle of a furnace of blazing fire.”

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, flute, ①lyre, trigon, psaltery, ②bagpipe, and all kinds of musical instruments, all the peoples, nations, and populations of all ③languages fell down and worshiped the golden statue that Nebuchadnezzar the king had set up. ▷ ①See notes v 5 ②MT omits bagpipe ③Lit tongues

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason at that time certain Chaldeans came forward and ①brought charges against the Jews. ▷ ①Lit ate the pieces of

column.name: text
column.value: They began to speak and said to Nebuchadnezzar the king: “O king, live forever!

column.name: text
column.value: You, O king, have made a decree that every person who hears the sound of the horn, flute, ①lyre, trigon, psaltery, and bagpipe, and all kinds of musical instruments, is to fall down and worship the golden statue. ▷ ①See notes v 5

column.name: text
column.value: But whoever does not fall down and worship shall be thrown into the middle of a furnace of blazing fire.

column.name: text
column.value: There are certain Jews whom you have appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon, namely Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. These men, O king, have disregarded you; they do not serve your gods, nor do they worship the golden statue which you have set up.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar in rage and anger gave orders to bring Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; then these men were brought before the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar began speaking and said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, that you do not serve my gods, nor worship the golden statue that I have set up?

column.name: text
column.value: Now if you are ready, at the moment you hear the sound of the horn, flute, ①lyre, trigon, psaltery and bagpipe, and all kinds of musical instruments, to fall down and worship the statue that I have made, very well. But if you do not worship, you will ②immediately be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire; and what god is there who can rescue you from my hands?” ▷ ①See notes 1, 2, 3 v 5 ②Or in the same hour

column.name: text
column.value: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego replied to the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we are not in need of an answer to give you concerning this matter.

column.name: text
column.value: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire; ①and He will rescue us from your hand, O king. ▷ ①Or then

column.name: text
column.value: But even if He does not, let it be known to you, O king, that we are not going to serve your gods nor worship the golden statue that you have set up.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with wrath, and his facial expression was changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. He answered ①by giving orders to heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated. ▷ ①Lit and ordered to

column.name: text
column.value: And he ordered certain valiant warriors who were in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego in order to throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.

column.name: text
column.value: Then these men were tied up in their trousers, their ①coats, their caps, and their other clothes, and were thrown into the middle of the furnace of blazing fire. ▷ ①Or cloaks

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason, because the king’s ①command was harsh and the furnace had been made extremely hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: But these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, fell into the middle of the furnace of blazing fire still tied up.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar the king was astounded and stood up quickly; he said to his counselors, “Was it not three men that we threw bound into the middle of the fire?” They replied to the king, “Absolutely, O king.”

column.name: text
column.value: He responded, “Look! I see four men untied and walking about in the middle of the fire ①unharmed, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods!” ▷ ①Lit there is no injury in them

column.name: text
column.value: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the door of the furnace of blazing fire; he said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, come out, you servants of the Most High God, and come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego came out of the middle of the fire.

column.name: text
column.value: The satraps, the prefects, the governors, and the king’s counselors gathered together and saw that the fire had no ①effect on ②the bodies of these men, nor was the hair of their heads singed, nor were their ③trousers ④damaged, nor had even the smell of fire touched them. ▷ ①Lit power over ②Lit their ③Or coats ④Lit changed

column.name: text
column.value: Nebuchadnezzar responded and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who has sent His angel and rescued His servants who put their trust in Him, ①violating the king’s command, and surrendered their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God. ▷ ①Lit and changed the king’s word

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore I make a decree that any people, nation, or population of any language that speaks anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego shall be torn limb from limb and their houses made a rubbish heap, because there is no other god who is able to save in this way.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king made Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego prosperous in the province of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: I am pleased to declare the signs and miracles that the Most High God has done for me.

column.name: text
column.value: How great are His signs And how mighty are His miracles! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, And His dominion is from generation to generation.

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and happy in my palace. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: in Aram

column.name: text
column.value: I saw a dream and it startled me; and these appearances as I lay on my bed and the visions ①in my mind kept alarming me. ▷ ①Lit of my head

column.name: text
column.value: So I gave orders to bring into my presence all the wise men of Babylon, so that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the soothsayer priests, the sorcerers, the ①Chaldeans, and the diviners came in and I related the dream ②to them, but they could not make its interpretation known to me. ▷ ①Probably master astrologers, diviners, etc. ②Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: But finally Daniel came in before me, whose name is Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, and in whom is ①a spirit of the holy gods; and I related the dream ②to him, saying, ▷ ①Or possibly the Spirit of the holy God, and so throughout the ch ②Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Belteshazzar, chief of the soothsayer priests, since I know that a spirit of the holy gods is in you and no secret baffles you, tell me the visions of my dream which I have seen, along with its interpretation.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘Now these were the visions ①in my mind as I lay on my bed: I was looking, and behold, there was a tree in the middle of the ②earth and its height was great. ▷ ①Or land, and so throughout the ch ②Lit of my head

column.name: text
column.value: The tree grew large and became strong And its height reached to the sky, And it was visible to the end of the whole earth.

column.name: text
column.value: Its foliage was beautiful and its fruit abundant, And in it was food for all. The animals of the field ①found shade under it, And the birds of the sky lived in its branches, And all ②living creatures fed from it. ▷ ①Or dwelt under it ②Lit flesh

column.name: text
column.value: ‘I was looking in the visions ①in my mind as I lay on my bed, and behold, an angelic watcher, a holy one, descended from heaven. ▷ ①Lit of my head

column.name: text
column.value: He shouted out and spoke as follows: “Chop down the tree and cut off its branches, Shake off its foliage and scatter its fruit; Let the animals flee from under it And the birds from its branches.

column.name: text
column.value: Yet leave the stump ①with its roots in the ground, But with a band of iron and bronze around it In the new grass of the field; And let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, And let ②him share with the animals in the grass of the earth. ▷ ①Lit of ②Lit his share be with

column.name: text
column.value: Let his ①mind change from that of a human And let an animal’s ②mind be given to him, And let seven ③periods of time pass over him. ▷ ①Lit heart ②Lit heart ③I.e., years

column.name: text
column.value: This sentence is by the decree of the angelic watchers, And the decision is a command of the holy ones, In order that the living may know That the Most High is ruler over the realm of mankind, And He grants it to whomever He wishes And sets over it the lowliest of people.”

column.name: text
column.value: This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, have seen. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, since none of the wise men of my kingdom is able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able, because a spirit of the holy gods is in you.’

column.name: text
column.value: “Then Daniel, whose name is Belteshazzar, was appalled for a while as his thoughts alarmed him. The king responded and said, ‘Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you.’ Belteshazzar replied, ‘My lord, if only the dream applied to those who hate you, and its interpretation to your adversaries!

column.name: text
column.value: The tree that you saw, which became large and grew strong, whose height reached to the sky and was visible to all the earth,

column.name: text
column.value: and whose foliage was beautiful and its fruit abundant, and in which was food for all, under which the animals of the field lived and in whose branches the birds of the sky settled—

column.name: text
column.value: it is you, O king; for you have become great and grown strong, and your ①majesty has become great and reached to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth. ▷ ①Lit greatness

column.name: text
column.value: And in that the king saw an angelic watcher, a holy one, descending from heaven and saying, “Chop down the tree and destroy it; yet leave the stump ①with its roots in the ground, but with a band of iron and bronze around it in the new grass of the field, let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let ②him share with the animals of the field until seven ③periods of time pass over him,” ▷ ①Lit of ②Lit his share be with ③I.e., years

column.name: text
column.value: this is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree of the Most High, which has come upon my lord the king:

column.name: text
column.value: that you be driven away from mankind and your dwelling place be with the animals of the field, and you be given grass to eat like cattle and be drenched with the dew of heaven; and seven ①periods of time will pass over you, until you recognize that the Most High is ruler over the realm of mankind and bestows it on whomever He wishes. ▷ ①I.e., years

column.name: text
column.value: And in that it was commanded to leave the stump ①with the roots of the tree, your kingdom will ②remain as yours after you recognize that it is Heaven that rules. ▷ ①Lit of ②Lit be enduring to you

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, O king, may my advice be pleasing to you: wipe away your sin by doing righteousness, and your wrongdoings by showing mercy to the poor, in case there may be a prolonging of your prosperity.’

column.name: text
column.value: “All of this happened to Nebuchadnezzar the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Twelve months later he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.

column.name: text
column.value: The king began speaking and was saying, ‘Is this not Babylon the great, which I myself have built as a royal ①residence by the might of my power and for the honor of my majesty?’ ▷ ①Lit house

column.name: text
column.value: While the word was still in the king’s mouth, a voice ①came from heaven, saying, ‘King Nebuchadnezzar, to you it is declared: ②sovereignty has been removed from you, ▷ ①Lit fell ②Or kingdom

column.name: text
column.value: and you will be driven away from mankind, and your dwelling place will be with the animals of the field. You will be given grass to eat like cattle, and seven ①periods of time will pass over you until you recognize that the Most High is ruler over the realm of mankind and bestows it on whomever He wishes.’ ▷ ①I.e., years

column.name: text
column.value: Immediately the word concerning Nebuchadnezzar was fulfilled; and he was driven away from mankind and began eating grass like cattle, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws.

column.name: text
column.value: “But at the end of ①that period, I, Nebuchadnezzar, raised my eyes toward heaven and my ②reason returned to me, and I blessed the Most High and praised and honored Him who lives forever; For His dominion is an everlasting dominion, And His kingdom endures from generation to generation. ▷ ①Lit the days ②Lit understanding

column.name: text
column.value: All the inhabitants of the earth are of no account, But He does according to His will among the army of heaven And among the inhabitants of earth; And no one can ①fend off His hand Or say to Him, ‘What have You done?’ ▷ ①Lit strike against

column.name: text
column.value: At that time my ①reason returned to me. And my majesty and splendor were ②restored to me for the honor of my kingdom, and my state counselors and my nobles began seeking me out; so I was reestablished in my ③sovereignty, and surpassing greatness was added to me. ▷ ①Lit understanding ②Lit returning ③Or kingdom

column.name: text
column.value: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of heaven, for all His works are ①true and His ways ②just; and He is able to humble those who walk in pride.” ▷ ①Lit truth ②Lit justice

column.name: text
column.value: Belshazzar the king ①held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he was drinking wine in the presence of the thousand. ▷ ①Lit made

column.name: text
column.value: ①While he tasted the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring the gold and silver vessels which his ②father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives, and his concubines could drink out of them. ▷ ①Or Under the influence of the wine ②Or forefather, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: Then they brought the gold vessels that had been taken out of the temple, the house of God which was in Jerusalem; and the king and his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank out of them.

column.name: text
column.value: They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

column.name: text
column.value: Suddenly the fingers of a human hand emerged and began writing opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace, and the king saw the back of the hand that did the writing.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king’s ①face became pale and his thoughts alarmed him, and his hip joints ②loosened and his knees began knocking together. ▷ ①Lit brightness changed for him ②Or shook

column.name: text
column.value: The king called aloud to bring in the sorcerers, the ①Chaldeans, and the diviners. The king began speaking and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Anyone who can read this inscription and explain its interpretation to me shall be clothed with purple and have a necklace of gold around his neck, and have authority as third ruler in the kingdom.” ▷ ①I.e., probably master astrologers, diviners, etc., and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: Then all the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the inscription or make known its interpretation to the king.

column.name: text
column.value: Then King Belshazzar was greatly alarmed, his ①face grew even more pale, and his nobles were perplexed. ▷ ①Lit brightness was changing upon him

column.name: text
column.value: The queen entered the banquet ①hall because of the words of the king and his nobles; the queen began to speak and said, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts alarm you or your ②face be pale. ▷ ①Lit house ②Lit brightness be changed

column.name: text
column.value: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is ①a spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of your father, illumination, insight, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. And King Nebuchadnezzar, your father—your father ②the king—appointed him chief of the soothsayer priests, sorcerers, Chaldeans, and diviners. ▷ ①Or possibly the Spirit of the holy God ②Or O king

column.name: text
column.value: This was because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge and insight, interpretation of dreams, explanation of riddles, and solving of difficult problems were found in this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Let Daniel now be summoned and he will declare the interpretation.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king began speaking and said to Daniel, “Are you that Daniel who is one of the ①exiles from Judah, whom my father the king brought from Judah? ▷ ①Lit sons of the exile

column.name: text
column.value: Now I have heard about you that ①a spirit of the gods is in you, and that illumination, insight, and extraordinary wisdom have been found in you. ▷ ①Or possibly the Spirit of God

column.name: text
column.value: Just now the wise men and the sorcerers were brought in before me to read this inscription and make its interpretation known to me, but they could not declare the interpretation of the ①message. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: But I personally have heard about you, that you are able to give interpretations and solve difficult problems. Now if you are able to read the inscription and make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed with purple and wear a necklace of gold around your neck, and you will have authority as the third ruler in the kingdom.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel replied and said before the king, “ ①Keep your gifts for yourself or give your rewards to someone else; however, I will read the inscription to the king and make the interpretation known to him. ▷ ①Lit Let...be for

column.name: text
column.value: ①O king, the Most High God granted ②sovereignty, greatness, honor, and majesty to Nebuchadnezzar your father. ▷ ①Lit You, O king ②Or the kingdom

column.name: text
column.value: Now because of the greatness which He granted him, all the peoples, nations, and populations of all ①languages trembled and feared in his presence; whomever he wished, he killed, and whomever he wished, he spared alive; and whomever he wished he elevated, and whomever he wished he humbled. ▷ ①Lit tongues

column.name: text
column.value: But when his heart ①was arrogant and his spirit became so ②overbearing that he behaved presumptuously, he was deposed from his royal throne, and his dignity was taken away from him. ▷ ①Lit rose up ②Lit strong

column.name: text
column.value: He was also driven away from ①mankind, and his heart was made like that of animals, and his dwelling place was with the wild donkeys. He was given grass to eat like cattle, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he recognized that the Most High God is ruler over the realm of mankind, and that He sets over it whomever He wishes. ▷ ①Lit the sons of mankind

column.name: text
column.value: Yet you, his ①son, Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, even though you knew all this, ▷ ①Or descendant

column.name: text
column.value: but you have risen up against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of His house before you, and you and your nobles, your wives, and your concubines have been drinking wine out of them; and you have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see, nor hear, nor understand. But the God in whose hand are your life-breath and all your ways, you have not glorified.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the ①hand was sent from Him and this inscription was written out. ▷ ①Lit palm of the hand

column.name: text
column.value: “Now this is the inscription that was written: ‘ ①MENĒ, ②MENĒ, ③TEKĒL, ④UPHARSIN.’ ▷ ①Or a mina (50 shekels) from verb “to count” ②Or a mina (50 shekels) from verb “to count” ③Or a shekel from verb “to weigh” ④Or and half-shekels (singular: perēs) from verb “to divide”

column.name: text
column.value: This is the interpretation of the ①message: ‘MENĒ’—God has numbered your kingdom and put an end to it. ▷ ①Lit word

column.name: text
column.value: ‘TEKĒL’—you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.

column.name: text
column.value: ‘ ①PERĒS’—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and ②Persians.” ▷ ①Or half-shekel from verb “to divide” ②Aram: Pāras

column.name: text
column.value: Then Belshazzar gave orders, and they clothed Daniel with purple and put a necklace of gold around his neck, and issued a proclamation concerning him that he now had authority as the third ruler in the kingdom.

column.name: text
column.value: That same night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.

column.name: text
column.value: ①So Darius the Mede received the kingdom at about the age of sixty-two. ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: ①It pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps over the kingdom, to be in charge of the whole kingdom, ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: and over them, three commissioners (of whom Daniel was one), so that these satraps would be accountable to them, and that the king would not ①suffer loss. ▷ ①Or come to grief

column.name: text
column.value: Then this Daniel began distinguishing himself ①among the commissioners and satraps because ②he possessed an extraordinary spirit, and the king intended to appoint him over the entire kingdom. ▷ ①Lit above ②Lit there was in him

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commissioners and satraps began trying to find a ground of accusation against Daniel regarding ①government affairs; but they could find no ground of accusation or evidence of corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was to be found in him. ▷ ①Lit the kingdom

column.name: text
column.value: Then these men said, “We will not find any ground of accusation against this Daniel unless we find it against him regarding the law of his God.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then these commissioners and satraps came ①by agreement to the king and spoke to him as follows: “King Darius, live forever! ▷ ①Or as a group

column.name: text
column.value: All the commissioners of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together that the king should establish a statute and enforce an injunction that anyone who offers a prayer to any god or person besides you, O king, for thirty days, shall be thrown into the lions’ ①den. ▷ ①Or pit, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: Now, O king, establish the injunction and sign the document so that it will not be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which ①may not be revoked.” ▷ ①Lit does not pass away

column.name: text
column.value: Thereupon, King Darius signed the document, that is, the injunction.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when Daniel learned that the document was signed, he entered his house (and in his roof chamber he had windows open toward Jerusalem); and he continued kneeling on his knees three times a day, praying and offering praise before his God, just as he had been doing previously.

column.name: text
column.value: Then these men came ①by agreement and found Daniel offering a prayer and imploring favor before his God. ▷ ①Or as a group

column.name: text
column.value: Then they approached and spoke before the king about the king’s injunction: “Did you not sign an injunction that any person who offers a prayer to any god or person besides you, O king, for thirty days, is to be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king replied, “The statement is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which ①may not be revoked.” ▷ ①Lit does not go away

column.name: text
column.value: Then they responded and spoke before the king, “Daniel, who is one of the ①exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the injunction which you signed, but keeps offering his prayer three times a day.” ▷ ①Lit sons of the exile

column.name: text
column.value: Then, as soon as the king heard this statement, he was deeply distressed, and set his mind on rescuing Daniel; and until sunset he kept exerting himself to save him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then these men came ①by agreement to the king and said to the king, “Recognize, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no injunction or statute which the king establishes may be changed.” ▷ ①Or as a group

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king gave orders, and Daniel was brought in and thrown into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “ ①Your God whom you continually serve will Himself rescue you.” ▷ ①Or May your God...Himself rescue you

column.name: text
column.value: And a stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing would be changed regarding Daniel.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting, and no entertainment was brought before him; and his sleep fled from him.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king got up at dawn, at the break of day, and went in a hurry to the lions’ den.

column.name: text
column.value: And when he had come near the den to Daniel, he cried out with a troubled voice. The king began speaking and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you continually serve, been able to rescue you from the lions?”

column.name: text
column.value: Then Daniel spoke ①to the king, “O king, live forever! ▷ ①Lit with

column.name: text
column.value: My God sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not harmed me, since ①I was found innocent before Him; and also ②toward you, O king, I have committed no crime.” ▷ ①Lit innocence was found for me ②Lit before

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king was very glad and gave orders for Daniel to be lifted up out of the den. So Daniel was lifted up out of the den, and no injury whatever was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

column.name: text
column.value: The king then gave orders, and they brought those men who had ①maliciously accused Daniel, and they threw them, their children, and their wives into the lions’ den; and they had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones. ▷ ①Lit eaten the pieces of Daniel

column.name: text
column.value: Then Darius the king wrote to all the peoples, nations, and populations of all ①languages who were living in all the land: “May your ②peace be great! ▷ ①Lit tongues ②Or welfare; or prosperity

column.name: text
column.value: ①I issue a decree that in all the realm of my kingdom people are to tremble and fear before the God of Daniel; For He is the living God and enduring forever, And His kingdom is one which will not be destroyed, And His dominion will be ②forever. ▷ ①Lit From me a decree is issued ②Lit to the end

column.name: text
column.value: He rescues, saves, and performs signs and miracles In heaven and on earth, He who has also rescued Daniel from the ①power of the lions.” ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: So this Daniel enjoyed success in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

column.name: text
column.value: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions ①in his mind as he lay on his bed; then he wrote the dream down and told the ②following summary of ③it. ▷ ①Lit of his head ②Or beginning ③Lit words

column.name: text
column.value: Daniel ①said, “I was looking in my vision by night, and behold, the four winds of heaven were stirring up the great sea. ▷ ①Lit began speaking and said

column.name: text
column.value: And four great beasts were coming up from the sea, different from one another.

column.name: text
column.value: The first was like a lion but had the wings of an eagle. I kept looking until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the ground and set up on two feet like a man; a human ①mind also was given to it. ▷ ①Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: And behold, another beast, a second one, resembling a bear. And it was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth; and they said this to it: ‘Arise, devour much meat!’

column.name: text
column.value: After this I kept looking, and behold, another one, like a leopard, which had on its ①back four wings of a bird; the beast also had four heads, and dominion was given to it. ▷ ①Or sides

column.name: text
column.value: After this I kept looking in the night visions, and behold, a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and extremely strong; and it had large iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, and trampled down the remainder with its feet; and it was different from all the beasts that were before it, and it had ten horns.

column.name: text
column.value: While I was thinking about the horns, behold, another horn, a little one, came up among them, and three of the previous horns were plucked out before it; and behold, ①this horn possessed eyes like human eyes, and a mouth uttering great boasts. ▷ ①Lit in this horn were eyes

column.name: text
column.value: “I kept looking Until thrones were set up, And the Ancient of Days took His seat; His garment was white as snow, And the hair of His head like pure wool. His throne was ①ablaze with flames, Its wheels were a burning fire. ▷ ①Lit flames of fire

column.name: text
column.value: A river of fire was flowing And coming out from before Him; Thousands upon thousands were serving Him, And myriads upon myriads were standing before Him; The court ①convened, And the books were opened. ▷ ①Lit took its place

column.name: text
column.value: Then I kept looking because of the sound of the ①boastful words which the horn was speaking; I kept looking until the beast was killed, and its body was destroyed and given to the burning ②fire. ▷ ①Lit great ②Lit of the fire

column.name: text
column.value: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but an extension of life was granted to them for an appointed period of time.

column.name: text
column.value: “I kept looking in the night visions, And behold, with the clouds of heaven One like a son of man was coming, And He came up to the Ancient of Days And was presented before Him.

column.name: text
column.value: And to Him was given dominion, Honor, and ①a kingdom, So that all the peoples, nations, and populations of all ②languages Might serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion Which will not pass away; And His kingdom is one Which will not be destroyed. ▷ ①Or sovereignty ②Lit tongues

column.name: text
column.value: “As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within ①me, and the visions ②in my mind kept alarming me. ▷ ①Lit its sheath ②Lit of my head

column.name: text
column.value: I approached one of those who were standing by and began requesting of him the ①exact meaning of all this. So he told me and made known to me the interpretation of these things: ▷ ①Lit what was certain

column.name: text
column.value: ‘These great beasts, which are four in number, are four kings who will arise from the earth.

column.name: text
column.value: But the ①saints of the Highest One will receive the kingdom and take possession of the kingdom forever, ②for all ages to come.’ ▷ ①Lit holy ones; i.e., God’s people ②Lit and unto the age of the ages

column.name: text
column.value: “Then I desired to know the ①exact meaning of the fourth beast, which was different from all ②the others, exceedingly dreadful, with its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze, and which devoured, crushed, and trampled down the remainder with its feet, ▷ ①Lit truth concerning ②Lit of them

column.name: text

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①At this point the revelation ended. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts were greatly alarming me and my ②face became pale, but I kept the matter ③to myself.” ▷ ①Lit To here the end of the word ②Lit brightness was changing upon me ③Lit in my heart

column.name: text
column.value: In the third year of the reign of Belshazzar the king, a vision appeared to me, ①Daniel, subsequent to the one which appeared to me ②previously. ▷ ①Lit I, Daniel ②Lit at the beginning

column.name: text
column.value: I looked in the vision, and while I was looking, I was in the citadel of Susa, which is in the province of Elam; and I looked in the vision, and I myself was beside the Ulai Canal.

column.name: text
column.value: Then I raised my eyes and looked, and behold, a ram which had two horns was standing in front of the canal. Now the two horns were ①long, but one was ②longer than the other, with the ③longer one coming up last. ▷ ①Lit high(er) ②Lit high(er) ③Lit high(er)

column.name: text
column.value: I saw the ram butting westward, northward, and southward, and no other beasts could stand against him nor was there anyone to rescue from his ①power, but he did as he pleased and made himself great. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: While I was observing, behold, a male goat was coming from the west over the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground; and the goat had a prominent horn between his eyes.

column.name: text
column.value: He came up to the ram that had the two horns, which I had seen standing in front of the canal, and rushed at him in his mighty wrath.

column.name: text
column.value: And I saw him come up beside the ram, and he was enraged at him; and he struck the ram and smashed his two horns, and the ram had no strength to withstand him. So he hurled him to the ground and trampled on him, and there was no one to rescue the ram from his ①power. ▷ ①Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: Then the male goat made himself exceedingly great. But once he became powerful, the large horn was broken; and in its place four prominent horns came up toward the four winds of heaven.

column.name: text
column.value: And out of one of them came a rather small horn which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the ①Beautiful Land. ▷ ①I.e., Israel

column.name: text
column.value: It grew up to the heavenly ①lights, and some of the ②lights, ③that is, some of the stars it threw down to the earth, and it trampled them. ▷ ①Lit host ②Lit host ③Or and some of the stars

column.name: text

column.value: And because of ①an offense the army will be given to the horn along with the regular sacrifice; and it will hurl truth to the ground and do as it pleases and be successful. ▷ ①Or a wrongdoing

column.name: text
column.value: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to that particular one who was speaking, “How long will the vision about the regular sacrifice apply, ①while the offense causes horror, so as to allow both the sanctuary and the army ②to be trampled?” ▷ ①Or possibly and the offense that horrifies ②Lit as a trampling

column.name: text
column.value: And he said to me, “For 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be ①properly restored.” ▷ ①Lit justified

column.name: text
column.value: When I, Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought ①to understand it; and behold, standing before me was one ②who looked like a man. ▷ ①Lit understanding ②Lit like the appearance of a man

column.name: text
column.value: And I heard the voice of a man between the banks of Ulai, and he called out and said, “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he came near to where I was standing, and when he came I was frightened and fell on my face; and he said to me, “Son of man, understand that the vision pertains to the time of the end.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now while he was talking with me, I was dazed with my face to the ground; but he touched me and made me stand at my place.

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Behold, I am going to inform you of what will occur at the final period of the indignation, because it pertains to the appointed time of the end.

column.name: text

column.name: text
column.value: The shaggy ①goat represents the ②kingdom of Greece, and the large horn that is between his eyes is the first king. ▷ ①Lit buck ②Lit king

column.name: text
column.value: The broken horn and the four horns that came up in its place represent four kingdoms which will arise from his nation, although not with his power.

column.name: text
column.value: And in the latter period of their ①dominion, When the wrongdoers have ②run their course, A king will arise, ③Insolent and skilled in ④intrigue. ▷ ①Or kingdom ②Lit finished ③Lit Strong of face ④Or ambiguous speech

column.name: text

column.name: text

He will even ⑤oppose the Prince of princes, But he will be broken without ⑥human agency. ▷ ①Lit hand ②Lit heart ③Or ruin ④Or secure ⑤Lit stand against ⑥Lit hand

column.name: text
column.value: And the vision of the evenings and mornings Which has been told is true; But as for you, keep the vision secret, Because it pertains to many days in the future.”

column.value: So I gave my ①attention to the Lord God, to seek Him by prayer and pleading, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes. ▷ ①Lit face

column.value: So He has confirmed His words which He had spoken against us and against our ①rulers who ruled us, to bring on us great disaster; for under the entire heaven there has not been done anything like what was done in Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit judges who judged us

column.value: So I was left alone and saw this great vision; yet no strength was left in me, for my complexion turned to ①a deathly pallor, and I retained no strength. ▷ ①Lit destruction

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “ ①You who are treasured, do not be afraid. Peace be to you; take courage and be courageous!” Now as soon as he spoke to me, I felt strengthened and said, “May my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.” ▷ ①Lit man of treasure

column.name: text

And there will be a time of distress such as never occurred since there was a nation until that time; and at that time your people, everyone who is found written in the book, will be rescued.

column.name: text
column.value: And the king of the South will be enraged and go out and fight ①with the king of the North. Then the latter will raise a great multitude, but that multitude will be handed over to ②the former. ▷ ①Lit with him, with ②Lit his hand

column.name: text
column.value: When the multitude is carried away, his heart will ①be haughty, and he will cause tens of thousands to fall; yet he will not prevail. ▷ ①Lit rise

column.name: text
column.value: For the king of the North will again raise a greater multitude than the former, and ①after an interval of some years he will ②press on with a great army and much equipment. ▷ ①Lit at the end of the times, years ②Or keep on coming

column.name: text
column.value: “Now in those times many will rise up against the king of the South; the violent ones among your people will also raise themselves up to fulfill the vision, but they will ①fall down. ▷ ①Lit stumble, and so throughout the ch

column.name: text
column.value: Then the king of the North will come, pile up an assault ramp, and capture a well-fortified city; and the forces of the South will not stand their ground, not even ①their choicest troops, for there will be no strength to make a stand. ▷ ①Lit the people of its choice ones

column.name: text
column.value: But he who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will be able to withstand him; he will also stay for a time in the ①Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand. ▷ ①I.e., Israel

column.name: text
column.value: And he will set his ①mind on coming with the power of his entire kingdom, ②bringing with him ③a proposal of peace which he will put into effect; he will also give him the daughter of women to ruin it. But she will not take a stand for him or be ④on his side. ▷ ①Lit face ②Lit and ③Lit equitable things ④Lit for him; i.e., for her father

column.name: text
column.value: Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put a stop to his taunting against him; moreover, he will repay him for his taunting.

column.name: text
column.value: So he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and not be found.

column.name: text
column.value: “Then in his place one will arise who will allow an ①oppressor to pass through the ②Jewel of his kingdom; yet within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger nor in battle. ▷ ①Or tax collector ②Lit splendor; i.e., prob. Jerusalem and its temple

column.name: text
column.value: And in his place a despicable person will arise, on whom the majesty of kingship has not been conferred; but he will come in a time of tranquility and seize the kingdom by intrigue.

column.name: text
column.value: And the overflowing forces will be flooded away from him and smashed, and also the prince of the covenant.

column.name: text
column.value: After an alliance is made with him he will practice deception, and he will go up and gain power with a small force of people.

column.name: text
column.value: ①In a time of tranquility he will enter the richest parts of the ②realm, and he will accomplish what his fathers did not, nor his ③ancestors; he will distribute plunder, spoils, and possessions among them, and he will devise his schemes against strongholds, but only for a time. ▷ ①Lit In tranquility and the rich...he will enter ②Lit province ③Lit fathers’ fathers

column.name: text
column.value: And he will stir up his strength and ①courage against the king of the South with a large army; so the king of the South will mobilize an extremely large and mighty army for war; but he will not stand, because schemes will be devised against him. ▷ ①Lit heart

column.name: text
column.value: Those who eat his choice food will ①destroy him, and his army will ②overflow, but many will fall down slain. ▷ ①Lit break ②Or be swept away, and many

column.name: text
column.value: As for both kings, their hearts will be intent on evil, and they will speak lies to each other at the same table; but it will not succeed, because the end is still to come at the appointed time.

column.name: text
column.value: Then he will return to his land with much ①plunder; but his heart will be set against the holy covenant, and he will take action and then return to his own land. ▷ ①Lit property

column.name: text
column.value: “At the appointed time he will return and come into the South, but ①this last time it will not turn out the way it did before. ▷ ①Lit it will not happen as the first and as the last

column.name: text
column.value: For ships of ①Kittim will come against him; therefore he will withdraw in fear and will return and curse the holy covenant and take action; so he will come back and pay attention to those who abandon the holy covenant. ▷ ①I.e., Cyprus

column.name: text
column.value: Forces from him will arise, desecrate the sanctuary fortress, and do away with the regular sacrifice. And they will set up the abomination ①of desolation. ▷ ①Lit that makes desolate; or that causes horror

column.name: text
column.value: And by smooth words he will ①turn to godlessness those who act wickedly toward the covenant, but the people who know their God will be strong and take action. ▷ ①Or ruin those

column.name: text
column.value: And ①those who have insight among the people will give understanding to the many; yet they will fall by sword and by flame, by captivity and by plunder for many days. ▷ ①Or instructors of the people will

column.name: text
column.value: Now when they fall they will be granted a little help, and many will join with them in hypocrisy.

column.name: text
column.value: And some of ①those who have insight will fall, to refine, purge, and ②cleanse them until the end time; because it is still to come at the appointed time. ▷ ①Or the instructors ②Or whiten

column.name: text
column.value: “Then the king will do as he pleases, and he will exalt himself and boast against every god and will speak ①dreadful things against the God of gods; and he will be successful until the indignation is finished, because that which is determined will be done. ▷ ①Or amazing

column.name: text
column.value: And he will show no regard for the ①gods of his fathers or for the ②desire of women, nor will he show regard for any other god; for he will boast against them all. ▷ ①Or God ②Or darling of

column.name: text
column.value: But ①instead he will honor a god of fortresses, a god whom his fathers did not know; he will honor him with gold, silver, precious stones, and treasures. ▷ ①Lit in his place

column.name: text
column.value: And he will take action against the strongest of fortresses with the help of a foreign god; he will give great honor to ①those who acknowledge him and will make them rulers over the many, and will parcel out land for a price. ▷ ①Lit the one who acknowledges

column.name: text
column.value: “And at the end time the king of the South will wage war with him, and the king of the North will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and with many ships; and he will enter countries, overflow them, and pass through.

column.name: text
column.value: He will also enter the ①Beautiful Land, and many countries will fall; but these will be rescued out of his hand: Edom, Moab, and the foremost of the sons of Ammon. ▷ ①I.e., Israel

column.name: text
column.value: Then he will reach out with his hand against other countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.

column.name: text
column.value: But he will ①gain control over the hidden treasures of gold and silver, and over all the precious things of Egypt; and Libyans and Ethiopians will follow at his ②heels. ▷ ①Lit rule over ②Lit footsteps

column.name: text
column.value: But rumors from the East and from the North will terrify him, and he will go out with great wrath to eliminate and ①annihilate many. ▷ ①Lit devote many to destruction

column.name: text
column.value: And he will pitch the tents of his royal pavilion between the seas and the beautiful Holy Mountain; yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

column.name: text
column.value: ①Say to your brothers, “ ②Ammi,” and to your sisters, “ ③Ruhamah.” ▷ ①Ch

column.name: text
column.value: “Dispute with your mother, dispute, Because she is not my wife, and I am not her husband; But she must remove her infidelity from her face And her adultery from between her breasts,

column.name: text
column.value: Otherwise, I will strip her naked And expose her as on the day she was born. I will also make her like a wilderness, Make her like desert land, And put her to death with thirst.

column.name: text
column.value: Also, I will take no pity on her children, Because they are children of infidelity.

column.name: text
column.value: For their mother has committed prostitution; She who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, ‘I will go after my lovers, Who give me my bread and my water, My wool and my flax, my oil and my drink.’

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, behold, I will obstruct ①her way with thorns, And I will build ②a stone wall against her so that she cannot find her paths. ▷ ①As in some ancient versions; MT your ②Lit her stone wall so that

column.name: text
column.value: And she will pursue her lovers, but she will not reach them; And she will seek them, but will not find them. Then she will say, ‘I will go back to my first husband, Because it was better for me then than now!’

column.name: text
column.value: “Yet she does not know that it was I myself who gave her the grain, the new wine, and the oil, And lavished on her silver and gold, Which they ①used for Baal. ▷ ①Or made into the

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, I will ①take back My grain at ②harvest time And My new wine in its season. I will also take away My wool and My flax That I gave to cover her nakedness. ▷ ①Lit return and take My ②Lit its time

column.name: text
column.value: So now I will uncover her ①lewdness Before the eyes of her lovers, And no one will rescue her from My hand. ▷ ①Or shame

column.name: text
column.value: I will also put an end to all her joy, Her feasts, her new moons, her Sabbaths, And all her festivals.

column.name: text
column.value: And I will destroy her vines and fig trees, Of which she said, ‘They are my wages for prostitution Which my lovers have given me.’ And I will turn them into a forest, And the animals of the field will devour them.

column.name: text
column.value: I will punish her for the days of the Baals When she used to ①offer sacrifices to them And adorn herself with her nose ring and jewelry, And follow her lovers, so that she forgot Me,” declares the LORD. ▷ ①Or burn incense

column.name: text
column.value: “Therefore, behold, I am going to persuade her, Bring her into the wilderness, And speak ①kindly to her. ▷ ①Lit upon her heart

column.name: text
column.value: Then I will give her her vineyards from there, And the ①Valley of Achor as a door of hope. And she will ②respond there as in the days of her youth, As in the day when she went up from the land of Egypt. ▷ ①Lit Valley of Trouble ②Or give answer

column.name: text
column.value: And it will come about on that day,” declares the LORD, “That you will call Me ①my husband And no longer call Me my ②Baal. ▷ ①Heb Ishi ②Also meaning husband in Heb, besides a name for false gods

column.name: text
column.value: For I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, So that they will no longer be ①mentioned by their names. ▷ ①Or remembered

column.name: text
column.value: On that day I will also make a covenant for them With the animals of the field, The birds of the sky, And the crawling things of the ground. And I will ①eliminate the bow, the sword, and war from the land, And will let them lie down in safety. ▷ ①Lit break

column.name: text
text
column.value: And I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness. Then you will know the LORD.

column.name: text
column.value: “And it will come about on that day that I will respond,” declares the LORD. “I will respond to the heavens, and they will respond to the earth,

column.name: text
column.value: And the earth will respond to the grain, to the new wine, and to the oil, And they will respond to ①Jezreel. ▷ ①I.e., God sows

column.name: text
column.value: I will sow her for Myself in the land. I will also have compassion on ①her who had not obtained compassion, And I will say to ②those who were not My people, ‘You are My people!’ And ③they will say, ‘You are my God!’ ” ▷ ①Heb Lo-ruhamah ②Heb Lo-ammi ③Lit he

column.name: text
