column.value: Therefore, be on the alert, remembering that night and day for a period of three years I did not cease to admonish each one with tears.

column.name: text
column.value: And now I entrust you to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and to give you the inheritance among all those who are sanctified.

column.name: text
column.value: I have coveted no one’s silver or gold or clothes.

column.name: text
column.value: You yourselves know that these hands served my own needs and the men who were with me.

column.name: text
column.value: In everything I showed you that by working hard in this way you must help the weak and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that He Himself said, ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: When he had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.

column.name: text
column.value: And ①they all began to weep aloud and ②embraced Paul, and repeatedly kissed him, ▷ ①Lit a considerable weeping of all occurred ②Lit threw themselves on Paul’s neck

column.name: text
column.value: ①grieving especially over the word which he had spoken, that they would not see his face again. And they were accompanying him to the ship. ▷ ①Lit suffering pain

column.name: text
column.value: Now it happened that while Apollos was in Corinth, Paul passed through the upper country and came to Ephesus, and found some disciples.

column.name: text
column.value: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” And they said to him, “On the contrary, we have not even heard if there is a Holy Spirit.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “Into what then were you baptized?” And they said, “Into John’s baptism.”

column.name: text
column.value: Paul said, “John baptized with a baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe in Him who was coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this, they were baptized ①in the name of the Lord Jesus. ▷ ①Lit into

column.name: text
column.value: And when Paul had laid hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them and they began speaking with tongues and prophesying.

column.name: text
column.value: There were about twelve men in all.

column.name: text
column.value: And he entered the synagogue and continued speaking out boldly for three months, having discussions and persuading them about the kingdom of God.

column.name: text
column.value: But when some were becoming hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of ①the Way before the ②people, he withdrew from them and took the disciples away with him, and had discussions daily in the school of Tyrannus. ▷ ①See John

column.name: text
column.value: This took place for two years, so that all who lived in ①Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks. ▷ ①I.e., west coast province of Asia Minor

column.name: text
column.value: God was performing extraordinary ①miracles by the hands of Paul, ▷ ①Or works of power

column.name: text
column.value: so that handkerchiefs or aprons were even carried from his body to the sick, and the diseases left them and the evil spirits went out.

column.name: text
column.value: But also some of the Jewish exorcists, who went from place to place, attempted to ①use the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had the evil spirits, saying, “I order you in the name of Jesus whom Paul preaches!” ▷ ①I.e., as an incantation

column.name: text
column.value: Now there were seven sons of ①Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, doing this. ▷ ①Lit some Sceva

column.name: text
column.value: But the evil spirit responded and said to them, “I recognize Jesus, and I know of Paul, but who are you?”

column.name: text
column.value: And the man in whom was the evil spirit, pounced on them and subdued all of them and overpowered them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

column.name: text
column.value: This became known to all who lived in Ephesus, both Jews and Greeks; and fear fell upon them all and the name of the Lord Jesus was being magnified.

column.name: text
column.value: Also many of those who had believed kept coming, confessing and disclosing their practices.

column.name: text
column.value: And many of those who practiced magic brought their books together and began burning them in the sight of everyone; and they added up the prices of ①the books and found it to be fifty thousand ②pieces of silver. ▷ ①Lit them ②Prob. Greek drachmas; a drachma was a day’s wages for a laborer

column.name: text
column.value: So ①the word of the Lord was growing and prevailing mightily. ▷ ①Or according to the power of the Lord the word was growing

column.name: text
column.value: Now after these things were finished, Paul resolved in ①the Spirit to go to Jerusalem after he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.” ▷ ①Or his spirit

column.name: text
column.value: And after he sent into Macedonia two of those who assisted him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in ①Asia for a while. ▷ ①I.e., west coast province of Asia Minor

column.name: text
column.value: About that time ①a major disturbance occurred in regard to ②the Way. ▷ ①Lit no small ②See John

column.name: text
column.value: For a man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of ①Artemis, was bringing ②considerable ③business to the craftsmen; ▷ ①Lat Diana ②Lit no little ③Or profit

column.name: text
column.value: he gathered these men together with the workmen of similar trades, and said, “Men, you know that our prosperity ①depends upon this business. ▷ ①Lit is from

column.name: text
column.value: You see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in almost all of ①Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a considerable number of people, saying that ②gods made by hands are not gods at all. ▷ ①See note v 22 ②Lit those

column.name: text
column.value: Not only is there danger that this trade of ours will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess ①Artemis will be regarded as worthless, and that she whom all of ②Asia and the ③world worship will even be dethroned from her magnificence.” ▷ ①Lat Diana ②See note v 22 ③Lit the inhabited earth

column.name: text
column.value: When they heard this and were filled with rage, they began shouting, saying, “Great is ①Artemis of the Ephesians!” ▷ ①Lat Diana

column.name: text
column.value: The city was filled with the confusion, and they rushed together into the theater, dragging along Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s Macedonian traveling companions.

column.name: text
column.value: And when Paul wanted to go into the assembly, the disciples would not let him.

column.name: text
column.value: Also some of the ①Asiarchs who were friends of his sent word to him and repeatedly urged him not to ②venture into the theater. ▷ ①I.e., political or religious officials of the province of Asia ②Lit give himself

column.name: text
column.value: So then, some were shouting one thing and some another, for the ①assembly was in confusion and the majority did not know ②for what reason they had come together. ▷ ①Gr ekklesia ②Or on whose account

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the crowd ①concluded it was Alexander, since the Jews had put him forward; and having motioned with his hand, Alexander was intending to make a defense to the assembly. ▷ ①Or advised Alexander

column.name: text
column.value: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, a single outcry arose from them all as they shouted for about two hours, “Great is ①Artemis of the Ephesians!” ▷ ①Lat Diana

column.name: text
column.value: After quieting the crowd, the town clerk *said, “Men of Ephesus, what person is there after all who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is guardian of the temple of the great ①Artemis and of the image which fell down from ②the sky? ▷ ①Lat Diana ②Lit Zeus; Lat Jupiter

column.name: text
column.value: So, since these are undeniable facts, you ought to keep calm and to do nothing rash.

column.name: text
column.value: For you have brought these men here who are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.

column.name: text
column.value: So then, if Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a complaint against anyone, the courts are in session and ①proconsuls are available; have them bring charges against one another. ▷ ①Or provincial governors

column.name: text
column.value: But if you want anything beyond this, it shall be settled in the ①lawful ②assembly. ▷ ①Or regular ②Gr ekklesia

column.name: text
column.value: For indeed, we are in danger of being accused of a riot in connection with today’s events, since there is no real reason for it, and in this connection we will be unable to account for this disorderly gathering.”

column.name: text
column.value: After saying this he dismissed the ①assembly. ▷ ①Gr ekklesia

column.name: text
column.value: Now when we had parted from them and had set sail, we ran a straight course to Cos, and on the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara;

column.name: text
column.value: and having found a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.

column.name: text
column.value: When we came in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left, we kept sailing to Syria and landed at Tyre; for the ship was to unload its cargo there.

column.name: text
column.value: After looking up the disciples, we stayed there for seven days; and they kept telling Paul, ①through the Spirit, not to set foot in Jerusalem. ▷ ①I.e., because of impressions made by the Spirit

column.name: text
column.value: When ①our days there were ended, we left and started on our journey, while they all, with wives and children, escorted us until we were out of the city. After kneeling down on the beach and praying, we said farewell to one another. ▷ ①Lit we had completed the days

column.name: text
column.value: Then we boarded the ship, and they returned home.

column.name: text
column.value: When we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais, and after greeting the brothers and sisters, we stayed with them for a day.

column.name: text
column.value: On the next day we left and came to Caesarea, and we entered the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, and stayed with him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now this man had four virgin daughters who were prophetesses.

column.name: text
column.value: As we were staying there for some days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.

column.name: text
column.value: And he came to us and took Paul’s belt and bound his own feet and hands, and said, “This is what the Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the man who owns this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: When we had heard this, we as well as the local residents began begging him not to go up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul replied, “What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but even to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”

column.name: text
column.value: And since he would not be persuaded, we became quiet, remarking, “The will of the Lord be done!”

column.name: text
column.value: After these days we got ready and started on our way up to Jerusalem.

column.name: text
column.value: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also came with us, taking us to Mnason of Cyprus, a disciple of long standing with whom we were to stay.

column.name: text
column.value: After we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers and sisters received us gladly.

column.name: text
column.value: And the following day Paul went in with us to ①James, and all the elders were present. ▷ ①Or Jacob

column.name: text
column.value: After he had greeted them, he began to relate one by one the things which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they heard about them, they began glorifying God; and they said to him, “You see, brother, how many ①thousands there are among the Jews of those who have believed, and they are all zealous for the Law; ▷ ①Lit ten thousands

column.name: text
column.value: and they have been told about you, that you are teaching all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to abandon Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to ①walk according to the customs. ▷ ①I.e., observe or live by

column.name: text
column.value: So what is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, do ①as we tell you: we have four men who have a ②vow upon themselves; ▷ ①Lit this which we ②I.e., a sacred duty to fulfill

column.name: text
column.value: take them along and purify yourself together with them, and ①pay their expenses so that they may shave their ②heads; and then everyone will know that there is nothing to what they have been told about you, but that you yourself also conform, keeping the Law. ▷ ①Lit spend on them ②Lit head (a requirement of the vow)

column.name: text
column.value: But regarding the Gentiles who have believed, we sent a letter, having decided that they should abstain from ①meat sacrificed to idols and from blood and what is ②strangled, and from sexual immorality.” ▷ ①Lit the thing ②I.e., to retain the blood

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul ①took along the men, and the next day, after purifying himself together with them, he went into the temple giving notice of the completion of the days of purification, until the sacrifice was offered for each one of them. ▷ ①Or took along the men the next day, and after purifying himself

column.name: text
column.value: When the seven days were almost over, the Jews from ①Asia, upon seeing him in the temple, began to stir up all the crowd and laid hands on him, ▷ ①I.e., west coast province of Asia Minor

column.name: text
column.value: crying out, “Men of Israel, help! This is the man who instructs everyone everywhere against our people and the Law and this place; and besides, he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place!”

column.name: text
column.value: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian in the city with him, and they thought that Paul had brought him into the temple.

column.name: text
column.value: Then the whole city was provoked and ①the people rushed together, and taking hold of Paul they dragged him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were shut. ▷ ①Lit a running together of the people occurred

column.name: text
column.value: While they were intent on killing him, a report came up to the commander of the Roman ①cohort that all Jerusalem was in confusion. ▷ ①Normally 600 men (the number varied)

column.name: text
column.value: He immediately took along some soldiers and centurions and ran down to ①the crowd; and when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul. ▷ ①Lit them

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commander came up and took hold of him, and ordered that he be bound with two chains; and he began asking who he was and what he had done.

column.name: text
column.value: But among the crowd, some were shouting one thing and some another, and when he could not find out the ①facts because of the uproar, he ordered that ②Paul be brought into the barracks. ▷ ①Lit certainty ②Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: When Paul got to the stairs, it came about that he was carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the ①mob; ▷ ①Lit crowd

column.name: text
column.value: for the multitude of people kept following them, shouting, “Away with him!”

column.name: text
column.value: As Paul was about to be brought into the barracks, he *said to the commander, “May I say something to you?” And he said, “Do you know Greek?

column.name: text
column.value: Then you are not the Egyptian who some ①time ago stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?” ▷ ①Lit days

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul said, “I am a Jew of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city; and I beg you, allow me to speak to the people.”

column.name: text
column.value: When he had given him permission, Paul, standing on the stairs, motioned to the people with his hand; and when there ①was a great silence, he spoke to them in the ②Hebrew dialect, saying, ▷ ①Lit occurred ②I.e., Jewish Aramaic

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①Brothers and fathers, hear my defense which I now offer to you.” ▷ ①Lit Men, brothers

column.name: text
column.value: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the ①Hebrew dialect, they became even more quiet; and he *said, ▷ ①I.e., Jewish Aramaic

column.name: text
column.value: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, educated ①under Gamaliel, ②strictly according to the Law of our fathers, being zealous for God just as you all are today. ▷ ①Lit at the feet of ②Lit according to the strictness of the ancestral law

column.name: text
column.value: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and putting both men and women into prisons,

column.name: text
column.value: as also the high priest and all the Council of the elders ①can testify. From them I also received letters to the brothers, and started off for Damascus in order to bring even those who were there to Jerusalem ②as prisoners to be punished. ▷ ①Lit testifies for me ②Lit having been bound

column.name: text
column.value: “But it happened that as I was on my way, approaching Damascus at about noon, a very bright light suddenly flashed from heaven all around me,

column.name: text
column.value: and I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?’

column.name: text
column.value: And I answered, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And He said to me, ‘I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom you are persecuting.’

column.name: text
column.value: And those who were with me saw the light, but did not ①understand the voice of the One who was speaking to me. ▷ ①Or hear (with comprehension)

column.name: text
column.value: And I said, ‘What shall I do, Lord?’ And the Lord said to me, ‘Get up and go on into Damascus, and there you will be told about everything that has been appointed for you to do.’

column.name: text
column.value: But since I could not see because of the ①brightness of that light, I came into Damascus being led by the hand by those who were with me. ▷ ①Lit glory

column.name: text
column.value: “Now a certain Ananias, a man who was devout by the standard of the Law and well spoken of by all the Jews who lived there,

column.name: text
column.value: came to me, and standing nearby he said to me, ‘Brother Saul, receive your sight!’ And ①at that very moment I looked up at him. ▷ ①Or instantly; lit at the very hour

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear a ①message from His mouth. ▷ ①Lit voice

column.name: text
column.value: For you will be a witness for Him to all people of what you have seen and heard.

column.name: text
column.value: Now why do you delay? Get up and be baptized, and wash away your sins by calling on His name.’

column.name: text
column.value: “It happened when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance,

column.name: text
column.value: and I saw Him saying to me, ‘Hurry and get out of Jerusalem quickly, because they will not accept your testimony about Me.’

column.name: text
column.value: And I said, ‘Lord, they themselves understand that in one synagogue after another I used to imprison and beat those who believed in You.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was being shed, I also was standing nearby and approving, and watching over the cloaks of those who were killing him.’

column.name: text
column.value: And He said to me, ‘Go! For I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: They listened to him up to this statement, and then they raised their voices and said, “Away with such a man from the earth, for he should not be allowed to live!”

column.name: text
column.value: And as they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,

column.name: text
column.value: the commander ordered that he be brought into the barracks, saying that he was to be interrogated by flogging so that he would find out the reason why they were shouting against him that way.

column.name: text
column.value: But when they stretched him out ①with straps, Paul said to the centurion who was standing by, “Is it ②lawful for you to flog a man who is a Roman and uncondemned?” ▷ ①Or for the whip ②Interrogation by torture was a procedure used with slaves

column.name: text
column.value: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and told him, saying, “What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman.”

column.name: text
column.value: The commander came and said to ①Paul, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” And he said, “Yes.” ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: The commander answered, “I acquired this citizenship for a large sum of money.” And Paul said, “But I was actually born a citizen.”

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, those who were about to interrogate him immediately backed away from him; and the commander also was afraid when he found out that he was a Roman, and because he had ①put him in chains. ▷ ①Lit bound him

column.name: text
column.value: Now on the next day, wanting to know for certain why Paul had been accused by the Jews, he released him and ordered the chief priests and all the ①Council to assemble, and he brought Paul down and placed him before them. ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin

column.name: text
column.value: Now looking intently at the ①Council, Paul said, “ ②Brothers, I have ③lived my life with an entirely good conscience before God up to this day.” ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin ②Lit Men, brothers ③Or conducted myself as a citizen

column.name: text
column.value: But the high priest Ananias commanded those standing beside him to strike him on the mouth.

column.name: text
column.value: Then Paul said to him, “God is going to strike you, you whitewashed wall! Do you sit to try me according to the Law, and in violation of the Law, order me to be struck?”

column.name: text
column.value: But those present said, “Are you insulting God’s high priest?”

column.name: text
column.value: And Paul said, “I was not aware, brothers, that he is high priest; for it is written: ‘YOU SHALL NOT SPEAK EVIL OF A RULER OF YOUR PEOPLE.’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul, perceiving that one group were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, began crying out in the ①Council, “ ②Brothers, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; I am on trial for the hope and resurrection of the dead!” ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin ②Lit Men, brothers

column.name: text
column.value: When he said this, a dissension occurred between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.

column.name: text
column.value: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, nor an angel, nor a spirit, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.

column.name: text
column.value: And a great uproar occurred; and some of the scribes of the Pharisaic party stood up and started arguing heatedly, saying, “We find nothing wrong with this man; suppose a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”

column.name: text
column.value: And when a great dissension occurred, the commander was afraid that Paul would be torn to pieces by them, and he ordered the troops to go down and take him away from them by force, and bring him into the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: But on the following night, the Lord stood near him and said, “Be courageous! For as you have testified to the truth about Me in Jerusalem, so you must testify in Rome also.”

column.name: text
column.value: When it was day, the Jews formed a ①conspiracy and put themselves under an ②oath, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had killed Paul. ▷ ①Or mob ②I.e., an oath with a self-imposed curse

column.name: text
column.value: There were more than forty who formed this plot.

column.name: text
column.value: They came to the chief priests and the elders and said, “We have put ourselves under an ①oath to taste nothing until we have killed Paul. ▷ ①See note 2 v 12

column.name: text
column.value: Now therefore, you ①and the ②Council notify the commander to bring him down to you, as though you were going to investigate his case more thoroughly; and as for us, we are ready to kill him before he comes near the place.” ▷ ①Lit with ②Or Sanhedrin

column.name: text
column.value: But the son of Paul’s sister heard about their ambush, ①and he came and entered the barracks and told Paul. ▷ ①Or having been present with them, and he also entered

column.name: text
column.value: Paul called one of the centurions to himself and said, “Take this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So he took him and led him to the commander and *said, “Paul the prisoner called me over to him and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you.”

column.name: text
column.value: The commander took him by the hand, and stepping aside, began to inquire of him privately, “What is it that you have to report to me?”

column.name: text
column.value: And he said, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down tomorrow to the ①Council, as though they were going to inquire somewhat more thoroughly about him. ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin

column.name: text
column.value: So do not ①listen to them, for more than forty ②of them are in hiding to ambush him, and these men have put themselves under an oath not to eat or drink until they kill him; and now they are ready and waiting for assurance from you.” ▷ ①Lit be persuaded by them ②Lit men of them

column.name: text
column.value: Then the commander let the young man go, instructing him, “Tell no one that you have notified me of these things.”

column.name: text
column.value: And he called to him two of the centurions and said, “Get two hundred soldiers ready by ①the third hour of the night to proceed to Caesarea, ②with seventy horsemen and two hundred ③spearmen.” ▷ ①I.e., 9 p.m. ②Lit and ③Or slingers; or bowmen

column.name: text
column.value: They were also to provide mounts to put Paul on and bring him safely to Felix the governor.

column.name: text
column.value: And he wrote a letter ①with the following content: ▷ ①Or to this effect

column.name: text
column.value: “Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.

column.name: text
column.value: When this man was seized by the Jews and was about to be killed by them, I came up to them with the troops and rescued him, after learning that he was a Roman.

column.name: text
column.value: And wanting to ascertain the basis for the charges they were bringing against him, I brought him down to their ①Council; ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin

column.name: text
column.value: and I found that he was being accused regarding questions in their Law, but ①was not charged with anything deserving death or ②imprisonment. ▷ ①Lit had no charge of ②Lit bonds

column.name: text
column.value: When I was informed that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once, also instructing his accusers to ①bring charges against him before you.” ▷ ①Lit speak against him

column.name: text
column.value: So the soldiers, in accordance with their orders, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

column.name: text
column.value: But on the next day they let the horsemen go on with him, and they returned to the barracks.

column.name: text
column.value: When these horsemen had come to Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul to him.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when he had read it, he also asked from what province Paul was, and when he learned that he was from Cilicia,

column.name: text
column.value: he said, “I will give you a hearing when your accusers arrive as well,” giving orders for ①Paul to be kept in Herod’s ②Praetorium. ▷ ①Lit him ②I.e., governor’s official residence

column.name: text
column.value: Now after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and an attorney named Tertullus, and they ①brought charges against Paul to the governor. ▷ ①Or presented their evidence or case

column.name: text
column.value: After ①Paul had been summoned, Tertullus began accusing him, saying to the governor, “Since we have attained great peace through you, and since reforms are being carried out for this nation by your foresight, ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: we acknowledge this in every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

column.name: text
column.value: But, that I may not ①weary you further, I beg you ②to grant us a brief hearing, by your kindness. ▷ ①Or impose on ②Lit to hear...briefly

column.name: text
column.value: For we have found this man a public menace and one who stirs up dissensions among all the Jews throughout ①the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes. ▷ ①Lit the inhabited earth

column.name: text
column.value: And he even tried to desecrate the temple, so indeed we arrested him. ① ▷ ①Late mss add as the remainder of v 6: We wanted to judge him according to our own Law. v 7: But Lysias the commander came along and took him out of our hands with much violence, and the first part of v 8: ordering his accusers to come before you.

column.name: text
column.value: By interrogating him yourself concerning all these matters, you will be able to ascertain the things of which we are accusing him.”

column.name: text
column.value: The Jews also joined in the attack, asserting that these things were so.

column.name: text
column.value: And when the governor had nodded for him to speak, Paul responded: “Knowing that for many years you have been a judge to this nation, I cheerfully make my defense,

column.name: text
column.value: since you can take note of the fact that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.

column.name: text
column.value: And neither in the temple did they find me carrying on a discussion with anyone or causing ①a riot, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city itself. ▷ ①Lit an attack of a mob

column.name: text
column.value: Nor can they prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.

column.name: text
column.value: But I confess this to you, that in accordance with ①the Way, which they call a sect, I do serve the God of our fathers, believing everything that is in accordance with the Law and is written in the Prophets; ▷ ①See John

column.name: text
column.value: having a hope in God, which these men cherish themselves, that there shall certainly be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked.

column.name: text
column.value: In view of this I also do my best to maintain a blameless conscience both before God and before other people, always.

column.name: text
column.value: Now after several years I came to bring charitable gifts to my nation and to present offerings,

column.name: text
column.value: in which they found me occupied in the temple, having been purified, without any crowd or uproar. But there were some Jews from ①Asia— ▷ ①I.e., west coast province of Asia Minor

column.name: text
column.value: who ought to have been present before you and to have been bringing charges, if they should have anything against me.

column.name: text
column.value: Or else have these men themselves declare what violation they discovered when I stood before the ①Council, ▷ ①Or Sanhedrin

column.name: text
column.value: other than in regard to this one declaration which I shouted while standing among them, ‘For the resurrection of the dead I am on trial before you today!’ ”

column.name: text
column.value: But Felix, ①having quite accurate knowledge about ②the Way, adjourned them, saying, “When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case.” ▷ ①Lit knowing more accurately ②See John

column.name: text
column.value: He gave orders to the centurion for ①Paul to be kept in custody and yet have some freedom, and not to prevent any of his friends from providing for his needs. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Now some days later Felix arrived with Drusilla his ①wife, who was Jewish, and he sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus. ▷ ①Lit own wife

column.name: text
column.value: But as he was discussing righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix became frightened and responded, “Go away for now, and when I have an opportunity, I will summon you.”

column.name: text
column.value: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given to him by Paul; therefore he also used to send for him quite often and talk with him.

column.name: text
column.value: But after two years had passed, Felix ①was succeeded by Porcius Festus; and Felix, wanting to do the Jews a favor, left Paul imprisoned. ▷ ①Lit received as a successor, Porcius Festus

column.name: text
column.value: Festus, then, after arriving in the province, went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea three days later.

column.name: text
column.value: And the chief priests and the leading men of the Jews brought charges against Paul, and they were pleading with ①Festus, ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: requesting a ①concession against ②Paul, that he might ③have him brought to Jerusalem (at the same time, setting an ambush to kill him on the way). ▷ ①Or favor ②Lit him ③Lit summon him to Jerusalem

column.name: text
column.value: Festus then answered that Paul was being kept in custody in Caesarea, and that he himself was about to leave shortly.

column.name: text
column.value: “Therefore,” he *said, “have the influential men among you ①go there with me, and if there is anything wrong ②about the man, have them bring charges against him.” ▷ ①Lit go down ②Lit in

column.name: text
column.value: After Festus had spent no more than eight or ten days among them, he went down to Caesarea, and on the next day he took his seat on the tribunal and ordered that Paul be brought.

column.name: text
column.value: After Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many, and serious, charges against him which they could not prove,

column.name: text
column.value: while Paul said in his own defense, “I have not done anything wrong either against the Law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against Caesar.”

column.name: text
column.value: But Festus, wanting to do the Jews a favor, replied to Paul and said, “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and ①stand trial before me on these charges?” ▷ ①Lit be judged

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul said, “I am standing before Caesar’s tribunal, where I ought to be tried. I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you also very well know.

column.name: text
column.value: If, therefore, I am in the wrong and have committed something deserving death, I am not trying to avoid execution; but if there is nothing to the accusations which these men are bringing against me, no one can hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then when Festus had conferred with ①his council, he answered, “You have appealed to Caesar; to Caesar you shall go.” ▷ ①A different group from that mentioned in Acts

column.name: text
column.value: Now when several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived in Caesarea, paying their respects to Festus.

column.name: text
column.value: And while they were spending many days there, Festus presented Paul’s case to the king, saying, “There is a man who was left as a prisoner by Felix;

column.name: text
column.value: and when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought charges against him, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.

column.name: text
column.value: I replied to them that it is not the custom of the Romans to hand over any person before the accused meets his accusers face to face, and has an opportunity to make his defense against the charges.

column.name: text
column.value: So after they had assembled here, I did not delay, but on the next day took my seat on the tribunal and ordered that the man be brought.

column.name: text
column.value: When the accusers stood up, they did not begin bringing any charges ①against him of crimes that I suspected, ▷ ①Lit in regard to him

column.name: text
column.value: but they simply had some points of disagreement with him about their own ①religion and about a dead man, Jesus, whom Paul asserted to be alive. ▷ ①Or superstition

column.name: text
column.value: And being at a loss how to investigate ①such matters, I ②asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and stand trial there on these matters. ▷ ①Lit these ②Lit said

column.name: text
column.value: But when Paul appealed to be held in custody for ①the Emperor’s decision, I ordered that he be kept in custody until I send him to Caesar.” ▷ ①Lit the Augustus’ (in this case Nero)

column.name: text
column.value: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I also would like to hear the man myself.” “Tomorrow,” he *said, “you shall hear him.”

column.name: text
column.value: So, on the next day when Agrippa and Bernice came amid great pomp and entered the auditorium, ①accompanied by the commanders and the prominent men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought before them. ▷ ①Lit and with

column.name: text
column.value: And Festus *said, “King Agrippa, and all you gentlemen present with us, you see this man about whom all the people of the Jews appealed to me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.

column.name: text
column.value: But I found that he had committed nothing deserving death; and since he himself appealed to ①the Emperor, I decided to send him. ▷ ①See note v 21

column.name: text
column.value: ①Yet, I have nothing definite about him to write to my lord. Therefore, I have brought him before you all and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the investigation has taken place, I may have something to write. ▷ ①Lit About whom I

column.name: text
column.value: For it seems absurd to me in sending a prisoner, not to indicate the charges against him as well.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now Agrippa said to Paul, “You are permitted to speak for yourself.” Then Paul extended his hand and proceeded to make his defense:

column.name: text
column.value: “Regarding all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate that I am about to make my defense before you today,

column.name: text
column.value: ①especially because you are an expert in all customs and ②questions among the Jews; therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently. ▷ ①Or because you are especially expert ②Or controversial issues

column.name: text
column.value: “So then, all Jews know my way of life since my youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem,

column.name: text
column.value: since they have known about me for a long time, if they are willing to testify, that I lived as a Pharisee according to the strictest sect of our religion.

column.name: text
column.value: And now I am standing trial for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers;

column.name: text
column.value: the promise to which our twelve tribes hope to attain, as they earnestly serve God night and day. For this hope, O king, I am being accused by Jews.

column.name: text
column.value: Why is it considered incredible among you people if God raises the dead?

column.name: text
column.value: “So I thought to myself that I had to act in strong opposition to the name of Jesus ①of Nazareth. ▷ ①Or the Nazarene

column.name: text
column.value: And this is ①just what I did in Jerusalem; not only did I lock up many of the ②saints in prisons, after receiving authority from the chief priests, but I also cast my vote against them when they were being put to death. ▷ ①Lit also ②Lit holy ones; i.e., God’s people

column.name: text
column.value: And as I punished them often in all the synagogues, I tried to force them to blaspheme; and since I was extremely enraged at them, I kept pursuing them even to ①foreign cities. ▷ ①Or outlying

column.name: text
column.value: “ ①While so engaged, as I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests, ▷ ①Lit In which things

column.name: text
column.value: at midday, O king, I saw on the way a light from heaven, ①brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who were journeying with me. ▷ ①Lit above the brightness of

column.name: text
column.value: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the ①Hebrew dialect, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? ②It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’ ▷ ①I.e., Jewish Aramaic ②An idiom referring to an animal’s futile resistance to being prodded with a spiked stick

column.name: text
column.value: And I said, ‘Who are You, Lord?’ And the Lord said, ‘I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.

column.name: text
column.value: But get up and stand on your feet; for this purpose I have appeared to you, to appoint you as a servant and a witness not only to the things in which you have seen Me, but also to the things in which I will appear to you,

column.name: text
column.value: rescuing you from the Jewish people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,

column.name: text
column.value: to open their eyes so that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the ①power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me.’ ▷ ①Or dominion

column.name: text
column.value: “For that reason, King Agrippa, I did not prove disobedient to the heavenly vision,

column.name: text
column.value: but continually proclaimed to those in Damascus first, and in Jerusalem, and then all the region of Judea, and even to the Gentiles, that they are to repent and turn to God, performing deeds consistent with repentance.

column.name: text
column.value: For these reasons some Jews seized me in the temple and tried to murder me.

column.name: text
column.value: So, having obtained help from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, stating nothing but what the Prophets and Moses said was going to take place,

column.name: text
column.value: as to whether the ①Christ was ②to suffer, and whether, as first from the resurrection of the dead, He would proclaim light both to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles.” ▷ ①I.e., Messiah ②Lit subject to suffering

column.name: text
column.value: While ①Paul was stating these things in his defense, Festus *said in a loud voice, “Paul, you are out of your mind! ②Your great learning is ③driving you insane.” ▷ ①Lit he ②Lit The many letters; i.e., education ③Lit turning you to madness

column.name: text
column.value: But Paul *said, “I am not insane, most excellent Festus; on the contrary, I am speaking out with ①truthful and rational words. ▷ ①Lit words of truth and rationality

column.name: text
column.value: For the king ①knows about these matters, and I also speak to him with confidence, since I am persuaded that none of these things escape his notice; for this has not been done in a ②corner. ▷ ①Or understands ②I.e., a hidden or secret place

column.name: text
column.value: King Agrippa, do you believe the Prophets? I know that you believe.”

column.name: text
column.value: Agrippa replied to Paul, “ ①In a short time you are going to persuade me to ②make a Christian of myself.” ▷ ①Or With a little ②Or act as a Christian

column.name: text
column.value: And Paul said, “I would ①wish to God that even ②in a short or long time not only you, but also all who hear me this day would become such as I myself am, except for these chains.” ▷ ①Or pray to ②Or with a little or with much

column.name: text
column.value: The king stood up and the governor and Bernice, and those who were sitting with them,

column.name: text
column.value: and when they had gone out, they began talking to one another, saying, “This man is not doing anything deserving death or ①imprisonment.” ▷ ①Lit bonds

column.name: text
column.value: And Agrippa said to Festus, “This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now when it was decided that we would sail for Italy, they proceeded to turn Paul and some other prisoners over to a centurion of the Augustan ①cohort, named Julius. ▷ ①Normally 600 men (the number varied)

column.name: text
column.value: And we boarded an Adramyttian ship that was about to sail to the regions along the coast of ①Asia, and put out to sea accompanied by Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica. ▷ ①I.e., west coast province of Asia Minor

column.name: text
column.value: The next day we put in at Sidon; and Julius treated Paul with consideration and allowed him to go to his friends and receive care.

column.name: text
column.value: From there we put out to sea and sailed under the shelter of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

column.name: text
column.value: When we had sailed through the sea along the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we landed at Myra in Lycia.

column.name: text
column.value: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy, and he put us aboard it.

column.name: text
column.value: When we had sailed slowly for a good many days, and with difficulty had arrived off Cnidus, since the wind did not permit us to go farther, we sailed under the shelter of Crete, off Salmone;

column.name: text
column.value: and with difficulty sailing past it, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.

column.name: text
column.value: When considerable time had passed and the voyage was now dangerous, since even the ①fast was already over, Paul started admonishing them, ▷ ①I.e., Day of Atonement in September or October, which was a dangerous time of year for navigation

column.name: text
column.value: saying to them, “Men, I perceive that the voyage will certainly be with damage and great loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.”

column.name: text
column.value: But the centurion was more persuaded by the pilot and the ①captain of the ship than by what was being said by Paul. ▷ ①Or owner

column.name: text
column.value: The harbor was not suitable for wintering, so the majority reached a decision to put out to sea from there, if somehow they could reach Phoenix, a harbor of Crete facing southwest and northwest, and spend the winter there.

column.name: text
column.value: ①When a moderate south wind came up, thinking that they had attained their purpose, they weighed anchor and began sailing along Crete, closer to shore. ▷ ①Lit a south wind having gently blown

column.name: text
column.value: But before very long a violent wind, called ①Euraquilo, rushed down from ②the land; ▷ ①I.e., a northeaster ②Lit it

column.name: text
column.value: and when the ship was caught in it and could not head up into the wind, we gave up and let ourselves be driven by the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: Running under the shelter of a small island called Cauda, we were able to get the ship’s ①boat under control only with difficulty. ▷ ①Or skiff: a small boat in tow for emergencies, transportation to and from shore, etc.

column.name: text
column.value: After they had hoisted it up, they used ①supporting cables in undergirding the ship; and fearing that they might run aground on the shallows of Syrtis, they let down the ②sea anchor and let themselves be driven along in this way. ▷ ①Lit helps ②Lit implement, an object designed to stabilize a boat from the stern against the wind.

column.name: text
column.value: The next day as we were being violently tossed by the storm, ①they began to jettison the cargo; ▷ ①Lit they were doing a throwing out

column.name: text
column.value: and on the third day they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.

column.name: text
column.value: Since neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small storm was assailing us, from then on all hope of our being saved was slowly abandoned.

column.name: text
column.value: ①When many had lost their appetites, Paul then stood among them and said, “ ②Men, you should have followed my advice and not have set sail from Crete, and thereby spared yourselves this damage and loss. ▷ ①Lit there being much lack of appetite ②Lit O men

column.name: text
column.value: And yet now I urge you to keep up your courage, for there will be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.

column.name: text
column.value: For this very night an angel of the God to whom I belong, whom I also serve, came to me,

column.name: text
column.value: saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and behold, God has graciously granted you all those who are sailing with you.’

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, keep up your courage, men, for I believe God that ①it will turn out exactly as I have been told. ▷ ①Lit it will be

column.name: text
column.value: But we must run aground on a certain island.”

column.name: text
column.value: But when the fourteenth night came, as we were being driven about in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors began to suspect that ①they were approaching some land. ▷ ①Lit some land was approaching them

column.name: text
column.value: And they took soundings and found it to be twenty fathoms; and a little farther on they took another sounding and found it to be fifteen fathoms.

column.name: text
column.value: Fearing that we might run aground somewhere on the ①rocks, they cast four anchors from the stern and ②prayed for daybreak. ▷ ①Lit rough places ②Or wished for

column.name: text
column.value: But as the sailors were trying to escape from the ship and had let down the ship’s boat into the sea, on the pretense that they were going to lay out anchors from the bow,

column.name: text
column.value: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain on the ship, you yourselves cannot be saved.”

column.name: text
column.value: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship’s boat and let it fall away.

column.name: text
column.value: Until the day was about to dawn, Paul kept encouraging them all to take some food, saying, “Today is the fourteenth day that you have been constantly watching and going without eating, having taken in nothing.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, I encourage you to take some food, for this is for your survival, for not a hair from the head of any of you will perish.”

column.name: text
column.value: Having said this, he took bread and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all, and he broke it and began to eat.

column.name: text
column.value: All of them ①were encouraged and they themselves also took food. ▷ ①Lit became cheerful

column.name: text
column.value: We were 276 ①people on the ship in all. ▷ ①Lit souls

column.name: text
column.value: When they had eaten enough, they began lightening the ship by throwing the wheat out into the sea.

column.name: text
column.value: Now when day came, they ①could not recognize the land; but they did notice a bay with a beach, and they resolved to run the ship onto it if they could. ▷ ①Lit were not recognizing

column.name: text
column.value: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea while at the same time they were loosening the ropes of the rudders; and they hoisted the foresail to the wind and were heading for the beach.

column.name: text
column.value: But they struck a ①reef where two seas met and ran the ship aground; and the prow stuck firmly and remained immovable, while the stern started to break up due to the force of the waves. ▷ ①Lit place

column.name: text
column.value: The soldiers’ plan was to kill the prisoners, so that none of them would swim away and escape;

column.name: text
column.value: but the centurion, wanting to bring Paul safely through, kept them from accomplishing their intention, and commanded that those who could swim were to ①jump overboard first and get to land, ▷ ①Lit throw themselves

column.name: text
column.value: and the rest were to follow, some on planks, and others on various things from the ship. And so it happened that they all were brought safely to land.

column.name: text
column.value: When they had been brought safely through, then we found out that the island was called ①Malta. ▷ ①Or Melita

column.name: text
column.value: The ①natives showed us extraordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and took us all in because of the rain that had started and because of the cold. ▷ ①Gr barbaroi, referring to people who did not speak Greek

column.name: text
column.value: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out ①because of the heat and fastened itself on his hand. ▷ ①Or from the heat

column.name: text
column.value: When the ①natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they began saying to one another, “Undoubtedly this man is a murderer, and though he has been saved from the sea, ②justice has not allowed him to live.” ▷ ①See note v 2 ②Or Justice; i.e., the personification of a goddess

column.name: text
column.value: However, ①Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no harm. ▷ ①Lit he

column.name: text
column.value: Now they were expecting that he was going to swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had waited a long time and had seen nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and began to say that he was a god.

column.name: text
column.value: Now in the neighboring parts of that place were lands belonging to the ①leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and entertained us warmly for three days. ▷ ①Prob. the Roman governor of the island

column.name: text
column.value: And it happened that the father of Publius was lying in bed afflicted with a recurring fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after he prayed, he laid his hands on him and healed him.

column.name: text
column.value: After this happened, the rest of the people on the island who had diseases were coming to him and being cured.

column.name: text
column.value: They also showed us many honors, and when we were about to set sail, they ①supplied us with ②everything we needed. ▷ ①Or put on board ②Lit the things pertaining to the needs

column.name: text
column.value: After three months we set sail on an Alexandrian ship which had wintered at the island, and which had ①the Twin Brothers for its figurehead. ▷ ①Gr Dioscuri; i.e., Castor and Pollux, twin sons of Zeus

column.name: text
column.value: After we put in at Syracuse, we stayed there for three days.

column.name: text
column.value: From there we sailed around and arrived at Rhegium, and a day later a south wind came up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli.

column.name: text
column.value: ①There we found some brothers and sisters, and were invited to stay with them for seven days; and that is how we came to Rome. ▷ ①Lit Where

column.name: text
column.value: And from there the brothers and sisters, when they heard about us, came as far as the ①Market of Appius and the ②Three Inns to meet us; and when Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage. ▷ ①Lat Appii Forum, a station about 43 miles or 69.2 km from Rome ②Lat Tres Tabernae, a station about 33 miles or 53.1 km from Rome

column.name: text
column.value: When we entered Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself, with the soldier who was guarding him.

column.name: text
column.value: After three days ①Paul called together those who were the leading men of the Jews, and when they came together, he began saying to them, “Brothers, though I had done nothing against our people or the customs of our ②fathers, yet I was handed over to the Romans as a prisoner from Jerusalem. ▷ ①Lit he ②Or forefathers

column.name: text
column.value: And when they had examined me, they were willing to release me because there were no grounds ①for putting me to death. ▷ ①Lit of death in me

column.name: text
column.value: But when the Jews ①objected, I was forced to appeal to Caesar, not that I had any accusation against my nation. ▷ ①Lit spoke against

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason, therefore, I ①requested to see you and to speak with you, since I am wearing this chain for the sake of the hope of Israel.” ▷ ①Or invited you to see me and speak with me

column.name: text
column.value: They said to him, “We have neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor has any of the brothers come here and reported or spoken anything bad about you.

column.name: text
column.value: But we desire to hear from you what ①your views are; for regarding this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere.” ▷ ①Lit you think

column.name: text
column.value: When they had set a day for ①Paul, people came to him at his lodging in large numbers; and he was explaining to them by solemnly testifying about the kingdom of God and trying to persuade them concerning Jesus, from both the Law of Moses and from the Prophets, from morning until evening. ▷ ①Lit him

column.name: text
column.value: Some were being persuaded by the things said by Paul, but others would not believe.

column.name: text
column.value: And when they disagreed with one another, they began leaving after Paul said one parting statement: “The Holy Spirit rightly spoke through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,

column.name: text
text
column.value: FOR THE HEARTS OF THIS PEOPLE HAVE BECOME ①INSENSITIVE, AND WITH THEIR EARS THEY ②HARDLY HEAR, AND THEY HAVE CLOSED THEIR EYES; OTHERWISE THEY MIGHT SEE WITH THEIR EYES, AND HEAR WITH THEIR EARS, AND UNDERSTAND WITH THEIR HEART AND RETURN, AND I WOULD HEAL THEM.” ’ ▷ ①Lit dull ②Or are hard of hearing

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will also listen.” ① ▷ ①Late mss add as v 29: When he had spoken these words, the Jews departed, having a great dispute among themselves.

column.name: text
column.value: Now Paul stayed two full years ①in his own rented lodging and welcomed all who came to him, ▷ ①Or at his own expense

column.name: text
column.value: ①preaching the kingdom of God and teaching things about the Lord Jesus Christ with all openness, unhindered. ▷ ①Or proclaiming

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore you have no excuse, ①you foolish person, everyone of you who passes judgment; for ②in that matter in which you judge someone else, you condemn yourself; for you who judge practice the same things. ▷ ①Lit O ②Or when you judge

column.name: text
column.value: And we know that the judgment of God ①rightly falls upon those who practice such things. ▷ ①Lit is according to truth against

column.name: text
column.value: But do you suppose this, ①you foolish person who passes judgment on those who practice such things, and yet does them as well, that you will escape the judgment of God? ▷ ①Lit O

column.name: text
column.value: Or do you think lightly of the riches of His kindness and ①restraint and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God leads you to repentance? ▷ ①I.e., from inflicting punishment

column.name: text
column.value: But ①because of your stubbornness and unrepentant heart you are storing up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, ▷ ①Or in accordance with

column.name: text
column.value: who WILL REPAY EACH PERSON ACCORDING TO HIS DEEDS:

column.name: text
column.value: to those who by perseverance in doing good seek glory, honor, and immortality, He will give eternal life;

column.name: text
column.value: but to those who are self-serving and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, He will give wrath and indignation.

column.name: text
column.value: There will be tribulation and distress ①for every soul of mankind who does evil, ②for the Jew first and also ③for the Greek, ▷ ①Lit upon ②Lit of the ③Lit of the

column.name: text
column.value: but glory, honor, and peace to everyone who does what is good, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

column.name: text
column.value: For there is no partiality with God.

column.name: text
column.value: For all who have sinned ①without the Law will also perish ②without the Law, and all who have sinned ③under the Law will be judged ④by the Law; ▷ ①Or without law ②Or without law ③Or under law ④Or by law

column.name: text
column.value: for it is not the hearers ①of the Law who are ②righteous before God, but the doers ③of the Law who will be justified. ▷ ①Or of law ②Or just ③Or of law

column.name: text
column.value: For when Gentiles who do not have ①the Law ②instinctively perform the requirements of the Law, these, though not having ③the Law, are a law to themselves, ▷ ①Or law ②Lit by nature ③Or law

column.name: text
column.value: in that they show the work of the Law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying and their thoughts alternately accusing or else defending them,

column.name: text
column.value: on the day when, according to my gospel, God will judge the secrets of mankind through Christ Jesus.

column.name: text
column.value: But if you call yourself a ①Jew and rely ②upon the Law and boast in God, ▷ ①Or Judean ②Or upon law

column.name: text
column.value: and know His will and ①distinguish the things that matter, being instructed from the Law, ▷ ①Or approve

column.name: text
column.value: and are confident that you yourself are a guide to people who are blind, a light to those in darkness,

column.name: text
column.value: a ①corrector of the foolish, a teacher of ②the immature, possessing in the Law the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth— ▷ ①Or instructor ②Lit infants

column.name: text
column.value: you, therefore, who teach someone else, do you not teach yourself? You who ①preach that one is not to steal, do you steal? ▷ ①Or proclaim

column.name: text
column.value: You who say that one is not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who loathe idols, do you rob temples?

column.name: text
column.value: You who boast ①in the Law, through your breaking the Law, do you dishonor God? ▷ ①Or in law

column.name: text
column.value: For “THE NAME OF GOD IS BLASPHEMED AMONG THE GENTILES BECAUSE OF YOU,” just as it is written.

column.name: text
column.value: For indeed circumcision is of value if you practice ①the Law; but if you are a violator ②of the Law, your circumcision has turned into uncircumcision. ▷ ①Or law ②Or of law

column.name: text
column.value: So if the ①uncircumcised man keeps the requirements of the Law, will his uncircumcision not be regarded as circumcision? ▷ ①Lit uncircumcision

column.name: text
column.value: And he who is physically uncircumcised, if he keeps the Law, will he not judge you who ①though having the letter of the Law and circumcision are a violator ②of the Law? ▷ ①Lit through the letter ②Or of law

column.name: text
column.value: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh.

column.name: text
column.value: But he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; and his praise is not from people, but from God.

column.name: text
column.value: Paul, a bond-servant of Christ Jesus, ①called as an apostle, set apart for the gospel of God, ▷ ①Lit a called apostle

column.name: text
column.value: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in the holy Scriptures,

column.name: text
column.value: concerning His Son, who was born of a ①descendant of David according to the flesh, ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: who was declared the Son of God with power according to the ①Spirit of holiness ②by the resurrection from the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord, ▷ ①Or spirit ②Or as a result of

column.name: text
column.value: through whom we have received grace and apostleship ①to bring about the obedience of faith among all the Gentiles in behalf of His name, ▷ ①Lit for obedience

column.name: text
column.value: among whom you also are the called of Jesus Christ;

column.name: text
column.value: to all who are beloved of God in Rome, called as ①saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. ▷ ①Lit holy ones; i.e., God’s people

column.name: text
column.value: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ ①for you all, because your faith is being proclaimed throughout the world. ▷ ①Or concerning you all, that...

column.name: text
column.value: For God, whom I serve in my spirit in the preaching of the gospel of His Son, is my witness as to how unceasingly I make mention of you,

column.name: text
column.value: always in my prayers requesting if perhaps now, at last by the will of God, I will succeed in coming to you.

column.name: text
column.value: For I long to see you so that I may impart some spiritual gift to you, that you may be ①established; ▷ ①Or strengthened

column.name: text
column.value: that is, that I may be encouraged together with you while among you, each of us by the other’s faith, both yours and mine.

column.name: text
column.value: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that often I have planned to come to you (and have been prevented so far) so that I may obtain some fruit among you also just as among the rest of the Gentiles.

column.name: text
column.value: I am ①under obligation both to Greeks and to the ②uncultured, both to the wise and to the foolish. ▷ ①I.e., non-Hellenes ②Lit debtor

column.name: text
column.value: So, for my part, I am eager to preach the gospel to you also who are in Rome.

column.name: text
column.value: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.

column.name: text
column.value: For in it the righteousness of God is revealed ①from faith to faith; as it is written: “ ②BUT THE RIGHTEOUS one will live by faith.” ▷ ①Or by ②Or But the one who is righteous by faith shall live

column.name: text
column.value: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth ①in unrighteousness, ▷ ①Or by

column.name: text
column.value: because that which is known about God is evident ①within them; for God made it evident to them. ▷ ①Or among

column.name: text
column.value: For since the creation of the world His invisible attributes, that is, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly perceived, being understood by what has been made, so that they are without excuse.

column.name: text
column.value: For even though they knew God, they did not ①honor Him as God or give thanks, but they became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless hearts were darkened. ▷ ①Lit glorify

column.name: text
column.value: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,

column.name: text
column.value: and they exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for an image in the form of corruptible mankind, of birds, four-footed animals, and ①crawling creatures. ▷ ①Or reptiles

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore God gave them up to vile impurity in the lusts of their hearts, so that their bodies would be dishonored among them.

column.name: text
column.value: For they exchanged the truth of God for ①falsehood, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed ②forever. Amen. ▷ ①Lit the lie ②Lit unto the ages

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason God gave them over to degrading passions; for their women exchanged natural relations for that which is contrary to nature,

column.name: text
column.value: and likewise the men, too, abandoned natural relations ①with women and burned in their desire toward one another, males with males committing ②shameful acts and receiving in ③their own persons the due penalty of their error. ▷ ①Lit of the female ②Lit shamelessness ③Lit themselves

column.name: text
column.value: And just as they did not see fit ①to acknowledge God, God gave them up to a depraved mind, to do those things that are not proper, ▷ ①Lit to have God in knowledge

column.name: text
column.value: people having been filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, and evil; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice; they are gossips,

column.name: text
column.value: slanderers, ①haters of God, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of evil, disobedient to parents, ▷ ①Or hateful to God

column.name: text
column.value: without understanding, untrustworthy, unfeeling, and unmerciful;

column.name: text
column.value: and although they know the ordinance of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, they not only do the same, but also approve of those who practice them.

column.name: text
column.value: What then shall we say that Abraham, ①our forefather according to the flesh, has found? ▷ ①Or our forefather, has found according to the flesh

column.name: text
column.value: For if Abraham was justified ①by works, he has something to boast about; but not ②before God. ▷ ①Lit out of ②Lit toward

column.name: text
column.value: For what does the Scripture say? “ABRAHAM BELIEVED GOD, AND IT WAS CREDITED TO HIM AS RIGHTEOUSNESS.”

column.name: text
column.value: Now to the one who works, the wages are not credited as a favor, but as what is due.

column.name: text
column.value: But to the one who does not work, but believes in Him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited as righteousness,

column.name: text
column.value: just as David also speaks of the blessing of the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:

column.name: text
column.value: “BLESSED ARE THOSE WHOSE LAWLESS DEEDS HAVE BEEN FORGIVEN, AND WHOSE SINS HAVE BEEN COVERED.

column.name: text
column.value: BLESSED IS THE MAN WHOSE SIN THE LORD WILL NOT TAKE INTO ACCOUNT.”

column.name: text
column.value: Is this blessing then on ①the circumcised, or on ②the uncircumcised also? For we say, “FAITH WAS CREDITED TO ABRAHAM AS RIGHTEOUSNESS.” ▷ ①Lit circumcision ②Lit uncircumcision

column.name: text
column.value: How then was it credited? While he was ①circumcised, or ②uncircumcised? Not while ③circumcised, but while ④uncircumcised; ▷ ①Lit in circumcision ②Lit in uncircumcision ③Lit in circumcision ④Lit in uncircumcision

column.name: text
column.value: and he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which ①he had while uncircumcised, so that he might be the father of all who believe without being circumcised, that righteousness might be credited to them, ▷ ①Lit was in uncircumcision

column.name: text
column.value: and the father of circumcision to those who not only are of the circumcision, but who also follow in the steps of the faith of our father Abraham which ①he had while uncircumcised. ▷ ①Lit was in uncircumcision

column.name: text
column.value: For the promise to Abraham or to his ①descendants that he would be heir of the world was not ②through the Law, but through the righteousness of faith. ▷ ①Lit seed ②Or through law

column.name: text
column.value: For if those who are ①of the Law are heirs, then faith is made void and the promise is nullified; ▷ ①Or of law

column.name: text
column.value: for the Law brings about wrath, but where there is no law, there also is no violation.

column.name: text
column.value: For this reason it is ①by faith, in order that it may be in accordance with grace, so that the promise will be guaranteed to all the ②descendants, not only to ③those who are of the Law, but also to ④those who are of the faith of Abraham, who is the father of us all, ▷ ①Lit that which is ②Lit that which is ③Or out of ④Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: (as it is written: “I HAVE MADE YOU A FATHER OF MANY NATIONS”) in the presence of Him whom he believed, that is, God, who gives life to the dead and calls into being things that do not exist.

column.name: text
column.value: In hope against hope he believed, so that he might become a father of many nations according to that which had been spoken, “SO SHALL YOUR ①DESCENDANTS BE.” ▷ ①Lit seed

column.name: text
column.value: Without becoming weak in faith he contemplated his own body, now as good as dead since he was about a hundred years old, and the deadness of Sarah’s womb;

column.name: text
column.value: yet, with respect to the promise of God, he did not waver in unbelief but grew strong in faith, giving glory to God,

column.name: text
column.value: and being fully assured that what God had promised, He was able also to perform.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore IT WAS ALSO CREDITED TO HIM AS RIGHTEOUSNESS.

column.name: text
column.value: Now not for his sake only was it written that it was credited to him,

column.name: text
column.value: but for our sake also, to whom it will be credited, to us who believe in Him who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,

column.name: text
column.value: He who was delivered over because of our wrongdoings, and was raised because of our justification.

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, having been justified by faith, ①we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ, ▷ ①Two early mss let’s have

column.name: text
column.value: through whom we also have obtained our introduction by faith into this grace in which we stand; and ①we celebrate in hope of the glory of God. ▷ ①Lit we boast; or let’s

column.name: text
column.value: And not only this, but ①we also celebrate in our tribulations, knowing that tribulation brings about perseverance; ▷ ①Lit we also boast; or let’s also boast

column.name: text
column.value: and perseverance, proven character; and proven character, hope;

column.name: text
column.value: and hope does not disappoint, because the love of God has been poured out within our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.

column.name: text
column.value: For while we were still helpless, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly.

column.name: text
column.value: For one will hardly die for a righteous person; ①though perhaps for the good person someone would even dare to die. ▷ ①Lit for

column.name: text
column.value: But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

column.name: text
column.value: Much more then, having now been justified ①by His blood, we shall be saved from the wrath of God through Him. ▷ ①Or in

column.name: text
column.value: For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved ①by His life. ▷ ①Or in

column.name: text
column.value: And not only this, but ①we also celebrate in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation. ▷ ①Lit also boasting

column.name: text
column.value: Therefore, just as through one man sin entered into the world, and death through sin, and so death spread to all mankind, because all sinned—

column.name: text
column.value: for ①until the Law sin was in the world, but sin is not ②counted against anyone when there is no law. ▷ ①Or until law ②Lit credited to

column.name: text
column.value: Nevertheless death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of the ①violation committed by Adam, who is a ②type of Him who was to come. ▷ ①I.e., of God’s command ②Or foreshadowing

column.name: text
column.value: But ①the gracious gift is not like the offense. For if by the offense of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one Man, Jesus Christ, overflow to the many. ▷ ①Lit not as the offense, so also is the gracious gift

column.name: text
column.value: The gift is not like that which came through the one who sinned; for on the one hand the judgment arose from one offense, ①resulting in condemnation, but on the other hand the gracious gift arose from many offenses, ②resulting in justification. ▷ ①Lit to condemnation ②Lit to an act of righteousness

column.name: text
column.value: For if by the offense of the one, death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the One, Jesus Christ.

column.name: text
column.value: So then, as through one offense ①the result was condemnation to all mankind, so also through one act of righteousness ②the result was justification of life to all mankind. ▷ ①Lit to condemnation ②Lit to justification

column.name: text
column.value: For as through the one man’s disobedience the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the One the many will be made righteous.

column.name: text
column.value: ①The Law came in so that the offense would increase; but where sin increased, grace abounded all the more, ▷ ①Or law

column.name: text
column.value: so that, as sin reigned in death, so also grace would reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

column.name: text
column.value: Then what ①advantage does the Jew have? Or what is the benefit of circumcision? ▷ ①Lit is the advantage of the Jew

column.name: text
column.value: Great in every respect. First, that they were entrusted with the actual words of God.

column.name: text
column.value: What then? If some ①did not believe, their ②unbelief will not nullify the faithfulness of God, will it? ▷ ①Or were unfaithful ②Or unfaithfulness

column.name: text
column.value: ①Far from it! Rather, God must prove to be true, though every person be found a liar, as it is written: “SO THAT YOU ARE JUSTIFIED IN YOUR WORDS, AND PREVAIL ②WHEN YOU ARE JUDGED.” ▷ ①Lit May it never happen! And so throughout the ch ②Or in Your judging

column.name: text
column.value: But if our unrighteousness ①demonstrates the righteousness of God, what shall we say? The God who inflicts wrath is not unrighteous, is He? (I am speaking from a human viewpoint.) ▷ ①I.e., by requiring His judgment

column.name: text
column.value: Far from it! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?

column.name: text
column.value: But if through my lie the truth of God abounded to His glory, why am I also still being judged as a sinner?

column.name: text
column.value: And why not say (just as we are slanderously reported and as some claim that we say), “Let’s do evil that good may come of it”? ①Their condemnation is deserved. ▷ ①Lit Whose

column.name: text
column.value: What then? ①Are we better than they? Not at all; for we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin; ▷ ①Or Are we worse

column.name: text
column.value: as it is written: “THERE IS NO RIGHTEOUS PERSON, NOT EVEN ONE;

column.name: text
column.value: THERE IS NO ONE WHO UNDERSTANDS, THERE IS NO ONE WHO SEEKS OUT GOD;

column.name: text
column.value: THEY HAVE ALL TURNED ASIDE, TOGETHER THEY HAVE BECOME ①CORRUPT; THERE IS NO ONE WHO DOES GOOD, THERE IS NOT EVEN ONE.” ▷ ①Or depraved

column.name: text
column.value: “THEIR THROAT IS AN OPEN GRAVE, WITH THEIR TONGUES THEY KEEP DECEIVING,” “THE VENOM OF ①ASPS IS UNDER THEIR LIPS”; ▷ ①I.e., venomous snakes

column.name: text
column.value: “THEIR MOUTH IS FULL OF CURSING AND BITTERNESS”;

column.name: text
column.value: “THEIR FEET ARE SWIFT TO SHED BLOOD,

column.name: text
